causal_research.bug_semantics: OpenClaw's HTML session exporter renders image content blocks by building in template.js (tool-result images and user-message images). mimeType is interpolated into an HTML attribute with no whitelist or escaping. An attacker who can place a crafted image block in session data (tool result or session manipulation) can supply mimeType=image/png" onerror="alert(...) , break out of the src attribute, and execute JavaScript when a user opens the exported HTML. The 2026.2.23 fix introduces sanitizeImageMimeType() (SAFE_IMAGE_MIME_RE of known image/* types, else application/octet-stream), which cannot contain quotes or event-handler text.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Feishu im.message.reaction.created_v1 is turned into a synthetic FeishuMessageEvent by resolveReactionSyntheticEvent and dispatched through handleFeishuMessage. Authorization is keyed off event.message.chat_type: bot.ts sets isGroup only when chatType === "group", and only that branch applies groupAllowFrom (group ID allowlist) and requireMention (default true). Before 2026.3.12, omitted or non-group event.chat_type was forced to p2p while chat_id still came from the event or from getMessageFeishu's looked-up group oc_ id. A group reaction that omitted chat_type was therefore authorized as a DM: groupAllowFrom was skipped and requireMention stayed false, so an unmentioned group reaction could drive an agent turn.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Arbitrary SQL execution via prompt injection in the multi-stage Text2SQL workflow (CWE-89/CWE-74, CVSS 6.3 medium, unreviewed VulDB-derived GHSA; CVE frames it as injection through the 'keywords' argument). User chat input flows through 4 LLM nodes (agent call-tool, information extraction producing rewrite_question/keywords, schema linking, SQL generation); the generated SQL is then executed directly with zero validation: _execute_sql in openchatbi/text2sql/generate_sql.py calls connection.execute(text(sql)) (SQLAlchemy). An attacker uses prompt injection to force the LLM into emitting arbitrary SQL (PoC: PostgreSQL COPY cmd_exec FROM PROGRAM 'id'), obtaining RCE on the database server. GitHub issue #11 (Ka7arotto, 2026-01-27) documents the full chain; exploit writeup github.com/Ka7arotto/cve/openchatbi-SQL.

causal_research.bug_semantics: expandapk.Split parses an APK as concatenated gzip members. After gzip.NewReader + Multistream(false) and reading the first tar header, it drains the rest of that gzip member with io.Copy(io.Discard, gzi) for the optional .SIGN. stream and again for the control stream, with no uncompressed-size or inflate-ratio limit. An attacker-controlled APK therefore forces the process to fully inflate those gzip members, causing unbounded CPU/time (CWE-400/770 availability). The leftover data section is then returned as the raw remainder of the input. The v1.1.0 fix wraps those gzip drains (and the data remainder) in limitio limited readers.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Gogs stores each owner's Git directories under UserPath(name)=filepath.Join(repositoryRoot, strings.ToLower(name)) and RepositoryPath(owner, repo)=filepath.Join(UserPath(owner), strings.ToLower(repo)+".git"). CreateOrganization then os.MkdirAlls that owner path. The web org form has always required AlphaDashDot (alphanumeric, dash, underscore, dot only), which rejects '/' and therefore '../' sequences. The JSON org-create API instead bound go-gogs-client CreateOrgOption.UserName with only Required. CreateOrganization's isUsernameAllowed/IsUsableName check is a reserved-name list, not a character class, so a name such as ../../../../data/gogs/data/tmp/local-r/{id}/nested is stored and materialized on disk. Creating a repository under that org writes a nested .git (including hooks/) into another repository's local worktree; the attacker then commits a malicious hooks/update through the outer repo and triggers it, getting RCE as the git user. Default self-registration plus POST /api/v1/user/orgs makes this unauthenticated-to-RCE after account creation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: NiceGUI client-side runMethod(target, method_name, args) treated an unknown method name as JavaScript and executed it with eval(method_name)(...). causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated DELETE /api/v1/folders/{id} (delete_folder_by_id in backend/open_webui/routers/folders.py) first resolves the folder as the caller's own row. On miss it loads the folder by id only. For a subfolder (folder.parent_id set), the gate was admin OR _has_folder_access(user.id, folder, 'write'). has_folder_access walks ancestors, so a write grant on a shared root is inherited by every descendant. After the check, folder_owner_id = folder.user_id and the handler deletes (or, with delete_contents=false, force-moves) chats and subfolders under that owner id, not the caller's. causal_research.bug_semantics: aiohttp's client follows 3xx responses by looping in ClientSession._request and sending a new ClientRequest built from the same caller headers mapping. Cookie-jar cookies are re-filtered per hop URL, but an explicit Cookie request header is copied into that reused CIMultiDict and then merged by ClientRequest into the outgoing Cookie header with no origin check. Proxy-Authorization supplied as a request header is likewise reused. On cross-origin redirect the client already dropped Authorization (and cleared auth) but left those two headers, so a first-hop server can 3xx to another origin and receive the caller's cookie and proxy credentials. The 3.13.4 fix pops Cookie and Proxy-Authorization in the same origin-change block.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated FAQ editor can persist an HTML whose src is a filesystem path that does not contain the substring 'content' (for example ../../../etc/passwd). During PDF export, TCPDF calls Wrapper::Image(), which parse_url()s the src and passes it to concatenatePaths(PMF_ROOT_DIR, $file). concatenatePaths() locates 'content' with strpos(); a miss returns false, which is used as substr() offset 0 (implicitly, then explicitly via (int)$pos), so the joined path is PMF_ROOT_DIR plus the attacker-controlled relative path. Image() then file_get_contents()s that path with no realpath() prefix check, so readable files outside the intended content/ tree can be pulled into PDF generation.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The advisory's defective heuristic was first written in 46436ed7c8a5f95c89e711cad3a155666dc11574, which replaced concatenatePaths()'s basename-prefix strip with $pos = strpos($trimmedFile, 'content'); $relativePath = substr($trimmedFile, $pos);. The immediate parent 434bb21dc5f2ef88fe048622ec69254922af1e0c still has the older basename body and no strpos('content'). The (int) cast in b4d6dd59a is a later type-hint that documents the same false->0 coercion rather than introducing it. Nine days after the BIC, 3cf01e8a3d9678b91ed919dedab383ef09474688 corrected Image()'s call from the broken file_get_contents(PMF_ROOT_DIR, concatenatePaths($file)) to file_get_contents(concatenatePaths(PMF_ROOT_DIR, $file)), making the already-written function body a live sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Kiota generate/show/info and related commands parse the user-supplied OpenAPI description with Microsoft.OpenApi LoadExternalRefs=true and the library default stream loader. An attacker-influenced description can therefore $ref an absolute http(s) URL (build-host SSRF plus remote schema inclusion) or an absolute/out-of-tree/relative file path (local file inclusion). Resolved content is inlined into the generated client. Kiota escapes generated identifiers/strings/comments, so this is not RCE; the host-side fetch/read is the vulnerability. The 2026 fix does not disable LoadExternalRefs; it default-denies external loads via AllowedExternalOriginsStreamLoader unless --allowed-external-origins opts specific origins back in.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Open WebUI's terminal proxy forwards the caller's identity to the upstream terminal/orchestrator as an unsigned claim. On the WebSocket path, ws_terminal interpolates the attacker-controlled session_id path parameter into the upstream URL and then appends ?user_id=<authenticated caller>. session_id is not validated or URL-encoded (unlike HTTP _sanitize_proxy_path), so an encoded query delimiter survives Open WebUI's single decode, is decoded again upstream, and injects a spoofed user_id that typical query parsers bind first. The HTTP path also forwards X-User-Id without integrity binding, but spoofing that header through Open WebUI itself is not the injection; it requires reaching the upstream by other means.

causal_research.bug_semantics: HAXcms ships an HTML force-download mitigation in the root .htaccess (added for CVE-2026-22704) using the case-sensitive directive `SetEnvIf Request_URI "/files/.*\.html?$" force_html_download=1` + `Header always set Content-Disposition "attachment" env=force_html_download`. HAXCMSFile.php's upload path validates extensions case-INSENSITIVELY (regex `/(jpg|...|html|md)$/i`) and writes the uploaded filename to disk verbatim (only the basename is sanitized; extension keeps original case). An uppercase `.HTML` upload passes validation, is stored verbatim under /files/, and the SetEnvIf rule fails to match, so Apache serves it as text/html and renders inline - stored XSS in the HAXcms origin, bypassing the CVE-2026-22704 mitigation. The mismatch is exploitable only once BOTH halves exist.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When the optional voice-call plugin is enabled with inboundPolicy allowlist or pairing, inbound provider webhooks deliver event.from into CallManager.processEvent, which gates call-record creation on shouldAcceptInbound. Affected code strips non-digits then treats a caller as allowed if either normalized number is a suffix of the other. Missing/empty From becomes "", and String.prototype.endsWith('') is true for every allowlist entry, so anonymous/restricted callers are accepted. Independently, any caller whose E.164 digits end with an allowlisted number (for example +99915550001234 vs +15550001234) is accepted. Accepted calls reach the voice-call agent auto-response path and tool execution. Default inboundPolicy is disabled, so only operators who install the plugin and opt into allowlist/pairing are exposed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When IRC Federation is enabled (IRC_Enabled, default false), RFC2813.onReceiveFromPeer splits the peer TCP stream and calls parseMessage(line). After prefix/command stripping, parseMessage uses String.search(/^:|\s+:/) to decide whether a trailing parameter exists. On a line with a long whitespace run and no following colon (PoC: valid ':nick!user@host PRIVMSG #channel Hello ' + 100000 spaces + NUL + 'Trailing'), the engine retries \s+: from successive offsets with greedy backtracking, which is quadratic in the whitespace length (measured 20k spaces ~318ms; 100k spaces seconds). CPU stall on the Meteor server is the impact. A second regex (.*?)(?:^:|\s+:)(.*) is used only when search hits; it is the same delimiter pattern and is also not linear. Reachability requires an enabled IRC bridge and a peer (or on-path injector) that can send the crafted line; this is not an unauthenticated HTTP route.

mechanism.impact: Event-loop starvation in the Meteor server process: parseMessage runs synchronously in the socket 'data' handler, so every HTTP/WebSocket request stalls for the duration of the regex work. Measured on the exact HEAD file: a 32 KB line blocks 830 ms, growth is quadratic, so a single 1 MB line extrapolates to roughly 13 minutes of blocked event loop, and the peer can repeat it (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L).

No registration is needed: parsing happens before the PASS/SERVER registration check in peerCommandHandlers.js, so an unregistered peer triggers it. mechanism.summary: A remote IRC peer line reaches parseMessage(), where `line.search(/^:|\s+:/)` scans the whole string while backtracking `\s+` inside a whitespace run for every start position; a long whitespace run with no following ':' burns quadratic CPU in the single-threaded Node event loop and stalls all Rocket.Chat traffic (CWE-1333 / CWE-400 denial of service).
mechanism.trigger: Any line arriving on the outbound RFC2813 peer socket whose text after prefix and command stripping is a long whitespace run followed by no ':' anywhere later, e.g. `:irc.example PRIVMSG #chan` + 32 KB of spaces + `X`; onReceiveFromPeer (RFC2813/index.js:138-173) splits the receive buffer on CRLF/CR/LF/BEL and calls parseMessage for every non-empty line that does not start with 'a' (RFC2813/index.js:155-157).

causal_research.bug_semantics: The deprecated oidc-provider plugin (and mcp, which constructs oidcProvider and copies the same registration schema) accepts OAuth client redirect URIs as an unvalidated string array. An attacker who can call POST /oauth2/register (authenticated by default; unauthenticated if allowDynamicClientRegistration is true) stores a javascript: URI. A client-side consent page that assigns that value to window.location.href/location.assign executes the payload in the authorization-server origin, exposing the session (stored XSS / account takeover). Server-side Location redirects and the demo consent-buttons.tsx path that reads a non-existent uri field are not this sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PinchTab's HTTP API authenticates with a bearer token on essentially all routes, including GET /health when a token is configured. A RateLimitMiddleware intended to cap 120 requests per 10 seconds per client was added in v0.7.7 but never inserted into the production handler chain through v0.8.3 (cmd_dashboard.go, then internal/server/server.go wrapped only Logging/Cors/Auth). An attacker who can reach the listener can therefore guess a weak token as fast as the server will accept, with no 429. The unused limiter also treated the first X-Forwarded-For hop as the rate-limit key with no trusted-proxy check, so even an enabled copy would have been spoofable. v0.8.4 enabled the middleware and keyed on the immediate peer IP, but still skipped /health and /metrics, leaving the same online-guessing path unthrottled until v0.8.5.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Control UI isTrustedRetryEndpoint(url) decided whether a gateway WebSocket URL was trusted enough to attach a cached device token after AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH. Loopback trust used hostname prefix matching (`host.startsWith("127.")`) instead of an IPv4 parse. code_evidence.summary: Claude-assisted adapter code let OUROBOROS_CLI_PATH choose the executable handed to the Claude SDK. Once Ouroboros loaded a cloned project .env, that path became repository-controlled and could run attacker code.
code_evidence.mechanism: A project-local .env populated OUROBOROS_CLI_PATH; the adapter resolved that value and supplied it as the executable path to the Claude Agent SDK.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When Parse Server GraphQL is mounted via ParseGraphQLServer.applyGraphQL, the GraphQL path is wrapped in the default npm cors() middleware (no origin callback) instead of the REST allowCrossDomain middleware. After allowOrigin exists, REST sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin from Config.allowOrigin (default '*'), but GraphQL still advertises unrestricted CORS. From Apollo v4 onward the Apollo context factory also does res.set('access-control-allow-origin', req.get('origin') || '*'), reflecting any attacker Origin. Trigger: a browser on a disallowed origin sends Origin plus GraphQL POST/OPTIONS to the configured graphQLPath. Vulnerable code: src/GraphQL/ParseGraphQLServer.js applyGraphQL corsMiddleware() and, later, the context header write. Impact: CWE-346 origin-validation bypass; sites the operator excluded can still make cross-origin GraphQL calls (and preflight succeeds). Preconditions: GraphQL enabled; allowOrigin configured to restrict origins. Counterevidence: REST /parse continues to enforce allowOrigin; default allowOrigin remains '*', so the bypass is only relative to a configured restriction.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Gogs treats attacker-controlled redirect_to as a same-site path if IsSameSite (historically isValidRedirect / IsSameSiteURLPath) returns true, then issues c.Redirect to that string. Through v0.14.2 the predicate only required length>=2, a leading '/', and that the second byte was not '/' or '\'. That accepts /a/../\example.com. Browsers normalize '\' to '/' in Location, so the path becomes /a/..//example.com and then a protocol-relative //example.com cross-origin redirect after login (and on other post-action redirect_to flows). The 0.14.3 fix normalizes raw and percent-encoded backslashes plus CR/LF/tab, then rejects any result that is not a single-slash-prefixed path or that contains '//'.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When hooks.enabled is true, createHooksRequestHandler (originally inline handleHooksRequest) extracts a caller-supplied hook token (Authorization: Bearer, later also X-OpenClaw-Token / historical x-clawdis-token or query token) and authenticates with JavaScript string inequality against the configured hooks.token. Because !== short-circuits on the first differing character and also on missing/unequal length, a network attacker who can reach the hooks HTTP surface can collect many 401 vs success timings and gradually recover the secret, then invoke POST /hooks/wake or /hooks/agent. The direct fix replaces that compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual via safeEqualSecret and rate-limits repeated auth failures.

causal_research.bug_semantics: BlueBubbles webhook reactions are handled by processReaction, a separate ingress from processMessage. After groupPolicy/allowlist allow, processReaction builds a 'reacted with …' / 'removed … reaction' string and calls core.system.enqueueSystemEvent into the group agent session. processMessage consults core.channel.groups.resolveRequireMention (plugin runtime: resolveChannelGroupRequireMention, default true) and drops group text that is not an explicit mention. Reactions never ran that check, so in a mention-gated group any allowed participant could tapback a message and inject an agent-visible system event without mentioning the bot. CWE-288 alternate-path bypass. Preconditions: BlueBubbles group chat, sender allowed by group policy, requireMention true (the default when unset).

causal_research.bug_semantics: An operator can configure a remote MCP server as transport SSE with headers.Authorization (npm package openclaw, src/agents/pi-bundle-mcp-tools.ts at introduction; later src/agents/mcp-transport.ts). OpenClaw constructs SSEClientTransport with those headers in requestInit and, after 32b7c00f, also in eventSourceInit.fetch. The MCP TypeScript SDK 1.28.0 EventSource wrapper copies requestInit into every SSE GET via _commonHeaders(); the eventsource client issues fetch(..., {redirect:'follow'}). Undici then follows 3xx Location hops while the Authorization header remains attached, so a configured bearer token is sent to a different origin. Streamable HTTP received a manual redirect scrub in 47eb2d48 (#80906); SSE kept default-follow until 3c6259. Impact is credential leakage (CWE-522) when the SSE feature is enabled and a lower-trust or attacker-controlled redirect target is reachable. Same-origin redirects keep auth; the defect is cross-origin forwarding.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the merge actually reaches the group allowlist path and not only the command path (resolveDmGroupAccessDecision consults effectiveGroupAllowFrom for groupPolicy=allowlist); that dmPolicy='allowlist' suppresses the store read so the bypass is policy-dependent; that the immediate parent has no storeAllowFrom in src/signal/monitor.ts (grep count 0) and no src/pairing/pairing-store.ts; that the parent's resolveGroupAllowFrom read only config (opts.groupAllowFrom / cfg.signal.groupAllowFrom / cfg.signal.allowFrom); and that the pre-fix unit tests asserted the fused group list as intended behaviour, so this was shipped behaviour rather than dead code.
mechanism.impact: Authorization bypass: DM pairing approvals leaked into group allowlist evaluation, so a DM-paired sender could participate in allowlisted groups without any groupAllowFrom entry; before 64de4b6 the same fused list also authorized group control commands for that sender. Advisory severity LOW (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R).
mechanism.preconditions: groupPolicy=allowlist explicitly configured for the Signal account; dmPolicy not 'allowlist' so the store is read (default 'pairing'); attacker identity present in the DM pairing store, which requires the owner to approve a DM pairing (UI:R); attacker then sends an inbound group message.
mechanism.summary: Under groupPolicy=allowlist a Signal sender holding only a DM pairing-store approval passed the group allowlist check, because resolveEffectiveAllowFromLists merged storeAllowFrom into effectiveGroupAllowFrom and the group check consumed that merged list; the same merged list also satisfied the group control-command authorizer, so a DM-paired sender could issue control commands in groups. This is an authorization-boundary bypass between DM pairing and group controls (CWE-863).
mechanism.trigger: Signal account configured with groupPolicy=allowlist, dmPolicy not 'allowlist' (default 'pairing'), and a sender whose identity is present in the Signal DM pairing store (owner-approved DM pairing) posts a group message.

code_evidence.mechanism: The webhook handler resolved payload.username through the Chat user list and passed that result to the outbound send path instead of retaining payload.user_id.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The Claude-coauthored change resolves a stable webhook user ID through mutable nickname or username data, then carries that resolved value into direct reply delivery. A renamed or colliding account can therefore redirect the bot's response.

causal_research.bug_semantics: App Router patches server-side fetch and keys the incremental fetch cache with generateCacheKey(url, init). For binary bodies the pre-fix code pushed UTF-8 TextDecoder output (or blob.text()/File.text()) into bodyChunks, then SHA-256 hashed JSON.stringify of those chunks. Invalid UTF-8 sequences are replaced with U+FFFD, so distinct byte strings such as 0xff vs 0xfe, or certain UTF-16 encodings of different text, hash to the same key. A later fetch to the same URL with a different non-UTF-8 body can be served the cached response body of the first request, leaking confidential POST response data. UTF-8 string bodies do not collide this way. Pages Router is out of scope. The request itself is not deduped.

mechanism.impact: Cross-request reuse of a cached response body: a fetch with a different but decode-equivalent byte body hits the cache entry written by the other request and returns that response body, disclosing the POST response body of a request with a different body. The request itself is not deduplicated; the response cache is what is confused.
mechanism.preconditions: App Router runtime (Pages Router is not vulnerable per the advisory); a server-side fetch that is cacheable (revalidate > 0, force-cache, unstable_cache, or the Server Components HMR cache); request body delivered as bytes (Uint8Array/Buffer, or a byte ReadableStream) whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 and whose charset is not UTF-8; the two colliding requests must share URL, method, headers and the other fields of the key.
mechanism.summary: A cacheable server-side fetch whose body is raw bytes reaches generateCacheKey, which (pre-fix) decoded the body with a non-fatal UTF-8 TextDecoder; two bodies that differ only in bytes that are invalid UTF-8 produce the same decoded string and therefore the same SHA-256 cache key, so the second request is served the first request's cached FETCH response body.
mechanism.trigger: fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body: new Uint8Array([...]), next: { revalidate: N } }) (or any other cacheable fetch path, e.g. force-cache, unstable_cache, or the Server Components HMR cache) where the body bytes are not valid UTF-8 - for example a non-UTF-8 charset payload such as the UTF-16LE bytes 0x83 0xC0 for a Hangul syllable versus 0x84 0xC0 for another, both of which decode to U+FFFD sequences.

The advisory is a real CWE-116 fetch-cache key collision: UTF-8 decoding of binary bodies collapses distinct invalid sequences to U+FFFD, so cached POST response bodies can leak across requests. The first write of that mechanism is named-human Wyatt Johnson in PR member 5117ed10 (parent still base64-encodes body bytes). The canary fix 025bf4a5 / member 65f6554 hex-encodes body bytes and is present via backports in the claimed patched tags. The advisory describes a real defect and it is reproducible from the local tree: before the fix, IncrementalCache.generateCacheKey read the request body through a non-fatal UTF-8 TextDecoder, so byte bodies that differ only in invalid UTF-8 sequences collapse to the same replacement-character string and hash to an identical SHA-256 cache key, letting a later POST be served the cached response body of a different POST to the same URL. causal_research.bug_semantics: Rekor accepts attacker-controlled proposed entries of type cose/v0.0.1. pkg/types/cose/v0.0.1/entry.go Unmarshal decodes spec, requires a public key, and calls validate(). validate() treats an empty spec.message as success (return nil) so CLI/retrieval can run without a COSE envelope, and therefore never assigns v.sign1Msg. When message is empty, sign1Msg stays nil and the Payload field access panics. The panic is recovered into HTTP 500; the process continues. Schema never required message, so an empty or omitted message plus a public key (and, after later Unmarshal hardening, a dummy envelope hash) is enough to reach Canonicalize.

descriptions:
### Summary
`system.run` exec allowlist analysis treated wrapper binaries as the effective executable and did not fully unwrap `env`/shell-dispatch wrappers.

This allowed wrapper-smuggled payloads (for example `env bash -lc ...`) to satisfy an allowlist entry for the wrapper while executing non-allowlisted commands.

### Impact
On affected versions, an actor who can trigger `system.run` requests under an allowlist policy could bypass intended allowlist restrictions by routing execution through wrapper binaries.

### Affected Packages / Versions
- Package: `openclaw` (npm)
- Affected: `<= 2026.2.21-2`
- Patched in next release: `2026.2.22` (pre-set below so publish can happen immediately after npm release)

### Fix Commit(s)
- `2b63592be57782c8946e521bc81286933f0f99c7`

### Release Process Note
`patched_versions` is pre-set to the planned next release (`>= 2026.2.22`).

After npm `2026.2.22` is published, this advisory can be published directly without further metadata edits.

OpenClaw thanks @tdjackey for reporting.

causal_research.bug_semantics: uutils rm implements --preserve-root (default) by testing whether the command-line path string looks like '/'. From first implementation that was filename != "/", later rewritten as path.has_root() && path.parent().is_none() in handle_dir. A symlink such as /tmp/rootlink -> / has a parent component, so is_root is false; rm -rf --preserve-root /tmp/rootlink/ (or an equivalent path that is a directory after following the link) therefore recursively removes through the link into the real root tree. GNU rm instead caches /'s device/inode and compares directories it enters. The 2026 fix adds is_root_path() that still accepts a literal '/', but also canonicalizes so a symlink (or nested symlink) to / is treated as root and rejected when preserve_root and recursive are set.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Gogs renders .ipynb files in the repository file viewer by parsing them with notebookjs, POSTing the rendered HTML to POST /-/api/sanitize_ipynb, and inserting the response into the DOM via jQuery append. causal_research.bug_semantics: Ray registers custom PyArrow extension types (ray.data.arrow_tensor, ray.data.arrow_tensor_v2, ray.data.arrow_variable_shaped_tensor) globally. When any Parquet reader in that process parses a file whose schema names one of those types, PyArrow invokes the registered __arrow_ext_deserialize__ with the column's serialized extension metadata. From PR #54831 until the 2.55.0 fix, that path called _deserialize_with_fallback, which attempted cloudpickle.loads on those bytes before falling back to JSON. A crafted Parquet file can therefore execute arbitrary Python during schema parsing, with no row-data read and no cluster authentication required. This reintroduced the same class of bug previously closed for PyExtensionType-based types (PR #45084).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Qwik City request handling parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data through formToObj. Starting with the complex-form rewrite, a dotted name such as items.0 made formToObj allocate items as a JavaScript Array because Number.isNaN(+nextKey) was false for numeric segments. A later field on the same path (items.toString, items.push, items.valueOf, items.length) then assigned onto that Array, overwriting methods or inflating length. Application code that treated parsed form data as a well-formed array could throw, confuse types, or do extra work. The 1.19.2 fix precomputes array paths and only creates an array when every key at that path is a canonical non-negative integer, dropping non-index keys instead of polluting the array.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A developer or CI that runs datamodel-codegen --extra-template-data <file> can supply a model-keyed JSON object whose comment string contains a literal carriage return (or VT/FF). DataModel.render() dumps extra_template_data into built-in Jinja2 context without neutralizing line terminators. Several shipped templates then emit `# {{ comment }}` on the same physical line as a class/alias statement. Python's tokenizer ends a `#` comment at a bare CR, so the remainder is compiled as Python in the generated module and executes at import. The schema itself can be benign; only the extras comment needs to be attacker-controlled. Custom templates are a separate, user-authored sink and are intentionally not sanitized by the fix.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Deriver::derive takes a caller &mut [u8], sets len = buf.len(), and passes (buf.as_mut_ptr(), &mut len) to OpenSSL EVP_PKEY_derive from otherwise safe Rust. PkeyCtxRef::derive does the same for Option<&mut [u8]>. The binding trusts OpenSSL to honor *keylen. On OpenSSL 1.1.x (and LibreSSL), the X25519, X448, DH, and HKDF-extract methods ignore the incoming length and unconditionally write the full shared secret (32, 56, or prime-size bytes). A short stack or heap slice is therefore overflowed. OpenSSL 3.x providers reject undersized buffers themselves, so the crash/corruption is specific to older OpenSSL. The 0.10.78 fix probes the natural size on 1.1.x/LibreSSL and, when it exceeds the caller buffer, derives into a temporary Vec then copies the leading bytes, closing the OOB while keeping ECDH truncation behavior.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS (CWE-79) in the lead index. An authenticated user with lead create/update access POSTs /lead/save; LeadRequest persisted the `name` field with only a max-length rule and no sanitization. GET /lead then rendered that stored value through two sinks in resources/views/lead/index.blade.php: (1) Blade's unescaped `{!! !!}` concatenated session('name') raw inside an HTML anchor in the save-confirmation alert (line 28 at the fix parent), so markup/script in the name executed in the app origin; (2) the delete control interpolated `$lead->name` into a JavaScript string literal in an onclick attribute (line 261). Blade `{{ }}` HTML-escapes quotes, but the HTML parser decodes them before the event-handler script runs, so a quote-breaking payload executes. The same view's text-context `{{ $lead->name }}` (line 100) is not exploitable. The CNA PoC uses the line-28 flash path in the creator's browser.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated non-master user PUTs JSON {expiresAt: null} (or createdWith: null) to /sessions/:objectId. RestWrite.prototype.handleSession on the update path (this.query set) used truthy tests this.data.expiresAt && !this.auth.isMaster && !this.auth.isMaintenance (and the same for createdWith). Because null is falsy, the INVALID_KEY_NAME throw is skipped and the client-supplied null is written onto _Session. Later Auth session validation does expiresAt = session.expiresAt ? new Date(session.expiresAt.iso) : undefined; if (expiresAt < now) reject; a missing/null expiresAt never compares as expired, so the session bypasses configured session length. The same truthy pattern also skipped installationId/sessionToken when those keys were null; the advisory impact is the expiresAt/createdWith immutability bypass.

mechanism.impact: Session expiry can be nullified so the session stays valid indefinitely, bypassing the configured session expiry/sessionLength policy and preserving a potentially stolen token; the same bypass nulls the createdWith audit metadata. mechanism.summary: An authenticated user sends a session update (PUT) whose body sets expiresAt (or createdWith) to null; the immutability guard used a truthiness test, so the null value slipped past it and the update persisted expiresAt: null, which Auth.js reads as no expiry, so the session never expires and configured session length policy is bypassed.
mechanism.trigger: HTTP PUT /parse/sessions/<own session objectId> with JSON body {"expiresAt": null} (or {"createdWith": null}) and the caller's own X-Parse-Session-Token.

The advisory is a real CWE-697: GHSA-jc39 added truthy immutability guards for expiresAt/createdWith on session UPDATE; null bypasses them and Auth treats a missing expiresAt as non-expired. The smallest first writer of those flawed comparison lines is named-human PR member 6277e9d (squash-decomposed from landing ea68fc0); immediate parent 94637aa lacks the lines. The minimum fix is the key-presence rewrite in 9a91fd1, squash-landed as 90802969 on 9.x (8.x twin ebccd7fe); patched tags 9.7.0-alpha.14 / 8.6.69 contain the landings. Repo-level AI-agent PR policy and later successful repair do not attribute the BIC. Verdict NOT_AI.
Independent re-derivation confirms the advisory as a real defect: before the fix, RestWrite.prototype.handleSession tested protected session fields by truthiness (this.data.expiresAt && ...), so a PUT to a session with body {"expiresAt": null} skipped the immutability guard, was written through as a Mongo $set null, and Auth.js treats a null or missing expiresAt as no expiry, leaving the session valid indefinitely. causal_research.bug_semantics: MISP non-REST event edit (EventsController::edit POST/PUT) mass-assigns Event.sharing_group_id from the submitted form via CakePHP fieldList and Event->save(), without checking that the current user may use that sharing group. The GET form only lists authorized groups (fetchAllAuthorised), but a tampered request can set distribution=4 and an arbitrary sharing_group_id. REST edit is not this bug: it calls Event::_edit(), which requires SharingGroup::checkIfAuthorised (and add() had an equivalent sgs[] membership throw since 2015). Successful assignment attaches the event to an undisclosed/unauthorized sharing group, exposing the group name on listings and changing distribution metadata. The 2026 fix runs SharingGroup::checkIfCanBeUsed when the SG actually changes under distribution 4, and clears sharing_group_id when distribution is not sharing-group.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated POST /system/api/saveFile accepts an uploaded .html file (HAXCMSFile.save allowlist includes html) and stores it under the site files/ directory. Visiting that URL is handled by the Express sites middleware: a /files/ match is sendFile'd with Content-Type from mime.getType (.html => text/html) and no Content-Disposition, so the browser executes the stored script in the HAXcms origin. Helmet CSP is off. The script POSTs the open /system/api/refreshAccessToken route; the browser attaches the HttpOnly haxcms_refresh_token cookie, the JSON body returns a fresh admin JWT, and the script exfiltrates it for account takeover. causal_research.bug_semantics: When the psf/black GitHub Action is invoked with use_pyproject:true, action/main.py reads the checked-out pyproject.toml (typically PR code) and treats a matching project.dependencies / optional-dependencies / dependency-groups entry as the Black requirement. find_black_version_in_array() strips extras and environment markers, then BLACK_VERSION_RE captures everything after the name 'black' once a non-name character appears. That capture is concatenated into req='black[colorama]'+specifier and passed as a single pip install argument. A malicious pull request can set 'black @ https://attacker/malware.git' (or git+https). The capturing regex accepts '@ https://...' so pip installs attacker-controlled code in the action's venv, giving RCE and access to the workflow's secrets/permissions. The version workflow input is not the GHSA path: pull_request workflows use the base workflow file, while pyproject.toml comes from the untrusted checkout. The 26.3.0 fix allowlists only version operators, so direct URL references no longer match.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Use-after-free in SQLite aggregate-function callbacks. Aggregate handlers (via create_aggregate/create_aggregate_handler/define_aggregator) are wrapped in C AggregatorWrapper objects whose Ruby VALUE is stored as the SQLite user_data pointer passed to sqlite3_create_function; the only Ruby-side reference keeping those wrappers reachable is the '-aggregators' instance variable on the SQLite3::Database. On Database#close/#discard the C code set that ivar to Qnil (rb_iv_set(self, "-aggregators", Qnil)), dropping the sole live reference so the GC could reclaim the wrapper objects while SQLite still held raw pointers to them inside its registered function callbacks. If an open statement calling that aggregate is stepped after the close, the xStep/xFinal callbacks dereference the freed wrapper -> invalid memory read / segfault, reliably reproducible after a GC full-mark.
causal_research.evidence: Fix commit b24e1e6076528b7f95f99acf7a81c70d0004c726 (PR #711, v2.9.5) deletes both rb_iv_set(self, "-aggregators", Qnil) lines in ext/sqlite3/database.c (sqlite3_rb_close and sqlite3_rb_discard) so the ivar keeps the wrappers alive for the DB lifetime; adds test test_step_on_statement_whose_database_was_closed_does_not_use_freed_aggregator. git log -S on the vulnerable string returns exactly two commits: 06ee4ac645e916f0f8c8d25596c1361e044baf6b (original, 2017) and 20025b40accbf37ec4fa4d1ac594eb5bc3787f03 (2024 discard-path re-carry). Parent 0ea5ff3415cf67059512c52b957104d4f0d1f85e:ext/sqlite3/database.c shows rb_sqlite3_aggregator_destroy_all(ctx) at lines 16/84 and no '-aggregators' ivar -> vulnerable line absent at parent. BIC is ancestor of v2.1.0 (advisory range start) and v1.4.0..v2.9.6; fix b24e1e60 lands in v2.9.5/v2.9.6 (patched version).
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 06ee4ac645e916f0f8c8d25596c1361e044baf6b (2017-03-28, 'Aggregators backed by ruby arrays, no xDestroy callback') first wrote the vulnerable line: it replaced the C-level rb_sqlite3_aggregator_destroy_all(ctx) call in sqlite3_rb_close with rb_iv_set(self, "-aggregators", Qnil), which merely drops the Ruby reference instead of keeping the wrappers alive, leaving the raw C pointers dangling. candidate_hunks.annotation: The constructor decodes attacker-supplied public keys and the self-signature, then returns the bundle without checking that signature. A comment leaves verification to every caller, so the trust boundary fails open.
candidate_hunks.code:
@@ -0,0 +328,34 @@ selected from new openssl_encrypt/modules/key_bundle.py
+    @classmethod
+    def from_dict(cls, data: Dict) -> "PublicKeyBundle":
+        """
+        Create bundle from dictionary.
+
+        SECURITY: Does NOT verify signature. Call verify_signature() after creation.
+
+        Args:
+            data: Dictionary from to_dict()
+
+        Returns:
+            PublicKeyBundle (unverified)
+
+        Raises:
+            KeyError: If required fields missing
+            ValueError: If data format invalid
+        """
+        try:
+            bundle = cls(
+                name=data["name"],
+                email=data.get("email"),
+                fingerprint=data["fingerprint"],
+                created_at=data["created_at"],
+                encryption_public_key=base64.b64decode(data["encryption_public_key"]),
+                signing_public_key=base64.b64decode(data["signing_public_key"]),
+                encryption_algorithm=data["encryption_algorithm"],
+                signing_algorithm=data["signing_algorithm"],
+                self_signature=base64.b64decode(data["self_signature"]),
+            )
+            return bundle
+        except KeyError as e:
+            raise ValueError(f"Missing required field in bundle data: {e}")
+        except Exception as e:
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid bundle data format: {e}")

candidate_hunks.annotation: to_identity() accepts that unverified bundle and copies its public keys into a usable recipient Identity. Encryption can therefore target a key chosen by the attacker before authenticity is established.
candidate_hunks.code:

+    def to_identity(self) -> "Identity":
+        """

causal_research.bug_semantics: On Unix recursive copy (-R/-r/-a) without --copy-contents, uu_cp treats character and block device nodes as stream sources. is_stream(metadata) is true for fifo||char||block. copy_helper recreates sockets and FIFOs in that mode but, before the fix, had no mknod path for devices, so copy_on_write called copy_stream: open the device, splice/read its bytes, and write them into a newly created regular file. That destroys device identity (a copied /dev/null is an empty regular file; major/minor are lost) and can hang or fill the disk when the source is an unbounded node such as /dev/zero. GNU cp instead mknods the destination unless --copy-contents is set. Non-recursive cp of a device as a file remains intended GNU behavior.

Mechanism (issue #9746 / Zellic 3.53 at 3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242): on recursive copy (-R/-a) without --copy-contents, uu_cp classifies char/block devices as streams (is_stream) and copy_helper falls through to copy_on_write/copy_stream, reading device bytes into a new regular file instead of mknod. GNU cp recreates the node unless --copy-contents.

Pre-fix copy_helper (parent 0f2821e75f7d6b28cd5b6225ff129ac859bee378 of the fix) preserved sockets/FIFOs under recursive && !copy_contents but had no char/block intercept, so is_stream routed devices into stream copy. Direct fix e6a3bb596f149628ba973eec3d099f3bb69f2464 (PR #11163) adds copy_node() via nix mknod for is_char_device/is_block_device when recursive && !copy_contents, matching GNU --copy-contents semantics.

code_evidence.summary: A Copilot-assisted TypeScript loader read file references without checking where they resolved. A malicious prompt could use an absolute path or traversal to read files available to the host process.
code_evidence.mechanism: The file-reference branch joined attacker-controlled text to the prompt directory and passed the resulting path straight to a synchronous file read.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: The new TypeScript runtime added file-reference expansion with no authorized-root check.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The fix enforces canonical allowed roots and rechecks the real target to stop both traversal and symlink escape.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The new loader chooses the prompt directory as a base but defines no allowed-root policy.
A file reference is resolved and immediately read, so absolute paths and traversal can escape the prompt directory.

fix_hunks.annotation: The fix imports canonical-path and relative-path primitives and adds an explicit option for trusted extra roots.
Loading now accepts the root policy and carries it into agent construction.
Agent construction receives the root policy together with the prompt path.
Agent construction passes the same root policy into reference preprocessing.
The prompt directory and any explicitly trusted roots are canonicalized before reference expansion.
The file protocol now uses the guarded resolver instead of reading the directly resolved path.
The resolver rejects lexical escape, verifies existence, canonicalizes the target, and checks again to block symlink escape.

mechanism: The TypeScript loader resolved file references relative to a prompt and read the result without proving that the target remained inside an authorized directory.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST /members/api/send-magic-link with emailType=signin looked up the email in the members store. causal_research.bug_semantics: django/db/models/sql/compiler.py order_by() compiler treated ANY field name containing a period as if it came from .extra(order_by=...) and passed 'table.column' through verbatim as RawSQL (col unquoted) - with no check that the field was actually in self.query.extra_order_by. FilteredRelation (django/db/models/query_utils.py) lets the caller choose the join alias via the annotate() keyword, and Query.table_alias() uses that user string as the literal table alias (alias = filtered_relation.alias if filtered_relation is not None else table_name). A crafted annotate alias containing a period therefore flows into ORDER BY and is re-parsed as a raw table.column pair, injecting SQL. Only FilteredRelation is exploitable in practice because other expressions are optimized to ordinal ORDER BY positions.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Administrator WEB_FETCH_FILTER_LIST is applied to server-side web fetches (RAG URL ingestion, URL-to-markdown, web-search content fetch). The shared helper is_string_allowed treated allow/block entries as raw string suffixes via str.endswith. validate_url passed the entire URL, so a blocklisted host with any path (https://blocked.example/x) never ended with the host and was fetched; an allowlist entry company.com rejected https://api.company.com/status and accepted https://attacker.example/path/company.com. get_filtered_results passed hostnames/IPs into the same helper, so corp.com matched evilcorp.com and 10.0.0.1 matched 110.0.0.1. An authenticated user who can trigger a fetch therefore reached publicly resolvable hosts the admin intended to block. Loopback/RFC1918/link-local/metadata remain covered by the separate is_global/ENABLE_RAG_LOCAL_WEB_FETCH guard.

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiteLLM proxy authenticates /key/block and /key/unblock with user_api_key_auth, then RouteChecks allows LitellmUserRoles.INTERNAL_USER onto any path in LiteLLMRoutes.internal_user_routes. After 220c9b22 / squash 4e81b2cab, that list includes key_management_routes, whose members KeyManagementRoutes.KEY_BLOCK ('/key/block') and KEY_UNBLOCK ('/key/unblock') are str enums, so check_route_access('/key/block', internal_user_routes) is true. The handlers then hash the caller-supplied target key and UPDATE litellm_verificationtoken.blocked with no check that the caller is proxy/team/org admin or owns the target. An INTERNAL_USER can therefore disable a proxy_admin key (DoS) or re-enable a blocked key. The same fix PR also found /key/update max_budget was not admin-gated; the published gist and CVE text target the block/unblock Admin Key Handler path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: concurrent POST /users (authData login) with a valid third-party provider token plus one MFA TOTP recovery code (or an SMS OTP). Counterevidence: username/password login was already array-locked by GHSA-2299 (UsersRouter.js); TOTP time-window codes are not single-use arrays and are out of this race.

mechanism.summary: An attacker who already holds a valid first-factor provider credential plus one MFA recovery code or the active SMS OTP sends N concurrent authData logins; every request validates the token against the same stored authData snapshot and the single UPDATE that consumes it carries no optimistic lock, so all N requests pass and each creates its own session - one single-use token yields N valid sessions.
mechanism.trigger: POST /users (authData login / logInWith) with body authData: { <provider>: { id, token }, mfa: { token: <recovery code or SMS OTP> } }, issued in parallel (the spec uses 10 concurrent requests) before any write lands; MFA must be enabled for the account (TOTP with recovery codes, or SMS).

causal_research.bug_semantics: On the default comm path (neither --check-order nor --nocheck-order), should_check_order calls are_files_identical(FILE1, FILE2) after open_file already opened both inputs. are_files_identical stats both paths, and if st_size matches it File::open + reads 8KiB chunks to EOF with no S_ISREG check. FIFOs/process-substitution pipes typically report size 0, so both streams are drained before LineReader consumes them, yielding silent truncated/wrong columns and false 'not in sorted order' errors (issue #9537). When both sizes are 0 and a path is an infinite char device (/dev/zero), the read loop never hits EOF and comm hangs. --check-order/--nocheck-order skip the helper; GNU comm does not pre-read pipe contents this way.

mechanism.counterevidence: The parent commit dca0ec0e65bfc09b6c9de6b1f9bbabbb0d1066f4 was fetched directly and contains zero occurrences of are_files_identical or paths_refer_to_same_file, with each input opened once in open_file, so the drain is genuinely new in the child. paths_refer_to_same_file at HEAD is metadata-only (FileInformation comparison, no reads), so are_files_identical is the only draining path. The guard added in January 2026 survived the August 2026 refactor into uucore, so HEAD is not silently re-broken, and the plain non-empty-regular-file pair is excluded by the size comparison.
mechanism.impact: Silent data loss: the pre-read consumes the first chunk(s) of each non-regular input, so the printed columns and --total counts miss or misplace lines (integrity, I:L); a non-regular stream without EOF hangs the pre-read (availability, A:L).
mechanism.preconditions: Both operands are non-regular files with equal metadata length (a FIFO's st_size is 0), neither --check-order nor --nocheck-order changes the path taken, and the size-equality early return at metadata.len() must not fire first; the hang additionally needs equal-size operands such as two FIFOs or two /dev/zero paths.
mechanism.summary: comm pre-classifies its two input paths inside the should_check_order computation with paths_refer_to_same_file(...) || are_files_identical(...); are_files_identical opens each path and reads it in 8192-byte chunks until the contents differ or EOF. For a FIFO or pipe argument those reads drain the stream before comm's own comparison loop re-reads it, so output silently misses the consumed prefix, and a non-regular stream that never reaches EOF blocks the pre-read forever.
mechanism.trigger: comm is invoked with two path arguments that resolve to non-regular files (FIFOs, /proc/<pid>/fd pipe descriptors, process substitutions such as comm <(cat a) <(cat b)) whose st_size values compare equal, which is the normal case because FIFOs report 0, and --nocheck-order is not passed.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: src/uu/comm/src/comm.rs:118-153 pub fn are_files_identical, called from comm() at :181-182 (b50a012d1302afb40dd49d1d5796d5fd74754d04); identical unguarded function/call at src/uu/comm/src/comm.rs:119/:182 in the audited snapshot 3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242; guarded copy now at src/uucore/src/lib/features/fs.rs:660 (HEAD 94d87a0da70443bb73d33b7de19e24db58240d43).

display_hunks.annotation: The auto-load path arrived with a sandbox-root guard and nothing else: the loader's options hold a byte limit and a sandbox root, so there was no workspace-only decision to make on this path.

The fix gives the loader a workspace-only flag, rejects any resolved path outside the allowed root before the file is read, and passes the flag from the auto-load caller, so the setting now reaches prompt and history images.
The flag is derived from the effective agent configuration, which is how a per-agent workspace-only setting reaches the image auto-load path the same way it already reached the file tools.

steps.detail: The vision feature added the auto-load path that scans a prompt and earlier turns for image references, loads the files and attaches them to the request; its only sandbox guard compared paths to a sandbox root, and the workspace-only setting that the file tools later gained was never consulted here.

steps.detail: The loader now takes the workspace-only flag from the effective agent configuration, rejects any resolved path that falls outside the allowed root, and skips the image; the new tests exercise a prompt reference and a history reference against a sandbox that mounts a directory outside the workspace.

code_evidence.summary: OpenClaw's native prompt image auto-load read images named in a message or kept from earlier turns and attached them to the model's context, but the loader resolved paths through the sandbox mount table without consulting the workspace-only setting, so an image mounted outside the workspace could still reach the vision model.

causal_research.bug_semantics: POST /api/v1/images/edit was a FastAPI route whose only authorization was Depends(get_verified_user). A verified non-admin could POST an image+prompt and the server would call the administrator-configured image-edit engine (OpenAI-compatible with IMAGES_EDIT_OPENAI_API_KEY, Gemini, or ComfyUI) and return edited images. After ENABLE_IMAGE_EDIT existed, chat middleware and the builtin edit_image tool both refused when the global switch was off or features.image_generation was denied; /generations had a matching generate_images() wrapper. The direct /edit route never received those checks, so a non-admin could bypass the global image-edit switch, bypass a denied image-generation permission, and spend admin provider credits. No cross-user data or credential disclosure.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The ungated /edit route and image_edits() implementation were first written in 72f8539fd2e679fec0762945f22f4b8a6920afa0 ('feat: image edit support') by Timothy Jaeryang Baek. The parent 8d34fcb586eeee1fac6da2f991518b8a68b00b72 has neither the route nor image_edits(). Subsequent commits added ENABLE_IMAGE_EDIT (557170c, first in v0.6.37) and generations permission wrapping (4b4743b, first in v0.7.0) without touching /edit, so the original handler remained the defective code until e038bab.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A documented AGUI FastAPI server exposes unauthenticated POST /agui that runs the configured agent. AGUI._attach_routes hardcodes Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Access-Control-Allow-Methods, and Access-Control-Allow-Headers: * on the SSE StreamingResponse and attaches no auth dependency. Starlette/FastAPI parse the body as JSON without requiring Content-Type: application/json, so a cross-origin browser POST with Content-Type: text/plain is a CORS simple request (no preflight), executes the agent with its tools, and is readable by attacker JavaScript because of ACAO *. Preconditions: victim has an AGUI server reachable from their browser (the class docstring shows localhost:8000) and visits an attacker page. Impact is silent agent/tool execution plus exfiltration of streamed tool results and environment data.

mechanism.summary: A page the victim visits (or any client that can reach the port) POSTs an AG-UI RunAgentInput to /agui; the route has no authentication and the response hardcodes Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so the browser lets the attacker read the streamed agent output, including tool-call results. causal_research.bug_semantics: SAML POST login decodes the attacker-controlled SAMLResponse XML and authenticates from the first samlp:Response / saml:Assertion's NameID and AttributeStatement. Signature verification used xml-crypto SignedXml.checkSignature on a Signature element found under that Response or Assertion (originally: the first Signature anywhere in the document) but never required the signature Reference URI to equal the processed element's ID, nor that the Response be the document root. An unauthenticated attacker who possesses any valid signature produced by the configured IdP certificate can wrap that signed node beside a forged Response/Assertion; checkSignature succeeds on the trusted signature while the parser consumes the unsigned identity attributes and logs the attacker in as an arbitrary user (CWE-287 XML signature wrapping).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Reflected XSS (CWE-79) via missing JSON parse error handling. The Express server mounts app.use(express.json({limit:3mb})) with no subsequent error handler for body-parser SyntaxError. On malformed JSON, express.json() throws a SyntaxError whose message embeds the raw user-supplied body; with no custom handler, Express's default error response reflects that input, so an attacker sending an HTML/JS payload as an unparseable JSON body gets it reflected back in the error response (XSS if Content-Type is not strictly enforced). Affects LibreChat up to v0.8.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When [auth] ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION is true, Gogs treats a client-supplied HTTP header (default X-WEBAUTH-USER; originally X-WEBAUTH-UID) as already-authenticated identity. authenticatedUser (historically SignedInId/SignedInUser) does ctx.Req.Header.Get(conf.Auth.ReverseProxyAuthenticationHeader), looks up or auto-creates that user, and returns it as the session principal. There is no check that req.RemoteAddr is a configured reverse proxy, so any remote client who can reach the Gogs port can forge the header and impersonate any account (including admins) or, if ENABLE_REVERSE_PROXY_AUTO_REGISTRATION is also on, create an activated account. Source: untrusted request header. Sink: authenticated user object used for all subsequent authorization. CWE-290. Closed by honoring the header only when the immediate remote IP is in [auth] TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS (default 127.0.0.0/8,::1/128).

causal_research.bug_semantics: datamodel-code-generator honors JSON Schema vendor extension x-python-type. From 0.51.0, JsonSchemaParser._get_python_type_override copies that string into DataType.type whenever it is judged incompatible with the schema type. DataType.type_hint then emits the string unescaped into generated field annotations. With default from __future__ import annotations, a value such as `X[1]; <python-stmt>` is a valid class-body line: the X[1] annotation is postponed, and the statement after the semicolon executes when the generated module is imported. No extra CLI flags are required. The only pre-fix transform (dotted prefix before the first '[') does not fire for this payload. The 0.60.2 fix rejects non-annotation ASTs via is_python_type_annotation before any DataType is built.

causal_research.bug_semantics: OS command injection (CWE-77) in the quick_capture MCP tool of the A-G-U-P-T-A wireshark-mcp server. pyshark_mcp.py builds a tshark command by f-string interpolation of the user-supplied MCP arguments and executes it through a shell: `cmd = f"tshark -i \"{interface}\" -c {packet_limit} -a duration:{duration} -T fields -e frame.number -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e _ws.col.Protocol"` followed by `subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, ...)`. interface is only wrapped in double quotes (breakout via embedded `"` or `$(...)`/backticks, which expand even inside double quotes), and packet_limit/duration are interpolated with no quoting at all, so a malicious MCP client (or any prompt-influenced tool call) can achieve arbitrary OS command execution on the host running the MCP server. NVD rates CVE-2026-7785 CVSS 7.3 HIGH, CWE-77, published 2026-05-05 (GHSA-v798-39xf-8fg2, severity medium, same advisory), listing repo snapshots edaf604416fbc94a201b4043092d4a1b09a12275 and 400c3da70074f22f3cce7ccb65304cafc7089c89 as affected; rolling release, no version numbers.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Remote code execution via eval on JSON-RPC command-string parameters (CWE-95, critical): the openc3-api JSON-RPC layer accepts the string form of API calls such as cmd(); attacker-controlled parameter text (e.g. an array literal) is parsed with String#convert_to_value, whose array branch executes 'return_value = eval(self)' - arbitrary Ruby code execution as the api server user. Because the cmd code path parses the command string BEFORE calling authorize(), an unauthenticated attacker can trigger Ruby code execution even though the request ultimately fails authorization (401).

causal_research.bug_semantics: On Ghost Admin login, the server loaded the existing express-session identified by the incoming ghost-admin-api-session cookie and wrote the authenticated user_id onto that same session_id (2018 createSession; later createSessionForUser via getSession + assignUserToSession). It never called req.session.regenerate, so a session identifier planted by another same-domain vulnerability survived privilege assignment. After login the attacker who knew that cookie could use it as the victim's admin session (CWE-384). CSRF origin checks and httpOnly cookies raise the bar but do not rotate the id. The 6.54.1 fix regenerates the session on every createSessionForUser call so the pre-login cookie is invalidated.

mechanism.counterevidence: Searched for any login-path rotation: api/endpoints/session.js only calls `auth.session.createSession`; middleware.createSession only forwards to the service; express-session.js `getSession` returns `req.session` when present; `assignUserToSession` only mutates fields. No store-level rotation exists. Cookie scoping (`path` /ghost, SameSite lax/none, origin/referrer requirement at login) narrows but does not remove the defect, consistent with the advisory's AV:A/AC:H rating.
mechanism.impact: Session fixation: the attacker's copy of the fixated session id resolves to the victim's authenticated Ghost Admin session (advisory CVSS 3.1 AV:A/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L).
mechanism.preconditions: The session id must exist before login (attacker plants/learns a cookie for the admin scope `path=<subdir>/ghost`, httpOnly, secure when SSL; the advisory states this needed another vulnerability on the same domain), and the victim must then sign in while presenting it.
mechanism.summary: A pre-existing `ghost-admin-api-session` cookie is carried into the signin request and `createSessionForUser` assigns the authenticated `user_id` onto that same express-session object instead of regenerating it, so the session id known to the attacker remains valid and authenticated after the victim logs in. Impact: Ghost Admin account takeover via session fixation.
mechanism.trigger: Victim holds (or has been given) a `ghost-admin-api-session` session id before login and submits valid admin credentials to the signin endpoint (`POST /ghost/api/admin/session/`; 2018 equivalent `core/server/api/v2/session.js` add() -> `auth.session.createSession`).

The advisory is a real CWE-384: login bound the authenticated admin to the pre-existing express-session id. The smallest original writer is the 2018 named-human PR member that added createSession without regenerate; the parent tree lacks that file; the 2026 fix regenerates on login and is in v6.54.1 not v6.54.0. The advisory describes a real defect that I verified in the tree: Ghost Admin's login bound the authenticated user onto the request's existing express-session object without rotating the session id, so a pre-planted `ghost-admin-api-session` cookie stayed valid and authenticated after signin (CWE-384 session fixation). causal_research.bug_semantics: STARTTLS stripping via predictable-tag OK injection (CWE-392/841/636, CVSS 4.0 HIGH): Net::IMAP#starttls returns 'success' without establishing TLS when a MITM injects a tagged OK response before the client finishes sending the command. Root mechanism: Net::IMAP#send_command writes the command line to the socket BEFORE registering the caller's response handler (add_response_handler after put_line), and the receiver thread only invokes handlers while processing lines; get_tagged_response then returns the pre-stored tagged OK without the block ever running - so start_tls_session is never called and the connection stays plaintext. causal_research.bug_semantics: WebSocket upgrade header smuggling (CWE-444): daphne reconstructs a raw HTTP request from Twisted's parsed headers and re-injects it into autobahn for WebSocket handshake processing. causal_research.bug_semantics: CorrelationsController::overCorrelations() (site-admin ACL) initialized a CakePHP find $query with limit, page, and order=>'occurrence desc', then overwrote any of those keys from $this->params['named'] / $this->request->params['named']. Because order was in that key set, an authenticated site admin could pass a named order parameter (for example /correlations/overCorrelations/order:<expression>) and replace the server-side ORDER BY. OverCorrelatingValue::getOverCorrelations() forwarded the array unchanged to Model::find('all', $query), so the untrusted order string reached CakePHP's query compiler. That is query-order manipulation and, depending on DboSource order handling, unsafe ORDER BY construction. The 2026 fix stops copying order from the request and assigns 'occurrence desc' after the user-parameter loop.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Scriban's recursive-descent expression parser treats nested parentheses as ScriptNestedExpression nodes. ParseParenthesis consumes '(' and immediately calls ExpectAndParseExpression, which re-enters ParseExpression; each nesting level consumes native stack. Through 6.5.8, ParserOptions.ExpressionDepthLimit is a nullable int defaulting to null, and EnterExpression only logs when that option is set, so the PoC template {{ ((((...1...)))) }} with thousands of parens reaches an uncatchable StackOverflowException and kills the host process (CWE-674 DoS). 6.6.0 turns on a default of 250 at EnterExpression (`ExpressionDepthLimit ?? 250`) so the existing depth counter fires without an explicit caller setting.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-770 (CWE-1333 ReDoS): Rack::Multipart mime-head parsing. MULTIPART_CONTENT_DISPOSITION = /Content-Disposition:(.*)(?=#{EOL}(\S|\z))/ni (lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb) is unanchored to line start; on crafted input containing many 'content-disposition:' occurrences and/or long comment/folded regions, the engine re-runs the greedy (.*) scan with lookahead from each candidate position, giving super-linear (quadratic) runtime -> DoS. Empirically reproduced: 200k repetitions of the literal 'content-disposition:' caused the old regex to run >180s (killed), while the anchored fix form is linear.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When password auth is off (the first-run default), POST /api/onboarding/setup, /api/onboarding/probe, and /api/onboarding/oauth/start treated a request as local if ipaddress.ip_address(X-Forwarded-For leftmost hop or X-Real-IP or socket peer) was loopback or RFC1918. A remote client can send `X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1` (or any private address) with no trusted proxy in front; the gate then allows unauthenticated onboarding. causal_research.bug_semantics: GHSA-7pr5-w74r-jjj7 / CVE-2025-6050 (published 2025-06-17, CVSS v4 4.8 medium, CWE-79 Stored XSS): Mezzanine CMS admin XSS in displayable_links_js(). The view /admin/displayable_links.js serializes Displayable objects (blog posts/pages) into a JSON link-list consumed by TinyMCE. Since the 2015 TinyMCE-4 refactor it returns HttpResponse(json.dumps([...])) directly; json.dumps does not escape <, >, & (ensure_ascii only escapes non-ASCII), so a blog-post title containing e.g. '</script><script>...' survives raw into JS/HTML output. causal_research.bug_semantics: JWT algorithm confusion in LightRAG API: AuthHandler.validate_token calls jwt.decode(token, self.secret, algorithms=[self.algorithm]) without explicitly denying 'none'; per GHSA-8ffj-4hx4-9pgf an attacker can forge unsigned tokens with header {'alg':'none'} (payload sub/role/exp attacker-chosen, e.g. admin) that the vulnerable decode accepts, yielding unauthorized access to protected API endpoints. causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: a node.owner (or other principal who can write node.driver_info) sets IPMI fields such as ipmi_address or ipmi_username to values containing socat address metacharacters (comma, colon, quotes, etc.), then starts serial console. Vulnerable path: IPMIConsole._get_ipmi_cmd joins unquoted _get_ipmitool_args() into a single string, appends ' sol activate', and passes it to start_socat_console. Sink: start_socat_console builds argv ['socat', ..., 'EXEC:"%s",pty,stderr' % console_cmd] and Popen's that list (no shell). socat then lexes the EXEC address and execvp's the result, so a metacharacter in driver_info can inject extra socat options or split the EXEC payload. Preconditions: non-default [conductor]/enabled_console_interfaces includes ipmitool-socat (or, per OSSA, ipmitool-shellinabox). Impact: conductor-host option/command influence as the ironic-conductor user (CVSS 6.6 AV:N/AC:H/PR:H). Counterevidence: socat EXEC is execvp not /bin/sh, so classic shell metacharacters are not a shell; Afonne-CID LP#2148331#24 argues shellinabox is likewise execvp and was not patched. Errata 2 states the original shlex.quote did not reopen injection.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On refresh_token grant, handleRefreshTokenGrant loads the oauthRefreshToken row and treats reuse as a security event only when revoked is already set. Rotation then happens in createRefreshToken: an adapter.update keyed solely on id marks the parent revoked, after which a new refresh row is inserted. Two concurrent POSTs with the same parent both observe revoked=null, both succeed the id-only update (last-write-wins, no rowcount), and both mint a child token. The family-invalidation deleteMany path is never entered for that race. Because rotation also extends refreshTokenExpiresAt, a stolen refresh token can be forked into independent live families until some later revocation. RFC 9700 §4.14 wants reuse to kill the family; this implementation's check is not atomic with consume.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On a live RTP/WebRTC session the multiplexed RTP/ICE UDP socket is advertised in ICE candidates and accepts packets before DTLS and before STUN MESSAGE-INTEGRITY. UdpReceiver.EndReceiveFrom copies the datagram and invokes OnRTPPacketReceived with no local catch. The vulnerable handler admitted any non-empty packet, then read packet[1] (TURN Data Indication discriminator) and/or called STUNMessage.ParseSTUNMessage. A 1-byte packet throws IndexOutOfRangeException; a STUN message with XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS/XOR-PEER-ADDRESS/XOR-RELAYED-ADDRESS (or MappedAddress) of length 0-7 throws NullReferenceException/IndexOutOfRangeException/ArgumentOutOfRangeException in STUNXORAddressAttribute/STUNAddressAttribute because those constructors index attributeValue[1], AsSpan(2) and AsSpan(4) without a length check. The EndReceiveFrom catch-all converted that exception into Close(), tearing down the media session. One unauthenticated packet is therefore a remote DoS (availability only).

mechanism.impact: Arbitrary read, create/overwrite and delete of files outside the content root in the process running the GraphQL API (tinacms dev/build server or a deployment host) -- source, configuration and secret files can be read through the media API, and arbitrary files can be overwritten or destroyed. mechanism.preconditions: FilesystemBridge used as the file/media backend (default filesystem datasource), a symlink/junction already present under the content root (plantable through any write path into the root that preserves attacker-chosen names), and a request touching the linked path; on Windows a junction serves the same role. mechanism.summary: If a symlink (or Windows junction) exists under the content root, assertWithinBase() passes any path that is lexically inside the root while the operating system resolves the link target, so FilesystemBridge.get()/put()/delete()/glob() read, create/overwrite and delete files outside the intended content root (CWE-22 path traversal reached through CWE-59 link following).
mechanism.trigger: An actor able to leave a link inside the content root (e.g. a media upload or extraction with an attacker-chosen name) plants pivot -> /outside. A GraphQL media/file operation then addresses pivot/owned.md: assertWithinBase('pivot/owned.md', contentRoot) accepts it because resolved = <contentRoot>/pivot/owned.md starts with <contentRoot>/ + sep, and the following fs.readFile / fs.outputFile / fs.remove follows the link to /outside/owned.md.

Fixed in 2.1.16 by validating the href with DOMPurify.isValidAttribute('a','href',href) before rendering. Reported by HackerOne researcher michaelcheers (report 3455133).

causal_research.bug_semantics: The HAX CMS PHP backend sets the haxcms_refresh_token cookie (the long-lived token used to mint new access JWTs) with the Secure flag hard-coded to false (setcookie('haxcms_refresh_token', $GLOBALS['HAXCMS']->getRefreshToken($u), $_expires = 0, $_path = '/', $_domain = '', $_secure = false, $_httponly = true);). With Secure=false the cookie is eligible to be sent on plain-HTTP responses, so an on-path attacker (packet sniffing/MITM on unencrypted network paths) can capture the refresh token and obtain unlimited new access tokens, i.e. session hijacking (CWE-614/S CWE-613 class). The companion cookie-clearing calls (setcookie('haxcms_refresh_token', '', 1)) also omitted secure/httponly. The flaw was present in every release from 25.0.0 through 25.x and was fixed in 26.0.0 by flipping $_secure to true and adding secure/httponly to the clearing calls.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Rack::Multipart::Parser unbounded in-memory buffering (memory-exhaustion DoS): the parser loop appends all uploaded bytes to an in-memory buffer (@buf, later StringScanner @sbuf) while scanning for the multipart boundary (preamble) or a complete mime part header, with no size cap on the buffered data; a client that never sends a boundary/header terminator forces unbounded memory growth. Fixed in rack 2.2.19 / 3.1.17 / 3.2.2 by adding BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT (16KB) and MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (64KB) checks in parser.rb (actual limit the higher of these and the 1MB default buffer size).

causal_research.bug_semantics: UrlGenerator::doGenerate validates each path/host variable by concatenating the raw requirement into preg_match('#^'.$req.'$#'). For an ungrouped alternation such as _locale: en|fr|vi|de, PCRE binds ^ only to the first alternative and $ only to the last, so a middle alternative matches as an unanchored substring. An attacker-supplied value /evil.com therefore satisfies vi. Tokens rebuild the path as separator '/' plus that value plus the remainder (route /{_locale}/blog → //evil.com/blog). After rawurlencode, decodedChars maps %2F back to '/', leaving a protocol-relative URL. If that string is used as a Location or href, the browser navigates off-site (CWE-601). Preconditions: strictRequirements enabled (default), a custom ungrouped | requirement, and a generated URL that is followed. The 2026 wrap '#^(?:'.$req.')$#' makes anchors apply to the whole alternation and rejects the payload.

mechanism.summary: Twig path()/url() (UrlGenerator) validates a route parameter against its requirement with preg_match('#^'.$requirement.'$#'); because the requirement string is pasted between the anchors without a group, a requirement written as a bare alternation anchors only the first and last alternatives, so any value containing a middle alternative as a substring passes validation and is written into the generated URL. mechanism.trigger: A route whose parameter requirement is a top-level alternation (for example _locale: 'en|fr|vi|de', or the long locale lists Symfony itself ships) plus an attacker-influenced parameter value that contains one of the middle alternatives as a substring, e.g. '/evil.com' or '//evil.com' (both contain 'vi'), passed to UrlGenerator::generate() / Twig path() / url().

causal_research.bug_semantics: On Unix, mv first tries rename(2). When that returns EXDEV, uutils falls back to copy-and-delete. From 0.8.0 (and since the 2020 fallback) that copy creates a new inode with fs::copy / create_dir_all / symlink recreation and never chown/lchown to the source uid/gid, so the destination is owned by the caller. A privileged operator moving another user's file onto another filesystem therefore silently produces a root-owned copy, which can hide the file from the intended owner or expose it under root policy. GNU mv restores ownership after the copy. Non-root callers cannot chown arbitrarily; the security-relevant case is privileged mv.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The legacy oidcProvider and mcp plugins (mcp wraps oidcProvider and duplicates discovery metadata) shipped two insecure cryptographic defaults. Discovery builders unconditionally advertised JWS alg "none" in id_token_signing_alg_values_supported (and mcp resource_signing_alg_values_supported). That metadata is served from /.well-known/openid-configuration; a client that takes the advertised alg set as the negotiation allowlist can accept an unsigned ID token. Independently, authorize() received merged opts with allowPlainCodeChallengeMethod defaulting to true and, before the method allowlist, rewrote a missing code_challenge_method to "plain". The token endpoint then treated the verifier as the challenge. Discovery still listed only S256, so the runtime silently offered weaker PKCE than advertised; a leaked authorization URL (Referer, logs, history) yields the verifier and enables authorization-code interception. Both surfaces are closed in 1.6.11 by dropping "none" from the alg lists, defaulting allowPlainCodeChallengeMethod to false, and rejecting unpaired PKCE parameters.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A crafted tiled JPEG2000 reaches j2k_decode_entry via Image.open(...).load(). Inside the infinite tile loop, each tile adds per-component byte widths into total_component_width and never resets it. tile_bytes = tile_width * tile_height * total_component_width is then written into tile_info.data_size when larger, and state->buffer is realloc'd to that size. Later tiles are treated as if they had the summed component width of all earlier tiles, so the scratch buffer grows toward full-image decompressed size even when each tile is small, causing high RSS and OOM denial of service (CWE-789). Parent code sized the buffer from a per-tile `components` assignment, so it did not accumulate across tiles.
