Subsequent 2.x commits only moved or re-expressed the same unguarded mutators, then added more of them. The minimum fix is PR #511's ->authorize('edit_orders') gates, squashed as fcd0c59 which is v2.8.0; v2.7.3 still lacks them. Fix-side AI is also absent and is not used for the verdict.
Every mutation surface named by the advisory is confirmed in the pre-fix tree at fcd0c592^: order-detail actions behind mount read_orders only, shipment actions behind browse_orders only, product sub-forms whose store() had zero authorize calls, Settings/Team/Index with no mount() authorization, RolePermission writes gated on the read-only view_users, unchecked PaymentMethods/Currencies/Carriers actions, Customers/Create re-passing a Hidden _password, unlocked public Eloquent properties, and a raw barcode {!! !!} sink. causal_research.bug_semantics: Memory-exhaustion DoS in decode_unknown_field (buffa/src/encoding.rs): unknown fields are preserved by default (preserve_unknown_fields=true); a LengthDelimited unknown field triggers alloc::vec![0u8; len] with len taken directly from untrusted wire data, and StartGroup recurses via nested.push(decode_unknown_field(...)) bounded only by a depth budget, giving ~22x allocation amplification (64MiB input -> ~1.4GB heap) and DoS on decode.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Claude HUD renders a status line by wrapping untrusted strings in OSC 8 terminal hyperlinks. hyperlink(uri, text) emits ESC]8;;${uri}ESC\${text}ESC]8;;ESC\ with no control-character stripping or URI encoding. Sources are stdin cwd (file://${ctx.stdin.cwd}), git remote/branch (branchUrl = httpsBase/tree/${branch}), and path.join(cwd, porcelain paths) for file links. A cwd or remote/branch containing ESC+backslash (OSC ST) closes the hyperlink early so the remainder is interpreted as arbitrary ANSI in the user's terminal (SGR spoofing, forged prompts, OSC 52 clipboard writes). Clicking an unsanitized branchUrl can also issue HTTP to an attacker-controlled origin. The same raw constructor is the CHVULN-04 / CVE-2026-47090 mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Special element injection (SQL injection) in CopyFromExternalStageToSnowflakeOperator (apache-airflow-providers-snowflake < 6.4.0): the operator builds the COPY INTO statement with an f-string that splices user-supplied `table` and `stage` constructor arguments directly into the SQL text (e.g. `into = f"{self.schema}.{self.table}"` then `COPY INTO {into} FROM @{self.stage}/{self.prefix or ""}`), with no quoting, escaping, or validation of those identifiers. A workflow author (or any caller that receives untrusted input for these fields) can inject extra Snowflake statements/semicolons through `table` or `stage`, e.g. table="t; DROP TABLE x" or stage="s; <other DML>", which are then passed verbatim to SnowflakeHook.run() and executed, allowing arbitrary SQL to run with the connection's credentials.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Open email/password registration can create an unverified user row for a victim address with an attacker-chosen password. Magic-link /magic-link/verify and email-OTP /sign-in/email-otp both resolve an existing row by email, set emailVerified=true, and mint a session. Before the fix they did not delete the credential account or revoke prior sessions. If requireEmailVerification blocked password use while unverified, the victim's later passwordless proof is exactly what makes the planted password valid, leaving the attacker with durable password access alongside the victim.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The first public write of that verify-existing-unverified-on-passwordless-signin pattern is 4f166443e946f3da7a06df5c0a5f0deff5b0f7d9, which added if (!user.user.emailVerified) { updateUser({emailVerified:true}) } to email-OTP sign-in. Immediate parent 793c91e5fc86c9e07976398f0fa041d201fb2e5b already signed existing users in but did not flip emailVerified, so the planted password stayed unusable under requireEmailVerification. Magic-link independently gained the same flip in a71e9f2e3f9bd66cbf31b18b4776e4aaedca225c (first in v1.1.3, matching the vendor lower bound). Original magic-link e407c545 and original email-OTP 7015962e signed existing users in without marking them verified and are not this BIC.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GET /sql upgrades to WebSocket without applying operator WebSocket size limits. An unauthenticated client can stream tungstenite frames up to the library defaults (16 MiB per frame, 64 MiB reassembled) into the per-connection read buffer. Those bytes are paid before handle_socket delivers the text to Datastore::execute, which only then runs check_anon and (on POST, not WS) HTTP-route/arbitrary-query capability checks. Concurrent connections therefore pin memory far above SURREAL_WEBSOCKET_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (applied only on /rpc from 3f43e74) and can degrade or OOM /sql. POST /sql was body-capped from the original handler (1 MiB, later HTTP_MAX_SQL_BODY_SIZE).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Multiple denial-of-service vectors in Scriban expression evaluation (CWE-400). Vector 1: string * int in ScriptBinaryExpression.CalculateToString loops unboundedly (for (int i = 0; i < value; i++) builder.Append(leftText)) with no LimitToString/LoopLimit guard -> OOM for e.g. 'AAAA' * 500000000. Vector 2: ShiftLeft in CalculateLongWithInt / CalculateBigIntegerNoFit does (BigInteger)left << (int)right with no cap (MaxBigInteger exists but is only used for Power) -> multi-MB BigInteger allocation for 1 << 2000000000. Vector 3: range operators .. and ..< yield lazy iterators (RangeInclude/RangeExclude) that builtin functions (array.size -> .Count(), array.join -> StringBuilder append) fully enumerate, bypassing LoopLimit -> CPU/memory exhaustion for (0..1000000000) | array.size.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An application that enables Symfony webhook routing for the Twilio SMS notifier accepts Twilio status callbacks at a public POST endpoint. WebhookController passes the configured routing secret into TwilioRequestParser::parse(), which forwards it to doParse(). From first introduction, doParse() read MessageStatus, MessageSid and To from the form body and emitted SmsEvent objects without reading $secret or X-Twilio-Signature. Any unauthenticated client who knows the URL can POST forged delivered/failed/undelivered payloads and drive delivery metrics or downstream consumers. Sibling Mailgun and generic webhook parsers in the same feature already HMAC-checked; Twilio omitted that check. The 2026 fix verifies HMAC-SHA1 over the request URL plus sorted POST params with hash_equals when a secret is configured.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CBORDecoder keeps a persistent per-instance registry of values marked shareable (CBOR tag 28) in self.shareables, and resolves sharedref values (CBOR tag 29) by indexing into that list. Nothing ever clears the list: decode()/decode_from_bytes() (or setting .fp to a new stream) does not reset shared state, so values registered during one decode operation remain indexed and reachable. When the same decoder instance is reused across a trust boundary (e.g., an HTTP server reusing a decoder for untrusted input), an attacker-controlled message containing tag 29 (sharedref) with a small integer index can read arbitrary objects from a previously decoded, trusted message via self.shareables[value]. The fix wraps each top-level decode in a context manager (_decoding_context) that clears _shareables and resets _share_index when decode depth returns to zero.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In the FAB auth manager, per-DAG access_control is applied to the resource name produced by resource_name(dag_id, resource). Before the fix, that helper returned dag_id unchanged whenever dag_id was a reserved global resource name (RESOURCE_DETAILS_MAP keys "DAGs" and "DAG Runs"). A real DAG may use dag_id "DAGs" because KEY_REGEX r"^[\w.-]+$" allows it. Sync then created/granted can_read/can_edit (and related DAG-level actions) on the global "DAGs" resource instead of the per-DAG resource "DAG:DAGs". A lower-privileged user given access_control only on that one DAG therefore received read/edit on every DAG. The same helper lived in the airflow-core permissions copy.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked and rejected: (a) at the fix's parent 8d9727a9 the short-circuit is live in both copies and the override.py sync paths pass the raw dag_id to resource_name(), so the collision is reachable, not dead code; (b) the pre-scheme parent 89d4dd88 has no such collision - its global view menu is 'all_dags' (DAG_VMS = {'all_dags'}; has_all_dags_access checks can_dag_read/can_dag_edit on 'all_dags') and per-DAG permissions used the bare dag_id, so a DAG named 'DAGs' could not resolve to the global resource; (c) the sibling reserved name 'DAG Runs' cannot be a dag_id (it contains a space) and the 'DAG:'/'DAG Run:' prefixes contain a colon, so only the 'DAGs' token is exploitable; (d) upstream's own regression test asserts resource_name(RESOURCE_DAG, RESOURCE_DAG) == 'DAG:DAGs', confirming 'DAGs' is treated as a valid dag_id that must get its own resource.
mechanism.impact: Privilege escalation: a user granted read/edit on the single DAG named 'DAGs' receives can_read/can_edit on the global 'DAGs' resource, i.e. on every DAG in the deployment (advisory severity HIGH, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N, CWE-269).
mechanism.preconditions: FAB auth manager in use; a DAG whose dag_id is exactly 'DAGs' (representable: KEY_REGEX = ^[\w.-]+$ at airflow-core/src/airflow/utils/helpers.py:45 permits word characters, dot and dash, so 'DAGs' passes while the colon inside the 'DAG:' prefix cannot be a dag_id); a role holding per-DAG access_control on that DAG; permission sync executed (DAG parse or sync-perm).
mechanism.summary: A DAG whose dag_id equals the global all-DAGs resource name ('DAGs', which is a legal dag_id) is mapped by resource_name() to that global resource instead of its own 'DAG:DAGs' resource, so per-DAG access_control for that DAG is materialised as can_read/can_edit on the global 'DAGs' resource and its holders silently gain access to every DAG (CWE-269 privilege escalation).
mechanism.trigger: A DAG with dag_id exactly 'DAGs' exists and its permissions are synced (airflow sync-perm, DAG parse/access sync through sync_perm_for_dag / _sync_dag_view_permissions / create_dag_specific_permissions), while a role is granted per-DAG access_control on that DAG; resource_name('DAGs', 'DAGs') then returns 'DAGs' (the global resource) rather than 'DAG:DAGs'.

The advisory is a real CWE-269 privilege-escalation in FAB resource_name(): a valid dag_id equal to the global "DAGs" resource is not prefixed, so access_control on that DAG is applied to every DAG. The first master commit that wrote the reserved-name no-op and used it when syncing DAG permissions is 7ab62100 by named human James Timmins in 2020, with no commit-object AI marker; its parent lacks the helper. Later resource_name() / FAB-copy commits are rewrites and moves of that logic. The minimum fix is PR #69106, landed as 447c20f and first released in providers-fab 3.7.2; the repairing member dc56f60 is AI-assisted, which is fix-side only. Therefore the case is a real vulnerability whose BIC is named-human with AI marker ABSENT: NOT_AI.
The described mechanism reproduces exactly at the fix's parent: resource_name() returns a dag_id unchanged when it is a reserved resource name, and 'DAGs' is both the global all-DAGs resource name and a legal dag_id, so a DAG named 'DAGs' has its per-DAG permissions written onto the global resource. The smallest original introducing change is 7ab62100af8a59694721e06b213a933869c6a1ed (2020-10-16, PR #11189), which created the 'DAG:' prefix scheme and the reserved-name short-circuit ('Dags' then, also a legal dag_id); its parent 89d4dd88026780daeef4dc024c16efa3e8b7b5ed has no prefix scheme, no RESOURCE_DAG constant and a distinct global view menu 'all_dags', so the collision is absent there. The minimum fix is 447c20fa2cf702ae3f76e5e7695187f8fa934f19 (2026-07-06, PR #69106), which deletes the reserved-name short-circuit in both copies of resource_name() and adds regression tests, and it is an ancestor of the providers-fab 3.7.2 tag that the advisory names as the upgrade target. The origin is therefore human and the verdict is NOT_AI, with the only residual surface being the deprecated back-compat helper resource_name_for_dag(), which still carries the old short-circuit but has no first-party production caller at HEAD.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Gitea associates uploaded files with releases by client-supplied attachment UUIDs. Web NewReleasePost/EditReleasePost pass form.Files into CreateRelease/UpdateRelease, which call AddReleaseAttachments. Before 1.25.4 that function resolved UUIDs with GetAttachmentsByUUIDs/getAttachmentByUUID and wrote attachment.ReleaseID without checking that the attachment's RepoID matched the release's repository (it only later denied UUIDs already bound to some release). An attacker who can upload in a private repository (uploadAttachment records that repo's ID and returns a UUID) and who can create or edit a release in a different public repository they control can submit the private UUID as a release file. After the ReleaseID update, the public release page lists the asset and ServeAttachment authorized downloads via LinkedRepository(ReleaseID), i.e. against the public repo's read permission, disclosing the private blob to unauthorized users. PR #36347 closes the source by requiring attachments[i].RepoID == rel.RepoID and hardens the sink so a mismatched repo URL cannot serve the file.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Rancher binds Project Owners to a per-project membership Role/ClusterRole on management.cattle.io/projects with verbs *. That wildcard includes the custom verb updatepsa. rancher-webhook authorizes namespace Pod Security Admission label changes by checking updatepsa on projects. A Cluster Member who owns a project can therefore set pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged on a project namespace and run privileged pods that disable container isolation (host access / breakout). causal_research.bug_semantics: Integer overflow in the FreeType text-sizing path. When each glyph's advance is an exceeding large value (font-controlled), Pillow accumulates the advances into a 32-bit int position/advanced while tracking the current draw position, causing an integer wraparound (CWE-190). Fixed by widening position/advanced from int to long.

causal_research.bug_semantics: HttpRequest.body (django/http/request.py) enforces settings.DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE solely by comparing the declared Content-Length header (int(self.META.get('CONTENT_LENGTH') or 0)) against the limit before reading the body into memory. On the ASGI path, chunked/missing-Content-Length requests carry no CONTENT_LENGTH, so the comparison evaluates to 0 and always passes; the handler then reads the entire request body into memory via self.read() with no bound on actual bytes consumed, letting a remote attacker load an unbounded request body into memory (DoS).

causal_research.bug_semantics: The Network-AI MCP SSE server (bin/mcp-server.ts, default port 3001) exposes POST /mcp JSON-RPC that parses the body and calls McpCombinedBridge.handleRPC, which dispatches tools/call into privileged orchestrator tools (config_set, agent_spawn, blackboard_write, token_*). From the server's introduction, _handleRequest set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and answered OPTIONS with 204, so a browser on a foreign Origin could both send the request and read the response. There was no Authorization check on POST /mcp or GET /sse. v5.1.3 added optional Bearer auth, but parseArgs defaulted secret to process.env['NETWORK_AI_MCP_SECRET'] ?? '' and McpSseServer stored options.secret ?? '', while _isAuthorized short-circuited to true when the secret was falsy — so a default-configured localhost server still required no credentials. A malicious page visited by an operator running that server can therefore invoke all exposed MCP tools. The GHSA PoC against v5.4.4 on 127.0.0.1:3001 showed OPTIONS /mcp ACAO=* and unauthenticated cross-origin POST /mcp config_set succeeding with HTTP 200.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Child processes spawned by Renovate's exec() incorrectly inherit the full parent environment: lib/util/exec/common.ts passes execa(cmd, opts) with env=childEnv but without extendEnv:false, so execa's default extendEnv:true merges the sanitized childEnv into the complete process.env, exposing all Renovate process environment variables (including secrets/credentials) to every spawned tool/child process.
evidence: Fresh full-history clone of renovatebot/renovate at .ai-slop/state/repos/renovate (blob:none filter, git checkout main). Advisory GHSA-8WC6-VGRQ-X6CF: child processes spawned by Renovate have full access to environment variables; introduced 42.68.1, fixed 42.96.3/43.4.4.

Fix: 9b59ffda 'fix(exec): don't extend env (#41024)' (2026-02-09, Michael Kriese) adds extendEnv:false to the execa call in lib/util/exec/common.ts; commit is a cherry-pick of a825cac81 (same PR #41024) and is the fix shipped in 42.96.3 (git merge-base --is-ancestor 9b59ffda 42.96.3 = yes; a825cac81 is on mainline and not an ancestor of 42.96.3).

Introducer: e773b3243 (2025-12-30, PR #40212, Jamie Tanna) migrated exec() from node:child_process spawn to execa. Pre-migration: spawn(cmd, {...opts, env: childEnv}) - node child_process with an explicit env option does NOT inherit process.env (env replaces). Post-migration: execa(cmd, {...opts, env: childEnv}) - execa defaults extendEnv:true, merging childEnv into process.env and thereby exposing the full parent env to child processes.

env: childEnv was passed both before and after (lib/util/exec/index.ts getRawExecOptions returns env: childEnv; childEnv built by getChildEnv -> getChildProcessEnv which sanitizes only when exposeAllEnv is unset). The leak is purely the execa extendEnv default semantic change.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/labels and GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/labels/{id} resolve the organization via orgAssignment(true) (name lookup only) and then org.ListLabels / org.GetLabel return every Label row for that org ID (id, name, description, color, url) without calling HasOrgVisible / HasOrgOrUserVisible. GET /api/v1/orgs/{org} already 404s for a private org the doer cannot see, so a non-member or anonymous caller who cannot read the org can still enumerate its labels. Mutations on the same routes require reqOrgOwnership() and were not writable by the unauthorized caller. The 1.26.3 fix attaches reqOrgVisible() to the labels group so invisible orgs 404 before the handlers run.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An Owner (database level or above) can DEFINE ACCESS ... TYPE JWT URL / TYPE RECORD ... WITH JWT URL pointing at a JWKS document. Before 3.2.0 the fetcher gated that URL with check_capabilities_url, which parsed the URL and matched only the hostname string (plus optional port) against --allow-net/--deny-net. The subsequent GET used a reqwest client with the default DNS resolver and, until #392, default redirects. An allow-listed hostname that resolved to loopback, link-local, cloud metadata, or RFC1918 therefore caused the server to issue a GET that a literal IP URL would have been denied. The response body is consumed only as JWKS (blind SSRF; liveness/parse timing only). CVE-2026-63736 / GHSA-5x4x-2946-qr67 is that hostname-vs-resolved-IP gap (CWE-918).

causal_research.bug_semantics: The public API role-assignment endpoints (POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign and /unassign) authorize role changes with a flag-level allowlist only: validateGlobalRoleUpdate() checks roleUpdate.admin (requires users.isAdmin) and roleUpdate.builder (requires users.isGlobalBuilder), and the GlobalRoleUpdate type only declares {builder?, admin?}. The per-app grant vectors appBuilder:{appId} and role:{appId,roleId} are destructured out of the request body and forwarded verbatim to sdk.publicApi.roles.assign/unAssign, where the SDK writes user.builder.apps += [prodWorkspace(appId)] and sets arbitrary data-plane roles (e.g. ADMIN) on the target app, with no check that the caller is a builder/admin of that target app. An app-scoped builder (user.builder.apps=[appA]) can therefore self-grant builder access or an arbitrary role in ANY other app in the tenant via the public API.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Prototype pollution via Object.assign() in mailbox store operations. src/proxy/mailbox/store.js _rebuildIndex() and _appendUpdate() merge attacker-controllable row.fields into existing message objects with Object.assign(existing, row.fields) / Object.assign(existing, fields). causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: a Unix environment entry whose name or value is not valid UTF-8 (advisory/issue repro: LD_PRELOAD=$'/tmp/lib.so\xff' printenv LD_PRELOAD). Vulnerable code: uu_printenv uumain in src/uu/printenv/src/printenv.rs (pre-fix) called std::env::var for named keys and std::env::vars for dump-all. env::var maps a present-but-non-UTF-8 value to Err(VarError::NotUnicode), which printenv treated like a missing variable (print nothing; later also exit 1). env::vars either panics on invalid unicode (Rust 1.85 docs) or omits the pair; it never yields the raw bytes. POSIX/GNU printenv emit the bytes, so inspection tools that wrap uutils printenv do not see adversarial loader paths (CWE-754 / CAPEC-176). Preconditions: local attacker/process can set a non-UTF-8 env value; impact is inspection bypass, not a memory-safety primitive.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the premise and the divergence: GNU /usr/bin/printenv emits the raw bytes for the same LD_PRELOAD value (2f 74 6d 70 2f 6c 69 62 2e 73 6f ff 0a, exit 0), so the uutils behaviour is a real deviation, not a POSIX-conformant choice; verified the audited revision still contains the UTF-8-only calls and that the file is byte-identical to the fix parent, so the audited state is genuinely unfixed; no later relocation weakens the analysis because the fix is present from 0.6.0 and at HEAD. One precision: the advisory says such entries are silently skipped, which matches the by-name path exactly (no output, no diagnostic, exit 1), while the listing path actually panics with exit code 101; both variants still fail to print the raw bytes, so the disclosed defect is present as described.
mechanism.impact: printenv cannot display the affected entries: the listing path aborts with a panic before printing them, and the by-name path prints nothing and exits 1, so an inspection that relies on this utility misses evidence of environment tampering, including library-injection payloads (CWE-116, CWE-754; CVSS 3.1 AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N, moderate).
mechanism.preconditions: The attacker must be able to place a non-UTF-8 name or value into the environment of the process or session that will later be inspected, and the inspection must run uutils printenv against that same environment, for example in a container or account the attacker can influence.
mechanism.summary: printenv resolved the environment through UTF-8-only standard-library APIs: the listing path iterated std::env::vars(), which converts every name and value with into_string().unwrap() and therefore panics (exit 101) on the first non-UTF-8 entry instead of emitting it, and the by-name path used std::env::var(), which returns Err(NotUnicode) for a non-UTF-8 value, producing no output and exit code 1. In both paths the raw bytes of such an entry are unreachable through uutils printenv, so a variable such as an adversarial LD_PRELOAD evades inspection, whereas POSIX permits arbitrary bytes and GNU printenv prints them verbatim.
mechanism.trigger: A local attacker sets an environment variable whose name or value contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8, for example LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/lib.so followed by byte 0xff, in the environment of a process or session that an administrator or security-audit tool later inspects with uutils printenv, either listing all variables or naming the variable.

causal_research.reasoning:
The published CVE/GHSA describe a real printenv inspection bypass: UTF-8-only std env APIs hide non-UTF-8 values that GNU printenv prints. The smallest first writer of those APIs is Joseph Crail's 2015 single-file commit 930896ba; its immediate parent still used os::env/os::getenv (lossy display). The defect is closed by 0bfbbc00 (PR #9728) switching to vars_os/var_os, shipped in 0.6.0 and absent from 0.5.0. The BIC commit object is a named human with no AI trailer or bot identity, so the case is a real vulnerability that is not AI-introduced.
The advisory's mechanism reproduces at the audited revision 3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242: printenv reaches the environment only through UTF-8-only APIs, so an entry carrying invalid UTF-8 bytes is never printed verbatim, while GNU printenv prints the raw bytes. The defect originates in the utility's first implementation, commit 9653ed81a2bf (2013-08-02, message Add the first four utils); its parent d4e96b33 contains only LICENSE and README.md, so the vulnerable construction is absent in the parent and present in the child. The 2015 commit 930896ba is a behaviour-preserving port from os::env() and os::getenv() to std::env::vars() and std::env::var(), a later exposure of the same String-only defect rather than a new introduction. The minimum fix is 0bfbbc00c7895c0fb6ea94987b4aab99e3d7ee52 (PR #9728, 2025-12-22), which switches both paths to env::vars_os()/env::var_os() with byte-level output and adds the test test_non_utf8_value; it is contained in release 0.6.0 as the advisory states and survives at HEAD through 6a3b559fa6. The BIC commit object carries no AI marker: a named human author, a 2013 date, a plain message and hand-written 2013 Rust, with no AI trailers anywhere on the object, and the file's later history is human-authored as well. Verdict: NOT_AI, with the advisory's mechanism and the full causal chain established from primary evidence.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Adjacent surface only, outside the advisory's mechanism, whose paths are fixed: command-line variable names remain Vec<String> at HEAD, so a variable whose name is not valid UTF-8 can be listed as raw bytes but cannot be queried by naming it; no advisory-defined behaviour remains unfixed and no unpatched case applies.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TOCTOU race condition (CWE-362/367) in Rack::Session::Pool: session is loaded at request start (prepare_session) and unconditionally stored back at request end (commit_session -> write_session -> @pool.store). A concurrent long-running request holding a session cookie can re-store (restore) a session that a logout/deletion request removed from the pool, letting an attacker retain illicit access after logout. Also delete_session generates a new sid without storing the empty session, so deletion is not atomically reflected in the pool.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Recursive container scanning (deep scan, --depth>0) fails to enforce the recursive size budget as a hard limit on compressed/archive inputs: single-stream decompressors (gzip/bzip2/lzma/xz) fully materialize decompressed content before the remaining budget is validated, and the recursive_scan continues when the residual budget is already negative; zip/tar/rpm multi-entry archives are checked only against the original per-entry budget rather than a shared cumulative budget, allowing many individually small members to exceed the aggregate limit. Exploitable by a crafted archive to force excessive memory/CPU consumption (CWE-400/CWE-409, DoS).
causal_research.evidence: introducer b3336a946a7c5e41bb797bd09b798d6c4d9bc373 (author Roman Babenko, 2022-07-12, single parent, no squash, no co-author/trailer AI markers); parent app.py data_scan grep count 0; commit adds data_scan() recursive container scan with per-entry zip budget check and recursive_limit default 1<<30. Git log -S'data_scan' confirms b3336a9 is the first written occurrence; later commits (4b764f8 gzip, e571ec9 tar/bzip2, c8ddb62 lzma, 0bd8fe56 refactor to deep_scanner) extend/relocate but introduce no new vulnerability pattern. Fix 8b9b111cb65e42410b6454665e172bdfe7869a37 (v1.16.0, #855, DeepScan refactoring) adds negative-budget guard 'recursive_limit_size -= data_size; if MIN_DATA_LEN > recursive_limit_size: return' to recursive_scan and structure_scan, plus limited/bounded read for gzip (and bzip2/lzma): direct fix verified.
causal_research.flaw_origin: atomic introducer b3336a946a7c5e41bb797bd09b798d6c4d9bc373 'ZIP archives scanner' (2022-07-12) first wrote app.data_scan() recursive container-scan in credsweeper/app.py; parent 4d09255ecd7140f8c1a3498423dd90a8332683c6 has zero occurrences of data_scan (grep count 0). The advisory names subsequent refactor 0bd8fe56ad2e08b12d47677f7dbe1a75913969ae (~ 1.4.9) as introducer, which merely moved this pre-existing logic from app.py into the deep_scanner package (bzip2/gzip/lzma/tar/zip scanners) and did not add it. causal_research.bug_semantics: Gitea migration/mirror policy is supposed to constrain outbound HTTP via NewMigrationHTTPTransport, whose DialContext runs hostmatcher.NewDialContext("migration", allowList, blockList) so allow/block lists and local-network policy cannot be bypassed by a 302 to an internal or blocked host. Initial repository migration already passed that transport into lfs.NewClient for LFS object download. Recurring pull-mirror LFS sync (services/mirror/mirror_pull.go runSync, StoreMissingLfsObjectsInRepository) and push-mirror LFS upload (services/mirror/mirror_push.go runPushSync, pushAllLFSObjects) instead called lfs.NewClient(endpoint, nil). newHTTPClient treats nil as &http.Transport{Proxy: proxy.Proxy()} with no DialContext, so LFS batch/transfer requests use the default net/http redirect behavior and never re-check the migration host/IP lists. An allowed-looking LFS endpoint (or a later DNS/redirect change on a stored mirror URL) can therefore reach hosts that migration transport protections would have blocked. CWE-284. Fixed in 1.25.5 by passing migrations.NewMigrationHTTPTransport() into those two NewClient calls.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint of `vllm serve` accepted per-request `chat_template` (an arbitrary Jinja template string) and `chat_template_kwargs` (an arbitrary dict) on ChatCompletionRequest and passed them straight into `tokenizer.apply_chat_template`, which renders the conversation through Jinja2. An attacker who can reach the API can supply a malicious template (e.g. deeply nested/recursive loops, heavy string operations) or kwargs that make the template perform expensive work, exhausting CPU and/or memory and causing a service outage (resource-exhaustion DoS). The fix (PR #25794) filters request kwargs down to the variables actually declared by the template (via jinja2.meta.find_undeclared_variables on a sandboxed parse) and adds a `--trust-request-chat-template` gate that refuses requests carrying a chat template unless explicitly enabled.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An admin caller supplies uuid on GET /agent-flows/:uuid or DELETE /agent-flows/:uuid. loadFlow and deleteFlow build normalizePath(path.join(flowsDir, uuid + '.json')). Node path.join resolves ../ before normalizePath runs; normalizePath only strips leading ../ from the already-resolved absolute path, so the check never confines the result to storage/plugins/agent-flows. The process then readFileSync/rmSync any reachable .json (for example MCP server configs with API keys, or package.json), which is CWE-29 information disclosure and deletion DoS. saveFlow kept the safer normalize-then-join order and was not the Huntr sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service / disk exhaustion (CWE-400). The Evolver proxy HTTP server binds to 127.0.0.1 (reachable by any local process, container host-netns neighbor, or malicious postinstall script) and its parseBody() in src/proxy/server/http.js reads the entire POST body (req.on('data') -> chunks.push, Buffer.concat(chunks)) with NO size cap. causal_research.bug_semantics: Ghost SSRF-hardens outbound HTTP in ghost/core/core/server/lib/request-external.js: got beforeRequest/beforeRedirect run errorIfHostnameResolvesToPrivateIp, which dns-looks up options.url.hostname and rejects when isPrivateIp(result.address) is true (skipped in development and for the configured site host). After IP-format normalization, isPrivateIp only treats IPv4-mapped IPv6 as mapped when the raw string matches ^::ffff: (dotted or hex). An expanded IPv6 literal such as 0:0:0:0:0:ffff:127.0.0.1 misses that prefix, normalizeIPv6 compresses it to ::ffff:7f00:1, loopback/ULA/link-local checks fail, and the function returns false so the request is treated as public. Node then connects to the mapped address (http.get of http://[0:0:0:0:0:ffff:127.0.0.1]/ yields ECONNREFUSED ::ffff:7f00:1:80), which is loopback/RFC1918/link-local. Compressed ::ffff:127.0.0.1 and ::ffff:7f00:1 are already blocked on the pre-normalize path; the bypass is the expanded form that only becomes ::ffff:... after normalizeIPv6.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When a BigQuery source configures allowedDatasets, bigquery-execute-sql treats the dry-run job's referencedTables as the security boundary. Specialized SQL (INFORMATION_SCHEMA views, EXTERNAL_QUERY, and other constructs whose dry-run returns an empty table list) is classified as SELECT, so the code skips both the allowlist loop and the non-SELECT TableParser fallback. An authenticated caller can therefore read DDL/schema of excluded datasets and pull federated rows through EXTERNAL_QUERY despite an explicit dataset restriction.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-94 code injection with CWE-470 use of externally controlled input to select a class. AuthXMLUtils.createCustomCallback resolves the className attribute of an incoming XML CustomCallback element with Class.forName(className) and immediately instantiates it with newInstance(); the DSAMECallbackInterface constraint is applied only as a cast after construction, so an attacker-chosen class is loaded, its static initialiser runs and its no-arg constructor executes before any type check can reject it. On the PLL /authservice endpoint the XML is parsed from the unauthenticated request, so a default OpenAM deployment exposes arbitrary class instantiation to a remote client.
evidence: Step 0, cveawg: curl https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-62379 returns an 84-byte 404 body {"error":"CVE_RECORD_DNE","message":"The cve record for the cve id does not exist."}, so that endpoint carries no record for this case and every advisory fact below comes from the vendor page, which is the authoritative record for this case.

Vendor mechanism text, page.txt: 'the remote authentication endpoint (/authservice, PLL) accepts an XML element that names an arbitrary Java class, which the server then loads and instantiates without validation. On a default configuration this is reachable without authentication'; 'All releases up to and including 16.1.1 (the defect predates the Open Identity Platform fork)'; Remediation: 'The fix resolves the class named in a <CustomCallback> element without running its static initialisers and rejects it unless it implements DSAMECallbackInterface, and it constrains deserialisation of the serialised Subject value to a class allowlist'; interim mitigation: 'Enabling sunRemoteAuthSecurityEnabled does not mitigate this issue. The remote-auth security token is checked in AuthXMLHandler.processAuthXMLRequest, which runs only after AuthXMLRequest.parseXML has already parsed the request and instantiated the class named in the <CustomCallback className="..."> element.'

causal_research.flaw_origin: Pre-git SVN origin with a verified external boundary. The unchecked instantiation is already present in the oldest reachable snapshot of the file, 0dbc9205d8 (2010-09-18, 'Tag for 9.5.1 RC2'), a truncated git-svn import whose message records svn.forgerock.org/openam/tags/9.5.1_RC2@389, i.e. SVN revision 389 of the OpenSSO/ForgeRock tree; the same four lines sit in e9c6e1db42 (2011-03-03, tags/9.5.2_RTM@660) at lines 1421-1422. The master lineage has a single root, 2689a3a2ad (2012-07-06), and the move 8af80418ba adds the file at its maven path while its parent 0075453649 contains no amserver tree and no AuthXMLUtils.java at all, so no reachable git object writes the parameterless Class.forName(className) plus newInstance() pair. Both available eras are human-written code that predates AI code generation by more than a decade.
causal_research.flip_condition: The verdict flips to an AI verdict only if first-party evidence binds an assistant disclosure to a reachable change that carries the defect, which cannot exist for a pre-2010 SVN revision and is absent from every reachable carrier; it moves to EVIDENCE_GAP if a reachable post-2012 git change is shown to re-introduce or newly expose the uncontrolled instantiation (the pickaxe currently shows none); it becomes FALSE_POSITIVE only if the vendor withdraws, rejects or duplicates GHSA-wg5r-wc3x-39vc.
causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: an unauthenticated HTTP request to /authservice (PLL) whose XML body carries <CustomCallback className="..."> naming an arbitrary class. Vulnerable code: AuthXMLHandler.handlePLLRequest calls AuthXMLRequest.parseXML at 16.1.1 AuthXMLHandler.java:194, which reaches AuthXMLUtils.createCustomCallback (declared line 1587) and the two unchecked lines at AuthXMLUtils.java:1612-1613; the remote-auth security switch is only consulted later, at AuthXMLHandler.java:306 (securityEnabled = AuthUtils.getRemoteSecurityEnabled(), backed by the sunRemoteAuthSecurityEnabled attribute) inside processAuthXMLRequest, which is invoked at line 246, i.e. after parseXML has already parsed the request. Impact: attacker-selected class initialisation and construction on the server, i.e. remote code execution and full compromise per the vendor. Preconditions: default configuration, HTTP reach to /authservice. Counterevidence: none that weakens the report; the vendor page's own correction documents that enabling sunRemoteAuthSecurityEnabled is not a mitigation because of that ordering, and the later sibling hardening 0594405c5a (2026-08-04) for AuthXMLRequest.setPrincipal shows maintainers treat the pattern as a real defect class.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory is real and active, and the vendor fix is a genuine minimum repair: 16.1.1 openam-core AuthXMLUtils.java:1612-1613 instantiates an attacker-named class before the interface constraint can apply, and the PLL handler parses the XML before consulting the remote-auth security switch, so a default deployment is remotely exploitable without credentials; edcf968cad, shipped in 16.1.2, removes the exposure by loading without initialisation, enforcing assignability first and then instantiating, plus the grouped deserialisation hardening. On the AI question the decisive fact is the boundary, not a missing hunk: the identical construct is already present in the 2010-09-18 git-svn import (SVN tag 9.5.1_RC2 at revision 389) and in the 2011 tag import, master's history starts 2012-07-06 with a single root, and the 2012 move that brought the file into openam-core has a parent with no copy of the file at all, so no reachable git object writes the defect. That makes the carrying change an SVN revision from 2010 or earlier, which cannot be AI-authored, and every reachable carrier (the 2012 move by a ForgeRock maintainer, the fix by the OpenAM maintainer) is human-authored with an empty body and no disclosure marker, so the record lands NOT_AI under the non-git boundary rather than an open verdict; the residual uncertainty is only the SVN revision label, which cannot move the defect into the AI era.
causal_research.remaining_gap: The identity of the SVN revision that first wrote the parameterless Class.forName(className) plus newInstance() pair in createCustomCallback is still unknown: tag snapshot 9.5.1_RC2 (svn.forgerock.org revision 389, 2010-09-18) already contains it and master's git history starts 2012-07-06, so nothing between those bounds is available locally. Next smallest question: does the pre-2012 ForgeRock/OpenSSO SVN trunk history (the amserver/source path before the maven merge, or a 2008-2009 OpenSSO 8.x source drop) show this helper gaining the unchecked instantiation, and in which revision? The exact svn.forgerock.org path from which the file reached the 2012 move is also unverified, which would only re-label the boundary, not move it out of the pre-AI era.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TOCTOU (CWE-367) in node-host system.run approval: interpreter/runtime commands (python, node, bun, deno, etc.) were treated as approval-backed by binding the approval to cmdText (rawCommand or formatted argv) without binding the actual local script file operand; a benign script could be approved and rewritten before execution, executing different code as the runtime user.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-XF99-J42Q-5W5P (CVE-2026-32979): affected <=2026.3.8, fixed 2026.3.11; approval flow treated interpreter/runtime forms as approval-backed when it could not bind a single direct local script file. git show ae0b4c49: created src/node-host/runner.ts (new file; parent 49bd2d96 lacks it) with handleInvoke binding cmdText = rawCommand || formatCommand(argv) and requesting approval via requestExecApprovalViaSocket({request:{command: cmdText}}); no script-operand binding. Fix daaf211e 'fix(node-host): fail closed on unbound interpreter approvals' (2026-03-11, Peter Steinberger) adds requiresStableInterpreterApprovalBindingWithShellCommand and returns SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED when resolveMutableFileOperandIndex returns null for interpreter-like safe bins. Fix 7289c19f 'fix(security): bind system.run approvals to exact argv text' (2026-03-11, Peter Steinberger) makes rawCommand always formatExecCommand(hardening.argv) with display-only previewText. Both fixes in 2026.3.11 release line.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that this is not merely documented administrative behaviour: the project edit view and the project API both resolve to project.edit, and the pre-fix weblate/utils/requests.py had no domain or address validation at all; confirmed the 200-character reflection and the request-on-validation both exist in the fix parent; and confirmed the fix's own regression test (test_install_machinery_blocks_private_project_target) reproduces the same non-superuser path and expects a 400 with 'URL domain is not allowed.'
mechanism.impact: The Weblate server performs HTTP requests to attacker-chosen internal addresses (CWE-918) and returns up to 200 characters of the response body to the attacker through the configuration error message (CWE-200), disclosing internal service banners and error payloads.
mechanism.preconditions: Authenticated user with project.edit on a project; the per-project Administration role is the full PERMISSIONS set (weblate/auth/data.py:49 project.edit, :186-188 Administration), so no superuser is needed; project-scope machinery editing must be enabled and a service with a configurable URL must be available.
mechanism.summary: A project.edit user installs a machine-translation service whose URL points at an internal address; Weblate validates the configuration by issuing a server-side request to that URL, and the failed-response detail embeds up to 200 characters of the response body in the ValidationError shown back to that user, giving SSRF plus partial response read from a non-administrative account.
mechanism.trigger: On a project machinery page (or the project machinery-settings API endpoint), a user with project.edit submits a configuration whose url/endpoint points at a private or loopback address, for example http://127.0.0.1:11434/.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: weblate/machinery/views.py:347 EditMachineryProjectView.dispatch, weblate/machinery/forms.py:36-44 BaseMachineryForm.clean (validate_settings -> download_languages -> request), weblate/machinery/base.py:184-210 check_failure with detail[:200], all at fix parent 1fd47a5176618dfc8a9261ed3237621fd32f6e2a

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real published SSRF (CWE-918) with partial response read (CWE-200). The smallest introducing commit that first wrote project-level URL configuration plus validation-time HTTP is 1804a951, verified absent in its parent. The minimum closing change is e619e90 in 5.17, which rejects private project machinery targets and stops reflecting untrusted bodies. AI attribution is BIC-object only: 1804a951 is named-human Michal Čihař with no AI trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Fix-side Copilot review does not change that.
Project-scoped machinery configuration was introduced by 1804a951c8 (2022-02-03), which added Project.machinery_settings plus weblate/machinery/views.py so that any user holding project.edit can set machine-translation service URLs, and which routes those settings through BaseMachineryForm.clean() -> validate_settings(), so the server issues the HTTP request at configuration-validation time. The URL field used there (WeblateServiceURLField -> WeblateServiceURLValidator) explicitly permits local addresses such as http://domain:5000, and no host validation existed in weblate/utils/requests.py at the fix parent, so a project administrator could point the service at loopback or internal targets. The second mechanism the advisory names, the partial response read, comes from 0b9e51d545 (2025-01-10), which put response.text into the HTTPError detail that validate_settings() turns into the user-visible ValidationError, capped at 200 characters by 320c26aa16. The defect is closed at clone HEAD by e619e90902, which sets allow_private_targets=False for the project view and the project API, adds outbound public-address validation with the ALLOWED_MACHINERY_DOMAINS allowlist, and suppresses error details from untrusted hosts, with 097866f9c3 later closing IPv6-transition and special-use bypasses of that guard. Both causal commits, and both fix commits, are authored by the named upstream maintainer Michal Cihař with no AI trailers, bot identity or AI-attributed change anywhere in the chain, so the defect is not AI-caused.

causal_research.bug_semantics: RSC (React Server Component) requests append a cache-busting `_rsc` search param derived from a weak 32-bit djb2 hash truncated to 7 hex chars (hexHash, ~28 bits). Deployments that rely on shared/CDN caches that ignore the Vary header partition responses only by URL; collisions in the `_rsc` value let different RSC request variants (prefetch/segment-prefetch/state-tree/next-url header combinations) share one cache entry, enabling cache poisoning across requests (users receive the wrong response variant for a given URL).

causal_research.bug_semantics: AddView (/add/) accepted an unvalidated form JSON field named config, merged it into crawl.config, then configset applied crawl.config at high priority and hooks.py exported remaining keys as subprocess environment variables. Archive plugins such as yt-dlp read YTDLP_ARGS_EXTRA from the environment and append it to the tool argv, so an attacker could inject yt-dlp --exec (or gallery-dl --exec / *_BINARY overrides) and get RCE. When PUBLIC_ADD_VIEW=True the endpoint is reachable without authentication and is csrf_exempt for anonymous POSTs.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A crafted npm tarball can put a Windows path-traversal name such as package/foo\..\..\.npmrc in a regular-file header. parseTarball strips the first path segment and, before the fix, normalized the remainder only when the string contained './'. Because '../' contains './' as a substring, POSIX '..' segments were collapsed with path.posix.join; a backslash spelling does not contain './', so the raw name became a filesIndex key. importIndexedDir then computed dest = path.join(packageDir, key). On Windows that join treats '\' as a separator and writes outside the package directory (for example overwriting .npmrc). Unix keeps backslash as a filename character, matching the Windows-only advisory.

An authenticated user who can create or edit template element attributes POSTs TemplateElementAttribute type and category through TemplateElementsController add/edit. causal_research.bug_semantics: A DAG using GCSToSFTPOperator or GCSTimeSpanFileTransformOperator lists objects from a GCS bucket and joins each returned object name onto a configured destination (SFTP destination_path, or a worker TemporaryDirectory) without normalising the result or requiring it to stay inside that base. GCS object names are attacker-controlled whenever a less-trusted principal can write the source bucket. A name with '..' segments or an absolute prefix is passed to SFTPHook.store_file or blob.download_to_filename, so the DAG run can overwrite files outside the intended directory on the SFTP host or the worker. Preconditions: the DAG points the operator at such a bucket; the writer need not be the DAG author.

mechanism.summary: Two listing-derived joins write attacker-named paths outside their base: GCSToSFTPOperator._resolve_destination_path joins a GCS object name (from GCSHook.list) onto destination_path and hands the result to SFTPHook.store_file, so a name with '..' segments or an absolute prefix lands outside the configured SFTP destination; GCSTimeSpanFileTransformOperator._download joins a blob name (from GCSHook.list_by_timespan) onto the worker temp dir, so the same name writes outside that temp dir on the worker host.
mechanism.trigger: A DAG runs GCSToSFTPOperator (wildcard listing or a plain source_object) or GCSTimeSpanFileTransformOperator against a source bucket whose write side is a different, less-trusted principal; that principal uploads an object whose name contains '..' segments (or an absolute path), and the operator resolves the joined path and copies the blob there.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated chat completion reaches async process_chat_payload, which always runs extract_skill_ids_from_messages (and, from v0.9.6, the overlapping strip_skill_mentions) on message text. SKILL_MENTION_RE r'<\$([^|>]+)\|?[^>]*>' lets [^|>]+ and [^>]* both consume the same run because | is optional, so a payload '<$' plus a long string with no '>' forces O(n^2) backtracking inside CPython re on the asyncio event loop. Default UVICORN_WORKERS=1, so one such message pins the worker and denies service to the whole instance. Skill injection's if all_skill_ids: guard does not wrap the regex. The original strip_re r'<\$[^>]+>' was linear; v0.9.6's keep-label strip_re reused the overlapping quantifiers and made small inputs enough to hang.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that guards really are absent: at v0.9.6 the extract call at :2625 precedes the `if all_skill_ids:` block and the strip call at :2662 stands alone; both are direct synchronous calls in the async coroutine, with no length cap or feature gate in between. Checked that the pre-0.9.6 strip pattern `<\$[^>]+>` (v0.9.5:2241) is linear (0.0-0.1 ms at 32-64k), so the O(n^2) is created by the ambiguous quantifier rather than by input size alone. Checked that the patched patterns are linear and preserve captures and substitution on `<$id|label>` and bare `<$id>`, and that no copy of either vulnerable pattern survives at v0.10.0 or HEAD (git grep over *.py).
mechanism.impact: Whole-instance denial of service: the worker's event loop is blocked inside the `re` module for seconds to minutes per request, so every other user's chat and API call on that worker stalls; the default deployment runs UVICORN_WORKERS=1 (backend/start.sh:95), so the entire instance is affected (advisory CVSS availability A:H). The thread cannot be interrupted from Python, so recovery requires killing the worker.
mechanism.preconditions: An authenticated account able to send chat completions (advisory PR:L; no admin or skill configuration required) and one piece of text of the hostile shape reaching form_data['messages'] on the default single-worker deployment; a multi-worker deployment still loses the handling worker.
mechanism.summary: A ReDoS in two skill-mention regexes: `<\$([^|>]+)\|?[^>]*>` (SKILL_MENTION_RE, extract path, present since v0.9.2) and `<\$[^|>]+\|?([^>]*)>` (strip_re, strip path, present since v0.9.6) each force the engine to retry every split point between an ambiguous quantifier pair, so input of `<$` plus a long run with no `>` costs O(n^2) CPU inside the C regex engine. Both run synchronously on the asyncio event loop for every chat completion and need no skill or setting, so one message from any authenticated user pins the single default uvicorn worker and freezes the instance for all users.
mechanism.trigger: Any authenticated user POSTs a chat message whose text contains `<$` followed by tens of KB (extract path, v0.9.2+) or ~50k+ characters (strip path, v0.9.6+) with no closing `>`; the same blob can arrive benignly in message history from a RAG chunk or tool output, in which case the trigger is accidental. Only the chat-completion pipeline needs to be reached: process_chat_payload calls extract_skill_ids_from_messages(form_data['messages']) at middleware.py:2625 (v0.9.6) before the `if all_skill_ids:` guard, and strip_skill_mentions(form_data['messages']) at :2662 with no guard at all.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: backend/open_webui/utils/middleware.py - SKILL_MENTION_RE = re.compile(r'<\$([^|>]+)\|?[^>]*>') at v0.9.6:2223 (v0.9.2:2192), used by extract_skill_ids_from_messages() via SKILL_MENTION_RE.finditer; strip_re = re.compile(r'<\$[^|>]+\|?([^>]*)>') at v0.9.6:2247 (introduced by 01810e32a), used by strip_skill_mentions() via strip_re.search/sub. Both are plain synchronous calls from the async process_chat_payload coroutine.

The smallest first writer of that server-side mechanism is d8b55afb00ee308bdfd482e39728e1401d2f2911; its parent tree lacks the backend lines; v0.9.2 contains it and v0.9.1 does not, matching the published affected range. No AI contribution to the introduction or to the v0.9.6 exposure is established from the BIC commit objects, so the record closes NOT_AI; it would flip to AI_ROOT_CAUSE if a BIC-side co-author trailer or AI disclosure surfaced.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MCP Toolbox serves unauthenticated MCP JSON-RPC over HTTP (default 127.0.0.1:5000). A malicious website can DNS-rebind its hostname to the victim loopback address so the browser sends same-origin requests whose Host is the attacker domain. Before v0.25.0 the server never checked Host or Origin on /mcp (POST JSON-RPC, later SSE/Streamable HTTP); mcpHandler dispatches initialize, tools/list, and tools/call into configured database tools, so the rebound page can steal data or mutate the backend. CORS --allowed-origins (862868f, 2025-11-27) does not stop rebinding. v0.25.0 adds hostCheck() against --allowed-hosts; both flags still default to '*' and only warn, which the CNA still records as the patch because operators can now set a strict list.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can influence patch-pipeline inputs in a melange YAML (patches, series, strip-components, fuzz) causes those values to be compile-time substituted into the builtin patch pipeline's runs script and then executed by /bin/sh. pkg/build/compile.go compilePipeline loads pkg/build/pipelines/patch.yaml and mutates pipeline.Runs with util.MutateStringFromMap, which splices ${{inputs.*}} values with no shell quoting. Before the fix the script assigned series='${{inputs.series}}' (quote-breakout if the value contains a single quote), tested [ -z $series ] and grepped $series unquoted, echoed '${{inputs.patches}}' into a temp series file, and ran patch '-p${{inputs.strip-components}}' --fuzz=${{inputs.fuzz}} --verbose < $patchfile, so backticks, $(...), ;, |, and redirections in those inputs execute as the melange process. license-check YAML/APK mode (pkg/cli/license_check.go -> pkg/source/source.go FetchSourceFromMelange) runs uses: patch steps on the host via exec.Command("/bin/sh", "-c", ...). melange build compiles the same pipeline into the build runner. Impact is OS command injection (CWE-78) with the privileges of that process.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked for sanitization that would falsify the advisory: pipeline runs receive raw substitution (no escaping; the quoting variant MutateAndQuoteStringFromMap is not used for runs), runs text reaches /bin/sh -c (pkg/build/pipeline.go:204), and a harness run of the exact acdbc00a script lines executed the injected touch (marker file created), so the defect is real rather than a false positive.
mechanism.impact: Arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the melange process on the build host (CWE-78; CVSS 3.1 AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) - build-host compromise, artifact or credential exfiltration, and tampering with the built package.
mechanism.preconditions: The attacker must be able to influence patch-related inputs of a melange configuration that a victim builds (PR-driven CI, build-as-a-service, untrusted third-party configs); the injected commands run wherever the pipeline executes, including on the host in license-check YAML mode.

evidence: When WebUI password/passkey auth is off (the default), check_auth() admits every caller. The embedded-terminal routes POST /api/terminal/start, /input, /resize, /close and GET /api/terminal/output were registered on that same dispatcher with no local-origin or credential check of their own. start_terminal() opens a PTY and execs the user shell as the server process; write_terminal() then copies request body bytes onto the PTY master. A remote unauthenticated client can create a WebUI session, start a terminal, and feed shell commands (the advisory's four sequential HTTP requests) for full RCE as the server user. The v0.51.788 gate reuses _onboarding_gate_allows so passwordless deployments only accept loopback/private origins unless HERMES_WEBUI_ONBOARDING_OPEN=1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Improper authorization (CWE-863, CVSS 8.1) in OpenClaw node browser control: node.invoke(browser.proxy) routes browser control messages to the browser control service with only an allowlist filter on profile names and NO check of whether the operation mutates a persistent browser profile. With the default empty allowProfiles config, POST /profiles/create, POST /reset-profile and DELETE /profiles/<name> are dispatched unguarded to the browser profile manager, letting an untrusted local process (assistant agent host) create/reset/delete persistent browser profiles, i.e. persistent profile mutation via browser.proxy. Fixed in v2026.4.8 by making the isPersistentBrowserProfileMutation guard unconditional in extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.ts and adding a gateway-side check in src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts ('node.invoke cannot mutate persistent browser profiles via browser.proxy').

causal_research.flaw_origin: Missing authorization check at the browser.proxy dispatch boundary: commit c3cb26f7ca933937e9675634041c74492dbc0749 introduced node browser proxy routing into src/node-host/runner.ts with only profile-name allowlist filtering (isProfileAllowed / early return when allowProfiles is empty) and no persistent-profile mutation guard; the /profiles/create, /reset-profile and DELETE /profiles/<name> routes already existed in src/browser/routes/basic.ts at that time. causal_research.bug_semantics: Untrusted renderer content builds a plain object with an enumerable own key named __proto__ (Object.defineProperty) and sends it across contextBridge, typically as an argument to a function exposed from preload, or as a nested object being copied. CreateProxyForAPI enumerates own enumerable keys, recursively copies values, then writes each key onto a fresh destination object created by gin_helper::Dictionary::CreateEmpty (ordinary object with Object.prototype). The write uses Dictionary::Set, which calls v8::Object::Set. For the name __proto__, Set invokes the inherited Object.prototype.__proto__ setter instead of installing an own data property, so the copied object's [[Prototype]] becomes the attacker-supplied object. Preload code that then reads properties without own-property checks observes attacker-controlled inherited values (prototype-pollution-style), even with contextIsolation enabled. Apps that only pass primitives or that validate with Object.hasOwn are outside the stated impact. Arrays are copied by index, not this named-key Set path.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The Set-based own-key copy was first written when contextBridge was added. Public PR #20307 member 5c4c9d56afd963f44c4c6a9c76f90c312b468913 introduced CreateProxyForAPI using mate::Dictionary::CreateEmpty plus proxy.Set(key_str, ...) for nested objects and primitives. Its immediate parent bb2ab01f99fb790f0d271211c1c3572ed4511e02 has no context-bridge source file. That member already used the same Set helper for reverse-binding copies from the main world. 4b79d73debc9162a7988683ce90bbb012239f4a8 later proxied function arguments through PassValueToOtherContext (later exposure of untrusted arguments onto the copy path) but did not introduce Set. GitHub squash-merge 0090616f7b720df7bbdea1b28d3669249e089fab is the landing commit on master, not the first writer. Later history only retargeted the same Set call (key_str->key, extra scopes, mate->gin_helper).
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 5c4c9d56af to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: An object literal {__proto__: x} sets the prototype instead of creating an own property and a non-enumerable own __proto__ is filtered out by the GetOwnPropertyNames(ONLY_ENUMERABLE) key filter, so neither triggers the copy path; primitives, arrays (indices only, cloned_arr->Set with numeric index) and symbol keys are unaffected; the dynamic-property accessor branch already used DefineProperty; serializable non-plain objects take the V8 serializer branch rather than this copy, so no parallel __proto__ surface was found there.
mechanism.impact: Prototype-pollution-style confusion across the context boundary (CWE-1321): the object the preload receives has an attacker-controlled prototype, so inherited property reads resolve to attacker values that own-property checks would have rejected, and the promised own-key __proto__ is missing. Advisory CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N, moderate.
mechanism.preconditions: App preload accepts object arguments from untrusted content and reads properties from them without own-property checks (advisory statement); the attacker can build an own enumerable __proto__ key; object must take the ordinary-object copy path (IsPlainObject in this file excludes only exotic built-ins such as Date, Map, ArrayBuffer, Proxy, so any ordinary object qualifies).
mechanism.summary: Untrusted main-world content passes an ordinary object with an own enumerable "__proto__" key to a function exposed through contextBridge; the bridge's CreateProxyForAPI copy assigns keys with Dictionary::Set on a plain destination object, so the inherited Object.prototype.__proto__ setter runs and the copy's prototype becomes the attacker-supplied object; preload code that reads properties off the copy without own-property checks then sees attacker-injected values.
mechanism.trigger: contextIsolation enabled; a preload uses contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld to expose a function (or exposes an API object) and accepts an object argument from the page; the page hands over an object that has an own enumerable property literally named __proto__, e.g. JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}}') or Object.defineProperty({data:1}, '__proto__', {value:{polluted:true}, enumerable:true, writable:true, configurable:true}).
mechanism.vulnerable_code: shell/renderer/api/electron_api_context_bridge.cc:728 CreateProxyForAPI (blob 78a5aae183, pre-fix parent d164b7af016aeb9fbd97e06e2f447ebf2856d883); introduced as shell/renderer/api/atom_api_context_bridge.cc:426 in 0090616f7b720df7bbdea1b28d3669249e089fab

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real, published CWE-1321 defect: contextBridge object copy used v8::Object::Set, so an enumerable own __proto__ key mutated the destination prototype. That Set write first appears in PR #20307 member 5c4c9d56afd963f44c4c6a9c76f90c312b468913; the parent tree has no context-bridge file. The master squash 0090616f7b720df7bbdea1b28d3669249e089fab is only the landing commit. The 2026 fix replaces that single Set with CreateDataProperty and is present in the four patched tags via #50900 plus trop backports. The BIC commit object is named-human Samuel Attard at Slack in 2019 with no AI trailers, so AI did not introduce, newly expose, or incompletely remediate the defect. Anthropic addresses on the later fix are employment identity, not BIC attribution. Verdict is NOT_AI.
CreateProxyForAPI copies own enumerable property names from the source object onto a fresh plain destination object with Dictionary::Set, so an own enumerable "__proto__" key (reachable from untrusted content via JSON.parse, Object.defineProperty or Object.fromEntries) invokes the inherited Object.prototype.__proto__ setter and replaces the copy's prototype with an attacker-influenced object in the preload's world. The smallest original introducing change is the module's own introduction in 0090616f7b (2019-10-18, PR #20307), whose added CreateProxyForAPI already contained proxy.Set(key_str, ...); no contextBridge code exists anywhere in that commit's parent, and a rename-following pickaxe shows the Set-based assignment was never rewritten before the fix. The fix abffba4548 (PR #50900) replaces Set with CreateDataProperty for every copied key, and the identical hunk was backported to the 39, 40, 41 and 42 release lines matching the advisory's fixed versions 39.8.9, 40.9.2, 41.2.2 and 42.0.0-beta.4. causal_research.bug_semantics: When an app defines a Next.js rewrite whose destination is an external http(s) origin, the request is forwarded with vendored http-proxy (proxy.web). causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: a cross-origin iframe with allow="serial" or allow="camera; microphone" performs a synchronous device permission check (navigator.serial or mediaDevices.enumerateDevices). Vulnerable code: WebContentsPermissionHelper::CheckPermission always used the primary main frame and web_contents_->GetLastCommittedURL() as the origin passed to ElectronPermissionManager::CheckPermissionWithDetails, while CheckMediaAccessPermission/CheckSerialAccessPermission did not thread the requesting RenderFrameHost they already had (or, for media, that WebContents::CheckMediaAccessPermission already received). Sink: session.setPermissionCheckHandler saw requestingOrigin (and details.isMainFrame/details.requestingUrl) as the top-level origin, so origin-based allow logic could grant the iframe device access intended only for the embedder. Preconditions: the app installs setPermissionCheckHandler with origin-based logic and embeds such iframes. Counterevidence: default handler-null allows all checks; apps that decide from details.securityOrigin for media, or that do not embed delegated iframes, are not affected. Distinct from the async RequestPermission/chooser origin bug closed earlier by #50052.

causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object eca3f59100 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: details.securityOrigin already carried the true iframe origin in the pre-fix code (set from the security_origin / embedding_origin arguments of CheckMediaAccessPermission / CheckSerialAccessPermission at blob 23f5e048 lines 314-334), which matches the advisory's stated workaround and confirms the defect is specific to the requestingOrigin argument rather than to all frame information. I also checked that nothing between 2018 and the fix corrects the frame: the March 2026 commit 2c6dd1156c45d16b48cbbdfaa15a276a88ddc0c7 changed only the request-path origin (RequestPermission) and the device choosers, leaving CheckPermission on GetPrimaryMainFrame()/GetLastCommittedURL() until April, and the advisory's affected range is confirmed by the clone's tags (0cbdf2f is contained in v39.8.7 and later 39.x tags).
mechanism.impact: The app's check handler is called with requestingOrigin = top-level URL, and the same frame also sets details.isMainFrame=true (GetPrimaryMainFrame has no parent) and details.requestingUrl = top-level URL; origin-based allow-list logic consequently grants an embedded cross-origin iframe serial/media device access intended for the top-level origin (moderate severity, CWE-346).
mechanism.preconditions: The app installs a check handler via session.setPermissionCheckHandler with origin-based logic (for example comparing requestingOrigin to a trusted origin) and embeds a cross-origin iframe that is allowed to request the device kind. Not affected: apps keyed on details.securityOrigin - which the helper fills with the real caller-supplied security_origin / embedding_origin - or on details.requestingUrl, and apps that do not embed such iframes.
mechanism.summary: An app that decides serial-port or media (camera/microphone) permission checks from the requestingOrigin argument of session.setPermissionCheckHandler is shown the top-level frame's origin even when the request comes from a cross-origin iframe, so a delegated device request can be authorized as if it originated from the trusted top-level origin (CWE-346).
mechanism.trigger: A cross-origin iframe with delegated device permission calls Web Serial requestPort() or getUserMedia()/getDisplayMedia() (audio or video capture); the synchronous chrome-side check reaches WebContentsPermissionHelper::CheckPermission, which resolves the request to web_contents_->GetPrimaryMainFrame() and web_contents_->GetLastCommittedURL() instead of the calling frame.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: shell/browser/web_contents_permission_helper.cc:230-239 WebContentsPermissionHelper::CheckPermission (pre-fix blob 23f5e04894d42b500c4aa195bd82f033f3334663 at 5442f1d7; same shape in the main-branch pre-fix blob 23332fe5554e715e41bbe18615b360f3a3a8b72f at 30cf60a9^) - line 233 GetPrimaryMainFrame(), line 236 GetLastCommittedURL(), line 237 CheckPermissionWithDetails(permission, rfh, origin, details); introduced as atom/browser/web_contents_permission_helper.cc:81-89 with GetMainFrame() at line 84 (blob 1a145747371240b01794a5202d977254b08263c7)

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory and pre-fix source agree on a real CWE-346 in synchronous permission checks: CheckPermission always attributed iframe serial/media checks to the top-level origin. That helper was first written in 2018 by named human Samuel Attard in eca3f59 (squash-decomposed from 68da311); the parent tree lacks it. The 2026 repair threads the requesting frame and ships in the stated patched tags. The BIC commit object has no AI authorship marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class. Fix-side Anthropic mailbox on d9a7e41 is a named-human company address and does not move attribution.
The defect is a synchronous permission check that always resolves to the top-level frame: WebContentsPermissionHelper::CheckPermission() builds its RenderFrameHost and origin from web_contents_->GetPrimaryMainFrame() and web_contents_->GetLastCommittedURL() and hands that pair to ElectronPermissionManager::CheckPermissionWithDetails(), which passes the origin as the handler's requestingOrigin argument and derives details.isMainFrame and details.requestingUrl from the same frame. Both paths the advisory names funnel into that one function - WebContents::CheckMediaAccessPermission already received the requesting render_frame_host but dropped it, and ElectronSerialDelegate::CheckSerialAccessPermission passed only frame->GetLastCommittedOrigin() - so a serial or camera/microphone check issued inside a cross-origin iframe was reported to session.setPermissionCheckHandler as if it came from the top-level origin. The behaviour enters the tree with 68da311ed1f5b37e3a86c90a9ed4570e13e98aa4 ("feat: add session.setPermissionCheckHandler (#13925)", 2018-08-29), whose file states contain CheckPermission with GetMainFrame()/GetLastCommittedURL() at lines 84/87 while the immediate parent afdb6c5f903cd49bd794998a6d7630097ed5e014 has no CheckPermission in either atom/browser/web_contents_permission_helper.cc or atom/browser/atom_permission_manager.cc. The repair is the April 2026 pair 30cf60a9356f48cb1740896ba63c7b3c0604e44b (main) and 0cbdf2f0375466d701aa393c92e0ec29eb89ea6c (the advisory's reference commit, contained in v39.8.7 and later 39.x tags), which thread the requesting RenderFrameHost through CheckPermission / CheckSerialAccessPermission / CheckMediaAccessPermission. The BIC object is an ordinary 2018 human commit - author Samuel Attard <samuel.r.attard@gmail.com>, committer Charles Kerr <ckerr@github.com>, no trailers of any kind - and Anthropic-related markers first appear in this repository in November 2025, so there is no AI evidence on the BIC side. With mechanism, parent-verified BIC, fix and a clean BIC-side AI check all established, the verdict is NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: The advisory's serial and media mechanism is closed, but the same family of sync checks is not fully converted: at the advisory commit 0cbdf2f the HID delegate (shell/browser/hid/electron_hid_delegate.cc:146-147), the USB delegate (shell/browser/usb/electron_usb_delegate.cc:185-186) and the File System Access permission context (shell/browser/file_system_access/file_system_access_permission_context.cc:271-273) still call CheckPermissionWithDetails with a null RenderFrameHost, so the manager emits no requestingUrl and isMainFrame=false for those permission types. Those call sites pass a caller-supplied requesting origin and are therefore not an origin-confusion path of this advisory - this is a residual consistency gap noted for the record, not an unresolved causal question about the serial/media defect, and it is out of the advisory's stated scope.

mechanism.preconditions: (1) Attacker holds any verified account (default role). causal_research.bug_semantics: Timing side-channel info leak (CWE-208, CVSS 3.1 2.6 low) in vLLM prefix caching: V1 engine's content-addressed KV-cache block hashing (hash_block_tokens / hash_request_tokens in vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py + KVCacheManager) reuses cached prefix blocks purely keyed on token-id hashes with no tenant isolation. In multi-tenant/shared-backend deployments an attacker can send probe requests with guessed prefixes and observe Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) differences (cache hit = faster prefill) to learn whether a victim's prompt contains a given prefix (leaking sensitive user inputs/system prompts; AUC 0.99 at 8-token prefix in the advisory's LLaMA2-70B test). Fixed by optional request cache_salt (PR #17045): salt is mixed into the extra hash keys of the FIRST block only (generate_block_hash_extra_keys / need_extra_keys in kv_cache_utils.py), so only requests sharing a salt reuse cached prefixes. Affected: all vllm <0.9.0 (introduced: 0 in PYSEC-2025-53); patched 0.9.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: LIVE SELECT persists the registering user's Auth (and, after #2661, the session value that supplies $auth, $token, $session, and $access) on the stored subscription. Notification dispatch in lives.rs rebuilds Options/Context from that snapshot and evaluates table- and row-level PERMISSIONS against it, never against the current RPC session. After invalidate() clears the session, after DURATION FOR SESSION TTL expiry, or after signin/signup/authenticate/refresh changes the principal on the same connection, the subscription keeps matching the old principal, so the client continues to receive real-time notifications until the connection closes. Impact is confidentiality-only continued reads of records the prior principal could already SELECT.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-22738 / GHSA-fvh3-672c-7p6c (Spring AI, CWE-94/917 SpEL injection): SimpleVectorStore evaluates metadata filter expressions by converting the parsed Filter AST to a SpEL expression STRING (SimpleVectorStoreFilterExpressionConverter) and then running SpelExpressionParser.parseExpression(...).getValue(context, Boolean.class) with a StandardEvaluationContext exposing #metadata. Affected 1.0.0 < 1.0.5 and 1.1.0 < 1.1.4; only applications that pass user-supplied input as a filter expression key are affected. Fixed by replacing string-based SpEL evaluation with a dedicated AST-walking SimpleVectorStoreFilterExpressionEvaluator (no string interpolation).

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated client sends a crafted Java serialized payload as the jato.clientSession query/form parameter to any JATO page whose JSP renders <jato:form> (password-reset JSPs are enough). JATO RequestContextImpl.getClientSession() constructs ClientSession, which stores the raw parameter. During form rendering, hasAttributes/getEncodedString/isValid/ensureAttributes calls ClientSession.deserializeAttributes, which Http64-decodes the parameter and passes it to Encoder.deserialize(..., false). Pre-16.0.6 Encoder.deserialize wraps the bytes in ApplicationObjectInputStream and calls readObject with no class whitelist (resolveClass only picks a ClassLoader). That is CWE-502 RCE: attacker-controlled gadgets on the OpenAM classpath (advisory chain PriorityQueue -> Column$ColumnComparator -> xalan TemplatesImpl) run as the application server user. CVE-2021-35464/OPENAM-5925 only wrapped jato.pageSession in ConsoleViewBeanBase via IOUtils.deserialise; clientSession kept the unfiltered Encoder path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS via SVG file upload (CWE-79). SVG is included in shopware.media.allowed_extensions in src/Core/Framework/Resources/config/packages/shopware.yaml (line 194) and is recognized by ImageTypeDetector as ImageType::VECTOR_GRAPHIC ('svg' => ImageType::VECTOR_GRAPHIC), but the media upload pipeline has zero SVG content sanitization (no DOMPurify/svg-sanitize/strip_tags). Any admin can upload a malicious SVG (onload, <script>, <foreignObject>) via the media manager; it is stored as public media and executes in the Shopware domain context when opened, leading to stored XSS / admin takeover. Fix adds a strict passive SVG allowlist (FileContentValidationStrategy + SvgContentValidator) rejecting active content. Affected since 6.6 (fixed 6.6.10.18) and 6.7.0.0 (fixed 6.7.10.1).

Public GET /api/public/share/<hash> and GET /api/public/dl/<hash> (withHashFile) later resolve that stored path against the owner's current filesystem. A share created for a non-existent path therefore 404s until a file is created at the same path, then immediately exposes the new object. That breaks the expected invariant that a share grants access only to an object that existed and was reviewed at creation time.
