causal_research.bug_semantics: Informational defense-in-depth (CWE-20). The AWS SDK for Rust / smithy-rs endpoint resolver accepted a caller-controlled region input and used it to construct the endpoint URL without validating that the region is a valid host label, so an actor who can influence the region value (e.g. app configuration) could route AWS API calls to non-existent or non-AWS hosts. Fixed in the 2025-11-06 release (PR smithy-lang/smithy-rs#4383) by validating the region in the generated endpoint ParamsBuilder::build() against is_valid_host_label before it reaches the URL template substitution. Advisory GHSA-g59m-gf8j-gjf5 is informational, LOW severity; the SDK behaved within the shared-responsibility model.

causal_research.bug_semantics: psd-tools decompress() is reached when parsing untrusted PSD/PSB channel payloads. For Compression.ZIP and ZIP_WITH_PREDICTION it called zlib.decompress(data) with no max_length, so a small compressed blob can expand to gigabytes and OOM the process before any expected-size check. Independently, width/height/depth were multiplied into allocation sizes (length = width * height * max(1, depth // 8) and RLE row_size) with no Adobe-spec upper bound, so a malformed header can request a huge buffer. The only post-decompress size integrity check was assert len(result) == length, which python -O removes. A separate Low Cython issue used 32-bit cdef int indices against Py_ssize_t row size, theoretically wrapping above INT_MAX. Attack path: feed a crafted PSD with ZIP-compressed channels (and/or huge declared dimensions) to PSDImage.open / composite / export.

causal_research.bug_semantics: After password login, Baserow issues a short-lived 2FA JWT (TwoFactorAccessToken.for_user) and requires a second request to POST /api/two-factor-auth/verify/. Require2faToken only checked that the Bearer token had token_type '2fa'; it did not authenticate request.user from the token. VerifyTOTPAuthView.post then forwarded the JSON body (including client-supplied email) into TwoFactorAuthHandler.verify / TOTPAuthProviderType.verify, which loaded the TOTP secret or backup hash by user__email, and finally logged in User.objects.filter(email=data['email']).first(). An attacker who already passed password auth for their own account could therefore splice a victim email plus the victim's TOTP or backup code onto their 2FA token and obtain the victim's session, skipping the victim's password. High complexity matches needing a valid second factor for the target.

causal_research.bug_semantics: write_file and patch in hermes-agent refuse writes to sensitive system prefixes by calling _check_sensitive_path. That helper resolves the user path with os.path.realpath and then tests whether the resolved string starts with /etc/, /boot/, or /usr/lib/systemd/. On macOS /etc is a symlink to /private/etc, so a write to /etc/hosts (or a symlink whose realpath is under /private/etc) becomes /private/etc/hosts, which does not start with /etc/, and the checker returns None. The write then proceeds at OS permission level. Issue #8734 reproduced this through the API server: write_file('/etc/hosts') was not policy-blocked on Darwin while /boot/grub.cfg was. The same list also omitted /private/var (macOS /var symlink). This is CWE-59: the blocklist is applied to a fully resolved path without including the platform's resolved sensitive prefixes (and without also matching the unresolved path).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: untrusted content in a sandboxed iframe with allow-scripts but not allow-popups synthesizes a MouseEvent click with ctrlKey/metaKey on a link (no real user gesture). Blink FrameLoader treats that as a new-window navigation and invokes Electron WebContents::OpenURLFromTab with disposition != CURRENT_TAB. Vulnerable code: OpenURLFromTab emitted -new-window (which runs setWindowOpenHandler and can create a BrowserWindow) without reading the initiating FrameTreeNode active_sandbox_flags for WebSandboxFlags::kPopups. Impact: the iframe sandbox popup restriction is bypassed, so a new window can be created or the handler invoked. Preconditions: the app embeds untrusted content in a sandboxed iframe and relies on missing allow-popups rather than denying in setWindowOpenHandler. Counterevidence: window.open / AddNewContents is a separate path; apps that always deny untrusted window opens are not affected. Complementary Chromium FrameLoader blocking of untrusted-event new-window from sandboxed frames is defense-in-depth, not a substitute for the Electron OpenURL check.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When graphQLPublicIntrospection is false (the default since GHSA-48q3-prgv-gm4w), Parse Server refuses public GraphQL introspection but still returns graphql-js validation/coercion errors. Create<Class>FieldsInput marks Parse required custom fields as GraphQL NonNull. A client with only the public application id that names a class and omits a required custom field — either via a variable (coerceInputValue) or an inline input literal (ValuesOfCorrectTypeRule) — receives 'Field "<name>" of required type "<type>" was not provided.' (inline form also embeds the generated input type name). That identifier is also copied into extensions.stacktrace. The IntrospectionControlPlugin only blocks __schema/__type queries; until GHSA-2fgh-8j2g-w354 the existing 'Did you mean' strip could not reach this template because it has no suggestion suffix. Optional field names, unreferenced class names, stored data, credentials, and Cloud Code names are out of scope for this channel.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The @tinacms/cli dev server (default port 4001) exposes /media/list/*, /media/upload/* and /media/* endpoints that decode user-controlled URL path segments (decodeURI / decodeURIComponent) and join them onto the configured media folder with path.join() without validating the resolved path stays inside the media root. Attackers can use ../ (or percent-encoded %2e%2e%2f) segments to read arbitrary files (GET /media/list/../../../etc/passwd), write arbitrary files (POST /media/upload/../../..), and delete arbitrary files (DELETE /media/../../..), leading to arbitrary file read/write/delete and potential code execution in dev setups.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal / arbitrary file write via unsanitized FileUpload.name. FileUpload.name exposes the client-supplied filename verbatim (SmallFileUpload/LargeFileUpload store `upload.filename or ''` with no sanitization), and SmallFileUpload.save()/LargeFileUpload.save() write to `target = Path(path)` with no traversal or absolute-path defense (only target.parent.mkdir). When application code follows the common community pattern `save_path = UPLOAD_DIR / e.file.name`, an attacker-supplied filename like '../../../app.py' escapes the upload directory and can overwrite application/config files -> RCE on restart. Exploitable unauthenticated via ui.upload endpoint. Advisory GHSA-9ffm-fxg3-xrhh / CVE-2026-25732; fixed in 3.7.0.

Introducer e663af224fab6fa0d35b6de29581bcfedfcb51b3 'Treat pytest warnings as errors (#5186)' (Falko Schindler, 2025-09-30) is the squash merge that introduced the new ui.upload API (PR #5178 per the commit message) and is the unique commit creating nicegui/elements/upload_files.py (git log --all --diff-filter=A shows only this commit; immediate parent ffac9971c59e4ce68a65219d9e7813561a59de98 has no upload_files.py, parent-absent true). causal_research.bug_semantics: LangGraph's default CachePolicy.key_func (default_cache_key) pickles _freeze(args, kwargs) as the task-result cache key. For non-hashable objects exposing .tobytes() (numpy arrays, PIL images), _freeze collapses the value to (type name, raw bytes, optional shape), omitting dtype and PIL mode/size/palette. Two semantically distinct inputs that share a byte layout therefore map to one key. Through the functional API, prepare_push_task_functional invokes key_func(*call.input[0], **call.input[1]); a keyword-argument array/image hits the Mapping recursion then the lossy tobytes branch, so a later request on a shared InMemoryCache/Redis/SQLite cache is served the first request's cached node result without re-execution (cross-request reuse / classification-bypass). Positional args after 331d5b07cebc9e0f271802f9436fcdf0f17c9c84 short-circuit because tuples are Hashable by type and pickle the real object, so they do not collide; that asymmetry is a later change, not the first write of the tobytes triple. VulDB's CWE-327/328 'weak hash' wording is inaccurate: pickle.dumps is a serializer, and the defect is insufficient key uniqueness.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Deno.env.toObject() (op_env) ignores --deny-env: with --allow-env plus --deny-env=<var>, listing all env vars returns the denied ones too. causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-497: sudo-rs check_list_permission only queried the invoking user's own matching rules and never verified authorization to list a different user. Downstream `sudo -l -U<other>` therefore enumerated any other user's sudoers privileges whenever the low-privilege invoker had ANY sudo rule (e.g. a single /usr/bin/ps), even though they were not authorized for the `list` command, unlike original sudo which denies the request.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-W9Q3-G4P5-5Q2R (CVE-2025-46718), fixed v0.2.6: a user with limited sudo (single /usr/bin/ps) can run `sudo -l -U<other>` and enumerate other users' privileges, which original sudo denies ('Sorry, user bob is not allowed to execute list'). Introducer d7bfaed47 (2023-07-21, Jorge Aparicio) created src/sudo/pipeline/list.rs and src/sudoers/mod.rs check_list_permission; in that version check_list_permission only calls check_list_permission(am_user, on_host) over the invoking user's matching rules and never denies when request.target_user (inspected_user via -U) differs from the invoking user. Parent d087a8c8 lacks src/sudo/pipeline/list.rs (cat-file exit 128 -> introducer_parent_absent=true). Direct fix bd780dcbd8 (2025-04-29, Marc Schoolderman, 'add checking logic to sudoers') rewrites check_list_permission: when request.inspected_user != invoking_user it calls self.check(invoking_user, hostname, Request{user: inspected_user, command: Path('list'), ...}).flags.or(root-only), denying the list unless the invoking user is authorized for the `list` command; verified ancestor of tag v0.2.6 (merge-base --is-ancestor exit 0). causal_research.bug_semantics: Operators set Vault-style secrets-backend kwargs as per-key environment variables (AIRFLOW__SECRETS__BACKEND_KWARG__SECRET_ID and AIRFLOW__WORKERS__SECRETS_BACKEND_KWARG__SECRET_ID). Those names match Airflow's generic AIRFLOW__{SECTION}__{KEY} env mapping, so conf.as_dict._include_envs materializes them as synthetic options secrets.backend_kwarg__secret_id and workers.secrets_backend_kwarg__secret_id. sensitive_config_values is built only from config.yml options marked sensitive:true, which includes the JSON blob backend_kwargs / secrets_backend_kwargs but not the synthetic per-key names. GET /config therefore returns the plaintext values when [api] expose_config is on (display_sensitive is forced false). GET /config/section/{section}/option/{option} uses has_option/get, which honor the env var, then applies only the same closed sensitive set, so a direct option read also leaks. Preconditions: authenticated principal with Config GET, expose_config enabled, and those per-key env vars actually set. Impact: CWE-200 disclosure of secrets-backend credentials (role_id/secret_id).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Arbitrary file read -> potential RCE via Active Storage variant processing (libvips). When config.active_storage.variant_processor = :vips (default since load_defaults 7.0), untrusted image uploads are passed to libvips with its 'unfuzzed'/'untrusted' image loaders and savers enabled, allowing a crafted attachment to invoke an unsafe operation that reads arbitrary files accessible to the Rails process (env vars incl. secret_key_base, credentials) which may escalate to RCE or lateral movement (CVE-2026-66066 'kindarails2shell', CVSS 9.5). Affected: <7.2.3.2, <8.0.5.1, <8.1.3.1. Fix disables unfuzzed ops via Vips.block_untrusted(true) at boot, minimums libvips 8.13 / ruby-vips 2.2.1.

The whole handler body, including that authentication-only guard, first appears in the tree in the squash object 18a3902d (feat(admin): enhance notification event handlers, #530); its parent 024f9512 holds only a one-line empty stub of the file. The squash is an aggregate whose member commits are not reachable after the bounded PR-ref fetch, so the member-level minimal change is unavailable and no per-hunk authorship can be bound to this object.
causal_research.flip_condition: Recovering any readable member commit of PR #530 (pre-2025-07-02 project snapshot, contributor fork, mirror, or PR-ref archive). If the member that adds the notification handlers carries an object-level AI marker or a first-party AI disclosure, the verdict becomes AI_ROOT_CAUSE; if it carries a named human author with no marker the verdict becomes NOT_AI, with the aggregate's Copilot trailer still non-attributable to that hunk. A first-party advisory revision that narrows the wording (unauthenticated to non-admin) would change the prose but not the mechanism or the verdict.
causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: an authenticated non-admin user calls the notification-target admin routes under the admin prefix with a valid access key and session token. Vulnerable code: SetNotificationTarget, ListNotificationTargets, ListNotificationTargetArns and RemoveNotificationTarget each call a local check_permissions helper whose body is only check_key_valid(get_session_token(...), access_key); no validate_admin_request call with an AdminAction, unlike the other admin handler files. Impact: shared notification configuration is readable and writable by any authenticated account; a read-only user can delete unbound targets and overwrite bound targets so that subsequent S3 events are delivered to an attacker-controlled endpoint. Preconditions: a valid non-admin account, no admin role needed. Counterevidence: the advisory own proof section records 403 for unauthenticated and invalid-credential requests and records that self-referencing webhook and confused-deputy escalation did not work, so the demonstrated impact is interception plus audit evasion, not direct code execution.
causal_research.reasoning: Mechanism and repair are established by first-party evidence: the four notification endpoints carry an authentication-only guard in the release declared affected, the vendor proof shows a read-only user succeeding where control routes return 403, and the fix replaces the helper with validate_admin_request wired to SetBucketTargetAction / GetBucketTargetAction on every call site, adds contract tests, and leaves no check_permissions call site anywhere in rustfs/src at that object; the same commit repairs the identical pattern in the audit-target handlers, which the advisory did not name, and later refactors preserve the guard. The advisory title word unauthenticated is contradicted by its own proof section (403 Signature required for unauthenticated requests), so the recorded precondition is an authenticated non-admin principal. What is not established is the causal change granularity and its authorship: the handler first lands inside the PR 530 squash, whose member commits are unreachable after the one bounded PR-ref fetch (the fetched ref is a later unrelated branch that merely contains the squash), and the protocol forbids reading an aggregate trailer set as hunk attribution. Because the missing fact decides between AI_ROOT_CAUSE and NOT_AI, the honest verdict is EVIDENCE_GAP with a precise next question rather than either label. The verdict does not change, but its ground does: NOT_AI is unavailable because the object is not marker-free, and AI_ROOT_CAUSE is unavailable because the marker is bound to another file's hunk and the member objects are absent from the clone entirely. Close-out (2026-09-12): the imported object graph is now bounded on both sides. The squash 18a3902d entered the public repository inside one recorded push on 2025-07-02 (size 1493 equal to rev-list --count of its head), the pre-migration project produced no public events at all on 2025-07-01, and the member commits are therefore not withheld by a ref accident: they were never public. Inside the clone the whole object store was scanned (32,389 blobs, 5,858 commits, 40,345 trees) and the member subject add event admin api occurs exactly once, inside the squash body itself; blame and --find-object show the handler blob first appearing in that squash. The author identity on the aggregate (houseme <housemecn@gmail.com>, committer GitHub <noreply@github.com>) is an aggregate identity and under protocol step 2 is not BIC attribution for the event.rs hunks, and the one AI-named trailer in the body binds by the repository's own squash layout to the ecstore member rather than to the handler member. Authorship of the introducing hunk is thus not obtainable from any public source, not merely unfound. The ledger has no EVIDENCE_GAP status, so this record lands as BLOCKED with the missing object named; mechanism, affected and patched boundary, and the atomic repair are closed and recorded.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Incorrect default file permissions (CWE-276). Hermes Agent stores conversation history in ~/.hermes/response_store.db (SQLite) and per-route HMAC secrets in webhook_subscriptions.json; both files were created with whatever the process umask allows (typically 0o644, world-readable), so on shared hosts any local user can read conversation history, tool payloads, prompts, and HMAC secrets. Affects hermes-agent < 0.16.0 (v2026.x releases).
causal_research.evidence: GHSA-99f9-j8r3-p853 / CVE-2026-53870 (CWE-276, MODERATE, CVSS 3.1 AV:L/AC:L/PR:L...VC:H): 'Hermes Agent before 0.16.0 creates response_store.db and webhook_subscriptions.json with world-readable permissions (mode 0o644), exposing conversation history and HMAC secrets'. Fixes: 3bace071 (fix(state): restrict sensitive store file permissions; ResponseStore._tighten_file_permissions chmod 0o600 on db + -wal/-shm sidecars after __init__; webhook _save_subscriptions uses tempfile.mkstemp with 0o600 + re-assert on destination) and 3c231eb (chore: release v0.16.0). Traced via git log -S 'response_store.db' / 'sqlite3.connect' in gateway/platforms/api_server.py -> first appearance 8d528e0045; git log -S 'webhook_subscriptions.json' in hermes_cli/webhook.py -> first appearance dabe3c34cc. (2) dabe3c34cc (2026-03-28, 'hermes webhook CLI') added hermes_cli/webhook.py writing webhook_subscriptions.json via tmp_path.write_text(...) with no permission hardening; parent lacks webhook_subscriptions (verified exit 1). causal_research.bug_semantics: nono-py (PyPI) policy handling fails open in two ways (CWE-284 / CWE-707): (1) resolving a policy-derived ProxyConfig (network policy groups with allow_domain/upstream_proxy) did not automatically enforce CapabilitySet.proxy_only / NetworkMode::ProxyOnly, so a sandboxed child still had direct network access and could bypass the proxy domain allowlist; (2) policy JSON parsing accepted unknown security-sensitive fields (serde structs without deny_unknown_fields, only #[serde(default)]), so misspelled or unsupported restrictions were silently ignored. Fixed in 0.10.1: strict policy parsing rejecting unknown fields, automatic blocking of direct network access for proxy-filtered groups, explicit connect-host filtering (allowed_hosts defaulting to deny-all with allow_all_hosts opt-in), and a seccomp supervisor fallback for proxy-only enforcement.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The MCP Python SDK (PyPI package mcp) exposes HTTP-based servers via FastMCP using streamable HTTP or SSE transport. When such a server is bound to localhost without authentication and the user has not configured TransportSecuritySettings, the SDK never enables its DNS rebinding protection: TransportSecurityMiddleware.__init__ defaults a None settings argument to TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False) 'for backwards compatibility', and FastMCP passes settings.transport_security (None by default) straight into SseServerTransport/StreamableHTTPSessionManager. As a result Host/Origin header validation is off, so a malicious website can DNS-rebind to 127.0.0.1, bypass same-origin restrictions, and invoke the local server's tools/resources from browser context on behalf of the user. The flaw is the missing default-on behavior (protection disabled unless explicitly enabled), not the validation logic itself.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory references point at fix commit d3a184119e4479ea6a63590bc41f01dc06e3fa99 ('Merge commit from fork', 2025-12-02, Paul Carleton), whose diff adds to FastMCP.__init__: 'if transport_security is None and host in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"): transport_security = TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=True, allowed_hosts=[...], allowed_origins=[...])' in src/mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py, plus tests/server/fastmcp/test_server.py (TestDnsRebindingProtection). git log -S 'transport_security: TransportSecuritySettings' -- src/mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py yields exactly 4 commits; the earliest, 86bb54cb284c6db293b280671f1a8d0915d93ccb (2025-06-17), is a single-parent commit adding src/mcp/server/transport_security.py (new file, 127 lines) with the default-disabled middleware and the None-default Settings field. causal_research.bug_semantics: Validation bypass for non-finite float parameters (CWE-20 / missing finite-check). SamplingParams temperature validation uses comparison operators only ('if temperature < 0.0: raise', 'if 0 < self.temperature < _MAX_TEMP' warning guard), and Python IEEE-754 semantics evaluate NaN and positive Infinity comparisons to False, so both values pass every gate and propagate to GPU sampling kernels where they cause undefined behavior / CUDA errors that crash the inference worker (DoS). Adversary controls sampling params via API, so a request with temperature=NaN or temperature=Infinity can crash the serving worker. repetition_penalty has an analogous gap (NaN <= 0.0 is False).

display_hunks.annotation: The Copilot-coauthored TypeScript runtime created a plain Nunjucks environment and sent prepared host values directly to renderString. Attacker-controlled templates could traverse constructor and prototype properties and invoke functions in the host Node.js process.

The fix replaces unrestricted JavaScript object traversal with own-data-only lookup, strips unsafe constructor and prototype keys from inputs, and blocks every template function call while Nunjucks renders. Restoring the original runtime hooks in finally confines those guards to this render operation.

The vulnerable sink previously passed prepared host values straight to the unrestricted environment. This call-site replacement makes both input sanitization and the guarded Nunjucks runtime mandatory on the actual render path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: phpMyFAQ stores an optional per-attachment encryption key. From the BIC through 4.1.3, AbstractAttachment::setKey($key, $default=false) hashed a custom key with PHP sha1() into $passwordHash and wrote it to faqattachment.password_hash (CHAR(40)). The stored SHA-1 is a CWE-328 weak hash of the AES key: a database dump can be cracked and the recovered key decrypts EncryptedFile contents. The property comment claimed the SHA-1 would be compared on later key presentation, but no comparison/verify path ever existed; AttachmentFactory::create() calls setKey($key) with the default flag, so production usually stored an empty hash unless a caller passed default=false. Collision-based 'bypass of attachment protection' in the GHSA write-up is therefore overstated relative to the code, but the published weak-hash finding is real. 4.1.4 removes the sha1() writes rather than switching to bcrypt.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated HTTP clients can authenticate to REST endpoints such as GET /api/v1/me by supplying a MongoDB operator in the access_token query string (for example access_token[$ne]=null). qs/Express nested query parsing turns that into query.access_token = {$ne:'null'}. oAuth2ServerAuth (originally API.v1.addAuthMethod) forwarded that value to getAccessToken -> OAuthAccessTokens.findOne({ accessToken: <user object> }). Because objects are truthy, the later empty-token guard does not reject them, so MongoDB returns the first stored OAuth access token and the corresponding user, enabling account takeover whenever an OAuth app has issued a token.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unprivileged principal who can CREATE/UPDATE records or DEFINE FUNCTION/FIELD/EVENT/API plants deferred logic (a <future> field, stored closure, custom function, event, or API body) that performs privileged statements such as DEFINE USER ... ROLES OWNER. Before the fix, evaluation uses the current session Options.auth: Function::Future computes its inner expression in the invoking Runtime/Options, and DEFINE FUNCTION/FIELD/EVENT/API bodies likewise run as the invoker. When a higher-privileged user queries or writes the record or calls the function, the planted logic runs with their permissions and can create a root owner or take over the server. Network-capable reads can also exfiltrate. The 2.5.0 / 3.0.0-beta.3 patches record the creator's AuthLimit on those definitions and cap execution to the weaker of creator and invoker; 2.5.0 also default-denies stored closures.

mechanism.impact: Confused-deputy privilege escalation: the planted logic executes with the privileged invoker's authority, allowing creation of a database or root OWNER (the fix's own test drives exactly this), reads and writes beyond the attacker's rights, and, with unrestricted network capability, data exfiltration; the advisory describes full privilege escalation and server takeover.
mechanism.preconditions: Auth-enabled SurrealDB with an attacker holding a limited role that can define or modify fields, functions, events or apis on a table; a more-privileged user subsequently reads or writes the affected records or signs in; the pre-fix tree enforces no definer bound on expression evaluation (no auth_limit exists before the fix).
mechanism.summary: A database editor defines or modifies a field (COMPUTED, or VALUE/DEFAULT expression), function, event or api whose logic is stored but evaluated later with the invoking user's Options rather than the definer's; the expression runs in the context of whoever reads or writes the affected record (or signs in against it), so the attacker executes statements with that user's privileges.
mechanism.trigger: An unprivileged user holding a limited role (e.g. database EDITOR) that permits defining or modifying fields, functions, events or apis plants logic on a table; a more-privileged user then loads or modifies the affected records, or authenticates against them (signin/signup compute field expressions), causing the stored expression to execute under that privileged user's auth context.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored/reflected XSS in App Router applications using CSP nonces (CWE-79). getScriptNonceFromHeader() in packages/next/src/server/app-render/get-script-nonce-from-header.tsx parses a nonce out of the incoming Content-Security-Policy request header with a permissive matcher (source startsWith "'nonce-", length>8, endsWith "'", then only rejects chars matching ESCAPE_REGEX /[&><\u2028\u2029]/). The extracted value is embedded into rendered HTML script nonce attributes (via createServerInsertedMetadata / stream nonce options). Malformed nonce values derived from request headers can therefore be reflected into rendered HTML in an unsafe way; behind shared caches an attacker can poison cached responses so script executes for later visitors. Fixed by rejecting/ignoring malformed nonces (strict regex ^'nonce-([A-Za-z0-9+/_-]+={0,2})'$ ) and adding htmlEscapeAttributeString for attribute-context escaping. Introduced 13.4.0, fixed 15.5.16 / 16.2.5.
causal_research.evidence: Direct code fix b4c6705c70a08fd82fbc6d140956528a8c30505b ('Ignore malformed CSP nonce headers', JJ Kasper, Apr 21 2026) replaces the permissive extraction in get-script-nonce-from-header.tsx with CSP_NONCE_SOURCE_REGEX = /^'nonce-([A-Za-z0-9+/_-]+={0,2})'$/ loop (malformed nonces ignored, not thrown), adds htmlEscapeAttributeString to packages/next/src/server/htmlescape.ts (ATTRIBUTE_ESCAPE_REGEX /[&"'<>]/g) and uses it in create-server-inserted-metadata.tsx, plus tests. causal_research.bug_semantics: Overmind bulk-delete endpoints EventReportsController::deleteSelection and SharingGroupsController::deleteSelection wrap CRUDComponent::deleteSelection, which looks up each posted id/uuid with find() and hard-deletes when checkModifyCallback returns true. The callbacks returned only the caller’s global role flags (perm_add for reports, perm_sharing_group for sharing groups) instead of the per-object ownership checks already used by the single delete() actions (EventReport::fetchIfAuthorized(..., 'delete') and SharingGroup::checkIfOwner()). ACL listed the actions as theming_enabled plus those same role flags (SharingGroups ACL added 12 minutes later in 85c63695), so an authenticated contributor or sharing-group-capable user with themes enabled could POST another organisation’s report or sharing-group ids/uuids and destroy them instance-wide. Site-admin bypass in ACL::checkAccess is intended; the defect is the missing per-row gate for non-owners who hold the broad role.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Heap buffer overflow in the JSON generator when dumping to an IO object (JSON.dump(obj, io)). fbuffer_do_inc_capa's IO fast path checks `if (RB_LIKELY(requested < fb->capa)) return;` against TOTAL capacity instead of REMAINING capacity (fb->capa - fb->len); when 16383-len <= requested < 16383 it returns without growing, so fbuffer_append writes past the allocated buffer -> heap OOB write (crash / memory corruption, CWE-787). Triggered by streaming a JSON document >= 16KB (FBUFFER_IO_BUFFER_SIZE = 16384-1) into an IO that blocks/does not consume (e.g. StringIO that grows via the IO path). Vulnerable in json gem since 2.9.0 (when the IO streaming path was introduced); fixed in 2.19.9 (CVSS 3.7 low, HackerOne #3785370, reported by tera-ny).
causal_research.evidence: resolved=true (member_map), identity exact: GHSA-x2f5-4prf-w687 cve_id == CVE-2026-54696, vuln in ruby/json generator.c, fixed 2.19.9. Fix commits (all Jean Boussier, 2026-06-08, CHANGES.md 'Fix buffer overflow in streaming mode [CVE-PENDING]'): master 996bac686d64e4e3aaeae03b14a7f9ee9695ebdb (parent 8144d4cb3473b9b48f10716a6ea7fcc83300e826), release-branch fd6a65bd08e5f3a429c03919ebfd8dd19158f095 (parent 5233dd9b851a4924f793aec1a1658ed8b66a34c7), release tag 2cff2678d5af54890a49da58345ac141b571f661 'Release 2.19.9' (2026-06-11); fix restructures fbuffer_init/fbuffer_do_inc_capa so the IO case no longer pre-allocates to IO_BUFFER_SIZE (capa stays the actual allocation until flush), making the remaining-capacity check safe. Introducer f017af6c is a single-parent linear commit; its diff (ext/json/ext/fbuffer/fbuffer.h) is the exact bug: `if (RB_LIKELY(requested < fb->capa)) return;` in the io!=Qnil branch with fb->len > 0 -> grow skipped while fbuffer_append proceeds -> heap OOB. causal_research.bug_semantics: CPU DoS via quadratic complexity in Rack::Utils.select_best_encoding. When an Accept-Encoding header contains many wildcard (*) entries, the code evaluates `(available_encodings - accept_encoding.map(&:first))` inside the loop over every entry, so `accept_encoding.map(&:first)` is recomputed for each wildcard (O(N^2) over the parsed header). Rack::Deflater calls Utils.select_best_encoding(ENCODINGS, Utils.parse_encodings(accept_encoding)) per request, so an unauthenticated attacker sending a single ~8KB header with ~1000 '*;q=0.5' entries triggers ~170ms CPU per request. Fixed in 2.2.23 / 3.1.21 / 3.2.6. Distinct from CVE-2024-26146 (ReDoS during Accept parsing).
causal_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-v569-hp3g-36wr / CVE-2026-34230 (details quote the exact quadratic line `(available_encodings - accept_encoding.map(&:first)).each do |m2|`; ~1000 wildcard entries in 8KB header => ~170ms CPU; fixed 2.2.23/3.1.21/3.2.6). Introducer 0f2dab573bb53d612bd93cc04327bf147909fb95 'Added support for Accept-Encoding (via Request#accept_encoding and Utils.select_best_encoding)' (Christoffer Sawicki <christoffer.sawicki@gmail.com>, committed by Christian Neukirchen, 2008-07-06) first wrote select_best_encoding in lib/rack/utils.rb with the wildcard branch `(available_encodings - accept_encoding.map { |m2, _| m2 }).map { |m2| [m2, q] }` recomputing the full parsed-header scan inside the loop; immediate parent 835cfd6860864d0d0d559b3e997544aeb374dc00 has 0 occurrences of select_best_encoding (parent-absent true). The 2019 rewrite 33af8f378f2d521e2db3cbecea0e500b53d9d4a5 (Krzysztof Rybka, 'Optimize Rack::Utils.select_best_encoding') preserved the same O(n^2) recompute as `(available_encodings - accept_encoding.map(&:first))`, so the vulnerability persists unmodified in intent. causal_research.bug_semantics: Ironic globally lowers the per-thread stack size via threading.stack_size() (default 64 KiB at introduction, later 128 KiB) to keep many conductor threads memory-cheap. Python's json parser recurses per nesting level of a JSON document; an unauthenticated attacker can therefore submit a deeply nested crafted JSON payload to an API or JSON-RPC endpoint whose parse recursion exceeds the reduced stack, segfaulting/crashing the API worker process (DoS) until restart. The crash occurs during initial payload parsing, before any validation, and the small default is applied process-wide so any endpoint that deserializes JSON is reachable.

causal_research.bug_semantics: X509Authenticator (and formerly X509AuthenticationListener) implements mTLS pre-authentication: the web server validates the client certificate, then Symfony reads the user identifier from SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email or, if that is missing, from SSL_CLIENT_S_DN via preg_match. From 30b4b3e onward the DN fallback matched emailAddress= anywhere in the string, including inside another RDN value. An attacker who can obtain a certificate from a trusted CA with a free-text CN such as CN=emailAddress=admin@target.example is authenticated as admin@target.example (CWE-290). The 2026 fix requires an RDN boundary (start of string or a comma/slash separator) before emailAddress or OID 1.2.840.113549.1.9.1, so a smuggled substring no longer matches. If the web server sets SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email, the regex path is skipped.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the pulled pre-fix line rather than the advisory's prose, and reproduced both patterns: the pre-fix pattern matches CN=emailAddress=admin@target.example and CN=foo,OU=emailAddress=admin@target.example, and the fixed pattern rejects both; the OID-form payload does not match pre-fix either (that form is a hardening addition, not the defect). mechanism.impact: Authentication as an arbitrary victim identifier with that user's roles and authorization decisions; CVSS v4 VC:N/VI:H from the advisory — integrity of the authenticated session, no confidentiality impact in the scoring.
mechanism.preconditions: Server-side client-certificate validation against a CA the attacker can get a certificate from; the attacker controls only the DN's free-text values; SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email must be unset so the earlier, dedicated-variable branch is skipped; the DN must reach PHP with the embedded text intact (no server-side escaping of the embedded emailAddress= or /).
mechanism.summary: mTLS terminates at the web server, which passes the client certificate's Subject DN to PHP as SSL_CLIENT_S_DN; X509Authenticator::extractUsername() matched emailAddress= anywhere in that string, so an attacker certificate whose CN value smuggles emailAddress=victim@target authenticated as the victim (CWE-290).
mechanism.trigger: The attacker obtains a certificate from a CA the server already trusts and chooses its free-text CN content, e.g. CN=emailAddress=admin@target.example,O=Attacker Corp or CN=foo,OU=emailAddress=admin@target.example,O=Attacker; the server validates the chain and exports the DN to PHP as SSL_CLIENT_S_DN without a dedicated SSL_CLIENT_S_DN_Email variable.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: src/Symfony/Component/Security/Http/Authenticator/X509Authenticator.php:49 extractUsername(), pre-fix content proven by the reverse hunk of 59ef484029 (pre-image revision 29ff9268d0); the identical pattern also sits in the legacy src/Symfony/Component/Security/Http/Firewall/X509AuthenticationListener.php:52 on 5.4.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-863 (incorrect authorization) in SslStream TLS/SSL auth (System.Net.Security): the server-side NegotiateAuthentication (used under NegotiateStream/SslStream secure connections) accepted an ExtendedProtectionPolicy with PolicyEnforcement.Always on platforms where ExtendedProtectionPolicy.OSSupportsExtendedProtection is false (all non-Windows), silently proceeding without channel-binding (CBT)/SPN enforcement; CheckSpn short-circuits to true for secure connections with ProtectionScenario.TransportSelected without verifying an actual channel binding, so the authorization check an app relies on is bypassed. causal_research.bug_semantics: Aiohttp's WebSocket client (ClientSession._ws_connect) installs a WebSocketReader on the upgraded connection. From Per-Message Deflate support onward, the reader treats RSV1 as a permessage-deflate marker and zlib-inflates the payload. The client handshake defaults to compress=0 (no Sec-WebSocket-Extensions offer) and historically constructed WebSocketReader without passing the negotiated compress flag, while the reader defaulted compress=True (and originally accepted RSV1 with no flag at all). A malicious or compromised server can therefore send FIN|RSV1 data frames that the client decompresses despite never negotiating PMCE, consuming CPU and memory (CWE-20). The server path did pass compress=bool(self._compress). Impact is availability-oriented; max_msg_size bounds the assembled payload.

mechanism.summary: A client that never offered permessage-deflate constructs its WebSocketReader without passing `compress`, so the reader's default `compress=True` makes `_compress` true and the RSV1 gate (`rsv1 and not self._compress`) passes un-negotiated compressed frames, which are then zlib-inflated instead of closing with PROTOCOL_ERROR.
mechanism.trigger: Client calls ws_connect() with compress=0 (the default, i.e. no permessage-deflate offer, no Sec-WebSocket-Extensions request header) and the peer sends a data frame with FIN|RSV1 set and a raw-DEFLATE payload.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When better-auth is started without an explicit baseURL (no options.baseURL and no BETTER_AUTH_URL/related env), the first HTTP request may set the process-wide ctx.baseURL. getBaseURL concatenates attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host into a URL string and passes it to withPath(). A proto value such as `some:` yields `some:://junk`, whose WHATWG pathname is `://junk`; a host value with a path (https://junk/poison) likewise injects a non-default pathname. That full URL is stored on the shared AuthContext; the router then does `new URL(ctx.baseURL).pathname` as better-call basePath, so later legitimate /api/auth routes 404 until restart. Persistence comes from assigning getOrigin(ctx.baseURL) onto ctx.options.baseURL, which skips re-inference on subsequent requests.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can place a .svg URL in an OAuth picture claim causes Open WebUI to fetch that URL and persist data:image/svg+xml;base64,... because _process_picture_url infers MIME from the URL extension via mimetypes.guess_type and writes through Users.update_user_profile_image_url_by_id, bypassing validate_profile_image_url on Pydantic forms. Any authenticated user who navigates to GET /api/v1/users/{attacker}/profile/image receives that payload as Content-Type image/svg+xml with Content-Disposition inline and, by default, no CSP or X-Content-Type-Options. The browser treats it as a same-origin SVG document, so onload/script can read localStorage.token and take over the victim account. Before PR #20171 the same endpoint forced image/png, so stored SVG did not execute as a document; after v0.8.0 the form path rejected SVG, leaving OAuth as the remaining write path through v0.9.4.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A repository administrator sets the external issue-tracker URL format to a string containing '{' without a matching '}'. Gogs stores that string unsanitized and, on any later render of an issue index such as '#1', passes it to github.com/unknwon/com.Expand. Expand finds '{' then does i = strings.Index(template, "}") which is -1 and slices template[:i], panicking the request. Pages in that repository that contain issue references become unavailable.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When Signup and CreateUserDir are both enabled, signupHandler copies defaults, clears Scope, and calls Settings.MakeUserDir(username, scope, root). MakeUserDir runs the username through cleanUsername (trim spaces, delete '..', replace any character outside [0-9A-Za-z@_.-] with '-', collapse repeated dashes) and joins that onto UserHomeBasePath. Distinct raw usernames such as teamone/x and teamone-x therefore resolve to the same directory. Username uniqueness is only storm-unique on the raw Username field, MkdirAll is idempotent, and until the fix nothing checked whether another user already owned the derived Scope. The second registrant is stored with the first user's home directory and can read and overwrite that user's files through the normal /api/raw and /api/resources handlers.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When a generic authService is configured with mcpEnabled (and scopesRequired at the auth-service and/or tool level), MCP traffic on /mcp is gated by mcpAuthMiddleware calling ValidateMCPAuth and, from v1.3.0, MCP tools/call additionally checks tool.GetScopesRequired(). The legacy HTTP tool-invocation router is mounted only if --enable-api/EnableAPI is set and never installs that middleware or scope check (internal/server/api.go uses authRequired/GetClaimsFromHeader only). An unauthenticated caller who can reach /api can therefore invoke tools that the operator believed were protected by scopeRequired, which is CWE-863 incorrect authorization rather than a missing HTTP handler.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SSE HTTP transport runs with no authentication and wildcard CORS on every endpoint, and httpServer.listen(port) binds 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces). GET /sse opens an SSE connection returning a session endpoint, and POST /messages?sessionId=<id> invokes any of the 86 exposed GitLab tools (including delete_repository, delete_group, push_files, create_merge_request) using the operator's GITLAB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN. Wildcard CORS enables a browser-tab vector (any visited web page can open an SSE connection and call tools cross-origin). Unauthenticated LAN/cloud/browser callers get full tool access. Fixed in 0.6.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated repository admin collaborator (AccessModeAdmin=3) can POST /{owner}/{repo}/settings/collaboration/access_mode?uid={self_or_other}&mode=4. The collaboration settings route is gated only by RequireRepoAdmin (AccessMode>=Admin). The web handler casts the raw query integer to AccessMode instead of ParseAccessMode. ChangeCollaborationAccessMode accepted any mode in (None, Owner], and AccessModeOwner is 4, so the exclusive upper bound `mode > AccessModeOwner` did not reject 4. The function then persisted mode=4 on the collaboration row and the access row. RepoContext.IsOwner() is AccessMode>=Owner, so the attacker gained owner-only operations (delete repository, transfer ownership, erase wiki). The API collaborator path was not this bug because ParseAccessMode never returns Owner. The intended collaborator set was read/write/admin only.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who supplies an OpenAPI description controls schema property names, discriminator mapping keys, URL-template/default values, and similar strings. Kiota's Ruby CodeMethodWriter emits those values inside generated Ruby double-quoted string literals used as deserializer hash keys, serializer wire names, discriminator case arms, indexer keys, query-name maps, and default assignments. Ruby evaluates #{...}, #$var, and #@var inside double-quoted strings when the generated client runs, so a payload such as #{system('id')} in a wire name or default becomes live code in the generated model. Shared SanitizeForQuotedLiteral/SanitizeDoubleQuote (introduced later for quote/newline breakout) never escaped '#', so the interpolation sink survived until a Ruby-specific sanitizer replaced those calls.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated client with query-execution privilege submits a single SurrealQL statement whose text is a long flat operator spine (example: RETURN 1 + 1 + ... with tens of thousands of terms, well under the HTTP 1 MiB /sql body limit). Parser::pratt_parse_expr walks that spine in an iterative loop and, for each infix/postfix token, calls parse_infix_op / parse_postfix, which boxes a new Expr::Binary { left: Box<Expr>, right: Box<Expr> } (or Prefix/Postfix) onto the left-hand spine. query_recursion_limit and object_recursion_limit only count bracketed/statement nesting, so they stay unused. The resulting tree is later walked with one Rust stack frame per node on Drop, ToSql formatting, and sql::Expr -> expr::Expr lowering; a long enough spine overflows the worker-thread stack and aborts the whole SurrealDB process (availability DoS across every namespace on that instance). Preconditions: query-execution rights; WebSocket /rpc makes the chain easier than HTTP /sql. Counterevidence that this is not a v1 leftover: the nom parser charged depth::dive on each binary operator and recursed on the RHS, so the same chain was rejected as ExcessiveDepth.

Immediate parent 8a0ddf171ed8769c2605bede60faf1052e084dc6 had only binding-power stubs. The merge-queue squash 2755f572fcd5de8f714e70205bf6cfdc4803f7b9 carried that code onto main as an experimental parser; #3762 later added query/object limits that still miss this path; #3801 made parser2 the default. The 3.0 AST (Box<Expr> Binary plus recursive lowering) is a later walk of the same unbounded tree, not the first write.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 1b6e1b9cee to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that v3.1.4 does charge the query-recursion budget once per expression parse at the entry wrappers, so nested queries remain bounded and the unbounded growth is specific to the iterative spine; checked the parent default parser (f7e6e028 lib/src/syn/v1/value/mod.rs:59-70) which recursed per binary operator under depth::dive() (lib/src/syn/v1/depth.rs, DEPTH_PER_DIVE=4 against cnf::MAX_COMPUTATION_DEPTH) and therefore rejected deep chains instead of building them; checked with git grep over the v3.1.4 tree that expr_recursion_limit is absent, so no earlier commit on the line already bounded the spine; and checked that the tree is genuinely walked recursively downstream, which is why bounding the parse alone closes the advisory.
mechanism.impact: One query aborts the entire process during query processing, before any data is read or written: every namespace and database on the instance is unavailable until an external supervisor restarts it (availability-only DoS; CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).
mechanism.preconditions: Authenticated principal with query-execution privilege (guest/record/system, not blocked by --deny-arbitrary-query) able to submit arbitrary SurrealQL; nothing else is required, since the object/query recursion limits (100/20) do not count spine levels and the crash needs no data access.
mechanism.summary: A single authenticated query with tens of thousands of chained operators (for example RETURN 1 + 1 + 1 + ...) is parsed by an iterative pratt loop that appends one AST node per operator without charging any parser depth budget, so the expression tree grows one level per term. The tree is then walked recursively, one call per node, when it is dropped, formatted or lowered for execution, overflowing the thread stack and aborting the whole server process.
mechanism.trigger: One query containing a long flat operator chain, e.g. RETURN 1 + 1 + 1 + ... with tens of thousands of terms, or an equally long chain of postfix operators and method calls, submitted by an authenticated user with query-execution privileges over /sql or over the /rpc transport (WebSocket /rpc accepts larger request bodies and therefore reaches greater chain lengths; the /sql 1 MiB body limit lowers but does not remove the achievable depth).
mechanism.vulnerable_code: surrealdb/core/src/syn/parser/expression.rs:658 pratt_parse_expr (iterative loop at :666; node append via parse_postfix at :674 and parse_infix_op at :693) as shipped in tag v3.1.4; depth charging happens only at the entry wrappers parse_expr_table/parse_expr_field/parse_expr_inherit (:37/:53/:64) through enter_query_recursion! (surrealdb/core/src/syn/parser/mac.rs:92).

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-674 stack-overflow DoS: the pratt parser builds an arbitrarily deep boxed Expr tree from a flat operator chain, then a later recursive walk aborts the process. The smallest first writer of that loop is named-human commit 1b6e1b9 inside squash PR #2885; the immediate parent tree lacks the loop. The minimum fix is 460fcfe57 (backported as 194c407c0 into v3.1.5), which charges a dedicated expr_recursion_limit on every pratt level and spine append. BIC commit-object AI markers are absent (named human, no generator trailers), so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class. Fix-side authorship is also named-human and is not used for attribution.
CVE-2026-63737 (GHSA-q3vg-g3wv-mfgg, alias of the SurrealDB advisory GHSA-jv2j-mqmw-xvv5, fixed in 3.1.5) is a stack-overflow denial of service: one authenticated query with a long flat operator chain builds an expression tree one level per operator, and the over-deep tree is later walked recursively (drop, format, lowering) until the thread stack overflows and the process aborts. The vulnerable code is verified at tag v3.1.4: surrealdb/core/src/syn/parser/expression.rs:658 pratt_parse_expr appends one node per operator inside an iterative loop (:666, postfix append :674, infix append :693), while the parser depth budgets enter_query_recursion (mac.rs:92; query_recursion_limit 20 / object_recursion_limit 100, parser/mod.rs:152-153) are charged once per expression parse, so chain depth is unbounded by construction. The BIC is 2755f572fcd5de8f714e70205bf6cfdc4803f7b9 (Introduce new experimental parser, PR #2885), which first adds lib/src/syn/v2/parser/expression.rs containing that iterative loop; its immediate parent f7e6e028a20af569865f2f684e3cff41f01f7a32 has no such file, and the parent default v1 parser charged depth::dive() per binary-operator recursion (value/mod.rs:59-70), so the unbounded-spine behaviour is absent in the parent. The iterative parser was later promoted to the only/default parser by e84251588257f5969571cb3a970e774c7728dc18 (Drop the old parser, PR #3814), which is exposure rather than a new introduction. The minimal repair is 194c407c0f4afbfe0b0d83c7f734f9d8e83b49b9 (fix(syn): bound expression operator-tree depth to prevent stack-overflow DoS, PR #384), contained in tag v3.1.5 and absent from v3.1.4, with 460fcfe572a5df55237038f92af5dc1b839a9cbf as the equivalent change on main (v3.2.0). Neither BIC-side commit object (2755f572f, e84251588) nor either fix commit carries any AI/agent marker, so the defect is human-authored and the verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The vantage6 server generates a fallback JWT signing key when the user does not set jwt_secret_key in the server config. The auto-generated fallback used Python's uuid.uuid1(), which derives from the machine MAC address and timestamp, so the key is predictable rather than cryptographically random. An attacker who can predict the UUID1 (e.g., knowledge of the host MAC address and approximate boot/startup time) can forge valid JWT tokens and bypass authentication of the privacy-preserving computation server.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory reference commit e39a262faf1cd4c554bf1b8e57eeea082da995c0 (merge 'Use truly random generator for the JWT server secret key') contains atomic fix 273f8fe70529f8853a6bd62274ecf40175387208 changing str(uuid.uuid1()) -> str(uuid.uuid4()) at vantage6-server/vantage6/server/__init__.py:305. git log -L on the JWT_SECRET_KEY lines shows the line's write history: 5ed8de221 (first wrote uuid1 fallback, in pytaskmanager/server/__init__.py) -> cc7c3adaa (2020-11-19 move into configure, carried) -> 7efa098b6 (2020-11-23 move into ServerApp method, carried) -> 4b8e907e8 (2024-01-19 black formatting, carried) -> 273f8fe70 (fix). git grep at parent b0fdd8ee confirms no uuid.uuid1 in the JWT secret config there (only unrelated API-key uuid1 in fixtures.py and resource/node.py). causal_research.mechanism: An actor able to supply text stored in a victim-used budget can influence name/value cells exported by the CLI. Authenticated budget selection and the registered payee list route reach the API read, printOutput, formatCsv, and syntax-only escapeCsv. The pre-fix serializer preserves formula-significant string content. If the victim selects CSV and imports it with formula evaluation enabled, budget data can become active spreadsheet cell content. This is a data-to-formula trust-boundary violation; budget-writing permission is not permission to execute spreadsheet formulas. The outcome depends on spreadsheet semantics and import options. No CLI code execution, automatic external disclosure, or universal cross-client impact was established.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Context isolation bypass via prototype hijack (CVE-2026-70601 / GHSA-h7rp-cf8h-j98x). In CreateProxyForAPI() of shell/renderer/api/electron_api_context_bridge.cc, the object-copy loop that mirrors an API object from the isolated preload context into the main world used v8::Object::Set(proxy.Set(key, value)) instead of an own-property definition. Because Set follows ordinary-set semantics, setting an own key named "__proto__" invoked the inherited Object.prototype.__proto__ setter on the freshly created plain proxy object, mutating its [[Prototype]] to whatever object the bridge just copied for that key. An untrusted page could therefore pass a payload with an own enumerable __proto__ key through a Promise-returning contextBridge function (the standard ipcRenderer.invoke wrapper pattern) or through exposeInMainWorld itself and hijack the prototype of objects materialized in the other realm; chaining this gives web content access into the isolated preload world and every capability the preload script has, escalating to Node.js in unsandboxed renderers or when nodeIntegration is enabled. Fixed by replacing Set with v8::Object::CreateDataProperty so __proto__ becomes an own data property.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Local privilege escalation via 'as-user' option spoofing in org.freedesktop.UDisks2.Filesystem.Mount() (CWE-863). handle_mount() derives caller_uid from the caller-supplied 'as-user' user name; in handle_mount_fstab() the polkit authorization block (including 'filesystem-mount-other-user') was inside the branch skipped when fstab options 'user'/'users'/'x-udisks-auth' are present, so an unprivileged console caller could mount on behalf of arbitrary users including privileged accounts; additionally a root fallback on BD_FS_ERROR_AUTH was available with 'user'/'users'. Fixed in udisks-2.11.2 by reworking fstab mount authorization (always enforce filesystem-mount-other-user when caller_uid != effective_uid, gate root fallback on x-udisks-auth, separate real caller identity from as-user target, pass as-user target to polkit details).

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-732: umask-dependent native DI credential persistence permits other local principals to read account credentials when ancestor traversal is allowed.
causal_research.mechanism:
In released 0.3.4, `Garmin.login` accepts an explicit tokenstore or GARMINTOKENS. A tokenstore string longer than 512 characters goes to `loads`, without this filesystem write. A short path is normalized and attempted through `Client.load`. On failed cache loading, ordinary successful credential login assigns `_tokenstore_path` and calls `Client.dump`; refresh also dumps when that path is set. MFA early-return/resume branches are distinct and do not imply the same immediate persistence. Examples choose `~/.garminconnect`. The actual serialization contains `di_token`, `di_refresh_token`, `di_client_id`.

The old writer selects `garmin_tokens.json` for a directory-style path (or uses an explicit .json filename), invokes mode-less `p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`, then `p.write_text(self.dumps())`. On new POSIX storage with umask 022, this yields 0755/0644. Other users can read the credentials when ancestor traversal and effective ACLs permit it. A private home or token directory prevents that access; sharing a machine alone does not establish exposure. Restrictive umask 077 protects newly created storage, but does not retroactively fix an existing 0644 file or 0755 directory. Our checks distinguish these cases. A single-user installation removes the described other-user adversary, not the insecure modes themselves.

Receipts: source-0.3.4-garminconnect_client.py.stdout, source-0.3.4-garminconnect___init__.py.stdout, source-0.3.4-example.py.stdout, and digest-verified archive members sdist-0.3.4-garminconnect_client.py and sdist-0.3.4-garminconnect___init__.py. AST-extracted dump/load checks establish local mode behavior without importing product networking code. They are method-level tests, not live login integration tests.

+"""Security regression tests for token-store file permissions.
+
+Guards against GHSA-wjhr-76vg-2hvc: ``Client.dump()`` must write the token
+file (which holds the DI refresh token) owner-only (0o600) inside an
+owner-only directory (0o700), regardless of the process umask, so it can't be
+left world-readable on a shared host.
+
+POSIX-only — file mode bits are not meaningful on Windows.
+"""
+
+import os
+import stat
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from garminconnect.client import Client
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="POSIX file modes only")
+
+
+def _make_client() -> Client:
+    c = Client()
+    c.di_token = "ACCESS_TOKEN_EXAMPLE"
+    c.di_refresh_token = "REFRESH_TOKEN_EXAMPLE"
+    c.di_client_id = "CLIENT_ID_EXAMPLE"
+    return c
+
+
+def _mode(path) -> int:
+    return stat.S_IMODE(Path(path).stat().st_mode)
+
+
+def test_dump_creates_owner_only_token_file(tmp_path):
+    """Under a permissive umask the token file must still be 0o600."""
+    old_umask = os.umask(0o022)
+    try:
+        token_dir = tmp_path / "tokens"
+        _make_client().dump(str(token_dir))
+        token_file = token_dir / "garmin_tokens.json"
+
+        assert _mode(token_file) == 0o600, oct(_mode(token_file))
+        assert _mode(token_dir) == 0o700, oct(_mode(token_dir))
+        # World/group bits must be clear
+        assert not (_mode(token_file) & (stat.S_IRWXG | stat.S_IRWXO))
+        assert not (_mode(token_dir) & (stat.S_IRWXG | stat.S_IRWXO))
+    finally:
+        os.umask(old_umask)
+
+
+def test_dump_tightens_preexisting_loose_permissions(tmp_path):
+    """A pre-existing world-readable dir/file is tightened on dump."""
+    old_umask = os.umask(0o022)
+    try:
+        token_dir = tmp_path / "tokens"
+        token_dir.mkdir(mode=0o755)
+        token_file = token_dir / "garmin_tokens.json"
+        token_file.write_text("{}")
+        token_file.chmod(0o644)
+
+        _make_client().dump(str(token_dir))
+
+        assert _mode(token_file) == 0o600, oct(_mode(token_file))
+        assert _mode(token_dir) == 0o700, oct(_mode(token_dir))
+    finally:
+        os.umask(old_umask)
+
+
+def test_dump_explicit_json_path(tmp_path):
+    """A direct ``*.json`` path is also written owner-only."""
+    old_umask = os.umask(0o022)
+    try:
+        token_file = tmp_path / "store" / "garmin_tokens.json"
+        _make_client().dump(str(token_file))
+        assert _mode(token_file) == 0o600, oct(_mode(token_file))
+    finally:
+        os.umask(old_umask)

comparison_hunks.code:
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+"""Security regression tests for token-store file permissions.
+
+Guards against GHSA-wjhr-76vg-2hvc: ``Client.dump()`` must write the token
+file (which holds the DI refresh token) owner-only (0o600) inside an
+owner-only directory (0o700), regardless of the process umask, so it can't be
+left world-readable on a shared host.
+
+POSIX-only — file mode bits are not meaningful on Windows.
+"""
+
+import os
+import stat
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from garminconnect.client import Client
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="POSIX file modes only")
+
+
+def _make_client() -> Client:
+    c = Client()
+    c.di_token = "ACCESS_TOKEN_EXAMPLE"
+    c.di_refresh_token = "REFRESH_TOKEN_EXAMPLE"
+    c.di_client_id = "CLIENT_ID_EXAMPLE"
+    return c
+
+
+def _mode(path) -> int:
+    return stat.S_IMODE(Path(path).stat().st_mode)
+
+
+def test_dump_creates_owner_only_token_file(tmp_path):
+    """Under a permissive umask the token file must still be 0o600."""
+    old_umask = os.umask(0o022)
+    try:
+        token_dir = tmp_path / "tokens"
+        _make_client().dump(str(token_dir))
+        token_file = token_dir / "garmin_tokens.json"
+
+        assert _mode(token_file) == 0o600, oct(_mode(token_file))
+        assert _mode(token_dir) == 0o700, oct(_mode(token_dir))
+        # World/group bits must be clear
+        assert not (_mode(token_file) & (stat.S_IRWXG | stat.S_IRWXO))
+        assert not (_mode(token_dir) & (stat.S_IRWXG | stat.S_IRWXO))
+    finally:
+        os.umask(old_umask)
+
+
+def test_dump_tightens_preexisting_loose_permissions(tmp_path):
+    """A pre-existing world-readable dir/file is tightened on dump."""
+    old_umask = os.umask(0o022)
+    try:
+        token_dir = tmp_path / "tokens"
+        token_dir.mkdir(mode=0o755)
+        token_file = token_dir / "garmin_tokens.json"
+        token_file.write_text("{}")
+        token_file.chmod(0o644)
+
+        _make_client().dump(str(token_dir))
+
+        assert _mode(token_file) == 0o600, oct(_mode(token_file))
+        assert _mode(token_dir) == 0o700, oct(_mode(token_dir))
+    finally:
+        os.umask(old_umask)
+
+
+def test_dump_explicit_json_path(tmp_path):
+    """A direct ``*.json`` path is also written owner-only."""
+    old_umask = os.umask(0o022)
+    try:
+        token_file = tmp_path / "store" / "garmin_tokens.json"
+        _make_client().dump(str(token_file))
+        assert _mode(token_file) == 0o600, oct(_mode(token_file))
+    finally:
+        os.umask(old_umask)
comparison_hunks.annotation: Adds POSIX regression tests asserting the token directory and file are written with owner-only modes even under a permissive umask, and that existing loose permissions are tightened on dump.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the OAuth credential connect flow. Source is the user-controlled OAuth2 Authorization URL (credential data field authUrl on type oAuth2Api / types that extend it). The backend authorize endpoint builds ClientOAuth2Options.authorizationUri from that field and returns CodeFlow.getUri() to the editor. Sink is oAuthCredentialAuthorize in CredentialEdit.vue, which assigns that string to window.open without restricting the URL protocol. A javascript: / data: / vbscript: payload therefore runs in the victim's n8n origin when they click the OAuth authorization control on a crafted (typically shared) credential, enabling session-token theft and API actions as the victim. The 2026-02-02 #25170 fix allowlists http/https on both the popup path and credential save/authorize.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-639 IDOR in the Maatwebsite Excel ToModel handlers. causal_research.bug_semantics: The FFI trampolines wrap OpenSSL PSK and cookie-generate callbacks. They build a bounded &mut [u8] over OpenSSL's output buffer and invoke a user Fn that returns Result<usize, _>. Before the fix, an Ok(len) was stored or cast and given back to OpenSSL with no len <= slice.len() check. A safe closure can therefore claim it filled more bytes than the slice allowed. OpenSSL then reads past the end of the PSK/cookie buffer and puts those adjacent bytes on the network (TLS PSK exchange or DTLS HelloVerifyRequest). On 64-bit targets, `psk_len as u32` truncation can also make an oversize PSK length look legal to OpenSSL's PSK_MAX_PSK_LEN check. Cookie generate is additionally off-by-one versus OpenSSL's DTLS1_COOKIE_LENGTH buffer, so returning buf.len()+1 passes OpenSSL's own bound.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The advisory pattern (slice in, unchecked usize out) was first written in 4de58596d930559f90cb96a993415ebc0b0ce876 while addressing review comments on PR #641. The immediate parent 16183f41 used a Vec-returning callback and unchecked ptr::copy, which is a different defect. 4de58596 replaced that with from_raw_parts_mut slices plus `Ok(psk_len) => psk_len as u32`. The merge 279bffcc only landed that branch. A later file move, the 2018 server-PSK trampoline, and the 2018 cookie trampolines copied the same missing bound check; they are later exposure of the same mechanism, not a new BIC.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 4de58596d9 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the fix parent directly: all four arms are unguarded and no earlier clamp exists in the tree; confirmed the four public setters map to exactly these four trampolines at 1d109020^ (mod.rs:1360, 1392, 1501, 1541); confirmed the fix's regression tests drive oversize returns (psk_len and Ok(buf.len()+1)) through the public setters, so the mechanism is reachable from safe application code; no OpenSSL-side clamping of the returned length exists, which is why the fix has to return 0 to abort the exchange.
mechanism.impact: Out-of-bounds read by libssl over the PSK/cookie buffer: for PSK the oversize length names more bytes than the slice holds, and for the cookie setters *cookie_len is copied into the HelloVerifyRequest cookie sent to the network peer, disclosing up to (returned - capacity) bytes of adjacent process memory to a remote peer (CWE-126 buffer over-read, CWE-130 improper handling of length parameter inconsistency; CVSS v4 AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/VC:H).
mechanism.preconditions: The application must use one of the four builder setters, its closure must return an oversize length (expressible entirely in safe Rust, no unsafe needed), and a peer must reach the callback path; the attacker controls the remote peer, while the oversize return is an application-programming defect that the safe API failed to contain, hence the advisory's AT:P (attack requirements present).
mechanism.summary: An application registers one of set_psk_client_callback / set_psk_server_callback / set_cookie_generate_cb / set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb; the trampoline builds a bounded &mut [u8] (max_psk_len, SSL_COOKIE_LENGTH, or DTLS1_COOKIE_LENGTH-1) and calls the safe closure, which may return any usize; the trampoline forwards that usize to OpenSSL as the produced length without comparing it to the slice, so OpenSSL reads past the buffer and the over-read bytes are serialised into the handshake data sent to the peer.
mechanism.trigger: The peer drives the handshake path that invokes the registered callback (TLS PSK client-hello processing for the two PSK setters, the stateless-cookie HelloVerifyRequest exchange for set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb, the DTLS cookie exchange for set_cookie_generate_cb), and the application closure returns a length larger than the slice it was handed, e.g. Ok(buf.len() + 1) as used in the fix's own regression tests.

causal_research.reasoning:
The GHSA/CVE describes a real, still-reproducible library bug: trampolines trusted a safe callback's usize against a bounded OpenSSL buffer. That pattern was first written by named human Ted Mielczarek in 4de58596 in 2017, confirmed absent in the immediate parent, then merged via PR #641. Later human commits copied it into server-PSK and cookie trampolines. The 2026 fix 1d109020 clamps all four surfaces and is in openssl-v0.10.78, not 0.10.77. Claude is a co-author of the fix only. Protocol requires BIC-object AI for an AI verdict; the BIC object has none, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
Four FFI trampolines (raw_client_psk, raw_server_psk, raw_stateless_cookie_generate, raw_cookie_generate) handed the application closure a bounded &mut [u8] but forwarded the closure's returned usize to OpenSSL as the data length with no clamp, so a closure returning more than the slice length makes OpenSSL read past the buffer and serialise adjacent memory to the peer; commit 1d109020 fixes all four by guarding len <= cap and returning 0 otherwise, and it is the version that first ships as openssl-v0.10.78. The introducing changes are named-human commits from 2017-2018: the client-PSK forwarding born in 4de58596 (Ted Mielczarek, first released in openssl-v0.9.24, matching the advisory's introduced range; parent 16183f41 has no such arm) plus the three sibling sites e04dbfa3, bbb1cb61 and 47a68e29 (Benjamin Saunders, Benjamin Saunders, Benjamin Cheng), each verified absent from its immediate parent. No BIC-side commit object carries a generative-AI trailer or an AI identity, and all four predate LLM code generation by years. The only AI marker in the case is the fix-side trailer on 1d109020 (Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7), which the batch rule records as informational and which cannot turn a human BIC into an AI verdict. Verdict would flip only if a BIC-side commit object (introduction, landing merge 279bffcc, or a later commit newly exposing the defect) carried a recovered AI marker or identity.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When the Vite dev server is exposed on the network and WebSocket is enabled, an unauthenticated client can connect to the HMR WebSocket (including with no Origin header) and emit a custom vite:invoke RPC. causal_research.bug_semantics: On Windows, the Ollama desktop app periodically calls the update API, downloads an installer to the staging directory, and later executes that .exe with Inno Setup silent flags. From the first Windows updater through v0.23.2 there is no Authenticode or publisher check on the payload: DownloadNewRelease writes whatever bytes the HTTP response body contains, and DoUpgrade execs the first staged *.exe. After the 2025 app rewrite the Windows verifyDownload hook exists but unconditionally returns nil, while Darwin actually verifies the bundle; CERT/CVE describe that stub. An attacker who can supply the update bytes (compromised update host, or adjacent-network influence per CVSS AV:A/AT:P) therefore stages and silently runs arbitrary code as the logged-in user.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Qwik City origin-based CSRF middleware (csrfCheckMiddleware) is installed by default (checkOrigin ?? true) on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE. It calls isContentType() and only then compares the Origin header to the server origin. isContentType took headers.get('content-type')?.split(/;,/, 1)[0].trim(). The regex /;,/ matches a semicolon immediately followed by a comma, so it does not strip RFC 9110 parameters such as '; boundary=...' or '; charset=UTF-8'. A cross-site browser multipart POST therefore presents Content-Type 'multipart/form-data; boundary=...' which does not equal 'multipart/form-data', isForm is false, and the Origin mismatch is never enforced. The attacker can submit a forged multipart form that performs a Qwik action/state change. Preconditions: checkOrigin left at default true; a mutating form endpoint; attacker can induce a cross-origin form POST (typical UI:R). Counterevidence: text/plain without parameters still matched; parent-of-BIC CSRF checked Origin on all POSTs and could not be skipped this way.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A record user with UPDATE on a document issues an UPDATE that applies an incompatible arithmetic operator or extend against a field that field-level SELECT permissions hide (example: UPDATE person:me SET probe = email + 1 when email is a string). UPDATE permission checks evaluate the unreduced document, so the hidden field is a live operand. Value::try_add (and try_sub/try_mul/try_div/try_pow/try_neg/try_rem/extend) then bail with Error::TryAdd(v.to_raw_string(), w.to_raw_string()) (and siblings), whose thiserror text is Cannot perform addition with '{0}' and '{1}'. The raw operand, including the hidden field value, is returned to the caller. One field per failing operation; the caller can repeat.

causal_research.bug_semantics: BlenderMCPServer.download_polyhaven_asset (addon.py, asset_type=models) fetches a JSON file listing from api.polyhaven.com and treats each key of file_info['include'] as a relative path under tempfile.mkdtemp(). Those keys are concatenated with os.path.join(temp_dir, include_path) and the corresponding include URL bytes are written with open(..., 'wb') after os.makedirs on the dirname. There is no abspath/normpath containment check, so a key such as '../../.bashrc' or an absolute path writes outside the temp directory as the Blender process user. The keys are attacker-controlled via a malicious or MITM'd Poly Haven files API response, or via an MCP prompt-injection that causes the LLM to call the download_polyhaven_asset tool. causal_research.bug_semantics: A safe caller of MdCtxRef::digest_final(&mut [u8]) after digest_init/digest_update can pass a slice shorter than the digest output size. The wrapper records out.len() in a u32 and calls OpenSSL EVP_DigestFinal, which ignores that value as a capacity and always writes EVP_MD_CTX_size(ctx) bytes to out.as_mut_ptr(). The write overflows the caller buffer (typically a stack array), which is memory unsafety from safe Rust (CWE-121/buffer overflow). Hasher::finish is not this bug: it allocates EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE itself.

mechanism.preconditions: The caller must supply a slice shorter than the digest size; the pre-fix API documents no minimum length and performs no check, so any such call is undefined behaviour. Remote exploitability requires a downstream caller that sizes the buffer from untrusted data.
mechanism.summary: A caller passes an out buffer shorter than the digest size (e.g. 16 bytes with SHA-256); digest_final forwards out.as_mut_ptr() and a len derived from out.len() to EVP_DigestFinal, which writes EVP_MD_CTX_size(ctx) bytes to that pointer regardless, overrunning the caller buffer (usually the stack) with no unsafe needed at the call site.
mechanism.trigger: Safe-Rust call to MdCtxRef::digest_final(&mut self, out: &mut [u8]) where out.len() < EVP_MD_CTX_size(ctx) for the initialized digest.

causal_research.bug_semantics: OS command injection / blocklist bypass (CWE-77/CWE-78) in DesktopCommanderMCP's CommandManager.validateCommand (src/command-manager.ts): the blocklist check only compares the first whitespace-separated token (command.split(' ')[0], later getBaseCommand) against config.blockedCommands. Chained commands (';', '&&', '||', '|'), subshells '(...)', command substitution '$()' and backticks, env-var prefixes, and absolute paths (e.g. /usr/bin/sudo) evade the check, so a low-privilege MCP client can execute commands the user explicitly blocked. executeCommand in src/tools/execute.ts enforces validateCommand before running the command. Fixed by PR #323 (recurse into $()/backticks, path.basename normalization, skip env vars) and hardened by PR #352 (fail closed on validation errors instead of allow).

OSV CVE-2025-11491 range: introduced b8d83310 (v0.2.0), last_affected 7f7c0e4e (v0.2.13; advisory understated, vuln actually persisted to v0.2.32). Vulnerable code at 7f7c0e4e: validateCommand -> extractCommands/extractBaseCommand; extractBaseCommand returns first token with no path stripping and no $()/backtick recursion; extractCommands skips over subshells and treats quoted text as literal. Introducer: git log --follow src/command-manager.ts first commit f396f08 (2024-12-16, eduardruzga, 'Updates'); parent 45fa26d1ab992c34a2f5b044fd2add844f2d8fbe has no src/command-manager.ts ('fatal: path exists on disk, but not in f396f08^') -> introducer_parent_absent True. Fix 5a85904 'fix command blocklist bypass via absolute paths and command substitution (#323)' (Dhiego Pagotto, 2026-02-01) adds $() and backtick extraction, path.basename() stripping, env-var skipping; message references fixes #218 (absolute path) and #217 (command substitution). Hardening 7090a5d 'security: fail closed when command validation errors (#352)' (Peter J McDade, 2026-02-24) changes the catch path from allow to deny. AI-marker scans (co-authored/assisted-by/anthropic/claude/copilot/codex/openai/grok) on f396f08, bb7fb63, 5d346e4, 5a85904: none. 7090a5d has 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>' x2 + 'Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6' - but 7090a5d is a post-bypass hardening FIX, not the introducer.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Human-authored commit f396f08 'Updates' (eduardruzga, wonderwhy.er@gmail.com, 2024-12-16) created src/command-manager.ts with the naive blocklist check 'const baseCommand = command.split(' ')[0].toLowerCase().trim(); return !this.blockedCommands.has(baseCommand)' and wired validateCommand into executeCommand; parent 45fa26d has no src/command-manager.ts. Later human commits (bb7fb63 2025-04-01, 5d346e4 2025-04-10) extended the extraction logic for analytics but the flawed first-token-only comparison persisted.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerable first-token-only blocklist comparison was first written by human commit f396f08 (2024-12-16) with no AI markers and evolved through human commits; the primary fix 5a85904 (PR #323) is also human-authored with no markers. Claude Opus 4.6 markers appear only on the later fail-closed hardening commit 7090a5d, which is a fix-side change and cannot make AI the root cause. Per the rule 'AI marker on the FIX of a human-introduced flaw -> NOT_AI', verdict NOT_AI.
