mechanism.counterevidence: Searched the pre-fix tree for a hidden bound: grep for pause/resume/backpress/water/limit/len(self._messages) in 5e898429:aiohttp/web_protocol.py returned no flow-control code, so the deque is genuinely unbounded. Verified the queue is not a pre-existing container by comparing the introducing child with its immediate parent b521674037d17ecc7849040ae12075a3884ec87b, whose server.py has only _request_handlers. Checked the version boundary: dfdfa9d5 is an ancestor of v3.14.1 (bc57b1751b5374f4d0342375c5d6e2b92004bcb0) and not of v3.14.0 (1fd3aa8adbb01bd604febc22ad84f94c279b1c82), matching the advisory. Considered that pipelining predates the queue (08a162147f0f5ce4c37542bc07f6afef9440ca1f), but that revision runs per-chunk handler tasks and leaves buffering to the stream reader, whose feed_data pauses the transport above its watermark.
mechanism.impact: Memory exhaustion / denial of service on the server process; the per-connection backlog is unbounded, so a single client sets the growth rate. CWE-770, CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VA:H, MODERATE.
mechanism.preconditions: Attacker can open a TCP connection to an affected aiohttp server (all versions on the 3.14 line before 3.14.1; advisory range introduced 0 / fixed 3.14.1, last known affected <= 3.14.0). No authentication or special negotiation is required; the handler must stay busy long enough for the client to have more requests parsed than the server drains.
mechanism.summary: A client opens one HTTP/1.1 connection and pipelines complete requests while the first request's handler is still running; aiohttp parses every additional request eagerly and appends (msg, payload) to RequestHandler._messages with no size limit and no transport backpressure, so the per-connection backlog and process memory grow with pipeline depth until the worker is starved (CWE-770, CVSS 4.0 VA:H).
mechanism.trigger: One attacker-controlled connection sends N complete pipelined HTTP/1.1 requests without waiting for responses while the application handler for the in-flight request stays busy (slow endpoint, blocked write, or simply a deep pipeline); each parsed request is appended to the unbounded _messages deque instead of being handed to a handler.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: aiohttp/web_protocol.py:244 RequestHandler._messages = deque(); append sites aiohttp/web_protocol.py:457 in data_received and aiohttp/web_protocol.py:738 in finish_response at 5e898429965eb98fad3525caed30640ac2b10fdf; origin aiohttp/server.py:128 (_messages deque), :132 (_waiters) and :312 (unguarded append) at 045dd8c4bfeae50ae92d1f32e06126ead6629443.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-770: HTTP/1 pipelined requests were parsed and queued per connection with no limit, which is DoS via memory. The smallest first writer of that queue is named-human commit 045dd8c4bfeae50ae92d1f32e06126ead6629443; its parent tree lacks the queue. The defect is closed by bounding emission and pausing the transport (master 93a2b1c369d69ca6fcdabea9a7c29cfc7947817c, 3.14.1 dfdfa9d5aad5d21f91c79fb2ceeba0f8046cb6cf). The BIC commit object has no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Fix-side review bots do not attribute the introducer.
GHSA-4fvr-rgm6-gqmc (CVE-2026-54273, CWE-770) describes aiohttp queueing pipelined HTTP/1.1 requests without a limit, so one client that keeps a handler busy can grow server memory until denial of service. The defect is real in the state the advisory's patch fixes: at 5e898429965eb98fad3525caed30640ac2b10fdf, aiohttp/web_protocol.py declares RequestHandler._messages as a bare deque (line 244), appends parsed requests in data_received (line 457) and finish_response (line 738), and contains no pause, resume, watermark or queue-size check anywhere. The smallest original introduction is 045dd8c4bfeae50ae92d1f32e06126ead6629443 ('refactor htpp message parsing', 2017-02-10): it creates _messages and _waiters and appends (msg, payload) whenever no handler slot is free, while its immediate parent b521674037d17ecc7849040ae12075a3884ec87b has neither container. Pipelining itself is older (08a162147f0f5ce4c37542bc07f6afef9440ca1f), but that model queued handler tasks and left incoming bytes to the stream reader's transport pause_reading backpressure, so an unbounded queue of parsed requests is new in 045dd8c4b, and later commits only move the construct (9cfa4fe39e2a3b8fe4e7052f8dda02a7adfe2123 creates aiohttp/web_protocol.py with the same bare deque()). The minimum fix is the advisory's patch dfdfa9d5aad5d21f91c79fb2ceeba0f8046cb6cf, the 3.14 backport of master 93a2b1c369d69ca6fcdabea9a7c29cfc7947817c (PR #12830), which caps the per-connection queue at MAX_MSG_QUEUE_SIZE=32 with parser accounting and transport pause/resume and is contained in v3.14.1 but not v3.14.0. The BIC commit object is a named human contribution (author and committer Nikolay Kim <nikolay.kim@affirm.com>, no trailer), so the causal evidence reads human and the verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A WebTransport peer sends an unknown capsule on the HTTP/3 CONNECT request stream with a large declared length. Session.parseNextCapsule (v0.11.0 session.go:147-175) calls http3.ParseCapsule, which returns a reader limited only by that declared length, then in the default branch runs io.ReadAll(r), allocating a contiguous buffer for the entire body. Reading the stream advances QUIC flow control, so the sender can keep filling the window while the receiver retains the bytes. Impact is memory exhaustion / DoS on client or server. Preconditions: established WebTransport session and a peer able to write capsules on the request stream. Counterevidence considered: CLOSE_SESSION is separately length-capped (maxCloseCapsuleErrorMsgLen) and is a different advisory; io.Copy/Discard after the fix does not retain the body.

mechanism.counterevidence: QUIC flow control limits buffered-but-unread stream data, but reading advances the flow-control window while io.ReadAll retains the consumed bytes, so total allocation is not bounded by the window (the advisory states this explicitly and the code confirms the read loop). The WT_CLOSE_SESSION message read used the same unbounded io.ReadAll in b9f56e5 but was separately bounded to 1024 bytes by 89a8061 (#202, 2025-12-22) with io.LimitReader, so that sibling path cannot be used to extend this mechanism; bounded capsule parsers (parseMaxDataCapsule etc.) check Remaining() and are not affected.
mechanism.impact: Excessive memory allocation on the receiving endpoint, leading to crash or resource exhaustion (DoS; CVSS:3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L).
mechanism.preconditions: The receiver runs the capsule parse loop on the session's request stream (Session.handleConn -> parseNextCapsule); the peer controls the request stream and may declare any capsule length, since the commit carried a '// TODO: enforce max size' comment and no cap was enforced.
mechanism.summary: A peer sends an unknown capsule type on the HTTP/3 request stream with an arbitrarily large declared body; the receiver's parse loop hits the unknown-capsule branch and calls io.ReadAll on the capsule body reader (bounded only by the declared length), retaining the full payload in memory until the capsule is consumed, which allows unbounded allocation and a memory-exhaustion DoS.
mechanism.trigger: The attacker (either a server attacking a client or a client attacking a server) sends a capsule whose type is not one of the known WT_* types and whose declared body length is very large, then streams the full body.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: session.go:169-173 Session.parseNextCapsule (default branch, at v0.11.0; introduced by b9f56e5; at HEAD the equivalent lives in capsule.go:90)

causal_research.bug_semantics: Network-AI ApprovalInbox (lib/approval-inbox.ts) is the HTTP surface of the human-in-the-loop ApprovalGate. Source: an unauthenticated GET to the inbox (default pathPrefix /approvals) — GET /?status=all, GET /:id, GET /stats, GET /sse. Sink: routeRequest() returns JSON/SSE of ApprovalEntry objects, including request.action/target (shell-command strings), file paths, justification, and riskLevel, with no checkAuth() call on those branches. After v5.12.2 an operator can set options.secret, which checkAuth() enforces only on POST /:id/approve and POST /:id/deny (constant-time Bearer). GET read routes skip that gate, so a configured secret does not stop disclosure. httpHandler() and addSSEClient() also set Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so any website the operator visits can read those responses. This residual is an incomplete fix of GHSA-mxjx-28vx-xjjj (which had already documented the GET disclosure). Closed in v5.13.4 by gating the entire routeRequest() pipeline with checkAuth() and replacing wildcard CORS with an explicit allowedOrigins allowlist.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An actor who can create or edit a watch (any network client when no password/API key is set, which is the product default; otherwise an authenticated user) supplies an include filter such as jq:env or jqraw:env. changedetectionio/html_tools.py _parse_json compiles that string with the Python jq bindings and runs it against fetched JSON. jq's env/$ENV builtins ignore the JSON input and return the server process environment. causal_research.bug_semantics: React Router Framework Mode single-fetch (and Remix Single Fetch) encodes server Errors into a turbo-stream .data body. turbo-stream v2 serializes a non-default Error.name and, on decode, does `new globalThis[errorType](message)` with no allowlist. React Router also copies that pattern in the SanitizedError plugin (`global[name]` constructor lookup). If errorType/name is attacker-controlled (reflected user input on an Error, a crafted stream, or any encode path that skips production sanitizeError), the client/runtime can invoke arbitrary global constructors such as Function or large typed-array/ArrayBuffer allocators, causing denial of service (CWE-770). Declarative/Data modes are out of scope per the GHSA.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When FrankenPHP runs a worker, php_request_startup runs once and the worker script loops on frankenphp_handle_request, so EG(symbol_table) is reused. session_start() stores $_SESSION in that symbol table as a reference to PS(http_session_vars). PHP session RSHUTDOWN decrements the session zval but leaves the _SESSION key in the symbol table. Until 24d6c99, worker recycle (frankenphp_reset_super_globals and its predecessors) reimported other autoglobals and only set $_SESSION's auto_global armed=0, so a subsequent client on the same worker that reads $_SESSION before session_start() observes the previous request's session payload (tokens, user ids, PII). Impact is cross-request confidentiality leakage and possible logic/impersonation bugs; preconditions are worker mode and application code that inspects $_SESSION before re-initializing the session.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In the App Router, next/script with strategy=beforeInteractive does not emit a native deferred <script src>. Instead Script() copies remaining props (including attacker-controlled string attributes and, for inline scripts, children / dangerouslySetInnerHTML.__html) through JSON.stringify into an inline script body: (self.__next_s=self.__next_s||[]).push(...), assigned via dangerouslySetInnerHTML. JSON.stringify does not encode '<' or '</script>'. When untrusted input is forwarded as a Script prop, the HTML tokenizer can close the intended script element and run a following attacker script in the visitor's origin (CWE-79). The same embedding style for RSC flight data already used htmlEscapeJsonString; this path did not. causal_research.bug_semantics: Shopware overrides Twig map/reduce/filter/sort in SecurityExtension so only allowlisted PHP function names run. After CVE-2023-2017, array callables were implode'd to 'Class::method' and then checked with the string allowlist. A 6.7 map() rewrite deleted that implode and gated on is_callable() instead. A template such as {{ values|map(['\\Some\\Class','method']) }} (or a context variable holding that array) is is_callable, is not a string, skips allowedPHPFunctions, and is invoked as $function($value, $key), which is arbitrary PHP static-method execution (CWE-94). Trigger requires a high-privilege actor who can supply Twig (admin / mail templates / themes). reduce/filter/sort were not regressed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Weblate enforces repository boundaries by asking whether a resolved absolute path string starts with the repository root string. In Repository.resolve_symlinks (weblate/vcs/base.py) the code does real_path = realpath(join(repo, path)) and repository_path = realpath(repo), then allows the path unless `not real_path.startswith(repository_path)`. That test is not path-segment-aware: `/data/repo_outside/secrets.po`.startswith(`/data/repo`) is true, so a symlink or Windows junction inside the component repository that points at a sibling directory sharing the repo prefix is accepted. Callers treat a non-raising result as proof the original in-repo path is in-tree: Component.check_file_is_valid returns that filename; translation discovery, add-on writes (addons/base.py), and git add then operate on the symlink, which the kernel follows to the colliding outside path. ComponentDiscovery.matches (weblate/trans/discovery.py) walks with followlinks=True and uses the same startswith(base) skip, so prefix-colliding outside translation files can be listed and ingested. Impact is CWE-22 path traversal with confidentiality leak across the component repository boundary (CVE CVSS S:C/C:L). Preconditions: a repository that contains such a symlink/junction and a Weblate user/path that causes resolve_symlinks or discovery to evaluate it (typically a project/component with VCS access, matching PR:L).

mechanism.summary: A malicious pickle resolves cProfile.run (or cProfile.runctx) via GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL and REDUCEs it with an attacker code string; fickling's checker does not flag the import because cProfile is missing from the module blocklist, so the file scores SUSPICIOUS instead of LIKELY_OVERTLY_MALICIOUS and is accepted by a severity-gated pipeline, where loading it executes the attacker's string (CWE-184 incomplete blocklist leading to CWE-502 RCE).
mechanism.trigger: Scan with check_safety()/is_likely_safe()/the fickling CLI of an attacker-supplied pickle containing GLOBAL cProfile run (STACK_GLOBAL; e.g. SHORT_BINUNICODE 'cProfile', SHORT_BINUNICODE 'run', STACK_GLOBAL, SHORT_BINUNICODE "print(...)", TUPLE1, REDUCE, STOP), followed by loading the same pickle in a consumer that trusted the scan severity.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: fickling/fickle.py:865-882 Pickled.unsafe_imports() at 9a2b3f8 (identical tuple in tag v0.1.6): the module tuple __builtin__, __builtins__, builtins, os, posix, nt, subprocess, sys, builtins, socket, pty, marshal, types, runpy lacks cProfile; its consumer fickling/analysis.py:331-340 UnsafeImports.analyze at the same revision yields Severity.LIKELY_OVERTLY_MALICIOUS only for nodes returned by that function, while UnusedVariables (analysis.py:343-354) yields SUSPICIOUS for the same file.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a published CVE/GHSA describing a real incomplete-denylist bypass in Fickling's unsafe-import gate, reproduced in the v0.1.6 tree and closed by adding cProfile on the 0.1.7 line. The smallest first writer of that gate is named-human commit e43e1eaa2f0c977a811cfdced2dec628736f5244; its parent lacks the control, it is not a squash/merge, and the BIC commit object has no AI marker. The minimum repairing commit is dc8ae12966edee27a78fe05c5745171a2b138d43 (also named-human, no AI trailer). Therefore the case is a real vulnerability with human BIC authorship: NOT_AI.
Fickling's severity gate escalates a pickle only when Pickled.unsafe_imports() in fickling/fickle.py matches an imported module, and cProfile was never in that blocklist, so a pickle that REDUCEs cProfile.run("...") scored SUSPICIOUS from the leftover UnusedVariables heuristic instead of LIKELY_OVERTLY_MALICIOUS and passed a severity-gated pipeline that then executed attacker code on load. The blocklist and the severity decision it feeds were introduced as one change by e43e1ea (2021-02-04, Evan Sultanik, human; parent 1c001477 has no unsafe_imports() or severity gate at all), and cProfile is absent from every revision of the blocklist until the fix commit dc8ae129 (2026-01-07, Thomas Chauchefoin) added it together with a regression test. Every pre-fix edit of the blocklist or its consumer is named-human, and the only AI-trailered commits in those files before the fix are build, demo and crash fixes that never touched the blocked-module set; the AI-co-authored blocklist work in this repository begins 2026-01-20, after the fix, under other advisories. No AI contribution (introduction, new exposure, or incomplete remediation) can be attributed to this defect from the commit objects, so the verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: kiota info treats an OpenAPI description as a trusted source of the package-install command. KiotaInfoCommandHandler then replaces the built-in Configuration.Languages templates with that spec object and prints string.Format(DependencyInstallCommand, name, version) as Kiota's own install example (later DisplayInstallHint: 'Hint: use the install command...'). kiota info --json serializes the same field for the VS Code extension, which can run it. An attacker-controlled or tampered description can therefore induce RCE when the suggested command is executed. The 1.32.5/1.29.1 fix stops reading and emitting the spec-supplied command and keeps only Kiota's built-in templates.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MISP's AadAuth plugin implemented the Azure AD OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow in AadAuthenticateAuthenticate::_getUserAad(). On the first request it built an authorize URL whose state query parameter was the live PHP session identifier (session_id()) and redirected the browser to Azure AD. On callback it accepted the flow when strcmp(session_id(), $_GET['state']) == 0. Because state is echoed through the IdP redirect, Referer headers, browser history, and intermediary logs, a leaked session ID is a reusable session credential (session hijacking). The same design forbade session_regenerate_id() after login (the call was present but commented with 'Generating a new session will fail the further flow of AAD'), enabling session fixation: an attacker who plants a known pre-auth session keeps

Server-side validation was limited to a block-list check gated by '!env.SELF_HOSTED' (skipped entirely in self-hosted deployments) plus, from 2026-02-03, active-content (svg/html etc.) checks restricted to PUBLIC users (isPublicUser). causal_research.bug_semantics: django-allauth's OAuth2 social-account provisioning uses Provider.extract_uid(data) to compute the SocialAccount.uid that keys third-party identities: on login, allauth looks up an existing SocialApp-scoped SocialAccount by uid and links or creates the local account on that basis. Both the Okta (allauth/socialaccount/providers/okta/provider.py) and NetIQ (allauth/socialaccount/providers/netiq/provider.py) providers implemented extract_uid as str(data["preferred_username"]). preferred_username is a user-visible, mutable OIDC claim - an Okta/NetIQ admin (or, under some tenant policies, the end user) can change or reassign it - so an attacker who obtains or is later assigned a victim's preferred_username value gets linked to the victim's pre-existing SocialAccount and thus their local django-allauth login: privilege escalation via identifier churn. Authorization-grade identity should come from the immutable 'sub' claim instead.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user with workflow:create posts a crafted workflow (save, update, or import) whose node.credentials object, after JSON.parse, has own enumerable keys such as __proto__ or constructor. replaceInvalidCredentials iterates those keys and uses them to index and write nested properties on plain-object caches (credentialsByName[type][name] and credentialsById[type][id]). Subsequent unauthenticated requests then see inherited req.user as truthy in AuthService (`if (req.user) next()`), so they are treated as a logged-in privileged user and can enumerate users and projects; pollution also corrupts global object state until process restart.

mechanism.impact: Prototype pollution leading to authentication bypass: an unauthenticated caller is treated as a privileged user (auth.service.ts:158), exposing the user and project listings, every account's personal data (email, role, MFA status) and all projects on the instance; the pollution can also corrupt global state and make parts of the instance unresponsive until restart (CVSS v4 HIGH, VC:H, CWE-1321).
mechanism.preconditions: Authenticated account with the default workflow:create permission able to save/update/import workflows through the API; instance on an affected version (before 1.123.61, or 2.0.0-rc.0-2.27.3, or exactly 2.28.0); payload must be JSON-parsed so that '__proto__' remains an own enumerable key (object-literal syntax cannot express it); the polluted property persists for the process lifetime and is cleared only by restart.
mechanism.summary: A user holding the default workflow:create permission saves, updates or imports a workflow whose node-credentials object carries an own '__proto__' (or other object-internal) credential-type key; replaceInvalidCredentials uses that key as a dynamic index into two cache objects, and because credentialsByName['__proto__'] / credentialsById['__proto__'] resolve to Object.prototype the cache writes land on Object.prototype; the inherited user property then satisfies the pre-fix auth middleware 'if (req.user) next()', so unauthenticated requests are treated as authenticated and user/project enumeration plus account data (email, role, MFA status) are exposed, with global-state corruption until restart.
mechanism.trigger: Create/update/import a workflow through the workflow API with a node credentials object that was JSON-parsed, e.g. {"__proto__":{"id":null,"name":"user"}}: JSON.parse keeps '__proto__' as an own enumerable key, Object.entries surfaces it as nodeCredentialType, and the by-name branch writes credentialsByName['__proto__']['user'] = {id:null,name:'user'} (i.e. Object.prototype.user, truthy), while the by-id branch writes credentialsById['__proto__'][nodeCredentials.id] = nodeCredentials at workflow-helpers.ts:469.

causal_research.bug_semantics: getUserIdFromRequest treats the first X-Forwarded-For value as the user identifier (base64url-encoded as user-*). That identifier is the DynamoDB quota partition key (checkAndIncrementRequest / recordTokenUsage when DYNAMODB_QUOTA_TABLE is set and the client does not supply its own API key), the Langfuse userId, and the log-feedback userId. Any client that can set or prefix XFF mints a fresh identity, bypasses per-user request/token/TPM limits, impersonates another IP-derived user, and poisons telemetry. The helper never validates the header, never requires a trusted proxy overwrite, and never falls back to the TCP peer address. Impact is highest for self-hosted/Docker deployments and for operator-paid model keys behind optional quota.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A staff admin POSTs /api/admin/users/impersonate/ with the PK of a deactivated (is_active=False) non-staff, non-superuser. UserAdminImpersonateView is IsAdminUser-only and trusts BaserowImpersonateAuthTokenSerializer, whose PrimaryKeyRelatedField queryset historically filtered only is_superuser=False and is_staff=False. Validation therefore succeeds and the view issues JWT session tokens for that inactive user. Downstream JSONWebTokenAuthentication and jwt user loading reject inactive users, so the token does not authorize ordinary API use; the defect is still incorrect privilege assignment at token issuance. The 2.3.3 fix adds is_active=True to the same queryset so the PK is invalid (HTTP 400).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Open WebUI's prompt version-history feature stores per-prompt snapshots in PromptHistory rows keyed by UUID. Three routes authorize the caller against the URL prompt_id but then act on caller-supplied history/version ids looked up globally by primary key, never checking history_entry.prompt_id == prompt.id: GET /api/v1/prompts/id/{prompt_id}/history/diff runs compute_diff(from_id,to_id) over arbitrary snapshot ids (cross-prompt content read); POST /id/{prompt_id}/update/version calls update_prompt_version(prompt.id, version_id), whose lookup returns any row regardless of owner and copies that snapshot's name/content/data/tags into the caller's own prompt (read exfiltration channel); DELETE /id/{prompt_id}/history/{history_id} deletes any PromptHistory row wherever prompt.version_id guard passes (integrity destruction of another user's private prompt versions). Any authenticated user controlling at least one prompt qualifies.

Theme::deleteProcess() takes that array from getPost('tables') and, if the table exists, calls Database::forge()->dropTable($table, true) with no check that the name came from that theme's migrations. deleteConfirm already derived the intended set by regexing $this->forge->createTable('...') in APPPATH/Database/Migrations/templates/<theme>/*.php and rendered those as checkboxes, but the server trusted the POST. The result is integrity/availability loss of any table, including authentication tables. The 0.31.8.0 fix copies that same migration parse into deleteProcess and drops a table only if it is in the allow-list.

causal_research.bug_semantics: org.freedesktop.UDisks2.Encrypted.HeaderBackup is a privileged D-Bus method on the root udisksd. handle_header_backup() in src/udiskslinuxencrypted.c takes caller-supplied backup_file, confirms the block is crypto_LUKS, then calls bd_crypto_luks_header_backup() and writes LUKS header plus keyslots to that path. The handler never called udisks_daemon_util_check_authorization_sync(), unlike sibling Encrypted methods such as handle_convert() which already required polkit (modify-device / modify-device-system). Any local unprivileged user who can talk to the system bus can therefore export encryption metadata without authorization, enabling offline cracking or analysis. The 2.11.1/master fix adds the same open-device / open-device-system polkit gate used by other device-open paths before launching the backup job.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: a caller of *_from_pem_callback (macros in openssl/src/macros.rs) supplies a safe FnOnce(&mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, ErrorStack> that returns Ok(len) with len > buf.len(), for example the length of an external secret instead of the number of bytes written into the OpenSSL scratch buffer. Vulnerable code: invoke_passwd_cb in openssl/src/util.rs builds a slice of length `size` from OpenSSL's `buf`, runs the closure, and (before the fix) returned that usize to OpenSSL as c_int with no `len > size` check. Sink: OpenSSL 1.1 / LibreSSL PEM decryption (EVP_BytesToKey) treats the returned length as the password length and reads past the stack buffer, leaking adjacent stack bytes into the derived key (CWE-125). Preconditions: encrypted PEM so the callback actually runs; linked OpenSSL 1.1 or LibreSSL (OpenSSL 3.x not affected per advisory). Impact: confidentiality of adjacent stack and possible crash (CVSS 1.7 Low).

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-54249 / GHSA-h7p7-w5gc-xj3w (PYSEC-2026-3692/3693, published ~2026-06, reporter via GitHub): UI adapters (Vercel AI and AG-UI) reconstruct file parts from client-submitted message history and forward them to model providers. FileUrl parts were validated against a scheme allowlist (allowed_file_url_schemes), but UploadedFile references - which point at a file by provider file ID or cloud-storage URI (s3://, gs://) - were forwarded with NO validation. The provider resolves an UploadedFile with server-side identity (IAM role / service account / provider API key), so a client that crafts message history containing an attacker-chosen UploadedFile can read arbitrary objects in the server's provider/cloud account (confused deputy / broken access control, CWE-284/863). Affected 1.65.0-1.105.0 and 2.0.0b1-b5; fixed in 1.106.0/2.0.0b6 by validating/dropping UploadedFile refs on client-submitted messages the same way file URLs are validated.

Backslash-containing authority sections diverge between urlparse (which stops the host at a backslash and treats the rest as userinfo/path) and other URL parsers used downstream (urllib3 parse_url / aiohttp per RFC 3986, which keep backslashes inside the host), e.g. http://evil.com\@allowed.com yields hostname=allowed.com under urlparse while requests/aiohttp connect to evil.com. causal_research.bug_semantics: The Open WebUI model upload route (POST /ollama/models/upload) built filesystem paths from the unvalidated multipart upload filename via os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, file.filename). causal_research.bug_semantics: After PR #8566 moved transparent script verification from C++ zcash_script_verify_precomputed (which parsed the full transaction and enforced known sighash types) to a Rust sighash callback, Zebra canonicalized the hash-type byte instead of following ZIP-244 / zcashd. For V5, zcash_script HashType::from_bits(..., false) / signed_outputs() mapping treats undefined bytes as ALL/ANYONECANPAY (0x84→0x81, 0x50→0x01) and Zebra computes that canonical sighash, so a signature over the canonical digest with an illegal type byte verifies; zcashd SighashType::parse rejects those bytes. For V4, zcashd serializes the raw hash-type byte into the ZIP-143 preimage (masking 0x1f only for selection); Zebra hashed HashType.bits() of the canonical type, so extra bits (0x41) produced a different digest and Zebra rejected txs zcashd accepted. Either split lets a peer drive Zebra off the zcashd-majority chain.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the pre-BIC parent computes the transparent sighash in C++ via zcash_script_verify_precomputed (so the canonicalization is new at 3650442ad, not pre-existing); checked whether the later API rework 886077020 changed the canonicalization (it did not, same signed_outputs/anyone_can_pay mapping); checked the fix's own tests and comments for the exact pre-fix mapping; checked that the later v5 SIGHASH_SINGLE divergence belongs to different advisories (GHSA-cwfq-rfcr-8hmp, GHSA-pvmv-cwg8-v6c8), so it does not extend or reopen this advisory's two mechanisms.
mechanism.impact: Consensus divergence: an attacker can push a V4 or V5 transparent transaction (and, via mining, a block) that affected Zebra nodes accept but zcashd nodes reject, partitioning the network and enabling double-spend/service-disruption scenarios; conversely Zebra rejects V4 transactions that zcashd accepts.
mechanism.preconditions: Zebra < 4.3.1 scripts verification (zebra-script crate); attacker can relay/mine transactions; honest miners/nodes use zcashd for the transaction to be rejected there. No authentication or special privileges needed (AV:N, PR:N).
mechanism.summary: Trigger: a transparent input whose signature carries a hash-type byte outside {0x01,0x02,0x03,0x81,0x82,0x83} (V5), or a V4 input signed over the raw non-canonical byte. The Rust sighash callback in zebra-script/src/lib.rs canonicalizes/converts that byte before zebra-chain computes the digest, so Zebra and zcashd derive different sighashes and one node accepts what the other rejects: accepted blocks/transactions diverge into a consensus split.
mechanism.trigger: V5 variant: submit (or mine) a transparent spend with hash_type byte 0x50/0x84/0x85/0xFF/0x00/0x04 - Zebra canonicalizes it to ALL or ALL|ANYONECANPAY and validates a signature zcashd rejects. V4 variant: submit a spend whose signature is valid only under the raw byte 0x41 digest - zcashd accepts, pre-fix Zebra computes the canonical 0x01 digest and drops it.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: zebra-script/src/lib.rs:160-176 (closure calculate_sighash) at 1f605eca5^ (9f2ffcb65): matches hash_type.signed_outputs()/anyone_can_pay() with no version check; and zebra-chain/src/primitives/zcash_primitives.rs:307-330 sighash() with hash_type.try_into().expect(...). The raw-byte loss originates in the same callback introduced at 3650442ad (extern "C" fn sighash with HashType::from_bits_truncate(hash_type as u32)).

causal_research.reasoning:
CVE-2026-41583 / GHSA-8m29-fpq5-89jj is a real consensus-split: the #8566 callback refactor stopped enforcing zcashd's known hash-type set for V5 and started hashing a canonicalized type for V4. The smallest first-writer is named-human Conrado Gouvea on 8ab59166d46a786d29d71fdab68991321ddbcf4d, with parent-tree absence of the callback verified at 736f5f54151c0ad2bfb914c4d45f9735a7913ee6. The BIC commit object has no AI trailers, so attribution is NOT_AI. The minimum shipped repair is squash 1f605eca5c55e3b65229fa01a97d9aa84fd37447 in zebrad 4.3.1 / zebra-script 5.0.1 (decomposed member 6dceef5), also named-human. GHSA's zebra-script 5.0.2 patched version is a metadata mix-up with zebra-consensus 5.0.2; the crate that actually contains the hunks is 5.0.1.
Both mechanisms named by the advisory are confirmed from first-party sources. For V5 transactions, the Rust sighash callback installed by 3650442ad canonicalizes undefined hash-type bytes (0x50 -> ALL, 0x84 -> ALL|ANYONECANPAY, 0xFF -> SINGLE|ANYONECANPAY, per the fix's own regression test) instead of rejecting them the way zcashd's SighashType::parse does, so Zebra can verify a signature that zcashd rejects; for V4 transactions the same callback collapses the raw byte to a canonical type before the preimage, while the C++ verifier it replaced serialized the raw byte. The BIC is 3650442ad (GitHub squash of PR #8566), whose immediate parent c6f5753 still verified through zcash_script_verify_precomputed with the sighash computed entirely in C++ and contains no Rust callback, so the vulnerable behaviour is absent at the parent and present in the child. The minimum fix is 1f605eca5 (squash of PR #10494, released in zebra 4.3.1), which adds the six-value allowlist {0x01,0x02,0x03,0x81,0x82,0x83} for V5+ and routes pre-V5 sighashes through the new sighash_v4_raw raw-byte API backed by zcash_transparent 0.6.4. AI attribution fails: the BIC commit object names human author Conrado Gouvea (Zebra/ZFND) with committer GitHub, and its only trailers are two reviewer trailers Co-authored-by: Marek <mail@marek.onl>; no Generated-by or AI-assistant marker exists in the commit object and the hunk set is an ordinary hand-written FFI/API migration. What would flip the verdict is an AI trailer or AI authorship disclosure inside the BIC commit object itself; a disclosure on the PR page alone would raise the admissibility question already recorded for alias-39207546, not establish a positive here.

causal_research.bug_semantics: open-webui validate_url attempts SSRF protection by DNS-resolving urlparse(url).hostname and rejecting private/loopback IPs (when ENABLE_RAG_LOCAL_WEB_FETCH is off). Because urllib.parse.urlparse and requests/aiohttp disagree on how to tokenize a URL containing backslash (or tab/CR/LF) around the netloc, a URL like http://127.0.0.1:6666\@1.1.1.1 is parsed as host=1.1.1.1 (public, passes the filter) by urlparse while the request library connects to 127.0.0.1 (internal). Result: SSRF bypass to private targets in file/image retrieval (CWE-918). Root cause is the parser-disagreement inherent to the DNS-check design, first written with that design in 2024.

causal_research.bug_semantics: QuerySet **kwargs keys become SQL column/table aliases: annotate()/aggregate()/extra()/values()/values_list()/alias() route each caller-supplied name into Query.check_alias() and thence into generated SQL (SELECT ... AS ... and FilteredRelation join definitions). Defense is a deny-list regex, FORBIDDEN_ALIAS_PATTERN in django/db/models/sql/query.py, matching quotes, whitespace (\s), semicolons, hashes and SQL comment delimiters. \s covers only tab/LF/VT/FF/CR; the C0 range 0x00-0x1F outside those five, DEL 0x7F, and C1 0x80-0x9F pass validation yet remain significant to database lexers, so a crafted alias for a FilteredRelation carried in via dictionary expansion could embed control characters, survive check_alias(), and inject attacker-controlled SQL fragments depending on backend quoting. Django rated it high severity.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Credential exfiltration via LLM-controllable proxy (CWE-863 incorrect authorization, CVSS 6.9 v4): the http_request tool exposed a 'proxies' parameter in the LLM-controllable tool input schema (TOOL_SPEC inputSchema in src/strands_tools/http_request.py) and forwarded it into the requests call ('proxies': tool_input.get('proxies', None)). HTTP_REQUEST_TOKEN_CONFIG binds secrets to an allowlist of hostnames checked only against the request URL, so an indirect prompt injection (web page/Slack/file content) can make the model set proxies to an actor-controlled endpoint: the allowlist check passes on the request URL, the Authorization header is attached, and the request is routed through the actor's proxy on the first hop, disclosing the credential in cleartext. GET requests additionally bypass the tool's consent gate (which prompts only on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE). Fixed in 0.8.2 by removing proxies from the schema.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can render the New Users or New Organisations dashboard widgets supplies a widget config fields list. Handler code starts $fields as [] when options['fields'] is set and copies only names present in a local $field_options whitelist, then (New Users) unsets email after that selection for non-site-admins when Security.disclose_user_emails is disabled. If the remaining map is empty—because every requested name was invalid, or because email was the only remaining field and was redacted—CakePHP find() is called with fields => array_keys($fields) equal to []. An empty fields list selects all model columns, so the widget JSON/HTML returns unintended User or Organisation attributes, including user e-mail addresses the redaction was meant to hide. causal_research.bug_semantics: System.Security.Cryptography.Cose decode path mishandles the COSE crit (critical headers, RFC 9052 section 4.1) parameter and header-value validation. Commit 97d96f2ab6f added ThrowIfMissingCriticalHeaders which parses the protected-header crit array under a value of CoseHeaderLabel.CriticalHeaders and only requires every listed label to be present in the protected map; it guarded the element count with Debug.Assert(length > 0). Because Debug.Assert is compiled out in release builds, a crafted message whose crit field is an EMPTY CBOR array passes the critical-header gate trivially (nothing to be missing), letting an attacker suppress RFC-required strict handling of critical parameters - a spoofing / undetected-data-manipulation security-feature bypass (matches MSRC description Improper handling of missing special element ... spoofing over a network). The same commit also rewired CoseMessage.DecodeBucket to call public CoseHeaderMap.Add(label,value) whose ValidateInsertion throws ArgumentException; during DecodeSign1/DecodeMultiSign this ArgumentException escapes raw instead of the documented CryptographicException, another contract break on attacker-controlled input.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Credential disclosure via HTTP redirect: UploadKerberosHub (machinery/src/cloud/kerberos_hub.go, was KerberosHub.go) sends the Hub credentials as custom headers X-Kerberos-Hub-PrivateKey / X-Kerberos-Hub-PublicKey (plus X-Kerberos-Hub-Region etc.) on requests to config.HubURI+paths, using a bare &http.Client{} with no CheckRedirect policy. net/http follows cross-host redirects automatically and only strips the standard sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, WWW-Authenticate) on host change; custom-named headers are forwarded verbatim, so if the configured HubURI redirects (e.g. compromised/malicious endpoint or misconfigured URL), the private Hub key is disclosed to the redirect target host. causal_research.bug_semantics: Unbounded allocation/DoS (CWE-770) in Scriban's array.insert_at builtin. ArrayFunctions.InsertAt creates a ScriptArray copy of the input list, then fills `index - array.Count` null elements in a tight C# for loop that never consults context.LoopLimit, LimitToString, ObjectRecursionLimit, or RecursiveLimit, and never calls StepLoop. A single template like `[1] | array.insert_at 200000000 'x'` therefore triggers OOM/process-wedge on a 1GB host in ~0.6s even with LoopLimit=10 and LimitToString=100. The 7.0.0 hardening pass (dde661d 'Apply LoopLimit to internal iteration paths' and 4227fde 'Harden string padding width limits') swept analogous loops but missed InsertAt.

descriptions: open-webui before 0.3.14 contains a cross-origin resource sharing misconfiguration allowing arbitrary origins with allow_origins=* and authenticated requests to the /api/v1/functions endpoint. causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: an unauthenticated client opens one GraphQL WebSocket, completes connection_init (graphql-transport-ws requires it; legacy graphql-ws did not until the sibling CVE), then floods subscribe/start messages with distinct IDs. Vulnerable code: BaseGraphQLWSHandler.handle_start and BaseGraphQLTransportWSHandler.handle_subscribe unconditionally allocate an asyncio.Task and retain the generator/Operation in per-connection dicts with no cap. Sink/impact: CWE-770 unbounded allocation on a single connection, linear RSS growth and event-loop saturation, availability loss (DoS/OOM). Preconditions: a reachable async subscription endpoint using either protocol. Counterevidence to FP: 0.312.2 still has the uncapped spawn; 0.312.3 rejects over-limit IDs with 'Subscription limit reached'. Pre-#333 ASGI handled GQL_START synchronously and closed the socket after one subscription, so concurrent per-connection flooding was not possible.

mechanism.counterevidence: Searched the parent tree for any existing bound: git grep -n max_subscriptions 36a2d530 is empty and neither handler enforces a message-count or memory bound; the duplicate-id guard (close 4409) only rejects repeated ids and does not bound unique ones; confirmed the vulnerable lines are present at the fix's immediate parent and the corresponding per-operation task creation is absent at the introducing commit's parent.
mechanism.impact: Linear memory growth plus event-loop saturation in the server worker, degrading or crashing the GraphQL endpoint (CWE-400/CWE-770, CVSS:3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/C:N/I:N/A:H).
mechanism.preconditions: Network access to the GraphQL WebSocket endpoint; the default on_ws_connect performs no authentication; transport-ws requires a completed connection_init, while the legacy path did not check it at all (closed by the same fix).
mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated WebSocket client sends subscribe (graphql-transport-ws) or start (legacy graphql-ws) messages with unique ids; each message unconditionally creates an asyncio task and stores it plus its async generator in the connection's handler dict, so active operations and memory grow linearly with the message count and the event loop saturates up to an OOM crash.
mechanism.trigger: A single WebSocket connection floods SubscribeMessage (graphql-transport-ws, after connection_init) or StartMessage (graphql-ws) messages with unique operation ids; no credentials are required under the default on_ws_connect, and the legacy handler did not even require connection_init before the fix.

The reported DoS exists exactly as described: at the fix's parent 36a2d530 neither WebSocket handler bounds the number of concurrent operations per connection, so one client socket can spawn unbounded tasks and async generators. causal_research.bug_semantics: In Pages Router apps with i18n and middleware/proxy authorization, compiled matchers require a locale prefix. Direct HTML requests to a default-locale page are rewritten to /<defaultLocale>/page before matching, so middleware runs. A locale-less Pages data request /_next/data/<buildId>/<page>.json is a valid default-locale data URL: the _next/data catchall (later middleware_next_data) strips /_next/data/<buildId> and .json, leaving /page with no locale, so the i18n-prefixed matcher does not fire. Routing still serves getServerSideProps JSON. An unauthenticated client that knows buildId (public in page payloads) can therefore read protected SSR props without the middleware auth check. The 2026 fix prefixes the inferred default locale onto that normalized data pathname so matching matches the HTML shape.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Across multiple MISP create/edit/import sinks, client-controlled JSON/form fields were copied into CakePHP save() data without stripping or re-pinning server-authorized identifiers. CakePHP treats a primary key in save data as the UPDATE WHERE target, so an authenticated user who passed an ACL check on one object could overwrite another object's row, re-parent attributes into another event, transfer ownership (org_id/user_id), spoof sharing-group organisation_uuid, or inject stored content into another user's context. The unifying helper was CRUDComponent::edit(), which loaded the authorized row, copied every payload field (including id) onto it, then saved; independent controllers and Event capture paths did the same by saving request/JSON bodies after create() with no id unset and no fie

causal_research.bug_semantics: During WebAuthn login, processCredentials decodes attacker-chosen userHandle, resolves that AMIdentity, and loadAuthenticators Java-deserializes each userAttribute blob before assertion verification. CVE-2026-45051 replaced Commons SerializationUtils.deserialize with ObjectInputStream plus an ObjectInputFilter that allowlists only AuthenticatorImpl at depth 1 and returns ALLOWED for every class at depth>1. Java consults the filter for every class in the graph, so a stream whose root is AuthenticatorImpl may nest an arbitrary gadget; the gadget's readObject/readResolve runs inside readObject() before the cast. That is pre-authentication CWE-502 RCE when a gadget is on the classpath and the selected identity's authenticator attribute is attacker-controlled.

mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated client in the WebAuthn login flow supplies an attacker-chosen userHandle; the module resolves that user and deserializes the serialized authenticator blob stored in the identity's userAttribute; the 16.1.1 ObjectInputFilter short-circuits to ALLOWED for every class at depth > 1, so a stream rooted at AuthenticatorImpl with a gadget nested inside executes the gadget's readObject/readResolve during readObject(), giving RCE when a gadget is on the classpath.
mechanism.trigger: Submit attacker-crafted credentials JSON (userHandle plus assertion fields) to the WebAuthn authentication module's credential-processing state; processCredentials() decodes userHandle to a userId, resolves the identity, and loadAuthenticators() deserializes the stored blob before any credential verification.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal in the SFTP provider's recursive download: SFTPHook.retrieve_directory and retrieve_directory_concurrently walk the tree returned by self.get_tree_map(remote_full_path) and compute every local destination path as os.path.join(local_full_path, os.path.relpath(entry, remote_full_path)) for both sub-directories (mkdir via Path(new_local_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)) and files (self.retrieve_file(file_path, new_local_path, prefetch)). Directory-entry names originate from the remote SFTP server, which a malicious or compromised server can craft to contain '..' components, so relpath() yields components that escape the destination root; because nothing validated that the joined path resolves inside local_full_path before the mkdir/retrieve_file write, the client writes attacker-placed directories and files anywhere on the local filesystem the Airflow worker can reach. No Airflow account is required; the attack surface is any deployment downloading a directory from an untrusted SFTP server (SFTPOperator operation=get).

causal_research.bug_semantics: vm2 sandbox defines a CallSite wrapper for the objects V8 hands to Error.prepareStackTrace. It stubs getThis() and getFunction() to undefined to prevent host object leaks, but proxies all remaining getters (getFileName, getLineNumber, getColumnNumber, getFunctionName, getMethodName, getTypeName, getEvalOrigin, isToplevel, ...) straight through to the host CallSite. A sandboxed caller can set Error.prepareStackTrace to a custom function and call s.getFileName() on each frame, extracting absolute host paths (/app/... or Node internal node:/internal/...), exact source line/column, and host function names. The default error.stack string (V8 native formatter active while prepareStackTrace is undefined) leaks the same paths. Source-to-sink: sandbox JS triggers an Error, V8 collects raw CallSite frames (including host modules), the wrapper exposes their fileName/location instead of redacting them, and sandbox code reads the host path/location info (CWE-209 information disclosure).

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated client POSTs to the public password-reset email endpoint (/!/auth/password/email) with a known victim email and an absolute attacker _reset_url. ForgotPasswordController::sendResetLinkEmail copies that value through URL::makeAbsolute into PasswordReset::resetFormUrl with no host allowlist. makeAbsolute leaves URLs that do not start with '/' unchanged, so http://attacker.example is stored. PasswordReset::url then builds the notification link as sprintf('%s?token=%s', $url, $token). If the victim clicks the unsolicited email, the reset token is delivered to the attacker (CWE-640 account takeover). The CP ForgotPasswordController calls the same parent method. Relative tag-generated reset_url values were the intended feature; the defect is trusting a request-controlled absolute host.

mechanism.impact: The password-reset token for the victim's account is attached to the attacker's URL in the emailed link; the victim's click transmits the token to the attacker, who can then hit password/reset/{token} to set a new password - account takeover (CWE-640).
mechanism.preconditions: Attacker knows the email address of a valid account; the victim clicks the link in the resulting email even though they did not request the reset (CVSS UI:R); no authentication or privileges on the site are needed (PR:N), and the forged value must be an absolute URL because URL::makeAbsolute() is applied before storage.
mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated attacker who knows a victim's email can POST a forged reset URL to the frontend forgot-password route; the controller records it as the reset form URL, and the password-reset email link is built as sprintf('%s?token=%s', $url, $token), so the victim's reset token is appended to the attacker's URL and leaks to the attacker when the victim clicks the link, enabling account takeover.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user with Code write on a target repository and only non-Code access (for example Issues-only via an org team) to a private source repository can reuse a known LFS OID/size. BatchHandler and UploadHandler call LFSObjectAccessible; that helper treated the object as reusable if any owning repository matched AccessibleRepositoryCondition(..., unit.TypeInvalid), which uses UserOrgTeamRepoCond (team_repo/team_user) and unit-independent access, not team_unit TypeCode. Target-repo write authorization is still required; the broken decision is source-object Code-unit authorization.

mechanism.counterevidence: Three falsification checks were run. (1) Pre-2019 parent: modules/lfs/server.go BatchHandler created LFS meta rows for any object without any accessibility check, so adopting the helper in 2021 was a narrowing and the first enforceable check on this path is the one with the unit flaw. (2) 2022 refactor: git show 6473bd333a^:models/repo/repo_list.go shows the old AccessibleRepositoryCondition(user) already OR-ed UserCollaborationRepoCond, userOrgTeamRepoCond (team_repo plus team_user, no team_unit join), owner and public-in-private-org, so unit.TypeInvalid preserved exactly the prior semantics and no behaviour change is attributable to that commit. mechanism.impact: Cross-repository confidentiality breach: Git LFS payloads of a private repository can be linked into and downloaded through an attacker-controlled repository without Code access to the source, plus unauthorized metadata association written into the target repository.
mechanism.preconditions: Git LFS server enabled; the object bytes already exist in the shared content store; the attacker holds Code write on the target repo (enforced by authenticate -> perm.CanAccess(AccessModeWrite, unit.TypeCode), services/lfs/server.go:538-560 at 7b4a1a1a11^) and non-Code access to the private source repo via org team membership; the attacker knows the OID and size, which are visible in pointer files, CI logs or a cloned bundle.
mechanism.summary: A user who holds only non-Code access (for example Issues access) to a private source repository is treated as having access to that repository's Git LFS objects, because LFSObjectAccessible resolved 'accessible repositories' with unit.TypeInvalid (team membership through team_repo plus team_user, with no team_unit filter) instead of a Code-unit condition; the Git LFS batch and upload handlers then auto-linked a private source object into an attacker-controlled repository, whose download endpoint subsequently served the private bytes.
mechanism.trigger: An authenticated attacker with Code write access to a target repo and only Issues-only team access to a private source repo, who knows an existing LFS object OID and size, posts a batch request with operation=upload for that OID to the target repo's Git LFS endpoint: services/lfs/server.go BatchHandler finds the object already in the shared content store, sees no meta row for the target repo, and calls git_model.LFSObjectAccessible(ctx, ctx.Doer, p.Oid); the unit-unaware condition returns true because the user's team is linked to the source repo through team_repo regardless of which units that team can use, so NewLFSMetaObject links the source object to the target repo. A following download batch on the target repo then finds the meta row plus the content store entry and hands the client a download link.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real published CWE-639/863 defect: LFS reuse treated Issues-level (or other non-Code) repository access as enough to authorize associating a private source LFS object. The 2026 fix is the TypeInvalid to TypeCode switch in LFSObjectAccessible/LFSAutoAssociate; v1.26.2 still has TypeInvalid and v1.26.3 has TypeCode via the #38050 backport. The smallest first writer of that predicate is the #7199 squash 5e6a008 / member fbd8b189 by named human Andrew Thornton (zeripath), with no commit-object AI markers. Fix-side Claude assistance on d551855 does not attribute the BIC. Therefore NOT_AI.
The fix repairs models/git/lfs.go by turning the source-object authorization condition from repo_model.AccessibleRepositoryCondition(user, unit.TypeInvalid) into unit.TypeCode at LFSObjectAccessible and LFSAutoAssociate, so the defect is the unit-unaware set of 'accessible repositories' used to decide whether an existing LFS object may be linked to another repo. Blame puts the literal unit.TypeInvalid text on 6473bd333a (2022-06-16, Hugo Hoitink), but that commit only added the parameter: its parent already called AccessibleRepositoryCondition(user), whose team branch (team_repo joined to team_user, no team_unit predicate) produced the same unit-unaware result, so the refactor rule excludes it. The causal introduction is 5e6a008fba (2019-10-28, zeripath, PR #7199), which created LFSObjectAccessible with cond := accessibleRepositoryCondition(user.ID) (models/lfs.go:162) and the same condition inside the new LFSAutoAssociate; both are absent from its parent af8957bc4c, verified by grep over the parent tree. The LFS API handlers named by the advisory only adopted the flawed helper later, in 2bb32006fd (2021-08-31, KN4CK3R, PR #16865), which replaced an unconditional auto-link and therefore narrowed rather than introduced the exposure. Every candidate BIC object is a named-human commit (zeripath; KN4CK3R; Hugo Hoitink with human co-authors wxiaoguang and Lauris BH) with a GitHub web-flow committer, PGP signature and no AI-attribution trailer, and the earliest landed in 2019, before AI code assistants existed, so the BIC-side evidence supports NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: The unit check closes the advisory's mechanism but not the underlying cross-repo auto-link exposure for identities that do hold Code access to the source: a single-repo write deploy key acts as the repository owner, so it could still link objects from any repo the owner can see, and upstream removed the cross-repo access check from both LFS handlers in 66a3723cbb (#38322, 2026-07-09), replacing it with proof of possession. That follow-up commit is outside this advisory's fix set and its own attribution was not audited here. Next minimal question: after 66a3723cbb, does any LFS content-authorization decision still call AccessibleRepositoryCondition(user, unit.TypeInvalid), and is routers/web/repo/setting/lfs.go:458 the only remaining consumer of LFSObjectAccessible at HEAD.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated client sends appid as a path parameter on /signalk/v1/applicationData/{user|global}/:appid. Handlers run validateAppId, which (before the fix) only rejected '/' and length>=30, then pass appid to dirForApplicationData: path.join(configPath, 'applicationData', 'users/<principal>' or 'global', appid). On Windows Node path.join treats backslash as a directory separator, so appid values such as '..\..\..\' walk out of the applicationData tree. listVersions then fs.readdirSyncs that directory; get/post read and write `${version}.json` via pathForApplicationData and mkdir the escaped appid path in saveApplicationData. Preconditions: security strategy enabled (dummy mode disables the API) and a valid token; writes need write or admin. On POSIX, '/' is blocked so only a single '..' component remains, matching the advisory. Impact is authenticated listing, reading, and writing of files outside the intended applicationData directory on Windows.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When an app uses React Router unstable RSC APIs, a redirect Response thrown during RSC render is encoded into an error digest (location header). RSCErrorHandler decodes that location and, without checking invalidProtocols (javascript:, about:, data:, file:, …), assigns it to window.location.href for external/reloadDocument redirects and renders <meta http-equiv=refresh content=0;url=…>. The SSR path in routeRSCServerRequest similarly sets Location and injects a meta refresh (escapeHtml does not strip schemes). An attacker-controlled redirect target therefore becomes a client-side XSS/dangerous-scheme navigation. causal_research.bug_semantics: Faraday connections are intended to pin requests to a configured base host. A caller-supplied path is parsed/merged as a URI against that base. Because RFC 3986 treats //host/path as a network-path reference, input such as //evil.com/steal populates URI.host (and URI#merge replaces the base authority), so get/post/build_url on a Faraday.new(url: 'https://api.internal.com') connection send the HTTP request to evil.com instead. The v2.9.2 ./ prefix guard skipped any string starting with /, so protocol-relative URLs bypassed it. The v2.14.1/v1.10.5 patches force a ./ prefix for //... strings so the authority is not taken from user input.

Mechanism: Faraday joins a connection base URL with a caller-supplied path. causal_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal / arbitrary file read in nltk.data.load via URL-encoded path separators and traversal segments in nltk: resource URLs. The unsafe-path regex (_UNSAFE_NO_PROTOCOL_RE) is applied only to the raw (encoded) resource string, then url2pathname() percent-decodes it when resolving to a filesystem path, a decode-after-check (TOCTOU-style) flaw. Payloads like nltk:%2fetc%2fpasswd or corpora/..%2f..%2fetc/passwd pass the filter and decode to a real absolute/traversal path allowing arbitrary local file reads. Fixed in 3.10.0-rc1 / 3.10.0.
evidence: Atomic introducer 51ceb7517 (Steven Xu, 2014-07-12, native git commit no trailers) added url2pathname() percent-decoding to the resource-resolution path in nltk/data.py find(): changed p=os.path.join(path_, resource_name) to p=os.path.join(path_, url2pathname(resource_name)) at data.py ~582 and the same for zipfile. Parent e8c09039f joined path_ with the raw resource_name (no decode), verified via git show parent:nltk/data.py showing os.path.join(path_, resource_name) with no url2pathname. This created the decode-after-check TOCTOU: encoded traversal %2f..%2f passes any raw-form filter and is later decoded to a filesystem path.

The incomplete raw-form-only check (_UNSAFE_NO_PROTOCOL_RE/_reject_unsafe_no_protocol) was later layered on in 4f9ecd278 (hyperps, 2025-11-20, human) but added checks on the encoded form only; this hardening did not introduce the exploitability (parent 51e0480a8 had no check and no nltk/pathsec.py at all, yet encoded traversal was already reachable via the url2pathname decode). decode-after-check is therefore a property introduced by 51ceb7517, not by the later hardening.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Rancher's authenticated proxy route /meta/proxy (pkg/httpproxy) supports signing outbound requests to whitelisted cloud-provider hosts with credentials stored as Rancher secrets. A client sends header X-API-CattleAuth-Header: <scheme> credID=<id>; newSigner() dispatches to awsv4/bearer/basic/digest/arbitrary signers, and each calls getAuthData -> getCredential(credentialID), which does credentials.Controller().Lister().Get(namespace.GlobalNamespace, id) and unpacks '*Config' data keys directly into the request signature. The secret lookup is performed with no authorization check on the requesting user whatsoever - any logged-in Rancher user knowing any valid cloud-credential ID can have Rancher attach those cloud credentials (AWS accessKey/secretKey, etc.) to arbitrary provider-API requests made through the proxy. The fix replaces the raw Lister fetch with p.secretGetter(req), which resolves request.UserFrom(ctx) and runs a k8s SubjectAccessReview authorizer.Authorize(verb=get on secrets/<ns>/<name>) before returning the secret, so only users already entitled to GET that secret can use it through the proxy.

A low-privilege user can store an HTML/JavaScript project name (AddEmpty validates only required|string|min:3 at 420.6). causal_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox code that holds any embedder-exposed host object sees a bridge Proxy. ECMA-262 §9.5.9 [[Set]] invokes the proxy set trap with Receiver equal to the original assignment recipient. When the sandbox writes through an inheriting object (Object.create(hostProxy).x = v, Object.assign(child, src), nested Object.create) or a forged receiver (Reflect.set(hostProxy, k, v, sandboxObj)), Receiver is not the canonical bridge proxy. Pre-fix BaseHandler.set in lib/bridge.js (v3.11.3 lines 1231-1260) declared receiver but never used it: after isProtectedHostObject / later isDangerousCrossRealmSymbol / __proto__ / array-constructor short-circuits it always did value = otherFromThis(value); return otherReflectSet(object, key, value) === true against the host target. The write therefore created an own property on the host-realm object. With key Symbol.for('nodejs.util.promisify.custom') this installed a sandbox function into Node's promisify dispatch slot so host util.promisify(hostFn)() ran attacker code; the same primitive injects arbitrary string keys. Preconditions: untrusted code inside VM/NodeVM plus a reference to a non-protected host object. Counterevidence: ReadOnlyHandler.set already defineProperty's onto receiver; ProtectedHandler.set installs function values on receiver; GHSA-m5q2's symbol guard blocks the symbol-key PoC but not string-key or forged-receiver variants. Impact is host integrity (CWE-693, CVSS 8.6) and RCE when host later consumes the injected slot.

mechanism.counterevidence: Before 10.3.0 the layer bbox was read with unsigned i32, so the same bytes became 4294967246 and PyArg_ParseTuple('i') raised OverflowError; I verified that converter behaviour directly against CPython 3.12.3 via ctypes (4294967246 -> OverflowError 'signed integer is greater than maximum', -50 accepted), which confirms the reachability really starts at the signed parse. mechanism.impact: Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): rows are written through row pointers read before the im->image array, and each destination is shifted left by xoff * pixelsize, corrupting memory outside the decoded image; CVSS 4.0 AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H.
mechanism.preconditions: Pillow 10.3.0 through 12.1.0; the process opens an attacker-supplied PSD and loads a layer frame whose bbox has a negative origin while xsize + xoff and ysize + yoff still fit the canvas, so the pre-fix extent check passes.
mechanism.summary: Opening a PSD whose layer bounding box is negative and loading that layer frame (or the last frame) passes bbox (x0, y0, x1, y1) with x0/y0 < 0 as tile extents into the C decoder; setimage accepted it because it only checked xsize <= 0 and xsize + xoff > im->xsize, so the raw decoder wrote through im->image[y + yoff] with negative yoff and at xoff * pixelsize before the row, an out-of-bounds heap write.
mechanism.trigger: Image.open(crafted PSD) then im.seek(layer frame) and im.load(); the fix's PoC seeks to the last layer and loads, using layer rects like (-50, -50, 50, 50).
mechanism.vulnerable_code: src/decode.c:189-190 _setimage at 12.1.0 (extent check without xoff < 0 / yoff < 0); write site src/libImaging/RawDecode.c:74-75 ImagingRawDecode at 12.1.0: im->image[state->y + state->yoff] + state->xoff * im->pixelsize.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On compute nodes using the Flat image backend (typically use_cow_images=False), a tenant who can write their instance disk can overwrite a previously raw root or ephemeral image with a crafted QCOW2 header (backing-file or data-file). A subsequent flavor resize reaches nova.virt.disk.api.extend(), which invoked qemu-img resize on the host path without -f. qemu-img then probed the file, treated it as qcow2, and followed attacker-controlled data-file/backing-file names, enabling destructive writes to host files (reproduced as zeroing/growing an arbitrary path). Glance safety checks can block snapshot exfiltration of backing-file content, but the resize-time qemu-img invocation itself is the integrity/availability sink. Preconditions: Flat backend, tenant disk write plus resize; not the default COW/qcow2 compute layout.

The immediate parent still used truncate and therefore did not probe image format. Later mechanical rewrites kept the same command without adding -f. The 2026 security fix constrains the format from disk.info rather than introducing a new mechanism.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object dd7aa02340 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the vulnerable call site directly: pre-fix extend() reaches the resize call with no format argument; earlier branches are only the non-LocalImage return, can_resize_image(), and the FORMAT_PLOOP privsep path, so the unconstrained call is reachable for raw/qcow2 Flat disks. Verified the parent-of-fix revision still carries the unconstrained call via raw file fetch (line 126) and that HEAD carries the fixed form with the explicit format constraint.
mechanism.impact: Host-side data corruption and writes beyond the guest disk boundaries driven by guest-controlled image metadata (CWE-669, HIGH per advisory database_specific).
mechanism.preconditions: Flat (non-cow) storage so the guest can write a header into its own raw disk; ability to trigger a resize of that disk; for the normal path, disk.info is present and trusted (this is the assumption the fix relies on).
mechanism.summary: The Flat backend permits a guest-writable disk whose intended format is recorded in disk.info; a guest rewrites its previously-raw disk with an attacker-crafted QCOW2 header, and a later resize runs 'qemu-img resize' without a format argument, letting qemu-img auto-detect the crafted header and operate on attacker-controlled metadata outside the intended image semantics, corrupting host data. The fix constrains the format, and the underlying flaw is an unconstrained qemu-img invocation in disk.extend().
mechanism.trigger: Instance on Flat ephemeral storage (use_cow_images=False) with a previously-raw disk writes a malicious QCOW2 (or other) header into its own disk; a subsequent resize path (instance resize/migrate or disk growth) calls imagebackend.Flat.resize_image() -> nova.virt.disk.api.extend().
mechanism.vulnerable_code: nova/virt/disk/api.py:108-126 extend() at 4b90fdf9af8de53fb6536d27b8fc654a0c011e2f (parent of the fix); the unconstrained call was first introduced as nova/virt/disk.py:61 extend() by dd7aa0234080d5c3512d0e9bab831a621aac10aa (2011)

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real, reproduced host-file overwrite via unconstrained qemu-img resize on the Flat backend. The smallest first writer of that command is the 2011 Scott Moser commit that replaced truncate with qemu-img resize and omitted -f; the parent tree uses truncate and therefore lacks the format-probing sink. Later 2013/2015/2018 edits only moved or renamed the same call. The 2026 Dan Smith change is the minimum fix (pass -f from trusted disk.info format). The BIC commit object is a named human with no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Claimed CVE versions 30.2.2/31.2.1/32.1.1 were never released; that is a version-label mismatch, not an open residual defect, because 30.3.0/31.3.0/32.2.0/33.0.0 contain the repairing hunks.
An instance disk served by the Flat backend (use_cow_images=False) with a previously-raw disk can have a crafted QCOW2 header written into it by its own guest, and when Nova later resizes that disk, extend() passed the image to 'qemu-img resize' with no format argument, so qemu-img auto-detected the guest-supplied header and performed its size arithmetic on attacker-controlled metadata with host privileges. The unconstrained invocation first appears in the one-line 2011 commit dd7aa0234080d5c3512d0e9bab831a621aac10aa ('use qemu-image resize rather than truncate to grow image files', author=committer Scott Moser <smoser@ubuntu.com>, LP #836759), whose immediate parent 3d542086f23b7b432fe776aed1498f9a7a6ebc7d still contains the previous truncate call and zero qemu-img occurrences. The commit object carries no AI markers, is a hand-written single-line substitution with a Launchpad bug reference, and predates LLM code generation by a decade. The minimum fix is 3eba22ff09c81a61750fbb4882e5f1f01a20fdf5, which passes an explicit '-f raw|qcow2' to qemu-img and raises InvalidDiskFormat for any other format; it is contained in 33.0.0, and same-author cherry-picks merged into stable/2024.2, stable/2025.1 and stable/2025.2 landed in 30.3.0, 31.3.0 and 32.2.0 respectively, matching the advisory's fixed versions. The record's only residual is the fix author's own NOTE 2 probe fallback, which needs host access or operator error and sits outside this advisory's guest-only preconditions. Verdict NOT_AI: neither the introducing change nor the remediation carries AI marks, and the full trigger -> vulnerable code -> impact chain is established from primary evidence.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Residual outside this advisory's preconditions (the fix commit's own NOTE 2): with disk.info missing or unreadable, imagebackend.Flat._get_driver_format() re-probes the image via qemu_img_info with no safety check and that probed format is passed to the format-constrained qemu-img resize. Next minimal question: whether that probe fallback is reachable without host access or an operator error; the guest-only resize mechanism described by this advisory is closed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Electron renders its native autofill popup (datalist/select suggestions) as a separate views widget attached to the owner window. The bounding rectangle for that popup travels from the renderer to the browser through the ElectronAutofillDriver mojo interface, and the browser code trusted those renderer-supplied coordinates as-is: AutofillDriver::ShowAutofillPopup (shell/browser/electron_autofill_driver.cc) copied gfx::RectF(bounds), optionally offset it for an embedder/webview, and passed it straight to autofill_popup_->CreateView() over the whole window content view, with no conversion into root coordinates and no clamping to the requesting frame viewport. Because any frame could invoke this IPC path, a cross-origin (OOPIF) iframe could position the native popup outside its own bounds, overlaying the embedding page's trusted UI (clickjacking / spoofing of trusted UI). The fix converts the origin via TransformPointToRootCoordSpaceF and Intersects the rect with the calling frame's visible viewport before creating the popup.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Logged-in File Browser UI interpolates the session JWT into GET query strings so browser-driven requests that cannot set Authorization (window.open download of /api/raw, and the command WebSocket upgrade to /api/command) still authenticate. The token then appears in the request URL, so it is copied into browser history, server/proxy access logs, Referer, and (for downloads) OS URL metadata. Anyone who can read those URLs can replay the JWT as the auth cookie or query and reach the user's files. v1 already authenticated XHR with Authorization Bearer and downloads via the auth cookie without putting the JWT in the URL. The v2 frontend added the query parameter; the v2 HTTP extractor also accepts r.URL.Query().Get("auth"), which is why the query form works.

causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: any S3/HTTP request that reaches the server directly. Vulnerable code: rustfs/src/auth.rs get_condition_values() reads header.get('x-forwarded-for') (first comma-separated value) or 'x-real-ip', falls back to 127.0.0.1, and inserts args['SourceIp'] = get_source_ip_raw(header, remote_addr); get_source_ip_raw (crates/utils/src/http/ip.rs, added in the same commit) prefers those headers over the connection address while _RUSTFS_API_XFF_HEADER defaults to 'on'. Impact: the condition map used by policy evaluation carries attacker-chosen SourceIp, so an IP-allowlist bucket/IAM policy (aws:SourceIp) is satisfied by a spoofed header; the GHSA PoC shows baseline ListBucket 403, X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.5 -> 200, X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4 -> 403. causal_research.bug_semantics: Fickling's MLAllowlist pass is supposed to flag pickle imports outside ML_ALLOWLIST, including standard-library modules that the UnsafeImports denylist never lists. AnalysisContext.shorten_code() is a formatter that also records each shortened snippet in a process-wide reported_shortened_code set. UnsafeImportsML walks every import and calls shorten_code() even when the import is not unsafe, so every import is marked reported. When MLAllowlist later walks the same nodes, already_reported is true and it continues without consulting ML_ALLOWLIST. check_safety() therefore returns LIKELY_SAFE for payloads such as from ast import parse. fickling.load() treats LIKELY_SAFE as permission to pickle.loads(), so the payload runs. UnsafeImportsML and MLAllowlist are each consistent in isolation; the defect is the shared mutable dedup set plus the allowlist iterating the same full import set the poisoner already marked.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Chained account-takeover-to-RCE. Langflow's FastAPI app registered CORSMiddleware with allow_origins=['*'] AND allow_credentials=True; Starlette reflects any caller Origin plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true, so every origin may send and READ credentialed cross-origin responses. Independently, the JWT session cookies minted by /api/v1/login and rotated by /api/v1/refresh were set with SameSite='none' (+Secure), so the victim's browser attaches refresh_token_lf on cross-site fetches. A malicious page can therefore silently call /refresh as the victim, read the fresh access_token/refresh_token pair out of the JSON response, use it against authenticated APIs including built-in Python code-execution endpoints, and gain arbitrary code execution on the host.

evidence: write_file accepts attacker-influenced path/content, calls validate_path(path, base_dir), then tokio::fs::write on the returned path. validate_path uses Path::exists() to decide whether to canonicalize. A dangling final symlink reports exists()==false, so the checker canonicalizes only an in-sandbox ancestor and re-appends the unresolved final component; the prefix check therefore passes. The later write follows the symlink and creates or overwrites a file outside base_dir (CWE-59). Local access and the ability to plant that symlink inside the sandbox are required. Issue #4797 reproduced this on ironclaw-v0.29.1.
