causal_research.bug_semantics: NoSQL parameter injection (CWE-943) in @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb MongoDBSaver.getTuple() (+ list/put/putWrites/deleteThread): thread_id, checkpoint_ns, checkpoint_id from config.configurable are used directly as MongoDB query fields without type/string enforcement, so attacker-controlled object payloads like {$gt: ''} / {$ne: null} are interpreted as query operators, bypassing thread/tenant scoping and leaking other tenants' checkpoint state, metadata, and pending writes. Affected <= 1.3.0, fixed in 1.3.1.
causal_research.evidence: Fix 284226c7ca164b3c81fe2d9e32b10f1fc6b99a3c 'fix(langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb): validate configurable checkpoint IDs (#2397)' (2026-05-18, Hunter Lovell, parent 428c4e3f2946cc2b06f8550aa6974d5bdb2352c2) adds shared getStringConfigValue runtime validator in libs/checkpoint-mongodb/src/checkpoint.ts applied to getTuple, list, put, putWrites, deleteThread, plus regression tests for object/operator payloads; git merge-base --is-ancestor 284226c7 origin/main -> FIX_IS_ANCESTOR; fix marker count = 1 but the only matching line is human trailer 'Co-authored-by: Itay <9601971+etairl@users.noreply.github.com>'. Introducer: git log --follow --diff-filter=A on the checkpointer -> 9d08d04696ebdd875796e1a41072e7d25b227dfb 'Adds MongoDB checkpointer (#352)' (2024-08-23, Jacob Lee, single parent 9c4bcaf2d1f9e3a01fa3b7f5fad29cb270b44923); the commit tree contains the vulnerable path in libs/checkpoint-mongodb/src/index.ts: getTuple at line 57 destructures thread_id/checkpoint_ns from config.configurable and builds 'query = { thread_id, checkpoint_ns }' (line ~71) for Mongo find(), plus put/putWrites reusing the same raw values; git grep -c 'getTuple' 9d08d046^ -- 'libs/checkpoint-mongodb/**' -> exit=1 (package did not exist at parent). Marker regex on full introducer message = 0. The vulnerable pattern was carried unchanged through the 2026-04-28 refactor 36916ed86e63eb07249a68ecf0508e3b986ba587 ('feat(langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb): add MongoDBStore for long-term memory with manual and auto embedding (#2326)', Sergey Zelenov) which moved the saver to libs/checkpoint-mongodb/src/checkpoint.ts.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Missing input validation at the saver boundary: the checkpointer was written to accept any configurable values and embed them raw into Mongo find()/update() queries; string coercion/validation of identifier fields was never present from initial implementation, and callers were trusted to pass string thread ids.
causal_research.reasoning: The unvalidated-configurable NoSQL injection surface was introduced with the MongoDB checkpointer package itself in a 2024 commit by LangChain maintainer Jacob Lee with zero AI markers in subject/body/trailers (marker regex count 0). The flaw is a missing-validation design gap (identifier fields not string-coerced at the saver boundary), present from the first implementation and preserved through a 2026 refactor; no AI authorship signal on the vulnerable lines. The fix (Hunter Lovell, 2026) has only a human co-author trailer. Closed causal chain with no AI signal -> NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Information disclosure: Gitea sends release notification emails for private repositories to users whose access has been revoked. When a repo is changed from public to private, users who previously watched it keep their watch rows (no cleanup on visibility change), and MailNewRelease (services/mailer/mail_release.go) selects recipients purely from GetRepoWatchersIDs without re-checking repo-unit read permission, so revoked users continue receiving release titles, tags, and content by email.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory CVE-2026-0798/GHSA-8fwc-qjw5-rvgp (fixed v1.25.4, PR #36319; OSV GIT fixed=369830ba which is the 1.25.4 release-notes commit). PR #36319 merge commit 8a98ac22 (2026-01-14, Lunny Xiao): (1) models/repo/watch.go + services/repository/repository.go - clean watches when a repository is made private; (2) services/mailer/mail_release.go - MailNewRelease now loads the repo, then slices.DeleteFunc removes publisher and any recipient failing access_model.CheckRepoUnitUser(ctx, rel.Repo, u, unit.TypeReleases); tests added in watch_test.go/mail_release_test.go/repository_test.go. BIC: git log -S MailNewRelease -> e7d65cbc6e (PR #12463, Add email notify for new release, 2020-08-23) creates services/mailer/mail_release.go selecting recipients = GetRepoWatchersIDs + GetMaileableUsersByIDs with no permission check (only excluding the publisher); parent e429c116 lacks the file (cat-file fatal) and has no MailNewRelease symbol (grep rc=1). causal_research.bug_semantics: Parse Server's default fileUpload.fileExtensions control is supposed to stop uploads that browsers will render as active content. FilesRouter.createHandler prefers the filename extension when the name contains a dot, and only consults Content-Type as a fallback. Independently, FilesController.createFile sets contentType = mime.getType(filename) || contentType, so an unrecognized extension (note.foo, data.bar, or no usable extension) stores the client Content-Type verbatim. A malformed Content-Type that is not a type/subtype token (image, image/, image//svg+xml) does not yield a blocklisted subtype: split('/')[1] is empty or the bare token image is not in the blocklist, so the upload is accepted. S3/GCS/Azure then serve that unparseable Content-Type; browsers MIME-sniff an HTML/script body and execute it in the application origin against other users who open the file URL. GridFS is not a sink because it recomputes Content-Type from the filename and sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Later GHSA-v8x7-r927-cc93 added a Content-Type subtype check when mime does not recognize the extension, but still used the same split('/') extraction, so malformed values continued to bypass.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A malicious local (or downloaded) model directory can ship a sharded-checkpoint index JSON whose weight_map values are ../ sequences or absolute paths. _get_checkpoint_shard_files in src/diffusers/utils/hub_utils.py trusted those strings and os.path.join-ed them onto the model directory, then returned the resulting paths. ModelMixin.from_pretrained / DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained opened those paths via _load_shard_file -> load_state_dict, so loading a sharded checkpoint could read safetensors (and attempt to open other files) outside the intended model directory without trust_remote_code. The 2026-07-17 fix rejects any weight_map value whose basename is not the whole string, which blocks traversal, absolute paths, and nested relative components.

A victim who opens the issue/file and clicks the link navigates to attacker-controlled HTML/JS in their Gogs origin context (stored XSS; CWE-79). The wrapImgWithLink data: skip added in the same BIC is an image-src convenience, not the XSS sink.

causal_research.reasoning:
CVE-2026-26022 / GHSA-xrcr-gmf5-2r8j is a real stored-XSS from an unbounded data: URL allowlist in Gogs' bluemonday sanitizer. The smallest original writer of that line is named-human PR member eae7d1f (2018), squash-landed as 9079fb6; the immediate parent tree lacks the line. The minimum repair is PR #8174's isSafeDataURI policy, first in 4f021e48, landed on main as 441c64d and cherry-picked to release/0.14 as 51cf4cbe, which is in v0.14.2. BIC commit objects have no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Fix-side Claude co-authorship does not change BIC attribution. A later ipynb-only AllowURLSchemes("data") in internal/app/api.go is a distinct sanitizer introduced by a43fc9ad1 and is not the GHSA-xrcr comment/markdown-file mechanism closed by #8174.
GHSA-xrcr-gmf5-2r8j describes a stored XSS in the raw-HTML anchor path: internal/markup/sanitizer.go weakens bluemonday's UGC policy with sanitizer.policy.AllowURLSchemes("data"), so a link such as <a href="data:text/html;base64,..."> stored in a repository file, issue or comment survives sanitization and a click executes attacker JavaScript in the gogs origin. I verified the vulnerable state at the fix parent 5c67d475127f6629ba06899a6fd635f9900404b6 (internal/markup/sanitizer.go:35-36 at 441c64d7^), the reachable render path (markup.Markdown -> Render -> RawMarkdown with raw HTML preserved -> postProcessHTML copying the <a> tag verbatim -> SanitizeBytes; callers include internal/route/repo/issue.go:530/:596 and internal/route/repo/view.go:155), and that the pinned bluemonday v1.0.27 disallows a scheme when no policy is registered for it (sanitize.go:948-968), so the explicit allowance is what lets the data: href through. The causal introduction is the squash landing 9079fb6a0df75e351800c434cdc226fd8bc47e71 ("pkg/markup: support data URL of base64 encoded images (#5391)", 2018-12-10), whose immediate parent db3f0048d80f4f7aaa903d367ace67b8cd0389dc contains no data: URL allowance in the same file - the causal atom is that sanitizer.go hunk, while the companion markup.go hunk only affects img src link wrapping. The fix 441c64d7bd8893b2f4e48660a8be3a7472e14291 (parent 5c67d4751, shipped in v0.14.2 via the release-branch backport 51cf4cbe7) replaces the blanket scheme with AllowURLSchemeWithCustomPolicy("data", isSafeDataURI), restricting data: URIs to image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp and image/x-icon, and its tests assert that data:text/html hrefs and SVG data URIs are stripped. The BIC commit object names humans only (author Nikita <6773262+Nikeron@users.noreply.github.com>, committer 无闻 <u@gogs.io>), carries a conventional 2018 feature message with zero AI trailers or tool mentions, and is a handwritten two-file feature diff, so no BIC-side AI involvement is evidenced and the verdict is NOT_AI.

Preconditions: local CLI running and a user-gesture navigation to the attacker page; the server need not bind 0.0.0.0.

mechanism.impact: Cross-origin reads of dev-server responses from any website the developer visits: GraphQL data and media listings, and - chained with the media path traversal - arbitrary files such as .env, .git/config and SSH or cloud credentials. mechanism.preconditions: tinacms dev running with default settings (no host binding and no extra configuration; localhost is enough), and the developer visiting an attacker-controlled page in a browser that can reach 127.0.0.1:4001. No credentials, no exposed port, no user interaction beyond the page load.
mechanism.summary: tinacms dev mounts a CORS middleware with no origin option on the server that serves /media/* and /graphql, so every origin is told Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, and a malicious page can read the dev server's responses while the developer has tinacms dev running. With the previously reported media path traversal and Vite's disabled fs.strict, the cross-origin read extends to arbitrary files on the developer's machine.
mechanism.trigger: The developer runs tinacms dev (default port 4001) and, while it is running, visits an attacker-controlled page; the page issues fetch('http://localhost:4001/media/list/...') or a /graphql request and the browser hands the response body to the page because the server answered Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal in Mako's TemplateLookup.get_template(): a URI starting with '//' (e.g. //../../../../etc/passwd) bypasses the directory-traversal check. root cause: inconsistency between two slash-stripping implementations - Template.__init__ strips ONE leading '/' with if/slice (self.uri[1:]), while TemplateLookup.get_template() strips ALL leading '/' via re.sub(r'^/+', ''). After get_template strips all slashes the path resolves to a file outside the template root via posixpath.join, and Template.__init__'s normpath+startswith('..') check is bypassed because only one '/' was stripped. Allows arbitrary file read when app passes untrusted input to get_template(). Fixed in 1.3.11.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated (or API) registration accepts a distinct login plus an email and persists the email in faquserdata without a uniqueness check. Source: Frontend RegistrationController::create / Api RegistrationController::create (4.0.12) pass the posted email into RegistrationHelper::createUser. Password reset matches username plus that user's stored email, so takeover is not automatic, but email-keyed notifications and admin actions become ambiguous.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The C parser gained a per-callback max_line_size check in 07923e44a (2017-02-15) but still stored only the latest fragment. PR #2325 member 0c2c5c69 (2017-10-15) introduced _buf accumulation so split status lines parse correctly, while leaving the fragment-only length check in place. That is the first tree in which an overlong line can be assembled in memory without LineTooLong. GitHub squash-merged the same parser blob as 411af984b, which is the ancestor present in v3.14.0.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 0c2c5c69de to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: The pure-Python parser is not affected: aiohttp/http_parser.py bounds the incomplete line with 'if len(self._tail) > self.max_line_size' at the fix parent (lines 489-491), which is what the fix restores in the C parser. The header callbacks cb_on_header_field/cb_on_header_value already compared accumulated sizes (len(_raw_name) + length, _header_name_size + size), so headers were never in scope. The settings wiring lists only on_url and on_status as accumulating line callbacks (_csettings.on_url/_csettings.on_status at lines 401-402); llhttp exposes no on_method/on_version callback, and echo of a single oversized fragment is caught by the same guard, so the bypass needs fragmentation.
mechanism.impact: Unbounded growth of the per-connection bytearray _buf while the line is incomplete (CWE-770 allocation without limits), so one attacker connection can consume memory that max_line_size was meant to cap, with no LineTooLong, on both server (request target) and client (response reason) paths.
mechanism.preconditions: C extension parser in use; attacker controls the request line (server side) or the status line of the response it serves (client side); attacker can spread one line over multiple reads; no other cumulative cap on the target/reason exists in the C parser before 3.14.1.
mechanism.summary: llhttp reports a request target or response reason phrase through on_url/on_status once per read, so one line split across reads reaches cb_on_url/cb_on_status several times; each call compared only its own fragment length with _max_line_size while appending the fragment to the shared _buf bytearray. A line delivered in fragments under the limit therefore accumulates past max_line_size without ever raising LineTooLong, and the whole oversized target/reason stays resident per connection until the message ends.
mechanism.trigger: Optimized C parser active (default in prebuilt wheels) and one request target or response reason phrase delivered in several reads, each fragment shorter than max_line_size (8190 by default), e.g. dribbling bytes of 'GET /aaaa...' and never sending the line terminator.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: aiohttp/_http_parser.pyx:784 cb_on_url and aiohttp/_http_parser.pyx:799 cb_on_status at 60b85e98ea338750036e8249558c7260c983b22b (fix parent); identical per-fragment guards in the affected release v3.14.0 at lines 782 and 797.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory describes a real C-parser max_line_size bypass for fragmented URL/reason lines. The smallest original writer of that mechanism is named-human PR member 0c2c5c69 (squash landing 411af984b), whose parent tree has no _buf accumulation. The 2026 two-line accumulated-length check (36df6c13, backported as 5ab61bb in v3.14.1) closes the defect. BIC commit objects have no AI authorship or co-authorship markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class. Fix-side AI is absent and does not affect the verdict.
The C parser's fragmentable line callbacks compared only the bytes of the current callback fragment with max_line_size while appending that fragment to the parser-level _buf, so a request target or response reason delivered in pieces that each stay under the limit accumulated past the limit and never raised LineTooLong; the fix enforces the limit on len(_buf) + length, closing both callbacks. The causal change is 411af984b (PR #2325, 'Accept partial status line'), which replaced the per-fragment overwrite of _path/_reason with pyparser._buf.extend(at[:length]) in cb_on_url and cb_on_status and left the pre-existing per-fragment guard untouched, so its parent 4ccf6816 stores no accumulated target and the unbounded allocation is absent there and present in the child. The guard text itself is older (07923e44a, 2017-02-15, guard absent in its parent 6fc71b364), but no line could exceed the limit in memory before 411af984b created the accumulator, and later commits touching these lines only reshaped the error message (ed6440ca4, 2026-01-12) or the extend() helper (28f15195c) without changing the comparison. The BIC commit object is attributed to a named human maintainer (Andrew Svetlov <andrew.svetlov@gmail.com>), committed by GitHub as a squash merge, references issue #2311, and carries no AI trailer, tool marker or bot identity. No AI contribution to the defect can therefore be established, so the verdict is NOT_AI; it would flip only on a positive AI marker inside 411af984b or in a BIC-side change that had newly exposed the flaw.

causal_research.bug_semantics: After OIDC authentication, MISP resolved the local user first by the token sub. If that missed, it searched User.email using the token email claim. A stored non-null sub that did not match the token was rejected, but a local account with sub IS NULL was accepted and then updated so User.sub became the attacker’s sub. With an IdP that issues unverified or attacker-controlled email claims, a valid OIDC token asserting a victim’s email therefore authenticated as that existing local user and bound the attacker identity to it (account takeover). The 2026 fix leaves sub-based login intact and makes the NULL-sub email-link path opt-in (allow_email_linking=false by default) plus email_verified=true unless explicitly disabled.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Jakub Onderka’s 2021-11-11 commit 6806cdf574eaf302abebb3dd277bc0192234d1b7 introduced the users.sub unique column and the OIDC lookup policy 'find by sub, else find by email and auto-bind when sub is NULL'. Immediate parent e52e7ae29cec376e865ce2f47d738f933964b3ca still treated email as the only OIDC identifier and had no sub field or NULL-sub linker. The 2022 move into Oidc.php copied that same fall-through; it did not originate the defect. GitHub PR #7954 is that single commit plus a merge carrier.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Use-after-free in SQLite3::Database#define_function/create_function (ext/sqlite3/database.c define_function_with_flags). The function passes the Ruby Proc block straight into sqlite3_create_function as (void*)user_data; SQLite retains that raw pointer for the lifetime of the registered SQL function, while the ONLY tracked Ruby reference lived in @functions, a Hash keyed by the function NAME. Defining the same name again (different arity or text encoding, so a second registration rather than an overwrite-per-advisory wording) replaced the Hash entry, dropping the last Ruby-visible reference to the previous Proc. At the next GC the Proc object is freed but SQLite's func structure still points its user_data at the freed VALUE, so invoking the previously defined function reads freed memory and can segfault.
causal_research.evidence: Fix commit 2bd436d17f77cdd4c31b00fe9d50b0d21cbaf033 (= PR #710, both advisory references): converts @functions Hash->Array, rb_hash_aset(...name, block)->rb_ary_push(...) in ext/sqlite3/database.c ~line 527 and @functions={} -> [] in lib/sqlite3/database.rb, plus regression test test_redefine_function_with_different_arity_does_not_use_freed_block; git tag --contains -> v2.9.5,v2.9.6 matching advisory 'fixed in 2.9.5'. BIC 46daaf239c09b57e83c1afaad626d575bf4e9318 (git show: adds exactly the two lines later changed by the fix, CHANGELOG.rdoc + ext/sqlite3/database.c). Parent absence VERIFIED: git show ef6dace102636e6299d419c3da0d893018225124:ext/sqlite3/database.c has sqlite3_create_function calls (lines ~348,~412) but grep finds zero '@functions'/'functions=' registration lines in parent .c/.rb. causal_research.bug_semantics: Arbitrary command execution (reported as CWE-78 command injection) in the terminal-controller-mcp FastMCP server: the `execute_command` tool accepts an arbitrary `command` string and runs it via `run_command()` using asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(cmd, shell=True, executable='/bin/bash' or shell=True on Windows) with no input validation other than a trivially bypassable blacklist (dangerous_commands = ['rm -rf /', 'mkfs']). An attacker able to invoke the MCP tool can execute arbitrary shell commands on the host. This is the tool's intended function (a terminal controller for MCP), with only a weak blacklist, so the 'command injection' classification reflects intended-but-dangerous design rather than a coding defect.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PHP object injection / Remote Code Execution (CWE-502) in the TYPO3 'Site Crawler' (crawler) extension: GuzzleExecutionStrategy passes the X-T3Crawler-Meta response header of a crawled URL directly to PHP unserialize(). Because the header of the crawled response is fully attacker-controlled when the crawled endpoint is external or compromised, arbitrary serialized PHP objects can be injected, leading to RCE on the TYPO3 server running the crawl. Exploitation requires admin privileges (configure crawler-enabled page + trigger crawl via Scheduler task). Fixed in 12.0.11 and 11.0.13.
causal_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin CVE-2026-8727 + GHSA-jr8m-x4p7-p3v5 (OSV valid: 'TYPO3 Remote Code Execution in extension Site Crawler (crawler)'; packsagist tomasnorre/crawler introduced 12.0.0 fixed 12.0.11 AND introduced 0 fixed 11.0.13; exploit requires admin to configure crawler page + scheduler crawl; attacker controls a crawled endpoint; refs typo3-ext-sa-2026-008). Fix: json switch - GuzzleExecutionStrategy 'return unserialize($response->getHeaderLine("X-T3Crawler-Meta"))' -> 'return json_decode($response->getHeaderLine("X-T3Crawler-Meta"), true)' and CrawlerInitialization 'withHeader(..., serialize($crawlerData))' -> json_encode with comment 'the receiving end would unserialize() a header of the crawled response'; on main via forward-port be7dbe77 (#1307, 2026-07-28, Jonas Eberle, no AI trailers, 'This forward-ports commit 2713c27'); releases 12.0.11 (2026-05-11) and 11.0.13 (2026-05-18) carried the original security commits (2713c27 not present in this clone); at HEAD further changed to json_decode of the header. causal_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the vulnerable behavior: commit 8a9b896721f479d7babc4bb5920536e8124a1797 '[BUGFIX] Change requests to write to Header to ensure StaticFileCache is working' (2021-11-01, Tim <tim@fruit-lab.de>, single parent d906b21078acf58c55f506de4b16ea050e827e10, no trailers, Resolves #837) which switched BOTH sides of the crawl metadata channel in one commit: GuzzleExecutionStrategy.fetchUrlContents changed 'return unserialize($contents)' with $contents from $response->getBody()->getContents() to 'return unserialize($response->getHeaderLine("X-T3Crawler-Meta"))', and CrawlerInitialization middleware changed from writing serialized crawl data into the response BODY ($response->getBody()->write(serialize(...))) to $response->withHeader('X-T3Crawler-Meta', serialize(...)). causal_research.bug_semantics: Agentic consent bypass (CWE-285 improper authorization, CVSS 4.0 8.2): the LLM agent can silently disable exec approval by writing gateway config. Exec approval settings tools.exec.ask ('off'|'on-miss'|'always') and tools.exec.security ('deny'|'allowlist'|'full') are plain config paths; the agent-facing gateway tool exposed raw unfiltered config writes (config.apply since 71c31266, config.patch since 60661441), so an agent could call config.patch {tools:{exec:{ask:'off'}}} to turn off human-in-the-loop exec confirmation without the user noticing. causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: unauthenticated GET to an app.add_media_file() or app.add_media_files() route with query nicegui_chunk_size=-1 (or 0 / a huge integer). Vulnerable code: FastAPI treats that annotated handler argument as a query parameter and forwards it to get_range_response, which does data.read(min(chunk_size, remaining_bytes)) with no bounds check. Python/aiofiles read(-1) reads to EOF, so one request can load an entire media file (or the rest of the file even under a small Range) into memory; concurrent requests amplify RSS until degradation or OOM. Preconditions: the application actually registered those media helpers (documented as world-readable). Counterevidence: add_static_file(s) uses FileResponse and is out of scope; On Air's air.py sets params['nicegui_chunk_size']=1024 as a client hint, which is not the unvalidated server path. Impact is availability (CWE-770), not confidentiality of the already-public media files.

It added FastAPI query parameter nicegui_cunk_size (typo; later renamed) on both media handlers and changed get_streaming_response to take that value instead of the previous hardcoded 8192 default. Immediate parent 6291615 lacked any request-controlled chunk size. Subsequent rename to range_response.py and the 2024 typo fix only moved/renamed the same unvalidated path.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 654e8e2fcf to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the BIC parent 6291615f keeps chunk_size server-side (content_reader's local default 8192) so the exposure is not older than 654e8e2f; ran -S searches for both spellings of the parameter and they surface only introduction (654e8e2f), typo rename (606aafb2) and clamp (9026962b), with no removal/reintroduction; read the AI-assisted 58d5f7b1 diff and it keeps min(chunk_size, remaining_bytes) unchanged, so it cannot be the exposure; confirmed FastAPI still coerces the parameter to int (non-numeric values give 422), so only integer abuse is needed; verified the read semantics locally (io.BytesIO: read(min(-1, n)) and read(min(10**12, n)) both return the whole buffer, read(0) returns nothing).
mechanism.impact: Memory exhaustion / OOM denial of service: every request allocates a single bytes object the size of the served media file (video/audio), so a handful of concurrent requests against a multi-GB file can push the process over its memory limit; CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L and CWE-20/CWE-770 per the advisory.
mechanism.preconditions: The application must register a streaming media route (add_media_files / add_media_file); those routes are public by design (documented as 'accessible to everyone'), so no authentication or session is needed; the served file must be large enough (or concurrent enough) for the amplification to matter.
mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated GET to a media route with ?nicegui_chunk_size=-1 (or any value >= the file size) flows into content_reader's data.read(min(chunk_size, remaining_bytes)), which turns the chunked stream into a single read of the whole file, so each request holds the full media file in memory (CWE-770 memory exhaustion, amplified by concurrency).
mechanism.trigger: HTTP GET to a route registered by app.add_media_files('/media', ...) or app.add_media_file(...) with the query parameter nicegui_chunk_size set to a negative integer (e.g. -1) or any integer at or above the remaining byte count of the served file; the Range header is optional because the default path already sets end = file_size - 1.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: nicegui/app/range_response.py:49 content_reader (blob at 9026962b^): 'chunk = await data.read(min(chunk_size, remaining_bytes))' with chunk_size arriving unvalidated from the route (nicegui/app/app.py:287 and :317 at 9026962b^, 'chunk_size=nicegui_chunk_size'); introduced at 654e8e2f as nicegui/app/streaming_response.py:34 content_reader ('chunk = data.read(min(chunk_size, remaining_bytes))') with the routes at nicegui/app/app.py:199,229 forwarding the query parameter.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real unauthenticated media-streaming memory-exhaustion bug: a FastAPI query parameter is fed to file.read() without bounds. The smallest original introducing change is named-human commit 654e8e2, verified absent in its immediate parent and isolated from the PR #2250 merge landing, later renames, and the typo fix. The minimum public repair is 9026962, which clamps chunk_size to [1024, 8192] and is in v3.9.0 but not v3.8.0. BIC commit-object AI markers are absent, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI. Claude co-authorship on the fix is recorded only as fix_ai_marker and does not create an AI-introduction or incomplete-remediation TP.
NiceGUI's media routes take the request query parameter nicegui_chunk_size (int, default 8192) and forward it unvalidated into get_range_response, whose content_reader calls data.read(min(chunk_size, remaining_bytes)); a caller-supplied -1 (or any value at or above the file size) collapses the chunk to the whole remaining file, so one request materialises the entire media file in memory and concurrent requests to large files exhaust the server. The exposure enters the tree at 654e8e2f (Rodja Trappe, 2023-12-26), the first commit that lets the request choose the chunk size: its parent 6291615f has no such parameter and keeps chunk_size as an 8192 constant inside content_reader, while the child routes (nicegui/app/app.py:199,229 at that commit) accept nicegui_cunk_size and pass it through. The later AI-assisted rewrite 58d5f7b1 (2026-02-02) only moved the generator to aiofiles and preserved the vulnerable expression verbatim, so it neither introduced nor widened the exposure. The minimum repair is the clamp in 9026962b (2026-03-19, first released in v3.9.0, matching the advisory's fixed version): chunk_size = max(MIN_CHUNK_SIZE, min(chunk_size, MAX_CHUNK_SIZE)) with MIN 1024 and MAX 8192, which removes both the negative and the oversized read sizes. The BIC commit object is a named human maintainer with no AI trailers and a hand-typed parameter name that even carried a typo (nicegui_cunk_size, corrected later by 606aafb2), so ai_on_bic is not established and the verdict is NOT_AI; the Claude Co-Authored-By trailer exists only on the fix commit and is fix-side information.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST /api/setup/backup is rewritten to api/index.php and dispatched to SetupController::backup(). The handler accepts any non-empty body as an 'installed version' string, constructs phpMyFAQ\Setup\Update, and calls createConfigBackup() on the configuration directory (content/core/config, or config/ for pre-4.0 trees). That method writes a ZIP named phpmyfaq-config-backup.YYYY-MM-DD.zip into that directory and returns a public URL under the site origin. The JSON response field backupFile is that URL. Because backup() performed no login, API-token, or permission check (SetupController originally did not even extend AbstractController), any remote caller can generate the archive and fetch it. The ZIP includes database.php and other config files, disclosing DB credentials. Default Apache/nginx rewrite rules expose the route. After 4.0.16, backup() calls userIsAuthenticated() (401 if not logged in) and content/*.zip is denied by .htaccess/nginx.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The RabbitMQ management HTTP API decoded every JSON request body through rabbit_mgmt_util:with_decode -> read_complete_body/2 (deps/rabbitmq_management/src/rabbit_mgmt_util.erl), which recursively accumulated cowboy_req:read_body chunks into an unbounded binary accumulator (<<Acc/binary,Data/binary>>) with no size cap. An authenticated user with sufficient credentials could POST an arbitrarily large body (e.g. definitions upload or binding creation) and force the node to buffer the whole payload in memory until it was terminated by an OOM-killer-like mechanism, i.e. remote denial of service. The fix adds a configurable rabbitmq_management.max_http_body_size limit (default 20 MiB) checked before each accumulated chunk, returning {error, Exceeded HTTP request body size limit} which handlers convert to a 400 bad_request.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-5603 / GHSA-xqv9-qr76-hfq2 (elgentos/magento2-dev-mcp <= 1.0.2, CWE-78 OS command injection): src/index.ts builds magerun2 command strings by template interpolation of tool arguments (e.g. ` --author-name="${authorName}"`, ` --scope="${scope}"`, ` "${path}"`, ` "${event}"`) and executes them via promisify(child_process.exec)(command) - a shell - allowing a locally-invoking client (the MCP user/LLM driving the server) to inject shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary commands as the server user. causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-340 predictable identifier leading to GCS bucket squatting (CVSS 4.0 score 7.7, high): Vertex AI Experiments save_model (google/cloud/aiplatform/metadata/_models.py) auto-generates the staging bucket name as project + '-vertex-staging-' + location whenever no uri or staging_bucket is configured, then creates the bucket if it does not exist. GCS bucket names are globally unique, so an unauthenticated attacker can pre-create (squat) gs://<victim-project>-vertex-staging-<location> in their own project; the victim SDK then stores experiment model artifacts in the attacker-owned bucket, enabling cross-tenant remote code execution, model theft, and model poisoning via malicious artifacts. causal_research.bug_semantics: When two-factor authentication is enabled, Statamic stores encrypt(json_encode(recovery_codes)) on the user as two_factor_recovery_codes (EnableTwoFactorAuthentication / GenerateNewRecoveryCodes). AugmentedUser::keys() includes every user data key, and FileUser only strips password/password_hash from that bag. AugmentedUser::get() has an explicit unrestricted branch for handle two_factor_recovery_codes that returns $this->data->get('two_factor_recovery_codes') as a template Value. Antlers default guards (ViewServiceProvider guardedVariablePatterns) only block config.app.key, so a dynamically rendered Antlers field can read {{ current_user.two_factor_recovery_codes }} and leak the viewing user's recovery-code material. The same BIC commit renamed User::recoveryCodes() to twoFactorRecoveryCodes(); AbstractAugmented::get() would otherwise invoke that decrypting method for this handle via methodExistsOnData(). The explicit branch short-circuits to User::get() (ciphertext) rather than excluding the secret. The intended listing API is the authenticated {{ user:two_factor_recovery_codes }} tag, not current_user augmentation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: macOS policy-bypass (CWE-863): ClearanceKit's opfilter Endpoint Security filter treats any process with an EMPTY Team ID but non-empty Signing ID as an Apple platform binary. An unprivileged attacker can ad-hoc sign a binary with an Apple-baseline-allowlisted signing identifier (codesign -f -s - -i 'com.apple.mds') and read any FAA-protected path, because the forged process matches platformBinary/Apple entries in the global allowlist and FAA policy rules. Advisory states the correct signal is es_process_t.is_platform_binary.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SQL injection and path traversal in the extract_to_json MCP tool of src/entry.py (CWE-89 / CWE-22): the tool builds the query via f-string interpolation of the user-supplied table_name ('query = f"SELECT * FROM {table_name};"') with no identifier validation, and writes results to a user-supplied output_filename via open(output_filename, 'w') with no path sanitization, so an untrusted MCP client can inject SQL (e.g., table_name like 'x; DELETE FROM users; --') and write JSON files to arbitrary filesystem paths via traversal sequences ('../../../../tmp/evil'). CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L (no auth required, remote). Fixed in change a5580cb by validating table_name with isidentifier(), bracket-quoting the identifier in the SQL, basename()-stripping output_filename, and anchoring writes to the database directory.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Denial-of-service in twisted.names DNS name decompression. In src/twisted/names/dns.py Name.decode, a per-name 'visited' set raises ValueError('Compression loop in encoded name') when the SAME pointer offset repeats, but there is no cap on the number of DISTINCT compression-pointer dereferences per name and, because 'visited' is re-created inside Name.decode for every Query/record, none across a whole Message. A remote unauthenticated attacker sends one TCP DNS packet with thousands of Question records all pointing into long, non-repeating chains of compression pointers; the bounded-per-name check never trips while total decode work grows without limit, so the single-threaded reactor hangs processing millions of recursive lookups. The fix adds a shared _DecodeContext (contextvars) installed by Message.decode that bounds total pointer jumps across every name in the message (default maxCompressionPointers=1000) and raises DNSDecodeError.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Secrets exposure / improper masking (CWE-200 info disclosure, CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L 5.1): the deprecated import path 'airflow.sdk.execution_time.secrets_masker' (kept for backward compatibility with providers) redirects mask_secret() to the single-process implementation in airflow.sdk._shared.secrets_masker. That implementation only masks secrets inside the task subprocess; the supervisor process, which actually writes the task logs, never receives the masking instructions, so secrets (including values from the Airflow config file / connections / variables) appear in plain text in DAG run logs UI. The correct supervisor-aware mask_secret lives in airflow.sdk.log. Fix redirects the deprecated path's mask_secret to airflow.sdk.log.mask_secret and switches the deprecation warning class to DeprecatedImportWarning.
causal_research.evidence: OSV GHSA-j86x-fwp2-qh7v (= CVE-2025-66236, PYSEC-2026-8); summary: 'Apache Airflow: Secrets from Airflow config file logged in plain text in DAG run logs UI'; details: before 3.2.0 the security model / workload isolation was under-documented; fixed in 3.2.0; primary reference https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/58662. PR #58662 (merged as 0afe6d3, 2025-11-26, milestone 3.1.4, cherry-pick 65f7af9 to v3-1-test + 9c26db9 via #58726) titled 'Mask secrets properly when using deprecated import path': 'The deprecated import path airflow.sdk.execution_time.secrets_masker was redirecting mask_secret() to a single-process implementation that only masked secrets in the task subprocess. This caused secrets to not be masked in logs because the supervisor process (which writes logs) did not receive masking instructions... The compatibility shim now redirects mask_secret to the supervisor aware implementation in airflow.sdk.log that properly masks secrets in both the task and supervisor processes.' Diff of 0afe6d3 modifies only task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/secrets_masker.py (+9/-1): adds 'from airflow.utils.deprecation_tools import DeprecatedImportWarning', changes warnings.warn to DeprecatedImportWarning, and in __getattr__ adds a special case: if name == 'mask_secret': from airflow.sdk.log import mask_secret; return mask_secret. Introducer located via git log --diff-filter=A on the file -> 439c5c79 (Amogh Desai, 2025-08-25); full history of the file: 439c5c79 (create shim) -> 0afe6d3 (fix); parent 6e0a4ce verified to lack the file (git grep -c exit=1); the file's prior incarnation lived at the same path before the move to airflow_shared (79825427) and was deleted/recreated - the recreated compat shim is what routes mask_secret to the wrong implementation. Repo clone at .ai-slop/state/repos/apache_airflow.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Feature/compat-shim creation: commit 439c5c79 'Adding a compat shim for secrets_masker that was moved to shared (#54915)' (2025-08-25) created task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/execution_time/secrets_masker.py as a NEW file whose module-level __getattr__ forwards every attribute (including mask_secret) to airflow.sdk._shared.secrets_masker - the single-process (task-subprocess-only) implementation introduced when the masker moved to the airflow_shared distribution (79825427, 2025-08-23). causal_research.bug_semantics: Rocket.Chat REST addRoute enforces manage-apps only when the options object contains the key permissionsRequired. In the Apps-Engine log endpoints, that key was misspelled permissionRequired. checkPermissions() therefore returned false, shouldVerifyPermissions stayed false, and GET /api/apps/logs plus GET /api/apps/:id/logs required only authentication. The fix restores the plural key so the existing permission middleware runs.

mechanism.counterevidence: Falsification checks: the two Join calls are the only name-derived path components in the dump writer - every filepath.Join in services/migrations/dump.go at HEAD and at the fix parent uses the base directory, a fixed file name (repo.yml, topic.yml, label.yml, release.yml, ...) or a uuid; git log -S 'filepath.Join(attachDir, asset.Name)' over all refs returns exactly three commits (introduction, main fix, backport), so no earlier partial repair exists; the fix's own comment concedes the premise ('we cannot use asset.Name because it might contains special characters'). Source-platform character rules (GitHub forbids '/' in asset names; git refnames forbid '..' sequences in tags) bound reachability and match the advisory's C:L rating, but do not falsify the code-level defect the advisory fixes.
mechanism.impact: Path traversal in the dump writer (CWE-22, advisory CVSS 3.1 5.3 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N): filepath.Join cleans its result, so '..' elements (and platform separators) inside an attacker-influenced name redirect asset writes outside `<baseDir>/release_assets/...`, and the same name is stored in the dumped release.yml as the local download path.
mechanism.preconditions: Release-asset dumping is enabled and the dumped repository's release data comes from a source the attacker can influence; attachment names are stored verbatim upstream (routers/web/repo/attachment.go:65 uses header.Filename, routers/api/v1/repo/release_attachment.go:229-246 uses header.Filename or an explicit name field), so a source instance can hold asset names carrying path-affecting characters, while tag names are bounded by git refname rules.
mechanism.summary: When a repository is dumped to a local directory with release assets enabled, RepositoryDumper.CreateReleases copies the source-provided release tag name and asset name straight into filesystem paths (`filepath.Join("release_assets", release.TagName)`, then `filepath.Join(attachDir, asset.Name)`), so a crafted name with path-affecting characters changes where the dumped asset bytes are written - a path-traversal / output-path control defect (CWE-22) in the dump output.
mechanism.trigger: An operator runs `gitea dump-repo` (cmd/dump_repo.go sets opts.ReleaseAssets = true) or an equivalent dump-to-local migration against a repository whose release tag or asset names are attacker-influenced; the dumper then downloads each asset and os.Create()s it under the name-derived path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated nil-pointer-dereference DoS in P2P transaction validation. A gossiped protobuf Transaction whose embedded RawData sub-message is omitted unmarshals to RawData == nil. Every transaction received on the libp2p pubsub transactions topic is decoded and validated synchronously inside the topic-validator callback: InterceptedTransaction.CheckValidity -> integrity() -> txVersionChecker.CheckTxVersion(tx), which dereferenced tx.RawData.Version with no nil guard (core/versioning/txVersionChecker.go). Neither the libp2p pubsub callback, go-libp2p-pubsub's validation worker, nor klever's network/p2p layer installed a recover(), so the panic propagated up through the pubsub validation path and crashed the entire node process. A ~3-byte protobuf payload from any peer — no validator key, stake, funds or on-chain account required — could halt nodes and potentially stop chain progress.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DocsGPT stores tool, MCP, and user-model secrets by JSON-serializing them, AES-256-CBC encrypting with PKCS7-style padding, and persisting base64(salt||iv||ciphertext) (encrypt_credentials in application/security/encryption.py). decrypt_credentials later splits salt/IV/ciphertext, decrypts CBC, unpads, and json.loads with no MAC or AEAD tag over salt, IV, ciphertext, or user_id. An attacker who can modify a stored blob (database/storage write, not necessarily a public decrypt endpoint) can flip IV or ciphertext bytes so that the first plaintext block changes in a controlled way; if the result is still valid JSON, the app silently accepts the tampered credentials and uses them for MCP auth, tool config, or API keys. Issue #2503 reproduced this by XOR-flipping one IV byte and observing {"a":"AAAA"} become {"a":"ZAAA"} without an authentication failure.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Integer truncation of tensor dimensions in vLLM's GGUF dequantize CUDA kernels (csrc/quantization/gguf/gguf_kernel.cu, later csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/gguf/). The function-pointer type to_cuda_ggml_t (and its predecessor to_fp16_cuda_t) declares the element-count parameter as 32-bit int while the caller ggml_dequantize() passes m * n, an int64_t product computed from the GGUF weight-tensor shape read from the model file. When m*n > INT_MAX the kernel grid covers only k elements, so torch::empty({m,n}) leaves (m*n)-k unwritten bytes that retain stale GPU memory from prior operations. In multi-tenant inference serving this residual memory may contain other users' tensor data, silently propagating through computation - CWE-200/CWE-681 information disclosure. Attack vector: attacker-hosted GGUF model with dims whose product exceeds INT_MAX.

mechanism.summary: An OAuth client that authenticates to POST /login/oauth/introspect can submit any other client's JWT access or refresh token and receive that token's metadata (active, scope, username, iss, sub, aud), because the handler never compares the authenticated introspecting client with the token grant's application.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An application that loads untrusted protobuf JSON descriptors via Root.fromJSON() or Namespace.addJSON() will recursively expand each nested object. Unmatched nested objects are treated as namespaces and Namespace.fromJSON immediately calls addJSON on json.nested, while Type.fromJSON/Service.fromJSON also walk json.nested and fall back to Namespace.fromJSON. Before the 2026 depth guards there was no recursionLimit on this path, so a single deep chain of nested namespace (or nested type/service) objects grows the JavaScript call stack until it overflows and crashes schema loading (DoS, CWE-674). Preconditions: attacker-influenced JSON descriptor input and the JSON expansion path rather than only .proto text parsing.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect (CWE-601) in next-intl middleware with localePrefix 'as-needed'. The middleware's pathname sanitizer (sanitizePathname in packages/next-intl/src/middleware/utils.tsx) only replaced backslashes (%5C) and collapsed consecutive slashes. It did not strip the WHATWG-control characters U+0009 (TAB), U+000A (LF), U+000D (CR), which the WHATWG URL parser silently removes during parsing. A crafted path such as '/en/<TAB>/example.org' therefore resolved as '//example.org' (scheme-relative) by new URL(path, base), so the middleware issued an off-site relative redirect while the user started from a trusted app URL.
causal_research.evidence: GHSA-8f24-v5vv-gm5j (CVE-2026-40299, CWE-601, moderate): open redirect when using next-intl middleware with localePrefix 'as-needed' because path handling + WHATWG URL parser resolve a relative redirect target to another host (scheme-relative // or control chars stripped by the parser); patched in next-intl@4.9.1, fix commit 1c80b668 (PR #2304, Jan Amann). git show 1c80b668: sanitizePathname gains .replace(/[\t\n\r]/g, '') with comment explaining decoded TAB in segment separator position causes new URL('/<TAB>/host', base) collapse to '//host' open redirect. git log -S 'sanitizePathname' shows first appearance in f42ac014 (PR #1208, 'Fix open redirect vulnerability for localePrefix as-necessary', Hblee, Co-authored-by Jan Amann). mechanism.impact: Arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the MISP web process (typically www-data) through librdkafka loading an attacker library from the parsed configuration; before the load, arbitrary librdkafka options also give attacker-chosen file reads and outbound TLS/material handling. mechanism.preconditions: Settings-edit rights (site admin) or a compromised admin account - this is a post-auth admin-to-RCE escalation, which is why the CVSS vector is PR:H; Kafka publishing enabled with at least one notification topic enabled so the tool is instantiated; a file the attacker can place in a path readable by the web user whose content parses as an INI; ext-rdkafka (librdkafka) installed, since without it the ini is still parsed but the plugin load is a no-op.
mechanism.summary: An authenticated site admin sets Plugin.Kafka_rdkafka_config to a filesystem path they can write; on the next Kafka notification MISP parse_ini_file()s that path and passes all parsed options to RdKafka\Conf::set(), so rdkafka's plugin.library.paths (or a sibling loader option) loads an attacker-supplied shared object into the MISP process - arbitrary code execution as the web user.
mechanism.trigger: Step 1: the admin saves Plugin.Kafka_rdkafka_config to e.g. app/files/<shard>/<uuid> (a file the attacker already placed there through an upload such as an attribute attachment or an admin image) via Server settings / REST /servers/serverSettingsEdit. Step 2: with Plugin.Kafka_enable and Plugin.Kafka_<topic>_notifications_enable on, any ordinary notification emission (event add/edit, organisation save, shadow attribute action, audit-log write) calls AppModel::n() -> publishKafkaNotification() -> kafkaTopic() -> getKafkaPubTool(), which runs parse_ini_file() on that path and hands the parsed array to KafkaPubTool::initTool(), where every non-empty key is passed to RdKafka\Conf::set(); librdkafka then loads plugin.library.paths at producer construction.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: app/Model/Server.php:7958 'Kafka_rdkafka_config' setting (pre-fix 'test' => 'testForEmpty') + app/Model/AppModel.php:3784-3796 getKafkaPubTool() -> parse_ini_file() (HEAD 4af1c16d3; first written as loadKafkaPubTool() in 9d59b1036) + sink app/Lib/Tools/KafkaPubTool.php:12-31 initTool() -> RdKafka\Conf::set() (created in 9d59b1036)

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory describes a real CWE-829 RCE: site-admin-controlled Kafka_rdkafka_config is parsed and fed to rdkafka without a directory allow-list. The smallest first-writer is named-human commit 9d59b10 (PR #4316), whose parent lacks the setting and loader. The CNA patch SHA points at the previous same-day log-path fix; the commit that actually adds testForRdKafkaConfig is 6fae77b, present in v2.5.42 and absent from v2.5.41. BIC commit-object AI markers are absent, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class. Fix-side authorship is also named-human and does not affect the BIC-side verdict.
The advisory describes one mechanism and it is present in the tree: a site admin can point Plugin.Kafka_rdkafka_config at any readable file, and when a Kafka notification fires MISP parses that file with parse_ini_file() and forwards every key/value pair into RdKafka\Conf::set(), so an ini containing plugin.library.paths makes librdkafka dlopen an attacker-controlled library inside the MISP PHP process. All three code atoms land in the single 2019 commit 9d59b1036 - the setting definition in Server.php with 'test' => 'testForEmpty', the parse_ini_file() read in AppModel::loadKafkaPubTool(), and the unvalidated set() loop in the new KafkaPubTool::initTool() - and its immediate parent 43f0010c contains no Kafka code at all, so the BIC is parent-verified and minimal. Upstream closure is 6fae77b40 (Server::testForRdKafkaConfig restricts the value to an absolute .ini under /etc, /usr/local/etc or APP/Config) together with 357bf6805 (cli_only => true, which closes the Server.force=1 bypass on the settings endpoint). The BIC commit object is a hand-written, signed-off feature contribution by Nikos Filippakis (CERN) with no AI trailers, from 2019, and the repository's AI-assisted commits (Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers, earliest 2026-01-29) never touch KafkaPubTool.php or the rdkafka setting, so there is no AI-causal evidence on the introducer side.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Remote code execution in vLLM via dynamic config resolution: the vendored Nemotron_Nano_VL_Config class (vllm/transformers_utils/configs/nemotron_vl.py), registered in _CONFIG_REGISTRY under model_type 'Llama_Nemotron_Nano_VL', calls transformers get_class_from_dynamic_module(*vision_config['auto_map']['AutoConfig'].split('--')[::-1]) and immediately instantiates the returned class when a model config.json carries an auto_map entry. get_class_from_dynamic_module fetches and imports Python from the remote HF repo named in auto_map, and this code path executes even when trust_remote_code=False (the get_config() callers pass trust_remote_code=False for config loading), so a malicious model repo (frontend repo whose auto_map points at a backend repo) achieves arbitrary code execution on the vLLM host. Fixed in vllm 0.11.1.

The admin session helper only requires cama_sign_in?; the drafts actions never call authorize!. create does CamaleonCms::Post.drafts.where(post_parent: params[:post_id]).first, copies attacker-controlled post fields onto that row (set_post_data_params also writes post_data[:post_parent] = params[:post_id]), and save(validate: false). causal_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox boundary bypass (CWE-20, CVSS 8.6 high): Codex sandbox policy conflated two concepts - the directory where the spawned command runs (command cwd) and the directory that anchors the sandbox's writable-root policy (policy cwd). The model-generated `cwd`/`workdir` field of the container.exec/shell tool call was passed into `get_writable_roots_with_cwd(cwd)`, so a model-generated path (resolved via session.cwd.join(workdir), i.e. an absolute path or `../` traversal) became the sandbox's writable root, enabling arbitrary file writes and command execution outside the folder where the user started the session; network-disabled restriction unaffected. causal_research.bug_semantics: When Security.auth includes a form-capable plugin such as LdapAuth.Ldap (LdapAuth.mixedAuth default true) and the user has TOTP/HOTP configured or Security.email_otp_enabled is set, a login POST is authenticated in AppController::_loadAuthenticationPlugins() during beforeFilter via Auth->startup(). That path writes AuthComponent::$sessionKey immediately. UsersController::login() may still redirect to /users/otp (or email_otp), but the session is already authenticated, so a subsequent GET to any other URL skips plugin re-auth (the beforeFilter guard is Session->read(AuthComponent::$sessionKey)) and never re-enters the login() OTP challenge. Impact is authentication bypass of the second factor for an attacker who already knows the primary password. Preconditions: web UI (not REST/API key), plugin listed in Security.auth, OTP expected (user.totp and not Security.otp_disabled, or email OTP). Counterevidence: with Security.auth unset, Form login stays inside login() and navigating away does not leave an Auth session.

_loadAuthenticationPlugins() calls Auth->startup($this), and on success writes Session->renew() and Session->write(AuthComponent::$sessionKey, $user) with no OTP check; beforeFilter reaches it at 271-273 when the session key is empty and the request is not REST/automation.

login() is the only place that triggers the TOTP/HOTP challenge (writes otp_user and redirects to otp at 1238-1246) and the email-OTP challenge (writes email_otp_user and redirects to email_otp at 1249-1256).

AppController parent count is 0 and the UsersController grep returns no match (rc=1), so the TOTP challenge and its session staging are absent in the immediate parent of the BIC.

causal_research.flaw_origin: 93ba84fd026d0b3f84ae265a1eadd51caeb03ea2 (2020-04-20) removed the only OTP check that applied to plugin-authenticated sessions (the beforeFilter redis otp_authed gate added with email OTP) and left plugin session establishment unchanged while moving OTP into login() only. Immediate parent 3436bc6ae54a5555e7d780a90d03d90f07e9a819 still has that gate. TOTP (6caccac9, 2023) and LdapAuth (3986ffab2, 2024) reused the gap; they did not first create it.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 93ba84fd02 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the alternatives and could not falsify the reading: the REST/automation branch authenticates with API keys (__loginByAuthKey, HEAD AppController.php:568) and is not an interactive OTP login; the native form login does challenge TOTP/HOTP and email OTP at the fix parent, so only plugin-established sessions skip it; AppController::__verifyUser (fix parent 732-741) only forces enrolment of users without a TOTP secret under Security.otp_required and never re-challenges a plugin session that already has totp, which is why the bypass survives it; the email_otp_enabled description at the fix parent warns that it cannot be combined with external authentication plugins (Server.php:7193), yet both the advisory and the fix also address the email-OTP path, so that warning is documentation, not mitigation; no public PoC or reproduction of the bypass exists, so exploitability rests on the code path rather than a live replay.
mechanism.impact: Second-factor authentication bypass: a session fully authorized as the target user is issued without a valid TOTP, HOTP or email OTP code (CWE-287, CVSS 4.0 8.2 HIGH per the CVE, VC:H), defeating the instance-wide Security.otp_required policy and the user's own OTP enrolment; the plugin session also updates the login times (AppController.php:1406), so the bypass looks like a normal login.
mechanism.preconditions: Plugin authentication enabled and usable for the victim account (LdapAuth.mixedAuth=true, the default, lets the LDAP plugin fall back to local DB credentials for users absent from LDAP); the account has TOTP/HOTP configured or the instance sets Security.otp_required=true (the advisory's Security.require_otp) or Security.email_otp_enabled=true; the attacker knows valid primary credentials (CVSS AT:P, PR:N); a non-REST request path so that the beforeFilter plugin branch at AppController.php:271-273 runs; plugin session establishment must precede the OTP challenge, which is exactly the pre-fix code shape.
mechanism.summary: Trigger: a user protected by OTP authenticates through an authentication plugin. Vulnerable code: _loadAuthenticationPlugins() authenticates the plugin user during beforeFilter and writes the CakePHP session directly (AppController.php:1403-1410 at bc27fafae511) with no OTP check, while the TOTP/HOTP and email-OTP challenges exist only in UsersController::login() (UsersController.php:1237-1256). Impact: browsing to any URL with that session reaches the application as the fully authenticated user without a valid TOTP, HOTP or email OTP code (CWE-287, CVSS 4.0 8.2).
mechanism.trigger: The instance has an authentication plugin configured (Security.auth with LdapAuth.Ldap; LdapAuth.mixedAuth defaults to true, LdapAuthenticate.php:42) and OTP enforcement active for the victim (the account has TOTP/HOTP set, or Security.otp_required is true - the advisory calls it Security.require_otp - or Security.email_otp_enabled is true). The attacker submits valid primary credentials (LDAP password, or a local password via the mixedAuth local fallback in LdapAuthenticate::getUser(), :230-235) with any non-REST web request; because the session is empty, beforeFilter calls _loadAuthenticationPlugins() (AppController.php:271-273), Auth->startup() succeeds through the plugin and the session is written at 1408-1409; the attacker then requests any other application URL and is served as the authenticated user without ever passing the OTP step.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: app/Controller/AppController.php:1388-1412 _loadAuthenticationPlugins() (session write at 1408-1409, called from beforeFilter at 271-273) together with app/Controller/UsersController.php:1237-1256 login() (the only place the TOTP/HOTP and email-OTP challenges are triggered), both at the fix parent bc27fafae511bbc842604481e23a6c31b1b8dc4b.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-287 OTP bypass, not withdrawn. Mechanism is confirmed in v2.5.38 source and in issue #10807. The smallest original change that created the plugin-path OTP hole is 93ba84fd, which dropped the covering beforeFilter gate; the parent tree still has that gate, so introducer_parent_absent holds. TOTP/LdapAuth are later exposures of the same hole and are also named-human commits without commit-object AI markers. The minimum fix is 39b3cb15, present in v2.5.39 and absent from v2.5.38. BIC commit-object AI markers are absent and the author mailbox is a named human, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Repo-level CLAUDE.md and fix-side identity are not used for BIC attribution.
MISP established the authenticated session for plugin logins (LdapAuth and the other Security.auth plugins) inside beforeFilter, while the TOTP/HOTP challenge and the email-OTP challenge lived only in UsersController::login(), so a user with OTP configured who authenticated through the LDAP plugin with LdapAuth.mixedAuth=true obtained a session by browsing to any other URL; the advisory's Security.require_otp maps to the real setting Security.otp_required (app/Model/Server.php:7174, 'Require authentication with OTP'). The causally minimal introduction of the login-flow-only TOTP challenge is 6caccac94dd2 ('new: [security] TOTP authentication', 2023-05-19): its immediate parent 3e543ad4df contains no TOTP code anywhere (no totp field read, no challenge, no totp_user session), so the vulnerable behaviour is absent in the parent and present in the child, while the plugin session write it collides with dates to 2015 (d2eaccec31, precondition rather than origin) and the email-OTP flavour of the same login-only pattern originates earlier in 93ba84fd02, which removed the global beforeFilter enforcement its parent 3436bc6ae still had. The repair 39b3cb15aa ('fix: [security] prevent otp bypass when LdapAuth.mixedAuth=true and Security.require_otp=true') checks OTP for a plugin-authenticated user before the session is written, stores otp_user or email_otp_user and redirects to the matching challenge, which closes the LDAP-plugin mechanism and first ships in v2.5.39 against a CVE-declared affected range of <=2.5.38. Every candidate BIC commit object names a human author (Christophe Vandeplas, Golbark/Loic Fortemps, Guilherme Capilé) with no co-author, generated-by or bot trailer, so no AI contribution to the defect is established and the verdict is NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Open surfaces and unverified steps. (1) The same session-before-OTP shape survives at HEAD in __customAuthentication() (AppController.php:232 call site, :1344 session write under Plugin.CustomAuth_enable), which the fix does not guard, so a header-authenticated user with TOTP is still not challenged on that path. (2) ApacheSecureAuthComponent::login() writes the session directly (app/Controller/Component/ApacheSecureAuthComponent.php) and its component wiring was not traced end-to-end in this audit, so it is an unresolved same-class surface rather than a confirmed bypass. (3) The fix commit adds no regression test and no public PoC or reproduction exists for CVE-2026-10611, so the bypass is established by code reading of the pre-fix flow, not by a live replay. Next minimal questions: does the CustomAuth header path authenticate users that have totp set on a stock configuration (i.e. is the residual exploitable), and should the __pluginLoginRequiresOtp() guard be called from __customAuthentication() as well?

causal_research.bug_semantics: Directory traversal / arbitrary local file read via the LiveReload HTTP+WebSocket socket (default port 35729). The dispatch handler parsed any plain GET request and, besides the intended './livereload.js' special case, served ANY file whose path exists and is readable relative to the Guard process working directory: commit a5a0f8d added 'elsif File.exist?(parser.request_path[1..-1]) -> serve_file(...)' which strips only the leading slash of the request URL path and applies no containment check against the served web root. A request like GET /. ./../etc/passwd (the '.'+prefix prepend made '../'-sequences resolvable) causes dispatch() to pass '../../../etc/passwd' to _serve/_serve_file, which streams the file contents back over the socket, letting any host that can reach the port read arbitrary user-readable files on the developer machine.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service (CWE-400/CWE-770, CVSS 7.5, network/unauthenticated) in the MessagePack hub protocol used by ASP.NET Core SignalR and Blazor Server. When parsing inbound frames, MessagePackHubProtocolWorker hands attacker-controlled bytes to MessagePack-CSharp. Several parse arms are opaque to the wire shape: CreateCompletionMessage with resultKind=NonVoidResult when ProtocolHelper.TryGetReturnType(binder, invocationId) yields null (unknown invocation ID) falls back to MessagePackReader.Skip(), and unknown-type arguments/results flow through the same skip/recursive-descent code. MessagePack-CSharp resolves nested array (0x91..) and map headers by mutual C# recursion, so recursion depth grows linearly with nesting depth with no limit. An attacker who can open any SignalR/Blazor Server connection sends one CompletionMessage whose result payload is ~100000 nested array headers plus terminator; the recursive walk overflows the stack, raising StackOverflowException, which cannot be caught and tears down the whole .NET process.

causal_research.bug_semantics: requestKeywordDenylist is a default-on deep scan of write/request payloads for prohibited keys/values (_bsontype/Code, constructor, __proto__, plus any custom entries). Enforcement goes source (attacker JSON body) -> RestWrite / Utils.checkProhibitedKeywords -> Utils.objectContainsKeyValue. The pre-fix scanner walked Object.entries and, on the first nested object or array, returned the recursive result immediately, so later sibling keys at that level were never tested. A payload such as {metadata:{}, _bsontype:'Code'} or {data:{}, constructor:{prototype:{...}}} therefore skipped the denylist and could reintroduce BSON Code / prototype-pollution gadgets the control was meant to block (CWE-693).

causal_research.bug_semantics: The UI adapters' inbound hardening (`UIAdapter.sanitize_messages`, AG-UI and Vercel AI) strips unresolved ('dangling') client-submitted tool calls from the tail of untrusted message history so the agent cannot execute a call the model never emitted. The strip was anchored to a tail index computed BEFORE sanitization ran (`last_index = len(messages) - 1`, checked as `index == last_index` per message). When the true trailing client message sanitized to empty and was dropped (default `manage_system_prompt='server'` strips a client `system` message, leaving an empty `ModelRequest` that is dropped), the pre-computed index no longer pointed at the actual surviving tail: a preceding `ModelResponse` carrying an unresolved tool call became the new tail and was never inspected. On the promptless resume path the trailing response's tool calls are dispatched directly, so the client-forged dangling call executed server-side with attacker-chosen (schema-validated) arguments. This is a defense-in-depth bypass: model-request hooks (`before_model_request`/`after_model_request`) gating tool execution are bypassed because the forged call skips the model turn; approval-gated tools still route through the deny-by-default approval pause.

causal_research.bug_semantics: AI Bridge proxy endpoints authenticate through Server.IsAuthorized in aibridgedserver rather than httpmw.ExtractAPIKey. IsAuthorized splits/looks up the Coder API key, rejects unknown/expired/invalid-secret keys and deleted or system users, then returns the key owner. It never inspects database.User.Status. Coder suspension does not revoke existing API keys, so a previously issued long-lived token of a suspended (or dormant) user continues to authorize LLM proxy calls and, if injected MCP tools are enabled, those tools, consuming billed provider resources until the token expires or is deleted. The standard HTTP API-key middleware already blocked non-active users; this parallel DRPC authorizer omitted that gate.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Git receive-pack runs Gitea's pre-receive hook with one stdin line per ref update (oldSHA SP newSHA SP refname LF). runHookPreReceive in cmd/hook.go reads that stream with bufio.NewScanner (default max token 64KiB) and, on each successful Scan, forwards branch/tag (and proc-receive) updates to private.HookPreReceive, which enforces protected-branch rules in routers/private/hook_pre_receive.go (preReceiveBranch: deletion, force-push, signed commits, protected files). bufio.Scanner.Scan returns false on ErrTooLong or other read errors without delivering the offending line. Before the fix the loop did not call scanner.Err(), so the hook treated a truncated stream as complete and returned nil. Git then accepted the whole push, including protected-branch updates never passed to HookPreReceive. Trigger: a push whose hook stdin contains a line longer than the scanner token limit (or another scanner error), typically an extra-long refname in the same receive-pack as a protected-branch update. Preconditions: attacker can push to the repository (push permission) and the target ref is protected. Impact: incorrect authorization (CWE-863) — branch-protection policy is skipped. Counterevidence considered: proc-receive uses bufio.Reader not Scanner; the CVE/fix surface is the two Scanner loops. Post-receive had the same fail-open but is not the authorization gate.

Gitea's git-hook entrypoints read the ref updates that receive-pack feeds on stdin with bufio.NewScanner and, until 2026-03-23, never checked scanner.Err(), so a scan error (notably ErrTooLong on an over-long line) silently ends the read loop, leaves the remaining ref updates unvalidated by private.HookPreReceive, and still returns success, letting the push land with branch-protection checks skipped (CWE-863 fail-open authorization, CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: sandbox code (allowAsync default true) defines an async generator that yield*-delegates to an inner async iterator with no return method, advances it with await i.next(), then await i.return({then(r){ f(); r(); }}). V8's yield* abrupt-return Awaits that thenable via PromiseResolveThenableJob, which invokes thenable.then and catches a synchronous throw in engine internals. The yield* continuation surfaces the captured value as a fulfillment {value: thrown, done:false}, not a rejection. Vulnerable code: at v3.11.2 the only host-exception chokepoints are transformer CatchClause rewriting (lib/transformer.js:145-164 → handleException) and globalPromise.prototype.then onRejected (lib/setup-sandbox.js:273-302). Neither runs: there is no user catch, and internal Await uses PerformPromiseThen rather than the user-visible .then override. Sink: a host-realm RangeError produced when stack overflow hits V8 C++ in the resolver job reaches sandbox as e; e.name==='RangeError' while !(e instanceof RangeError) identifies the host realm; e.constructor.constructor('return process')() yields host process and RCE (CWE-668). Counterevidence considered: sync Generator.prototype is not wrapped by the fix because sync generators do not Await thenables; host-realm async iterators already go through the bridge apply trap. causal_research.bug_semantics: When a template interpolates an object ({{ a }}), TemplateContext.Write calls ObjectToString. For a ScriptObject this reaches ScriptObject.ToString (IFormattable), which walks each member and recursively ObjectToString's the value. A cycle such as a['self']=a therefore re-enters ObjectToString forever. ObjectRecursionLimit is checked only when non-zero, and through 6.5.8 it defaulted to 0 (unlimited), so the thread stack is exhausted and .NET raises an uncatchable StackOverflowException that terminates the host process (DoS). Enabling a positive default (20) makes the existing depth check throw a catchable exception instead.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A logged-in user triggers POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}/update (API, optional style=rebase) or the web Update Pull Request action. Both call services/pull/update.go IsUserAllowedToUpdate, then pull_service.Update, which merges base into the PR head or rebases (force-pushes) the head. After 12cb1d2998, a protected head with CanPush=false no longer hard-denies the update: mergeAllowed is IsUserAllowedToMerge / isUserAllowedToMergeInRepoBranch, which treats code-write (or merge whitelist) as sufficient, so a writer who cannot push the protected head can still move that branch via the PR update button. AllowMaintainerEdit ORs the doer's merge permission on the base branch (post-#36002) or feeds base-repo write into the swapped-PR merge check (pre-#36002), so a maintainer can update a head they cannot push and without inheriting the poster's actual CanUserPush/CanUserForcePush. Impact is integrity of the head branch (unauthorized commits / history rewrite), not unauthenticated RCE.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stripe charge credential replay in mppx (npm, TypeScript machine-payments protocol): the stripe/charge payment method creates PaymentIntents with an idempotency key derived from (challenge.id, spt) but never checks Stripe's 'Idempotent-Replayed' response header. An attacker can replay a valid credential (same spt token) against a new challenge; Stripe returns the already-created PaymentIntent with idempotent-replayed: true, which the server accepts as a new successful payment without charging again, letting an attacker pay once and consume unlimited resources. Fixed in 0.4.11.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data leading to remote code execution in vLLM's PyNcclPipe KV-cache transfer integration (V0 engine). The CPU-side control channel sends Python objects pickled through torch.distributed.TCPStore: PyNcclPipe._recv_impl -> _recv_metadata -> vllm.distributed.utils.StatelessProcessGroup.recv_obj -> pickle.loads(self.store.get(...)). An attacker who can reach the store's TCP port sends an arbitrary __reduce__ payload that executes arbitrary commands when unpickled. Exposure exists because PyTorch's TCPStore master listens on ALL interfaces regardless of the host/IP passed in (the --kv-ip value was used client-side only), so the intended private-network-only scoping never happened; the server bound 0.0.0.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The nbconvert HTTP handlers NbconvertFileHandler (GET /nbconvert/html/<path>) and NbconvertPostHandler (POST /nbconvert) render a user-authored notebook through nbconvert's HTMLExporter, whose default behavior does not sanitize HTML in display_data outputs, and then write that HTML straight to the HTTP response under the Jupyter origin with no sandbox directive in the Content-Security-Policy header. An attacker who can plant an HTML payload in a notebook output therefore gets stored XSS executing in the trusted Jupyter origin against any authenticated victim who opens the exported page: cookies/XSRF token exfiltration, full authority over /api/* endpoints, and kernel RCE. The fix adds an overriding content_security_policy property appending '; sandbox allow-scripts' (configurable via nbconvert_csp_sandbox setting) so executed script content is confined to a unique opaque origin.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated non-SuperAdmin who holds the delegable USER_EDIT right and a CSRF token from the admin UI can PUT JSON to admin/api/user/edit with a chosen userId and is_superadmin. UserController::editUser() in 4.1.3 only calls userHasPermission(USER_EDIT), loads the target via getUserById, then executes User::setSuperAdmin((bool)$isSuperAdmin) (an unguarded UPDATE faquser SET is_superadmin=...). That promotes the actor (or any other account) to SuperAdmin, which short-circuits BasicPermission::hasPermission. The sibling admin/api/user/update-rights path uses the same USER_EDIT gate then Permission::grantUserRight on attacker-supplied right IDs, so the actor can grant rights they do not hold. overwritePassword() in the same file already enforced SuperAdmin/self/protected checks after GHSA-xvp4-phqj-cjr3; these two siblings did not.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Opening a crafted McIdas AREA file from a filesystem path lets attacker-controlled 32-bit header words set image size, file offset, and row stride on a single raw tile. For mode L (and, after 2025, I;16B) that tile is mmap'd. PyImaging_MapBuffer only replaces stride when it is <= 0, then validates offset+ysize*stride against the mapped length and plants row pointers that far apart. Consumers still read im->linesize = xsize*pixelsize bytes from each row, so a stride smaller than the natural row width reads past the mmap into adjacent process memory (disclosure) or faults (SIGBUS). The 12.3.0 fix forces stride to at least one full row before the size check, so the PoC is rejected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PIL/PcfFontFile.py _load_bitmaps() reads per-glyph dimensions (xsize = right - left, ysize = ascent + descent) from the attacker-controlled PCF METRICS section and passes them directly to Image.frombytes("1", (xsize, ysize), ...) without calling Image._decompression_bomb_check(). causal_research.bug_semantics: POST /api/v1/users/{username}/tokens is intended to require password Basic auth via reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth (IsBasicAuth). Basic.Verify nonetheless accepts a PAT as username when the password is empty or x-oauth-basic, or as the password otherwise, sets IsApiToken, and returns the user. group.Verify then stores AuthedMethod as the method name "basic", so AuthShared sets IsBasicAuth and the guard passes without a password. CreateAccessToken next Normalizes caller-supplied form.Scopes and assigns them to the new token with no subset check against the authenticating token's ApiTokenScope. A write:user (or similarly restricted) PAT can therefore mint an all-scoped token and reach endpoints the original token cannot (PoC: GET /api/v1/repos/search forbidden then OK).
