mechanism.impact: Privilege escalation: a low-privilege token yields full account access (the advisory's CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N, CWE-287); an attacker with a leaked restricted token (e.g. write:user) obtains an all-scoped token usable against every API endpoint of the account, including admin/self endpoints.
mechanism.preconditions: The instance has API basic authentication enabled (ENABLE_BASIC_AUTHENTICATION defaults true), the attacker holds any valid PAT for the target account (any scope, no password needed), and the token is supplied in the x-oauth-basic form so parseAuthBasic treats the username as the token. Reverse-proxy API auth being enabled is not required, and the request target must be the token owner's own username (reqSelfOrAdmin).
mechanism.summary: A token-authenticated request in the Authorization: Basic <token>:x-oauth-basic form is marked IsBasicAuth=true because AuthedMethod is the authenticator's name rather than the credential type; that satisfies reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth on POST /users/{username}/tokens, and CreateAccessToken assigns the caller-supplied scopes without any ceiling against the authenticating token's scope, so a restricted token mints a fully privileged all-scoped token without the account password.
mechanism.trigger: Attacker holds any valid PAT of the victim account (the reporter's PoC uses a write:user-scoped token, e.g. a leaked CI secret) and calls POST /api/v1/users/{username}/tokens with body {"name": "poc-escalated", "scopes": ["all"]} and header Authorization: Basic base64(<token>:x-oauth-basic). The route group (routers/api/v1/api.go:1004-1008, reqSelfOrAdmin() + reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth()) passes because ctx.IsBasicAuth is true, and CreateAccessToken normalizes and assigns the requested scope.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real, published CWE-284: token-via-basic fools IsBasicAuth so reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth does not require a password, and CreateAccessToken applies unconstrained request scopes. The smallest first writer of that unconstrained assignment is named-human PR member 2a5ce25 (parent lacks it); the squash landing is only the carrier. The minimum fix is the parent-scope ceiling in #38406/#38426, present in v1.27.0 via de4b827. BIC commit objects have no AI markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Fix-side Assisted-by on fce961b is recorded and does not change BIC attribution. Discovery by a security agent is not introduction.
The advisory's two-part mechanism is verified in the fixed-from tree: a personal access token presented as Authorization: Basic <token>:x-oauth-basic is parsed as a token by services/auth/basic.go parseAuthBasic (isUsernameToken when passwd == "x-oauth-basic"), VerifyAuthToken validates it and sets IsApiToken=true with ApiTokenScope=token.Scope, group.Verify() stores AuthedMethod="basic" (the authenticator's name, not the credential type), routers/common/auth.go:27 maps that to IsBasicAuth=true, and the reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth guard (routers/api/v1/api.go:392-402) checks only that flag, so the request reaches POST /users/{username}/tokens without a password. The handler CreateAccessToken then normalized the caller-supplied scopes and assigned them directly (t.Scope = scope at routers/api/v1/user/app.go:128 in 9155a81b, line 127 at the fix parent d2bd1589) with no subset check against the authenticating token's scope, so a write:user token could mint an all-scoped token -- exactly the reporter's PoC. The BIC is d2128b44f714fcaacdc88865e62f6f9dd8216577 ("Add scopes to API to create token and display them (#22989)", 2023-02-20): its parent 330b16642305458339d12222eea2ee9a1bbb3b64 has no form.Scopes, no t.Scope and no Normalize() in that file, the child adds the Normalize call (line 116) and t.Scope = scope (line 121), and a full-history pickaxe for t.Scope = scope over that path returns only d2128b44f7. The guard-bypass half is a pre-existing enabler: the x-oauth-basic token handling already existed at fb3ffeb18d^:modules/auth/sso/basic.go:71 and was only moved by the 2021 services/auth extraction, and the fix does not touch it; the escalation capability enters with the un-ceilinged scope assignment. The repair is the ceiling added by f69e15af (#38406) and its backport de4b8277 (#38426) -- byte-identical patches over the two mechanism files -- which refuse a child scope the parent does not hold (CanCreateChildScope) and carry public-only down (EnforcePublicOnlyFrom); v1.27.0 contains the fixed form and v1.26.0 still has the bare t.Scope = scope. The BIC commit object carries the named human author zeripath <art27@cantab.net> with a Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton trailer and committer GitHub <noreply@github.com> (PGP-signed squash landing), and no AI trailer, AI co-author or machine-shaped attribution, so a recovered named human identity with no marker closes the case NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Public directory shares are resolved by withHashFile in http/public.go. After loading the share record, directory requests re-rooted d.user.Fs with afero.NewBasePathFs using filepath.Dir(link.Path) (the parent of the shared folder) and then interpreted the extra URL path against that parent. A share of /documents/shared therefore exposed /documents, so unauthenticated GET /api/public/share/{hash} listed sibling directories and GET /api/public/dl/{hash}/<sibling> downloaded sibling files (CWE-200). The 2.61.0 fix keeps BasePathFs but roots it at filepath.Clean(link.Path), the shared directory itself.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Prompt-injection weakness (CWE-94/77 class, "Injection issue") in the hermes-agent memory system: the affected function _scan_memory_content (tools/memory_tool.py) applies a regex BLOCKLIST of injection/exfiltration threat patterns to memory content before it is injected into the system prompt as a frozen snapshot. causal_research.reasoning: Minimum atomic introducer of the vulnerable behavior (paired node can dispatch a full-tools gateway agent run via node.event agent.request) is eace21dcaec, the commit that created node pairing AND the event dispatch together; parent-absence verified (no node pairing, no agent.request event anywhere in parent tree). All later commits are refactors preserving the behavior. The introducer and every subsequent commit on the path are by Peter Steinberger with no Co-Authored-By/Assisted-by trailers or notes (verified via %N and %(trailers) on eace21dcaec, d19bc1562b0, 6a125b554b8, 2f8206862a6). The fix (a77928b1, Jacob Tomlinson) also has no AI markers. Closed causal chain: human-authored code introduced the authorization gap -> verdict NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Advisory's 'broader gateway-side tool access than node RPCs' comparison implies node RPC tool restrictions now exist; I did not inventory the full node RPC tool policy at fix time to quantify the exact escalation width (the RCE claim rests on exec/bash being in the default gateway toolset, which the fix's allowlist removal of exec confirms). Maintainer triage rates severity 'narrow' (critical overstated) because a trusted paired-node foothold is required, but this does not affect the introducer attribution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Environment variable injection (CWE-454/untrusted input in env): OpenClaw loads a workspace .env from the process CWD at startup (dotenv.config) and applies its entries to the process environment with an incomplete deny-list. A malicious workspace .env can set runtime-control variables (update sources, gateway URL/port, ClawHub resolution, browser executable paths, TLS/registry base URLs) thereby redirecting updates, exfiltration endpoints, and executed binaries. Untrusted workspace files were trusted as configuration, and the deny-list was a patch-up effort.

Parent f6dd362d39b8e30bd79ef7560aab9575712ccc11 has no dotenv usage in src (git grep: no hits) -> parent_absent. causal_research.bug_semantics: IDOR / missing authorization (CWE-284/639) in LobeChat's KnowledgeBaseModel.removeFilesFromKnowledgeBase (packages/database/src/models/knowledgeBase.ts), exposed via the tRPC router knowledgeBase.removeFilesFromKnowledgeBase. causal_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox escape (RCE, CVSS 10.0) in @enclave-vm/core: vm context global exposes host closures as own enumerable properties (root: __safe_console holding host-bound console methods called with raw args, __safe_callTool host closure; later __host_memory_track__); raw intrinsic Object (getOwnPropertyDescriptors etc.) is reachable (at root the global Object IS the raw intrinsic since no SafeObject existed; after PR #20 SafeObject only shadowed the global name, {}[['__proto__']].constructor still yields the intrinsic). getOwnPropertyDescriptors(this) leaks host references; host fn .constructor chain yields host Function -> Function('return process')() for RCE; console passthrough also triggers host util.inspect via Symbol.for('nodejs.util.inspect.custom').
causal_research.evidence: Root commit is the single root (git rev-list --max-parents=0 -> 63535a26 only), author David Antoon <david@frontegg.com>, 'initialize project structure with essential configuration files and setup', empty message body (no AI trailers). Root libs/enclave/src/adapters/vm-adapter.ts: baseSandbox=vm.createContext({}); sanitizeVmContext removes only Iterator/AsyncIterator/ShadowRealm/WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry/Reflect/Proxy/performance/Temporal per level (not host refs, not Object statics); Object.entries(safeRuntime) defineProperty'd non-writable/non-configurable/enumerable (includes __safe_callTool host async closure); __safe_console=createSafeConsole which rate-limits but calls method(...args) with original args (host console.log.bind(console)); code wrapped in async IIFE run via script.runInContext(this.context) -> top-level this = contextified global; NO SafeObject at root. Empirical reproduction with these exact shapes on node v22: getOwnPropertyDescriptors(this) exposes __safe_console/__safe_callTool/plain props; PoC1-style (plain host fn own prop .constructor('return process')()) -> [object process]; PoC2-style (g.__safe_console.value.log(obj) with Symbol.for('nodejs.util.inspect.custom') -> inspect.constructor('return process')()) -> [object process]. Advisory GHSA-f229-3862-4942/CVE-2026-27597 (published 2026-02-25) rates critical, claims all <=2.10.1 vulnerable (incl. 1.x), PoCs by c0rydoras, fixed v2.11.x. Fix 9e1a930cd8efa1c4b6fb699f79bba6b4889d1910 (PR #52, squash merge, contains v2.11.0/v2.11.1) neutralizes intrinsic Object statics, makes __host_memory_track__ configurable then deletes it, pre-stringifies console output; commit message carries 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>' (AI-marked FIX, not introducer). Advisory also references release commit 09afbebe4cb6d0586c1145aa71ffabd2103932db (v2.11.0 bump).
causal_research.flaw_origin: Root import commit 63535a26 introduced the whole vulnerable design: host closures defined as non-writable own props of vm.createContext({}) sandbox, user code run via script.runInContext with this=context global, no protection of the intrinsic Object descriptor API, createSafeConsole wrapping host console but calling method(...args) with original args. Later commits (PR #11 double-VM, #14 SecureProxy, #16 memory tracking adding __host_memory_track__, #20 SafeObject) layered defenses/surface but the escape class existed continuously from the initial import through v2.10.1.
causal_research.reasoning: Step 1: vuln = vm sandbox escape via host-object leakage + reachable intrinsic Object descriptor API + raw console passthrough (CWE-94). Step 2: atomic introducer = root commit 63535a26: it is the first writer of every required element (host closures as own context global props, raw intrinsic Object, raw-args console passthrough, runInContext with this=global), it has no parent (root of repo; introducer_parent_absent=true), and it is not a squash (initial import; no decomposition). Later commits added more leak surfaces (e.g., __host_memory_track__ in ef05e863) but the same escape class was demonstrably present at root (reproduced both PoC routes with root shapes). Step 3: root commit has no AI markers (human author, empty body, no co-author trailers, no AI-tool references); the only AI marker in this story is on the FIX commit (Claude Opus 4.6), and an AI-authored fix does not make the introducer AI-written. Closed causal chain: vulnerable design shipped in v1.0.0 from the root import, persisted through v2.10.1, fixed by 9e1a930. Verdict: NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Repo history begins with the monolithic import; any pre-import (private) drafting of the vulnerable module is not visible in git, so AI assistance in the import's composition cannot be fully excluded, but no marker evidence exists.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TLS hostname verification disabled by default (CWE-297 Improper Verification of Certificate with Host Mismatch): jruby-openssl OpenSSL::SSL::SSLContext::DEFAULT_PARAMS sets :verify_hostname => nil, so connecting with VERIFY_PEER validates the certificate chain but never checks that the certificate hostname matches the target host. A MITM can present any valid certificate for a domain they own and JRuby accepts it. PoC in advisory: CRuby 3.4.3 fails with "certificate verify failed (hostname mismatch)" while JRuby 10.0.0.0 / 9.4.2.0 (jruby-openssl 0.15.3) accept. Fixed in jruby-openssl 0.15.4 / jruby 10.0.0.1 / 9.4.12.1.
causal_research.evidence: Identity: class repos include rubysec/ruby-advisory-db (advisory DB repo) but cohort/precise GHSA match pins the real affected repo github.com/jruby/jruby-openssl; member_map/advisory GHSA-72qj-48g4-5xgx ("JRuby-OpenSSL has hostname verification disabled by default", alias CVE-2025-46551; affected rubygems:jruby-openssl introduced 0.12.1 fixed 0.15.4, org.jruby:jruby 10.0.0.0->10.0.0.1 and 9.3.4.0->9.4.12.1; PoC against bad.substitutealert.com with a cert for s8a.me). Fix: 96444ea340a3642b882a53fd5258b9531853d44b (2025-05-07, Charles Oliver Nutter <headius@headius.com>, "Verify hostname by default", single parent 80d37ce600dd584ac9cc6ffefbe137ab4880fcda, released as 0.15.4 on same day via 31a56d690 merge/4a835668 version bump): flips DEFAULT_PARAMS :verify_hostname => nil to :verify_hostname => true; commit message explicitly states "This addresses CVE-2025-46551 and GHSA-72qj-48g4-5xgx". BIC: aefb8235d (2022-01-27, kares) as above; parent 1f9c1366 has verify_hostname => true -> introducer_parent_absent=1. causal_research.bug_semantics: Fickling's safety gate is an incomplete stdlib denylist. check_safety() runs NonStandardImports, UnsafeImports, OvertlyBadEvals, and UnusedVariables. A pickle that STACK_GLOBALs _posixsubprocess.fork_exec, site.execsitecustomize, or atexit._run_exitfuncs is a standard-library import, so NonStandardImports is silent and OvertlyBadEvals treats the imported name as likely_safe. UnsafeImports is silent because those modules are missing from UNSAFE_IMPORTS. SETITEMS/GET can mark the REDUCE result used so UnusedVariables is also silent. check_safety() therefore returns LIKELY_SAFE with zero findings, and fickling.load()/loads() deserializes the payload with pickle.loads, executing the gadget (C-level fork/exec, site customization, or atexit callbacks).

causal_research.bug_semantics: django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware caches successful (200) GET/HEAD responses to requests bearing an Authorization header without ever adding "Authorization" to the response Vary header, unless the view explicitly opted out. Because learn_cache_key() derives the cache key from request.build_absolute_uri() plus only the headers listed in the response Vary header, the credentials-bearing response is stored in the shared server-side cache under the bare URL key, and FetchFromCacheMiddleware then serves that private/authenticated body to any subsequent unauthenticated request for the same URL. The fix teaches UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response to call patch_vary_headers(response, ("Authorization",)) whenever the request carries Authorization and the response is not marked Cache-Control: public (RFC 9111 Section 3.5), which partitions the cache by credential.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can POST a proposal on some event they may read (ShadowAttributesController::add, gated by fetchSimpleEvent on the URL event id) supplies ShadowAttribute.id of an existing proposal. The controller copies request data into $this->request->data['ShadowAttribute'] and calls ShadowAttribute->save() without stripping id. CakePHP Model::set() copies that primary key onto $this->id, so save() UPDATEs the victim row instead of INSERTing. The action also overwrites org_id/email from the caller and event_id from the URL event, so the attacker can poison the proposal value and move/re-own it. Batch import is one trigger (PoC uses batch_import=1); the single-item path has the same save. Setting $this->ShadowAttribute->id = null on the batch path does not help because save() re-reads id from the data array.

mechanism.summary: A client-controlled pageURL is fetched with an authenticated HTTP client: the tool reads the URL from the invocation payload and issues GET on it through a client built from the session OAuth bearer token (or the server ADC/service-account credentials), so an attacker-chosen endpoint receives the caller credentials while the Toolbox server acts as the request origin. The oauth2 transport attaches the token to every destination host, so the SSRF is also a credential leak.
mechanism.trigger: Invoke cloud-healthcare-fhir-fetch-page with pageURL aimed at any host: directly in the tool payload, or indirectly when the agent follows a next-link (Bundle.entry.link.url) returned by a previous FHIR search/everything call, which is exactly what the parameter description tells the model to pass.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: internal/tools/healthcare/fhirfetchpage/fhirfetchpage.go:138 Tool.Invoke, unvalidated GET at line 162 with the token client built at lines 151 (oauth2.NewClient) and 156 (google.DefaultClient) (1f833fb1a12); after the #2273 refactor the same logic is internal/sources/cloudhealthcare/cloud_healthcare.go:292 Source.FHIRFetchPage (pre-fix parent 0cc7b37b733b6a99dad5281af4024b26d730106a).

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-918: fhir-fetch-page takes an arbitrary pageURL and the OAuth HTTP client attaches Bearer credentials regardless of destination. The smallest original introducing change is named-human commit 3b453a4 (PR #1745 member), whose parent tree lacks fhirfetchpage. Main squash 1f833fb and healthcare squash e7ae885 are rejected as BIC because public finer members exist and the first-writer blob is unchanged. The defect shipped from v0.19.1 through v1.4.0 and is closed by 9abf47d in v1.5.0 (host/scheme/path allowlist plus redirect re-validation). The BIC commit object has no AI authorship or co-authorship marker, so the case is NOT_AI. Fix-side AI is also ABSENT and is not used for the verdict.
The described defect is real: the cloud-healthcare-fhir-fetch-page tool passes the client-supplied pageURL straight into http.NewRequestWithContext with no scheme, host or path validation, and the oauth2 transport attaches the caller Authorization bearer token to whatever host is requested. It enters the tree with the squashed healthcare feature commit 1f833fb1a12 (PR #1853), whose parent 22c0b4609d8 contains no healthcare source or tool paths at all. The causal atom inside that squash is PR member 5 (85b16ccfa6001091db88c8e6f8136ef58852539f, feat(tools/healthcare): Add healthcare fhir tools (#1745)), which adds the same unvalidated fetch as internal/tools/healthcare/fhirfetchpage/fhirfetchpage.go; member 9 only renames healthcare to cloud-healthcare. Every causal object on that side carries named-human authorship (Marwan Tammam as author, Yuan Teoh as co-author), no bot identity and no AI trailer, and the AI-marked commits that touch this file are later mechanical refactors that did not write the URL or credential handling. The fix 9abf47d55c0 (PR #3453) adds an https-only two-host allowlist plus a path check against the source project, region, dataset and fhir stores, and re-validates redirects, closing both the SSRF and the exfiltration legs before any client is built.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user with perm_sharing_group POSTs SharingGroupsController::add() (non-REST). The UI packs fields into SharingGroup[json]; the controller json_decodes that blob to $sg = $json['sharingGroup'], calls SharingGroup->create() (which clears $this->id), then save(array('SharingGroup' => $sg)) with no fieldList and no unset of id. CakePHP Model::set() copies a nonempty primary key onto $this->id, _doSave() treats the row as existing, and the datasource updates that sharing group instead of inserting a new one, skipping edit() ownership/extend checks. The caller can therefore change name, membership-related fields, and other columns of an arbitrary sharing group. REST add() is a separate captureSG() path that constructs a new-SG array without id.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the alternative entrance: the REST branch passes request data to SharingGroup::captureSG, which looks an existing SG up by uuid and either whitelists fields in captureSGExisting behind checkIfAuthorised/ownership/site-admin or builds a fixed whitelist array without an id key in captureSGNew, so the id-redirection is specific to the non-REST save of $sg. Checked that create() alone does not neutralise the payload: CakePHP's create() resets the model, but set() then re-assigns $this->id from SharingGroup.id before _doSave decides between update and insert. Checked that only uuid is unset for non-site-admins and that no unset touched $sg['id'] at either the introducer or the fix parent.
mechanism.impact: A low-privileged user holding perm_sharing_group can overwrite fields of any sharing group id they name (name, releasability/distribution, description, active/roaming, org_id and the nested org/server lists), i.e. take over sharing groups they have no edit rights on; the advisory's CVSS v4 vector rates confidentiality high and integrity low (VC:H/VI:L).
mechanism.preconditions: Authenticated MISP account with the perm_sharing_group permission (the add action's ACL is 'sharingGroups'/'add' => perm_sharing_group); a victim sharing group id that exists; an affected build, i.e. before v2.5.40 on the 2.5 line and before v2.4.220 on the 2.4 line.
mechanism.summary: An authenticated user with perm_sharing_group posts an add payload that carries an existing sharing group's primary key; because add() calls $this->SharingGroup->create() and then $this->SharingGroup->save($sg) without removing $sg['id'], CakePHP 2.x sets $this->id from the payload during set() and _doSave issues an UPDATE instead of an INSERT, letting the attacker rewrite a sharing group they were never authorised to edit.
mechanism.trigger: A POST to /sharing_groups/add with data[SharingGroup][id] set to the victim sharing-group id plus the fields to overwrite - either directly as form fields on the legacy entrance or inside the non-REST data[SharingGroup][json] blob as sharingGroup.id - performed by an authenticated account holding perm_sharing_group.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: app/Controller/SharingGroupsController.php add(): the form entrance at bdc6b5fa8 lines 21-25 ($this->SharingGroup->create(); $this->request->data['SharingGroup']['organisation_uuid'] = ...; if ($this->SharingGroup->save($this->request->data))), and the json entrance at the fix parent 3c199cef7 lines 71-90 ($json = json_decode($this->request->data['SharingGroup']['json'], true); $sg = $json['sharingGroup']; ... create(); ... unset($sg['uuid']); ... save(array('SharingGroup' => $sg))), which strips uuid but never id.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-639 mass-assignment on SharingGroupsController::add(): user-controlled id in create()+save() updates another sharing group and bypasses edit ACL. The smallest first-writer is bdc6b5fa8f1b4060a5e4e2624c02d24dba7d419a, whose parent tree has no sharing-group code; later JSON and PSR-2 commits are rewrites/restyles of that missing-id-strip, not new introductions. 687e7cb530ae0e2faaadf5e3e44712258fb3ef1b is the minimum direct fix (unset($sg['id'])), present in v2.5.40 and cherry-picked to v2.4.220. The BIC commit object is named-human iglocska with no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
The GHSA describes a mass-assignment flaw in MISP's sharing-group creation endpoint: add() handed the attacker-controlled payload to create() followed by save(), so a primary key in the payload turned the insert into an update of an existing sharing group outside the edit ACL. The vulnerable save pattern enters this tree with bdc6b5fa8 ('Initial commit', 2015-02-23, 17 files, +932 lines), a commit whose immediate parent 6dcffe1d5 contains no SharingGroupsController.php at all. The non-REST json entrance that the advisory's exploit uses was added by 1afa15120 (2015-04-07), which also saves $sg without removing id, so both entrances are recorded in candidate_set. The official fix 687e7cb53 (2026-06-11) adds unset($sg['id']) right after create(), restoring the insert path; it is an ancestor of HEAD and was cherry-picked to the 2.4 line as 1ab44b01e5. Every BIC-side commit object is an attributed commit from a named human maintainer with an empty trailer block and no AI markers, and the only AI-marked commits in this area are later fix-side sweeps that record this defect as already closed by the human fix. Nothing on the BIC side establishes an AI role, so the verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: HTML-safety bypass / XSS (CWE-79) in ViewComponent: ViewComponent::Base#around_render can return HTML-unsafe strings that bypass the escaping applied to normal #call return values - the around_render return value replaces rendered_template in render_in without any safety re-check. Downstream apps using around_render to wrap/replace/instrument content with user-controlled data become XSS-vulnerable. Amplifier: ViewComponent::Collection#render_in joins per-item results and marks the entire joined output html_safe (ActiveSupport::SafeBuffer), converting raw unsafe output into trusted markup. Fixed in view_component 4.12.0.

ActionView::Helpers::OutputSafetyHelper) so unsafe parts are not promoted to trusted markup; regression tests added (unsafe_around_render_component sandbox fixture + collection/rendering tests). causal_research.bug_semantics: Infinite loop / uncontrolled resource consumption (DoS) in JSON parser: fio_json_parse hits a bare i or I token inside a nested array/object, jumps to the numeral: label, fio_atol consumes zero characters leaving tmp==pos, and since JSON_NUMERAL[i]==0 the integer path is taken without advancing pos; with parser->depth>0 the outer loop spins forever pegging one CPU core. Reachable from http_parse_body -> fiobj_json2obj on Content-Type: application/json. Also affects iodine gem which vendors the same parser (ext/iodine/fio_json_parser.h).
causal_research.evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-41146/GHSA-2x79-gwq3-vxxm) details pinpoint lib/facil/fiobj/fio_json_parser.h numeral block lines 434-468: for bare i/I, fio_atol consumes zero chars, JSON_NUMERAL check misses, pos not advanced, infinite loop while depth>0. Fix commit 51287473 (merge of fork) decomposes to atomic fix 574adfe by Michael Knap (ping@mknap.com, 2026-04-13): adds tmp==pos guards so zero-progress falls to error. git log -S JSON_NUMERAL shows block first appears at 0aa7f47e (2018-01-16, Bo <Boaz@2be.co.il>, committer same, no trailers); parent f6f012f has no strtoll/numeral (grep rc=1) and its if-based parser requires leading digit / NaN / Inf before number parsing, so bare i errored; intermediate commits 91887f6 (extract to header) and 93d08a4 (0.7.0 remaster, file moved to lib/facil/fiobj/) preserve the block unchanged. Fix-side commits carry no Co-Authored-By or AI trailers; merge committer is GitHub merge machinery.
causal_research.flaw_origin: introduced_by_refactor: the 0.7.0-era parser remaster (Refactor JSON for future maintainers) replaced the old if-based dispatch (which only entered number parsing on a leading digit or full NaN/Inf match, else error) with a switch-based parser where case i/I fall through into the numeral: label whose zero-progress path is accepted as an integer
causal_research.reasoning: The minimum atomic introducer is 0aa7f47e (Refactor JSON for future maintainers), authored and committed by Bo Segev (human maintainer) in 2018 with no AI markers of any kind. No evidence of AI co-authorship anywhere in the causal chain -> NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: None material. Iodine gem vendored copy shares the same code and upstream fix; not separately analyzed. OSV GIT range marks introduced at 0 (old tags), but the described flaw mechanism demonstrably begins at 0aa7f47e.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Missing authorization: 9 read-only admin API configuration endpoints in ConfigurationTabController.php used the login-only check userIsAuthenticated() instead of the CONFIGURATION_EDIT permission check userHasPermission(). A logged-in user without admin rights could enumerate system configuration metadata (permission model, cache backend, mail provider, translation provider, template, environment, search/SEO settings) via /admin/api/configuration/* GET endpoints, violating least privilege. CWE-862 Missing Authorization.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated File Browser users are supposed to need Perm.Delete to remove files. DELETE /api/resources/{path} enforces that via resourceDeleteHandler. causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker uploads a file whose filename extension passes fileUpload.fileExtensions (default excludes HTML; e.g. evil.txt) while sending Content-Type text/html (REST header or JSON _ContentType). FilesRouter validates the extension independently of MIME and forwards the user Content-Type into FilesController.createFile. Before the fix, createFile only derived MIME from the filename when contentType was missing; if both extension and Content-Type were present, the user MIME was stored. Adapters that persist and serve that header (S3, GCS) then deliver the body as text/html, enabling stored XSS / content-type confusion (CWE-436). Parse Server's own GET path and GridFS derive Content-Type from the filename at serve time, so the default adapter is not a sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DoS via an unbounded work-queue loop in XmlDecryptionTransform.ProcessElementRecursively, reachable through EncryptedXml decryption of XML-ENC payloads. After each EncryptedData element is decrypted and spliced into the document, the transform selects ALL //enc:EncryptedData nodes under the freshly decrypted content with SelectNodes("//enc:EncryptedData") and enqueues them for further processing; attacker-controlled plaintext can therefore keep injecting new EncryptedData items faster than the queue drains, and the sentinel-style loop (dequeue until the non-generic Queue returns null) has neither a member-count bound nor a depth bound - CWE-835/CWE-400. Network attacker supplies a crafted encrypted XML document to any service decrypting it; result is an effectively unreachable exit condition and CPU exhaustion.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can authenticate to a Budibase-trusted OIDC IdP with a distinct sub and an unverified email claim equal to a victim's address is mapped onto the victim account. oidc.ts buildVerifyFn copies getEmail(profile, jwtClaims) into SSOAuthDetails with no email_verified read; sso.authenticate then loads by IdP sub, and on 404 falls back to users.getGlobalUserByEmail(details.email). The returned victim document is spread through syncUser, so _id, tenantId, roles, admin, and builder are preserved and a session is issued as the victim. Preconditions: OIDC configured; IdP asserts the victim email with email_verified false or absent (Keycloak/Authentik default Verify Email off, self-registration, or profile edit). Counterevidence: a strict IdP that only asserts verified emails makes the token-side claim true, so the Budibase-side missing check is not exploitable there; Google SSO used requireLocalAccount=true but still hit the same email fallback for existing users. Impact: full takeover of any existing user, including global admin.

impact.affected: GitPython through 3.1.50 is affected by the advisory's unsafe-option routes (Repo.archive, Repo.iter_commits/Commit.iter_items, and Repo.blame). Because the AI-authored partial fix 701ce32 first shipped in 3.1.51, GitPython 3.1.51 through 3.1.62 additionally retains the Git.ls_remote ext:: residual: an application forwarding an attacker-controlled remote URL into Git.ls_remote can execute a helper when the target git configuration permits the ext transport. 3.2.0 is the first release with the omitted protocol guard.
impact.effect: Through 3.1.50, unsafe options can execute a helper as the Python process user or truncate a writable file. In 3.1.51-3.1.62, an unclosed helper URL can execute commands as that user when the victim's git transport policy permits ext; otherwise GitPython surfaces a fatal refuse from Git rather than its own UnsafeProtocolError.
impact.prerequisites: For 3.1.50, an application must forward attacker-influenced option names, values or revision strings into a named unsafe-option route. For 3.1.51-3.1.62, an application must forward an attacker-controlled URL to the high-level Git.ls_remote API and the victim's git transport policy (for example ext) must permit the transport helper; current stock git configurations may refuse that helper. No remote service is contacted without such application forwarding.

causal_research.mechanism: Caller-controlled values reach git argv without the library's existing unsafe-option guard. Repo.archive forwards **kwargs through transform_kwargs/dashify into option tokens that land before '--' (git archive --remote=. --exec=<cmd> -- <rev>), git.ls_remote is served by the dynamic Git.__getattr__/_call_process path with no guard (git ls-remote --upload-pack=<cmd>), and Repo.iter_commits/Repo.blame place the caller revision before '--' so --output=<path> makes git open and truncate the file before validating the revision. The guard exists (Git.check_unsafe_options, git/cmd.py:963 at 3.1.50) but is called only from clone/clone_from, fetch, pull and push.
mechanisms: Unguarded transformed keyword options reach git archive (--exec with --remote) and git ls-remote (--upload-pack), giving command execution.
Unguarded leading-dash revision reaches git rev-list / git blame --output=<path>, truncating an arbitrary file before revision validation.
causal_research.reasoning: GHSA-956x is active and valid. The unsafe-option behavior originates at the earliest observable human import boundary, and e6108c79 does not introduce the named routes. The AI-attributed 701ce32 claims to close them and does close the tested unsafe options, but it constructs Git.ls_remote without the reusable protocol guard GHSA-w8jc-g24h-crhw identifies as a residual of this hardening. Thus under the protocol 701ce32 is an incomplete AI remediation and AI_CODE_FLAWED; 9ad28cc4/3.2.0 adds the missing guard. The generic dynamic dispatcher is still outside the named API boundary.
causal_research.remaining_gap: No unresolved route remains in the researched chain: 3.1.51 added the option guards; 3.2.0 added the omitted Git.ls_remote protocol guard. Published 3.1.51 through 3.1.62 retain the residual until that 3.2.0 boundary.

residual_triage.basis: First-party repository advisory GHSA-w8jc-g24h-crhw explicitly names Git.ls_remote's omitted check_unsafe_protocols as a residual of the CVE-2026-67323 hardening; 9ad28cc4 adds that exact guard in 3.2.0.

causal_research.verdict_basis: The earlier human origin is the 2008 import boundary 33ebe7ac, whose named human author has no AI marker. The AI-attributed 701ce32 is the BIC because it claims to harden the CVE-2026-67323 surfaces but adds Git.ls_remote's check_unsafe_options only and omits check_unsafe_protocols/allow_unsafe_protocols; an ext:: URL therefore still reaches git when that victim's transport policy permits it. GHSA-w8jc-g24h-crhw explicitly identifies this as a residual of the 2026 hardening, and 9ad28cc4 adds the omitted protocol guard first shipped in 3.2.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The langgraph-checkpoint-postgres and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite stores persist hierarchical namespaces (tuples like ("memories","alice")) as dot-joined strings (memories.alice) and scope reads with naive SQL string-prefix matching: search builds WHERE prefix LIKE '<flattened>%' from _namespace_to_text(op.namespace_prefix) with no escaping, and list_namespaces used prefix/suffix LIKE '%<path>%' conditions built by the same helper, also without escaping LIKE metacharacters. Because LIKE has no notion of the '.' separator, a scoped search or list_namespaces also matched sibling namespaces whose flattened form shares leading characters (a search scoped to ("foo",) returned rows under ("foobar",)), and unescaped '_'/'%' in labels acted as wildcards (("user_1",) matched ("userX1",)). Since applications commonly use the namespace as a tenant boundary, an ordinary authenticated scoped request returned items belonging to another tenant/user across the Postgres and SQLite stores; no crafted input was required.

code_evidence.summary: Cursor-assisted authentication code added an environment switch that skipped every credential check. On an externally reachable server configured with that switch, anyone could invoke registered agents without a token.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated Public API caller with execution:retry on their API key and only workflow:read on a shared workflow (for example project:viewer) POSTs /api/v1/executions/:id/retry. retryExecution in packages/cli/src/public-api/v1/handlers/executions/executions.handler.ts builds the accessible workflow set with getSharedWorkflowIds(req.user, ['workflow:read']) and passes that set to ExecutionService.retry, which starts a new execution. That crosses the read/execute boundary: project:viewer includes workflow:read and not workflow:execute, while the pre-existing internal REST retry already required workflow:execute. Impact is unauthorized re-execution of a shared workflow (integrity/side effects; CWE-863). Preconditions: sharing or cross-project access, an API key that includes execution:retry, and a reachable Public API. Not unauthenticated.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: an authenticated non-site-admin user whose organisation is not the one stored in Plugin.Import_<module>_restrict POSTs (or otherwise invokes) EventsController::importModule($moduleName, $eventId) with a known restricted import-module name, against an event they can access. Vulnerable code: importModule resolves the module via Module::getEnabledModule($name, 'Import'), which checks only that the Import module is globally enabled and typed as import; it never calls canUse() / Plugin.Import_<module>_restrict. The listing path importChoice() uses getEnabledModules($user, false, 'Import'), which does apply canUse(), so the UI hides the module and the attacker must know the name. Sink: importModule then queryModuleServer() against the Import family and feeds the module result into the event (handleModuleResult / handleMispFormatFromModuleResult), so a module that should have been organisation-scoped can still run and, depending on the user's event modify rights, import or change event data. CWE-863 incorrect authorization; not an unauthenticated issue.

That commit created Plugin.{family}_{name}_restrict, enforced it in getEnabledModules(), and passed $user into importChoice's list lookup, while leaving the already-existing single-module lookup getEnabledModule() and importModule()'s call to it without an org check. Immediate parent 4e44f8dd0ba2be27378192f036a88bac962a5229 has no restrict setting and no org filter, so the bypass did not exist yet. mechanism.impact: CWE-863 module-restriction bypass (GHSA severity MODERATE, CVSS 4.0 VI:L/SA:L): an organisation that was administratively forbidden to use an import module can execute it, and when the caller holds event-modify rights the module output is written into the event through processModuleResultsDataRouter(), i.e. unauthorised import/modification of event data via a module that should have been unavailable to that organisation.
mechanism.preconditions: MISP with the misp-modules integration enabled and at least one import module enabled but restricted to a different organisation (Plugin.Import_<module>_restrict != attacker org_id); attacker is an authenticated user from the excluded organisation who can fetch the target event (Event::fetchSimpleEvent ACL). The attacker does not need site-admin role; results are saved only if the caller also has event-modify rights ($mayModify gate), otherwise the module still executes and returns its output to the caller.
mechanism.summary: An authenticated user whose organisation is excluded by Plugin.Import_<module>_restrict can still invoke that import module by posting its name directly to /events/importModule/<moduleName>/<eventId>: EventsController::importModule() resolves the module through Module::getEnabledModule(), which checks only Plugin.Import_<name>_enabled, so the interface restriction that getEnabledModules() enforces on the module list is bypassed.
mechanism.trigger: Authenticated request to /events/importModule/<moduleName>/<eventId> (the import picker links there, app/View/Themed/Overmind/Events/populate_from.ctp:193) with Plugin.Import_<moduleName>_services_enable/Plugin.Import_<moduleName>_enabled true and Plugin.Import_<moduleName>_restrict set to another organisation's id; the caller does not need to see the module in any list.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-863 gap: per-org Import module ACL is enforced on the list API (getEnabledModules/canUse) but not on the single-module execution path used by importModule (getEnabledModule). The smallest introducing change is the 2018 human commit that added that ACL to only the list path; its parent lacks the ACL entirely. The 2026 fix is the first canUse() on getEnabledModule and is present in v2.5.43 as claimed. The BIC commit object has a named-human author and no AI trailer, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Claude co-authorship on the fix is recorded in fix_ai_marker and does not move BIC-side attribution.
The advisory mechanism is present in this 2.5 tree: EventsController::importModule resolves the requested module with Module::getEnabledModule($name, 'Import') (app/Controller/EventsController.php:7539 in the pre-fix tree d0725fc34f), which applied only the Plugin.Import_<name>_enabled check and never the per-organisation restriction that getEnabledModules() enforces, so a user from an organisation excluded by Plugin.Import_<module>_restrict could still run that import module through /events/importModule/<module>/<eventId>. The restriction control and that list-vs-single asymmetry were introduced together by a2205fba312d72bf4df577679cdbc4bff79b1890 (2018-01-13, 'new: Limit modules to a single organisation'): its parent 4e44f8dd0ba2be27378192f036a88bac962a5229 has no '_restrict' string anywhere in app/Model/Module.php, and the importModule call site is unchanged by the commit, so the parent cannot exhibit the bypass while the child can. The introducing object is a plain human commit by iglocska with no AI trailer, no bot committer and no machine-shaped payload, and both the 2016 lookup it builds on (1f1c8c814) and the 2022 refactor that moved the same inline condition into canUse() (beab72d61) are not introductions. The advisory-referenced fix 0ed79b4d3177f4b9e44040962161a1a436d2587d (2026-07-08, parent d0725fc34f) adds the optional $user argument to getEnabledModule() and rejects the module when canUse() fails, and EventsController::importModule now passes $this->Auth->user(); that hunk set closes the advisory-named path, while the other request-facing callers of the helper were checked and already enforce canUse() themselves. The fix commit carries a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer, but fix-side AI markers are informational only and do not decide the verdict. Verdict NOT_AI: the defect is human-origin, and no AI-authored change introduced, newly exposed or incompletely remediated the advisory mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated delete of a directory whose URL path has a trailing slash (DELETE /api/resources/a/) still removes the directory via Fs.RemoveAll(r.URL.Path), but share cleanup calls DeleteWithPathPrefix(file.Path, userID) with the untrimmed path. Bolt share rows are keyed by Path, typically stored as /a without a trailing slash. s.db.Prefix("Path", "/a/", &links) therefore returns descendants such as /a/child and never the exact /a share. The leftover public hash stays in storage; if the same path is later recreated, unauthenticated GET /api/public/share/<hash>/ serves the new contents.

code_evidence.summary: Claude-assisted MCP servers inserted tool inputs such as agent names, tasks, keys, and namespaces directly into shell command strings. A caller could break out of the quoted argument and run commands on the server; the fix passes each value as a separate process argument.
code_evidence.mechanism: Two Claude-marked commits introduced independent MCP command paths that interpolated request-controlled values into execSync strings. The atomic fix replaces those sinks with execFileSync argument arrays and disables shell interpretation.

steps.title: First AI origin
steps.detail: The restored stdio server built one shell string from MCP key and namespace values and executed it with execSync.

steps.title: Second AI origin
steps.detail: The separate HTTP/SSE server exposed the same command-building pattern to remotely supplied tool arguments.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The fix changed both paths to pass every value as a distinct argv element to execFileSync with shell disabled.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The first origin creates a stdio MCP handler that inserts caller-controlled key and namespace values into one command string. execSync sends that string through a shell, so embedded shell syntax is interpreted instead of treated as data.
The independent HTTP/SSE origin appends remote tool fields such as agent, task, model, provider, and directories to the same shell string before execSync, making the injection path network reachable.

fix_hunks.annotation: The fix removes the stdio command string and passes key and namespace as separate argv entries. They can no longer become shell syntax.
The HTTP/SSE fix builds an argv array for every request-controlled field and invokes npx without shell interpretation, directly reversing the exposed sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A party who can CREATE TABLE in the MySQL database backing a Budibase datasource plants a table name that contains a backtick and a stacked statement. When an administrator runs schema discovery, queryTableNames() (INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES; originally SHOW TABLES) returns that name and buildSchema interpolates it into DESCRIBE wrapped only in literal backticks, without doubling embedded backticks. With the mysql2 connection created using multipleStatements: true, the closed identifier plus semicolon starts a second statement that runs as the datasource user (arbitrary SQL during routine introspection). Preconditions: CREATE TABLE on that database, a later admin schema fetch, and multipleStatements enabled. User-authored SQL queries and the PostgreSQL/MSSQL connector bugs in the same PR are separate surfaces.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that both required components are present in the vulnerable tree and that release 3.38.1 does not contain the fix while 3.39.18 does; checked that the fix is not a cosmetic refactor (quoteMySqlIdentifier doubles embedded backticks) and that its integration tests actually replay the break-out payload and assert the marker table is not created; verified each immediate parent directly (92bab31 lacks the backticked form, b6e6463 lacks multipleStatements); checked that no other table-name interpolation remains in mysql.ts at 3.39.18. mechanism.impact: Arbitrary SQL execution in the datasource during routine introspection (DROP, INSERT, UPDATE, GRANT depending on the connector account's privileges) without the attacker controlling Budibase configuration; CWE-89, HIGH, CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H.
mechanism.preconditions: A MySQL datasource using the built-in connector (multipleStatements: true since 1afc0fbdf8e); the attacker can create or rename a table to a crafted name in that database (or is a malicious tenant in a shared one); a user who can trigger datasource schema refresh does so; the connector account holds the privileges the injected second statement needs.
mechanism.summary: The MySQL connector ran schema introspection with multipleStatements enabled and interpolated INFORMATION_SCHEMA table names into a backtick-quoted DESCRIBE without escaping embedded backticks, so a maliciously named table could break out of the identifier and execute an attacker-chosen second statement during routine schema discovery.
mechanism.trigger: An attacker with CREATE TABLE privilege on the configured MySQL database creates a table whose name embeds a backtick break-out followed by a payload (for example the literal name containing foo, a backtick, then the text: ; DROP TABLE users; -- ); an admin then performs routine schema discovery (opening or refreshing the datasource), causing Budibase to read that name from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES and issue the crafted DESCRIBE.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: packages/server/src/integrations/mysql.ts line 172 multipleStatements: true (introduced by 1afc0fbdf8e) and line 305, the sql template DESCRIBE ${tableName}; wrapped in literal backticks with no escaping (introduced by 4a3f5964152); both present in release 3.38.1 and at the fix parent d0afbb99.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-89 in MySQL schema discovery: unquoted then incompletely backtick-quoted interpolation of database-derived table names into DESCRIBE, made stacked-query-exploitable by multipleStatements. The smallest first writer of that sink is human commit 21b59195; the parent tree has no DESCRIBE. Later human commits only wrap backticks or enable multipleStatements. The BIC commit object has a named human identity and no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI. The minimum MySQL repair is PR member d232bd9 (quoteMySqlIdentifier), landed by merge 2c61f38 and first released in 3.39.18. Successful human repair does not change BIC-side attribution.
Mechanism confirmed: with multipleStatements enabled (mysql.ts:172) the DESCRIBE at mysql.ts:305 interpolated the table name inside unescaped backticks, so a table whose name embeds a backtick plus a second statement breaks out and that statement executes when an admin triggers schema introspection. The exact vulnerable line enters at 4a3f5964152 (2021-12-09), whose parent 92bab31 has the plain un-backticked form; the multi-statement enabler enters independently at 1afc0fbdf8e (2022-09-22), whose parent b6e6463 lacks multipleStatements, and the two compose into arbitrary SQL execution, so both are recorded in candidate_set. The upstream fix (PR #18989, merge 2c61f389, first tag 3.39.18 at the advisory boundary) adds quoteMySqlIdentifier (backtick doubling) and uses it at the DESCRIBE site, with an integration test that creates the malicious table name and asserts the injected marker table is never created. AI role: both causal commits are named-human landings from 2021 and 2022 whose commit objects contain no AI attribution at all, and the repo-level AI activity and fix-side commits are excluded by the protocol. Verdict: NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: multipleStatements: true remains enabled on the MySQL connection after the fix (line 173 at 3.39.18), so protection rests on exhaustive identifier/value quoting rather than disabling multi-statement execution; next minimal question: does any other table- or user-derived value on this connection reach an unquoted SQL position in 3.39.18+ (none found in mysql.ts during this audit)?

causal_research.bug_semantics: On a fresh Open WebUI instance, LDAP ldap_auth and OAuth registration assign admin by reading user-table emptiness (has_users / get_num_users==0) and then inserting with that precomputed role. Because the check is not atomic with the insert (and sessions are not shared by default), concurrent first-user LDAP or OAuth logins can all observe zero users and all become admins, yielding multiple unrestricted administrators. Regular signup_handler had already switched to insert-with-DEFAULT_USER_ROLE then promote only if get_num_users()==1; LDAP and OAuth kept the old check-then-insert window until v0.9.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When NodeVM is constructed with nesting:true, vm2 injects a NESTING_OVERRIDE builtin that makes require('vm2') succeed regardless of the outer require configuration (including require:false). causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can set a conversion name/description or an evaluation comment injects Markdown/HTML resource URLs (http://, https://, file://, or markdown image syntax). causal_research.bug_semantics: In Pydantic v2 generation, untrusted validators objects from --extra-template-data (and from --validators, which copies into extra_template_data) are read by BaseModel._process_validators. Field names and mode are interpolated into Python string literals with unescaped single quotes (fields_str = ", ".join(f"'{f}'" for f in fields); mode_str = f"mode='{mode}'") and emitted verbatim into BaseModel.jinja2 as @field_validator({{ v.fields_str }}, {{ v.mode_str }}). A quote in field or mode breaks the literal and injects a positional Python expression that runs at class-definition time when the generated module is imported. causal_research.bug_semantics: Token-scope propagation flaw (CWE-441) in Gitea's own package registries (conan/container/nuget): package clients authenticate via JWT exchange endpoints (conan /v1/users/authenticate, container /token, nuget api-keys) that issue a 24h package authorization JWT (packageClaims{UserID}) without embedding or checking the caller's API-token scope. The JWT is exchanged once for read-only AND write operations, so a token scoped e.g. read:notification or read:package can mint a full-privilege package token and upload/delete packages (uploads succeed with any token because CreateAuthorizationToken carries no scope and reqPackageAccess' ApiTokenScope check is bypassed: conan/container auth routers never set store Data IsApiToken/ApiTokenScope from the exchange JWT, so the scope gate silently no-ops). Affected < 1.22.2.

Advisory GHSA-f85h-c7m6-cfpm / CVE-2025-68944 (published 2025-12-26, from NVD): 'Gitea before 1.22.2 sometimes mishandles the propagation of token scope for access control within one of its own package registries', patched 1.22.2, reference PR go-gitea/gitea#31967. causal_research.bug_semantics: Cache poisoning / exposure of private data (CWE-1023): django.utils.cache.has_vary_header() compares Vary header values against header_query after lowercasing but without stripping leading/trailing whitespace. causal_research.flaw_origin: Human (non-AI) origin: PR #5470 added the opt-in cookie state-storage strategy in packages/better-auth/src/oauth2/state.ts. Its first member commit, by maintainer Alex Yang, wrote the encrypted oauth_state cookie without the OAuth nonce and left the pre-existing state-cookie equality check in the database branch only, so the new cookie branch had no binding between the callback state query parameter and the cookie payload. The parent tree already contained that equality check (stateCookieValue !== state), so the change dropped it for the new path rather than never having it.
causal_research.flip_condition: Evidence that an AI-attributed object authored the cookie branch itself rather than a later member edit would flip the verdict to AI_ROOT_CAUSE: for example a first-party disclosure binding the aggregate trailer to cfae751f6 or to the cookie-branch hunk, or a recovered member that rewrites that branch before landing. Evidence that the missing binding was introduced by an AI-authored edit while the equality check already covered it would instead support AI_CODE_FLAWED. A future advisory revision withdrawing the cookie-only condition (for example narrowing to a different caller) would change the scope, not this attribution.
causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: attacker sends the victim browser to /api/auth/oauth2/callback/<providerId> with a forged state and an attacker code while the victim holds a live oauth_state cookie. Vulnerable code: the cookie branch of generateState wrote only callbackURL, codeVerifier, errorURL, newUserURL, expiresAt, link and requestSignUp into the encrypted cookie, and the cookie branch of parseState checked decryption and expiresAt only; the equality check that existed before the change (stateCookieValue !== state) survived only in the database branch. Impact: forced login as the attacker identity plus persistent attacker-account linking to the victim row. Preconditions: account.storeStateStrategy set to cookie (the default database is unaffected because the verification row is keyed by state, so a forged state finds no row); genericOAuth with pkce false or a custom getToken/tokenUrl path that does not require the stored codeVerifier; a provider that returns arbitrary code values to the callback URL. Counterevidence: stock social providers with PKCE on are unaffected, and the database branch enforces equality by construction, so the bypass is cookie-strategy only.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory is live and specific, and the mechanism is verifiable in-tree, so this is a real defect rather than a false positive: the cookie branch of the state parser never binds the callback state query parameter to the stored payload, and the fix adds exactly that binding. BIC minimality: the cookie strategy and its unvalidated parse branch first exist in cfae751f6, the first member of PR #5470, which also drops the equality check from the new path while the parent tree applied it; the shipped object is the single-parent squash b5f3bad63, so the granularity is SQUASH_DECOMPOSED with the six members recorded and cfae751f6 as the atomic introducing change. Later history does not move the origin: the e597e18ba member edit changes only optional chaining, the relocation commit 34c8a4bd2 carries the same unbound logic into state.ts (pre-move file has the cookie branch and zero nonce fields), and the oauth-proxy stateless change simply adds another caller after v1.5.0. AI role: the introducing object is authored and committed by a named human maintainer with no AI trailer, and the repository demonstrably emits the review-bot trailer elsewhere in the same window (86 of 2561 commits), so the absence on the BIC object is informative rather than ignorance; the aggregate trailer and the later marked edits are not BIC attribution under the protocol, and the AI-marked relocation and proxy changes do not introduce or enable the missing check beyond paths that were already exposed from v1.4.0. That makes NOT_AI the defensible verdict, with the attribution-level question recorded as the open next step.
causal_research.remaining_gap: No residual mechanism gap was found in the repaired path: the equality check is present in both branches for every caller and shipped in v1.6.2. The open question is attribution-level only, and it is the next smallest question: whether any first-party statement binds the aggregate trailer to the introducing cookie-branch hunk (the snapshotted vendor advisory and the PR page text did not); without that, the marker can only be attached to a later member edit, which the protocol does not treat as BIC attribution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Algorithmic-complexity DoS (CWE-770/772, CVSS 4.0 HIGH): the global gin i18n middleware runs on every request and hands the raw Accept-Language header (up to 1 MiB; MaxHeaderBytes not overridden) to goi18n.NewLocalizer -> golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage. CVE-2022-32149's guard caps '-' chars at 1000 but not '_' (which the parser aliases to '-'), so a 1 MiB '_'-separated malformed tag list drives the parser's quadratic gobble path: ~1.5 s server CPU per unauthenticated request (~7.9 s with X-Locale: en; ~370x amplification). Fixed in 5.0.1 by capping '-'+'_' separators at 32 in the middleware path (fix a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09, 2026-06-04).

causal_research.bug_semantics: In users-permissions legacy JWT mode (the default), verify() authenticates Content API bearers by calling jsonwebtoken.verify with the shared jwtSecret. When the algorithms option is omitted (empty {} options), jsonwebtoken accepts whatever HMAC alg is declared in the token header, so an attacker who already has jwtSecret can mint HS384 or HS512 tokens that verify successfully even if operators expected HS256-only. After #24346, refresh/session mode pins HS256 via SessionManager, but the default legacy path still used {} unless plugin::users-permissions.jwt.algorithm was set. jsonwebtoken@9 already blocks alg=none and asymmetric/HMAC key-confusion; the residual issue is an unpinned HMAC allowlist. The 2026 fix always passes algorithms: [configured || 'HS256'].

causal_research.bug_semantics: On the self-hosted Next.js Node server, WebSocket upgrade requests are handled by upgradeHandler in packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts. resolveRoutes parses req.url (including HTTP absolute-form targets such as GET http://127.0.0.1:internal/secret HTTP/1.1) and returns parsedUrl.protocol whenever that URL has a scheme. Before the fix, the upgrade path proxied with proxyRequest/httpxy as soon as parsedUrl.protocol was set, without requiring that routing had finished an explicit external rewrite (finished) and without rejecting redirect statusCodes. That lets an untrusted client force the origin to open a WebSocket/HTTP proxy to an arbitrary internal or external host, including cloud metadata, which is CWE-918 SSRF. The ordinary HTTP request handler already gated proxying on finished && parsedUrl.protocol, so the same absolute-form request was not treated as a safe rewrite on that path. The May 2026 guard applies those same checks to upgrades: proxy only when finished && parsedUrl.protocol && !statusCode, otherwise end the socket. Configured ws/http external rewrites still work because they set finished without a redirect statusCode.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-424 improper protection of alternate path: the AWS API MCP Server's file-access restriction (workdir confinement, default WORKING_DIRECTORY, and no-access mode; unrestricted opt-in) validates file:// and fileb:// path arguments only through the server-side parameter parser and, after aa937bb2, through a swapped-in validated RESTRICTED_URI_HANDLER (get_file_validated) registered on awscli's 'load-cli-arg' event. AWS CLI SHORTHAND syntax arguments (compact key-value lists parsed by awscli.shorthand.ShorthandParser, e.g. --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=file:///etc/passwd,...}]', --metadata 'key=file://...', or any argument containing embedded file:// inside shorthand) are expanded through awscli.shorthand.LOCAL_PREFIX_MAP, which still mapped file:// -> raw awscli get_file with NO validation. A malicious MCP prompt can thus read arbitrary local files (e.g. /etc/passwd, ~/.aws/credentials) into AWS API request parameters even in workdir and no-access modes, exposing the contents in the MCP client context (e.g. reflected in CLI output or exfiltrated via AWS service calls). Advisory scope: >= 0.2.14, < 1.3.9 (fixed 1.3.9)

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-73/CWE-200 arbitrary local file read: IndexFile.remove() and Head.checkout() forward **kwargs into `git rm` (git/index/base.py remove: self.repo.git.rm(args, paths, **kwargs)) and `git checkout` (git/refs/head.py checkout: self.repo.git.checkout(self, **kwargs)) with no unsafe-option guard. Combined --pathspec-from-file=<file> + --pathspec-file-nul makes git treat the whole file as one NUL-delimited pathspec; the unmatched-pathspec error quotes it verbatim, returning the entire contents of a caller-chosen file in GitCommandError.stderr.
causal_research.evidence: Identity: alias-962f88a9b146432859cc9a82 = sha256(sorted-members hash) of singleton {GHSA-hh9p-6wh2-4mfc} (verified by brute-force single-id hash over all 32 gitpython-developers/gitpython GitHub security-advisories IDs). GHSA-hh9p-6wh2-4mfc (medium 6.5, CWE-73/CWE-200, published 2026-08-04, vulnerable <= 3.1.57 (pip)): unguarded **kwargs forwarding lets a caller pass --pathspec-from-file=<file> + --pathspec-file-nul to IndexFile.remove() (-> git rm) and Head.checkout() (-> git checkout); git's unmatched-pathspec error then quotes the whole file, leaking its contents in-band via GitCommandError.stderr (PoC in advisory; verified on 3.1.57; precision controls: `git status` and the guarded checkout-index leak 0/3 lines). (2) ace1fed6321bb8dd6d38b2f58d7cf815fa16db7a 'head.checkout method added including test' (2009-11-04, parent f1e9df152219e85798d78284beeda88f6baa9ec7) first wrote `def checkout(self, force=False, **kwargs)` forwarding `self.repo.git.checkout(self, **kwargs)`; parent has no def checkout (grep count 0). code_evidence.summary: Copilot-assisted sandbox code silently fell back to a plain subprocess when Landlock was unavailable, letting untrusted code bypass the configured filesystem and network restrictions.
code_evidence.mechanism: SandlockSandbox.execute() and run_command() treated unavailable Landlock as a cue to instantiate SubprocessSandbox with the same configuration. That backend did not enforce the requested Landlock filesystem allowlist or network=False boundary, so execution continued with the host user's filesystem and network access.

steps.detail: The Copilot-coauthored file created both execution entry points with an automatic SubprocessSandbox fallback whenever the Landlock backend reported unavailable.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The later patch rejects insufficient Landlock support during construction and removes both fallback branches; callers must explicitly choose the weaker backend.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated remote code execution in the crawl4ai Docker API deployment. The POST /crawl (and /crawl/stream) endpoint accepts a hooks parameter containing attacker-controlled Python source. UserHookManager.compile_hook() in deploy/docker/hook_manager.py compiles and runs that source with exec(hook_code, namespace) inside a namespace whose __builtins__ is a hand-built whitelist ('safe_builtins') that explicitly includes __import__ (and __build_class__), with asyncio/json/re pre-imported into the namespace. The AST 'validation' in compile_hook only checks syntax/function-shape and imposes no import capability restriction, so the sandbox whitelist is the sole security boundary and its inclusion of __import__ defeats it.

causal_research.bug_semantics: command_injection
causal_research.evidence: GHSA-75xq-5h9v-w6px / CVE-2026-42258 (ruby net-imap, CWE-77/CWE-93, medium severity; affected >=0 <=0.4.23, >=0.5.0 <=0.5.13, >=0.6.0 <=0.6.3; first patched 0.4.24/0.5.14/0.6.4): Net::IMAP command argument handling accepted Symbol (IMAP system flag) arguments and serialized them directly as the atom '\'+symbol.to_s with no validation; a Symbol containing atom-specials (SP, CRLF) is sent verbatim to the socket, allowing CRLF/IMAP command injection (e.g., terminate current command, inject 'DELETE mailbox'). Fix: master commit 9db3e9d60 (nick evans, 2026-02-19, 'Strictly validate symbol (\flag) arguments', first release v0.6.4) adds class Flag < Atom with Flag.validate (ASCII-only + rejects ATOM_SPECIALS via ResponseParser::Patterns) in lib/net/imap/command_data.rb; validate_data now calls Flag.validate(data) for Symbols and send_data routes through Flag[data].send_data instead of the old send_symbol_data (put_string('\\'+symbol.to_s), since deleted). Backports: v0.5.14 via merge 6bf02aef (PR #662, cherry-pick 9a0a851 of 9db3e9d60), v0.4.24 via merge aec06996 (PR #663); verified v0.4.24 contains Flag.validate and v0.4.23 does not (git grep rc=1).
causal_research.flaw_origin: introduced_with_feature
causal_research.reasoning: The unvalidated Symbol-flag serialization was born with the library: root commit ffd0f98c (2000-10-13, shugo, first import of lib/net/imap.rb from ruby SVN, git-svn-id trunk@1000) already contains format_symbol(symbol) returning '\\'+symbol.to_s in format_data's 'when Symbol' branch, with zero validation and no parent commit (root of the repo history); the behavior was preserved verbatim through renames (send_symbol_data, c7c0f78 2004) and refactors (move to command_data.rb, 64d1080d 2021). The fix (2026) adds the missing validation 26 years later. Introducer author shugo is a long-time Ruby core committer; fix author nick evans is net-imap maintainer; 13-term AI-marker scan clean (0 hits) on all of introducer, fix, and both backport merges. No AI authorship signal on the vulnerable lines or the fix; flaw is an original human design omission (assumption that Symbol inputs are always vetted atoms).

causal_research.bug_semantics: When prompt/multimodal embedding inputs are enabled, vLLM deserializes attacker-controlled base64 torch.save blobs with torch.load(weights_only=True) and, on the Completions prompt-embeds path, immediately calls tensor.to_dense(). From PyTorch 2.8.0 onward, sparse COO/CSR/CSC invariant checks are off by default, so negative or out-of-bounds sparse indices are accepted and to_dense() can crash the process, exhaust memory, or perform an OOB write-what-where. CVE-2025-62164's 0.11.1 remediations only defaulted --enable-prompt-embeds/--enable-mm-embeds to false; the same loaders remain reachable and unvalidated when an operator turns the feature on. CVE-2026-56340 is that residual missing-validation bug, closed in 0.13.0 by wrapping load+densify in torch.sparse.check_sparse_tensor_invariants() (and applying the same check to image/audio embedding MediaIO).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Kiota's PHP writer interpolates OpenAPI-controlled strings into generated PHP double-quoted literals. PHP evaluates $var, ${expr}, and {$obj->prop} inside those literals when the generated client runs, so a malicious spec can inject PHP/OS commands. The first executable sink was request-body media types: KiotaBuilder copied operation.RequestBody.Content keys into CodeMethod.ContentType, and WriteRequestGeneratorBody emitted them as "{contentType}" in setContentFromParsable. Additional sinks later used the same unescaped double-quote pattern for Accept headers, discriminator property names, query-parameter annotations, and (after a 2024 single-to-double quote switch) enum wire values. Shared SanitizeDoubleQuote only escaped quotes/backslashes/controls, not $, so ${...} survived sanitizer wrapping until SanitizePhpDoubleQuoteLiteral ($ -> \$) was added.
evidence: bundle sha256sum matched b08a741c9131a3e3ac3ff9217714c8ba1f97fd0612cd7cb232ac9d56712afdc9; clone HEAD 7c0a5da389e3048bf5e2a176017662a201e6903c.
https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-59859 state=PUBLISHED; description: PHP generator embedded OpenAPI strings via SanitizeDoubleQuote() without escaping $; fixed in 1.29.1 and 1.32.4.

causal_research.bug_semantics: RAG collection-level ACL bypass via Milvus filter-expression injection in multitenancy mode. On POST /api/v1/retrieval/query/collection and /query/doc, an authenticated non-admin supplies arbitrary collection_names; filter_accessible_collections/_validate_collection_access treat any name that is not a known KB id (and matches no other internal prefix) as a legacy/ephemeral collection and allow it. With VECTOR_DB=milvus and ENABLE_MILVUS_MULTITENANCY_MODE=true, that same user-controlled name becomes a resource_id and is interpolated UNESCAPED into a Milvus boolean expression `resource_id == '<name>'`; a payload like x' or resource_id != '' or resource_id == 'x turns the filter into a tautology over the shared backing collection, so Milvus returns private knowledge-base chunks belonging to other users.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated remote code execution via command injection in Coolify's CA certificate management feature (GHSA-7g97-c4xv-3cjx, affected < 4.0.0-beta.464). Any authenticated user with access to the server CA certificate management UI (app/Livewire/Server/CaCertificate/Show.php, saveCaCertificate -> writeCertificateToServer) could submit the CA certificate content which was interpolated verbatim into a remote shell command string: "echo '{$this->certificateContent}' > $caCertPath/coolify-ca.crt" passed to remote_process/instant_remote_process over SSH; appending shell metacharacters (e.g. a valid PEM followed by '; id > /tmp/pwned ; echo ') executed arbitrary commands as the configured SSH user (typically root or docker-group), giving complete compromise of the managed server. Fix (fe36b7068) base64-encodes the cert content before embedding it in the command (echo '<base64>' | base64 -d | tee ...) and re-exports the saved certificate through openssl_x509_export so only a normalized PEM (no shell metacharacters) is ever embedded; same pattern also hardened in app/Actions/Server/InstallDocker.php and app/Models/Server.php generateCaCertificate().

causal_research.bug_semantics: DoS via livelock: Concurrent::AtomicReference#update enters a permanent busy retry loop ('true until compare_and_set(...)') when the stored value is Float::NAN. The numeric CAS wrapper (numeric_cas_wrapper.rb) guards the underlying atomic swap with a Ruby equality pre-check ('return false unless old == expected'); since Float::NAN == Float::NAN is always false in Ruby, compare_and_set never succeeds and #update spins forever, repeatedly evaluating the caller's block (CPU burn / thread hang).
causal_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2026-54904 / GHSA-h8w8-99g7-qmvj ('AtomicReference#update livelocks when the stored value is Float::NAN', fixed in 1.3.7). OSV GIT 'fixed' commits: 4c8fc28ab6bb9bd8258a4c0c2fa6d35ebe77b3cb = the 1.3.7 release commit (version.rb/CHANGELOG only); actual code fix 6e37e0644b83b182971dc540d2e4bee38df61386 (2026-06-08, Joshua Young, 'Fix AtomicReference#update livelock when stored value is Float::NAN') special-cases NaN in numeric_cas_wrapper.rb compare_and_set ('expected_nan = old_value.respond_to?(:nan?) && old_value.nan?') and adds spec coverage (test_update_nan, test_numeric_cas_nan) with Timeout. Introducer verification: git show b52632d shows both files added with the exact vulnerable constructs; parent fb916663ab6cf42b62e565a8bf241b93ab94d66a has no numeric_cas_wrapper.rb, no atomic_reference files, and no Atomic#update (only unrelated TimerTask/DataFlow update methods). Content identical from 2014 through the 2023 file split (45bcb660) until the 2026 fix.
causal_research.flaw_origin: b52632d9da311b69a6bdb8bfdac0d0fd0fbda65c 'wip: Initial import of ruby-atomic.' (2014-06-04, Jerry D'Antonio) imported the ruby-atomic implementation into concurrent-ruby, which contains BOTH required components in their original form: lib/concurrent/atomic_reference/numeric_cas_wrapper.rb (the ==-based numeric CAS guard plus its own retry loop) and lib/concurrent/atomic_reference/direct_update.rb (Atomic#update with 'true until compare_and_set(old_value = get, new_value = yield(old_value))'). causal_research.bug_semantics: SSRF via unchecked redirects (CWE-918): the shared axios SSRF guard (packages/service/common/api/axios.ts addSSRFInterceptor) validates only the INITIAL request URL with isInternalAddress() before handing the request to axios, and axios follows redirects by default (follow-redirects auto-jump happens after the request interceptor). causal_research.bug_semantics: APK packages are consumed (by apko during image builds, including in melange's build/test flows) with an incomplete integrity chain: only the control section (.PKGINFO etc.) hash is checked against the signed APKINDEX (PkgHash over control.tar.gz), while the data section hash (sha256 of data.tar.gz, emitted by melange as 'datahash' in .PKGINFO and by apko metadata) is never re-verified against the actual installed payload. An attacker who controls a mirror, poisons the APK cache, or MITMs the fetch can substitute arbitrary data.tar.gz contents while the signed control hash still validates, so attacker-controlled files end up inside built images/build environments.

causal_research.bug_semantics: IDOR in AnythingLLM TTS endpoint: GET /api/workspace/:slug/tts/:chatId returns the text-to-speech audio of another user's chat response within the same workspace. causal_research.bug_semantics: In uutils coreutils rm, the dot/dotdot guard in handle_dir() calls clean_trailing_slashes() first (which collapses './//' to './') and then path_is_current_or_parent_directory(). The latter is a byte-pattern matcher that only accepted exactly '.', '../', '../', './.', or strings ENDING in '/.', '/..', '/./', '/../' — it never matched the bare current-directory form './', so 'rm -rf ./', './/', './//' (and '../') fell through to remove_dir_recursive(), which silently deleted every file and subdirectory of the current directory, then printed a misleading "cannot remove './': Invalid input" as the recursive walk unwound, masking the data loss. GNU rm refuses all of these without deleting anything.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py SessionMiddleware.process_response, the 'Vary: Cookie' header was emitted only when the session had been accessed (request.session.accessed). When SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST=True, the separate (modified or SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST) and not empty branch still calls response.set_cookie() with a fresh session key even though no code touched the session, so responses can carry a per-user Set-Cookie without Vary: Cookie. An intermediate cache serving a public page that never accesses request.session stores and then replays that Set-Cookie to other visitors, letting a remote attacker fixate/steal another user's session.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CRUDComponent::delete() optionally runs params['validate'] and is supposed to skip the delete when that callback throws. The success gate was written as `$validationError === null && request->is('post') || request->is('delete')`. Preconditions: an authenticated caller who can hit a delete endpoint that both accepts DELETE and supplies a validate callback (roles still-in-use, template authorisation, galaxy fetchIfAuthorized). Impact: unauthorized or policy-forbidden deletion of those records.
