causal_research.bug_semantics: .NET corehost library-host (libhost) scenarios - COM activation, C++/CLI (IJW), and custom component hosts calling hostfxr/hostpolicy directly - have no managed app and therefore no app directory. In deps_resolver_t::resolve_probe_dirs the fallback taken when the app's .deps.json is missing unconditionally adds m_app_dir as a probe path and sets m_coreclr_path via file_exists_in_dir(m_app_dir, LIBCORECLR_NAME). With an empty m_app_dir those lookups collapse onto the process current working directory, so coreclr.dll / libcoreclr.so is discovered relative to wherever the host process was launched, and related loader paths (hostfxr, hostpolicy, coreclr) were handed to pal::load_library without any absolute-path validation. An attacker who can place files in the launch directory (CWD) of such a process supplies his own coreclr binary and gains arbitrary native code execution inside it (DLL/preload hijack, network-reachable per CVSS).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Ruby on Rails Action View tag helpers XSS via blank attribute names: tag_options()/tag_option() emit an attribute whenever the value is non-nil, without skipping blank (empty-string/nil) attribute names; ERB::Util.xml_name_escape('') returns an empty string, so tag('img', 'src' => '/nonexistent.png', '' => '/onerror=alert(1)') renders . The HTML tokenizer treats the unexpected '=' as a parse error, and the attacker-controlled attribute VALUE ("...") is then misparsed as a separate attribute name (onerror=...) - malformed HTML susceptible to mXSS (HackerOne report 3078929). Apps that let users specify custom HTML attributes are affected (CWE-79, cvss_v4 2.3).

Root commit db045dbbf6 (2004-11-24, 'Initial', git-svn r4, no parents - git rev-list --parents shows only itself) already emits blank names: options.collect { |pair| "#{pair.first}=\"#{html_escape(pair.last)}\"" }. mechanism.counterevidence: Checked six falsification routes. (1) REST path returns restResponsePayload before the dropdown block (parent edit() lines 96-97), so no leak via API. (2) On save success CRUD->edit redirects to index, so only the failed-validation re-render exposes the dropdown. causal_research.bug_semantics: In vLLM's V0 engine with tensor parallelism spanning multiple hosts, MessageQueue (vllm/distributed/device_communicators/shm_broadcast.py) mediates writer-to-reader broadcast of Python objects. A secondary host constructs its queue via MessageQueue.create_from_handle(), which opens a ZeroMQ SUB socket and connects to the primary host's XPUB socket; dequeue() then receives raw bytes from that socket and deserializes them with pickle.loads(recv). ZeroMQ PUB/SUB here has no authentication or encryption, and pickle is a code-executing deserializer, so anyone who can send bytes to a secondary host's SUB endpoint (spoofed peer, compromised or malicious primary host, ARP/DNS/IP redirection inside the cluster network) gets arbitrary code execution on every reader host. Because compromise flows outward from the primary, the advisory frames it primarily as a lateral-movement escalation: an attacker who controls the primary host pivots to all secondaries when they deserialize crafted payloads (advisory-referenced vulnerable lines: shm_broadcast.py L295-L301 SUB connect and L468-L470 recv+pickle.loads at ref c21b99b91241409c2fdf9f3f8c542e8748b317be).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Potential denial-of-service (algorithmic complexity, CWE-407) in django.utils.text.Truncator: TruncateHTMLParser.handle_endtag() used deque.remove(tag) to remove a tag from the stack on every end tag; with crafted HTML input containing a large number of unmatched end tags, each remove() triggers a linear full-stack scan, making overall runtime quadratic. causal_research.bug_semantics: Serialization injection (CWE-502). Serializable.toJSON() in langchain-core serializes free-form constructor kwargs without escaping plain objects that carry the internal 'lc' marker key (lc:1, type, id). When such JSON is later deserialized via load()/parse(), the trusting reviver interprets any object with the lc structure as a legitimate LangChain constructor/function/secret marker: it instantiates registered classes from the import map and substitutes values from the loader's SecretMap for {lc:1,type:'secret',id:[key]} entries. Attacker-controlled free-form data (e.g. message content/kwargs reaching JSON.stringify of a serialized graph) can therefore inject constructor or secret markers that, once the serialized payload is loaded by a downstream consumer, instantiate arbitrary registered constructors or exfiltrate the loader's secret values (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY). Affected @langchain/core <0.3.80 / <1.1.8 and langchain <0.3.37 / <1.2.3.
causal_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2025-68665 (aliases GHSA-r399-636x-v7f6): toJSON() did not escape objects with 'lc' keys when serializing free-form data in kwargs, so such keys are treated as legitimate LangChain objects during deserialization; patched in core 0.3.80/1.1.8, langchain 0.3.37/1.2.3. GIT ranges: introduced 822db857 (v1.0.0 release commit, 2025-10-20) and '0'; fixes listed de32b32b (version-packages release, 2025-12-22)/d0c905dd (release, 2026-08-14)/2954498b (docs commit; OSV artifact)/e5063f9c. Direct code fix: e5063f9c 'fix!(core/langchain): hardening for load (#9707)' (Hunter Lovell, 2025-12-22) adds libs/langchain-core/src/load/validation.ts (LC_ESCAPED_KEY='__lc_escaped__', needsEscaping/escapeObject) and rewires Serializable.toJSON() to run every kwarg through escapeIfNeeded BEFORE replaceSecrets/mapKeys, so plain objects containing an 'lc' key serialize as {"__lc_escaped__":{...}} and are returned as data by the loader. Pickaxe: first occurrence of replaceSecrets at f78b0c1f (reformat), first occurrence of the whole system at fb60a1a9 (git log --all --diff-filter=A langchain/src/load/index.ts -> fb60a1a9; parent 2835c133 lacks both load/index.ts and schema/load.ts, verified via git cat-file -e exit 128). First tag containing introducer: 0.0.1 (vulnerability present since the first release).
causal_research.flaw_origin: Human-authored foundational serde design. The entire serialization system - Serializable.toJSON() passing constructor arguments through unescaped and the load() reviver that trusts embedded serialized markers - was first written by Nuno Campos (LangChain co-founder) in commit fb60a1a9 (2023-05-26, 'Implement new serialization format...'); both langchain/src/load/index.ts and langchain/src/schema/load.ts are brand-new (A) in that commit and absent from its parent. The 2023-06-01 follow-up f78b0c1f ('Review serde format, implement secret management') renamed the marker from v:1/identifier to lc:1/id and added the secret marker type, but its parent already carried the identically-shaped vulnerable pass-through (v-format toJSON with unescaped arguments + trusting v-reviver), so f78b0c1f is a format change, not the first writer. Code lineage: langchain/src/schema/load.ts -> langchain-core/src/load/serializable.ts (via 2023 core split, 2025-08 rearrange acfaf7050, 2025-10 v1 main replacement 9e6eb913). Exploitability persisted until the Dec 2025 hardening.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Two chained flaws let any network-reachable caller of the --transport streamable-http server (1) invoke MCP tools with no authentication and (2) recover the operator's long-lived Meta access token. Tool handlers then fall back to the META_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable, so an unauthenticated caller executes tools with the operator's credentials. Second, make_api_request() error handling in meta_ads_mcp/core/api.py:262-270 serializes the raw httpx response/request URLs — 'url': str(e.response.url) and 'request_url': str(e.request.url) — into the JSON-RPC error body ('full_response'); Meta's Graph API sends access_token as a query parameter, so a 4xx response echoes the operator credential verbatim to whoever triggered the error, which after flaw (1) is any unauthenticated network caller.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Apache Airflow XCom PATCH endpoint acceptance of forbidden keys: PATCH /api/v2/xcomEntries/{key} (XComUpdateBody model) never validates FORBIDDEN_XCOM_KEYS (reserved serialization keys: return_value, __classname__, etc.), unlike the POST create path (XComCreateBody validator added in #64148 as the CVE-2026-33858 fix). causal_research.bug_semantics: Fission Package CRDs carry spec.environment.namespace. buildermgr, running with a cluster-wide service account, used that field as the namespace argument to Environments(...).Get without requiring it equal Package.metadata.namespace, then selected the Environment's builder pod (in the Environment's namespace when not default) and invoked the user/env build command. Build stdout is stored verbatim in Package.status.buildlog. A subject with packages.fission.io/create in ns-attacker can point spec.environment.namespace at ns-victim, run code (for example an npm preinstall hook) inside the victim builder, and exfiltrate that namespace's fission-builder bearer token, which can read Secrets and ConfigMaps in the victim namespace. Empty env namespace remains accepted and defaults to the package's own namespace.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated SSE and stateful Streamable HTTP servers treated the client-supplied session key as the only authorization for attaching a request to an existing session. SseServerTransport.handle_post_message resolved request.query_params['session_id'] to a writer in _read_stream_writers and forwarded JSON-RPC without comparing scope['user'] to the creator. StreamableHTTPSessionManager._handle_stateful_request did the same with the Mcp-Session-Id header against _server_instances. A second bearer-authenticated principal who obtained the UUID could inject messages; SSE delivered results to the original event stream, while Streamable HTTP returned them to the injector. The 1.27.2 fix stores AuthorizationContext (OAuth client_id plus token iss/sub when present) at session creation and answers a mismatched principal with the same 404 as an unknown session.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Default-config authentication bypass (CWE-1188). The installation/update seeds api.apiClientToken as an empty string; AbstractController::hasValidToken() compares it to the client-supplied x-pmf-token using strict inequality (`!==`). When no token is configured, an attacker sending an empty x-pmf-token header passes `'' !== ''` == false so no exception is thrown, reaching write endpoints (faq/create, faq/update, category, question) that rely solely on this guard and allowing unauthenticated FAQ/category/question creation and modification. Fix in 4.1.3 rejects empty configured tokens and switches to constant-time hash_equals with a string type guard.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A workflow that uses the Guardrails node classifies untrusted end-user text with a connected chat model. runLLM places default system rules (LLM_SYSTEM_RULES / per-check prompt) in the system message and the user text in a separate human '{input}' turn. Those default rules told the model to ignore contradictory instructions and that anything below a ######## marker was data to validate, but the marker sat at the end of the system prompt with nothing after it, so crafted human-turn text could override the default instructions. Classifier JSON was parsed with a non-strict Zod object, so extra or nested fields were stripped and a payload such as {analysis:{flagged:true,confidenceScore:0.8}, flagged:false, confidenceScore:0.2} could be accepted as not-flagged. Impact is integrity of the guardrail decision (Pass vs Fail routing), not a sandbox escape. Preconditions: a workflow actually runs an LLM Guardrails check (jailbreak/NSFW/topical/custom) on attacker-controlled input.

mechanism.preconditions: Guardrail node in classify mode with an LLM-backed check enabled and a chat model attached; the customize-system-message option left off so the default rules (the advisory's 'default guardrail instructions') apply; attacker-controlled text reaches the node's text input. mechanism.summary: Trigger: end-user text carrying crafted instruction-style content reaches the Guardrail node's LLM check. Vulnerable code: the check builds a system message from default rules ending with the '########' delimiter instruction and accepts the model's verdict through a non-strict zod schema that silently tolerates extra or shadowed fields. Impact: the guardrail records a steered 'safe' verdict, so content the workflow owner believed was filtered passes downstream (workflow integrity; CWE-20).
mechanism.trigger: A workflow item carries attacker-controlled end-user text into a Guardrail node configured with at least one LLM-backed check (jailbreak, nsfw, topical alignment, or a custom LLM guardrail) while the node's customize-system-message option is off, so the default LLM_SYSTEM_RULES apply; the crafted input either redefines the '########' boundary (supplies its own delimiter/instructions or claims the guardrail was already satisfied) or dictates an alternative JSON shape, steering the model into a verdict that is not the guardrail's own judgement.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Filesystem path traversal family (CWE-22/CWE-697; LangChain < 1.3.9). (1) FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware (libs/langchain_v1/langchain/agents/middleware/file_search.py) validates only the starting base dir: glob_search runs base_full.glob(pattern) on an unchecked pattern (a '..' pattern like '../../etc/passwd' escapes the root; absolute patterns raise but are unhandled) and grep_search's _search_content walks base_full.rglob('*') following symlinked directories, so files outside root_path are enumerated/read and returned; results are only converted with relative_to(self.root_path) after the fact. causal_research.bug_semantics: Multichannel audio ingested through vLLM's audio pipeline was loaded via librosa.load(..., sr=None) with librosa's default mono=True, which downmixes multi-channel input with numpy.mean (librosa.core.audio to_mono), plain channel averaging rather than the ITU-R BS.775-4 weighted downmix used by consumer playback. causal_research.bug_semantics: Any caller with a valid Better Auth session can POST /sso/register (createOIDCProvider originally; registerSSOProvider later) with attacker-chosen oidcConfig.tokenEndpoint, userInfoEndpoint, jwksEndpoint, and discoveryEndpoint as unconstrained strings. mechanism.counterevidence: Checked and rejected: the discovery branch (skipDiscovery false) already routed supplied URLs through validateDiscoveryUrl and the isTrustedOrigin predicate inside discoverOIDCConfig at 23094a628, so the omission is specific to the direct registration and update path rather than the whole plugin; issuer is URL-format validated, which restricts syntax but not host; a grep of the f9102b154 blob for private, loopback, 169.254 and trustedOrigins returns nothing, so no earlier private-host gate existed anywhere in the plugin; the unauthenticated case is excluded because both routes require a session; and the advisory's account-takeover limb does not apply unless trustEmailVerified is explicitly enabled.
mechanism.impact: Non-blind SSRF: the auth server fetches attacker-chosen URLs and the fetched bodies are reflected back through the mapped user profile fields (id, email, name, image) and error messages, reaching loopback services, RFC 1918 hosts, link-local addresses and cloud metadata FQDNs such as 169.254.169.254 and metadata.google.internal. With sso({ trustEmailVerified: true }) the attacker's userInfo response can assert emailVerified: true for a chosen email and trigger OAuth auto-linking against a pre-existing account row, turning the SSRF into account takeover.
mechanism.preconditions: The sso() plugin is enabled. Any valid session can reach both routes: they use only [sessionMiddleware], and providersLimit defaults to 10 and is enforced before the schema branch. For registration the shipped schema requires skipDiscovery: true for the supplied endpoints to be persisted as-is; in the original 2024 handler the endpoints were always persisted as-is. The takeover escalation additionally requires the deployment to set trustEmailVerified: true and to have an account whose email matches the attacker's claim.
mechanism.summary: An authenticated user registers or updates an SSO provider with attacker-chosen OIDC endpoint URLs; the handler stores those URLs on the ssoProvider row without any origin validation, and the OIDC callback then fetches the token endpoint (validateAuthorizationCode), the userInfo endpoint (betterFetch) and the JWKS endpoint (validateToken) server-side, giving the attacker non-blind SSRF into internal services and cloud metadata.
mechanism.trigger: POST /sso/register with oidcConfig endpoints pointing at an internal or attacker-controlled host (flat body endpoints in the original 2024 handler; oidcConfig with skipDiscovery: true in the shipped schema), then completing the OIDC callback for that provider, which the attacker can do because they control the IdP the endpoints point at. The same primitive is reachable on POST /sso/update-provider by an authenticated user.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: packages/better-auth/src/plugins/sso/index.ts:192-206 (/sso/register handler persistence at f9102b1542175ffb89f0c286759944e7b9dc2314); in the shipped @better-auth/sso package at 23094a628f007f801be6d26e5b15dc5fc6fc4eb8 the same omission is packages/sso/src/routes/sso.ts:696-724 (buildOIDCConfig skipDiscovery branch) and packages/sso/src/routes/providers.ts:486-500 (updateSSOProvider merge and write), with fetch sites packages/sso/src/routes/sso.ts:1495 validateAuthorizationCode(config.tokenEndpoint), :1541 betterFetch(config.userInfoEndpoint) and :1583 validateToken(token, config.jwksEndpoint).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox escape (DoS). vm2 replaces the sandbox-visible Promise constructor with `class localPromise extends globalPromise {}` but delegates `new Promise(executor)` straight to the native constructor without wrapping the user executor. When sandboxed code runs `new Promise(function(r,j){var e=new Error(); e.name=Symbol(); e.stack})`, V8's internal FormatStackTrace (C++) coerces the Symbol() name to a string inside the executor, throwing a host-realm TypeError that no sandbox try/catch can see (it occurs inside engine machinery). Because `localPromise` doesn't wrap the executor, that host TypeError becomes an unhandled rejection that propagates to the host process; Node >= 15 terminates the process on unhandled rejection by default. `allowAsync:false` makes it worse: `.then()/.catch()` are overridden to throw, guaranteeing the rejection goes unhandled. Fix wraps the executor (reject(handleException(e))) so the rejection surfaces as a sandbox-realm value, and attaches a benign swallow tail so the host's unhandledRejection hook never fires.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An invoker of the prebuilt bigquery-forecast tool supplies history_data, data_col, timestamp_col, and id_cols. Invoke concatenates those strings into SELECT * FROM AI.FORECAST(...) with fmt.Sprintf and runs the result on the configured BigQuery client. Column names were placed inside single-quoted literals without escaping, so a quote in timestamp_col/data_col/id_cols breaks out of the literal and injects SQL (CWE-89), including extra table references. history_data is either wrapped as a subquery (SELECT/WITH) or as TABLE `id` with no identifier sanitization, so backticks or a crafted query also execute attacker SQL. From v0.16.0, allowedDatasets was intended as a dataset allowlist, but it only dry-ran or parsed history_data; the assembled AI.FORECAST statement was executed without re-checking ReferencedTables, so quote injection or views behind an allowed table bypassed the operator boundary (CWE-863) and could read arbitrary datasets the service account can access.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SSRF (CWE-918) via HTTP redirect in the authenticated parse_urls API. The API validates only the INITIAL url with is_global_host() (src/pyload/core/api/__init__.py:600-604) and then fetches it through RequestFactory.get_url(), which constructs HTTPRequest with default settings. Since commit 33c55da08 that default is allow_private_ip=True; pycurl follows redirects (FOLLOWLOCATION=1, MAXREDIRS=10), so _pre_request_callback -- which would abort connections to non-global addresses when allow_private_ip is False -- evaluates to a no-op on every hop. An attacker-controlled server responding 302 to an internal/private IP (e.g. cloud metadata 169.254.169.254 or localhost services) bypasses the guard entirely; RE_URLMATCH parsing of the fetched page leaks URL-like strings from the private response back to the attacker.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Sandbox escape on Linux via D-Bus (CWE-863, incomplete mediation of local IPC): nono's Landlock/seccomp policies allow sandboxed processes to access local Unix domain sockets (pathname and abstract). A process running under `nono run -s --profile claude-code` can connect() to the per-user systemd D-Bus socket (pathname socket under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, e.g. /run/user/<uid>/bus) and invoke `systemd-run --user` to spawn an unsandboxed sibling with full user authority. On Landlock V4+ kernels (AccessNet available) no seccomp-notify socket mediation is installed at all, so pathname AF_UNIX connect/bind is governed solely by Landlock fs rules; profiles like claude-code grant the runtime/home dirs, permitting the connect. On <V4 kernels the seccomp fallback explicitly allowed pathname AF_UNIX (denying only abstract/unnamed). The 0.55.0 fix adds Landlock V6 abstract-socket scoping, an explicit pathname-socket allowlist in the seccomp fallback, and a seccomp-notify `af_unix_mediation` mode requiring explicit filesystem.unix_socket grants.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SSRF protection bypass in vLLM's MediaConnector media fetching. The domain-restriction defense validates user-supplied URLs with urllib3.util.parse_url() and enforces allowed_media_domains against the urllib3-derived hostname, but then hands the ORIGINAL raw URL string to the actual HTTP client. The sync path uses requests and the async path load_from_url_async uses aiohttp, whose yarl parser disagrees with urllib3 on backslash-before-@ URLs: urllib3 treats '\' as a literal path character (encodes it %5C) yielding hostname=127.0.0.1 for http://127.0.0.1:PORT\@example.com/x, while yarl parses '\@' as a userinfo separator yielding effective host example.com. An attacker supplies such a URL, passes the urllib3-based allowlist check, and the client connects to the attacker-influenced host instead of the validated one — SSRF exfiltration despite an explicit admin-configured allowlist.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-22 path traversal in CowAgent memory content reads. User-controlled filename from GET /api/memory/content (MemoryContentHandler in channel/web/web_channel.py) or from MemoryService.dispatch(action='content', payload.filename) is passed to get_content, which calls _resolve_path. For any name other than the literal 'MEMORY.md', _resolve_path returns os.path.join(self.memory_dir, filename) without rejecting '..', normalizing, or confining to memory_dir. get_content then open()s that path, so sequences such as ../../../../../../../etc/passwd or a relative path to config.json read arbitrary files the process can open. The same resolver is also reached via CloudClient.on_memory. The 2.0.5 fix canonicalizes with os.path.realpath and raises ValueError when the result escapes the allowed directory.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Pillow's PdfParser.PdfStream.decode() treats a PDF FlateDecode stream as fully trusted zlib input. It reads the attacker-controlled stream dictionary Filter plus Length (or DL) and calls zlib.decompress(self.buf, bufsize=int(expected_length)). Python documents bufsize as the initial output-buffer size only; zlib.decompress grows until the full plaintext is produced, so Length equal to the compressed size does not bound memory. PdfParser.get_value() already materializes PdfStream objects from stream/endstream pairs while parsing xref-reachable objects, so any application that opens an untrusted PDF with PIL.PdfParser and decodes a compressed stream can be forced to allocate ~1000x the file size (advisory: ~950 KB -> 1 GB) and OOM. The 12.3.0 fix keeps FlateDecode support but decompresses through zlib.decompressobj().decompress(buf, max_length) defaulting to ImageFile.SAFEBLOCK (1 MiB) and raises ValueError on unconsumed_tail, which is a true output cap rather than a post-hoc len() check after unbounded allocation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Callback origin mutation (CWE-441/345, unverified origin trust) in Plivo voice-call webhook handling: baseWebhookUrlFromCtx builds the callback base URL from the incoming request context via reconstructWebhookUrl (Host / X-Forwarded-Proto/Host headers), not from a pinned public origin. parseWebhookEvent stores this base in callUuidToWebhookUrl and buildActionUrl embeds it in Plivo XML action URLs (GetInput speech-capture action). An attacker replaying a captured valid callback with a different Host/X-Forwarded-* set mutates the in-process callback origin before/independent of signature-based replay rejection, so follow-up callback traffic (e.g., speech transcriptions) can be redirected to an attacker-chosen origin.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When serving a pyfunc model with enable_mlserver=True (originally the mlserver flag), MLflow builds a shell command in mlflow.pyfunc.mlserver.get_cmd by interpolating the caller-controlled model_uri into f"mlserver start {model_uri}" with no quoting. PyFuncBackend.serve (and the conda/container wrappers) then run that string via bash -c. A model path containing shell metacharacters such as $(...) or backticks is expanded by the shell, so a lower-privileged user who can place a maliciously named model directory can execute arbitrary commands as the serving process.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SSRF via unvalidated URL fetching (DCR/Protected-Resource-Metadata flow): the MCP client takes URLs from untrusted parties - the resource_metadata URI embedded in a server-supplied WWW-Authenticate header, the computed .well-known/oauth-protected-resource URLs, the OAuth2 authorization-server metadata (registration_endpoint), and the auth-server URL - and fetches them with a RestClient with no scheme/host validation, so a malicious/compromised MCP server can point the client at internal hosts (e.g. cloud metadata 169.254.169.254, intranet services). causal_research.bug_semantics: MONAI's CheckpointLoader (monai/handlers/checkpoint_loader.py), an Ignite event handler used to restore network/optimizer/engine state in training and evaluation loops, loaded user-supplied checkpoint files with plain torch.load(self.load_path) and passed them to ignite.handlers.Checkpoint.load_objects. PyTorch persists .pt/.pth files via pickle, and pickle deserialization executes embedded __reduce__/__reduce_ex__ opcodes at load time, so any checkpoint downloaded from an untrusted source (model hubs, shared artifacts) triggers arbitrary code execution the moment CheckpointLoader.__call__ deserializes it. The advisory PoC embeds MaliciousPayload.__reduce__ = os.system('touch /tmp/hacker2.txt') in a saved checkpoint; the traceback shows /tmp/hacker2.txt created during loader(engine) even though load_state_dict subsequently raises RuntimeError. At MONAI <= 1.5.0 most other torch.load sites in the project were also unpinned (only monai/bundle/scripts.py used weights_only=True); PyTorch 2.6 flipped the default safely in March 2025 but MONAI explicitly pinned weights_only=False here (commit 7c26e5af385eb5f7a813fa405c6f3fc87b7511fa), preserving the insecure path.
evidence: PoC target: GHSA advisory HTML (github.com/Project-MONAI/MONAI/security/advisories/GHSA-6vm5-6jv9-rjpj, fetched raw) shows poc calling CheckpointLoader(load_path=str(checkpoint_file)) with a pickled MaliciousPayload and its execution traceback hitting site-packages/monai/handlers/checkpoint_loader.py line 146 in __call__ -> Checkpoint.load_objects -> ignite/handlers/checkpoint.py:624 load_objects -> :613 _load_object -> obj.load_state_dict, with /tmp/hacker2.txt proving payload execution

causal_research.bug_semantics: GitPython's config writer serializes section names into git-config headers with fp.write('[%s]\n' % name) and, until 3.1.53, sanitized names only for CR/LF/NUL. Git treats an unquoted ']' as the end of a section header, so a name containing '] [' opens a second same-line section and injects an arbitrary directive (no newline required). Attacker-controlled submodule names reach this sink: sm_section wraps the name as submodule "<name>", then Submodule.add / submodule_update writes it into the parent .git/config via set_value. A name such as x"] [core] sshCommand=CMD # becomes [submodule "x"] [core] sshCommand=CMD #"], which git parses as core.sshCommand (the trailing #" ] is an inline comment). The next ssh git operation then executes the injected command. Direct GitConfigParser.set/set_value/add_section with a delimiter-bearing section name is the same sink without the submodule wrapper. This is a distinct same-line variant of the 3.1.50 newline-injection fix (GHSA-mv93-w799-cj2w / 54538428), whose [\r\n\x00] guard does not stop the bracket payload.

causal_research.evidence: Advisory GHSA-v6f2-g4gw-r4rc/CVE-2025-9556 (critical, SSTI via gonja include/extends reading /etc/passwd). Verified lineage: local clone openclaw/openclaw (114k commits, no shallow). BIC a4c68d890 (author AkosCz, 2026-02-09 22:05:42 -0600, verified via GitHub commit page + .patch; parents:[c92c3ad224]) is the first write of runGeminiSearch/resolveRedirectUrl/REDIRECT_TIMEOUT: main parent 3f03cdea56 and PR parent c92c3ad224 web-search.ts both contain zero occurrences (830-line parent file checked via raw.githubusercontent), so parent is vulnerability-free. BIC landed on main 2026-02-23 as GitHub squash merge 3a3c2da916 (committer GitHub, squash aggregates several PR member commits). Intermediate hardening 5eb72ab769 (2026-02-24, Peter Steinberger) wrapped resolveRedirectUrl in fetchWithSsrFGuard but with TRUSTED_NETWORK_SSRF_POLICY={dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork:true} (trusted-network model), leaving private-network reachability - matches advisory wording 'private-network-allowing SSRF policy'; that commit is not the origin because the raw redirect-following HEAD fetch already reached private networks without any guard. Direct minimal fix 085c23ce (2026-03-02, Peter Steinberger): removes the dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork policy from the resolveRedirectUrl fetchWithSsrFGuard call so strict SSRF defaults (undici DNS lookup blocking localhost/metadata/private ranges) apply; 1-line code change plus docs/test/CHANGELOG. causal_research.bug_semantics: Kiota's C# generator copies attacker-controlled OpenAPI text (operation/schema/parameter description; later also externalDocs.description as DocumentationLabel and externalDocs.url as DocumentationLink) into generated single-line /// XML documentation comments. The C# writer prefixes each WriteLine with '/// ' but, until the 2026 fix, only XML-escaped the payload (CleanupXMLString) and never stripped line terminators. A newline in the OpenAPI field terminates the comment; the remainder is emitted at namespace/type scope and is compiled when a developer or CI builds the generated client. causal_research.bug_semantics: Command injection (CWE-74/77) in the MCP server's auto.capture tool. The MCP tool 'auto.capture' (src/index.ts, case 'auto.capture': const commitHash = (args.hash as string) || 'HEAD') forwards the user-supplied hash argument to AutoLearnManager.captureCommit (src/autolearn/AutoLearnManager.ts:253) -> AutoLearner.captureCommit (src/autolearn/AutoLearner.ts:136) -> GitHooksManager.getCommitInfo() (src/autolearn/GitHooksManager.ts). getCommitInfo builds shell commands with the hash interpolated unquoted into a template string passed to execSync: `git show -s --format="..." ${commitHash}`, `git show --stat --format= ${commitHash}`, and `git show --pretty=format: ${commitHash}`. A hash value containing shell metacharacters (e.g. 'HEAD; <cmd>') allows a malicious MCP client to execute arbitrary commands on the host running the MCP server. GHSA-rrf2-j3h9-99wg (alias CVE-2026-19282) rates it CWE-74, CVSS 5.3 (NVD MEDIUM / GHSA LOW), published 2026-08-08, affected version <= f11dc8bcff3ff8cf943a2945f99ff3b0bdc8a6d0. The advisory was filed via issue #21; no fix has been released and the vulnerable code is still present at HEAD. Local attack surface: the MCP server is intended to run on a user's workstation, so the injection is exploited by a malicious/compromised MCP client or by any prompt-induced command in the git-hash parameter.

potential_fix.approach: In GitHooksManager.getCommitInfo, stop interpolating commitHash into a command template string. Pass it as a separate argv element without a shell (execFileSync/execFile('git', ['show', '-s', '--format=...', commitHash])), or, if the shell path must remain, validate commitHash against a strict grammar such as /^(HEAD(~[0-9]+)?|[0-9a-f]{7,40})$/ before any use.
potential_fix.rationale: The injection occurs because ${commitHash} is concatenated into a string executed by execSync, so a value like 'HEAD; <cmd>' is tokenized by the shell into two commands. Passing the hash as a distinct argv element (no shell interpretation) or rejecting values that do not match a git-hash/HEAD grammar ensures metacharacters are never evaluated, closing the CWE-74/77 sink.

impact.affected: GitPython releases 3.1.47 through 3.1.50. The decided gate flip was independently checked at its source objects: parent da545232 blocks `-u/nonexistent-adjudicator-helper`, BIC 14219588 allows it, repair member 56806080 blocks it, and default-branch merge 65a72839 first carries that closure relative to first parent 3e59876f, which allowed the identical joined token before the merge. 3.1.47-3.1.50 share `git/cmd.py` blob 096900819f8eea6fd458fce013317a8cbfb600f5; 3.1.51 has the repaired blob 2a4f36024bf66a2647d24e82763f5978e636d9cc. BIC 14219588 and repair 56806080 have the required tag ancestry. The published ranges disagree: GHSA-v396/GHSA-cw2r say `= 3.1.50` (under-covers 3.1.47-3.1.49); NVD's `versionEndExcluding: 3.1.50` contradicts 3.1.46, which blocks the joined form.
impact.effect: The supplied value reaches git as `--upload-pack=<value>` (or `-c` configuration injection such as `protocol.ext.allow=always`), so git executes the attacker-chosen program during the clone with the privileges of the calling application: CWE-78 command injection, CVSS 3.1 9.8 per the CVE and CVSS 4.0 8.7 per GHSA-v396. The effect is read from the advisory text, the observed gate outcome and git's documented `-u` semantics; no clone against a live target was performed.
impact.prerequisites: The application, not git, is the exposure path: it must forward attacker-influenced strings through `multi_options` to either public clone route (`Repo.clone_from(url, path, multi_options=[...])` or an existing repository's `Repo.clone(path, multi_options=[...])`, including repository-like receivers) and must keep the default `allow_unsafe_options=False`. Both wrappers pass the same `multi_options` to the shared `_clone` gate and its subsequent `git.clone` activation site. A kwargs-only spelling is outside this bypass: `_clone` checks only kwargs key names and the process transformer renders a one-character key as two arguments while a longer key becomes a normalized long option. Callers that never forward untrusted options are not exposed; the long forms and the bare `-u` / `-c` tokens stay blocked in every tested release, so this is a bypass of an existing gate.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Remote crash (CWE-590 free of invalid address / CWE-825 expired pointer deref, DoS) in OAI CN5G AMF N2 handling: ngap_app::handle_receive() validates a decoded NGAP PDU by dereferencing ngap_msg_pdu->choice.initiatingMessage->procedureCode without first checking ngap_msg_pdu->present (so a successfulOutcome/unsuccessfulOutcome PDU - or any malformed union state - is read as an initiatingMessage pointer), and on the invalid-procedure-code path frees the PDU with ASN_STRUCT_FREE(asn_DEF_Ngap_NGAP_PDU, &ngap_msg_pdu) passing the ADDRESS of the local pointer variable instead of the pointer itself, so CHOICE_free interprets the pointer's bytes as the ASN.1 struct and frees a non-heap address -> AddressSanitizer crash ('attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed' in CHOICE_free, frame ngap_app.cpp:81). Any remote gNB/attacker on N2 can crash the AMF by sending e.g. a message with procedure code 56-65 (spec-valid but beyond the then-hardcoded max 55) or a wrong PDU type.
causal_research.evidence: Clone .ai-slop/state/repos/gitlab.eurecom.fr_oai_cn5g_oai-cn5g-amf (gitlab.eurecom.fr/oai/cn5g/oai-cn5g-amf; includes GitLab history via mirror). CVE-2026-30078 (gitlab issue #74, repro packet in issue, ASan trace at ngap_app.cpp:81 'attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed' in CHOICE_free, log 'Invalid procedure code 59 or present 1'); advisory's referenced fix is GitLab MR 414. Crash mechanism introduced by fe70f4816f54aae247fac968ce6e727f41c72d17 (2025-03-03, Tien Thinh NGUYEN <Tien-Thinh.Nguyen@eurecom.fr>, 'Free NGAP Msg content if necessary'): added ASN_STRUCT_FREE(asn_DEF_Ngap_NGAP_PDU, &ngap_msg_pdu) (wrong &-parameter) on the decode-failure AND invalid-procedure-code paths; parent 61797fd0d581aee2805bb06b2df4d94147015286 has only a bare 'return' on the invalid path (no free, no crash) -> parent_absent. Contributing pre-existing flaw: be475096a (2022-08-18, same author) dereferences choice.initiatingMessage->procedureCode without a present==initiatingMessage check (invalid PDU-type read). Both commits are in tag v2.2.0 (merge-base --is-ancestor both true); v2.2.0 file confirms vulnerable free on invalid path. Fix chain 2026-02-18..20 (branch fix_ngap_decode_failure, merged 0db0ca99eb1d36b90b29903af66eb323686e018e): d68daf8061db95b0a9fe668c606d8d24abb18e69 (MR 414, 2026-02-18, 'Update NGAP Procedure Code according to 3GPP TS 38.413 version 16.14.0', NGAP_PROCEDURE_CODE_MAX_VALUE 55->66 with handler-table entries 55-65) + 7d79fcff (2026-02-18, 'Fix wrong parameter for ASN_STRUCT_FREE', &ngap_msg_pdu -> ngap_msg_pdu; the effective crash fix) + 48ea63da (+null guard, 2026-02-19), ff4f3af1 (CONTENTS_ONLY, 2026-02-19), 1626bde8 (null after free, 2026-02-20), 576f2f8b (double-free fix, 2026-02-20). causal_research.bug_semantics: The unified keyserver stores the uploading JWT subject as KSKey.owner_client_id and passes the authenticated client_id into KeyserverService.revoke_key, but never compares them. POST /api/v1/keys/register issues a JWT with no prior auth. POST /api/v1/keys/{fingerprint}/revoke then accepts any valid keyserver JWT plus an ML-DSA revocation signature over the fingerprint and sets revoked=True. A different registered client who can produce that signature (i.e., who holds the bundle signing private key) can unpublish another client's key without the original uploader's credentials. Signature verification is a cryptographic possession check; the stored owner_client_id is an unused account-authorization control (CWE-862 / CWE-639). The GHSA-named lines 195-270 match this function exactly at the i

causal_research.bug_semantics: Vite dev-server transform middleware treats any request whose URL starts with the optimized-deps cache prefix and ends in .map as an optimizer sourcemap. isOptimizedDepUrl is a startsWith check on the raw URL, so /node_modules/.vite/deps/../ segments still match. The handler then converts that URL to a filesystem path (fsPathFromId for /@fs, otherwise path.resolve(root, url.slice(1))) and readFile/JSON.parse-sends the contents without testing that the resolved path remains under the deps cache directory. When the server is network-exposed, an attacker can retrieve predictable off-root .map files that parse as source-map JSON, bypassing server.fs.strict. The 2026 fix keeps the same resolver but returns next() unless isOptimizedDepFile(sourcemapPath) is true.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A victim visits an attacker page. The attacker rebinds that hostname to the MLflow tracking server (often 127.0.0.1:5000). The browser then issues same-site-looking XHR/fetch to REST paths such as /api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/search (and create/update/delete). Pre-3.5.0 the Flask/FastAPI server never checked Host or Origin, so those calls ran unauthenticated against experiment APIs, enabling exfiltration and mutation. The 3.5.0 middleware rejects unexpected Host headers and blocks state-changing cross-origin Origin values unless explicitly allowlisted.

mechanism.preconditions: The MLflow server must be reachable from the victim's browser (documented multi-user deployments bind non-loopback and operators routinely expose it; the CLI default host is 127.0.0.1 in mlflow/utils/cli_args.py, which narrows but does not remove the exposure), and the victim must load attacker-controlled content while the server is reachable. mechanism.summary: The MLflow tracking REST server never validates the Host header or the Origin header of incoming requests. causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-22 arbitrary file write on remote systems (path traversal via unvalidated binary filename metadata): the SSH node 'upload' operation builds the remote destination as parameterPath + '/' + (fileName || binaryData.fileName) in packages/nodes-base/nodes/Ssh/Ssh.node.ts with no sanitization, trusting the binary item's fileName metadata. That metadata is attacker-influenced: an unauthenticated webhook multipart upload stores the client-supplied filename via prepareBinaryData(..., fileJson.name, ...) (Webhook.node.ts), and copyBinaryFile persists/re-attaches it unsanitized. A filename like ../../../etc/cron.d/backdoor or ../../.ssh/authorized_keys escapes the intended remote directory, so the transferred content is written to an attacker-chosen location on the SSH target host -> arbitrary file write -> RCE on remote systems. Prerequisites: a workflow that (a) receives file uploads on an unauthenticated endpoint and (b) forwards them via the SSH node; CVSS 4.0 9.0 (SC:H/SI:H/SA:H), affected < 1.123.12 and < 2.4.0

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiteLLM's MCP gateway accepts stdio transport configs whose command and args fields are attacker-controlled JSON (create/update MCP server, config.yaml, DB rehydrate, and /mcp-rest/test/* preview). Those strings are copied onto MCPServer and passed to MCPClient as MCPStdioConfig. MCPClient.connect() feeds them to the Anthropic MCP SDK StdioServerParameters/stdio_client, which spawns a host subprocess with no command allowlist. That is authenticated command execution as the LiteLLM process (CWE-77). CVE/NVD CVSS lists PR:N, but the vendor documents that the affected endpoints sit behind LiteLLM API-key auth; test endpoints originally omitted auth on /test/connection, then gained auth (9002f752, 2025-12-20) before they began forwarding request.command (34b500c7, 2025-12-22). The MITRE affected version '1.18.10' predates MCP and is not the true range.

causal_research.bug_semantics:
Dragonfly's EvalSerializer serializes Lua script results into the RESP stream of the EVAL/EVALSHA connection. Its OnError and OnStatus handlers passed the attacker-controlled string returned by redis.error_reply()/redis.status_reply() straight to RedisReplyBuilder::SendError/SendSimpleString without sanitizing CR/LF bytes. A Lua script like redis.error_reply('foo
+INJECTED
') therefore emitted raw, forged RESP frames mid-stream, desynchronizing the request/response framing of pooled or multiplexed clients so a later command's reply can be substituted with attacker-chosen data.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-835 denial-of-service in Kestrel's HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 request-header processing. For an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 HEADERS frame, Http2Stream.TryValidatePath / Http3Stream.TryValidatePath copies each UTF-16 char of the :path pseudo-header segment into a byte buffer (pathBuffer[i]=(byte)ch) guarded only by Debug.Assert(32 < ch && ch < 127) with the comment 'The header parser should already be checking this'. In Release builds the assert is compiled out, so any client-supplied :path containing a char > byte.MaxValue (e.g. U+0161, codepoint 353; reachable because HPACK/QPACK header values are not ASCII-revalidated for chars >255 on that path) silently truncates modulo 256, producing a decoded/normalized Path that does not round-trip against RawTarget while the server accepts the request instead of aborting the stream. Attacker-controlled mismatch between the validated-normalized path bytes and the raw target then drives request-dispatch state handling into a repeat-processing situation where a worker thread spins in a loop that never reaches its exit condition, consuming CPU until the connection dies or a restart - classic availability-only infinite-loop DoS (CVSS 7.5 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H), affecting .NET 8.0<=8.0.26, 9.0<=9.0.15, 10.0<=10.0.7.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GitHub Actions OIDC publish auth was bound to a single global audience string mcp-registry instead of a per-deployment identifier. A workflow that obtained a GitHub ID token with that audience (the publisher CLI always requested audience=mcp-registry regardless of --registry/--registry-url) posted the token to whichever registry URL was selected. Every registry deployment running this code called validator.ValidateToken(..., "mcp-registry") and, on success, minted a registry JWT granting publish on io.github.<repository_owner>/*. A token captured by a staging, self-hosted, or attacker-controlled registry could therefore be replayed to any other deployment sharing that audience, impersonating the same GitHub owner namespace.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The /gradio_api/file={path_or_url} handler (and /file/ alias) treated any HTTP/HTTPS string as a file URL and returned 302 Location: <attacker URL> without checking that the host is public or allow-listed. A visitor of a Gradio app can be sent to an arbitrary site (CWE-601). Independently, gradio_client follows redirects when downloading FileData, so a malicious Space can return url=/gradio_api/file=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/... and the victim client fetches cloud metadata (client-side SSRF / CWE-918). Sink is file_fetch() in route_utils.py (moved from routes.py file()); source is the unsanitized path parameter. The 2026 fix stops redirecting and server-fetches only hosts that safehttpx resolves to a public IP, pinning that IP.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MLflow FileStore treats any root subdirectory as an experiment and uses unconstrained depth-1 find() in _find_run_root to map a caller-supplied run_id onto a directory of that name. An unauthenticated Tracking Server client can create_experiment with artifact_location equal to the FileStore root so a run's artifacts land at {root}/{run_id}/artifacts; that {root}/{run_id} folder is then listed as an experiment. After run_id validation was relaxed to alphanumeric 1-256 characters, get_run('artifacts') (and artifact APIs using the same lookup) resolve to the artifacts folder. A planted meta.yaml there supplies an arbitrary artifact_uri, so later artifact file operations read/write outside the intended store and can execute code as the service account (CWE-22, ZDI-CAN-26649).

causal_research.bug_semantics: The encrypt/decrypt CLI accepts the encryption password as a plaintext --password/-p argparse value. CRYPT_PASSWORD (added later) is a related /proc/[pid]/environ exposure. --keystore-password is a later similar argv sink; the GHSA/CVE primary mechanism is --password on the encrypt/decrypt CLI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-redis, RedisSaver.list() and ShallowRedisSaver.list() build a RediSearch query by concatenating filter clauses. String filters were interpolated as (@${key}:{${value}}) with no escaping of RediSearch syntax. An attacker who can supply list()/getStateHistory() filter values (typical of user-facing history APIs) can inject | (OR) and braces, e.g. source="x}) | (@thread_id:{*", producing (@thread_id:{victim}) (@source:{x}) | (@thread_id:{*}). RediSearch AND-binds tighter than OR, so the second clause matches every thread and returns other tenants' checkpoint documents from ft.search on the checkpoints index. The 1.0.2 patch escapes filter keys and values via escapeRediSearchTagValue before interpolation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Prompt injection via memory poisoning in PromptChatMemoryAdvisor (CWE-1336, high): when no conversation ID is supplied via the advisor context, getConversationId falls back to the shared constant DEFAULT_CHAT_MEMORY_CONVERSATION_ID ('default'); all such callers (potentially all users of an app) read/write ONE shared memory store. A malicious user's crafted input is stored as a USER memory message and later replayed into the augmented SYSTEM prompt of other users'/sessions' requests (memory rendered via PromptTemplate into the system text), manipulating model behavior across conversation turns.

steps.detail: The hardening pass that closed command injection through archive, ls-remote and the revision APIs added a rev-list denylist and enforced it inside the commit iterator, leaving the counting method that forwards the same keyword arguments unchecked.
steps.title: AI change

steps.detail: The completing change runs the same unsafe-option check inside the counting method and adds the matching escape hatch, so an output option now raises an error instead of truncating the named file.
steps.title: Fix

code_evidence.summary: An AI-assisted change added option screening for revision traversal but wired it only into the iterator that walks commits, so the counting method on the same commit kept forwarding a file-overwriting option to git and could blank any file the caller named.

attempted_remediation.changed: Added unsafe_git_rev_options with --output and -o, the allow_unsafe_options parameter and the check_unsafe_options call inside Commit.iter_items, as part of the same four-file hardening pass that guarded Repo.archive and git.ls_remote.
attempted_remediation.missed: Commit.count kept forwarding the same options to rev_list without consulting the denylist, so the guard covered the method named in the report instead of the option surface the two methods share.

final_closure.closed: Commit.count gains the allow_unsafe_options escape hatch and the check_unsafe_options call, so the rev-list invocation refuses output and the other denied options before the command is built; released in 3.1.56 with a regression test in test/test_commit.py.

ir_chain.original_mechanism: The AI-authored guard for the git option-injection family added the rev-list denylist (--output, -o), the allow_unsafe_options parameter and the check_unsafe_options call to Commit.iter_items only, so the same caller-supplied options stayed free to reach git rev-list through the sibling method Commit.count.
ir_chain.original_sink: Commit.count() in git/objects/commit.py, which forwards **kwargs into rev_list and so into git rev-list --output=<path>
ir_chain.residual_bypass: commit.count(output='/path/to/victim') still reached git rev-list --output and truncated the target file to 0 bytes in every release from 3.1.51 through 3.1.55, because only iter_items consulted the denylist.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated POST /system/api/login (src/routes/login.js) reads username/password from the body and calls HAXCMS.testLogin(name, pass, true). testLogin accepts the request when they match this.user or this.superUser. Before 11.0.10 those objects were hardcoded in the HAXCMSClass constructor to admin/admin, with no install prompt and no UI to change them, so any self-hosted instance using the shipped defaults could be logged in from the public source. Success sets an httpOnly refresh cookie and returns a JWT. The 2020 first-write also hardcoded JWT privateKey to NEEDTOGETTHIS; by the 2024 npm split Node generated per-instance uuidv4 keys into .pk/.rpk, so GitHub-readable JWT literals were no longer the shipped Node mechanism, but the default credentials remained.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DoS (CWE-400/CWE-776): REXML 3.3.3-3.4.1 parsing invalid XML containing multiple XML declarations can cause increased execution time and memory usage. causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated callers of Saltcorn mobile-sync POST /sync/load_changes and POST /sync/deletes supply syncInfos in the JSON body. getSyncRows() embeds syncInfo.maxLoadedId (and Date-derived syncFrom/loadUntil milliseconds) directly into PostgreSQL template-literal strings, and getDelRows() embeds syncFrom/syncUntil timestamps the same way. Identifier sanitization (db.sqlsanitize) is used for table/pk names only; the values are neither parsed as integers nor bound as query parameters. A low-privilege user with read access to at least one syncable table can therefore inject SQL that runs as the application database role, returning attacker-chosen rows in the sync payload (full DB exfiltration, including hashes/secrets) and, depending on the backend, writes or destructive statements.

causal_research.bug_semantics: vLLM embed loaders (image_embeds, prompt_embeds, audio_embeds) deserialize client-supplied tensor bytes via torch.load(weights_only=True) without sparse-tensor invariant checks. PyTorch disables sparse invariant validation by default, so a crafted sparse tensor with out-of-range or negative indices loads successfully and triggers out-of-bounds writes at tensor.to_dense() (CWE-20/CWE-787 DoS). PR #27204 only gated prompt embeds behind a flag without validating tensors, leaving the flaw live when enabled; PR #30649 closes it with torch.sparse.check_sparse_tensor_invariants().

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mayan EDMS ships an inline script in the plain-template mayan/apps/appearance/templates/appearance/base_plain.html (extended by every authentication template, e.g. authentication/templates/authentication/login.html line 1 '{% extends "appearance/base_plain.html" %}', hence the advisory's /authentication/ element) that runs whenever window.location.hash is non-empty: it extracts the URL fragment with URI.js and performs an unconditional client redirect 'window.location = uriFragment'. Assigning an attacker-controlled string to window.location executes javascript:/data: URLs instead of navigating, so a crafted victim link such as https://<host>/authentication/login/#javascript:<payload> yields DOM XSS in the application origin. causal_research.bug_semantics: Sibling-prefix path traversal in the /cache/{path} endpoint of open-webui. serve_cache_file() resolved the request path and validated containment with file_path.startswith(os.path.abspath(CACHE_DIR)) but omitted the trailing os.sep, so the prefix check is a string-prefix test rather than a directory-boundary test. causal_research.bug_semantics: GitPython's documented defense Git.check_unsafe_options is supposed to reject command-executing git options (--upload-pack/-u, --receive-pack, --exec, --config/-c) unless allow_unsafe_options=True. Clone, fetch, pull, and push pass caller kwargs keys and multi_options into that guard, then emit dashified long options to git. Git uniquely expands unambiguous long-option prefixes, so upload_p / --upload-p is executed as --upload-pack=<helper>. From 3.1.30 the guard compared startswith(full-unsafe-name) or exact bare name, which blocks --upload-pack=value but not --upload-p. The 3.1.47 GHSA-rpm5 rewrite dashifies underscores and does exact dict lookup, blocking upload_pack but still missing upload_p. The helper runs in the caller process (RCE) when a host application forwards attacker-controlled kwarg names.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Fail-open authorization (IDOR / CWE-862 / CWE-639 / CWE-613) in the MCP tool layer: scoped (agent) callers can perform cross-task and cross-session mutations. The MCP server authenticates all outbound gRPC with the full server API key and backend gRPC handlers do no caller-based authorization, so the MCP tool layer is the sole authorization boundary. Several destructive tools (task_update, task_delete, task_resume, session_kill, session_resume) omit the assertCallerIsAncestor ancestry/workspace check that their siblings (task_complete, task_start, session_attach, session_send_input) perform; a workspaceless scoped token also skips the task_show workspace check and fails open to all workspaces (F7). Advisory bundles findings F2/F6/F7/F12.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The fail-open design originates with the scoped-agent tool surface. 2f075f99 (PR #434, 2026-03-14) first mapped the full CLI tool surface to 35 MCP tools including the destructive handlers (task_update/task_delete/task_resume/session_kill/session_resume) with no per-tool authorization. 0ce6e77e (PR #616, 2026-03-19) added scoped-token access to task_start/task_complete/session_send_input and introduced assertCallerIsAncestor for those three only, leaving the destructive siblings unchecked. causal_research.bug_semantics: When an operator enables MLflow HTTP basic auth (`mlflow server --app-name basic-auth`) without a custom MLFLOW_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH, the packaged mlflow/server/auth/basic_auth.ini is read and create_admin_user/create_root_user bootstraps a built-in admin if the user store is empty. That ini shipped a publicly known default password (originally password, later password1234), so any network attacker can authenticate as that admin and use unrestricted tracking/registry APIs. Auth is opt-in, but once enabled the default is in the wheel (package-data). ZDI additionally claims administrator-context code execution; this audit did not independently reconstruct an RCE gadget beyond the default-credential admin bypass.

mechanism.summary: A server started with basic auth and no MLFLOW_AUTH_CONFIG_PATH loads the packaged basic_auth.ini, whose admin password is the published constant password1234; create_app then creates admin/password1234 on first start, so an unauthenticated remote attacker who can reach the port logs in as administrator and takes over user/permission management (ZDI frames the follow-on impact as arbitrary code execution as the service account).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Expression sandbox bypass (CWE-95, RCE) in n8n expressions. The expression compiler (tournament/babel) compiles user expressions in {{ }} and runs them inside a Proxy-based vm sandbox; the AST sanitizer PrototypeSanitizer (packages/workflow/src/expression-sandboxing.ts, formerly ExpressionSandboxing.ts) blocks member lookups of forbiddenMembers ['__proto__','prototype','constructor','getPrototypeOf'] but never bans `with` statements. A `with(function(){}){...}` block inside an expression creates a scope object function whose prototype chain resolves the free variable `constructor` to the Function constructor, bypassing the sanitizer and the sandbox Proxy, enabling arbitrary code execution (PoC: {{ (function(){ var constructor = 123; with(function(){}){ return constructor("return process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('env').toString().trim()")() } })() }}). Affects n8n <1.123.17, [2.0.0,2.4.5), [2.5.0,2.5.1). JFrog-discovered (Natan Nehorai), published 2026-01-27.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The /script-api/scripts/ endpoints (ScriptsController in openc3-cosmos-script-runner-api) and several cmd-tlm-api controllers accept a script file path in the :name request parameter. ApplicationController#sanitize_params neutralizes it by translating a fixed character set to '-' via String#tr: the non-forward-slash branch strips %$|:;/\t\r\n\\, but '.' is NOT in the translate set, so sequences of dots pass validation unchanged. With allow_forward_slash=true ('/' is kept so nested script paths work), a name like 'scripts/../etc/passwd' or '../../tmp/x.py' survives sanitize_params intact and flows into Rails routes that resolve scripts under the scope's script directory, letting an authenticated attacker read or write files outside the intended directory (directory traversal). The fix adds an allow_parent_dir guard that gsubs /(\.|%2e){2}/i to '-', collapsing parent-directory segments including URL-encoded ones before the 400 check.

causal_research.evidence: GHSA-mjqp-26hc-grxg / CVE-2025-10156 (picklescan, first patched 0.0.31, vulnerable <= 0.0.30): zipfile's per-file CRC check raises BadZipFile on entries with corrupted CRC; scan_zip_bytes cannot read such entries, so the archive's pickles are never scanned while PyTorch (which disables CRC on load) still executes/loads them - scanner bypass. Empirically reproduced with picklescan 0.0.30 in a venv: malicious eval-based pickle (Malicious1 __reduce__) inside a bad-CRC zip returns issues=0/scanned=0 (missed), while the identical content with a good CRC is flagged (issues=1), and direct .pkl scan flags it (issues=1). Fix commit 28a7b4ef (Matthieu Maitre, 2025-09-08, 'Fix various vulnerabilities (#50)', first tag v0.0.31) modifies src/picklescan/relaxed_zipfile.py: after opening an entry via ZipExtFile it sets zef._expected_crc = None (disabling CRC validation to align with PyTorch), and adds regression fixtures tests/data2/malicious1_crc.zip + assert_scan('malicious1_crc.zip', [Global('builtins','eval',...)]).
causal_research.flaw_origin: introduced_with_feature
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (ZIP-archive scanning that validates per-entry CRC with stdlib zipfile.ZipFile, so bad-CRC entries skip scanning entirely) was introduced atomically on 2022-09-04 by c1d5abd 'Implement Pickle scanner' (Matthieu Maitre): its scan_zip_bytes opens zipfile.ZipFile and reads entries with no CRC tolerance and no exception handling; parent 6a76b8c3 ('Add boilerplate', 2022-09-03) contains only .gitignore/LICENSE/README.md/conda.yaml/requirements.txt/setup.cfg - zero picklescan code, verified via ls-tree. A later intermediate e58e45e0 (2025-03-08, Trevor Madge/Sonatype + Matthieu Maitre, fork merge) replaced stdlib ZipFile with RelaxedZipFile (still keeping CRC validation on, ZipExtFile(..., ..., pwd, True)), preserving the flaw; the GHSA recommendation and the actual fix were to disable CRC there (zef._expected_crc = None). Author of introducer and fix is the human maintainer Matthieu Maitre; 13-term AI-marker scan on both commit bodies is clean (rc=1 both). Flaw is a human design gap (stdlib CRC validation kept while PyTorch skips CRC), not an AI artifact.

causal_research.bug_semantics: HTTP header injection (CWE-93/CWE-20) via newline acceptance in DomainNameValidator: the validator regex is compiled as re.IGNORECASE '^' + hostname_re + domain_re + tld_re + '$' and the '$' anchor in Python regex matches end-of-string OR immediately before a trailing newline, so a value ending with '\n' passes validation; when such a validated domain/name is later interpolated into an HTTP response header, the embedded newline splits the header and lets an attacker inject arbitrary headers (reported by Bence Nagy; inherent flaw, no separate CWE assigned)

display_hunks.annotation: The imported plugin builds the mention-stripping pattern from the mention name and the mention key themselves, and its caller runs that helper on every inbound message, so sender-controlled metadata becomes pattern syntax.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Conductor evaluates caller-supplied JavaScript with Nashorn via ScriptEvaluator.eval, binding the input map as `$`. Nashorn's default configuration exposes the Java type system, so an INLINE (or SWITCH/event-condition) javascript expression can call java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(...) and run OS commands on the server. The demonstrated remote path is: POST /api/metadata/workflow with an INLINE task whose inputParameters.expression contains the Java interop payload and evaluatorType=javascript, then POST /api/workflow/<name> to execute it. JavascriptEvaluator is only a wrapper; the unsandboxed engine is ScriptEvaluator. The 2025 fix forces NashornScriptEngineFactory.getScriptEngine("--no-java"), which disables Java class access.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SSRF/credential disclosure (CWE-918) in the strands-agents-tools Python package's elasticsearch_memory tool. causal_research.bug_semantics: URL-parameter injection in LangSmith Studio (CWE-74): the web client trusts an attacker-controllable baseUrl parameter when constructing deep links. An authenticated user who clicks a crafted link causes the client to transmit their session bearer token, user ID, and workspace ID to an attacker-controlled server, enabling full impersonation within the victim's workspace (tokens expire after ~5 minutes, so repetition requires renewed social engineering). causal_research.bug_semantics: Argument injection / arbitrary file overwrite (CWE-88): Diffable.diff() forwards **kwargs straight into git diff/diff-tree with no check_unsafe_options guard, and inserts caller-supplied 'other' ref BEFORE the '--' separator (git/diff.py args.insert(0, other)), so a value like --output=/path is parsed by git as an option; git diff --output=<path> then truncates and writes real diff/patch bytes to an attacker-chosen path (e.g. ~/.ssh/authorized_keys). Affects Commit/Tree/IndexFile/Submodule diffs; fixed in 3.1.54.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A crafted HDF-EOS swath file can supply unquoted DimensionName metadata that still passes HDF-EOS parsing. SWnentries() in frmts/hdf4/hdf-eos/SWapi.c sizes the name list by adding strlen(utlstr)-2 for every entry, which is only valid if the value is wrapped in double quotes. SWinqdims() then REMQUOTE-no-ops on unquoted names and strcat()s the full name (plus commas) into the caller buffer. GDAL's HDF4SwathGroup::GetDimensions (frmts/hdf4/hdf4multidim.cpp) heap-allocates std::string of that undercounted size and passes &dimNames[0] to SWinqdims, producing a heap-buffer-overflow of 2 bytes per dimension (ASan WRITE in strcat). Local trigger via gdalmdiminfo / the HDF4 multidimensional API.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect (CWE-601) in WebOb Location header normalization: Response._make_location_absolute (src/webob/response.py) validates the redirect target with SCHEME_RE and a leading-'//' escape, then joins it to the request URI via urlparse.urljoin. Since Python 3.10, urlsplit strips ASCII tab/CR/LF before parsing, so a target like '\thttps://evil.com' or '\t//evil.com' passes WebOb's checks (which run on the raw value) yet urljoin reinterprets it as an absolute/protocol-relative URL on an attacker-controlled host. Bypasses the CVE-2024-42353 fix (GHSA-mg3v-6m49-jhp3) that escaped a leading double slash.
causal_research.evidence: OSV CVE-2026-44889 (fixed 1.8.10, GIT range fixed b24085795 = 'Merge commit from fork' by Delta Regeer, parents 5e52ea46 + 57d78a39 'Release 1.8.10'). causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated JSON-auth client sends PUT /api/users/{id} with which containing Title Case 'Password' and a new data.password, omitting a valid current_password. userPutHandler (http/users.go) first looks up each which token in a map whose keys are lowercase ('password', 'all', ...). The lookup is case-sensitive, so 'Password' misses and CheckPwd is skipped. Later the same handler Title-cases which with cases.Title(language.English, cases.NoLower), matches v=='Password', hashes the new secret, and storage/bolt/users.go Update writes it via reflect FieldByName('Password'). A stolen JWT therefore becomes an account-takeover password reset. The stock UI sends lowercase 'password' and is not the trigger. Non-JSON auth skips this check by design. Non-admins remain blocked when LockPassword is set.

mechanism.summary: PUT /api/users/{id} with which=[Password] (title case) bypasses the JSON-auth current-password gate in userPutHandler because sensibleFields is keyed in lower case but probed with the un-normalized field name, while the later title-casing still processes Password; a token holder can therefore rewrite a password (own account, or any account when the token is an admin's) without knowing the current password.
mechanism.trigger: Authenticated PUT /api/users/{id} with body which=[Password], data.id equal to the caller's id (or, with an admin token, the target's id), data.password set and no current_password; the same request with which=[password] returns 400 ErrCurrentPasswordIncorrect.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-53355 / GHSA-gjv4-ghm7-q58q (CWE-77, CVSS 3.1 8.8 AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R, fixed 2.5.0): command injection in several kubectl/helm MCP tools. Tools build shell command strings by interpolating MCP tool input parameters (helm install/upgrade name/chart/repo/namespace, kubectl apply/create/delete/describe/get/logs/patch/rollout/scale/context params) and run them via child_process.execSync(command, ...), which executes through /bin/sh. An MCP client (e.g. a malicious prompt or compromised model) that controls tool arguments can inject shell metacharacters (; | & $ ` etc.) to run arbitrary commands on the host running the MCP server, which typically has full kubeconfig access. Fix ab165f5a migrates all 13 tool files from execSync(string) to execFileSync(binary, args[]) so arguments are passed verbatim, plus a related hardening in cyanheads/git-mcp-server (0dbd6995) for the same researcher-reported pattern (equixly.com blog 'MCP server new security nightmare').

causal_research.bug_semantics: sqlfluff's Python parser resolves nested brackets recursively: resolve_bracket() in src/sqlfluff/core/parser/match_algorithms.py calls itself for every nested opening bracket found while scanning for the closing bracket (the 'Recurse into a new bracket matcher' branch, ~line 502 at the rewrite, ~line 450 pre-fix). Matching grammars additionally recurse through anyof/sequence via ParseContext.deeper_match() which only increments match_depth without ever checking a limit, and default_config.cfg set no parsing depth bound (only an optional Python recursion_limit = None, i.e. off by default). A query with deliberate excessive nesting therefore drives unbounded call-stack growth until CPython raises RecursionError/MemoryError exhaustion - resource-exhaustion DoS in any service that lints untrusted SQL. Affected: everything before 4.1.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ASGIRequest.__init__ in django/core/handlers/asgi.py builds the META header dict by re-concatenating an ever-growing string for every repeated header: value = self.META[corrected_name] + "," + value (and since #36399 also value = self.META[corrected_name] + "; " + value for HTTP_COOKIE). causal_research.bug_semantics: SAML authentication bypass via XML Signature Wrapping (parser differential, incomplete fix of CVE-2025-25292). SignedDocument#validate_signature parsed self.to_s twice: a REXML @working_copy supplied SignedInfo/SignatureValue/DigestValue while the ID-referenced element was looked up and canonicalized via a separate Nokogiri.parse(self.to_s). REXML and Nokogiri disagree on XML details (entity/namespace/attribute handling), so an attacker can craft a document where the digest verifies over a benign referenced element but the consuming app (also Nokogiri-based) sees a different, attacker-controlled element - re-enabling signature wrapping. Fixed in v1.18.0 (commit e9c1cdbd) by adding XMLSecurity::BaseDocument.safe_load_xml (rejects DOCTYPE, strict Nokogiri options) and cache_referenced_xml, validating the reference against the single strict Nokogiri parse of the serialized doc, eliminating the dual-parser differential.
causal_research.evidence: Pickaxe git log -S 'Nokogiri.parse(self.to_s)' -- lib/xml_security.rb resolves to 5e7f13e1757217a2ed3a5e87bda46481eaf872a7 (2012-10-11 Stephen Touset); its diff adds 'document = Nokogiri.parse(self.to_s)' and 'hashed_element = document.at_xpath(...)' while keeping REXML::XPath reads for signature/digest. Parent 2d3d46c02d2523fa84cf6258a1938635fcfe721f contains zero Nokogiri references (grep count 0). validate_signature method name first appears in 77f1281cbda4674097fb82fd2f33a0163b6c06c5 (2014-02-20 Ben Radler, rename only, content already present in pre-image). Fix: OSV GHSA-9v8j-x534-2fx3 range introduced 0, fixed 1.18.0, reference commit e9c1cdbd0f9afa467b585de279db0cbd0fb8ae97; e9c1cdbd is contained in v1.18.0 (git describe v1.17.0-28-ge9c1cdb, merged via PR #750) and absent from v1.17.0. git show -s --format=%B scans: no AI markers (co-authored/assisted-by/anthropic/claude/copilot/codex/openai/grok) on either 5e7f13e or e9c1cdbd.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Human-authored pre-AI code. The dual-parser validation construct (REXML for signature elements + Nokogiri.parse for reference canonicalization) was introduced 2012-10-11 by Stephen Touset in 'Add support for canonicalization-algorithm detection' while porting XMLSecurity from the Onelogin Java sampler. The parser differential persisted through 13 years of maintenance and the CVE-2024-45409 fixes; CVE-2025-66567 is the incomplete-fix disclosure requiring the 1.18.0 rework.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is a 2012-era design flaw: mixing REXML and Nokogiri parses in signature validation. The minimum atomic introducer is 5e7f13e, which first coupled Nokogiri reference canonicalization with REXML signature reading; its parent lacks the construct entirely (introducer_parent_absent=true, no squash decomposition needed). The commit predates AI-assisted coding by years and carries no AI markers; the fix commit (e9c1cdbd, Mar 2025) is also marker-free human work by a Workato engineer. Under the ledger rule that an AI marker on a fix of a human-introduced flaw cannot flip attribution, this case is NOT_AI despite the 2025 remediation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In Rancher Manager, when a user (or group) is bound to an 'admin-equivalent' GlobalRole — either the builtin `admin` GlobalRole or a custom GlobalRole whose rules include a `*` on `*` in `*` resource rule plus a `*` on `*` nonResourceURLs rule — the downstream-cluster RBAC controllers create a ClusterRoleBinding named `globaladmin-<subject>` in every user cluster binding that subject to the Kubernetes `cluster-admin` ClusterRole. These CRBs are create-only: the user-context GRB handler's sync() and the per-cluster clusterHandler.doSync() both return early on DeletionTimestamp and never enqueue deletions, so when the custom admin GlobalRole or its GlobalRoleBinding is deleted, the orphaned `globaladmin-` ClusterRoleBindings survive in every cluster and the user retains full cluster-admin access after being de-admined (CWE-281, incorrect privilege preservation / account access removal).

causal_research.bug_semantics: DotGit treats a Git reference name as a relative filesystem path under the repository's .git directory. SetRef writes the loose-ref file with d.fs.Create(r.Name().String()) (later fileName := r.Name().String() into setRef); Ref reads via readReferenceFile(".", name.String()); RemoveRef deletes via d.fs.Join(".", name.String()). Because the name is not required to stay under refs/ (or a one-level [A-Z_] pseudo-ref) and is not stripped of '.'/'..'/NTFS/HFS disguises, a name such as refs/heads/../../config or a mapped refs/remotes/origin/../../config resolves to .git/config. A malicious Git server can advertise such a name; clone/fetch refspec mapping can preserve the traversal. Only filesystem-backed storage/filesystem/dotgit is affected; storage/memory never turns names into paths. The 2026 patches add validReferenceName (IsSafe plus control-character and NTFS/HFS hardening) at those storage entry points and reject ErrReferenceNameEscape before any path join.
