steps.detail: The final patch classified private and IPv4-encoding IPv6 forms and invoked that classifier before returning success.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The attempted security fix adds a synchronous validator that checks metadata hosts, localhost, and IPv4 ranges, but reaches success without classifying IPv6 forms.

fix_hunks.code:
@@ -51,6 +52,55 @@ const PRIVATE_IP_RANGES = [
 ];
 
 export class SSRFProtection {
+  /**
+   * IPv6 addresses that must be blocked: loopback, unspecified, link-local,
+   * unique-local, site-local (deprecated), IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible,
+   * 6to4, and NAT64-mapped addresses. All of these either represent private
+   * networks or embed an arbitrary IPv4 address that would bypass IPv4-only
+   * SSRF checks.
+   *
+   * Hostname must be lowercased and bracket-stripped. WHATWG URL parser
+   * canonicalizes IPv6 literals (zero compression, dotted-quad → hex pairs),
+   * so prefix matching works against the normalized form.
+   *
+   * @security See GHSA-56c3-vfp2-5qqj. The sync validator previously had no
+   * IPv6 gate, letting `::ffff:169.254.169.254`, `::169.254.169.254`,
+   * `2002:a9fe:a9fe::`, and `64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe` reach the HTTP client.
+   */
+  private static isPrivateOrMappedIpv6(hostname: string): boolean {
+    // Gate on net.isIPv6 so domain names starting with hex-like labels
+    // (e.g. "fcexample.com") are never misclassified as private IPv6.
+    if (!isIPv6(hostname)) return false;
+
+    // ::/96 reserved block: unspecified (`::`), loopback (`::1`), IPv4-mapped
+    // (`::ffff:X`), and deprecated IPv4-compatible (`::X:Y` per RFC 4291) all
+    // live here. Blocking the whole prefix avoids enumerating subforms.
+    if (hostname.startsWith('::')) return true;
+
+    // Defensive long-form IPv4-mapped — WHATWG URL normally compresses this,
+    // but keep the check in case normalization ever changes.
+    if (hostname.startsWith('0:0:0:0:0:ffff:')) return true;
+
+    // Link-local fe80::/10
+    if (hostname.startsWith('fe80:')) return true;
+
+    // Site-local fec0::/10 (deprecated, RFC 3879) — still honored by some stacks.
+    if (/^fe[c-f]/.test(hostname)) return true;
+
+    // Unique local fc00::/7 (RFC 4193). Covers fc00-fdff in the first hextet.
+    if (/^f[cd]/.test(hostname)) return true;
+
+    // 6to4 2002::/16 (RFC 3056) — bits 16-47 embed an arbitrary IPv4 address,
+    // so any 2002: address can tunnel to RFC1918 or metadata endpoints.
+    if (hostname.startsWith('2002:')) return true;
+
+    // NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 (RFC 6052) and 64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 8215) — embedded
+    // IPv4 in the low 32 bits, same tunneling concern as 6to4.
+    if (hostname.startsWith('64:ff9b:')) return true;
+
+    return false;
+  }
+
   /**
    * Validate webhook URL for SSRF protection with configurable security modes
    *
fix_hunks.annotation: The closing patch adds a dedicated classifier for mapped, compatible, local, 6to4, and NAT64 IPv6 representations that the earlier IPv4 expressions could not recognize.
The synchronous validator now calls the IPv6 classifier immediately before its success return, directly closing the residual bypass on the same request boundary.

ir_chain.original_mechanism: The earlier AI-marked multi-tenant change accepted caller-controlled X-N8n-Url and X-N8n-Key headers and passed the selected instance URL and credential into the outbound n8n client without SSRF validation.
ir_chain.original_sink: The authenticated multi-tenant HTTP path used the selected n8n instance URL for outbound requests and forwarded x-n8n-api-key to that destination.

attempted_remediation.changed: Added synchronous hostname and IPv4 private-address checks in SSRFProtection.validateUrlSync.
attempted_remediation.missed: Did not cover IPv4-mapped or IPv4-compatible IPv6, 6to4, NAT64, ULA, link-local, or site-local addresses.

ir_chain.residual_bypass: An IPv6 encoding of a private destination could pass the IPv4-only validator and receive the forwarded x-n8n-api-key.

final_closure.closed: Extended the same synchronous validator across the missing IPv6 address families in version 2.47.14.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Apache Airflow's standalone Log server (airflow-core/src/airflow/utils/serve_logs/log_server.py, class JWTAuthStaticFiles) authorizes each request by comparing the JWT 'filename' claim against the filename extracted from the URL path: request_filename = request.url.path.lstrip("/log/"); token_filename != request_filename -> 403. Python str.lstrip() strips any member of the CHARACTER SET {'/', 'l', 'o', 'g'} from the left end of the string, not the literal '/log/' prefix, so the comparison string is silently mangled whenever the real requested Dag/task log path starts with characters drawn from that set (e.g. '/log/dag_a/task' vs '/log/_log_dag_b/task' can collapse to the same extracted value). An authenticated Airflow worker holding one valid Log-server JWT (issued for at least one Dag it may read) can therefore construct request paths for OTHER Dags whose names begin with a subset/superset of {/,l,o,g} such that the stripped value equals its own token's filename while Starlette StaticFiles serves the actual (different) file on disk, yielding unauthorized cross-Dag worker-log disclosure.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CPU starvation / denial of service in Synapse (Matrix homeserver): the WaitingLock/WorkerLocksHandler wait-loop first written in synapse/handlers/worker_lock.py doubles its retry timeout on every iteration via _get_next_retry_interval() (next = self._retry_interval; self._retry_interval = max(5, next*2)) with NO upper cap, and wraps the wait in 'except Exception: pass'. Under lock contention a local authenticated user can drive the interval to astronomically large values (doubling ~35 times reaches 10^10 seconds; per fix message an interval grew until its string conversion hit CPython's 4300-digit int_max_str_digits limit -> ValueError crash, failing/sterving other users' requests (CWE-400 / improper resource control).

causal_research.bug_semantics: vLLM's /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint caps the COMPRESSED upload size (VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB, default 25MB, enforced in vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/base/serving.py / earlier speech_to_text.py) but places no limit on the DECODED PCM output. causal_research.bug_semantics: Open redirect via protocol-relative (network-path) redirect target in google_sign_in gem (basecamp/google_sign_in, lib/google_sign_in/redirect_protector.rb). ensure_same_origin only origin-checks targets that match QUALIFIED_URL_PATTERN (scheme-required, \A#{URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.make_regexp}\z); any other non-blank target passes validation, and browsers resolve '//attacker.com/path' as a network-path reference, so proceed_to=//attacker.com after OAuth completes redirects the user off-site. Empirically verified with ruby -ruri: '//evil.com/path' =~ make_regexp => nil (so pre-2025-08-22 code raised no Violation), and '//evil.com/path' =~ URI::DEFAULT_PARSER.regexp[:ABS_PATH] => 0 (so the 2025-08-22 ABS_PATH allowance also admitted it).

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-346 improper origin validation, exploitable as browser-mediated request forgery against a loopback-bound service. The Assistant API accepts any request whose TCP source address is loopback, which is what the victim's own browser presents when a malicious page issues a cross-origin fetch to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/assistant/*. The server's CORS defense covers only paths that start with /api/ (is_api_endpoint), so /ajax-api/ state-changing calls were exempt from CORSBlockingMiddleware, and the default branch of init_fastapi_security added CORSMiddleware(allow_origins=['*']), so the attacker page's preflight succeeded. Writing the Assistant config with permissions.full_access=true then makes the Claude Code provider run with --permission-mode bypassPermissions, giving arbitrary command execution as the user running the MLflow server.

That member is the squash landing of PR #19805 and carries an AI co-author trailer on the member object itself. It adds mlflow/server/assistant/api.py whose only access gate is the _require_localhost dependency (an ipaddress.is_loopback check on request.client.host) and mounts the router at prefix /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/assistant, i.e. outside the /api/-only path predicate of the pre-existing CORSBlockingMiddleware and with no Origin validation at all. The parent tree b223e990e00d36e8500e458b0dc84992720d882b has no mlflow/server/assistant/ directory, so the browser-reachable privileged local Assistant API, and with it the advisory's config-write path, is new in this object.

On closure, evidence that a released 3.10.x still answers a cross-origin state-changing /ajax-api request from a non-loopback origin, or that CORSBlockingMiddleware can be bypassed for the advisory's config-write path, would make the remediation incomplete and reopen the case.
causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: a user runs MLflow 3.9.0 locally (default configuration, no wildcard MLFLOW_SERVER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) and visits a malicious web page, which matches the advisory's CVSS UI:R. The page's script issues PUT/POST to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/assistant/config (and /message, /skills/install). Those requests reach the Assistant because (a) the browser's source address is loopback so _require_localhost passes, (b) CORSBlockingMiddleware returns early for every path that is not an api endpoint and is_api_endpoint matched only /api/, and (c) CORSMiddleware answered allow_origins=['*'] so the preflight was approved. Vulnerable code: mlflow/server/assistant/api.py (APIRouter prefix /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/assistant with dependencies=[Depends(_require_localhost)]), mlflow/server/security_utils.py is_api_endpoint, mlflow/server/fastapi_security.py CORSBlockingMiddleware plus the wildcard CORSMiddleware. Impact: the attacker rewrites Assistant providers/projects/permissions through PUT /config (v3.9.0 api.py line 276), sets full_access, and the Claude Code sub-agent is then launched with bypassPermissions (v3.9.0 claude_code.py lines 379-381), i.e. arbitrary commands on the victim host. Preconditions: local MLflow server with the Assistant feature and a browser request from an attacker-controlled page; non-browser remote clients already fail the loopback IP check. Counterevidence: the endpoints did gate on a loopback source IP, so this is not unauthenticated remote access, and the exploit is browser-mediated and requires user interaction; a user who explicitly sets MLFLOW_SERVER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to a wildcard opts into wildcard CORS, and the fix deliberately leaves that explicit-wildcard branch intact.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory is live and matches the code, so this is not a false positive. BIC: the vulnerable behaviour is a privileged local HTTP API that trusts any loopback source address and lives outside the server's only anti-CSRF/CORS path predicate. That behaviour does not exist before member 280bf76cffc - the parent tree has no mlflow/server/assistant at all - so the smallest atomic introducing object is that member, which is the [1/N] member of the squash 99b5a3dd85e that lands the Assistant branch on master; hence bic_granularity SQUASH_DECOMPOSED with the five branch members listed and the squash recorded as landing_commit. The older /api/-only predicate of CORSBlockingMiddleware and the pre-existing wildcard CORSMiddleware are not the carrier: before the Assistant there was no privileged non-/api/ endpoint to protect, and the advisory's mechanism (cross-origin config write that turns on full_access and reaches command execution) first becomes reachable with this object. Verdict AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than AI_CAUSAL_CONTRIBUTOR or AI_CODE_FLAWED: the vulnerable behaviour itself first enters the tree in an AI-attributed change, and the object's own trailer marks that change, so no human origin has to be posited for the defect. AI evidence: member 280bf76cffc carries the Claude co-author trailer on its own commit object (ai_on_bic true), the landing squash carries the same trailer but was not used for attribution, and the later config/permission objects in the same cycle are human-signed without trailers, which shows the marker is specific rather than a repository habit. causal_research.remaining_gap: For this advisory's mechanism the repair is complete in the shipped releases: 3.10.0/3.10.1 block cross-origin state-changing requests to /ajax-api/* and no longer answer with a wildcard allow-origin in the non-wildcard branch, and both tags contain the fix through the release-branch twin 4b9fa88d. Three residual surfaces adjacent to the reported defect stay open: (1) CORSBlockingMiddleware still exempts every state-changing path outside /api/ and /ajax-api/, so a future privileged endpoint mounted elsewhere would inherit the same gap; (2) the Assistant gate remains an IP-based loopback check and the new allow-list trusts any loopback origin, so a page served by another local service, or any local process, can still drive the Assistant - that is the deliberate localhost-trust boundary behind this feature, not the remote malicious-page vector the advisory reports; (3) the advisory-cited sha 8f9c8a53 is unreachable from every release tag, so version checks must use the twin 4b9fa88d. No closing commit exists or is expected for (1) and (2) because they lie outside this advisory's scope.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated client POSTs an arbitrarily large body to the MCP HTTP transport (router mounted at /mcp, handler mcpHandler later renamed httpHandler). The handler does body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body) before JSON-RPC parse or auth, so the entire stream is copied into a single heap buffer with no MaxBytesReader or Content-Length cap. A single multi-gigabyte request linearly consumes process memory until OOM, denying service (CWE-770). The immediate parent decoded with json.NewDecoder, which does not materialize the raw body; switching to ReadAll is what makes a non-JSON bulk POST (the #3103 PoC) exhaust memory. The #3216 wrap of r.Body with http.MaxBytesReader (default 10 MiB) stops that allocation; oversize MCP requests then fail the ReadAll with MaxBytesError.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that no earlier or later guard already bounded this read: git grep MaxBytesReader at 4c860b66^ finds nothing repo-wide, git grep ContentLength in internal/server/ at that commit finds nothing, and the only other body read in the package (api.go toolInvokeHandler) uses util.DecodeJSON rather than ReadAll. mechanism.impact: Memory-exhaustion denial of service (CWE-770): the server allocates memory in proportion to the attacker-supplied body size, ending in an Out-Of-Memory kill of the toolbox process and loss of service for all connected MCP clients.
mechanism.preconditions: Network reachability of the HTTP endpoint and no MCP-enabled auth service configured, in which case mcpAuthMiddleware passes the request straight through; the OSS/default deployment binds an HTTP listener without MCP auth, so POST /mcp/... is unauthenticated. The attacker must be able to send a large body over one request.
mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated POST to /mcp (or /mcp/{toolsetName}) reaches httpHandler, which read the full request body with io.ReadAll and no size bound, so a single arbitrarily large body is buffered into process memory until the Go process is OOM-killed.
mechanism.trigger: The attacker sends one HTTP POST with an arbitrarily large body (chunked transfer or a huge Content-Length) to /mcp/ or /mcp/{toolsetName}/ with Content-Type: application/json; chi's AllowContentType middleware only checks the content type, and no read limit is applied.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: internal/server/mcp.go:180 mcpHandler (8d32a38a433ce74cc36692df867a874877f66af3); at the last vulnerable commit the same read is internal/server/mcp.go:496 httpHandler (4c860b66b03f0ebf86205e73cd8521ad90ccebe4)

causal_research.bug_semantics: Fickling's pickle safety analyzer judged a pickle LIKELY_SAFE unless it matched hardcoded detection rules. One rule was a static list of 'unsafe import' module names inside Pickled.unsafe_imports() (fickle.py, formerly pickle.py): any STACK_GLOBAL/Global import of a listed module was flagged overtly malicious and forced severity above LIKELY_SAFE. The module 'pty' was never added to that list, so a pickle doing pty.spawn('id') (an arbitrary shell-command execution primitive exposed through the pseudo-terminal module) imported an unlisted stdlib module and produced no unsafe-import result; with the leftover REDUCE value consumed by a BUILD opcode to defeat the unrelated unused-variable heuristic, check_safety() returned Severity.LIKELY_SAFE for a pickle that executes arbitrary commands. Any user or system vetting pickle files with fickling < 0.1.6 got a false 'safe' verdict.

causal_research.bug_semantics: call_user_func_array (and wrapper call_user_func) accepts a PHP-style array callback [classOrObject, method]. For a string class name it builds and eval()s cb[0] + "['" + cb[1] + "']". The PoC uses that breakout plus the subsequent 'is not a valid function' throw to surface command output.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When passkeys are enabled and at least one credential exists, POST /api/auth/passkey/options is public/CSRF-exempt so an unauthenticated client can start WebAuthn login. authentication_options() always mints a fresh 32-byte challenge and _store_challenge() loads STATE_DIR/.passkey_challenges.json, inserts another {kind,rp_id,origin,ts} entry, and atomically rewrites the entire file. Before the fix the only bound was a 300s TTL prune inside _load_challenges(); there was no global or per-context cap and no lock. Repeated options requests without completing assertion therefore grow the on-disk JSON without limit and force a full rewrite per request, causing CPU/disk I/O exhaustion (CWE-770). Login-assertion rate limits do not apply until after this allocation.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The unbounded store was first written in public commit 2a432ba12d8fe199ff53528ad61bc7656fc93a23 (PR #2859 'feat: add passkey sign-in' by AJV20). That commit added api/passkeys.py blob dbfbb65 with _store_challenge at lines 120-123 (append + rewrite, TTL 300, no cap), plus the public options route. Immediate parent d450ef8a has no passkey files or strings. Maintainers cherry-picked the same blob onto master as c60ff543 (same author date/message; not a squash). 1b48643 later added passkey-only auth/clear_credentials but left _store_challenge uncapped (blob 2aadf980), which is what v0.51.132–v0.51.269 shipped.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TracingMiddleware: arbitrary server-side file read. Two cooperating defects: (1) CWE-346 - TracingMiddleware() passes ALL inbound request headers into the trace context (tracing_context(parent=headers)), and RunTree.from_headers -> _Baggage.from_header parses the 'baggage' HTTP header key langsmith-metadata as JSON which is merged into the run's extra.metadata and extra.attachments, so an external caller controls the attachment shape; (2) CWE-843 - the filesystem guard in create_run/update_run/multipart_ingest only rejects attachments that are isinstance(x, tuple) with a pathlib.Path second element, so list/str shaped attachments like ["text/plain", "/etc/passwd"] pass the guard and the SDK opens the given path server-side and uploads its contents as a trace attachment, leaking arbitrary files. Fix replaces the three copy-pasted checks with a fail-closed _reject_filesystem_attachments helper.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The hand-rolled SSRF guard networking.IsPrivateIP (pkg/networking/utilities.go, originally pkg/networking/http_client.go) maintains a static privateIPBlocks CIDR table that never included the IPv6 NAT64 translation prefixes 64:ff9b::/96 (RFC 6052) or 64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 8215). A NAT64 address such as 64:ff9b:1::a9fe:a9fe - the translation of the cloud-metadata link-local 169.254.169.254 - is syntactically global unicast, so IsPrivateIP returned false and protectedDialerControl allowed the dial. causal_research.bug_semantics: Actual sync-server mounts bank-sync Express sub-apps at /simplefin and /pluggyai. Those apps expose POST /status, /accounts, and /transactions that read server-side SimpleFIN/Pluggy secrets and proxy account balances and transactions. Unlike GoCardless, which wrapped the same class of routes with validateUser (later validateSessionMiddleware), SimpleFIN and Pluggy registered only express.json() (later plus requestLoggerMiddleware). The server has no global session gate in app.js, so an unauthenticated network client can call the six endpoints and exfiltrate configured users' bank data. CWE-306. Fixed by inserting validateSessionMiddleware in both apps.

steps.detail: The change that moved code execution into a subprocess also wrote the list of forbidden attribute names, and that list never named the attribute that hands back the builtins module.
steps.title: AI change

steps.detail: The default sandbox mode skips the older text-pattern list, so the guard was the static syntax scan alone, and every release from the first subprocess-mode version through 1.6.39 shipped that list as written.
steps.title: Reachable window

steps.detail: The repair adds the leaking attribute and the helper call to the blocked sets, screens calls written as attribute access, and runs the same syntax check at the entry to sandboxed execution, so the proof is refused before it starts.
steps.title: Fix

code_evidence.summary: The execute_code tool's subprocess sandbox screened submitted programs against a fixed list of dangerous attribute names, and that list omitted the attribute that exposes the live builtins module, so a short program could still run operating system commands as the server user.

attempted_remediation.changed: Added the _execute_code_sandboxed subprocess wrapper with a blocked_attrs screen and a restricted builtins dictionary, and made sandbox mode the default.
attempted_remediation.missed: The attribute screen listed the usual dunder names but not __self__, so a bound method still leaked its module: print.__self__ handed the snippet the builtins module.

final_closure.closed: Blocks __self__ and vars and validates the snippet's AST before execution ('Security Error: Access to attribute __self__ is restricted').

ir_chain.original_mechanism: execute_code handed caller-supplied Python to the interpreter with no sandbox wrapper and no attribute screen, so a snippet could reach interpreter internals such as the builtins module.
ir_chain.residual_bypass: print.__self__ reached the builtins module through the attribute screen, so a sandboxed snippet could rebuild imports and leave the sandbox.

causal_research.bug_semantics: POST /api/public/v1/roles/assign is an Enterprise EXPANDED_PUBLIC_API endpoint. builderOrAdmin allows any builder for the x-budibase-app-id workspace, including users with only builder.apps. The public controller destructures userIds and forwards the rest of the JSON body to sdk.publicApi.roles.assign. That SDK, with no caller identity check, sets user.builder={global:true} and/or user.admin={global:true} for every supplied user id and bulk-updates the global user DB. A workspace-scoped builder with an API key can therefore promote themselves or any other tenant user to global admin (CWE-915 mass assignment of global privileges). The same path unassigns global roles. The 2026-05-12 controller check requires isAdmin for admin grants and isGlobalBuilder for builder grants, which closes this escalation without changing the SDK write.

causal_research.bug_semantics: WeCom outbound media loading (WeComAdapter._load_outbound_media) accepts an attacker-influenced media_source. HTTP(S) sources are fetched via _download_remote_bytes; file:// sources become Path(unquote(parsed.path)).expanduser() and any other string becomes Path(source).expanduser(). Relative paths are resolved against cwd, but absolute file:// URLs such as file:///etc/passwd are used as-is. After only exists()/is_file() checks, local_path.read_bytes() loads the file and _upload_media_bytes ships it to the WeCom API through send_image/send_document/send_voice/send_video. There is no is_relative_to/allowlist bound, so any file readable by the Hermes process can be exfiltrated as a WeCom media attachment. The reporter's separate read_file API-server PoC is a different, by-design tool path and is not this sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal (CWE-22) in the MCP document tools. Every tool-supplied filename flows through two helpers that impose no confinement: ensure_docx_extension() merely appends '.docx' when missing, and check_file_writeable() performs only os.path.exists/os.access permission probes plus a lock probe open(filepath,'a') — it never resolves realpaths nor restricts paths to a base directory. causal_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service via improper handling of length-parameter inconsistency (CWE-770 / CWE-20): MemoryFileUploadHandler.new_file() activates the in-memory upload path based solely on the declared Content-Length ('self.activated = content_length <= settings.FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE'). In ASGI deployments Content-Length is not guaranteed to reflect the actual body size (absent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, or understated), so an unauthenticated attacker can upload an arbitrarily large file that is buffered fully in memory (bypassing FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE and the memory-budget expectation), causing service degradation / DoS. Affects Django 5.2 (<5.2.14) and 6.0 (<6.0.5); fixed 2026-05-05 security release.
causal_research.evidence: Identity: hash reversal over plan pool -> {CVE-2026-5766, GHSA-w26r-rmm8-9c29} (aliases PYSEC-2026-54, BIT-django-2026-5766; PyPI django introduced 5.2/6.0, fixed 5.2.14/6.0.5; advisory: ASGI requests with missing/understated Content-Length bypass FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, reported by Kyle Agronick). causal_research.bug_semantics: Command injection in the git-mcp-server MCP tool suite: tool logic files (git_add, git_init, git_clone, git_cherry_pick, git_rebase, etc.) build shell command strings by interpolating user-controlled inputs (targetPath resolved from input.path, filesArg, branch names, messages, etc.) and execute them via promisified child_process.exec. Because exec runs through the shell, shell metacharacters (|, >, &&, ;, $(...)) in inputs are interpreted, so a malicious or prompt-injected MCP client gains arbitrary command execution as the server user. Representative line: `const command = \`git -C "${targetPath}" add -- ${filesArg}\`; await execAsync(command)`. Fixed in v2.1.5.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: an IPv6 client sends authentication (or any rate-limited) requests while rotating source addresses inside a typical /64 allocation, or while rewriting one address into another RFC 4291/5952 textual form (case, compression, IPv4-mapped, hex-encoded IPv4-in-IPv6) in x-forwarded-for or the configured IP header. Vulnerable code: getIp returned that header token as the client identity after at most a validity check, and the limiter stored counters under that string (originally the IP alone in getRateLimitKey; later `ip + path` in onRequestRateLimit). Impact: each distinct string is a fresh counter, so production-default rate limits on /sign-in/email, /sign-up/email, /forget-password and other paths do not bind a single IPv6-capable attacker. Preconditions: rate limiting enabled (production default after the core move), IPv6-reachable deployment, and the stock leftmost-forwarded-for IP header path. Counterevidence: IPv4-only deployments are outside the prefix-rotation vector; disabling the limiter or setting advanced.ipAddress.ipv6Subnet to 64 on >= 1.4.16 closes the remaining default-prefix hole without an upgrade.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In PPR/Cache Components deployments (minimalMode), Next.js treats POST requests with header next-resume: 1 as an internal concatenating resume: it drains the request body as postponed state (originally unbounded for-await on req.body; later readBodyWithSizeLimit) and stores it as request meta. That header is a proxy-to-origin protocol and is never sent by browsers. Because it was read from untrusted req.headers and was omitted from INTERNAL_HEADERS / filterInternalHeaders, a client can attach Next-Resume to a crafted POST, including a Server Action. The resume body consumer then races with Server Action body parsing and/or waits on an incomplete body, leaving connections and file descriptors open until capacity is exhausted (CWE-770).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Branch deletion permission bypass after merging a pull request (CWE-284 improper access control): when a PR is merged with 'delete branch after merge' set (form.DeleteBranchAfterMerge), both the web handler (routers/web/repo/pull.go MergePullRequest -> deleteBranch) and the API handler (routers/api/v1/repo/pull.go MergePullRequest) call repo_service.DeleteBranch on the HEAD repo with no write-permission check on that repo. DeleteBranch (services/repository/branch.go) only checks default-branch and protected-branch status, never whether the acting user can write to the head repo. A user who can merge a PR into the base repo (write on base) but has no write access to the head repo (e.g., the PR head is a fork owned by another user) can then delete the head branch in that fork. The pre-existing manual delete-branch-after-merge button (CleanUpPullRequest in routers/web/repo/pull.go) DID enforce perm.CanWrite(models.UnitTypeCode) on the head repo; the automatic path added by #16049 skipped that check entirely. Fixed by extracting repo_service.CanDeleteBranch (perm.CanWrite(unit.TypeCode) plus default/protected checks) and gating both merge flows on it.

fix_hunks.annotation: Landing squash 2222fe3 closes the genericAuthType bypass: unresolved expressions are no longer trusted as literal credential types (isExpression returns null so the checker falls back to every referenced credential). Atomic n8n-private SHA is not public; squash bullet is private PR #215. The same file also gained checkForUser for inline sub-workflows (private #263).
Guards genericAuthType with isExpression at the point the checker reads the parameter, so an unresolved expression can no longer select which credential type is treated as active.

comparison_hunks.annotation: The checker reads the genericAuthType parameter and adds its literal value straight to the active credential type set, trusting whatever string is present without resolving what it becomes at execution time. A node can therefore name a credential type the requesting user never actually shared.

The checker now loads the triggering user and resolves which credentials that user can read, throwing a dedicated inaccessible-credential error for anything not in the accessible set. Expression-valued credential type parameters make the static filter bail out instead of trusting the unresolved literal.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Code injection in @aws/agentcore CLI (npm) 'agentcore add agent --type import': the CLI interpolates the Bedrock collaborator's collaborationInstruction field directly into a Python triple-quoted docstring in the generated main.py. The line used escapePySingleQuote (escapes \ and ' only), which leaves """ unescaped, so a crafted collaborationInstruction can break out of the docstring and inject arbitrary Python into the generated file. Injected code executes on the developer's machine (agentcore dev) and in the AgentCore runtime (agentcore deploy+invoke) under the agent's IAM role. Impacted @aws/agentcore >=0.4, fixed 0.14.2.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CodexBar's release notarization script Scripts/sign-and-notarize.sh writes the App Store Connect API private key from APP_STORE_CONNECT_API_KEY_P8 to the world-shared predictable path /tmp/codexbar-api-key.p8 and stages the notarization zip at /tmp/CodexBarNotarize.zip (later /tmp/${APP_NAME}Notarize.zip). A local same-host attacker can pre-create the names as files or symlinks (CWE-59 link following / CWE-377 insecure temporary file) to capture the notarization credential or tamper with the archive before submission. Cleanup via trap happens only after the files exist, so it does not prevent the exposure window. This is a local release-host issue, not a remote RCE or Developer ID certificate compromise. The fix isolates both artifacts in a 0700 mktemp -d workspace with a 0600 key file.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Source-to-sink: a host pushes a live CLR object into TemplateContext global scope; template member-assignment evaluates the target, obtains the member accessor via context.GetMemberAccessor, and calls TypedObjectAccessor.TrySetValue (ScribanAsync.generated.cs L2297). TrySetValue looks up the member in _members (built by PrepareMembers, which enumerates every public-getter public field/property) and, regardless of setter visibility, invokes reflection PropertyInfo.SetValue (sink L120) or FieldInfo.SetValue. Because reflection ignores C# accessibility and the code never checks GetSetMethod/CanWrite/IsExternalInit, a template can write to private/internal/init setters and to readonly fields (CWE-284), and mass-assign any public setter (CWE-915). The write lands on the live host object and persists after Render(). MemberFilter is read/write-symmetric, so no read-only exposure control exists.

causal_research.bug_semantics: UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response (and hence the cache_page() decorator) contains a guard meant to refuse caching responses that set a cookie while varying on Cookie. The guard was gated on `not request.COOKIES`, i.e. it only fired when the incoming request carried NO cookies at all. A request carrying any unrelated cookie (e.g. analytics, consent) therefore bypassed the guard: a response that set a user-specific cookie (e.g. a newly issued session cookie) and varied on Cookie was stored in Django's shared server-side cache under a Vary: Cookie key basis that does not reliably discriminate users, letting a later remote attacker read another user's private Set-Cookie data from the shared cache.

Parent absence verified: `git grep -E 'COOKIES|has_vary' 8b93b31487d6d3b0fcbbd0498991ea0db9088054 -- django/middleware/cache.py` matches nothing (only Vary docstrings); the file at c083 contains the guard at lines 85-88 (`if not request.COOKIES and response.cookies and has_vary_header(response, 'Cookie'):`). causal_research.flaw_origin: c083e3815aec23b99833da710eea574e6f2e8566 (2014-04-20, Aymeric Augustin, 'Prevented leaking the CSRF token through caching') first wrote the guard in django/middleware/cache.py as `if not request.COOKIES and response.cookies and has_vary_header(response, 'Cookie'): return response`. causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: two concurrent POST /oauth2/token (or legacy /mcp/token) requests with grant_type=authorization_code and the same code. Vulnerable code: checkVerificationValue / oAuth2token does findVerificationValue(code) then a separate deleteVerificationByIdentifier/deleteVerificationValue, so both requests can observe the row before either delete completes, then both run PKCE checks and mint access, refresh, and id tokens. Sink: RFC 6749 §4.1.2 single-use is not enforced under concurrency; an attacker who obtains one code (network, logs, or a cooperating client) can race a second redemption and hold an independent token set for the original user's scopes. Preconditions: the app exposes the OAuth/OIDC token endpoint (oauth-provider, or legacy oidc-provider/mcp) and has no external serialize-by-code mitigation. Counterevidence: sequential reuse after a completed delete fails; the defect is the TOCTOU window, not missing delete.

mechanism.impact: Authorization-code single-use is broken: one code yields two independent token sets (access plus refresh, plus id token when the openid scope is used). mechanism.summary: An OAuth authorization_code is redeemed by a non-atomic find-then-delete: two concurrent POST /oauth2/token requests sharing one code both pass the verification lookup and each mints an independent access/refresh/id-token set, violating single-use redemption.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated admin with category-edit permission POSTs /admin/category/update with existing_image set to a traversal path such as ../../core/config/database.php. System::checkInstallation() treats absence of that file as 'not installed', so unauthenticated GET /setup/ serves the wizard and a new superadmin can be created. Preconditions: valid admin session, CATEGORY_EDIT then CATEGORY_DELETE, valid CSRF tokens, and a single-language category so delete() actually unlinks. Normal uploads still generate category-{id}-{lang}.{ext} names; the free-text existing_image field is the attacker-controlled source.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MLflow pyfunc Spark UDF / model-env restore creates a process-wide temp directory via get_or_create_tmp_dir() and, when NFS is not used, places virtualenv trees under that directory (PyFuncBackend.prepare_env → {tmp}/envs → {tmp}/envs/virtualenv_envs). After tempfile.mkdtemp() creates the directory mode 0o700, the helper immediately chmod's it to 0o777 so Spark UDF workers can see it. Any local user who can write /tmp can then race to create or overwrite files in that world-writable tree, including .py modules inside the restored virtualenv, yielding arbitrary code execution when the victim later imports/runs the env. The Databricks-repl branch of the same function uses os.makedirs without 0o777 and is outside the CVE's /tmp mkdtemp story. CVSS local/high-complexity matches the race plus local /tmp write.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that mkdtemp alone yields 0o700 and that only the explicit chmod creates the world-writable property; that the immediate parent 05f431081e4f has no 0o777 in mlflow/utils/file_utils.py or mlflow/pyfunc/__init__.py; that the venv-routing commit 191ce7038e7aee44bd8ee55917338229f70e55a0 (2022-04-08) put the env root there while the helper was still 0700-private, so it fails the parent-absence test for world-writability; that the 2.0-merge squash 9972267786d895b42c1d7d5e4bdc07aad37bbb95 only moved that helper from mlflow/pyfunc/__init__.py to mlflow/pyfunc/backend.py; that a pickaxe over all refs finds no other commit touching os.chmod(tmp_dir, 0o777) before the fix; and that the advisory's fix is real, released (ancestor of v3.4.0) and followed by a partial-repair advisory for the NFS sibling.
mechanism.impact: Local privilege escalation to the MLflow process owner with arbitrary code execution through attacker-modified venv .py files, plus environment and model-artifact tampering; advisory CVSS 3.0 AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H (HIGH, 7.0), CWE-379, and the CISA ADP enrichment marks technical impact total with proof-of-concept exploitation.
mechanism.preconditions: A pre-fix version (the chmod is present from 2022-04-13 through 1d7c8d4^; verified on v2.20.3 and on the fix's parent); a second local principal able to list and write the tmp root (default /tmp is 1777, and the attacker needs no account on the MLflow side); an MLflow code path that sets create_env_root_dir=True so the venv env root is placed under get_or_create_tmp_dir(); the attacker must act while the world-writable root exists, which is per process and removed at exit, hence the advisory's race framing and the AC:H rating.
mechanism.summary: A local user of the same host can subvert the Python virtual environment MLflow builds for a pyfunc model: get_or_create_tmp_dir() chmods its mkdtemp directory to 0o777, the pyfunc env-root helper creates the venv root at <tmp>/envs inside that world-writable directory, and an attacker who substitutes or plants content there gets code executed as the victim when the environment is populated or imported.
mechanism.trigger: Victim runs an MLflow flow that prepares a model environment with create_env_root_dir=True (mlflow.pyfunc.spark_udf without a prebuilt env, or the local scoring path in mlflow/pyfunc/__init__.py:1293 which sets create_env_root_dir=not is_port_connectable) on a host where another local user can list and write the tmp root; that user inspects /tmp, and because the root is world-writable they may rename or delete the envs entry (write permission on the root suffices for entries in it) or pre-plant files, so the victim's makedirs(envs, exist_ok=True), python -m venv and pip install run inside an attacker-controlled tree and the victim later imports attacker .py as the victim user.

Introduced by bd8854fb2b4b168a4384ebddc6c4a0b5d56aff01 in mlflow/utils/file_utils.py (file hunk @@ -503,6 +503,9 @@) and at the same time for the model and NFS tmp dirs.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-379: an explicit chmod 0o777 on the mkdtemp() directory that later hosts pyfunc virtualenvs under /tmp. Immediate-parent verification shows those chmod lines were first written by named human Weichen Xu in PR #5684 member f9dd2d64; the master squash bd8854 is only the landing carrier. The minimum shipped repair is 1d7c8d4 (#17544), which changes that helper to 0o750 and is present from v3.4.0rc0. The BIC commit object has a named-human author/committer and no AI markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class or EVIDENCE_GAP. Successful later repair does not attribute the defect to AI. A same-pattern NFS chmod from the same PR was out of this CVE's cited /tmp surface and was addressed under a different huntr id.
mlflow's shared tmp helper get_or_create_tmp_dir chmod'ed its private mkdtemp directory to 0o777 from 2022-04-13 until 2025-09-09, and the pyfunc env-root helper builds the virtualenv tree under <that dir>/envs, so a local user who can list and write the shared tmp root can rename or plant the envs entry while the victim prepares the environment and have the victim's venv creation and later imports execute attacker-supplied .py as the victim user (CWE-379, privilege escalation). The introduction is bd8854fb2b4b168a4384ebddc6c4a0b5d56aff01, the single-parent squash landing of PR #5684: the immediate parent 05f431081e4fdbad6a783a0c1a4e0d40345cb375 has no 0o777 anywhere in mlflow/utils/file_utils.py or mlflow/pyfunc/__init__.py, the child adds exactly that chmod, and a pickaxe over all refs returns no other commit that adds or alters the line before the fix. The referenced repair 1d7c8d4cf0a67d407499a8a4ffac387ea4f8194a (PR #17544) turns the chmod into 0o750 and is an ancestor of v3.4.0rc0 and v3.4.0, matching the advisory's patched version, but it is partial: the sibling get_or_create_nfs_tmp_dir kept 0o777 through v3.4.0 and was only repaired by 1dcbb0c2fbd1f446c328830e601ca13a28219b8a (PR #20960, 2026-02-25), which is the fix recorded by the follow-up advisory CVE-2026-4137 that calls CVE-2025-10279 only partially fixed. On the AI side the BIC commit object names the human author WeichenXu <weichen.xu@databricks.com>, committers as GitHub web-flow, carries five human DCO Signed-off-by trailers with empty Co-authored-by, Generated-by and Assisted-by trailer sets, and contains no AI token in its message; the venv-routing commit 191ce7038e7aee44bd8ee55917338229f70e55a0 that first pointed the env root at this helper and the 2.0-merge move 9972267786d895b42c1d7d5e4bdc07aad37bbb95 are likewise human-authored and trailer-clean. No BIC-object AI marker exists anywhere in this causal chain, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Fix completeness rather than AI provenance. The advisory's reference patch closes only the default tmp path: get_or_create_nfs_tmp_dir in the same file kept chmod 0o777 at 1d7c8d4 and in v3.4.0 and still supplies the virtualenv env root when NFS is in use, so on NFS-enabled deployments (for example Databricks with the NFS cache) the CVE-2025-10279 mechanism remained available until 1dcbb0c2 (PR #20960, 2026-02-25); that residual is exactly what the follow-up advisory CVE-2026-4137 describes as CVE-2025-10279 being only partially fixed, and it is human-authored, so it does not change the verdict. A second boundary, by design rather than defect: 0o750 keeps group read and execute for Spark UDF accessibility, so a same-group principal can still read the environment, and the helper is cached per process so the directory lives for the whole process lifetime. No AI question remains open on this case.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who controls a JSON Schema/OpenAPI document sets customBasePath to a string containing a newline and a Python expression with no '.' characters (so Import.from_full_path will not split the payload). JsonSchemaObject accepts the field without identifier validation and the parser copies it into DataModel.custom_base_class (originally directly; later via _resolve_base_class, which only normalizes lists). set_base_class calls Import.from_full_path, which splits only on '.', then Imports.create_line renders 'from {module} import {name}' verbatim. The embedded newline becomes a new physical line in the generated module, so the injected statement runs when that module is imported. The same sink already existed for operator-controlled --base-class; this CVE is the schema-controlled ent

causal_research.bug_semantics:
Reflected XSS in the OAuth callback page (CWE-79): create_callback_html() in src/fastmcp/client/oauth_callback.py composes the callback HTML page via f-string interpolation of message, title, and server_url with no HTML escaping (e.g., the template contains
{message}
and Connected to: {server_url}). The /callback route handler reads the error and error_description query parameters and passes f'OAuth Error: {error}
{error_desc}' as the message, so GET /callback?error= on the localhost callback server executes attacker-controlled JS in the callback page's origin (reflected XSS, CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:P/SC:L/SI:L). A malicious OAuth authorization server can trigger it automatically by returning the crafted URL in authorization_endpoint, which the client then opens in the browser. causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated remote OOM/event-loop DoS in vLLM's OpenAI-compatible API server from v0.1.0 through before 0.19.0. The `n` sampling parameter (number of output sequences per request) is parsed by ChatCompletionRequest/CompletionRequest Pydantic models without any upper-bound Field constraint; SamplingParams._verify_args only enforces the lower bound (n >= 1). A single HTTP request with an astronomically large n reaches vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py, where a synchronous for-loop over range(n) copies request objects millions of times inside the single-threaded asyncio event loop, blocking all other connections and driving RSS up gigabytes per second until the OS OOM-killer terminates the process.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Role-restriction bypass / missing authorization check (CWE-863; GHSA-4phw-6824-6cfp = CVE-2026-33551, CVSS 3.1 3.5 LOW, NVD published 2026-04-10, OSSA-2026-005 reported 2026-04-07 by Maxence Bornecque of Orange Cyberdefense; affects keystone >=14.0.0 <26.1.1 and ==27.0.0/28.0.0/29.0.0, first_patched 26.1.1): keystone application credentials carry an 'unrestricted' flag (originally 'allow_application_credential_creation'); a RESTRICTED app credential may only be used for operations its limited role set (e.g. reader) permits, and its token records auth method 'application_credential'. The EC2 credential endpoints (POST /v3/users/{user_id}/credentials/OS-EC2, DELETE /v3/users/{user_id}/credentials/OS-EC2/{credential_id}) predate application credentials (keystone/contrib/ec2/controllers.py since 2012) and never received the _check_unrestricted_application_credential guard that the application-credential create/delete endpoints had from the start. Their only enforcement is the pre-existing policy identity:ec2_create_credential = RULE_ADMIN_OR_OWNER, which any token owner passes for their own IDs. An authenticated user holding only a reader role but owning a restricted app credential can authenticate with it and mint EC2/S3 credentials bound to the FULL parent user; those EC2 credentials carry the parent user's complete S3 permissions, bypassing the role restriction (reader escalates to full-user S3 access). The fix adds the unrestricted guard to EC2 create/delete and tightens both policies to a new ADMIN_OR_MEMBER_AND_CRED_OWNER rule so reader-role tokens can no longer mutate EC2 credentials at all.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Hermes Agent streaming paths try to hide model reasoning by suppressing known XML-like think tags as tokens arrive, then also strip those tags case-insensitively from the final stored reply. GatewayStreamConsumer._filter_and_accumulate (copied into the gateway from the CLI _stream_delta state machine) detected tags with case-sensitive str.find() against a hardcoded tuple that listed only some casings (<think>, <thinking>, <THINKING>, <thought>, <reasoning>, <REASONING_SCRATCHPAD>). Mixed-case or missing-case variants such as <THINK>, <Think>, <ThInK>, <THOUGHT>, and <REASONING> never matched, so the filter never entered the in-think state and streamed the inner reasoning live to CLI/gateway users (Discord/Telegram/Slack/etc.). Prompt injection that tells the model to wrap reasoning in those variants is the disclosed remote trigger. The final post-process path using re.IGNORECASE still removed the tags from the kept message, so the leak is mid-stream information disclosure of hidden chain-of-thought.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Transport-security flaw (CWE-319) in the OpenClaw Android gateway client: non-loopback remote gateway endpoints were accepted and connected over cleartext ws:// (the scheme picked 'wss' only when a TLS config was present, with no loopback/emulator exemption logic and no TLS requirement for remote hosts), and the client sent STORED gateway credentials (token/password loaded from SecurePrefs) over that unencrypted connection. Discovery beacons or forged setup codes could thereby steer the client onto an attacker-controlled cleartext remote endpoint, disclosing stored credentials in plaintext. Affected <= 2026.4.1 (npm openclaw), fixed >= 2026.4.2.
causal_research.evidence: Identity: member_map pin CVE-2026-40045 + GHSA-83f3-hh45-vfw9 (OSV valid: 'OpenClaw: Android accepted cleartext remote gateway endpoints and sent stored credentials over ws://'; npm openclaw <= 2026.4.1 affected, >= 2026.4.2 fixed; fix commit a941a4fef9bc43b2973c92d0dcff5b8a426210c5 'require TLS for remote Android gateway endpoints'; thanks @zsxsoft). causal_research.bug_semantics: With GraphQL mounted and graphQLPublicIntrospection false (default since GHSA-48q3 / 8.2.2), an unauthenticated client that knows only the public application ID and a Pointer or Relation field name can force graphql-js validation or input-coercion to fail before authentication, authorization, or any resolver. Parse Server generates GraphQL types whose names embed the field's TARGET class (for example SecretAuthor, SecretAuthorPointerInput, SecretAuthorRelationWhereInput, CreateSecretAuthorFieldsInput) and maps Pointer/Relation fields to those types in parseClassTypes.js and transformers/outputType.js. graphql-js interpolates the type name into base error templates that the earlier SchemaSuggestionsControlPlugin did not redact (it only stripped 'Did you mean' suffixes and the required-field coercion sentence). The resulting error therefore discloses hidden class names, partially defeating schema-hiding. Master-key and public-introspection callers are out of scope; no object data or credentials leak.

mechanism.impact: Disclosure of hidden schema metadata: target class names of Pointer and Relation fields are reconstructed from error messages, partially defeating the schema-hiding protection of graphQLPublicIntrospection: false. No object data, credentials or user records are disclosed.
mechanism.preconditions: graphQLPublicIntrospection is not enabled (default false) and the caller presents no master/maintenance key; the deployment schema contains Pointer or Relation fields (or output object types) whose target class names are meant to stay hidden.
mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated caller holding only the public application id sends a GraphQL operation that touches a Pointer/Relation field and fails validation or input coercion; graphql-js interpolates the generated type name ('<Target>PointerInput', '<Target>RelationWhereInput', 'Create<Target>FieldsInput', or the target output type) into the error text, and Apollo returns that text unchanged because graphQLPublicIntrospection=false only blocks __schema/__type and no pre-9.10.0 post-processing sanitized these templates. The attacker thus reads hidden class names (CWE-209, class metadata only).
mechanism.trigger: GraphQL request authenticated with the public X-Parse-Application-Id only (no master or maintenance key), e.g. 'query { diagBooks(where: { writtenBy: 123 }) { edges { node { id } } } }' or a mutation variable '{ input: { fields: { writtenBy: { createAndLink: 5 } } } }', against a schema whose class has a Pointer/Relation field to a target class that should stay hidden.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The web_crawl/crawl_web tools' HTTP fallback fetcher (_crawl_with_httpx in src/praisonai-agents/praisonaiagents/tools/web_crawl_tools.py) validated each user URL once before fetching: it parsed the host and called socket.gethostbyname(hostname), rejecting loopback/private/link-local/multicast/unspecified results unless ALLOW_LOCAL_CRAWL=true. But the actual fetch used httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True) or, without httpx, urllib.request.urlopen(url) (redirect-following by default), and both re-resolved DNS at connect time with zero further validation. This validate-here/fetch-there TOCTOU gap (CWE-367/CWE-918) allows two independent bypasses: (1) an approved public attacker domain replies 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/ or another internal target, followed unchecked; (2) DNS rebinding — low-TTL name answers public to the validator and private/loopback to the fetcher. Response bodies are returned to the agent, leaking internal services and cloud metadata credentials.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With open email/password registration, an attacker signs up at the victim's address with an attacker-chosen password. The row stays emailVerified=false, so password sign-in is blocked when requireEmailVerification is on. When the victim later proves mailbox control, magic-link GET /magic-link/verify and email-OTP POST sign-in both resolve that existing user, set emailVerified=true, and mint a session without deleting the credential account or revoking sessions. The planted password then authenticates as the now-verified owner. New-user auto-signup in the same handlers (createUser with emailVerified:true) is not the hijack; the defect is adopting an unproven pre-existing credential row as verified. The fix treats current mailbox proof as authoritative: revokeUnprovenAccountAccess strips credential accounts and sessions before the verify flip.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-400/770 (resource exhaustion, CVSS 7.5): Rack::QueryParser parses query strings and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies by splitting on & and iterating every key-value pair into a Hash (parse_query/parse_nested_query -> _normalize_params) with NO upper bound on the number of parameters and no total bytesize limit, so a single crafted request with hundreds of thousands of parameters consumes excessive memory and CPU, stalling or crashing the Rack server (full DoS). The earlier key_space_limit partial mitigation (capping total parameter-key bytes at 65536, 2011) was determined ineffective (nested params bypassed it) and was neutralized in 2022, leaving parsing fully unbounded until the 2025 fix added RACK_QUERY_PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT/ PARAMS_LIMIT (defaults 4MB and 4096) and QueryLimitError.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MLflow basic-auth (opt-in via mlflow server --app-name basic-auth) stored user passwords with werkzeug generate_password_hash but imposed no server-side minimum length. SqlAlchemyStore.create_user validated only the username, then hashed whatever password string it received. Until #9700, POST /api/2.0/mlflow/users and GET /signup were unprotected, so a remote client could create an account with a trivial password and then authenticate. Client-side minlength=4 and non-empty checks from #13854 did not block that default. The 12-character create_user check plus lengthening the default to password1234 is the vendor closure cited by ZDI/GHSA.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GitPython guards dangerous git options through Git.check_unsafe_options(), but that guard is opt-in per call site via allow_unsafe_options. IndexFile.checkout() (git/index/base.py, repo.git.checkout_index(*args, **kwargs)) and TagReference.create() (git/refs/tag.py, repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs)) forwarded caller-controlled **kwargs straight into git without any guard. A caller could pass git-checkout-index's --prefix=<path> to write checked-out files to an arbitrary filesystem path, or git-tag's --file/-F <path> to read an arbitrary file as the tag message (its content exposed in the created tag object), enabling arbitrary file overwrite and arbitrary file read.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated remote code execution in Spree < 0.60.2 via the product search functionality. GET /?search[send][]=eval&search[send][]=Kernel.fork%20do%60<cmd>%60end (metasploit module spree_search_exec, exploit-db 17941, joernchen@phenoelit disclosure 2011-10-05): products_controller builds @searcher = Spree::Config.searcher_class.new(params); Spree::Search::Base#prepare calls @product_group.from_search(params[:search]) when params[:search] is present; ProductGroup#from_search iterates raw (scope_name, scope_attribute) pairs into add_scope, which stores ProductScope {name => scope_name.to_s, arguments => [*args]} with NO name validation; ProductScope#apply runs Product.send(self.name, *self.arguments) - so an attacker-controlled scope name is dispatched via Ruby send on Product with attacker-controlled args, reaching arbitrary method invocation (send/eval/system etc. CVSS v2 9.0, v3 9.8, v4 10.0 per rubysec advisory). Fixed in 0.60.2 by rejecting scope names matching /eval|send|system|[^a-z0-9_!?]/ in ProductGroup#add_scope.

Fix commit 453f4078e1c694b8a8ff11a118c9fb4474b56e85 (2011-10-04, parent 24455e9e) 'Added scope_name filtering': add_scope raises ArgumentError when scope_name matches /eval|send|system|[^a-z0-9_!?]/; also changed Product.search -> Product.metasearch; tag v0.60.2 contains it (range v0.60.1..v0.60.2 ~9 commits, others unrelated). Introducer: git log -S 'Product.send(self.name' --all -> first writer 05de3d6909d7134da35d1d78189c82add79f08be which CREATED core/app/models/product_scope.rb (line: Product.send(self.name, *self.arguments)) and core/app/models/product_group.rb with from_search/add_scope (git log -S 'from_search' --all also starts at 05de3d6909); git cat-file -e 0ecbaab999:core/app/models/product_scope.rb -> rc=128 (absent at parent, first-appearance-in-history confirmed by pickaxe order). git grep from_search at 05de3d6909: only the definition (no callers yet - HTTP wiring added later, before 0.60.1, in the same unguarded form; the shipped+metasploit'd attack surface is 0.60.1, whose primitive traces to 05de3d6909; fix touched the exact primitive site).
causal_research.flaw_origin: Missing allowlist/validation on product scope names at creation: add_scope stored the raw name (scope_name.to_s) with no character/method check, and ProductScope#apply blindly dispatched it via Product.send(self.name, ...). The entire vulnerable primitive (from_search + unvalidated add_scope + Product.send dispatch) first entered the repository atomically in the refactoring commit that created core/app/models/product_group.rb and core/app/models/product_scope.rb; HTTP wiring (products_controller params[:search] -> searcher -> from_search) was added between 2010-06 and 0.60.1, but the unguarded dispatch point remained untouched until the scope_name filtering fix landed 15 months later.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: an attacker POSTs /sign-up/email (or the earlier /sign-up/credential) for a victim address, creating a local user with emailVerified=false and a password credential. Sink: when the victim later completes any OAuth/SSO callback that reaches handleOAuthUserInfo (or the one-tap copy), the library looks up that row by email and, if the IdP reports email_verified or the provider is trusted, calls linkAccount onto the attacker user id. Impact: the victim's OAuth identity is bound to the attacker account (pre-account hijacking / nOAuth-class). A later post-link step (cf2cac4) also sets local emailVerified=true, so emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification does not stop password login after the link. Preconditions: email+password enabled, at least one OAuth/SSO provider, implicit linking not disabled. Counterevidence to 'trusted providers only': the original 8f4b2d8 gate already auto-linked on provider emailVerified with no trustedProviders list.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory describes a real nOAuth-class account-takeover: implicit OAuth linking treated an IdP email_verified claim as ownership of any local row with that email, including attacker-created unverified password accounts. The smallest first-writer of that gate is human commit 8f4b2d8f106340ab7ca61afafff11f66fac46c95; the parent tree has no linking. The GitHub-squash fix da7e50beee849c59a2ed1ec6b3a38cc6ab9fb563 (PR #9578) is in v1.6.11 and not in v1.6.10. The BIC commit object has a named-human author/committer and no AI trailers, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI. Fix-side Copilot review does not attribute the defect.
Pre-account hijacking as described: an attacker pre-registers a victim email through the email/password sign-up path, which writes a row with emailVerified: false (packages/better-auth/src/api/routes/sign-up.ts:272 signUpEmail at the fix parent), and the victim's later OAuth or SSO sign-in implicitly links the provider identity onto that row because the auto-link gate only inspects the provider's email_verified claim. I reproduced the vulnerable gate at the fix parent 29599d32: packages/better-auth/src/oauth2/link-account.ts handleOAuthUserInfo admits the link when `(!isTrustedProvider && !userInfo.emailVerified) || ...` is false (line 56), never reading the local row's emailVerified, then calls linkAccount with `userId: dbUser.user.id` (lines 71-74) and promotes the local row to verified (lines 91-95), which defeats emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification. The origin is 8f4b2d8f1 (feat: callback oauth, 2024-08-18): its parent 93f11a633 contains only `await c.adapter.createUser(user)` at callback.ts:33 with no linking code, and the new adapters/internal-adapter.ts is absent at that parent, while the child adds findOAuthUserByEmail (adapters/internal-adapter.ts:43) and links on the provider's user.emailVerified at callback.ts:51-64. The intermediate history tightened and relaxed the same gate (811ba1267, f4e1d9666, 4795b2201, 8078b79d, e7c46e035) and extracted it to link-account.ts (9cddaad62) without ever adding the local-row check, and packages/better-auth/src/plugins/one-tap/index.ts restated the same primitive at 0a47a402e. The official fix da7e50bee (v1.6.11, ancestor of release commit f41514ef0) adds `(requireLocalEmailVerified && !dbUser.user.emailVerified)` to the gate and the matching check plus toBoolean normalization to one-tap, closing the takeover while leaving a declared requireLocalEmailVerified: false opt-out and two FIXMEs deferring the unconditional gate. The BIC commit object carries a named human author and committer (Bereket Engida <bekacru@gmail.com>, 1723976810 +0300) with a one-line message and no trailers, and a raw-object marker scan finds nothing; no AI-marked commit on this surface newly exposed or partially remediated the defect, so the record is NOT_AI with the pre-2025 attribution-convention caveat recorded in remaining_gap.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Attribution minimality: 8f4b2d8f1 predates this repo's AI attribution convention (earliest AI co-author trailer 2025-10-05, earliest AI bot author 2026-01-13; 2024 Co-authored-by trailers are human co-authors only), so the clean BIC object is evidence against AI origin but cannot positively exclude unmarked AI assistance in August 2024 - the next minimal question is whether any external record (e.g. the author's own statements or tool provenance for this commit) shows AI assistance, since no primary object evidence exists in the clone. Fix residual by design: `account.accountLinking.requireLocalEmailVerified: false` reopens the takeover as a declared backward-compatibility opt-out, and the FIXME(next-minor) comments in link-account.ts and one-tap/index.ts defer the unconditional gate; the separate SSO domainVerified trust hardening (cb1cbfa4ccba1ce13f7fea419a6fc37dcbdc2f15) is outside this record's minimum fix set.

causal_research.bug_semantics: HAX CMS Node.js serves the admin UI and generated sites through Express. From the first commit the app called helmet() with contentSecurityPolicy:false (helmet 7.1.0), so responses did not include Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors. HTML templates (public/index.html, later src/boilerplate/site/index.html) had no CSP/X-Frame-Options meta, and generated-site .htaccess set only X-Content-Type-Options. An unauthenticated attacker who can cause a user to load the login page or other UI in a cross-origin iframe can UI-redress clicks (CWE-1021). The vendor fix adds helmet directives.frameAncestors=['self'] so Express-served pages emit CSP frame-ancestors 'self'. Note: helmet 7.1.0 still default-sets X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, and custom CSP without useDefaults:false merges default frame-an

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated workspace Git APIs in api/workspace_git.py run git as a subprocess in the session workspace without neutralizing repository-local executable Git configuration. A malicious or restored workspace can place helpers in .git/config so that read-only git status executes core.fsmonitor, and default-enabled git fetch --prune (POST /api/git/fetch is not gated by HERMES_WEBUI_WORKSPACE_GIT_DESTRUCTIVE) executes protocol.ext ext:: remotes, credential.helper, core.askPass, core.gitProxy, or core.sshCommand. Inherited GIT_SSH_COMMAND/GIT_ASKPASS were also honored. That yields host command execution as the WebUI process user (CWE-78). The v0.51.311 fix forces git -c overrides on every workspace Git invocation and scrubs the remaining executable env vars.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The smallest public first-write of the patched sink is 5fc7aee78187a71283be22577c3b977a88fb0916, which added api/workspace_git.py with _run_git() calling subprocess.run(["git", *args]) and git_status/git_fetch wrappers. Immediate parent 9c983e693aed0cc502507bfa9ec78f56e398c43f has no that file. This is not a move of api/workspace.py:git_info_for_workspace (that older status helper remains in place). PR #2625 merge 45c7a693 is the carrier; 9ac94d3 only widened env scrubbing and left repo-local .git/config executable. Unmerged #2578 4d5c75cd is not in product history.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-345/CWE-20 content-type verification bypass: ActiveStorage::DirectUploadsController#blob_args permits an arbitrary client-supplied metadata hash (permit(metadata: {})), and ActiveStorage::Blob stores internal state flags 'identified'/'analyzed'/'composed' in that same metadata store (store :metadata, accessors:, coder: JSON). A direct-upload client can therefore set identified/analyzed to skip MIME detection and analysis, uploading arbitrary content while claiming a safe content_type, defeating validations that rely on Active Storage's automatic content-type identification. Fixed by filtering PROTECTED_METADATA = %w(analyzed identified composed) out of user metadata in Blob.create_before_direct_upload!. Affected < 7.2.3.1 / 8.0.4.1 / 8.1.2.1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Ghost's public Content API endpoints (posts/pages/authors browse & read) accept an NQL `filter` query parameter that is translated into DB WHERE clauses. Since GHSA-r97q-ghch-82j9 (May 2023) these endpoints attached a mongoTransformer (rejectPrivateFieldsTransformer) meant to drop any filter statement touching private user fields (password, email). The transformer matched keys too narrowly: it used lowerCaseKey.startsWith('authors.password'/'authors.email') (and in later refactors split('.').pop() last-segment matching plus startsWith prefix checks), so compound/table-qualified keys such as users.password:'<bcrypt-hash>' or authors.password.x:'<hash>' slipped past validation and were applied as real query conditions. Because filtering is reflected in result inclusion, an unauthenticated attacker could brute-force password hashes character-by-character via 'starts with'-style operators; with SQLite the full hash was recoverable, while MySQL case-insensitivity largely defeated further cracking. GHSA CVSS 3.1: AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SQL injection (CWE-89) in QuerySet.filter()/exclude()/get() and Q() via a crafted '_connector' keyword argument (dictionary expansion). Q.__init__ accepted an arbitrary connector string and propagated it into a WhereNode whose connector is interpolated verbatim into the WHERE clause in WhereNode.as_sql ('conn = " %s " % self.connector; sql_string = conn.join(result)'), allowing SQL breakout, e.g. Q(_connector='evil').
causal_research.evidence: Members hash-verified: sha256('CVE-2025-64459\nGHSA-frmv-pr5f-9mcr\n')[:24] == d7eed19fe6fad427cfa30299. GHSA-frmv-pr5f-9mcr = CVE-2025-64459 (aliases PYSEC-2025-108), published 2025-11-05, affects Django 5.1<5.1.14, 4.2<4.2.26, 5.2<5.2.8. Fix commits (all Jacob Walls, 2025-11-05): 98e642c69181c942d60a10ca0085d48c6b3068bb (main), 06dd38324ac3d60d83d9f3adabf0dcdf423d2a85 [6.0.x], 6703f364d767e949c5b0e4016433ef75063b4f9b [5.2.x], 72d2c87431f2ae0431d65d0ec792047f078c8241 [5.1.x], 59ae82e67053d281ff4562a24bbba21299f0a7d4 [4.2.x]; diff adds 'connectors = (None, AND, OR, XOR)' validation raising ValueError in Q.__init__ + tests/queries/test_q.py::test_connector_validation. Introducer commit verified: parent 19b2dfd1 (2017-02-23, Ian Foote) has Q.__init__(*args, **kwargs) -> super().__init__(children=list(args)+list(kwargs.items())) with no _connector special-casing, so a '_connector' kwarg was an inert field lookup there; where.py at parent already interpolates ' %s ' % self.connector verbatim (sink pre-exists, unsafe source added by 508b5debfb). Propagation at BIC: models/query.py filter_obj=Q(*args,**kwargs); add_q->_add_q: connector=q_object.connector; target_clause=where_class(connector=connector,...); where.add(clause, AND). BIC is a normal single-parent commit (not a squash).
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 508b5debfb (2017-02-23, 'Refs #11964 -- Made Q objects deconstructible') first special-cased kwargs.pop('_connector', None) / '_negated' in Q.__init__ (django/db/models/query_utils.py), turning '_connector' from a plain (parameterized) field lookup into a raw connector string that flows through Query._add_q -> where_class(connector=...) -> WhereNode.as_sql verbatim SQL join. The deconstruct() method added in the same commit exposed _connector via kwargs in serialization paths. No validation existed until the CVE fix; any caller-supplied _connector string reached SQL directly.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior (unvalidated caller-supplied SQL connector string reaching verbatim SQL interpolation) was introduced on 2017-02-23 by human maintainer Ian Foote in a refactor commit making Q objects deconstructible - 8 years before the advisory and well before AI-assisted coding was common. Neither the introducer nor any of the five 2025 fix commits carries AI markers (bodies scanned for co-authored/assisted-by/copilot/claude/codex/openai/grok/etc.: 0 hits; author Ian Foote, committer Tim Graham; fixes by Jacob Walls). Per the closed-causal-chain rule, remediation-side tooling is irrelevant here and the origin is fully human.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CORS wildcard + credentials misconfiguration (CWE-942 / OWASP A05:2021): the LightRAG API server defaulted to CORS_ORIGINS="*" combined with allow_credentials=True in Starlette CORSMiddleware. Starlette echoes the requesting origin in preflight responses when credentials are enabled, so every origin is effectively whitelisted for credentialed cross-origin requests - any malicious website can perform authenticated API calls (Bearer token / X-API-Key) on behalf of a logged-in user. Fixed in lightrag-hku 1.5.4 (PR #3317).

mechanism.impact: Incorrect authorization (CWE-863): files and subdirectories that the share owner explicitly blocked with rules become readable and browsable - and includable in directory downloads - by anyone holding the share URL, which for unpassworded shares is unauthenticated internet-reachable information disclosure; advisory severity HIGH, CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N.
mechanism.preconditions: The share must target a directory (file shares keep filePath empty and cannot address descendants); the owner must have at least one deny rule whose path lies below the share root, expressed relative to the owner's scope; unauthenticated exploitation requires a share without a password token (password-protected shares require authenticateShareRequest to pass, http/public.go:26-29); the owner account must hold Share and Download permissions (http/public.go:36-38).
mechanism.summary: Public directory shares rebase the owner's filesystem onto the shared root (`afero.NewBasePathFs(d.user.Fs, basePath)`) and then authorize the request-relative path with `d.Check`, which prefix-matches that relative path against rules that are still written relative to the owner's original scope; a deny rule such as /projects/private therefore no longer matches a request for /private/secret.txt even though the rebased filesystem resolves it to the real blocked path /projects/private/secret.txt, so rule-blocked descendants of a public share are served (CWE-863, incorrect authorization).
mechanism.trigger: An attacker fetches a descendant path below a public directory share - `GET /api/public/share/<hash>/<rel>` (listing) or `GET /api/public/dl/<hash>/<rel>` (content or directory archive) - where the share owner has a deny rule on that descendant path (for example rule /projects/private under share root /projects/); no session is required when the share is not password protected.

causal_research.bug_semantics:
When aria2c is the external downloader for a fragmented manifest format (HLS m3u8 / DASH mpd), yt-dlp extracts fragment URLs and writes them into an aria2c input file passed via -i, using per-URI option lines (out=<fragment filename>) because aria2c treats any line beginning with whitespace after a URI as options. The fragment URLs and derived fragment filenames are not sanitized: (1) in DASH manifests an attacker-controlled fragment URL containing the HTML escape 
 is unescaped to a real newline when written to the input file, letting the attacker inject arbitrary aria2c option lines; (2) with --no-windows-filename, newlines and magnet URIs from attacker-controlled metadata (e.g. title used in the output template) survive filename sanitization and are injected into the input file. Injected options/URIs yield arbitrary file writes (out=, dir, dry-run magnet writes), leading to arbitrary code execution on Windows via a written ffmpeg.exe invoked during postprocessing, and on any platform via a written yt-dlp.conf with a malicious --exec on the next invocation. CWE-74 injection, CVSS 8.3 high.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Rack::Multipart parser buffers non-file form fields (parts without a filename) entirely in process memory as Ruby Strings with no size cap; a single multi-hundred-MB text field in a multipart/form-data request exhausts worker memory (CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption, DoS). File parts are streamed to Tempfiles; the unbounded in-memory path is only for non-file fields, from the parser's first commit to 2025.

Introducer: git log --reverse -S 'Multipart' -- lib/rack/utils.rb => 4fe5360a 'Make Rack::Request read multipart form data', Christian Neukirchen <chris@...> (project creator), 2007-02-28; diff shows module Multipart with `body = ''` / `body = Tempfile.new('RackMultipart') if filename` / `body << buf.slice!(0, i)` - the vulnerable in-memory accumulation verbatim. Parent 758f9287: git grep -i 'multipart' at parent rc=1 (no multipart code anywhere); no part-buffering patterns in utils.rb (rc=1). Fix: 589127f4/d869fed6/e08f78c6 (identical 'Fix denial of service vulnerbilties in multipart parsing', Jeremy Evans, 2025-09-15, one per maintained branch) add BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT (16KB), MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (64KB) and update_retained_size enforcing BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (default 16MiB) on BufferPart (non-file) bodies; verified in v3.2.1..v3.2.2 diff; 4c4ea296/8d141b30/bce149b1 are patch version bumps (2025-10-07).

causal_research.bug_semantics: org.freedesktop.UDisks2.Block.RestoreEncryptedHeader is a privileged D-Bus method implemented by handle_restore_encrypted_header() in src/udiskslinuxblock.c. A local unprivileged caller can invoke it on the system bus; udisksd (root) resolves the target block, takes the caller UID, launches a job, and calls libblockdev bd_crypto_luks_header_restore() on udisks_block_get_device(block) using the caller-supplied backup_file path. Unlike neighboring Block handlers (Format, Rescan, Open*), this path never calls udisks_daemon_util_check_authorization_sync(), so no polkit action is required. The overwrite destroys LUKS headers and keyslots (integrity/availability DoS; original passphrase no longer unlocks). The handler also does not require the target to be LUKS, so it can clobber non-LUKS devices. CWE-862.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Command-line injection on Windows when executing batch files (CWE-77): Windows CreateProcess implicitly spawns cmd.exe when the target is a .bat/.cmd file, so arguments passed unquoted by Deno.Command.spawn()/node:child_process compatibility (e.g. args: ['&calc.exe']) are interpreted by cmd.exe as additional commands. causal_research.bug_semantics: Four independent @better-auth/sso paths let an attacker obtain a victim session when self-service provider registration (providersLimit>0) and default implicit account linking are on. (1) Domain mismatch: verifyDomain proves one hostname via tldts/URL parsing of the whole domain string, while sign-in/org routing uses domainMatches comma-split, so https://attacker.com/path,victim.com verifies as attacker.com but later trusts victim.com. (2) Orphan accounts: deleteSSOProvider removes only the ssoProvider row; providerId becomes re-registrable and stale (providerId, accountId) rows still resolve. (3) Unbound SAML: processSAMLResponse checks signature/issuer/status/timestamps/replay but not assertion AudienceRestriction, bearer Recipient, or response Destination, so a signed assertion issued for another SP at a shared IdP is accepted. (4) SLO XSS: with saml.enableSingleLogout, the unauthenticated /sso/saml2/sp/slo handler (origin check skipped, LogoutRequest unsigned by default) emits createSAMLPostForm with an IdP-supplied javascript: or data: Location as form action. Shared impact is account takeover without the victim acting, except the XSS path which needs a lure.
