mechanism.counterevidence: A: checked that the verifier is the only gate that marks a provider verified and that it queries exactly one hostname (domain-verification.ts:178-205 at v1.6.20) while the matcher honours every entry via split/trim (utils.ts:38-46); the fix's own normalization test confirms tldts maps 'https://company.com/path' to company.com, which is what lets the URL-shaped entry prove the attacker host while the plain victim entry matches at sign-in. B: checked the v1.6.20 delete path touches only model ssoProvider and that git grep 'model: "account"' is empty in packages/sso; checked the later 68f70b7b1 (#7903) is a method/path change to POST /sso/delete-provider and not an introduction. D: checked the template does escape HTML entities, so tag injection is not the vector and the scheme handling is, and the fix's new tests model javascript: and data: actions explicitly.
mechanism.impact: A, B and C are account takeover: an attacker obtains a session or account mapping for a victim user, matching the advisory's CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N (HIGH), and the advisory's summary that attackers can sign in as arbitrary users. D is reflected script execution in the victim's browser on the application origin (CWE-79), enabling session or credential theft during the logout flow.
mechanism.preconditions: A: the attacker can create an SSO provider and publish TXT records for a domain he controls; the victim's domain sits in the same provider's comma-separated list; sign-in routes email domains through the naive matcher, which v1.6.20 does at routes/sso.ts:1176 and in validateEmailDomain (utils.ts:53-68). B: an SSO provider is deleted while its account rows exist and a second provider with the same providerId is later created (or already configured) and used for sign-in. C: the attacker can obtain a signed assertion from the same IdP for a different audience/SP, or can otherwise craft a response bound to a context this SP does not check; the plugin accepts the response before any session creation. D: the configured IdP's SLO Location is attacker-influenced, for example a rogue IdP or tampered SAML metadata, and a user follows the SLO flow.
mechanism.summary: Four independent authentication defects in @better-auth/sso before 1.6.21: (A) domain verification proves only the single hostname that tldts extracts from the whole comma-separated provider.domain string while sign-in matching accepts every comma entry, so an attacker can prove a host he owns and still have victim domains routed to his IdP; (B) deleting an SSO provider removes only the ssoProvider row, leaving account rows keyed by providerId that a later provider with the same providerId re-binds to the victim's user; (C) the SAML ACS parses assertions without validating audience, bearer recipient or destination, so an assertion the trusted IdP issued for a different audience is accepted and mapped to a local account; (D) the SLO POST form emits the IdP-supplied endpoint as the form action after HTML-escaping only, so a javascript: or data: URL executes as script on the application origin (CWE-79).
mechanism.trigger: A: an attacker registers a provider whose domain list leads with a URL-shaped entry for a host he controls, for example 'https://attacker.com/path,victim.com', publishes the verification TXT token under attacker.com, completes verification, and afterwards any victim.com email is matched to this provider at sign-in. B: an administrator deletes an SSO provider; account rows linked to its providerId survive because only the ssoProvider row is removed; a later provider created with the same providerId is used to sign in, and the orphaned account rows are reused for its accountId. C: the attacker presents a SAML response signed by the trusted IdP but issued for a different audience or service provider, or otherwise not bound to this SP, to /sso/saml2/callback/:providerId. D: the victim's browser is made to run the SLO flow against a provider whose IdP SLO Location uses a javascript: or data: scheme, and the auto-submitting POST form executes it.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: A: packages/sso/src/routes/domain-verification.ts:178 (getHostnameFromDomain(provider.domain) then dns.resolveTxt('${identifier}.${hostname}'), one hostname for the whole comma string) together with packages/sso/src/utils.ts:38-46 (domainMatches splits on commas and accepts one entry or a subdomain suffix), both at v1.6.20 (c342f42f); the mismatch enters with 75ee9ea2a, which added domainMatches at utils.ts:35 and the multi-domain matcher. causal_research.reasoning:
CVE-2026-67328 / GHSA-8g2f-78cq-p655 alias the vendor GHSA-prpr-5gj3-qqhg cluster. All four described mechanisms exist in v1.6.20 and are closed in v1.6.21 / v1.7.0-beta.10 by four named-human squash-merges. The smallest original first-writer of the earliest mechanism (unbound SAML) is #3185 member e0384a275, a named-human commit with no AI marker after rejecting the cubic-dev-ai-coauthored landing aggregate. The other three first-writers are also named-human with empty trailers, and the 1.7 #9055 audience helper is an incomplete human remediation rather than an AI introduction. Successful human repair does not create a TP. Verdict is NOT_AI.
The advisory names four independent pre-1.6.21 authentication defects in @better-auth/sso, and all four reproduce in primary code. Verification accepted a provider whose comma-separated domain string led with a URL-shaped entry for an attacker-owned host: tldts extracted only that one hostname for the TXT proof while the naive split-based matcher used at sign-in accepted the victim domain listed beside it, so victim email domains were routed to the attacker's IdP (A). deleteSSOProvider deleted only the ssoProvider row, and because sign-in re-binds account rows by the mutable providerId string, a later provider with the same providerId inherited the orphaned account links to the victim's user (B). The SAML ACS parsed the assertion with samlify's sp.parseLoginResponse and created a session without checking AudienceRestriction, SubjectConfirmationData Recipient or Destination, so an assertion the trusted IdP minted for a different audience was accepted (C). The SLO POST form interpolated the IdP-supplied endpoint into a form action after HTML-escaping only, with no scheme allow-list, so a javascript: or data: action executed in the victim's browser (D). Each mechanism was fixed on 2026-06-26 by 1a8b7ccc8 (D), fcabaaffc (A), 7a7a7b311 (B) and fa1e036ae (C), all ancestors of v1.6.21 and of HEAD, and each was traced to a distinct minimal introducer whose immediate parent lacks the vulnerable behaviour. The four introducer commit objects are named-human commits (Paola Estefania de Campos for 75ee9ea2a/4f5c7c812/95a5a6e1f, Bereket Engida for the a6a66d9c7 squash), and the only AI marker in the cluster, cubic-dev-ai[bot]'s co-author trailer inside the a6a66d9c7 squash message, decomposes to docs-only PR members that are not ancestors of the squash parent, so no AI role is established and the verdict is NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Three residual surfaces, none of which changes the AI attribution. (1) The A fix leaves a TODO(next) in parseProviderDomains: provider.domain stays a serialized string and URL/path-shaped entries are normalized rather than rejected at register/update, so the next minimal question is whether any current consumer still splits provider.domain without normalization (the fix added parseProviderDomains precisely to avoid that). (2) The B fix leaves a TODO(next) about moving SSO account links to an immutable provider instance; account rows stay keyed by the mutable providerId string, and the next minimal question is whether the new collision checks cover a providerId that enters outside provider registration, for example a pre-existing row or a SCIM-created provider. (3) The C fix binds audience, bearer recipient and destination but adds no InResponseTo/request-correlation check; the next minimal question is whether the ACS RelayState/session-key handling already prevents replay of a captured assertion within its validity window. What would flip the verdict: an AI trailer or bot author inside any of the four BIC commit objects, or cubic-dev-ai's credit mapping to the SSO member instead of the docs members.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unbounded per-part MIME header buffering in Rack::Multipart::Parser: the parser reads chunks into a buffer waiting for CRLFCRLF to finish a part header, with no size cap (CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption / memory DoS). An attacker can send a multipart body with an endless header section and exhaust server memory.

causal_research.bug_semantics: fast-uri parse() for HTTP-family URLs (scheme handlers with domainHost:true) runs an IDN conversion when the host matches nonSimpleDomain. After the node:url import was removed, that path called URL.domainToASCII on the global WHATWG URL constructor, where the helper does not exist. The resulting TypeError was swallowed into parsed.error while parsed.host stayed in its original Unicode form, and parse()/normalize()/equal() still returned that object/string. An attacker can therefore present a host such as 127。0。0。1 that fails a fast-uri denylist/loopback/redirect check but is canonicalized to 127.0.0.1 by Node's URL parser and fetch(), producing a policy/use desync (CWE-436 / CWE-551).

That is the first appearance of the CVE's null-userId skip. Squash landing on develop is 69662f46ce841a99d68683d8ee0765765fd12234; the PR member is the atomic first writer.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 93cf43f6a6 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the parent revision did protect message-attached files: there the call was Meteor.callAsync('deleteMessage', msg), and deleteMessage throws error-invalid-user when Meteor.userId() is null, so an unauthenticated caller could not delete a file that had a message before 69662f46ce. Checked that deleteMessageValidatingPermission itself throws on a null userId (apps/meteor/app/lib/server/functions/deleteMessage.ts:16-19 at the fix commit), so the bypass comes from the guard, not from the helper. Checked that all other deleteById callers in the tree are authenticated internal paths (temporary uploads cron, deleteUser, cleanRoomHistory, moderation, avatar change), and that getMessageByFileId queries both message file fields, so the msg branch is not avoidable for attached files.
mechanism.impact: Permanent deletion of arbitrary uploaded files (storage object plus Uploads document) by any unauthenticated network client: availability/integrity loss, CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H. Deletion is not recoverable through application state, and message-attached files are covered because getMessageByFileId matches both file._id and files._id.
mechanism.preconditions: Network reachability of the DDP endpoint; the target file ID known or guessable (IDs leak through public channel payloads and download URLs). No account, token, room membership or session is needed. On the vulnerable revision the msg lookup succeeds for attached files but the short-circuit 'msg && userId' is false for a null userId, so the permission helper is never called.
mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated DDP client calls deleteFileMessage(fileID); Meteor.userId() returns null, the guard 'if (msg && userId)' is false even when the file belongs to a message, and execution falls through to FileUpload.getStore('Uploads').deleteById(fileID), which deletes the stored file and its Uploads record with no permission check. Every upload whose ID the caller knows is deletable, with no login, token or room membership required.
mechanism.trigger: Unauthenticated DDP WebSocket call to the Meteor method deleteFileMessage with a target file ID, e.g. via /websocket; file IDs are exposed in public channel message payloads and in file download URLs.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: apps/meteor/server/methods/deleteFileMessage.ts:21-27 async deleteFileMessage (introducing commit 69662f46ce841a99d68683d8ee0765765fd12234); identical lines at apps/meteor/server/methods/deleteFileMessage.ts:21-27 on the pre-fix release lines, e.g. b3c635d20e^

causal_research.reasoning:
CVE.org publishes a real CWE-287 in deleteFileMessage: null Meteor.userId() skipped the only authorization branch and deleted arbitrary uploads. The smallest first writer of that skip is named-human commit 93cf43f6 (PR #28909 member), whose parent still routed files-with-messages through deleteMessage's invalid-user throw. The 2026 security hotfix 6741cc6e, squash-landed as 1a9ced99 and cherry-picked to the listed patch tags, requires a userId before any delete and restores permission checks for both message-backed and orphan files, closing the unauthenticated path. BIC commit-object AI markers are absent, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class or FALSE_POSITIVE.
The advisory holds at code level: before the fix, the deleteFileMessage DDP method skipped every permission check for an unauthenticated caller and reached FileUpload.getStore('Uploads').deleteById(fileID) unconditionally. causal_research.bug_semantics: Active Storage proxy-mode DoS via Range requests (CWE-789 uncontrolled memory allocation, CVSS 6.6 moderate): ActiveStorage::Blobs::ProxyController#show -> send_blob_byte_range_data parses the client Range header with Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges and, for a single range, loads the ENTIRE requested byte range into memory via blob.download_chunk(range) before send_data. A large or unbounded Range header (e.g. bytes=0-) makes the server allocate memory proportional to file size, allowing remote unauthenticated memory-exhaustion DoS in proxy delivery mode. Fixed by capping total range size to ActiveStorage.streaming_chunk_max_size (default 100MB): ranges whose sum exceeds the cap now get 416 range_not_satisfiable. Affected activestorage <7.2.3.1, >=8.0.0.beta1 <8.0.4.1, >=8.1.0.beta1 <8.1.2.1.
causal_research.evidence: Introducer fcc46228c626b02f7ace689843dbbcf400d118df (2021-08-05, Tom Prats <tprats108@gmail.com>, 'Squashed commit of the following' = PR #42493 'Add Active Storage support for byte ranges'; single parent 7f5ebc4b43030f99dc06cb79fd3b3ad3faa3af6e, verified absent: git grep for send_blob_byte_range_data/get_byte_ranges in parent activestorage tree returns 0) created activestorage/app/controllers/concerns/active_storage/streaming.rb with send_blob_byte_range_data: ranges = Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges(range_header, blob.byte_size); single-range branch does data = blob.download_chunk(range) and send_data(data, ...) - entire requested range materialized in memory with no cap (bytes=0- yields whole-file allocation); multi-range branch concatenates all chunks into one String (data << chunk), unbounded sum. Pre-squash sub-commits (b9553e3698a7af5105171f9d63bd7b89cbb7e2c3 'Added Active Storage support for byte ranges' 2021-06-23 etc.) are not present in any reachable ref (git cat-file: could not get object info), so the squash is the minimum atomic introducer; commit message contains only human Co-authored-by: Rafael França. Fix 2cd933c366b777f873d4d590127da2f4a25e4ba5 (2025-12-02, Gannon McGibbon <gannon.mcgibbon@gmail.com>, 'Configurable maxmimum streaming chunk size', [CVE-2026-33174] [GHSA-r46p-8f7g-vvvg]) is the advisory-referenced patch on 8-0-stable/8-0-sec; identical cherry-picks 42012eaaa88dfc7d0030161b2bc8074a7bbce92a (8-1-sec) and 8159a9c3de3f27a2bcf2866b8bf9ceb9075e229b (7-2-sec). AND ranges.sum { |r| r.end - r.begin } < ActiveStorage.streaming_chunk_max_size (new mattr_accessor default 100.megabytes, configurable via config.active_storage.streaming_chunk_max_size in engine.rb), returning head(:range_not_satisfiable) on overflow; adds 'Byte Range is too big' / 'too big overall' tests (bytes=0- under 1KB cap -> 416) + CHANGELOG + configuring.md entry. causal_research.bug_semantics: A committed .kiota/workspace.json (documented team workflow) is deserialized on kiota client generate / kiota plugin generate. Each consumer's outputPath is copied into GenerationConfiguration.OutputPath with no workspace-root confinement. KiotaBuilder then CreateDirectory/writes the generated client (and can CleanOutput-delete) at that path. An attacker who lands a malicious PR or poisons a repo can set outputPath to an absolute POSIX path, UNC, Windows drive path, or a .. traversal; a teammate or CI running the documented regenerate command writes attacker-chosen files outside the workspace (CWE-22). Vendor states descriptionLocation generation-time fetch is intentional and not this vulnerability; only outputPath is patched.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unsafe pickle deserialization allowing arbitrary (zero-byte) file creation via the logging.FileHandler gadget (CWE-502): picklescan's blocklist in src/picklescan/scanner.py (_unsafe_globals) blocked RCE-focused modules (os, subprocess, builtins, ctypes, functools.partial, _io.FileIO, etc.) but did not cover the Python standard library logging module. An attacker can craft a pickle whose __reduce__ returns (logging.FileHandler, ('evil.log',)); on deserialization the handler opens the file in append mode, creating a zero-byte file at an arbitrary path when it does not exist, with no overwrite of existing content. Since scanning occurs on untrusted pickle input, this yields filesystem pollution / logic disruption (e.g., planting lock files the application checks, DoS), though not direct RCE. Fixed in 1.0.1 by adding logging.FileHandler to _unsafe_globals (plus a regression fixture tests/data2/logging_FileHandler.pkl).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CWE-89 in phpMyFAQ's built-in captcha. BuiltinCaptcha stores the raw User-Agent header and client IP at construction, then interpolates those strings into sprintf-built DELETE (garbageCollector) and INSERT (saveCaptcha) queries against faqcaptcha with no Database::escape() or bound parameters. getCaptchaImage() always runs both methods. GET /api/captcha (api.private.captcha) is an unauthenticated image endpoint that calls getCaptchaImage(), so a crafted User-Agent such as x' OR SLEEP(2) OR 'x executes in both sinks. Quote-breaking payloads can time-based-exfiltrate other tables (faquser hashes, faqconfig secrets) or widen the DELETE WHERE clause. validateCaptchaCode() in the same class already escaped the captcha id, showing the omission on userAgent/ip was not universal. MySQL/MariaDB query() is single-statement, so stacked queries are not the primitive; time-based blind SQLi and WHERE rewrite still work.

causal_research.bug_semantics: NodeVM's builtin allowlist supports '*' wildcard expansion. With config builtin:['*', '-child_process'], BUILTIN_MODULES enumerates Node's builtinModules (which includes 'module'). addDefaultBuiltin() gives 'module' the generic handler vm.readonly(hostRequire('module')) because 'module' is not in SPECIAL_MODULES. ReadOnlyHandler blocks only mutation traps (set/setPrototypeOf/defineProperty/deleteProperty/isExtensible/preventExtensions) and inherits BaseHandler.get/apply, so sandbox code can call Module._load('child_process'), which is forwarded to the host realm and loads child_process bypassing the allowlist, achieving RCE via child_process.execSync.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Cleartext interception (CWE-319, related STARTTLS stripping) in django.core.mail.backends.smtp.EmailBackend: EmailBackend.open() assigns self.connection = connection_class(host, port, ...) and only then calls starttls(context=...) / login(...) inside a try/except OSError that swallows the error when fail_silently=True. candidate_hunks.annotation: The released Claude-assisted hardening imports net so namespace verification can resolve and classify addresses before dialing.
The default HTTP fetcher is routed through safeDialContext, making its address classifier the security boundary for attacker-controlled publisher domains.

safeDialContext blocks the usual private, loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified, and CGNAT ranges, but its list omits 6to4, both NAT64 prefixes, and deprecated site-local IPv6. Routed IPv6 wrappers can therefore carry an internal IPv4 destination through this allow decision.

fix_hunks.annotation: The direct fix adds fail-fast CIDR parsing and explicitly rejects 2002::/16, 64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48, and fec0::/10 before dialing. Iterating those prefixes closes each IPv6 translation or site-local route omitted by the original classifier.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: an HTTP source is configured (baseUrl plus optional headers/query) and an HTTP tool is invoked. User- or LLM-controlled pathParams (from v0.3.0 static path plus later pathParams) are interpolated into the request path. v1.4.0 getURL rejects scheme/host/userinfo overrides and dot-segment traversal, so the first request stays under the configured base host. Sink: Source.Initialize builds a net/http.Client with Timeout (and later Transport) but no CheckRedirect and no IP allow/deny. Source.RunRequest / Tool.Invoke call Client.Do. Go's default redirect policy follows 3xx Location up to 10 hops to any host, including loopback, RFC1918, and link-local/metadata. Impact: CWE-918 SSRF; confidentiality/integrity of internal services if the configured backend (or a still-allowed relative path that the backend redirects) issues an open redirect or destination swap. Preconditions: HTTP source/tool enabled; attacker can cause a redirect off the intended host (malicious/compromised backend, open redirect, or residual path tricks). Counterevidence: path sanitization in v1.4.0 blocks direct host override, but does not close redirect following.

causal_research.flaw_origin: PR #332 first added the HTTP source. Member 1ce486af5925f4c2e262e5ff74587f3a09383ef9 is the smallest first writer of `client := http.Client{ Timeout: 30 * time.Second }` with no CheckRedirect in internal/sources/http/http.go; its parent f6c81df has an empty http.go. 08430cc then stored that client on Source and used it in tools/http. GitHub squash 64da5b4 landed the complete feature on main and shipped in v0.3.0. The missing redirect/IP policy remained through v1.4.0 until 24d7d29.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 1ce486af59 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that v1.4.0's tool already rejects absolute path templates ('path must be relative and cannot override base host', internal/tools/http/http.go:213) and '..' segments, so the advisory's 'direct destination swap' half is mitigated in the later affected versions; checked the tree at the fix parent for any redirect or IP guard on this client (only the auth clients and cloudhealthcare set CheckRedirect) and confirmed this source's client has none, so the redirect half stands. The public PR #332 page was also inspected and discloses no AI use, but PR-level text is not causal evidence and is not relied on.
mechanism.impact: Requests to internal or metadata endpoints (for example 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10) are performed with the toolbox's network position and credentials, and the response body is returned to the caller, exposing internal services and cloud metadata.
mechanism.preconditions: An HTTP source/tool must be configured and callable by an untrusted actor, and the destination must be reachable from the toolbox process. Tool-level host override was blocked from v0.29.0 (3856913e1cf) and dot-segment escape from v1.3.0 (80a66021205), so in the late affected releases (through 1.4.0) the surviving vector is the followed redirect (plus DNS resolution to a blocked IP), not a direct path swap.
mechanism.summary: An attacker-influenced HTTP tool request, or a redirect returned by the configured backend, reaches the toolbox's unguarded HTTP client, which neither inspects the destination IP nor constrains redirects, so the toolbox issues requests to loopback/RFC 1918/link-local/CGNAT services with its own network access (SSRF, CWE-918).
mechanism.trigger: An http-type source/tool is configured; the caller (or a malicious data-driven prompt) supplies path/query parameters, and/or the configured backend responds with a 3xx Location pointing at an internal address, which the client follows.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: internal/sources/http/http.go:89 Initialize() at pre-fix 24d7d29b748^ (`client := http.Client{Timeout: duration, Transport: tr}` with no CheckRedirect and no dial-time IP validation); introduced at 64da5b4efe7:56 as `client := http.Client{Timeout: duration}`.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-918 in the HTTP source client: no CheckRedirect and no IP validation, so Client.Do follows redirects off the sanitized base URL. The first writer of that client is PR 332 member 1ce486a (parent empty file); the GitHub squash 64da5b4 is only the landing carrier. The minimum shipped repair is 24d7d29 in v1.5.0, which adds CheckRedirect plus connect-time IP checks; v1.4.0 still lacks them. The BIC commit object is named-human duwenxin@google.com with no AI markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class or EVIDENCE_GAP. Fix-side Gemini review does not change BIC attribution.
The HTTP source initializes its own http.Client with only a timeout and a transport, so Go's default redirect policy follows up to ten 3xx hops and nothing validates the destination IP before dialing; a request steered by tool arguments, or a redirect returned by the configured backend, is therefore executed against loopback, RFC 1918, link-local (169.254.169.254) or CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) endpoints from the toolbox's own network position (CWE-918). The defect enters the tree with 64da5b4efe7 (first released in v0.3.0), the feature commit that first adds internal/sources/http/http.go, whose parent 559cb66791e does not contain the file; every later change to those lines is a refactor, TLS toggle or config-version migration, not an introduction. The advisory's referenced fix PR #3448 landed as 24d7d29b748 (first released in v1.5.0) and adds SSRFGuard with dial-time Control and CheckRedirect hooks, closing both the direct-dial and redirect paths; the default predicate's CGNAT blind spot was closed later by a0f36f42c33 (#3625, v1.8.0). The BIC commit object carries a named human author (Wenxin Du, GitHub account identity), a GitHub-signed committer, a conventional feature message, no trailers, and a diff of ordinary Go source, config, docs and tests, so no AI marker is present or recoverable at the causal change. With complete lineage and no positive AI evidence on the introducer, the AI-role claim fails and the case is NOT_AI; a disclosed AI-authored change or an AI trailer on 64da5b4efe7 would flip it.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Nothing open on the advisory's internal-reachability mechanism at HEAD. One scoped-out residue of the same default predicate remains: RFC 6890 192.0.0.0/24 (global-unicast, non-private) is still admitted, as the author of a0f36f42c33 documents and deliberately leaves out; it is not a loopback/RFC1918/link-local/CGNAT internal target and has no closing commit at HEAD.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A crafted PSD supplies layer bounding-box integers. Since 10.3.0 those four values are parsed as signed 32-bit (si32be) in PsdImagePlugin._layerinfo and copied into tile extents by _maketile for the C raw/packbits codecs. ImageFile then calls decoder/encoder _setimage with (x0,y0,x1,y1). In C, xoff=x0 and xsize=x1-x0 are 32-bit ints; the safety check was state->xsize + state->xoff > im->xsize (and the y equivalent). If x0 is non-negative but x1 is a large negative (e.g. INT_MIN), x1-x0 wraps to a huge positive xsize, then xsize+xoff wraps again so the comparison against a small image width succeeds. The codec then writes that huge tile into the image buffer (OOB write in src/decode.c / src/encode.c), which can crash or execute code. Pillow 12.1.1 (CVE-2026-25990) added xoff<0/yoff<0 short-circuit checks but left the overflowing sum, so this bypass remained until 12.2.0, which rejects x0<0 or x1<=x0 or x1>im->xsize on the original extents before any addition.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The smallest first-write of the reachable defect is c2907dc04967109391a77eea00f7d583a0a0395f (PR #7706 member, not the merge). Its parent still parses the PSD layer bbox with unsigned i32, so attacker-controlled negative/overflowing extents cannot reach C int setimage (values > INT_MAX raise OverflowError; negatives do not exist). Switching to si32 first creates signed tile extents that overflow the pre-existing C int sum check. The overflow-prone check itself is older (present in 10.2.0 decode.c; originally from the 2010 PIL fork) and is not the 10.3.0 exposure. 12.1.1's #9427 is incomplete remediations of the same OOB, not a new first-write of the overflowing addition.

causal_research.bug_semantics: pretalx mail templates interpolate user-controlled placeholder values (account display name, speaker name, proposal title, question answers, ...) into outgoing emails, and most outgoing mails carry both a plain-text and an HTML part. Before 2026.1.0 the HTML body was produced by running the already-substituted template text through a permissive markdown->HTML pipeline (markdown.markdown -> bleach.clean with extra allowed tags -> bleach.linkify) with no escaping of the user-controlled substitution values, so malformed raw HTML or markdown link syntax embedded in e.g. the attacker-chosen account display name survived into the rendered HTML body. The most direct vector is the password-reset flow: an unauthenticated attacker registers an account with a malicious name, enters any victim's email address, and triggers a password reset; the resulting email carries attacker-controlled markup from the instance's legitimate configured sender address and passes SPF/DKIM/DMARC, making arbitrary-HTML-content phishing email injection possible. Fixed in 2026.1.0 by a trust-aware two-pass formatter that escapes user content and fences it off from the autolinker.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DoS (CWE-400, disk-space exhaustion) in the AutoGPT platform block executor: StepThroughItemsBlock iterates an unbounded input list (no loop-count limit) and can feed every item to FileStoreBlock, whose store_media_file() downloads remote URLs into the execution working directory with only per-file access-time timeouts and no disk-space cap; a malicious user can slowly download many ~100MB files and exhaust disk. Secondary vector: CountdownTimerBlock accepts unbounded seconds/minutes/hours/days/repeat, so an agent can sleep e.g. ~1 year, pinning the execution (and its temp directory) alive for a persistent DoS.
causal_research.evidence: Advisory CVE-2025-32422 = GHSA-9fr4-9jj9-mhh6 (published 2026-06-11/18, Critical, CWE-400, 'AutoGPT has a DoS vulnerability in FileStoreBlock with StepThroughItemsBlock', affected <= autogpt-platform-beta-v0.6.62, patched v0.6.63). Vulnerable snapshot cited by advisory: 62361ccc48327b3124549543b45d933d16f622d2 (2025-04-09) shows FileStoreBlock.run calling store_media_file(graph_exec_id=..., file=input_data.file_in) (backend/blocks/basic.py:33-45) and StepThroughItemsBlock.run looping unboundedly over items/items_object/items_str (backend/blocks/iteration.py:56-73) with no MAX_ITEMS. Fixes: (1) 57a06f70883ce6be18738c6ae8bb41085c71e266 (#10798, 2025-10-02, Zamil Majdy) added MAX_ITEMS=10000 + MAX_ITEM_SIZE=1MB to StepThroughItemsBlock and MAX_FILE_SIZE=100MB + MAX_TOTAL_DISK_USAGE=1GB-per-exec-dir checks to store_media_file (later moved to Config().max_file_size_mb); present in all tags >= v0.6.32 yet the advisory still lists <= v0.6.62 as affected. (2) d00d4f0a973b84b258710fd349df30e4a85effb1 (#13237, 2026-06-04, Krzysztof Czerwinski/kcze - the advisory reporter) bounds CountdownTimerBlock: repeat ge=1 le=1000, cumulative per-iteration x repeat capped at MAX_TOTAL_SECONDS=7 days, negatives rejected, execution_timeout_seconds=MAX_TOTAL_SECONDS+60; tests include run(block, days=365, repeat=1) (time_blocks_test.py) mirroring the advisory's 'delay for 1 year' PoC; lands in the 0.6.62..0.6.63 window. OSV GIT fixed anchor = 5b603c0bd04c8db2afc12098d5af2d391b7816e7 (2026-06-09 'Merge branch master into dev' = v0.6.63 tag). Introducers: bb3be444de072ca87c01047f5c041bd46598b46c (2025-01-26, PR #9320, single parent 996efaf4fcba010f6cc0edb7bee5e54cdfaa177f, squash-merge landing) added FileStoreBlock + store_media_file; parent verified absent of both 'class FileStoreBlock' and 'def store_media_file' (git grep exit 1 on 996efaf4). causal_research.bug_semantics: Python stdlib re on several vLLM parsers can catastrophically backtrack (CWE-1333). The earliest production sink is is_regex_target_modules() in vllm/lora/utils.py: when a LoRA adapter_config.json supplies target_modules as a string, vllm/lora/models.py calls that helper, which compiles the string then re.search(r"\((.*?)\)\$?$", load_modules). Later independent sinks parse model/tool-call text: phi4mini_tool_parser.py runs re.search(r'functools\[(.*?)\]', model_output, re.DOTALL) on complete model output, and serving_chat.py runs re.search(r'.*"parameters":\s*(.*)', current_text) while streaming tool_choice='required' deltas. Crafted nested/repeated input can pin a worker CPU. The May 2025 fix does not change the patterns; it swaps the engine to the third-party regex module.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In OpenID multi-user mode, sync-server authenticates the caller (validateSessionMiddleware / session user_id) but most /sync file endpoints authorize only that the target fileId exists (verifyFileExists / filesService.get). A second authenticated user who knows or is given a fileId can download the budget blob, read or rotate encryption-key metadata, overwrite the file, reset sync state, rename it, or read file info. list-user-files is scoped, so discovery is via admin listing, sharing, or guessing. delete-user-file already denied non-owner/non-admin after #6338; the other endpoints did not. CWE-862 IDOR on hosted budget files.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In ironic/common/molds.py, save_configuration() and get_configuration() attach an authorization header built by _get_auth_header(task) to outbound requests.put()/requests.get() calls whose URL is taken verbatim from the user-supplied import/export configuration-mold request for the idrac driver, with no endpoint validation. With molds storage='swift' the header carries Ironic's own time-limited Keystone X-Auth-Token (valid across every OpenStack service Ironic is authorized for); with storage='http' it carries HTTP Basic credentials configured for molds storage. Any authenticated user permitted to invoke the molds import/clean step can therefore aim the flow at an attacker-chosen remote endpoint and capture those credentials server-side (OSSA-2026-010 / CVE-2026-42997, CVSS 3.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N per the GHSA/PYSEC record).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Incomplete local-only gate for spawn-capable MCP/tunnel/CLI routes. After CVE-2026-46339, proxy() in src/dashboardGuard.js began rejecting /api/mcp/* (and later /api/tunnel/*, /api/cli-tools/*) unless isLocalRequest() returned true. isLocalRequest() treated the client-controlled Host header (and Origin, if present) as proof the caller was on loopback (localhost/127.0.0.1/::1), not the TCP source address. Behind a reverse proxy, Cloudflare Tunnel, or Tailscale — all first-party deployment modes — an attacker sets Host: localhost and Origin: http://localhost, the gate opens, and with a second factor (JWT cookie, or the deterministic machine-id CLI token x-9r-cli-token = getConsistentMachineId("9r-cli-auth")) the client can GET /api/mcp/<plugin>/sse and POST JSON-RPC onto the child process stdin (npx/node/python/uvx/bun), recovering remote code execution. From v0.4.55, canAccessLocalOnlyRoute() made CLI token sufficient even without a loopback Host, and restored Host+JWT as an alternate path, so Host spoofing remained a locality bypass for authenticated browser sessions.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service (engine crash) via invalid regex in structured output (guided decoding) in vllm-project/vllm (case repo pypa/advisory-database; actual vulnerable repo vllm-project/vllm). With the default v1 guided-decoding backend 'auto' (DecodingConfig.backend = 'auto' if VLLM_USE_V1 else 'xgrammar'), a request with guided_regex (e.g. '[.*') goes through validate_xgrammar_grammar, whose xgr.Grammar.from_regex raises ValueError -> auto fallback switches backend to 'guidance' WITHOUT validating the grammar; the invalid regex then reaches llguidance compilation inside the engine worker and raises an uncaught exception, crashing the vLLM server (ReDoS-style DoS, PYSEC-2025-55: 'Version 0.8.0 up to but excluding 0.9.0 have a Denial of Service (ReDoS) that causes the vLLM server to crash if an invalid regex was provided while using structured output'). Fix restores validation on the fallback path so the request is rejected with HTTP 400 (test test_invalid_regex in the fix commit uses guided_regex=r'[.*').

causal_research.bug_semantics: apko key discovery treats a repository JWKS document as a list of RSA public keys. InitDB walks configured repositories, fetchChainguardKeys calls DiscoverKeys, which GETs `{repository}/apk-configuration`, reads `jwks_uri`, decodes the JWKS, and for each key does an unchecked `key.Key.(*rsa.PublicKey)` before PKIX/PEM-encoding it as `{kid}.rsa.pub`. If that endpoint (attacker-influenced or simply EC/Ed25519) returns a non-RSA key, Go's type assertion panics and the process exits. Impact is availability only (CVSS 6.5, UI:R). The 1.2.7 fix keeps RSA-only behavior but returns a typed error instead of panicking.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stack-based buffer overflow in the GDAL netCDF driver (frmts/netcdf/netcdfsg.cpp): scanForGeometryContainers() and SGeometry_PropertyScanner::open() read the CF_SG_GEOMETRY attribute into fixed-size stack buffers (char c[NC_MAX_CHAR] / char buf[NC_MAX_CHAR+1]) via nc_get_att_text() without checking the attribute length first, so an oversized geometry attribute in a crafted NetCDF file overflows the stack and can achieve code execution on the server (also the attrf() helper reads into a fixed 257-byte stack buffer without length validation). Affects GDAL 3.1.0 through 3.13.0; fixed in 3.13.1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GitPython's GitConfigParser._write.write_section interpolates the in-memory section name as a raw git-config header via fp.write(("[%s]\n" % name).encode(...)). Repo.config_writer().set_value(section, option, value) (and add_section/set/add_value/rename_section) stored that name without rejecting CR, LF, or NUL. An attacker-controlled section such as "user]\n[core" is therefore serialized as two valid headers, [user] then [core], so a following option like hooksPath=/tmp/evil_hooks becomes core.hooksPath in .git/config. Git honors that path; a later commit/merge/checkout runs hooks from the attacker directory (RCE). This is a residual bypass of the 3.1.49 value-only guard, which blocked the same outcome when newlines were smuggled in the value argument (indented [core] continuation) but left the section/option names unsanitized.

causal_research.bug_semantics: mruby's compiler scope_new zero-initializes codegen_scope (nregs=0), then sets the stack pointer and nlocals to the local-variable count plus self without assigning nregs. nregs is only raised later if push() runs nregs_update (if sp > nregs). scope_finish copies the possibly-zero nregs into the irep (uint16_t). A nested class/module body executed via OP_EXEC does stack_extend(irep->nregs) then stack_clear(regs+1, irep->nregs-1). When nregs is 0, the uint16_t subtraction wraps to 65535, so stack_clear writes past the 128-slot (1024-byte) VM stack allocated by stack_init, which is the ASan heap-buffer-overflow in #6509.

mruby/mruby#6509 (closed completed 2025-04-07 by matz) reports ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8 in stack_clear at src/vm.c:101 called from mrb_vm_exec:2957 on commit dd68681002f570233e6603360e70c32b2414eeba, 1024-byte region from stack_init.

At fix parent 8c2ea232ea873ac400b2b5489486e5424e719bb7, scope_new zero-inits the scope, does s->sp += node_len(nlv)+1 and s->nlocals = s->sp, and never assigns s->nregs; nregs starts at 0 and is raised only by nregs_update in push_n_.
scope_finish copies irep->nregs = s->nregs and irep->nlocals = s->nlocals (include/mruby/irep.h: both uint16_t). If codegen never push()es, irep->nregs stays 0 while nlocals > 0.

OP_EXEC at src/vm.c:2939 does stack_extend(mrb, irep->nregs) then stack_clear(regs+1, irep->nregs-1). With nregs==0, uint16_t underflow makes count 65535; STACK_INIT_SIZE 128 * sizeof(mrb_value) is 1024 bytes, matching the ASan first OOB write. Fix message: nregs should not be smaller than nlocals.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Portainer CE shipped Docker environment security flags that defaulted to allowing non-admin users bind mounts, privileged mode, host PID/IPC namespace, device mapping, extra capabilities, and sysctls. An authenticated regular user with access to an endpoint could create a container or stack that bind-mounts host paths (researcher PoC read /etc/shadow) or otherwise obtain root-equivalent host execution. The flags existed as opt-out restrictions (UI: 'Disable bind mounts for non-administrators') rather than secure-by-default denials. After 2021 they lived on per-endpoint EndpointSecuritySettings and were copied as true onto every newly created environment; 2.33.2 still initialized them true. The 2.38.0/2.39.0 fix flips those defaults to false via DefaultEndpointSecuritySettings() (stack management remains allowed) and always validates non-admin stack files.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mattermost interactive button callbacks could run action handlers (button-click dispatch to the agent) before normal sender authorization/allowlist checks completed. The interaction handler verified only an HMAC context token (_token) and then dispatched as a system event + synthetic inbound message, so a crafted callback could invoke an action without going through the channel's sender/allowlist authorization path (unauthorized action execution). Fixed by adding an optional authorizeButtonClick callback in createMattermostInteractionHandler and wiring monitorMattermostProvider to route callback authorization through authorizeMattermostCommandInvocation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Webhook routes authenticate inbound POSTs with HMAC. The adapter also honors a magic secret string INSECURE_NO_AUTH that skips signature validation entirely, then treats the body as an agent prompt (tools/terminal). At introduction the default bind was 0.0.0.0 and connect() did not refuse INSECURE_NO_AUTH on a public host, so a config that followed the documented 'testing only' secret published unauthenticated remote agent dispatch. causal_research.bug_semantics: Integer overflow (CWE-190 -> CWE-125) in the encode-path buffer validation of pillow_heif/_pillow_heif.c. _CtxWriteImage_add_plane() (~line 158), _CtxWriteImage_add_plane_la() (~line 344), and _CtxWriteImage_add_plane_l() (~line 449) validate the caller's input buffer with `if (stride_in * height > buffer.len)` where stride_in and height are 32-bit int while buffer.len is Py_ssize_t (64-bit). For large image dimensions (e.g. stride_in=98304, height=32768 -> true product 3,221,225,472 > INT_MAX) the int32 multiplication wraps negative, the check evaluates false, and the copy loops `memcpy(out + stride_out*i, in + stride_in*i, real_stride)` read far beyond the input Py_buffer: heap out-of-bounds read under default settings, giving information disclosure (heap bytes copied into the encoded HEIF/AVIF, Heartbleed-like) or SIGSEGV/SIGBUS denial of service. real_stride = width*n_channels (int*int) overflows independently for huge widths. Unlike the decode path, the encode path has no libheif security limits; reachable whenever an app calls pillow_heif.encode()/from_bytes() or saves via Pillow with format=HEIF/AVIF.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-178: Windows-compatible env override keys (e.g. `ProgramFiles(x86)`) could bypass the system.run approval binding. causal_research.bug_semantics: mlflow.pyfunc.spark_udf accepts prebuilt_env_path, a tar.gz of a prebuilt Python env. On the NFS/shared-cluster path it calls extract_archive_to_dir(prebuilt_env_path, dest_dir). That helper opens the archive and extracts members into dest_dir without checking that member.name stays under dest_dir. A crafted archive with ../ or absolute member names (classic tar slip / CWE-29) writes files outside the intended directory. Preconditions: the operator supplies or is induced to use that archive (CVSS UI:R) in Databricks Connect / shared-cluster spark_udf extraction. Impact: arbitrary file overwrite and possible sandbox escape in multi-tenant clusters.

mechanism.impact: Arbitrary file overwrite or creation outside the extraction directory with the driver user's filesystem rights - overwriting shell startup files, other tenants' staged files under a shared NFS/local_disk0 tree, or interpreter paths - which gives code execution or privilege escalation in the multi-tenant and shared-cluster settings the advisory names. The GHSA rates it CRITICAL (CVSS:3.0 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H, CWE-29) and states the attacker-controlled tar can overwrite arbitrary files and escape the sandbox directory.
mechanism.preconditions: (1) Attacker influence over the archive bytes at the path the victim passes (shared or multi-tenant cluster, an exchanged environment bundle, or an attacker-writable staging path); (2) the victim runs the extraction (UI:R - user interaction: calling spark_udf with that archive path); (3) the runtime's tarfile honors the archive: Python up to 3.13 defaults extractall to filter='fully_trusted' (3.12 only warns), PEP 706's 'data' default arrives in 3.14, so on the interpreters MLflow supported at the time the call is exploitable; (4) in DBConnect mode the archive basename must still split into <env_sha>-<runtime_version>-<platform_machine> because _verify_prebuilt_env compares those three filename fields with the model environment - that constrains naming, never content.
mechanism.summary: A tar.gz whose member names or link structure are attacker-chosen is unpacked with a bare tarfile.extractall() inside extract_archive_to_dir, with no validation of member paths, so names such as ../x or /x, or a regular file written through an in-archive symlink, land outside dest_dir with the rights of the driver process that runs the prebuilt-env extraction; that is arbitrary file overwrite/creation, i.e. sandbox escape in shared or multi-tenant clusters.
mechanism.trigger: Victim calls mlflow.pyfunc.spark_udf(..., prebuilt_env_path=<archive>) - or any caller that hands an archive to mlflow.pyfunc.dbconnect_artifact_cache.extract_archive_to_dir - with an archive whose bytes the attacker influences. The vulnerable call site at the introducer is mlflow/pyfunc/__init__.py:2154, inside the 'if prebuilt_env_path:' branch that extracts the archive into the NFS tmp dir whenever the dbconnect-artifact mode is off; the parameter is a public spark_udf argument documented as the path of the prebuilt env archive file created by build_model_env.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In django.http.response.HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__ (base of HttpResponseRedirect, HttpResponsePermanentRedirect, and django.shortcuts.redirect), every redirect target was passed whole to urllib urlsplit/urlparse without any length limit. On Windows, Python's NFKC normalization (applied to large Unicode inputs inside the parsing/IRI path) is extremely slow, so an attacker-supplied redirect URL containing a very large number of Unicode characters causes disproportionate CPU consumption in the request thread -- a denial of service. The 2025 fix (CVE-2025-64458) bounds the input by raising DisallowedRedirect when str(redirect_to) exceeds MAX_URL_LENGTH (1024) before parsing.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CTI-Transmute's website mounts Vue 3's runtime compiler over server-rendered page HTML with custom delimiters ['[[',']]'] so the compiler does not collide with Jinja {{ }}. Stored conversion names are attacker-controlled (anonymous users may create public conversions). When the detail template interpolates that name with Jinja (Share {{ convert.name }}), the browser receives literal [[ ... ]] text inside the mounted region. Vue compiles container.innerHTML as a template, so a name such as [[[].constructor.constructor('alert(document.domain)')()]] becomes a JavaScript expression executed in the CTI-Transmute origin. Jinja HTML escaping does not neutralize '['/']'. A short first-stage payload can fetch the uncapped conversion description and eval a second stage. causal_research.bug_semantics: Portainer's shared JWT authentication path accepted a bearer token from the URL query parameter token in addition to the Authorization header. Because that lookup ran inside AuthenticatedAccess (later JWTAuthLookup -> extractBearerToken in api/http/security/bouncer.go), any authenticated HTTP API could be authorized with ?token=<JWT>, not only WebSocket exec/attach/pod shell. Browsers and the UI put the session JWT into those WebSocket URLs; reverse proxies, access logs, browser history, and Referer headers then recorded the full JWT. Anyone who obtained the leaked token inherited the victim's Portainer privileges until expiry (default 8 hours). The 2023 cookie-auth rewrite still accepted and then deleted the query parameter from r.URL.RawQuery, which does not stop upstream log/referer leakage. The 2026 fix removes query-token acceptance entirely and relies on the Authorization header and the HttpOnly portainer_api_key cookie (sent automatically on same-origin WebSocket upgrades).

causal_research.bug_semantics: OS command injection (CWE-78) via the jarFilePath argument of the decompile-from-jar tool: DecompilerService.decompileFromJar() in index.js shells out with template-interpolated user input - execPromise with template `jar tf "${jarFilePath}" | grep ".class$"` and `cd "${tempDir}" && jar xf "${jarFilePath}"` - jarFilePath is only wrapped in double quotes, so an attacker-supplied value containing a double-quote character (e.g. "; <command>; ") breaks out and executes arbitrary OS commands on the server. potential_fix.approach: Remove the shell from the jar invocations in DecompilerService.decompileFromJar: call execFile/spawn with argv lists (e.g. execFile('jar', ['tf', jarFilePath]) and, for extraction, spawn 'jar' with ['xf', jarFilePath] in tempDir) so jarFilePath is a distinct argument, and validate it first (must exist, isFile, and stay within an allowlisted directory and/or match a .jar/.zip extension).
potential_fix.rationale: The injection arises because jarFilePath is interpolated into a shell string and only wrapped in double quotes, so a value like '"; <command>; "' breaks out. Passing jarFilePath as a shell-less argv element (plus path/extension validation) prevents the shell from interpreting the injected quote/metacharacters, closing the CWE-78 sink in both the `jar tf` and `jar xf` commands.

An attacker holding a member role can create an application credential with unrestricted=True and then create/use a trust that delegates victim roles: keystone/trust/controllers.py (_check_unrestricted) only blocked trust create/delete when the token's auth methods contained 'application_credential' AND application_credential['unrestricted'] was False (or when the context was admin it returned early), so an UNRESTRICTED application credential could manage trusts, including delegating the victim's admin role to the attacker's identity (trustor validation passes because the impersonated token carries the victim identity). Fix (14a1447) replaces the restricted-only check with _check_application_credential() which blocks ALL application credentials (restricted and unrestricted) on ALL trust operations (create/delete/list/get/list-roles/get-role) unless the new opt CONF.security_compliance.allow_insecure_application_credential_trust_escalation is set. Affected: >=14.0.0 <27.0.2, >=28.0.0 <28.0.2, >=29.0.0 <29.0.2.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (CWE-79) escalating to Remote Code Execution (CWE-94) in the Dive MCP-host desktop app: the Mermaid diagram renderer src/views/Chat/preview/mermaid.tsx calls mermaid.initialize({ securityLevel: 'loose', ... }), overriding the library's safe default. With securityLevel loose, Mermaid renders HTML labels and javascript: URLs in diagram nodes, so a diagram originating from an untrusted source (a malicious MCP server configuration injected through the LLM/MCP tool pipeline) can execute arbitrary JavaScript when the node is rendered or clicked. In the desktop renderer that JS reaches privileged IPC, enabling full RCE on the victim machine. Fixed by switching securityLevel to 'strict'.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-94 code injection through an insecure-by-default endpoint. POST /execute_js accepts {url, scripts:[...]} and runs the caller's JavaScript in the server's own Chromium context, whose default launch args in the same deployment include --disable-web-security; the route's only guard was Depends(token_dep), and at v0.8.6 token_dep resolves to an always-None dependency because the shipped config has security.enabled false, jwt_enabled false and api_token empty, so a default Docker deployment exposes arbitrary in-browser JavaScript execution and, through the browser's network stack with origin checks disabled, SSRF into internal services. The defect is the enabled-by-default exposure of an inherently powerful primitive, not a memory-safety or injection-into-safe-code bug.

causal_research.flaw_origin: Human (non-AI) origin: the maintainer's own feature commit 5297e362f34b27f8d63b830f2a69bb6858a5009d (author and committer UncleCode <unclecode@kidocode.com>, 2025-04-21) added the POST /execute_js route to the Docker API server as an endpoint that forwards caller-supplied JavaScript fragments into CrawlerRunConfig(js_code=...) with no capability limit, and the same-named ambient browser flag the advisory names (--disable-web-security) had been set one commit earlier by the same human author (a58c8000aab067d51db15a871a0c3fe377e73788, 2025-04-20, deploy/docker/config.yml), so both halves of the exposure are human-authored.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party disclosure bound to 5297e362f (a pull-request body, release note or trailer naming an AI tool for that change) or a commit-object marker on it would flip the verdict to AI_ROOT_CAUSE; a reachable earlier object that already contains @app.post("/execute_js") would move the BIC off 5297e362f; a v0.8.7-or-later build in which execute_js is reachable without CRAWL4AI_EXECUTE_JS_ENABLED=true, or that still ships --disable-web-security in the default browser args, would reopen the fix side.
causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: an unauthenticated POST /execute_js with a caller-supplied url and a list of JavaScript snippets against a default Docker API deployment. Vulnerable code at the introducing commit 5297e362f, deploy/docker/server.py: @app.post("/execute_js") / @limiter.limit(config["rate_limiting"]["default_limit"]) / @mcp_tool("execute_js") / async def execute_js(request, body: JSEndpointRequest, _td: Dict = Depends(token_dep)), whose body builds CrawlerRunConfig(js_code=body.scripts), opens AsyncWebCrawler(config=BrowserConfig()) and returns results[0].model_dump(); the request model added by the same commit is class JSEndpointRequest(BaseModel) with url: str and scripts: List[str]. Impact: attacker-controlled JavaScript executes inside the server's browser profile; with --disable-web-security the same-origin policy is off, so the script can read cross-origin responses and drive requests to internal addresses and cloud metadata (the advisory scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1 / CVSS 4.0 9.2 and pairs it with SSRF). Preconditions: network reachability to the API port; shipped defaults security.enabled=false, jwt_enabled=false, api_token="" make the token dependency a no-op, so no credentials are needed out of the box. Counterevidence: running the caller's scripts is the documented purpose of the route, so the flaw is the default posture (no auth, web security disabled, enabled by default), not an injection into an otherwise safe path; a deployment that sets CRAWL4AI_API_TOKEN or enables JWT, or that removes the browser flag, does not present the same exposure - the vendor's own workaround says exactly that.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory is live and its item 5 describes a real exposure, so this is not a false positive, and the smallest introducing change is unambiguous: the POST /execute_js route, its JSEndpointRequest model and its js_code forwarding body appear only in 5297e362f, verified against the parent tree (zero occurrences of execute_js in the parent's server.py, three in the commit's). The commit is a direct push on the release line with a single child, no pull-request association and no merge on its ancestry path, so bic_granularity is ATOMIC and no squash members exist; landing_commit is left null rather than copying the introducer, because no merge/squash object carried it. The ambient --disable-web-security flag that amplifies the impact came one commit earlier from the same human author, so the exposure is human in both parts. On AI: the introducing object carries a named human author and committer with no trailer or disclosure, the repository demonstrably uses distinct AI identities for AI work in the same history (Devin, Claude, copilot-swe-agent, coderabbitai) while this object has none, and no AI-identity commit exists at all before the BIC date; the assistant-style phrasing of the commit body is a stylistic observation, not admissible attribution, so the marker state is ABSENT and the verdict is NOT_AI rather than EVIDENCE_GAP, since the decisive fact (no attribution on the object that carries the defect) is established rather than missing. The fix is minimal and shipped: an env-var gate answering 403 by default, an SSRF blocklist call on the destination URL, and removal of the web-security flag, with the validator coming from the sibling commit 7976b458 of the same release; ancestry confirms the affected boundary '<= 0.8.6' / '0.8.7' the advisory states.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal in Active Storage DiskService (CWE-22, CVSS 8.0): ActiveStorage::Service::DiskService#path_for (activestorage/lib/active_storage/service/disk_service.rb) joins the blob key directly onto the storage root ('File.join root, folder_for(key), key') with no validation that the resolved path stays inside root; a blob key containing '../' segments (used by apps passing user input as keys) lets an attacker read, write, or delete arbitrary files on the server via the disk service (upload/download/delete and the DiskController HTTP endpoints). Fixed in 7.2.3.1 / 8.0.4.1 / 8.1.2.1.
causal_research.evidence: ruby-advisory-db gems/activestorage/CVE-2026-33195.yml (published 2026-03-23) lists three fix commits: 4933c1e3b8c1bb04925d60347be9f69270392f2c / 9b06fbc0f504b8afe333f33d19548f3b85fbe655 / a290c8a1ec189d793aa6d7f2570b6a763f675348, all 'Prevent path traversal in ActiveStorage DiskService' (2026-03-13) by Mike Dalessio (main + 7.2/8.0 backports; no trailers). Fix rewrites path_for: raises ActiveStorage::InvalidKeyError on blank keys, on dot segments ('.','..'), on Encoding errors, on null bytes (ArgumentError), and enforces 'path.start_with?(File.expand_path(root) + "/")'; DiskController rescues InvalidKeyError as not_found/422. Introducer metadata: author AND committer David Heinemeier Hansson (direct commit, not squash), 2017-07-01 pre-LLM era, no AI markers, commit message 'No need to normalize since we generate our own keys'. History chain verified via -S 'normalize(key)' and -S 'File.join root, folder_for(key), key' (only the 2026 fix touches the final string). Advisory patched ranges match 4933c1e3 origin (main) with branch backports.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The unvalidated key join 'File.join(root, folder_for(key), key)' in path_for was first written by ce44746ea3a98fab1af65c75ec32eeadd67b1b5f 'No need to normalize since we generate our own keys' (2017-07-01, David Heinemeier Hansson) as an immediate follow-up to the Active Storage (then 'Active File') initial implementation: the file-creation commit d30231e983c019fbe3fcd6a2a06a461fefa58dab (2017-07-01 00:04) created lib/active_file/sites/disk_site.rb with path_for calling 'normalize(key)' (a helper that did not exist at that commit — only normalize_key existed), and ce44746e (00:13, same day) removed the normalize call, leaving the raw key joined into the filesystem path with no containment check. Parent 3959d32aa09206518f4c1ea2cd96fa62be383dcd still has 'File.join(root, folder_for(key), normalize(key))' (verified). The 'folder_for' key prefixing ('[key[0..1], key[2..3]].join("/")') never limited traversal since '../<segment>' keys still escape. File renamed over time: lib/active_file/sites/disk_site.rb → activestorage/lib/active_storage/service/disk_service.rb (2017-08 renames), same code.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerable raw-key path join was written on 2017-07-01 by Rails creator David Heinemeier Hansson while bootstrapping Active Storage — nine years before AI coding assistants existed; the only key-filtering helper (normalize_key) was added and dropped within the same hour by the same human author. The 2026 fix is by human Rails security maintainer Mike Dalessio with no AI markers. No AI involvement possible on either side; verdict NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: None material. Note the advisory's framing ('blob keys are expected to be trusted strings... defense-in-depth, not a trust boundary') — the vulnerable code is unambiguous and the introducer is the commit that removed the normalize call, verified against its parent.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Permission bypass (contradictory global flags): 'deno run --allow-read --deny-read main.ts' results in read allowed even though deny should be stronger; same for all global --allow-* / --deny-* pairs. Cause: the fast-exit permission check skip_check_if_is_permission_fully_granted! macro calls UnaryPermission::is_allow_all(), which returned true whenever granted_global is set and the flag/prompt denied LISTS are empty, but ignored the deny-GLOBAL fields (flag_denied_global / prompt_denied_global). With --allow-read --deny-read both set at global scope, granted_global=true and flag_denied_global=true but the lists stayed empty, so is_allow_all() short-circuited the check to Ok(()) and never consulted the deny state. 'Nonsensical combination of flags' per advisory, likely low real-world impact.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In anchor-lang's Program<'info, T> account-constraint, the generic TryFrom<&'a AccountInfo<'a>> implementation computed `let is_unit_type = T::id() == Pubkey::default()` and skipped the program-ID equality check whenever that held. The default type parameter is T = (), whose Id::id() returns Pubkey::default() (all-zeros) purely as a sentinel so Program<'info> without a type parameter means 'any executable account'. But the real System type also has Pubkey::default() as its id (system program address is all zeros), so declaring Program<'info, System> hit the same is_unit_type shortcut and accepted ANY executable account instead of requiring the system program id; programs that then CPI into 'System' with attacker-chosen accounts could be driven into arbitrary CPI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Pillow ImageCmsTransform.apply(im, imOut) is a public API that, before 12.3.0, forwarded a caller-supplied output image into native pyCMSdoTransform() without checking that im.mode equals the transform input mode or that imOut.mode equals the transform output mode. The C wrapper only requires imOut to be at least as large in x/y. LittleCMS then writes according to the transform's LCMS type: findLCMStype maps RGB/RGBA/RGBX to TYPE_RGBA_8 (4 bytes/pixel). An RGBA->RGBA transform applied to an L output image therefore writes 4*width bytes into a 1*width-byte row, a controlled heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The higher-level applyTransform() wrapper did not pass a caller imOut, but the class method did, which is the path in GHSA-9hw9-ch79-4vh6 / CVE-2026-59205.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Path traversal / arbitrary file write in the @mobilenext/mobile-mcp MCP server (< 0.0.49, patched 0.0.49). Two tools pass user-controlled paths directly to filesystem operations without validation: (1) mobile_save_screenshot 'saveTo' param -> fs.writeFileSync(saveTo, screenshot) in src/server.ts (pre-fix line 591); (2) mobile_start_screen_recording 'output' param -> passed as adb screenrecord --output <outputPath> via mobilecli.spawnCommand. causal_research.bug_semantics: On 9router 0.4.59 a remote attacker reaches OS command execution with no operator interaction. POST /api/auth/login with password 123456 succeeds on a fresh install (no passwordHash) and sets a JWT cookie. dashboardGuard LOCAL_ONLY_PATHS (/api/cli-tools/cowork-settings, /api/mcp/, and related host-secret routes) call isLocalRequest(), which treats the client Host header as the loopback proof and only consults Origin if present; Host: localhost:20128 with no Origin bypasses the gate regardless of source IP. POST /api/cli-tools/cowork-settings then registers customPlugins whose command basename is in ALLOWED_MCP_COMMANDS (npx, node, uvx, python, python3, bunx, bun) while args are String-mapped with no flag denylist. GET /api/mcp/<name>/sse calls stdioSseBridge getOrSpawn, which does spawn(command, args). node plus args ["-e", "<javascript>"] is CWE-78 on the host. causal_research.bug_semantics: Header-injection / parsing ambiguity (CWE-20): the HTTP header parser accepted null bytes and control characters (0x00-0x08, 0x0B-0x1F, 0x7F) in header values instead of rejecting them per RFC 9110 s5.5-5. Both parser backends were permissive: the pure-Python HeadersParser performed NO value-side character validation (only header-NAME charset via HDRRE and length limits), and the C parser (llhttp in lenient mode, default since aiohttp 2.0) accumulated values verbatim via on_header_value callbacks with no CTL check. Consequences: a server can send response header values that aiohttp's client interprets differently from what a reverse proxy / other parser understood (e.g. request.url.origin() disagreeing with the raw Host header), enabling header/request smuggling-style security bypasses. All versions since 0.x affected; fixed in 3.13.4.
causal_research.evidence: Identity: hash reversal over plan pool -> {CVE-2026-34520, GHSA-63hf-3vf5-4wqf} (aliases PYSEC-2026-2102; PyPI aiohttp introduced 0, fixed 3.13.4; GHSA patch reference 9370b971). Introducer forensics: aiohttp/http_parser.py (pure-Python parser) created 2017-02-18 (5ace287d refactor) from aiohttp/protocol.py, which itself was moved in b26262e0 (2013-10-25 'rename package') from the original package 'asynchttp/protocol.py', CREATED in the repo's root commit f382b5ff (2013-10-01, 'initial import', no parent) - parse_headers in that root tree validates only names/sizes, never values (verified by reading f382b5ff:asynchttp/protocol.py). The C parser (_parser.pyx, adf00e73 2017-02-14) also collects values without CTL checks; C path made default in aiohttp 2.0 (2017). Partial-mitigation history (not origins): 85713a48 (2023-10-06, Sam Bull #7661, GHSA-gfw2-4jvh-wgfg era) wrote the incomplete '\n/\r/\x00' check - pickaxe -S '"\n" in value or "\r" in value' finds exactly that commit (+ merge 454092d1 and 3.8 backport d5c12ba8), proving values had ZERO CTL validation before 2023; 2026-03-07 bad4131d (#12210, Sam Bull, human Co-authored-by vmfunc) added the \x00-only check to the pyx; the 2026 advisory fix 7043bc56 (#12231, Rodrigo Nogueira, 2026-03-11, no AI trailers) replaces the partial check with full _FIELD_VALUE_FORBIDDEN_CTL_RE rejection in HeadersParser (lax mode keeps the old check); 3.13.4 backport = 9370b971 (#12235). No AI markers anywhere in the introducer or fix chain (all human trailers).
causal_research.flaw_origin: The permissive header-value handling was first written in the repository ROOT COMMIT f382b5ff (2013-10-01, 'initial import', Nikolay Kim, asynchttp/protocol.py parse_headers at lines 47-115: 'name, value = line.split(":", 1)' with validation only of the header name and field sizes, values passed through unvalidated; no parent commit exists). The C-parser path inherited the same lack of value CTL validation when introduced (adf00e73, 2017-02-14, 'initial implementation', _parser.pyx llhttp callbacks). The behavior was first partially mitigated only 10+ years later: 85713a48 (2023-10-06, Sam Bull, #7661) added the incomplete check 'if "\n" in value or "\r" in value or "\x00" in value' to HeadersParser (file-scoped pickaxe shows that check was written exactly once, by 85713a48, replacing a no-check state), and 2026-03-07 bad4131d (#12210) added a bare '\x00' rejection to the C parser _process_header. These partial checks are mitigations, not the origin - the flawed behavior (accepting other CTLs) is first writer of the original permissive parsing in the root commit.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerable behavior - accepting null bytes/control characters in header values - was first written in the repo's very first commit (2013-10-01, founder Nikolay Kim), fourteen years before any AI coding tooling existed; no AI markers on the introducer (root commit), on the 2023/2026 partial mitigations, or on the 2026 fixes. Closed causal chain -> NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Pydantic AI SSRF-protects FileUrl downloads in _ssrf.py: validate_and_resolve_url resolves the host, then always calls is_cloud_metadata_ip and, unless force_download='allow-local', is_private_ip, before safe_download connects to the resolved IP. The original protection compared metadata IPs as raw strings and unwrapped only IPv4-mapped IPv6 for the private list. After CVE-2026-46678, _normalize_ip also unwrapped 6to4 and NAT64 well-known 64:ff9b::/96, but still left IPv4-compatible ::a.b.c.d, RFC 8215 local-use NAT64 64:ff9b:1::/48, operator-chosen NAT64 prefixes, and ISATAP undecoded. On a NAT64- or ISATAP-routed network, an allow-local URL using those wrappers is treated as a non-metadata IPv6 address and is forwarded to the embedded IPv4 metadata endpoint (e.g. 169.254.169.254), leaking cloud IAM credentials. Standard dual-stack VMs that do not route those forms are not exploitable in practice.

causal_research.evidence: GHSA-r277-3xc5-c79v / CVE-2026-24780 (AutoGPT Platform, agpt <=0.2.2, CWE-94/276/863): the /blocks/{block_id}/execute endpoints (main web API backend/api/features/v1.py and external API backend/api/external/v1/routes.py) execute any block by UUID without checking the 'disabled' flag; the BlockInstallationBlock (id 45e78db5-03e9-447f-9395-308d712f5f08) is marked disabled=True with a documented note 'This block allows remote code execution on the server' - it writes attacker-supplied Python to the server filesystem and executes it via __import__(), so any authenticated user (self-registerable in default self-hosted deployments) achieves RCE. Fix 75ecc4de9 (Swifty/craigswift13, 2026-01-26, 'fix(backend): enforce block disabled flag on execution endpoints (#11839)', first tag containing it: agpt-platform-beta-v0.6.45) adds 'if obj.disabled: raise HTTPException(403)' to both API routes plus the chat run_block tool, and a test. Historical chain: /blocks/{block_id}/execute endpoint first added by d9c9b2288 (2024-07-09, rnd/autogpt_server/server/server.py, no disabled check), BlockInstallationBlock added by e70e613f7 (2024-07-16, also no disabled field), then 8ccd14c4b (2024-07-24, 'fix(rnd): Disable BlockInstallationBlock and add disable field for block (#7583)') introduced the Block.disabled attribute (default False) and set disabled=True on BlockInstallationBlock - creating the security-relevant mismatch: the flag existed and was documented ('If the block is disabled, it will not be available for execution') but no execution path ever enforced it; endpoint moved through refactors (3d4aca9fc, 594aa996d, c61317e44 external API, de78d062a) preserving the missing check until 75ecc4de9.
causal_research.flaw_origin: introduced_with_feature
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability's enabling condition - a 'disabled' block flag that is documented as blocking execution but is never enforced by any execution endpoint - was introduced atomically by 8ccd14c4b (Zamil Majdy, 2024-07-24, PR #7583): it added the Block.disabled attribute and marked BlockInstallationBlock disabled=True while the pre-existing /blocks/{block_id}/execute route (d9c9b2288, 2024-07-09) only checked existence (404) with no disabled check; parent 3e384c97 has no 'disabled' attribute in data/block.py (grep rc=1) and the same unguarded endpoint, so parent_absent holds. The RCE capability itself (writing+importing attacker code) dates to e70e613f7 (2024-07-16); both BIC candidates are authored by Zamil Majdy (agpt.co human dev), and the 2026 fix by Swifty. 13-term AI-marker scan: 0 hits on d9c9b2288, e70e613f7, 8ccd14c4b, 75ecc4de9, and all endpoint-refactor intermediates (3d4aca9fc, 594aa996d, c61317e44, de78d062a). causal_research.bug_semantics: On a HERMES_WEBUI_PASSKEY=1 instance with no password hash and zero passkeys, is_auth_enabled() is false. api.auth.check_auth therefore returns True for every path, and api.routes._check_csrf also returns True when auth is disabled, so a remote unauthenticated POST to /api/auth/passkey/register/options and /api/auth/passkey/register reaches registration_options()/finish_registration() and writes the first credential to passkeys.json. After that write, are_passkeys_enabled() is true, is_auth_enabled() becomes true, and the attacker completes passkey login on the public /api/auth/passkey/options and /api/auth/passkey/login paths, taking permanent administrative ownership. Password first-run was already locality-gated; passkey first-run was not.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The unauthenticated register handlers already existed from PR #2859's first commit, but they were not an ownership primitive while is_auth_enabled() depended only on a password hash (passkey login refused with 'Auth not enabled'). 85dc24dc58f543aa0dac657a24d818db7194838e is the smallest commit that first made a stored passkey enable auth (is_auth_enabled = password OR passkeys_available) without adding a first-run onboarding/session gate on registration. Immediate parent d6dfaa9 lacks that combined predicate. The change was cherry-picked onto master as 1b48643f63ccba769dcea5519d98860f2cc9fa3b and first released in v0.51.132.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Hermes WebUI POST /api/git/discard with delete_untracked=true reaches git_discard() in api/workspace_git.py. For an untracked path the function resolves the workspace-relative path with safe_resolve_ws() (after an earlier containment check via _repo_rel), then deletes using ordinary pathname APIs: shutil.rmtree(target) for directories and Path.unlink(missing_ok=True) for files. Those APIs follow a symlink that appears after validation, so a local workspace writer who replaces a validated path component (for example repo/d) with a symlink to an outside directory between the check and the unlink/rmtree can cause Git discard cleanup to delete files outside the configured workspace. The 0.51.303 fix re-anchors the final delete through unlink_anchored/rmtree_anchored so a swapped component is r

causal_research.bug_semantics: An administrator with CONFIGURATION_EDIT posts edit[upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage] to POST /admin/api/configuration. ConfigurationTabController::save copies posted edit[*] keys into Configuration::update(), which UPDATEs any existing faqconfig row except a small runtime/token denylist, so the internal updater path is overwritten. The attacker plants a ZIP with entry phpmyfaq/<file>.php via ATTACHMENT_ADD (upload allows non-HTML MIME types including ZIP). POST /admin/api/extract-package then urldecodes the stored path and Upgrade::extractPackage() ZipArchive::extractTo()s it into content/upgrades/new/ with no origin or hash re-check, bypassing downloadPackage()'s download.phpmyfaq.de/github.com plus MD5 verifyPackage() flow. POST /admin/api/install-package copies new/phpmyfaq/ into PMF_ROOT_DIR, so GET /<file>.php runs as the web-server user.
