causal_research.flaw_origin: 5cc5d7010d363d7798c20310ceedcdefd07fec30 first created upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage as trusted updater state and added a separate extract-package endpoint that reads that config value without re-verifying origin. The bulk configuration save already wrote arbitrary posted keys, so the new key immediately became an integrity-check bypass. Parent 80ab6deb798cafeb443dce85bfce9a4d2220c44c had download+verify only in-request and no extract-package.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 5cc5d7010d to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the pre-fix parent directly instead of trusting the advisory: Upgrade::extractPackage() at :208 verifies nothing but is_file($path) before ZipArchive::open($path) and extractTo($this->upgradeDirectory . '/new/') at :226, with no realpath containment and no per-entry name validation; UpdateController::extractPackage() at :178 applies only urldecode to the stored value, so both path and archive content are attacker-controlled. Checked that the write primitive is genuinely older than the BIC (the 2005 AJAX configuration page already called $faqConfig->update() at phpmyfaq/admin/configuration.php:101), so the BIC is the change that first renders write-then-extract-and-install reachable, not a new write sink. Checked the destinations to rule out a non-executable location: PMF_CONTENT_DIR is phpmyfaq/content (phpmyfaq/src/constants.php:38) inside the application tree and installPackage() copies the extracted phpmyfaq/ subtree into PMF_ROOT_DIR, so a plain update-shaped archive suffices. Checked the fix side for a residual: the fixed extractPackage() resolves and confines both the package and the extraction root, installPackage() re-checks the staging root with realpath, and the setting can no longer be written through the bulk API, so no pre-fix bypass of the CSRF layer alone remains on this path.
mechanism.impact: Arbitrary file write of attacker-chosen PHP into the application root, executed by the web server: remote code execution with the privileges of the web-server user (CWE-494 trust of an unverified control-plane value; the advisory rates it CVSS 4.0 critical, AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:H/UI:N with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact). The chain also defeats the updater's normal control that packages come from download.phpmyfaq.de or github.com with checksum verification.
mechanism.preconditions: An authenticated administrator with CONFIGURATION_EDIT to write the setting, and a way to place a file readable by the web server (ATTACHMENT_ADD with default unencrypted attachment storage, as the advisory states, or any equivalent stored file), plus the ability to reach the admin update API actions; no victim interaction and no maintenance mode is required for the config write, and the attacker ZIP needs no path traversal. A same-named defect is absent for non-admin users because the write endpoints require the admin permission.
mechanism.summary: An authenticated administrator with CONFIGURATION_EDIT writes the internal upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage setting through /admin/api/configuration and points the updater at an attacker-supplied ZIP; Upgrade::extractPackage() opens that path with no origin verification, no containment and no entry validation, extracts it under the content directory, and installPackage() copies the phpmyfaq/* entries into PMF_ROOT_DIR, writing attacker PHP into the web root and achieving remote code execution as the web-server user.
mechanism.trigger: As an admin holding CONFIGURATION_EDIT (plus ATTACHMENT_ADD to store the archive), POST the bulk configuration save at /admin/api/configuration with edit[upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage] set to the absolute path of a malicious ZIP (URL-encoded, since the reader applies urldecode), then call the updater actions /admin/api/extract-package and /admin/api/install-package; the ZIP only needs a normal phpmyfaq/<file>.php layout because the target is the application root, so no traversal is required. The same path is reachable from the legacy AJAX configuration page (phpmyfaq/admin/configuration.php:101 $faqConfig->update($newConfigValues)) and from the CLI updater (Setup/UpdateRunner.php:191 $upgrade->installPackage).
mechanism.vulnerable_code: phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Setup/Upgrade.php:208 extractPackage() and :292 installPackage() ($destinationDir = PMF_ROOT_DIR at :295, copy at :308) at pre-fix parent 9aec52a9f488918f476d9fabb88dca200fa1e02e, fed by phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Controller/Administration/Api/UpdateController.php:178 extractPackage() (urldecode of the setting at :183, downloadPackage writes it at :172) and by phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Configuration.php:425 update() whose pre-fix filter accepts every key except main.phpMyFAQToken and $runtimeConfigs; the writing endpoint is phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Controller/Administration/Api/ConfigurationTabController.php:87 save() calling update() at :194.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory describes a real CWE-494 chain: bulk config write of upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage plus extract/install that trust that path. The smallest first-writer of those lines is 5cc5d7010d363d7798c20310ceedcdefd07fec30; the parent tree lacks the key and extract-package endpoint. The minimum 4.1.6 repair is fe24bc9a4f0e69831e4f91fd0b3bf7577aff3cf1, which both ignores the key in Configuration::update() and refuses extract paths outside the upgrade directory, matching the vendor patched version. The BIC commit object is named-human Thorsten Rinne with no AI authorship markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class. Fix-side AI is also absent and is not used for attribution.
The advisory mechanism reproduces exactly from the pre-fix tree: the configuration API writes every posted edit[...] key through Configuration::update(), which pre-fix filtered only runtimeConfigs and main.phpMyFAQToken, and the updater URL-decodes upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage and hands it to Upgrade::extractPackage(), which gates only on is_file(), opens the named ZIP and calls extractTo() into the update staging directory, after which installPackage() copies staging/phpmyfaq/* into PMF_ROOT_DIR, so a CONFIGURATION_EDIT administrator who can stage a ZIP (ATTACHMENT_ADD) drops attacker PHP into the web root and executes it as the web-server user. The defect is born in 5cc5d7010d363d7798c20310ceedcdefd07fec30 (#2492, 2023-09-30): its immediate parent 80ab6deb798cafeb443dce85bfce9a4d2220c44c contains zero occurrences of lastDownloadedPackage in the updater controller, has no extractPackage() in Upgrade.php, and its predecessor unpackPackage() has no caller anywhere in the tree, while the child creates the setting, the admin/api/extract-package route and the JS/Twig trigger that wire it into a live extract-and-install path. The upstream fix fe24bc9a4f0e69831e4f91fd0b3bf7577aff3cf1 adds three layers - a protectedConfigs refusal for upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage in Configuration::update(), CSRF isValidUpdatePackageToken() checks on every package action, and realpath containment plus per-entry Zip-Slip rejection in Upgrade::extractPackage() - and is contained in release 4.1.6 (58c1d7f2fa36f7074664fc6d862afee0ca8bcc89) but not in 4.1.5 (e807a988bb58682211bd2e03c17d86fb1c70ea34), matching the advisory's patched boundary. AI attribution fails at the only causal object: the raw BIC commit bytes carry author and committer Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de> (1696083646 +0200) and the message 'refactor: now using PHP ZipArchive class (#2492)' with no trailer block, AI identity, session or generated-by bytes, and the change is ordinary PHP (ZipArchive switch plus route, JS, Twig and setup edits), not machine-shaped output. All nine commits in all history that ever touch upgrade.lastDownloadedPackage are the same named human with an empty trailer set, and the single AI-marked commit among the 241 commits touching the causal files (512029eae6a26f9189c6f63576c23927aa1c0b04, Copilot SWE-agent, LDAP/AD groups) never touches update(), protectedConfigs or the updater path. With no AI marker on the introduction, no AI-marked new exposure and no AI-marked incomplete remediation, the verdict is NOT_AI; what would flip it is an AI trailer or AI authorship on 5cc5d7010 or on a later commit that first rendered the unverified updater path reachable.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Agent.handleBgCommand in src/core/agent.ts implements the '/bg' chat command family: '/bg <shell command>' calls this.backgroundTasks.spawnShell(command, cwd) (agent.ts:838-841 at v1.1.12) and BackgroundTasks.spawnShell executes the raw string via spawn(command, [], { shell: true }) (src/core/background-tasks.ts), while '/bg:' spawns an LLM sub-agent and other subcommands cancel/inspect tasks. Unlike the normal run_command tool path, which routes every command through PermissionManager.checkShellCommand() and prompts for approval in 'Ask Me' mode before non-safe commands, the /bg path never invokes any permission check. An authenticated web-dashboard user can therefore POST '/bg touch <canary>' through the documented chat API (POST /api/auth/login then POST /api/chat/send) and get arbitrary OS command execution with the Mercury process privileges and zero approval prompts, output returned to the requesting channel. This is incorrect authorization / approval-boundary bypass on an alternate shell entry point of the same authenticated chat surface.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Daphne constructed its WebSocket server factory (WebSocketFactory, subclassing autobahn.twisted.websocket.WebSocketServerFactory) and configured it via setProtocolOptions(...) without ever passing maxFramePayloadSize or maxMessagePayloadSize. Autobahn defaults both values to 0 (unlimited), so every daphne release accepted arbitrarily large WebSocket frames/messages from unauthenticated clients, buffering them fully in server memory; a remote attacker could exhaust RAM and cause denial of service.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-200/CWE-201 environment-variable exfiltration. Git.polish_url() (git/cmd.py, v3.1.50 lines 907-925) unconditionally runs os.path.expandvars(url) on its input on the non-Cygwin branch, and Repo._clone() (reached via public Repo.clone_from()/Repo.clone(), git/repo/base.py:1407-1418) passes the polished post-expansion URL to the git clone subprocess after running the unsafe-protocol check on the raw URL. mechanism.impact: Full vm2 sandbox escape: attacker-supplied sandbox code executes arbitrary code in the host Node process (host-realm Function), CWE-913, advisory severity CRITICAL, npm vm2 all versions <= 3.11.3.
mechanism.preconditions: A runtime exposing JSPI: Node 24 with --experimental-wasm-jspi or Node 26+ where it is default-on; wasm not disabled (default is enabled, lib/vm.js allowWasm = options.wasm !== false); attacker code running inside the sandbox with async support; the rejection path requires a host-realm rejection to reach the attacker closures through the species construction.
mechanism.summary: WebAssembly JSPI promises are sandbox-visible but walk a cross-realm prototype chain to host Promise.prototype without bridge interposition, so p.finally() runs host native code with an attacker-controlled species constructor and delivers a raw host-realm rejection into sandbox closures, yielding host RCE.
mechanism.trigger: Sandbox code (default options; wasm enabled unless the embedder passes wasm:false) obtains a JSPI promise p = WebAssembly.promising(fn)(...), installs Object.defineProperty(p, 'constructor', {get(){return F}}) directly on it, then calls p.finally(fn2); when the JSPI promise rejects with a host-realm error such as the TypeError from WebAssembly.compileStreaming(Promise.resolve(0)), V8 dispatches the rejection through the raw resolve/reject closures F supplied, and e.constructor.constructor('return process')() evaluates in the host realm.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: lib/setup-sandbox.js:348 globalPromise.prototype.then override (and :380 catch, resetPromiseSpecies at :312) at 01a7552add345d5a6862623884e6b79a85bf0568 - the pre-fix sandbox intercepts only promises inheriting globalPromise.prototype and never .finally; carrier of the enabled wasm surface: lib/main.js:145 vm.createContext codeGeneration.wasm wiring at 902e40cbc170b235de6954c8f19590cdffe256aa.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Insecure deserialization / arbitrary class reconstruction leading to RCE in LangGraph Checkpoint's JsonPlusSerializer (libs/checkpoint/langgraph/checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py, versions <=2.1.2). loads() = json.loads(data, object_hook=self._reviver); _reviver treats any dict with lc:2/type:constructor/id as instructions to importlib.import_module the module named by id, getattr the class/method, and call it with attacker-controlled args/kwargs (cls(*args, **kwargs) / method(*args, **kwargs)). Malicious payloads (e.g., constructors such as subprocess.Popen or os-level classes with attacker-controlled args) yield code execution when deserialized. By default the serializer prefers msgpack, but dumps_typed fell back to the 'json' type whenever msgpack serialization failed (e.g., illegal Unicode surrogates), so json-mode payloads reach the vulnerable loads() path. Fixed in checkpointer 3.0.0 (commit c5744f583, PR #6269: removed untyped loads/dumps and restricted deserialization to an allow list).

causal_research.bug_semantics: With FileUpload_ProtectFiles enabled, GET /file-upload/:fileId/:name is authorized for Livechat guests via query/cookie rc_room_type=l, rc_rid, and rc_token. requests.ts loads the upload by :fileId only (:name is ignored) and calls FileUpload.requestCanAccessFiles(req, file). The livechat branch then invokes roomCoordinator.getRoomDirectives('l').canAccessUploadedFile({rc_rid, rc_token}) without the file object. livechat canAccessUploadedFile returns true iff the visitor token matches that livechat room (findOneByIdAndVisitorToken / originally findOneOpenByVisitorToken), so isAuthorizedByRoom short-circuits true before membership checks. A guest who can start Livechat therefore downloads arbitrary protected uploads, including files whose rid is a different room, by enumerating MongoDB ObjectIds. JWT file tokens already bound fileId and rid; this bypass is the unbound livechat room path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Package.Unmarshal() in pkg/types/alpine/apk.go decompresses the signature.tar.gz and control.tar.gz gzip members of an Alpine APK into in-memory bytes.Buffer objects with no cap on decompressed size; the #nosec G110 annotations explicitly waive gosec's G110 (potential DoS via decompression bomb) warning. The max_apk_metadata_size config (default 1MB) was only checked against individual tar entry header sizes after decompression, so a crafted ~1000:1 gzip bomb submitted as spec.package.content of an Alpine ProposedEntry makes the server expand the payload fully on the heap during request processing, causing a fatal Go runtime out-of-memory condition (remote DoS).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Public REST write endpoints for categories, FAQs, and questions authorize only via hasValidToken(), which hash-compares the shared configuration secret api.apiClientToken to request header x-pmf-token. causal_research.bug_semantics: Camaleon CMS registers a custom field type select_eval whose options include a stored Ruby 'command'. Authenticated users who can manage custom field groups POST field_key=select_eval and field_options[command]=<ruby> through CustomFieldsController, which at 2.9.1 forwards permit!-ed params into CustomFieldGroup#add_fields with no type or command allowlist. The admin form hides the select_eval button, but get_items and a direct POST still persist the field. On any later render of a post-edit (or other) form that includes the field group, _select_eval.html.erb executes instance_eval(field.options[:command]) in the view binding, yielding RCE as the web process. CVE-2026-66748/GHSA-7xm9-634w-f5r7 describe this CWE-94 chain for 2.1.1–2.9.1. The 2.9.2 fix does not remove instance_eval; it requires can?(:manage, :select_eval) (admins via manage :all) before creating or modifying such fields.

causal_research.bug_semantics:
1-click Remote Code Execution (CWE-94, GitHub advisory severity HIGH, CVSS 3.1 10.0 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N) in the Eigent desktop agent. The renderer executes untrusted document previews with full Electron privileges: the main BrowserWindow is created with webSecurity:false + nodeIntegration:true + webviewTag:true (electron/main/index.ts ~717/796/798); the preload exposes generic ipcRenderer.invoke plus executeCommand (ipcMain.handle('execute-command') at electron/main/index.ts:319 spawns an arbitrary command string in the main process); protocol.handle('localfile') (index.ts:948) serves arbitrary local files as text/html; and FileReader.openFile (electron/main/fileReader.ts) parses downloaded csv/xlsx/docx/pptx into unescaped HTML (e.g. html += `${cellValue}`, `
  • ${text}
    • `), rendered in src/components/Folder/index.tsx via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (line ~287) or iframe src=localfile://+encodeURIComponent(content). Clicking a file chip in chat renders attacker-controlled file content as HTML/JS in the privileged renderer, enabling executeCommand RCE. Advisory's vulnerable range 0.0.60, patched 0.0.61; the publisher (Wendong-Fan, published 2025-12-26) lists no credits/reporter. Advisory is imprecise: v0.0.60..v0.0.61 contains no security fix; the real fix landed in v0.0.72.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Improper validation of uploaded-file validity in MISP's module/import file-upload path (app/Controller/EventsController.php): the guard condition `(isset($fileupload['error']) && $fileupload['error'] == 0) || (!empty($fileupload['tmp_name']) && $fileupload['tmp_name'] != 'none') && is_uploaded_file(...)` suffers an operator-precedence flaw (&& binds tighter than ||) so `error == 0` alone satisfies the check and is_uploaded_file() is never consulted; an attacker-supplied tmp_name (any readable local path) is then passed to FileAccessTool::readAndDelete(), enabling file read/deletion outside genuine uploads.
causal_research.evidence: Identity: cases-pC.jsonl lists repo misp/misp with advisory_ids CVE-2025-66384 + GHSA-863h-c4v7-h5fv. OSV CVE-2025-66384: 'app/Controller/EventsController.php in MISP before 2.5.24 has invalid logic in checking for uploaded file validity, related to tmp_name'; GIT range introduced 0, fixed 6867f0d3157a1959154bdad9ddac009dec6a19f5 (and merge 1b4f6b3bf93b8933f04d3fd78ed565c1bbfb9d9d). Fix commit: 'fix: [security] fix invalid check for uploaded file validity - Thanks to Raphael Lob from NATO Cyber Security Center' (iglocska, 2025-10-28), +10/-1 in EventsController.php rewriting the condition to require (!isset(error)||error==0) && (!empty(tmp_name)&&tmp_name!='none') && is_uploaded_file(tmp_name). Pickaxe -S on the exact vulnerable snippet across app/Controller/EventsController.php yields exactly two writers: 1f1c8c814 (2016, introduced) and f720706a4 (2022 refactor, logic preserved). Introducer metadata: author/committer Iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>, 2016-08-01, subject 'new: First revision of the new import system'; AI-marker grep on %B = 0 hits; f720706a4 %B also 0 hits. Parent 2d3b3aa7728be55a16c1e90da2bbaf2dedcd388b's EventsController.php contains 0 '$fileupload' occurrences => block absent => introducer_parent_absent True. Release checks: git merge-base --is-ancestor 6867f0d3 v2.5.24 => YES; v2.5.23 still contains the vulnerable is_uploaded_file check => confirmed affected-before-fixed.
causal_research.flaw_origin: First writer of the flawed upload-validity check: commit 1f1c8c814e63c7fb3dbcc07cc156fa6c888c4396 'new: First revision of the new import system' (Iglocska/Andras Iklody, 2016-08-01), which introduced the entire module file-upload block including the precedence-broken condition. The 2022 refactor f720706a4f2e9fc3f895b7a0709c1aa9a511bff8 (Jakub Onderka) renamed variables and switched to readAndDelete but preserved the same flawed logic; the bug persisted unchanged until the 2.5.24 security fix.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is a 2016 operator-precedence bug in the upload-validation condition, first written by MISP's founder Iglocska (Andras Iklody) and merely refactored (logic untouched) by Jakub Onderka in 2022; the 2025 fix was authored by iglocska crediting a NATO CSC reporter. No AI authorship markers exist on the introducer, the refactor, or the fix. The vulnerable behavior predates AI coding tools by years -> NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Langroid file tools treat curr_dir as a workspace sandbox but never enforce it. ReadFileTool.handle, WriteFileTool.handle, and ListDirTool.handle resolve curr_dir (from the injected getter or cwd), chdir into it, then pass the caller-supplied file_path/dir_path straight to read_file/create_file/list_dir. Those helpers open the given path as-is. Because chdir does not block .. segments, absolute paths, or in-dir symlinks, a tool caller (LLM agent or user-controlled tool arguments) can read or write files outside the configured directory, matching the GHSA PoC of ReadFileTool(file_path='../secret.txt') and WriteFileTool(file_path='../written_by_tool.txt').

causal_research.bug_semantics: Denial of service / uncontrolled memory consumption (CWE-400) in Spring AI pdf-document-reader: a maliciously crafted PDF processed by ForkPDFLayoutTextStripper triggers unreasonable memory allocation, OOM-ing the host. Two attacker-controlled allocation vectors: (1) per-character writing builds each line via completeLineWithSpaces() which concatenates SPACE_CHARACTER one char at a time ('line += ' loop, O(n^2) char copies) for a length derived from the PDF page width (lineLength = pageWidth/OUTPUT_SPACE_CHARACTER_WIDTH_IN_PT -> unbounded); (2) text-position parsing computes numberOfLines = floor(textYPosition - previousTextYPosition)/height from attacker-controlled coordinates (tiny heights / huge gaps -> huge counts) and createNewEmptyNewLines() materializes that many TextLine objects, each triggering the per-line allocation. Affected spring-ai-pdf-document-reader 1.0.0-1.0.5 (fixed 1.0.6) and 1.1.0-1.1.4 (fixed 1.1.5).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trust/authorization gap enabling arbitrary shell command execution (CWE-77/CWE-284) in the Paperclip workspace runtime service. server/src/services/workspace-runtime.ts resolves the shell via resolveShell() (SHELL env or /bin/sh) and runs `spawn(shell, ['-lc', command], {cwd: serviceCwd, env})` where `command` comes directly from workspace runtimeConfig set through PATCH /projects/{id}/workspaces/{workspaceId} and start via POST /projects/{id}/workspaces/{workspaceId}/runtime-services/start. An agent/skill that can modify that config (or convince an authorized agent) can execute arbitrary shell commands in the server OS context, exfiltrating host env vars such as API keys, JWT secrets, and DATABASE_URL, or destroying data. The mechanism is the un-sanitized command-plus-shell execution path in workspace-runtime.ts; the fix adds agent-side authorization gates preventing agents from mutating host-executed workspace commands and from managing runtime services without workspace-management permission.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When basic-auth is enabled, CreateModelVersion is authorized only on UPDATE of the caller’s registered model. Core _validate_source_run/_validate_source_model in mlflow/server/handlers.py only prove that a local source path sits inside the artifact directory of the supplied run_id or model_id (store.get_run/get_logged_model with no permission check). After the version is stored, GET /model-versions/get-artifact is gated on registered-model READ (validate_can_read_model_version_artifact), whereas GET /get-artifact requires experiment/run READ (validate_can_read_run_artifact). An authenticated user who can create or update a registered model can therefore pass another user’s run_id (or model_id) and that run’s artifact URI as source, then download the victim’s files through their own model version, bypassing the experiment-level READ gate. The first-party fix closes the gap at create time by requiring READ on any supplied run_id/model_id.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An operator can point ATOMIC_AGENTS_MCP_SERVER_REGISTRY_BACKEND=http at a catalog URL. Through v1.0.0 the factory make_http_mcp_server_registry_backend_from_url accepted both http and https. The catalog JSON is parsed into MCPServerSpec values whose command/args are type-checked (string / list of strings) but content-unrestricted. Agent construction materializes those specs onto AgentProfile.mcp_servers_resolved; MCPClientPool then stdio-spawns StdioServerParameters(command=spec.command, args=spec.args) with no command-basename allowlist. On a cleartext http:// catalog a network MITM can rewrite the response to inject an arbitrary executable and obtain host RCE with no LLM in the loop. Policy mcp_allow_fn is None unless a Policy backend is configured, and even then default enforce_noncap=False only logs denials. The https path is not this bug: httpx.Client is constructed with library defaults verify=True and follow_redirects=False.

causal_research.bug_semantics: getHTMLFromAtext builds an HTML tag string from plugin-supplied [name, value] pairs that originate in the pad attribute pool. From ed526265 those pairs are concatenated as span data-<name>="<value>" and later emitted as raw opening tags. Pool values are not HTML-attribute-escaped; a collaborator who can write a changeset (or import) can store a value such as '" onload="alert(1)' (author attributes are validated; other keys/values are stored verbatim via moveOpsToNewPool -> AttributePool.putAttrib). When a plugin registers exportHtmlAdditionalTagsWithData (bundled ep_font_color / ep_font_size), HTML export serves <span data-color="" onload="alert(1)"> as text/html, causing stored XSS for anyone who opens the export. The 3.3.0 fix sanitizes the data-* name and escapes the value with Security.escapeHTMLAttribute before interpolation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GHSA-92hr-gmr6-h8cp is a published medium hardening cluster (no CVE, not withdrawn) of six independent source-to-sink flaws, all still present at tag 3.2.0 and closed together by 7ea9970 in 3.3.0. (1) CWE-330: pad_utils.randomString samples Math.random to mint author/session/readonly IDs (generateAuthorToken prefixes t.); those IDs are cookies/identifiers, so a predictable PRNG is the source and token acceptance is the sink. (2) CWE-208/307: POST /interaction/:uid login maps settings.users then compares user.password === password in non-constant time with no failure delay, enabling password/oracle timing and prototype-key lookup. (3) CWE-22: plugin package.json dependency names are interpolated into path.join(pluginInstallPath, dependency, ...) / symlink targets without an npm-name grammar check (admin-gated). (4) CWE-235: /api/2 RestAPI merges every request header into the API field set via Object.assign({}, headers, params, query, formData), so header names collide with API parameters (authorization included). (5) appendChatMessage omits existence checking; sendChatMessageToPadClients/getPad creates an arbitrary pad as a side effect. (6) CWE-209: the admin static file handler echoes fs.readFile err to the client.

causal_research.bug_semantics: vm2's bufferAllocLimit (opt-in, default Infinity) is enforced only on sandbox Buffer.alloc, Buffer.allocUnsafe, Buffer.allocUnsafeSlow, and deprecated Buffer(N)/new Buffer(N) via checkBufferAllocLimit() in lib/setup-sandbox.js before those calls reach host C++. An embedder who sets a finite cap (e.g. 10 MiB) blocks Buffer.alloc(20 MiB) with RangeError but still allows a ~200-byte payload to commit gigabytes of host RSS and OOM-kill the process in Docker/K8s/Lambda. Source is untrusted vm.run() constructor calls; sink is host-process RSS.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A top-level GET to a backend URL whose action segment is a public controller method name is dispatched as a page action. Backend routes are Route::any, so GET reaches BackendController, which parseAction()s the segment and treats it as a page action when Controller::actionExists() returns true. actionExists() accepted every public method (and extension methods) except a small hiddenActions list, so AJAX handler names such as index_onEmptyLog and onDelete were never reserved from URL dispatch. Controller::run() skips CSRF for HEAD/GET/OPTIONS, and the default session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so a cross-site link from an attacker page sends the victim's backend session with no token. execPageAction() then call_user_func_array-s the handler. Preconditions: the victim is an authenticated backend user who holds the handler's permission (system.access_logs and similar default to the Developer role) and follows the link. Impact is state-changing, not confidential: EventLogs::index_onEmptyLog() truncates the event log; Cms Index::onDelete() deletes a template using Request::input() (query string); other core handlers reset settings or alter backend user state. POST AJAX via X-WINTER-REQUEST-HANDLER remains the intended path and is CSRF-gated.

BrandSetting::compileCss() / EditorSetting::compileCss() feed that string to the LESS parser; a payload such as .x { content: ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; } compiles into markup that breaks out of the backend <style> element. renderCss() stores the raw compiler output with Cache::forever() and, before v1.2.14, returned Cache::get() unsanitized on every later request. modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php prints that string into <style> on the standard backend head and the auth layout, so the stored XSS executes for other backend users and on unauthenticated sign-in/restore/reset pages. v1.2.13 applied strip_tags() only to the cache-miss return, so the first render after save looked clean while priming a poisoned cache entry exploitable from the second render onward.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Trigger: an authenticated backend user who passes a controller's coarse $requiredPermissions but lacks a finer import[permissions] or export[permissions] key posts an AJAX handler (onImport/onExport/...) or hits the download action. Vulnerable code: ImportExportController::userHasAccess() (historically checkPermissionsForType()) is the only granular gate and, through v1.2.13, was invoked only from the import() and export() page actions. Backend\Classes\Controller::run() dispatches execAjaxHandlers() and returns before execPageAction(), while the behavior constructor still bindToController()s the import/export form widgets, so the handlers run fully formed. Sinks: onImport() calls $model->import() with attacker-supplied column_match (write/overwrite); onExport() calls $model->export() then download() streams the file (exfil). CSRF is still checked, so this is session-bound IDOR/missing authorization on the opted-in granular keys only (userHasAccess is default-permissive when those keys are unset).

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked whether the page action still runs before the handler (it does not: run() returns the AJAX response at l.313, before execPageAction at l.338, and runAjaxHandler resolves an on* method on the controller via methodExists without executing the page action); whether the granular check ever existed on the handlers (git log -S'checkPermissionsForType' and -S'userHasAccess' on the file return only 9ecf75307 and the d2c1d591a rename, both page-action-only); whether other public behavior methods form a separate unguarded path (importRender/exportRender/exportFromList and friends are hidden from controller actions by $actions = ['import','export','download'], and exportFromList is only called from the guarded export() action); and whether the handlers even work without the page action (the constructor binds all four form widgets to the controller on every request, so they do).
mechanism.impact: Read: onExport() plus download() stream any dataset the configured export model can list. Write: onImport() runs the configured import model with attacker-supplied column mappings and option data, so records can be created or overwritten under the backend session.
mechanism.preconditions: The controller implements the behavior and declares import[permissions]/export[permissions] more restrictive than its own coarse $requiredPermissions; the attacker has a valid backend session with a CSRF token and can reach that controller; userHasAccess() is default-permissive, so controllers that never configured the keys are unaffected.
mechanism.summary: A controller using the ImportExportController behavior may declare granular import[permissions]/export[permissions]; userHasAccess() enforces them only in the import() and export() page actions, but Backend\Classes\Controller::run() dispatches AJAX handlers before any page action, so onImport() -> $model->import() and onExport() -> $model->export(), plus the download() action, executed with no granular check. Impact: an authenticated backend user who passes the controller's coarse $requiredPermissions but lacks the granular permission can exfiltrate the whole export dataset and write or overwrite records.
mechanism.trigger: Logged-in backend POST to /backend/<controller>/<action> carrying the X_WINTER_REQUEST_HANDLER header set to onExport, onImport, onImportLoadForm, onImportLoadColumnSampleForm or onExportLoadForm, or a request to the download action, by a user who holds the controller's coarse $requiredPermissions but not the configured import[permissions]/export[permissions].

causal_research.reasoning:
The GHSA describes a real incomplete-authorization bug: a documented granular import/export permission gate never ran on the AJAX handlers or download action that perform the work, because those paths skip execPageAction. The smallest commit that first wrote that incomplete gate is 9ecf75307b9960283a571433d9cb03b780d25609; its parent lacks the helper entirely, and later userHasAccess is only a rename. The minimum closing change is 84c81f153f2dc3e2c7b03ab14a4a3ca8456d0e4f, present in v1.2.14 and absent from v1.2.13. The BIC commit object is named-human Samuel Georges in 2015 with no AI trailer, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class or FALSE_POSITIVE.
This is a real, upstream-confirmed permission-bypass defect whose root cause is human. The granular import/export gate entered the tree in 9ecf75307 (2015-08-04), which added checkPermissionsForType() and wired it into the import() and export() page actions only, leaving the already-existing AJAX handlers and the download() action without it. That incomplete gate is exactly what the advisory describes: a controller declaring import[permissions]/export[permissions] gets a check that silently does not cover the handlers that do the work, so an authenticated backend user holding only the coarse $requiredPermissions can still run onExport()/download() to exfiltrate the export dataset and onImport() to write records. Parent 8166c5ad6 contains no permissions config in the file at all, so the vulnerable behaviour is present only from 9ecf75307 onward, and the 2025 rewrite d2c1d591a merely renamed the helper to userHasAccess() while keeping the page-action-only scope, making it a refactor rather than an introduction. The BIC commit object is a named-human 2015 commit with hand-written PHP content and no trailers, and the upstream fix 84c81f153 (shipped in v1.2.14) guards all three page actions and all five AJAX handlers, closing the mechanism. No AI contribution to the defect is visible in the BIC object or anywhere on the introduction path, so the verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Any authenticated Winter backend user can open Backend\Controllers\MyAccount because requiredPermissions is an empty array, so Controller::run() skips hasAnyAccess. MyAccount implements FormController, whose public create/update/preview actions are inherited and, with default $guarded=[], pass actionExists() as non-own extension methods. Those actions take a caller-supplied record id; formFindModelObject() runs an unscoped Backend\Models\User query (formExtendQuery is a no-op). GET /backend/backend/myaccount/preview/{id} therefore returns another user's first_name, last_name, login, email and avatar; GET .../update/{id} also renders role, groups, is_superuser and throttle. Password widgets are masked. Cross-user writes via create_onSave/update_onSave/update_onDelete are blocked by User::canBeManagedByUser() introduced in the same v1.2.13 series, so the confirmed impact is IDOR disclosure. Preconditions: a valid backend session of any privilege; user ids are sequential. This is not GHSA-j5jq-cr68-v2xx (postback handler-name bypass on Users).

causal_research.bug_semantics: A plugin Backend list column with type=image causes Lists::getColumnValue() to call evalImageTypeValue(). That method turns attachOne/attachMany File models, absolute URLs (str_contains $value '://'), data URIs, media-library paths, or a column default into $image, then sets $imageUrl = ImageResizer::filterGetUrl($image, $width, $height, $options). filterGetUrl() returns the input string when the resizer cannot identify the image. evalImageTypeValue interpolated that string into a single-quoted HTML src (and width/height from column config) without e()/htmlspecialchars. The list body partial prints getColumnValue() raw, so a stored value such as http://example.com/a.jpg'/onerror='... breaks out of src and injects event-handler attributes into the backend list viewed by another backend user. Core ships no image list column; exploitation needs a plugin that renders attacker-influenced values through one. Attacker must already store the value; a backend user must open the list.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated Winter backend user who can edit CMS Twig (cms.manage_pages, cms.manage_layouts, or cms.manage_partials) renders attacker-controlled template code under System\Twig\SecurityPolicy, which is installed as a global Twig sandbox. From 1.2.7 the policy used a class-scoped method blocklist: save/update/delete/forceDelete are denied on Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model, but equivalent writers (saveQuietly, deleteQuietly, forceFill, destroy) are not listed, and checkMethodAllowed only matches the receiver's class. Eloquent Model::__call forwards unknown methods to the query builder, so increment/decrement/when/each and newQuery()/getConnection()/getConnectionResolver() execute on the live database layer. Those calls read or modify arbitrary rows, run raw SQL (including DDL), or write PHP into Halcyon page/layout/partial code for RCE. Higher-order collection methods that take callables are a parallel sandbox hole because the policy cannot see arguments. Preconditions: backend session plus one CMS template permission; the sandbox is the extra control this advisory is about, not the permission itself.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-280 confidentiality bug in the Pages admin API: get_base_queryset returned every Page for any admin-authenticated user, and serializers emit api_fields. The smallest introducing change is the 2015 PR #2485 member that first overrode get_queryset to Page.objects.all(); the parent tree only had an empty subclass inheriting the public live filter. That member is Karl Hobley with no commit-object AI marker, so BIC-side attribution is named-human. The 2026 explorable_instances repair closes the default listing/detail path on the stated release lines. Successful human/maintainer repair does not make the case AI. Therefore the verdict is NOT_AI.
The internal Pages admin API has shipped since 2016 with a base queryset of every page (`Page.objects.all()`), so any session user holding only the `access_admin` permission could list and fetch pages they had no page-level permission for, including drafts and restricted branches, with `api_fields` content serialized. The introducing change is the endpoint's creation in 2f8d00222d (PR #2507); its immediate parent bdd80dd33e has no `wagtail/wagtailadmin/api/` package at all, and the two later commits that touched the same expression (a2b97737eb, f0de04f0bd) are pure extractions verified against their own patches. The fix de1e3fd686 swaps the base queryset for `policy_registry.get_by_type(Page).explorable_instances(self.request.user)` on main, with identical backports on stable/7.0.x, 7.3.x, 7.4.x and 8.0.x. The BIC commit object carries named human identities (author Karl Hobley, committer Mikalai Radchuk in 2016) with no AI trailers, and no later commit in the file's history removes a user filter, so no AI contribution to the defect is attributable.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated backend IDOR in Backend\FormWidgets\FileUpload. Mutation handlers trusted attacker-controlled attachment ids instead of the widget's own attachOne/attachMany relation. getFileRecord() (and originally inline File::find($file_id)) loaded any System\Models\File row from system_files by primary key; onLoadAttachmentConfig, onSaveAttachmentConfig (via getConfigFormWidget()->model), and onRemoveAttachment then operated on that row. onSortAttachments() fed posted sortOrder ids directly to setSortableOrder(), an unscoped UPDATE ... CSRF is still required; the miss is object-level authorization, not CSRF. The 2026 fix scopes both lookups through getRelationObject()->withDeferred($sessionKey).

causal_research.bug_semantics: JSONata evaluates user expressions against nested environments created by createFrame. Each frame stored variables in `var bindings = {}` and resolved names with ordinary property access (originally `bindings[name]`; later a bypassable `bindings.hasOwnProperty(name)`). The GHSA PoC first overwrites `$hasOwnProperty` (so the later instance-method check no longer gates own-property lookup), then uses that chain to invoke `Function('return process.getBuiltinModule(...)')()` and run host code. The 2.2.1/1.8.8 fix uses Object.create(null) plus Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call, which blocks both inherited lookups and method replacement.

causal_research.bug_semantics: JSONata name steps and $lookup both resolve keys through evaluateName/lookup. The object branch performed result = input[key] (originally input[expr.value]) with no Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty test, so ordinary [[Get]] walked Object.prototype. A page at http://localhost.attacker.com therefore sent a permitted Origin, posted JSON-RPC as Content-Type text/plain (no CORS preflight; request.json() still parses the body), and invoked tools/call without a session. That executes unauthenticated state-changing tools, including praisonai.rules.create writing attacker content under ~/.praison/rules that RulesManager later loads with activation always.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The PraisonAI async Jobs API (FastAPI app in src/praisonai/praisonai/jobs/) installs its router with only CORS middleware and no authentication dependency on any route. Every /api/v1/runs operation (POST submit, GET list, GET {id}, GET {id}/result, POST {id}/cancel, DELETE {id}, GET {id}/stream) is pre-authenticated: source = any caller able to reach the jobs server; sink = job submit runs the attacker's prompt against the operator's configured LLM credentials (executor -> Agent(instructions=...).start(job.prompt)) and the global in-memory store exposes all jobs' results to any caller. Reachability requires binding/publishing the default 127.0.0.1 service (default bind is loopback; remote exposure needs --host 0.0.0.0, container publish, reverse proxy, or tunnel). Impact: unauthenticated job execution, cross-tenant result theft (list/read any job), and cancel/delete of other callers' jobs (CWE-306, CVSS 8.6).

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can submit a PraisonAI job with webhook_url points that field at a hostname that fails DNS during Pydantic validation (NXDOMAIN, timeout, or other socket.gaierror). JobSubmitRequest.validate_webhook_url and Job.validate_webhook_url in src/praisonai/praisonai/jobs/models.py resolve the hostname with socket.gethostbyname and reject private/loopback/link-local/multicast results, but the gaierror handler is 'pass', so the URL is stored. When the job later succeeds or fails, JobExecutor._send_webhook in src/praisonai/praisonai/jobs/executor.py opens a new httpx.AsyncClient and POSTs the job result JSON to job.webhook_url, which performs an independent DNS lookup. If the hostname now resolves to a private or loopback address, the server issues an internal POST (SSRF / DNS TOCTOU). Literal localhost names and already-private resolved IPs are blocked at check time; the bypass is specifically fail-open on resolution failure. This is a patch bypass of CVE-2026-40114, which had added these validators.

mechanism.impact: Server-side request forgery (CWE-918) with a TOCTOU race (CWE-367) and incorrect control-flow scoping (CWE-705): the server POSTs the job payload to an attacker-chosen internal destination, enabling interaction with internal services (potential command execution where POST bodies are interpreted as commands), internal reconnaissance, and exfiltration of job results; CVSS 3.1 7.1 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N).
mechanism.preconditions: The jobs API is reachable by the attacker (the related advisory GHSA-8frj-8q3m-xhgm documents this API as unauthenticated by default), the attacker controls DNS for the submitted webhook hostname with a short TTL (or can ride a transient resolver failure), and job execution is delayed enough after submission for the DNS change to land.
mechanism.summary: An attacker submits a job to the jobs API with a webhook_url whose hostname does not resolve at validation time; the fail-open validator accepts it, and when the job completes JobExecutor._send_webhook resolves the same hostname again and POSTs the job result to whatever address it now points to, including loopback, private or internal services (TOCTOU / DNS-rebinding SSRF).
mechanism.trigger: POST to the jobs API (jobs router, e.g. POST /jobs or POST /api/v1/runs) with an attacker-controlled webhook_url whose hostname is NXDOMAIN or transiently unresolvable during validation, then repointing that hostname at 127.0.0.1 or another internal address before the job finishes.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PraisonAI code-agent tools treat a configured workspace as a path-traversal security boundary. The shared helper is_path_within_directory() (docstring: 'prevents path traversal') canonicalizes with os.path.abspath() rather than realpath()/Path.resolve(), then uses a startswith prefix test. A symlink whose link path is inside the workspace therefore passes, while open() follows the link to an outside target, so read_file/write_file/apply_diff/search_replace can read or overwrite files outside the workspace (CWE-59). Independently, list_files() never calls the helper (../ and absolute paths escape), and execute_command()/code_execute_command() resolve a relative cwd against the workspace without containment, so commands run outside the workspace (CWE-22). causal_research.bug_semantics: web_crawl()/crawl_web() accept attacker- or LLM-supplied URLs and, in the httpx fallback provider, fetch them with httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True) or urllib.request.urlopen (redirects on by default), returning the response body as tool output. From praisonaiagents 1.5.126 an SSRF check resolves the initial hostname once via socket.gethostbyname and rejects loopback/private/link-local results, but it never pins that IP and never re-validates redirect Location targets. An attacker domain that resolves public at check time can therefore (1) 302 to 169.254.169.254/loopback/RFC1918 or (2) DNS-rebind to a private address at connect time, leaking internal HTTP and cloud-metadata contents into the agent. Direct loopback URLs are blocked after the incomplete check, which is why the advisory's control vs redirect/rebind PoCs distinguish a genuine validate-then-fetch gap.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PraisonAI spider tools accept a user/LLM URL and fetch it with requests. After 3cd664bf7, scrape_page (and extract_links/crawl/extract_text, which call scrape_page) run SpiderTools._validate_url, later factored as _host_is_blocked. That gate only inspects the urlparse hostname as a literal: localhost/loopback aliases, dotted-decimal or hex/int IP parses, inet_aton, and suffixes such as .local/.internal. It never calls DNS. A public wildcard name such as 127.0.0.1.nip.io or 169-254-169-254.sslip.io therefore returns not-blocked, _validate_url returns True, and session.get is issued; the HTTP client then resolves the name to loopback/private/link-local and returns internal content (including cloud IMDS). 004dcfef closed parser-smuggling of IP literals but left this DNS gap; 2f9677abb closes it by resolving with getaddrinfo and fail-closing on DNS errors.

mechanism.counterevidence: Whole-tree greps at the immediate parent 9b4cc1d4 return no hits for mcp_post, session_ttl, _cleanup_sessions or _cancelled_requests, and the new http_stream.py blob does not exist anywhere in the parent tree, so the pattern was not moved in from another path. The older praisonaiagents/mcp/mcp_http_stream.py HTTPStreamTransport is the client-side transport (it calls session.initialize() and logs 'Session expired (HTTP 404)') with no server-side session store. The fix parent 9991e00f still contains the uncapped insert, so the defect was live through v4.6.57.
mechanism.impact: Unbounded memory growth that exhausts the server process and ends in an OOM kill, i.e. denial of service of the MCP HTTP server; availability-only impact (CVSS 3.1 6.5, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H, CWE-400 and CWE-770).
mechanism.preconditions: The HTTP-stream transport must be running and reachable by the attacker (direct routable bind, or a victim browser through the separate Origin-validation gap); default configuration carries no API key, so the Origin check is the only gate and it allows requests without an Origin header.
mechanism.summary: An unauthenticated caller can POST repeated initialize requests to the MCP HTTP-stream server; each one stores a new entry in self._sessions while _cleanup_sessions is never invoked and session_ttl (3600 s default) is never enforced on the write path, so the dict grows monotonically until the process is OOM-killed. The same unbounded-growth pattern applies to self._cancelled_requests, which is added to on every notifications/cancelled notification but never pruned.
mechanism.trigger: Repeated JSON-RPC initialize requests to the MCP HTTP endpoint, each creating a session dictionary that is never reclaimed; the endpoint is unauthenticated by default (api_key defaults to None) and initialize requires no prior session. Repeated notifications/cancelled notifications drive the second path. The advisory notes the Origin check is the only gate, allows a missing Origin header, and is separately bypassable by a startswith flaw (companion report), so a malicious web page can also reach it.

The advisory is a real CWE-400: initialize writes unbounded in-memory sessions while the TTL helper is dead code, and cancelled-request IDs accumulate without a cap. The smallest first-writer of those lines is 985a6122; its parent tree lacks the files, grafted later roots only re-expose the same blob, and no public PR members split the landing. The minimum repair is the session cleanup/cap plus cancelled-set bound in 2f9677a, which is the first-parent predecessor of tag v4.6.58 and is absent from v4.6.57. AI attribution is taken only from the BIC commit object: named human Mervin Praison with no AI trailer, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Cursor co-authorship on the fix does not change BIC-side attribution.
The advisory names two unbounded-growth paths in the new PraisonAI MCP server, and both are confirmed in the code: mcp_post appends a session on every initialize POST while _cleanup_sessions has no call site anywhere in the tree, and handle_message adds every notifications/cancelled requestId to a set that is never pruned. The earliest reachable occurrence is the single-parent commit 985a612273df078a87fae69e9f4004efe708669f ('Release v2.7.7', 2025-12-30), whose immediate parent 9b4cc1d4720795310b25690e3d7fce8eb841d5b5 contains none of mcp_post, session_ttl, _cleanup_sessions or _cancelled_requests anywhere in its tree and does not contain the new file blob, so this is an introduction rather than a move. The BIC object carries no AI evidence: author and committer are the named maintainer Mervin Praison, the full message is the subject 'Release v2.7.7' with no trailers, and the 40 preceding first-parent commits are all his. The upstream fix 2f9677abb2ea68eab864ee8b6a828fd0141612e1 (ancestor of tag v4.6.58, absent from v4.6.57) caps sessions through PRAISONAI_MCP_MAX_SESSIONS, wires session cleanup into every POST, and bounds the cancelled-requests set, closing both mechanisms. causal_research.remaining_gap: Three limits, none of which change the verdict: (1) no live end-to-end OOM reproduction was run because the audit environment cannot import the server runtime dependencies (starlette/httpx), so the mechanism rests on static call-site/control-flow evidence plus the advisory observation, and the advisory PoC script was not executed; (2) BIC minimality is limited to the file-pair additions inside the aggregate 'Release v2.7.7' commit because the shallow clone does not expose pre-release branch commits; (3) the cancelled-requests cap evicts with set.pop() (arbitrary, not age-ordered) and session cleanup runs only on POST, both asserted from source only, without runtime exercise of the 1000-session cap or the eviction path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PraisonAI MCP HTTP Stream transport (_validate_origin in src/praisonai/praisonai/mcp_server/transports/http_stream.py) treated an Origin header as trusted if it equaled or started with an allowlisted origin. With the default localhost bind, allowed_origins included the bare prefix http://localhost, so a browser Origin such as http://localhost.evil.example passed the DNS-rebinding-style check. The CLI default --api-key None skipped Bearer authentication, then POST /mcp parsed JSON-RPC and MCPServer._handle_tools_call invoked registered tools with attacker-controlled arguments, including praisonai.files.create (local file open) and praisonai.todo.add (write ~/.praison/todo.json). Default bind is 127.0.0.1, so the attack is browser-mediated against a local unauthenticated server.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In ALSA USB-audio implicit-feedback playback, snd_usb_handle_sync_urb() (sound/usb/endpoint.c) converts each inbound isochronous packet's actual_length into a playback frame count by dividing by the sync-source (sender) stride and writes that value straight into out_packet->packet_size[i] with no min() against ep->maxframesize. A connected USB audio device fully controls those IN packet lengths. Because playback then multiplies the stored frame count by the (often larger) playback stride, an oversized capture packet becomes an even larger outbound packet. The unclamped sizes are enqueued and memcpy'd into ctx->packet_size by snd_usb_queue_pending_output_urbs(), then consumed by prepare_playback_urb() (sound/usb/pcm.c) and prepare_silent_urb() to set urb->iso_frame_desc[].length and to memset/copy into the URB DMA buffer allocated as maxsize * packets. Before the Feb 2026 consumer-side cap, that produced URB submissions past the endpoint's hardware frame/packet limit and out-of-bounds writes into kernel-coherent USB buffers (C/I/A high via local USB gadget). The 2026-07-28 fix clamps the computed frame count at the store site in snd_usb_handle_sync_urb().

causal_research.bug_semantics: sch_teql keeps a circular singly linked list of slave qdiscs in teql_master->slaves / teql_sched_data->next. teql_qdisc_init() inserts, teql_destroy() unlinks, teql_master_xmit() rotates the head after a successful slave xmit or neighbour resolve, and teql_dequeue() also rewrites the head, all as plain pointer stores with no list lock and no RCU accessors. Concurrent RTM_NEWQDISC/RTM_DELQDISC on slaves (CAP_NET_ADMIN, including a user/netns) races with teql0 transmit: teql_destroy() can unlink a Qdisc that teql_master_xmit() still holds, the object is then freed after the qdisc RCU grace period, and the xmit walk (not in an RCU-bh read-side section covering that list) dereferences the stale pointer. KASAN: slab-use-after-free read of size 8 in teql_master_xmit of a freed kmalloc-512 qdisc. Attack path is local rtnetlink qdisc churn plus packet injection through teql0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: irdma_copy_user_pgaddrs walks every ib_umem DMA block and writes each address through *pbl, advancing the pointer with irdma_next_pbl_addr. The only explicit cap is if (++pbl_cnt == palloc->total_cnt) break. irdma_setup_pbles with lvl/use_pbles==0 skips irdma_get_pble, leaves the kzalloc-zeroed palloc->total_cnt at 0, and aims pbl at the 4-slot iwmr->pgaddrmem array (IRDMA_MAX_SAVED_PHY_PGADDR). Because pbl_cnt is pre-incremented from 0, it never equals total_cnt==0, so the loop continues until the umem is exhausted and writes attacker-controlled DMA addresses past pgaddrmem[4] into adjacent irdma_mr/iwpbl heap fields. For QP/CQ/SRQ, lvl is derived from a separate udata field (e.g. req.cq_pages > 1), so a local uverbs irdma_reg_user_mr caller can request the lvl==0 path while supplying a umem with more DMA blocks than the 4-entry array.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In Traefik's Kubernetes CRD provider, configBuilder.nameAndService (pkg/provider/kubernetes/crd/kubernetes_http.go) is the service-resolver for IngressRoute/TraefikService backendRefs. After the BIC, names without '@' still DeepCopy, fill Namespace from the parent, and reject via isNamespaceAllowed(allowCrossNamespace, parentNs, service.Namespace). Names containing providerNamespaceSeparator ('@') skip that entire branch. The only remaining gate is isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed(crossProviderNamespaces, parentNs), which returns true when the allowlist is nil (the default). Sibling resolvers (Provider.resolveReference for middlewares/TLS options; makeServersTransportKey for HTTP ServersTransport) already reject strings.HasSuffix(name, '@'+providerName) when allowCrossNamespace is false; nameAndService never did. A tenant confined to namespace attacker can therefore set services: [{name: '<victim-ns>-<svc>@kubernetescrd', kind: TraefikService}]. fullServiceName then splitSvcNameProvider-s the suffix, takes the pName==providerName (kubernetescrd) arm, and returns provider.Normalize(fmt.Sprintf('%s-%s', service.Namespace, name)). Because Namespace was never filled, service.Namespace is empty, so Normalize strips the leading hyphen and yields the victim TraefikService id ('<victim-ns>-<svc>'). causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-770 HTTP/2 connection-window starvation: when a stream's response body outruns the connection send window (default 65,535 bytes, shared across streams), Bandit.HTTP2.Connection queues the remaining bytes plus a reply closure in pending_sends and the stream/Plug process blocks forever inside GenServer.call(..., :infinity) to the connection process. The queue drains only on connection-level WINDOW_UPDATE/SETTINGS; nothing bounds the wait and nothing purges the queue. A client RST_STREAM is delivered to the blocked stream's mailbox but is never read while stuck in the call, so cancel frees nothing; periodic PINGs keep the transport read timeout from firing. Each stalled stream pins its process, Plug state, and any resource held across the write (e.g. a pooled upstream connection). Stream-window waits were later bounded at 15s; the connection-window path was not. Affects bandit 0.3.4 through 1.12.4.

causal_research.bug_semantics: selinux_sctp_bind_connect() is the SELinux implementation of security_sctp_bind_connect(). From its first write it copies sk->sk_socket into a struct socket * and passes that pointer into selinux_socket_bind() and selinux_socket_connect_helper(), which immediately load sock->sk and never otherwise need the socket object. SCTP Dynamic Address Reconfiguration (ASCONF ADD_IP/SET_PRIMARY) invokes the same hook from net/sctp/sm_make_chunk.c on asoc->ep->base.sk in the receive/softirq path. After userspace close(), sk->sk_socket can already be NULL while associations still process authenticated ASCONF chunks, so the SELinux hook NULL-dereferences sk_socket and oopses/panics the host. setsockopt bindx/connectx/set_primary and sendmsg-connect hold a file reference and are not the crashing path. The 2026 fix stops touching sk_socket by teaching the bind/connect helpers to take struct sock * directly.

causal_research.bug_semantics: AF_PACKET mmap RX-ring teardown races with poll/recvmsg pressure clearing. packet_set_ring() updates rx_ring.pg_vec and related ring fields under sk_receive_queue.lock, then historically published tpacket vs non-tpacket receive mode by writing po->prot_hook.func after releasing that lock. packet_poll() (already holding the queue lock) and packet_recvmsg() consult prot_hook.func to decide whether __packet_rcv_has_room() should walk the tpacket ring. In the window after the ring has been swapped to NULL/freed but before the hook is switched off tpacket_rcv, those paths still take the tpacket branch and dereference stale or NULL pg_vec / prb_bdqc block storage (NULL deref or UAF). The attacker controls both sides via local PACKET_RX_RING reconfiguration versus poll/recvmsg while PACKET_SOCK_PRESSURE is set.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker-controlled account value can be reflected by the REST error path in ExceptionMessage and the JSON response body. The account_rse_usage WebUI error callbacks passed the raw jqXHR.responseText through string concatenation to jQuery.html(), so the victim's browser parsed payload markup such as an img onerror handler in the Rucio WebUI origin instead of displaying it as text. A crafted link therefore executes script when an authenticated user opens it, exposing the WebUI token/session and permitting actions with the victim's authority.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-59 link following in Git LFS working-tree population: git lfs checkout and git lfs pull (and, in 0.5.2–0.5.x, git lfs fetch/get when the fetched ref was HEAD) opened the destination path with Go os.Create, which dereferences a terminal symlink and truncates an existing hard-linked inode. A colliding symlink or hard link at an LFS-tracked path therefore caused LFS object bytes to be written to an attacker-chosen location the user can access, including outside the work tree. A later MkdirAll on the parent path also traversed intermediate directory symlinks, and a bare-repo path-join bug (empty LocalWorkingDir joined with strings.Join, producing /<repo-relative-path> then filepath.Rel) could write outside a bare repository. Git's smudge filter path was not the issue: it writes to stdout and Git creates the file.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In the rtl2832_sdr V4L2 SDR driver, vb2 delivers capture buffers to rtl2832_sdr_buf_queue() (list_add_tail onto dev->queued_bufs) before it calls rtl2832_sdr_start_streaming(). That start callback can fail on missing USB device (-ENODEV), interrupted v4l2_lock (-ERESTARTSYS), or any of six setup steps (subdev s_power/tuner, tuner frequency, ADC, stream-buffer alloc, URB alloc, URB submit). Those paths returned the error without vb2_buffer_done() on the already-owned queued buffers, so vb2_start_streaming() hits WARN_ON(owned_by_drv_count), the buffers leak, and later URB completion or buf_queue list_add_tail can operate on freed vb2 objects (local ioctl UAF). The original function also fell through a shared err label on success, so cleanup could not be added there without an explicit success return.

causal_research.bug_semantics: AF_QIPCRTR (QRTR) is a datagram protocol to global modem/remote-processor endpoints. Socket creation (qrtr_create) accepted any network namespace while port/node tables (qrtr_local_nid and qrtr_ports) were module-global and used by lookup/enqueue with no netns check. An unprivileged process in a new user+net namespace could therefore send QRTR datagrams, including control-plane NEW_SERVER/BYE, that init_net sockets and the in-kernel nameservice treated as local node-1 traffic, breaking netns isolation. The 2026 fix rejects qrtr_create() outside init_net with -EAFNOSUPPORT.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DNSIncoming._decode_labels_at_offset recurses once per RFC 1035 §4.1.4 DNS-name compression pointer. Cycle detection (seen_pointers) and MAX_DNS_LABELS=128 capped repeated offsets and label count, but a chain of unique forward pointers that add no extra labels was unbounded. A single ~3 kB mDNS datagram with ~1500 such pointers exceeds CPython's default recursion limit. DECODE_EXCEPTIONS was (IndexError, struct.error, IncomingDecodeError) and omitted RecursionError, so the exception escaped DNSIncoming.__init__ to asyncio's default handler. Any unauthenticated host on the local link (UDP/5353, 224.0.0.251 / ff02::fb) can force sustained CPU burn and log flooding.

causal_research.bug_semantics: After granular PM, an async UVC control's extra uvc_pm_get can be the last status_users reference. When the status interrupt queues async_ctrl.work, uvc_ctrl_status_event_work clears that handle and uvc_pm_put drops status_users to zero, so uvc_status_stop runs on the same work item and cancel_work_sync waits for itself. Impact is a kernel deadlock (DoS) on a camera that implements asynchronous controls; preconditions are that control pending, not streaming (or otherwise holding another PM ref), and a status-endpoint value-change event.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked whether the deadlock predates a32d9c41bdb8: in the parent, an open /dev/videoN holds uvc_pm_get() for the fd lifetime (uvc_v4l2.c:671) and uvc_v4l2_release() runs uvc_ctrl_cleanup_fh(handle) - which clears pending async control handles and puts their pm references (uvc_ctrl.c:3237-3256) - while the fd reference is still held and only drops it at :710, so the work's uvc_pm_put() can never observe status_users == 1 there. Checked the neighbouring unregister-path fixes c5fe3ed618f9 and a67f75c2b5ec (uvc_status_suspend in uvc_status_unregister and the dev->status guard): both are process-context paths, not work context, and neither touches the refcount floor. Checked remaining uvc_pm_put() call sites in uvc_v4l2.c (ioctl bodies and the DEFINE_FREE cleanup at :1384) - all run in ioctl/process context, so uvc_ctrl_clear_handle() from the work is the only work-context route into uvc_status_stop().
mechanism.impact: Hard deadlock in a kernel workqueue thread: cancel_work_sync() blocks until the currently executing work item completes, which cannot happen because that work item is the caller. The uvcvideo status/control pipeline stops and anything serialized behind the work (including tasks touching the same control mutex or waiting on the status URB) hangs: a local denial of service triggered by opening a UVC device and exercising an asynchronous control.
mechanism.preconditions: A UVC device with an asynchronous control and a reachable state where the async control's pm reference is the last outstanding one when its status event is processed (after a32d9c41bdb8 no file handle pins the status pipe, e.g. streaming stopped or the fd closed); requires the async_ctrl work to be the active work item so current_work() == &w->work in the unpatched code. Physical or emulated (v4l2-loopback/vhci-style) UVC hardware is needed to drive the status endpoint.
mechanism.summary: An asynchronous uvcvideo control event is processed by the status workqueue: uvc_ctrl_status_event_work() -> uvc_ctrl_status_event() -> uvc_ctrl_clear_handle() -> uvc_pm_put() -> uvc_status_put(); when the async control's own reference is the last one, uvc_status_put() calls uvc_status_stop(), whose cancel_work_sync(&w->work) waits for the very work item that is running, so the workqueue thread deadlocks and the uvc status pipeline hangs.
mechanism.trigger: A UVC device that has an asynchronous control: userspace sets the control via ioctl (uvc_ctrl_set_handle() takes uvc_pm_get(), uvc_ctrl.c:2118) and the device later reports the change through the status URB, whose completion queues async_ctrl.work; the work runs when no other pm/status reference is outstanding, so its own uvc_pm_put() drives status_users to 0.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: drivers/media/usb/uvc/uvc_status.c:322 uvc_status_stop() (cancel_work_sync(&w->work) at :343 and :355) called from uvc_status_put() at :403-408, plus drivers/media/usb/uvc/uvc_ctrl.c:2137 uvc_ctrl_clear_handle() and :2142 uvc_ctrl_status_event() at 940f161f734b25f175a95d2684c2021f6323693a

The advisory is a real kernel deadlock, not withdrawn. The smallest original introducing change is a32d9c41: it is the first commit whose parent lacks the reachable last-user uvc_status_stop-from-work path. The BIC commit object is named-human Ricardo Ribalda with no AI authorship or co-authorship markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI. The minimum repair is mainline 6d27f92 (current_work early return); fix-side AI is absent and does not affect the verdict.
The advisory describes a self-deadlock in uvcvideo: the asynchronous status work calls uvc_ctrl_clear_handle() -> uvc_pm_put() -> uvc_status_put(), which at status_users == 1 reaches uvc_status_stop() and calls cancel_work_sync() on the work item that is currently executing. causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan disassembles pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL references and, in the default scan result, counts a finding only when the referenced module/name matches its hard-coded unsafe-globals blocklist. Through v0.0.34 the blocklist omitted both the serialized global _io.FileIO and urllib.request.urlopen, so a crafted pickle could open an arbitrary local file and pass that file object as the body of an attacker-directed HTTP request without either global being counted as dangerous. A consumer relying on the scan could then deserialize the payload, causing arbitrary file read plus SSRF/data exfiltration.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The initial scanner implementation introduced the incomplete-denylist security model: src/picklescan/scanner.py enumerated selected suspicious globals and scan_pickle_bytes incremented issues_count only for exact blocklist matches, silently leaving unlisted callable globals such as _io.FileIO and urllib.request.urlopen outside the failing result. Later classification of unknown globals as Suspicious did not cure the default-pass behavior because only Dangerous globals incremented issues_count; the vulnerable mechanism therefore originates in the initial scanner commit rather than in a later refactor or blocklist expansion.

causal_research.evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/security/advisories/GHSA-9726-w42j-3qjr specifies affected versions <0.0.35, patched version 0.0.35, and the io.FileIO -> urllib.request.urlopen exfiltration chain. PR https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/pull/55 and release https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/releases/tag/v0.0.35 identify the remediation. In the validated clone, `git log -L 14,24:src/picklescan/scanner.py c1d5abd...` attributes the original suspicious-globals dictionary to c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e, and `git log -L 77,89:src/picklescan/scanner.py c1d5abd...` shows that same new-file commit introduced scan_pickle_bytes with exact blocklist lookup and issues_count increment only on a match. `git cat-file -e 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326:src/picklescan/scanner.py` fails because the path is absent, while `git ls-tree -r --name-only` for that parent shows no src tree, directly verifying parent absence. The BIC's setup.cfg reports version 0.0.1; `git describe --contains --tags` reports c1d5abd... is contained by v0.0.2~12, and `git merge-base c1d5abd... v0.0.34` returns c1d5abd..., proving the mechanism precedes the last vulnerable tag. At v0.0.34, src/picklescan/scanner.py:356-391 maps non-blocklisted globals to Suspicious but increments issues_count only for Dangerous entries, and its unsafe table at lines 110-186 contains neither _io.FileIO nor urllib.request. `git log -S` for both `"_io": {"FileIO"}` and `"urllib.request": "*"` finds only a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1. That commit adds both unsafe entries plus regression pickles/tests and changes setup.cfg 0.0.34 -> 0.0.35; v0.0.34 resolves to its immediate parent 323bd004691e442b109b00a1251cd9acc1a4be98, v0.0.35 resolves exactly to a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1, and `git describe --contains --tags a01c58d...` returns v0.0.35. Finally, `git cat-file -p c1d5abd...` supplies the human author/committer and trailer-free message quoted in ai_marker.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is a scanner-detection bypass, not execution performed by picklescan itself: the scanner exposes pickle globals, but its default failing result is driven by a finite dangerous-global dictionary. The advisory's payload serializes io.FileIO as _io.FileIO to open a local file and then invokes urllib.request.urlopen with that file as an iterable request body, so omitting both globals permits the malicious pickle to avoid a Dangerous finding and creates the unsafe trust decision before downstream unpickling. History tracing distinguishes the true origin from later churn: f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9 merely renamed _suspicious_globals to _unsafe_globals during PyTorch work, whereas c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e created both the finite blocklist and exact-match reporting logic in one direct, single-parent implementation commit. Its immediate parent has no scanner source at all, so the vulnerable mechanism is directly absent there; no squash/member decomposition or move is needed. The BIC shipped in the initial 0.0.1 code and is ancestral to v0.0.34, while the direct fix a01c58d5dd7960db557b849817c0ab83ab111ef1 is exactly tag v0.0.35 and adds the two missing dangerous globals. AI attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it has human author and committer identities, a plain one-line message, and no AI/co-author/generated trailers. Therefore the proven smallest BIC is human-authored and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A remote ActivityPub Create/Note can supply an Emoji tag whose icon.url and name are attacker-controlled. NodeBB converted a matching shortcode into an img element by interpolating those values into quoted HTML attributes after the original note content had already been sanitized, then stored the generated HTML. Remote-post rendering could bypass markdown/sanitize-html, so an attribute breakout in the generated markup became persistent same-origin JavaScript for viewers.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 introduced incoming ActivityPub emoji expansion in src/posts/create.js before database storage and first wrote the causal unescaped sink, interpolating tag.icon.url directly into img src. Commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 added the unescaped title attribute from tag.name one day later. Commit 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3 later moved/generalized the existing mechanism as Helpers.renderEmoji; it is a refactor, not the BIC.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names author and committer Julian Lam <julian@nodebb.org>, contains only the message 'feat: #12683, parse incoming emoji tags and replace in content prior to storage in database', has no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and uses no bot identity.

Version checks: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 09b1e119^` returns v4.0.0-beta.4, while `git describe --tags --contains 09b1e119` returns v4.0.0-rc.1~32 and tags containing the BIC begin at v4.0.0-rc.1/v4.0.0. The URL-validation guard is absent from v4.14.10 (`git grep` has no match) and present at v4.15.0:src/activitypub/helpers.js:592. The advisory's direct patch c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e adds `if (!Helpers.isUri(tag.icon.url)) return;`; its equivalent branch cherry-pick 7da65694f9934e6f36be0a7f732b22ebc195c6d8 and c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e are both ancestors of release tag v4.15.0 (fbdbb00d01e01a92baf64534a05fd13685cf3d88). causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability begins when 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 makes untrusted ActivityPub emoji metadata executable HTML state: it inserts tag.icon.url into an img attribute and does so before the post is persisted. The direct parent copies content to postData and stores it without any emoji-tag HTML generation, proving immediate-parent absence. causal_research.mechanism: The coordinated LPM-tree update serves route-node link and unlink. Used VRs sharing a protocol tree are rebound through RALTB register writes. If earlier VRs move to the new tree and a later bind fails, i decrements while vr still names the failed VR. That failed VR keeps its old tree in the introducing implementation, or restores it in the repair-parent implementation; its test for new_id therefore normally fails on every reverse iteration. Earlier VRs keep unintended, still-reachable new-tree references and rollback is incomplete. Spectrum hardware/driver, relevant multi-VR/FIB state, a prefix-set change, partial progress and a binding failure are prerequisites. Administrative rtnetlink mutation requires CAP_NET_ADMIN in the relevant network namespace; no attacker-controlled hardware failure, ordinary unprivileged remote path, measured DoS or permanent unreachable leak is proved.
causal_research.cause: Route-node link/unlink -> collective LPM tree replacement -> partial forward success plus binding error -> stale VR pointer in unwind -> earlier VR-held references not returned as intended.

Zero progress leaves no prior VRs to restore; unchanged prefix sets may avoid replacement. Those contrary observations narrow impact without refuting the defect.

causal_research.bug_semantics: FRR bgpd process_type2_route in bgpd/bgp_evpn.c accepts an EVPN Type-2 NLRI whose overall length psize is one of {33,36,37,40,49,52} and whose inner IP-length field is independently 0, 32, or 128, without requiring psize == 33+(ipaddr_len/8) or psize == 36+(ipaddr_len/8). A remote EVPN BGP speaker can therefore present a legal total length while declaring a mismatched IP length so that IP octets are consumed as MPLS/VNI labels or leftover bytes are treated as a second VNI, installing a MAC-IP route with the wrong IP and/or VNI. After the 2020 STREAM_GET conversion, over-reads fail closed, but the inconsistent-length path still yields a wrongly decoded route rather than a reject. CVE-2026-5107/VulDB label this CWE-266/CWE-284; the concrete flaw is missing NLRI-length vs IP-length cross-validation in Type-2 parsing.
