causal_research.bug_semantics: The manage-downloads admin deletion handler accepted attacker-controlled POST fields `file` and `file_name` independently of the integer `file_id`; when `unlinkfile=1`, it concatenated the configured download directory with `file` and passed the result to `unlink()`. Neither the original `trim()` nor the later `sanitize_text_field()` removes `../` segments or proves containment, so an authenticated administrator holding the normal delete nonce could alter the hidden `file` field and delete an arbitrary server file outside the download directory. Deleting a critical file such as wp-config.php can cause denial of service and can enable follow-on site compromise/RCE.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable trust boundary was present in the first public upstream source revision, WordPress Plugin SVN r7446 (2007-01-21): `trunk/downloadmanager/download-manager.php` read `$_POST['file']` and used it in `unlink($file_path.'/'.$file)` rather than deriving the path from the database row selected by `file_id`. Later renames, SVN-to-Git deployment, sanitization, and formatting preserved that mechanism. Git commit d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208 fixed the root cause by accepting only `file_id`, reloading the downloads-table row, and unlinking the stored `$file->file` value.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated Jolokia exec of BrokerView.addNetworkConnector(String)/addConnector(String) accepts discovery URIs. CVE-2026-34197 added a scheme deny-list (vm, later other transports) in BrokerView.validateAllowedUrl/validateAllowedUri, but nested-component inspection is gated on URISupport.isCompositeURI(), which is true only when the scheme-specific part starts with '('. Discovery wrappers such as static: and masterslave: also accept non-parenthesized forms (static:vm://..., masterslave:vm://...,...); URISupport.parseComposite still splits those into inner URIs. The inner vm://...?brokerConfig=xbean:... therefore skips the deny-list, reaches VMTransportFactory, and loads attacker-controlled Spring XML via ResourceXmlApplicationContext before BrokerService validation, yielding RCE (CWE-20/CWE-94). Patched by always calling parseComposite so missing parentheses are walked the same way transports construct the objects.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Traefik Kubernetes Gateway provider option crossProviderNamespaces is documented as allowing only listed Gateway API route namespaces to declare TraefikService backendRefs such as api@internal, dashboard@internal, or rest@internal. For HTTPRoute rules with a single internal backend, the provider correctly checks route.Namespace. For mixed/WRR rules, loadService overwrites namespace from backendRef.Namespace (legitimate for core Service lookup and ReferenceGrant) and then loadHTTPBackendRef runs isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed against that target namespace. An HTTPRoute in a non-allow-listed namespace can therefore add an @internal TraefikService to the generated WRR graph by setting backendRef.namespace to an allow-listed namespace that has issued a Gateway API ReferenceGrant, exposing the dashboard/API on the data plane without changing Traefik static config or RBAC.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When a broker has a network connector with syncDurableSubs=true, TransportConnection.processBrokerInfo() treats an inbound OpenWire BrokerInfo (networkConnection=true) as a durable-sync request and immediately dispatchSync()s a BrokerSubscriptionInfo that enumerates every durable topic subscription on the broker (copied ConsumerInfo: clientId, subscriptionName, destination, JMS selector). That reply is sent as soon as BrokerInfo is processed, before ConnectionInfo is run through broker.addConnection() and the authentication plugin chain. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the OpenWire port therefore spoofs a network-bridge BrokerInfo and receives the full durable-subscription metadata set.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Yggdrasil exports com.redhat.Yggdrasil1.Dispatch() on the system bus and forwards the caller's directive, message id, metadata, and payload to a named worker (including package-manager workers that can add repos and install/remove RPMs). The installed D-Bus busconfig used <policy context="default"> with <allow send_destination="com.redhat.Yggdrasil1"/>, so any local uid could send to that destination, and Dispatch itself took no dbus.Sender argument and performed no uid/authorization check (unlike Dispatcher.Transmit). A local unprivileged user could therefore force a privileged worker to install arbitrary packages, yielding LPE (CWE-280).

causal_research.flaw_origin: Not a product introduction. The prefix deny-unless-under-base-path check already existed in editor::edit before the named 21.5_20250307 tag (present in 2023 sources such as 99f54fc; 94924d1 only adjusted realpath/false handling). The public report misstates that check.

mechanism.counterevidence: Three falsification attempts, all supporting the verdict: (1) operator check - the guard is !== 0 (reject), not == 0, at 21.5 and at HEAD; (2) realpath interplay - realpath('phar:///etc/passwd') is false for a non-existent archive, so the original wrapper string is what reaches the unchanged guard; (3) alternate read paths - edit()'s only direct read is gated by file_exists() plus extendOther, editorZen::buildContentByAction() reads only for edit/override under file_exists(), and helper::safe64Decode() is a plain base64_decode(strtr($s, '.', '/')) that cannot inject a base-path prefix. No wrapper-prefixed path can satisfy strpos(path, basePath) === 0. Checked statically against the pinned tag (this host has no PHP CLI, so no live request was run); the rejection follows from the documented strpos contract - false when the needle is absent, and false !== 0 returns editFileError - not from a runtime outcome. The report itself publishes no response body or PoC output: its only artefact is dists/zentaopms_phar.png, an IDE screenshot of the source with the file_exists/file_get_contents lines boxed.
mechanism.impact: As described by the advisory: arbitrary file read and phar-metadata deserialization. In the reported version: none - the request returns the editor editFileError response before any filesystem function runs, and the reads that remain reachable are confined to existing paths inside the application base path.
mechanism.preconditions: A session able to reach m=editor. For any read form to be considered at all, filePath must decode to an existing path that also begins with the app base path, and the action must be extendOther (control.php:80) or edit/override (zen.php buildContentByAction), not the action=edit of the exploit URL.
mechanism.summary: Claimed: a request to index.php?m=editor&f=edit with base64 phar:///etc/passwd in filePath bypasses the base-path check in editor::edit() and reaches file_get_contents(), giving arbitrary file read and phar-metadata deserialization in ZenTao 21.5_20250307. Actual: the strict strpos(...) !== 0 guard on line 79 returns editFileError for any wrapper-prefixed path, and every read additionally requires file_exists() plus the extendOther/edit/override action, so the payload terminates in an error response with no file access.
mechanism.trigger: GET/POST /index.php?m=editor&f=edit&filePath=cGhhcjovLy9ldGMvcGFzc3dk&action=edit (base64 decodes to phar:///etc/passwd) from a session that can reach the editor module (the advisory's own CVSS rates PR:L).
mechanism.vulnerable_code: module/editor/control.php:79-80 editor::edit() at tag zentaopms_21.5_20250307 (commit f33027b762cd7a187d661cfb15f0c3fcc5291317; same lines at upstream HEAD ab2efdde9fb7d9b3434b37fca4d61216750ee4af). Line 79 is the deciding guard; line 80 is the file_get_contents() the advisory calls vulnerable, reachable only under $action == 'extendOther' and file_exists($filePath). The advisory's quoted snippet and the tagged tree are statement-for-statement identical over lines 69-80.

causal_research.reasoning:
CVE.org is PUBLISHED and GHSA is not withdrawn, so this is not a withdrawn-ID FP. The first-party product code for the exact named tag still falsifies the advisory: Edit() allowlists paths that start with the app filesystem root and returns fail otherwise, so the disclosed phar:///etc/passwd PoC cannot reach the highlighted file_exists/file_get_contents calls or read /etc/passwd. The reporter's bypass rationale is the logical inverse of that check. Remaining PHAR-deserial stories require a planted archive plus a filesystem function that actually opens phar://; that is not the published PoC, and realpath is not a documented trigger. Therefore the advisory is wrong. A later unrelated delete() path-traversal fix on main does not rehabilitate this CVE. No BIC or AI attribution.
The advisory quotes code that rejects the payload it uses, so it is a false positive. In module/editor/control.php at tag zentaopms_21.5_20250307 (commit f33027b762cd7a187d661cfb15f0c3fcc5291317) editor::edit() decodes filePath and then returns editFileError for every path that does not begin with the application base path (strpos(...) !== 0, line 79); the string phar:///etc/passwd can never begin with that base path, so the wrapper never reaches a file function. The report's inference that wrappers 'bypass this check since they don't start with the application base path' inverts the operator: !== 0 is exactly the rejection case. The read the report points at is gated twice more - if($action == 'extendOther' and file_exists($filePath)) file_get_contents($filePath) at line 80, and editorZen::buildContentByAction() reading only when ($action == 'edit' or $action == 'override') && file_exists($filePath) - so the reported action=edit URL cannot read anything, and file_exists('phar:///etc/passwd') is false because no such archive exists. The guard has been present since 2017-10-25 (04528419bd3c35a2a21d121a93c8f6487805904c) and is unchanged in operator form at upstream HEAD ab2efdde9fb7d9b3434b37fca4d61216750ee4af (22.5); no upstream change ever made a wrapper-prefixed path pass it.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SAML 2.0 HTTP-Redirect binding payloads (login SAMLResponse or logout SAMLRequest) are Base64-decoded then inflated through java.util.zip.InflaterOutputStream into an unbounded ByteArrayOutputStream. An unauthenticated attacker can send a small DEFLATE bomb on a GET to the ACS or SLO endpoint; the inflater writes without a size cap and can exhaust heap (CWE-400 DoS). POST binding skips inflate and is not this bug. The 2026 fix wraps the writer in CappedOutputStream (1 MiB) and, for login, also recommends OpenSaml5AuthenticationTokenConverter#setShouldConvertGetRequests(false).

causal_research.bug_semantics: OliveTin registered local-auth SIDs in server-side SessionStorage for about one year and authenticated requests that replayed the olivetin-sid-local cookie. Its implemented Logout flow expired only the browser cookie and did not delete the corresponding SID, so a copied pre-logout cookie remained accepted after the user appeared to log out; the eventual fix also revoked OAuth2's separate server-side state.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 8686a5629e6a8fae3d99f2af0a3e8c3c0c37aae0 is the smallest real BIC because it first implemented the advisory's exact vulnerable behavior: its new UI called Logout, and its Logout RPC returned an expired olivetin-sid-local cookie without revoking the already-authenticated provider/SID. The reviewer's earlier a7e7bf869ecbf87aa176337aac191e69bbcd90f9 added cookie-to-session authentication, but Logout at that tree was still a nonfunctional return-nil stub and did not clear a browser cookie; it supplied a prerequisite, not the post-logout bypass described by the advisory.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When CFG_WIDEVINE_PTA is enabled, core/pta/widevine.c:open_session() gates callers by UUID but unconditionally dereferences the calling session: ts_get_calling_session() is stored and is_user_ta_ctx(session->ctx) is invoked with no NULL test. A Normal World client that issues OPTEE_MSG_CMD_OPEN_SESSION directly on the Widevine pseudo-TA has no calling TA on the thread session stack, so ts_get_calling_session() returns NULL; the session->ctx load faults at S-EL1 and panics the TEE (CWE-476 DoS). causal_research.bug_semantics: The standard HR employee-create form collected an email and employee details but no password, while EmployeeSaveController::save() assigned bcrypt($request->input('password', 'changeme')). Consequently, every employee created through that product flow received the same predictable literal credential. The created record was App\Models\User, an Illuminate Authenticatable model used by the normal login path, so a remote attacker who knew an onboarded employee's email could log in as that employee with changeme; no first-login change or reset step invalidated the credential.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SoupServer handle_partial_get() honors a request Range by slicing the accumulated response body with g_bytes_new_from_bytes(full_response, ranges[i].start, ranges[i].end - ranges[i].start + 1). soup_message_headers_get_ranges_internal() treated a range as unsatisfiable only when cur.start >= total_length; a valid start with cur.end past the body was still returned as 206 Partial Content. GLib g_bytes_new_from_bytes() bounds checks are compiled out under G_DISABLE_CHECKS, so the oversized slice can read and return heap past the intended body (CWE-125). The same unbounded slice existed earlier via soup_buffer_new_subbuffer(), which performed no length check at all.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-2443 state=PUBLISHED (CNA Red Hat, not rejected/withdrawn); NVD vulnStatus=Modified; GHSA-hg24-p7xv-jhq8 withdrawn_at=null. Issue https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libsoup/-/issues/487 (closed): handle_partial_get() + g_bytes_new_from_bytes() with unvalidated Range end; G_DISABLE_CHECKS heap leak. RHBZ#2439671 / access.redhat.com confirm CWE-125 in handle_partial_get().

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user able to create and run workflows could supply the Git node with a staged working repository whose configured push remote was another attacker-controlled local repository. For push and pushTags, vulnerable releases left Git's file transport enabled, causing local git-receive-pack to run receive-side hooks in the target repository as the n8n process. Setting core.hooksPath=/dev/null on the initiating repository did not suppress hooks in that local receive target. The fix validates configured remotes and removes file from GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL for write operations when hooks are disabled.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The original Git node accepted a workflow-selected baseDirectory, constructed simple-git for that repository, and exposed git.push() without restricting repository-controlled local remote targets or Git's file transport. That original trust-boundary crossing, rather than a later move, import, refactor, or aggregate landing, is the flaw origin.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A remote unauthenticated ForwardOpen can supply a mixed-class CIP application path (Assembly as path1 plus a non-Assembly endpoint such as Identity instance 1 or Ethernet Link). check_path()/ResolveInstances() accept any existing class+instance and bind those objects as consuming/producing I/O endpoints; class 0/1 handling does not require kCipAssemblyClass. CipConnMgrClass::forward_open then dispatches via mgmnt_class (path1 Assembly) into CipAssemblyClass::OpenConnection -> OpenIO -> ConnectionData::CorrectSizes, which forces attribute 3 and casts instance data to ByteBuf*/CipByteArray. Identity attribute 3 is uint16_t product_code_ and Ethernet Link attribute 3 is a 6-byte MAC, so ByteBuf::size() (limit-start) reads off the true object (ASan global-buffer-overflow on product_code_, heap-buffer-overflow on physical_address) and aborts the POSIX sample server.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Tor conflux shares one conflux_t (cfx) across all legs of a set. linked_circuit_closed() removes a closing linked leg and, when it is the last remaining leg, deletes the cfx from the linked pool but deliberately leaves circ->conflux pointing at that still-alive object so linked_circuit_free() can free it later. A recovery leg for the same nonce (conflux_launch_leg -> unlinked_get_or_create) reuses that same cfx with is_for_linked_set. When the recovery leg later finishes linking (conflux_process_linked -> try_finalize_set -> cfx_add_leg), it re-adds the cfx to the linked pool and sets recovery->circ->conflux to it, creating two distinct circuits that both own the same object: the already-closed last original leg (not yet reaped) and the revived recovery leg. On post-loop reap, linked_circuit_free() on the first empty-legs circuit calls conflux_free(cfx); the second circuit then dereferences circ->conflux->legs (heap UAF) and would otherwise conflux_free again (double free). A malicious exit can drive link -> recover -> close last linked leg -> relink recovery -> close/reap to crash the client. CWE-911 / TROVE-2026-026 / bug 41306.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DNSCache._async_add stored every incoming mDNS response record under the lowercased name in cache, _expirations, _expire_heap, and (for DNSService) service_cache with no entry-count cap. RecordManager.async_updates_from_response feeds every non-expired answer from any UDP/5353 multicast packet (224.0.0.251 / ff02::fb) into that path. An unauthenticated LAN peer can flood unique names (RFC 6762 §11, up to 253 bytes) so the maps grow without bound; the only pre-existing controls were a PTR TTL floor (_DNS_PTR_MIN_TTL=1125s) that actually prolongs attacker records and async_expire every _CACHE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL=10s, which cannot keep up. Unique-name floods OOM memory-constrained consumers; a second variant replays cached records with shifting TTLs so _expire_heap grows between cleanups without changing cache/_total_records.

The CVE description and the CISA ADP record label it CWE-400 uncontrolled resource consumption, which is a mislabel: no resource is exhausted, the AMF panics and exits. HandleAuthenticationFailure reads ue.AuthenticationCtx.AuthType with no nil check, so a NAS AuthenticationFailure delivered while the AuthenticationCtx is still nil panics; the NGAP connection goroutine's deferred recover logs via Fatalf, which exits the AMF process.

causal_research.flaw_origin: Human (non-AI) origin: the AMF GMM failure handler dereferenced ue.AuthenticationCtx without a nil guard from the repository's initial import. The introducing object bc52451ce662dc700f7b574d4a1804726a64e472 is the amf repo root commit (2020-04-28, free5gc-org <free5gc.org@gmail.com>) and its tree already contains func HandleAuthenticationFailure with the unguarded ue.AuthenticationCtx.AuthType access, while the sibling func HandleAuthenticationResponse in the same file carries a nil guard. The window that makes the deref reachable (identity request sent, AUSF not yet called, AuthenticationCtx still nil) is in the same import.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party authoring disclosure bound to bc52451ce662dc700f7b574d4a1804726a64e472 (impossible for a 2020 import) or a reachable earlier object that carries the same unguarded deref would change the BIC; an AI-attributed object that either introduces the unguarded deref or is an attempted nil-hardening of this handler that leaves the deref reachable would flip the verdict to AI_ROOT_CAUSE or AI_CODE_FLAWED. Evidence that the crash is unreachable without an already-established security context, or a first-party advisory revision withdrawing the CVE, would flip the case to FALSE_POSITIVE.
causal_research.mechanism: Trigger: a UE/gNB establishes N2 and sends RegistrationRequest with a 5G-GUTI and no SUCI. AuthenticationProcedure (internal/gmm/handler.go:1632) takes the IdentityVerification false branch, sends IdentityRequest and returns false,nil at line 1646 without calling AUSF, so ue.AuthenticationCtx is still nil; it is only assigned at handler.go:1700 after the AUSF call. The AMF stays in the Authentication state, and the Authentication state's GmmMessageEvent dispatches nas.MsgTypeAuthenticationFailure straight to HandleAuthenticationFailure (internal/gmm/sm.go:212-215). Vulnerable code: internal/gmm/handler.go:2093 switch ue.AuthenticationCtx.AuthType dereferences nil. Impact: panic in the NGAP connection goroutine; internal/ngap/service/service.go handleConnection deferred recover calls Fatalf (comment: Fatalf() will let program exit), so the AMF process exits and N2/NAS service drops. Preconditions: an N2 connection and the ability to send NAS messages; no UE authentication completes, so it is pre-auth on the NAS layer, but it is not unauthenticated network access, the sender needs a gNB/N2 peer. Counterevidence: the reporter's repro uses a normal UE and UERANSIM, not a raw packet injection.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory names the AMF function HandleAuthenticationFailure and a remote DoS; the assigned clone carries the AMF only as a submodule gitlink, so the decisive evidence had to come from the submodule repository. Once there, the claim checks out end to end: line 2093 of the vulnerable release is exactly the deref the reporter's stack names, the Authentication state routes an AuthenticationFailure message to it with no context check, the identity-request branch leaves AuthenticationCtx nil, and the NGAP recover handler exits the process. The smallest object that carries the defect is the amf root import bc52451 (2020), where the same file already guards the sibling response handler, and the later root v1.0.0 re-imports the identical omission; nothing in between removed a guard, so no earlier or smaller change exists. Since the object that carries the defect is a 2020 human import with no authoring trailer, and the later lint reword and the eventual guard both have named human authors and empty bodies, the AI role is nil and the verdict is NOT_AI rather than EVIDENCE_GAP. The advisory's CWE-400 label and the 'remote attacker' phrasing are looser than the mechanism (a NULL deref reachable pre-authentication from an N2 peer), which is why the record states the precondition explicitly instead of treating the CVSS vector as proof.
causal_research.remaining_gap: None for the advisory's named surface: the unguarded deref in HandleAuthenticationFailure is guarded at every rev from a7bcfc9 through HEAD, and free5gc v4.2.2 (amf v1.4.3) is the first umbrella release that carries it, so the crash path the advisory names is closed. Two scope notes stay on the record: (a) the guard shipped one release later than the CVE text implies, since free5gc v4.2.1 still pins amf v1.4.2, the fix's parent; (b) the same class of unguarded nil dereference exists elsewhere in the AMF and was repaired separately, for example PR #222 (fix/uplink-ran-config-transfer-nil-deref, amf v1.4.5), which is outside this advisory and not part of its fix.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When providers.kubernetesCRD.allowCrossNamespace=false, Traefik rejects direct IngressRoute middleware refs that name another namespace, but createChainMiddleware still honors MiddlewareRef.namespace on spec.chain.middlewares[] and emits makeID(foreignNS, name) with no isNamespaceAllowed check. A principal who can write a local Chain CRD can therefore bind and apply another namespace's middleware (stripPrefix, headers, forwardAuth, etc.) onto routes in their own namespace, bypassing the documented CRD isolation boundary.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When SECURITY_REDIRECT_ALLOW_SUBDOMAINS is True and Flask SERVER_NAME is a base domain, validate_redirect_url() treats any urlsplit netloc that equals or endswith('.' + SERVER_NAME) as an allowed redirect target. Python leaves a literal backslash (or %5C) inside the authority, so http://evil.com\.whitelist.com parses as netloc evil.com\.whitelist.com and passes the suffix check. Login/register next handling then returns that URL from get_post_action_redirect() into Flask redirect(), emitting a 302 Location with the unquoted host. Browsers treat the backslash as an authority separator and send the user to evil.com instead of a whitelist.com subdomain. Exact netloc matching without the subdomain suffix exception would have rejected the payload. The 5.8.1 fix does not tighten the suffix check; it percent-encodes the hostname before building Location so browsers no longer mangle it.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in multipart/form-data parsing only. AdonisJS BodyParser feeds attacker-controlled multipart field names into FormFields.add(), which does lodash.set/get on a plain object store (`this._fields = {}` originally; later `#fields: any = {}`) without rejecting reserved keys. A field such as `__proto__.polluted` or `constructor.prototype.polluted` therefore writes onto Object.prototype at runtime. The sink at the patched versions is Multipart.#handleField(key, value) → FormFields.add(key, value) (and file fieldName via the same class). JSON and application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies use other parsers (qs/co-body) and are out of scope. Impact is unexpected behavior, logic bypass, or further issues depending on how polluted prototypes are later consumed. Affected: @adonisjs/bodyparser <= 10.1.2 and 11.0.0-next.0 .. 11.0.0-next.8. Patched by switching the store to Object.create(null) in 10.1.3 and 11.0.0-next.9.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Traefik ForwardAuth always buffers the authentication server HTTP response body in memory with no size cap. In ServeHTTP it did `body, readError := ioutil.ReadAll(forwardResponse.Body)` (later `io.ReadAll` after the Go 1.16 ioutil migration; v2.11.37 `pkg/middlewares/auth/forward.go:128`, v3.6.8 line 211). The body is required because a non-2xx auth response is copied back to the client. An auth server that returns a large or infinite chunked body can force Traefik to allocate until OOM, taking down every route on the process. CWE-770. Request-body forwarding later gained `maxBodySize`; the response-body path had no equivalent until the 2026 patch.

causal_research.bug_semantics: RabbitTemplate.sendAndReceive() with a configured fixed reply queue correlates replies by a messageTag written into the AMQP correlationId (or a custom correlation header). That tag was generated from a per-instance AtomicInteger (messageTagProvider.incrementAndGet()), producing sequential, guessable identifiers that restart at 1 on each new RabbitTemplate. Two templates sharing one reply queue therefore overlap in identifier space; an actor who can publish to that queue can inject a forged reply or steal a legitimate one before the real response arrives (CWE-330 reply poisoning). The same counter also tagged the temporary-queue path; the CVE attack is the shared fixed-queue case. userCorrelationId only opts out when the caller already supplied a unique id.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DjangoBlog OwnTracks ingest at POST /owntracks/logtracks is wired to manage_owntrack_log in owntracks/views.py. causal_research.bug_semantics: Outbound HTTP/1.1 start-line fields are serialized to the wire without neutralizing CR/LF or other illegal bytes. HTTPRequestEncoder writes HTTPRequestHead.uri and HTTPMethod.RAW verbatim into the request line; HTTPResponseEncoder writes a custom HTTPResponseStatus.reasonPhrase verbatim into the status line. An attacker who can influence those fields (proxy-forwarded URL/method, client redirect to a crafted URL, or a custom reason phrase) injects a second request or response on the same connection (request smuggling / response splitting, CWE-93). From 2.42.0 the default NIOHTTPRequestHeadersValidator / NIOHTTPResponseHeadersValidator (enableOutboundHeaderValidation=true on addHTTPClientHandlers / addHTTPServerHandlers) only gated header names and values via areValidToSend, so a CRLF URI/method/reason still reached the encoder.

causal_research.bug_semantics: deepExtend() enumerated attacker-controlled own keys and used Reflect.has() on the merge receiver. For a JSON-parsed __proto__ key, Reflect.has({}, '__proto__') is true through Object.prototype's inherited accessor; because both resolved values are objects, the recursive branch calls extendObject(Object.prototype, attackerValue), and the attacker's nested keys are then assigned onto Object.prototype. Every subsequently created ordinary object inherits the injected properties, enabling application-dependent integrity, availability, or authorization failures wherever untrusted data reaches deepExtend().

causal_research.bug_semantics: netty_unix_socket_recvFd (JNI, used by Epoll/KQueue DomainSocketChannel in DomainSocketReadMode.FILE_DESCRIPTORS) allocates a control buffer of CMSG_SPACE(sizeof(int)) — 24 bytes on 64-bit Linux — and accepts an SCM_RIGHTS cmsg only when cmsg_len == CMSG_LEN(sizeof(int)) (20). A peer can send two fds in one cmsg (cmsg_len = CMSG_LEN(8) = 24). That payload fits the buffer exactly, so the kernel installs both descriptors with no MSG_CTRUNC. The equality check then fails, the accept/close branch is skipped, and neither installed fd is closed. The native for(;;) retries recvmsg; on a non-blocking socket the retry returns EAGAIN, Java maps that to 0, and the Java read loop exits normally. Two fds leak per crafted message. There is no MSG_CTRUNC handling and extra SCM_RIGHTS fds are never closed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated Jolokia/JMX callers of DestinationView.sendTextMessage* build a VM transport URL by concatenating "vm://" with ManagedRegionBroker.getBrokerName(). ResourceXmlApplicationContext instantiates singleton beans before BrokerService validates the configuration, so factory methods such as Runtime.exec() run in the broker JVM.

causal_research.bug_semantics: tcpliveplay accepts a user-supplied pcap, obtains an IPv4 header from libpcap's caplen-bounded packet buffer, and rewrites the packet before replay. fix_all_checksum_liveplay derives the TCP checksum length solely from the packet-controlled IPv4 total-length field (ntohs(ip_len) minus ip_hl) without proving that the claimed length fits the captured buffer. do_checksum_liveplay forwards that length to do_checksum_math_liveplay, whose loop reads successive 16-bit words until the claimed length is exhausted. A crafted pcap can therefore claim an IP length larger than caplen and make the checksum loop read past libpcap's heap buffer, causing the reported heap-buffer-overflow and denial of service.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS / FileSystemStorage.directory_permissions_mode is set, Django created intermediate directories by temporarily calling os.umask() in the current thread, then os.makedirs(), then restoring umask. FileBasedCache._createdir used the same process-wide umask(0o077) pattern to force 0o700. os.umask is process-global, so a concurrent thread handling another request can mkdir/open while the mask is wrong, producing files or directories with unintended permissions (CWE-362). Source is attacker-controlled concurrent requests that trigger storage saves or file-cache writes; sink is kernel file-creation permission bits. The 2026 fix stops mutating umask and applies the requested mode with os.chmod after os.mkdir.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SoupServer multi-range handling sorts SoupRange entries with sort_ranges() in soup-message-headers.c, then merges overlapping ranges. The comparator subtracts two goffset (gint64) start values and returns that difference as int. When requested start offsets differ by more than INT_MAX (~2.1e9), truncation flips the comparison sign, violating qsort's ordering contract. The subsequent merge then treats mis-ordered non-overlapping ranges as overlapping and silently drops requested spans from HTTP 206 Partial Content responses on bodies larger than about 2 GB, with no error status.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Cargo CanonicalUrl always chopped a trailing .git from registry index URLs. That is correct for git indexes, where host/index and host/index.git are the same repository, but wrong for sparse indexes, which are ordinary HTTPS paths and treat those URLs as distinct registries. SourceId equality and hashing use kind plus CanonicalUrl, so sparse+https://host/index and sparse+https://host/index.git intern as the same identity and share the configured Cargo token. An attacker who can publish on a sparse registry that allows cross-registry dependencies and who can host a sibling *.git sparse index requiring auth can publish a crate depending on the sibling; when the victim fetches it, Cargo sends the victim's token to the malicious index.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Netty's HAProxy PROXY protocol v2 decoder recursively parses nested PP2_TYPE_SSL TLVs, each as a retainedSlice of the channel cumulation buffer. readTlvs() flattens only the immediate children of top-level SSL TLVs into HAProxyMessage.tlvs(); depth-2+ encapsulated TLVs stay solely on HAProxySSLTLV.encapsulatedTLVs(). HAProxySSLTLV does not override deallocate, and HAProxyMessage.deallocate() only walks the flattened list, so a syntactically valid nested-SSL header parses, fires downstream, and is released by the application while the depth-2+ slices permanently pin the pooled ByteBuf (CWE-401).
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-48059 (CNA GitHub, updated 2026-06-12) describes nested PP2_TYPE_SSL TLV memory leak prior to 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final; GHSA-h2qv-fj59-j46j withdrawn_at=null, github_reviewed, CVSS 7.5 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H. Not withdrawn/rejected.

GHSA impact: leak is on the successful parse path; application releases HAProxyMessage normally; cumulation ByteBuf remains pinned. Distinct from GHSA-cc37-9q2j-3hfv/CVE-2026-44893 (invalid TLV length IOOBE leak, #16866) and GHSA-fx2c-96vj-985v/CVE-2022-41881 (nested SSL stack overflow).

causal_research.bug_semantics: PluginImportGuard.restore_hidden_modules() restored saved entries, cleared self.hidden_modules, and only then evaluated len(self.hidden_modules), so every restoration audit message reported zero regardless of the number restored. In setup, hide_dangerous_modules() deleted blocked modules from the process-global sys.modules before sys.meta_path.insert(0, import_guard) installed the blocking finder; a thread scheduled between those two operations could re-import a deleted blocked module and retain access to it, bypassing the intended sandbox in a multi-threaded process.
causal_research.evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-43r4-3hf9-m84q identifies openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py, the clear-before-log defect, the hide/import-hook race, affected range <1.4.0, and direct fix 85cdb6b. `git log -L '/^    def restore_hidden_modules/,/^    def find_module/':openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py 85cdb6b...` has exactly the relevant origin e588aaa3a53ef291406b02745c20fdea8cea7f7c and change 85cdb6bedf3a0fbfb49e2f2e29cd66f1f36f3101; `git log --all -S'Restored {len(self.hidden_modules)}' -- .../plugin_sandbox.py` likewise shows e588 adding and 85c removing the vulnerable expression. The e588 patch adds the entire PluginImportGuard, stores/deletes blocked sys.modules entries, clears hidden_modules before logging its length, then calls import_guard.hide_dangerous_modules() before sys.meta_path.insert(). Direct parent-tree command `git grep -n -e 'class PluginImportGuard' -e 'restore_hidden_modules' -e 'hide_dangerous_modules' 5f8412ee11ac37e57190d6af4fe02f2cf7f2a5bd -- openssl_encrypt/modules/plugin_system/plugin_sandbox.py` returned no matches (exit 1), while the e588 diff is a 131-line addition containing the mechanism. `git cat-file commit e588...` proves the single parent, human author/committer, Claude Code generation line, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 co-author trailer in the BIC commit object. The 85c patch captures count before clear and adds a per-guard threading.Lock; its parent is 0c7418bab59e80a2b40913d8ad8523e6bbab196b. Version checks are unusually important here: `git tag --contains` for both e588 and 85c starts at v1.4.0; v1.3.6 source has no PluginImportGuard, while v1.4.0 contains `_modules_lock` and `logger.debug(f"Restored {count} hidden modules")`. Finally, inspection of 85c's tree shows hide_dangerous_modules() and sys.meta_path.insert() remain consecutive separate calls; the new private lock is acquired only inside hide/restore and is not acquired by other importing threads. causal_research.bug_semantics: openstack_auth.views.login() copies request.GET['next'] into Django's server-side session as post_login_redirect before authentication. The assignment marks the session modified, so SessionMiddleware persists a new backend entry and Set-Cookie for every unauthenticated GET /auth/login/?next=URL that lacks a session cookie. Repeated requests exhaust Memcached/Redis/DB session storage, evicting legitimate sessions (unauthenticated DoS). HorizonMiddleware._process_request still early-returns for unauthenticated users (the CVE-2014-8124 guard), but the new view-layer write runs after request middleware and bypasses it. CWE-696 incorrect behavior order; regression of CVE-2014-8124.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener, HTTP/2 content decompression uses a per-stream EmbeddedChannel whose tail ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter is the sole owner of each pooled decompressed ByteBuf. channelRead calls listener.onDataRead and then connection.local().flowController().consumeBytes before buf.release(). If the flow controller (or onDataRead) throws, release is skipped, leaking one direct ByteBuf per DATA frame. A remote peer can force that throw path and exhaust native/direct memory until JVM OOME.

causal_research.bug_semantics: NIOHTTP1's HTTPDecoder accumulates every HTTP/1 header field into an unbounded [(String,String)] (then HTTPHeaders) before any application handler runs. After the llhttp switch the decoder enforced only an 80 KB cap on a single field name/value (currentFieldByteLength, reset in finish() per field). There was no running total of header-block bytes and no field-count cap, so a remote peer could send hundreds of thousands of small valid headers on one request/response and exhaust memory (or crash consumers that bridge into swift-http-types HTTPFields). Attack path: unauthenticated HTTP/1 bytes -> BetterHTTPParser on_header_field/on_header_value -> HTTPDecoder.didReceiveHeaderValue headers.append -> HTTPServerRequestPart.head / HTTPClientResponsePart.head. Fixed in 2.100.0 by NIOHTTPDecoderLimitConfiguration (maxHeaderFieldSize 80 KB, maxHeaderListSize 2 MB, maxHeaderFieldCount 256) rejecting overflow with HTTPParserError.headerOverflow.
evidence: GHSA-rj37-6j9x-74q6 / CVE-2026-28980 (https://github.com/apple/swift-nio/security/advisories/GHSA-rj37-6j9x-74q6, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rj37-6j9x-74q6): HTTPDecoder accepted unbounded HTTP/1 header blocks; affected <2.100.0 / <=2.99.0; patched 2.100.0; withdrawn_at null; CWE-400/CWE-770. causal_research.bug_semantics: XORMappedAddress.GetFromAs decodes the STUN address family with bin.Uint16(value[0:2]) before checking that the XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS attribute value is long enough. Message.Decode stores attr.Value as a subslice of the remaining buffer (b[:aL]); STUN pads lengths 1–3 to 4 bytes, but a 0-length value has no padding. When that 0-length attribute is last in a tightly allocated Raw buffer (cap==len), the value slice has cap 0, so value[0:2] is a runtime slice-bounds panic. A remote Binding-success (or any parsed STUN/ICE message) carrying a trailing 0-length XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS therefore DoSes the process (CWE-20). The later len(value)<=4 check sat after the family read and could not prevent this panic.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated Jolokia exec of BrokerView.addNetworkConnector(String) accepts a discovery URI whose outer scheme is masterslave. MasterSlaveDiscoveryAgentFactory parses that URI as a composite (parentheses optional) and MasterSlaveDiscoveryAgent.configureServices rewrites the inner components into failover:(inner1,inner2)?.... When an inner component is vm://...?brokerConfig=xbean:<resource>, VMTransportFactory loads a Spring ResourceXmlApplicationContext; singleton beans are instantiated before BrokerService validates the configuration, so factory methods such as Runtime.exec() run in the broker JVM. After CVE-2026-34197, BrokerView.DENIED_TRANSPORT_SCHEMES blocked vm (and later static/failover/http) but omitted masterslave, so a no-paren wrapper such as masterslave:vm://...?brokerConfig=...,tcp://... passed validateAllowedUrl because URISupport.isCompositeURI required a leading '(' and only the outer scheme was checked.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In authenticated HTTP mode, an attacker-controlled Bearer token was treated as a session-file basename without restricting its alphabet or confining the resulting path. causal_research.bug_semantics: ChaiScript's built-in async() launched a script closure with std::async(std::launch::async, ...) but did not make the Dispatch_Engine own or join the worker. Later edits only adjusted registration syntax, module passing, namespaces, or formatting while retaining the same untracked launch.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2025-71346 is a downstream packaging of libxml2 CVE-2025-32415. Nokogiri CRuby vendors libxml2 and exposes XML Schema validation (Nokogiri::XML::Schema → xmlSchemaParse / xmlSchemaValidateDoc / xmlSchemaValidateFile). In libxml2 before 2.13.8 (and 2.14.0–2.14.1), xmlSchemaIDCFillNodeTables in xmlschemas.c copies bind->nbNodes into a local nbNodeTable and later iterates with that stale count after the identity-constraint node table can shrink, causing a heap buffer under-read (CWE-125). The path is reachable when validating an untrusted XSD, or when validating an untrusted document against a trusted schema that uses xsd:keyref together with recursively defined types that have additional identity constraints. Upstream/MITRE rate it 2.9 LOW; impact is availability (crash/DoS), not a Nokogiri-authored memory bug. JRuby is off this libxml2 path; CRuby built against a patched system libxml2 is also unaffected.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2025-71346 state=PUBLISHED (CNA VulnCheck, datePublished 2026-08-25, not rejected/withdrawn). GHSA-2ph4-3vr8-f2m3 withdrawn_at=null. Vendor GHSA-5w6v-399v-w3cc (flavorjones, 2025-04-21) is the first-party advisory: Nokogiri < 1.18.8 affected, 1.18.8 patched; CRuby vendored libxml2 2.13.8 addresses CVE-2025-32415 (CVE-2025-32414 Python-only, no Nokogiri impact).

Upstream mechanism: GitLab GNOME/libxml2#890 and commit 384cc7c182fc00c6d5e2ab4b5e3671b2e3f93c84 / 487ee1d8 change xmlSchemaIDCFillNodeTables from if (nbNodeTable) / while (j < nbNodeTable) to bind->nbNodes because the local can be stale. Maintainer: affects all libxml2 older than 2.13.8 / 2.14.2. CVE-2025-32415: libxml2 from 0 before 2.13.8 and 2.14.0 before 2.14.2.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In seven OSPF Traffic Engineering / Segment Routing TLV parsers, a uint16_t loop accumulator (sum/len) is incremented by TLV_SIZE(), which is a uint32_t (TLV_HDR_SIZE + ROUNDUP(ntohs(tlvh->length), 4)). A crafted sub-TLV length near 0xffff makes TLV_SIZE() >= 65536; the add truncates/wraps so `sum < length` never becomes false while the for-increment still does tlvh = TLV_HDR_NEXT(tlvh) and walks off the LSA buffer. An adjacent OSPF peer can trigger that path with a Type 10/11 Opaque LS Update and crash ospfd (CWE-190 then CWE-125).
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-28532 state=PUBLISHED (cveMetadata.datePublished=2026-04-30, dateUpdated=2026-05-25); CNA VulnCheck; not rejected/withdrawn. GHSA-wjc3-2qjv-c8fp withdrawn_at=null. Affected FRRouting frr < 10.5.3.

Advisory mechanism: uint16_t accumulator truncates uint32_t TLV_SIZE() in seven OSPF TE/SR TLV parsers; crafted Type 10/11 Opaque LSA after OSPF adjacency causes OOB reads/crash. Finder credit: Kazuma Matsumoto (GMO Cybersecurity by IERAE).

Pre-fix parsers at d3e8aedb87671f38db59b0df908e25e1d4af027d^: ospfd/ospf_sr.c get_ext_link_sid:982 (uint16_t sum at 992), get_ext_prefix_sid:1060 (sum at 1069), ospf_sr_ri_lsa_update:1368 (sum at 1377); ospfd/ospf_te.c ospf_te_parse_te:2115 (uint16_t len,sum at 2122), ospf_te_delete_te:2344 (2351), ospf_te_parse_ri:2439 (2445), ospf_te_parse_ext_link:2752 (2759). Each loop does sum += TLV_SIZE() and advances with TLV_HDR_NEXT.

Pre-fix macros in ospfd/ospf_opaque.h: TLV_BODY_SIZE = ROUNDUP(ntohs(length), sizeof(uint32_t)); TLV_SIZE = (uint32_t)(TLV_HDR_SIZE + TLV_BODY_SIZE); TLV_HDR_NEXT = tlvh + TLV_SIZE. ROUNDUP(65535,4)=65536 so TLV_SIZE can be 65540, which wraps uint16_t.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TemplateContext caches an IObjectAccessor solely under the target's System.Type. For ordinary .NET objects, the cached TypedObjectAccessor eagerly computes its member dictionary using the context's then-current MemberFilter (and MemberRenamer). If the same TemplateContext is later reused after MemberFilter is tightened, GetMemberAccessor returns the permissive accessor already cached for that Type, so reads or writes of members now denied by policy remain available.
causal_research.flaw_origin: ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d first added TemplateContext.MemberFilter and, in the same commit, passed that mutable per-context policy into TypedObjectAccessor while leaving the pre-existing Type-only _memberAccessors cache unchanged and without invalidation. The later 2e95889099c3ee5e7a4c0147b7355ecd309200af added TemplateContext.Reset with an explicit safe-reuse contract but likewise retained the accessor cache, making the stale-policy flaw directly reachable during pooled/cross-request reuse; that later commit amplified but did not originate the flawed filter/cache composition.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com> as both author and committer, and its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
causal_research.evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-5wr9-m6jw-xx44 identifies the vulnerable path as TemplateContext.GetMemberAccessor's Type-keyed _memberAccessors cache, GetMemberAccessorImpl constructing TypedObjectAccessor with MemberFilter/MemberRenamer, TypedObjectAccessor.PrepareMembers precomputing exposed fields/properties, and Reset not clearing the cache; it declares <= 6.6.0 affected and 7.0.0 patched. `git log -S'MemberFilter' --all --reverse -- src/Scriban src/Textamina.Scriban` makes ace7a0ebafa6d01500f83c35975cde38d559fa3d the first MemberFilter commit. `git log -L 940,940:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs 8180fb6c^` traces the decisive constructor call from `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberRenamer)` to `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberFilter, MemberRenamer)` at ace7a0e; its diff also adds the mutable TemplateContext.MemberFilter property and TypedObjectAccessor's _filter field/filter checks. Cache-line `git log -L 858,864:src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs 8180fb6c^` shows the Type-only cache predates that commit, so the large 2017 namespace move is not misclassified as the BIC. Direct parent-tree verification against c525ebfc8bfb31853da2e0280d2a24045893badb finds zero `MemberFilter` references in TemplateContext.cs and TypedObjectAccessor.cs; that tree constructs `new TypedObjectAccessor(type, MemberRenamer)`, so the advisory's filter/cache composition is absent. `git cat-file -p ace7a0e` shows one parent, human author/committer Alexandre Mutel, and no trailers, so no squash decomposition or commit-object AI signal applies. The BIC is five commits before tag v0.16.0 (`git describe --contains --tags ace7a0e` => v0.16.0~5), while its parent describes from v0.15.0; `git tag --contains ace7a0e` includes 6.6.0. Fix 8180fb6cd1f6c2727c99f8f5a745a0b991b06cfc adds `_memberAccessors.Clear()` to TemplateContext.Reset plus the stale-filter regression case. `git tag --contains 8180fb6c` begins at 7.0.0; `_memberAccessors.Clear()` is absent from tag 6.6.0 and present at src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs:982 in tag 7.0.0, matching the advisory boundary.
causal_research.reasoning: The attack requires a context to first encounter a model Type under a permissive filter, causing TypedObjectAccessor to snapshot that Type's allowed members, and then to reuse the context under a stricter filter. Because lookup consults only the Type key, later member-expression access receives the old accessor and bypasses the new sandbox policy. Historical decomposition separates three stages: the Type cache existed from the initial repository history; ace7a0e was the smallest normal commit that made it security-sensitive to MemberFilter by adding the policy and feeding it into the cached accessor; 2e95889 later formalized safe TemplateContext reuse without flushing that cache. The immediate parent lacks MemberFilter and the filter-bearing constructor entirely, while ace7a0e's own diff writes both causal additions, establishing parent absence and the BIC. The direct fix clears the stale accessors during Reset and is released exactly at the declared 7.0.0 patched boundary after 6.6.0. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it is a one-parent human-authored commit with no AI marker. causal_research.bug_semantics: CodeIgniter 4 file-upload rules is_image and mime_in classify an upload solely by content-derived MIME type and never independently enforce that a non-empty client filename extension is a safe image/matching type. is_image maps UploadedFile::getExtension() (MIME-guessed, not the client name) through Mimes::guessTypeFromExtension() and accepts the file if that type starts with 'image'. mime_in compares UploadedFile::getMimeType()/getType() (finfo of the temp file) against the allowed list. An attacker can prepend image magic bytes (for example GIF89a) to a PHP webshell named shell.php; both rules pass, and if the application then saves the upload with the client-supplied name into a web-accessible script-enabled directory, the file is executed as PHP (CWE-434). The attack requires all three of: is_image/mime_in used without a separate safe-extension check (ext_in on patched versions), preservation of the original filename, and a public executable upload path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SctpMessageCompletionHandler reassembles incomplete SCTP DATA chunks per streamIdentifier. For every non-complete fragment it stored fragments.put(streamIdentifier, Unpooled.wrappedBuffer(previousAccumulator, newSlice)), creating a new CompositeByteBuf whose first component is the previous composite. After N fragments the readableBytes()/getBytes() path recurses N levels, and each layer retains component arrays. There was no cap on fragment count N, total buffered bytes, or distinct streamIdentifiers (each map entry is an independent nested chain). A remote peer that never sets the complete flag can force unbounded nested composites from 1-byte chunks, exhausting memory/stack (CWE-770 DoS). The 2026 fix stores a flat List<ByteBuf> per stream, enforces maxIncompleteSctpMessages and maxFragments (default 128), and builds one CompositeByteBuf only when the message completes.

causal_research.reasoning: The advisory is a live published GHSA/CVE (not withdrawn). The source-to-sink is unbounded nested CompositeByteBuf reassembly in SctpMessageCompletionHandler: each incomplete SCTP fragment wraps the prior accumulator, and each streamIdentifier is a separate map entry, so a peer that withholds the complete flag can grow depth and map size without limit. The smallest first-write of those surviving lines is 64ebece730e06be174dbb9e7b4558bab7b5f32e1 (2012-09-29), a single-parent new-file commit; the parent tree lacks the class, and an earlier decoder wrap was deleted in the same commit rather than moved into this handler. The mechanism is closed by da1e96e21fa3758dba3f6499862d4c1f0daef3cb on 4.2 (first patched 4.2.15.Final) and backport cef5395186369f6bf7a8caac34e4de1596ba9f15 on 4.1 (first patched 4.1.135.Final), which flatten fragments and cap inflight streams/fragments. causal_research.bug_semantics: A user with lang-edit can upload a ZIP on a Language Support translation field (InputfieldFile unzip=1 → WireUpload extractArchives). saveUploadZip() writes the archive under site/assets/files/<language_id>/.zip_tmp/ and immediately calls WireFileTools::unzip() / historically wireUnzipFile(). unzip() iterates every ZipArchive entry and extractTo()s it with only a later '..' substring skip and no cap on uncompressed bytes, entry count, depth, or time. Extension and size filtering in saveUploadZip() run only after extraction, so a small highly-compressible ZIP of allowed-looking *.json entries can expand to multi-GB (CPU/disk DoS, ENOSPC cascade) before cleanup. Nested leftover ZIPs are a secondary post-extract cleanup bug, not the zip-bomb sink.

mechanism.impact: Deterministic remote denial of service against the UDM SDM service: the request never needs a well-formed body, only the absence of the optional query parameter, and the panic repeats on every call (availability H, confidentiality and integrity none).
mechanism.preconditions: A vulnerable udm revision (the index entered 2024-05-13 and survived until the 2025-08-19 len guard) and a caller authorized to reach the Nudm_SDM shared-data endpoint; the endpoint does not require the optional parameter to be present.

mechanism.summary: A Nudm_SDM shared-data GET without the optional supported-features query parameter indexes an empty []string at the request-derived call site and panics the handler, which gin's recovery turns into HTTP 500, so any consumer of the UDM can deny service with a single cheap request (CVSS AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H). Three sibling 5xx surfaces on the same API were repaired in the same campaign and are written up in sibling_mechanisms.
mechanism.trigger: GET /nudm-sdm/v2/<supi|gpsi>/shared-data on a vulnerable udm revision without the optional supported-features parameter; the handler reads it with c.QueryArray and indexes element 0 unconditionally, producing runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0 and a 500 response (issue 700 log trace).

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real Nudm-SDM panic: missing supported-features -> QueryArray empty -> supportedFeatures[0]. Immediate-parent verification shows that index was first written in udm 2d42b1a (PR #37 member), not in the later move or the landing merge. The BIC commit object is named-human (hjkja0511@gmail.com / a3828162 JamesWu) with no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI. The minimum panic fix is the length guard in dae4b2b, landed by e776c42 and pinned by free5gc v4.1.0. Bundled 500-vs-4xx issues are separate mechanisms with later fixes; they do not change BIC-side AI attribution or reopen the panic.
This cluster resolves to four denial-of-service surfaces in the udm Nudm_SDM handlers, repaired by one developer between 2025-08 and 2025-09: free5gc/free5gc issue 700 is an index-out-of-range panic when shared-data is requested without the optional supported-features parameter, and issues 701-703 are sibling 500s on a missing single-nssai, an invalid nfInstanceId and a mis-mapped UDR 404. The panic enters the tree in udm commit 2d42b1a8 (2024-05-13): its one-line hunk changes internal/sbi/processor/retrieval_of_shared_data.go to pass supportedFeatures[0] into the renamed consumer method, while the immediate parent 1e67491d passes the whole slice and the parent-era callee only wraps the string in optional.NewString. Later commits only relocate the expression (dfb83129, 4e578fd2, and the 2025 server refactor that moves it to internal/sbi/api_subscriberdatamanagement.go:142), and dae4b2bd's len guard is the minimal repair that closes it. The BIC commit object carries a recovered named human identity (GitHub account a3828162, profile JamesWu, author field ubuntu <hjkja0511@gmail.com>), a single subject line with a human typo, no trailers and no AI-shaped content, so the AI-role evidence is negative on the BIC side. The fix-side commits show no AI markers either and are informational only, so the case closes NOT_AI with the submodule-based verification limits recorded in bic_note.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Public safe ruint::algorithms::div::reciprocal_mg10 is a 256-entry MG10 reciprocal lookup. Callers must pass d >= 2^63 so that d9 = d >> 55 is in [256, 511] and (d9 - 256) indexes TABLE. The only guard is debug_assert!(d >= (1 << 63)), which is compiled out in release. The live load is unsafe TABLE.get_unchecked((d9.0 - 256) as usize). Passing d = 0 (or any d < 2^63) makes d9 < 256; the unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge usize and get_unchecked reads outside TABLE, which is UB/memory corruption in safe Rust. The function is re-exported as algorithms::div::reciprocal and is callable by downstream crates.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MultipartFile.move(location, options) treats the attacker-controlled multipart filename as the destination basename. When options.name is omitted, the method defaults to this.clientName (the Content-Disposition filename) and builds the path with path.join(location, name) with no sanitization, prefix check, or basename() confinement. A crafted filename containing ../ (or an absolute path, which path.join can treat as the new root) writes the uploaded body outside the intended directory. After 900627c1500bb38155ee3f9620a89ed7609b996e the overwrite default is true, so an existing target is replaced. Reachable whenever an app calls move() without an explicit sanitized name.

causal_research.bug_semantics: django.contrib.admin.utils.display_for_field() special-cased models.URLField by emitting format_html('{}', value, value) using the raw stored field value as the href. Admin changelist cells and read-only change-form widgets call this helper, so a stored unsafe scheme (javascript:, data:, etc.) became a clickable link for staff. Clicking the link is XSS in the authenticated admin session (CWE-83). The 2026 fix runs URLValidator() first and falls back to plain text on ValidationError. This is a new display_for_field sink from the 5.2 #36032 feature, not leftover AdminURLFieldWidget XSS from CVE-2019-12308.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Applications that install DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener decompress HTTP/2 DATA via an EmbeddedChannel. Http2Decompressor.decompress() (and historically onDataRead) does decompressor.writeInbound(data.retain()). Java evaluates data.retain() before writeInbound, bumping ByteBuf refCnt 1->2. EmbeddedChannel.writeInbound begins with ensureOpen(); if cleanup()/finish() already closed the channel (stream removal or END_STREAM with the decompressor property still attached), ClosedChannelException is thrown before the pipeline takes ownership, so the decoder finally-release never runs. The surrounding catch rethrows Http2Exception/streamError without data.release(), so the extra reference is never dropped. The frame reader then releases once (refCnt 2->1) and the typically direct buffer is leaked. Repeating DATA on a long-lived connection exhausts direct memory (CWE-400/401 DoS).

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion in MessagePack-CSharp JSON conversion (not typed MessagePack deserialization). ConvertFromJson's FromJsonCore recursively walks nested JSON objects and arrays without consulting MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth, so attacker-controlled nesting can exhaust the call stack. TinyJsonReader.ReadNextToken self-recurses on comma and colon separators, so even malformed JSON with long separator runs consumes one stack frame per character before structural validation. ConvertToJson applies DepthStep to arrays and maps, but the typeless ext-100 branch recursively calls ToJsonCore without DepthStep, so nested typeless wrappers bypass UntrustedData. Each path yields an uncatchable StackOverflowException instead of a bounded parse/serialization failure.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CWE-918 SSRF with HTTP-error reflection in the OIDC token-exchange path. Exchange() takes the Authorization bearer JWT, reads the unverified iss claim via apiauth.ExtractIssuer, and immediately performs OIDC discovery against that string (originally oidc.NewProvider(ctx, issuer); later provider.Get → oidc.NewProvider). go-oidc GETs {iss}/.well-known/openid-configuration and follows redirects using the default HTTP client, so a crafted iss (http://internal-host, link-local metadata, attacker HTTPS that 302s internally) causes the server to fetch attacker-chosen URLs before any signature or trust-policy check. Discovery failures are wrapped into the gRPC error (go-oidc formats '%s: %s' with status and body), so internal response bodies can reflect to the caller; later logging of provider/token-exchange errors added a second leak. causal_research.bug_semantics: Netty's DNS resolver, in DnsResolveContext.buildAliasMap, walks every CNAME in a response ANSWER section and writes owner->target into DnsCnameCache without checking that the owner is the queried name or a descendant of it (RFC 5452 bailiwick). An attacker who can inject extra CNAME RRs (off-path with a guessed query id, or an on-path/malicious nameserver) can cache mappings such as cname.netty.io. -> evil.com. while answering a query for x.netty.io. Later lookups of the poisoned owner skip the real nameserver and follow the cached alias, enabling cache poisoning. The 2026 fix only gates cache.cache(); the in-response alias map is unchanged, confirming the vulnerability is the unvalidated cache write.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2024-58135/GHSA-3r5v-gmfp-3mh9 is CWE-338 in Mojolicious, not hashcat. causal_research.bug_semantics: A template-controlled reverse range such as (100000000..1) makes evalRangeToken charge high - low + 1, a large negative count. Limiter.use accepted that negative count and added it to its cumulative base, creating artificial budget credit. Later append/replace operations could therefore exceed the configured memoryLimit; flattening the resulting large V8 cons-string could terminate the Node.js process, producing denial of service.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 added ctx.memoryLimit.use(high - low + 1) to src/render/expression.ts without constraining the charge to a non-negative range size. The pre-existing Limiter.use implementation accepted and accumulated signed counts, so this new attacker-controlled negative callsite completed the underflow/budget-bypass mechanism. Reverse ranges themselves return an empty array because range(start, stop) loops only while start < stop, making the negative charge pure budget credit rather than a matching allocation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When HTTP/3 is enabled, Traefik selects the QUIC TLS config with GetTLSGetClientInfo: a raw map lookup hostHTTPTLSConfig[info.ServerName]. Router TLSOptions keys are lowercased domains from Host rules, so mixed-case SNI (API.EXAMPLE.COM) misses and falls back to the default TLS config, which often does not require a client certificate. From v3.7.0, Host(`*.example.com`) also stores a wildcard key that never equals a concrete SNI, producing the same fallback. After the handshake, HTTP Host matching is case-insensitive and (in v3.7+) wildcard-aware, so the request is still routed to the router that declared mTLS. HTTP/2/TCP does not share this selector: it matches via the TCP muxer / ToLower routing table, so the same hosts still demand a certificate. Attack: UDP to an HTTP/3 entrypoint, no client cert, reach an mTLS-protected backend.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SAML.getSession in internal/pkg/auth/interceptor/saml.go treats a saml-session token as single-use by reading SAMLAssertionSpec.used via safe.StateGet and only later writing Used=true in a separate safe.StateUpdateWithConflicts that does not re-check the flag. causal_research.bug_semantics: getRecommendTitleFromMarkdownString synchronously applies /#{1,6} {1,}(.*\S.*)(?:\n|$)/g to Markdown supplied to the save/save-as path. For a heading prefix followed by a long run of spaces and a newline, the required non-space cannot match, while the adjacent space repetition and broad repetitions repeatedly repartition and rescan the same input. causal_research.bug_semantics: nltk.data.find() validates a still-percent-encoded resource name and later passes it to url2pathname() while constructing a filesystem path. Percent encodings such as %2e%2e therefore survive the raw-string check, decode to .. only at filesystem resolution, escape the configured NLTK data root, and let find()/load() read an arbitrary process-readable file. The pathsec routing present in 3.9.4 only warned because ENFORCE was false, so it did not prevent the read.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Apache Neethi policy normalization (Policy.normalize -> AbstractPolicyOperator.normalizeOperator) resolves wsp:PolicyReference children by registry lookup and then recursively normalizes the referenced Policy's components with no cycle set. A WS-Policy graph where Policy A references Policy B and B references A therefore re-enters normalizeOperator on the same policies until StackOverflowError or an unbounded hang. The pre-3.2.2 TYPE_POLICY_REF branch (3.2.1 AbstractPolicyOperator.java:128-148) looks up the URI, wraps the resolved Policy's children in All, and calls normalizeOperator again; PolicyReference.normalize is only an entry point into that same operator path. Attackers supply or register such a circular document and trigger normalize(true), causing DoS (CWE-400). Patched in 3.2.2 by tracking resolving policy ids and throwing RuntimeException on a repeat.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated Project Manager or Owner can store a repository git_url beginning with Git's --upload-pack= option. The server-side schedule commit-hash poller passes that value directly after `git ls-remote` without an end-of-options delimiter; Git parses it as an option and invokes the attacker-selected upload-pack command through a shell, yielding command execution in the Semaphore server process.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit a30df1527e15c4c0060979bc2b7b120a8234111f changed GetLastRemoteCommitHash from running `git ls-remote origin <branch>` in the already-cloned repository to running `git ls-remote <Repository.GetGitURL()> <branch>` in the temporary directory. That single-line data-flow change first placed the stored, attacker-controlled GitURL in Git's option-parsing position; the existing makeCmd helper appended the arguments to exec.Command("git") without `--`.

The assigned GHSA-93jq-5gw9-rx3q is an unreviewed alias of that issue; NVD now marks assigned CVE-2026-73682 rejected in favor of CVE-2026-73294.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When a plugin lacked READ_FILES, PluginSandbox attempted to confine filesystem access by replacing only builtins.open with restricted_open. pathlib.Path.open/read_text/read_bytes/write_text/write_bytes and io.open retained independent file-opening paths, and pathlib/io were available to plugin code, so an untrusted plugin could read or modify paths outside the sandbox's allowed directories without passing _is_safe_path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: mailboxes/detachall.cgi saves each MIME attachment into a temp directory then zips the result. When an attachment has a filename, the CGI sets $fn from decode_mimewords($a->{'filename'}) and writes with open_tempfile(FILE, ">$temp/$fn", 0, 1). The fourth argument is $notemp=1, so web-lib-funcs.pl open_tempfile writes directly via Perl open(">$file") with no basename check; it only rejects CR/LF/NUL. An attacker-controlled Content-Disposition filename such as ../../etc/cron.d/pwn therefore escapes $temp and overwrites an arbitrary path as the Webmin process user (often root). Trigger is an authenticated Read User Mail user invoking detach-all on a crafted message (CVE-2026-49103: CWE-24, CVSS 9.4, PR:L, affected < 2.640).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Traefik's Kubernetes Gateway provider turns HTTPRoute matches into Traefik router rules by interpolating tenant-controlled header and query values into backtick-delimited matcher literals (Header(`name`,`value`), Query(`name`,`value`)) and AND-ing them with the listener Host(...) constraint. Because backtick is the rule-language string delimiter and the generated string is parsed by pkg/rules/parser.go (vulcand/predicate AND/OR), a value containing `) || HostRegexp(`.*`) || ... terminates the literal and injects an OR branch that is not gated by Host(...). In shared Gateway deployments that rely on listener hostname isolation, that lets a tenant with HTTPRoute write access steal victim-host traffic to attacker backends. The same unescaped pattern was later copied to GRPCRoute headers.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated WordPress administrator can submit a download_path such as WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/../..'. The validation compares the uncanonicalized string prefix with WP_CONTENT_DIR, so the traversal-bearing string passes even though filesystem resolution escapes wp-content. The value is persisted as the plugin's filesystem root; download-add.php and download-manager.php pass that root to the recursive print_list_files()/print_list_folders() browser, allowing the administrator to enumerate files outside wp-content and select them for management/access.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit a141c14127eb8d72413ac6a11dd3e7ad66aef9b1 added the advisory-specific containment check in download-options.php using substr($download_path, 0, strlen(WP_CONTENT_DIR)) on the raw path. It neither canonicalized the candidate nor rejected traversal components, so it first wrote the flawed prefix-check mechanism later replaced by the fix. Before this hardening commit the setting had no containment check at all; that explains the advisory description's broader 'all versions' exposure, but the specific traversal-bypass predicate named by the advisory originates in a141c14127eb8d72413ac6a11dd3e7ad66aef9b1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Attacker-controlled WKT, WKB, or hex-encoded WKB containing deeply nested GEOMETRYCOLLECTION values is accepted by django.contrib.gis.geos.GEOSGeometry (and by gis.forms.GeometryField.to_python and BaseSpatialField spatial lookups, which construct GEOSGeometry from lookup/form strings). Django forwarded that payload to the GEOS C WKT/WKB readers with no collection-depth or collection-count bound. GEOS then recurses until it stack-overflows and segmentation-faults the Django process (CWE-674 / CAPEC-230). GeoJSON is parsed via GDAL and is out of scope. The 2026 fix rejects WKT nesting deeper than 198 collections and WKB with more than 198 collection headers before calling GEOS.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-601 open redirect (and cache-poisoning amplifier) in @angular/ssr: an unsanitized X-Forwarded-Prefix is passed into joinUrlParts() and then addLeadingSlash() when emitting a redirect Location. addLeadingSlash only treats a leading '/' as already-absolute, so a prefix of '\evil.com' becomes '/\evil.com'. Browsers treat the '/\' sequence as a protocol-relative '//', sending the client to the attacker host. After CVE-2026-27738, INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX /^[/\\]{2}/ rejected two leading slash-or-backslash characters (//, \\, /\, \\/) but still accepted a single leading backslash; the same prepend-slash transform therefore remained exploitable. Redirects also omitted Vary: X-Forwarded-Prefix, so a poisoned Location could be cached.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-33397 state=PUBLISHED (cvelistV5 2026-03-30, not rejected); GHSA-vfx2-hv2g-xj5f withdrawn_at=null; NVD/OSV alias the same GHSA. Real incomplete-fix open redirect of CVE-2026-27738, not a false positive.

causal_research.bug_semantics: FileBinding.write and ZipFileBinding.write join a FileCredentials-supplied name onto a per-build secrets directory with FilePath.child and then copyFrom/unzipFrom that path. FilePath.child honors ../ and path separators, so a credential whose getFileName() is a traversal payload (e.g. ../../../../p0wn3d.txt, as in Security3672Test) writes the secret bytes (or extracts a zip) outside the intended UUID secrets dir on the node filesystem. If a low-privileged user can supply file/zip credentials used by a job on the built-in node, the write can land under JENKINS_HOME (init.groovy.d, plugins) and become RCE. FileCredentials javadoc claimed a simple basename, but the binding never enforced that contract; FileCredentialsImpl UI upload strips prefixes, yet programmatic/XML constructors and other implementations can return unsanitized names.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Flask-Security-Too 5.8.0 OAuth reauthentication (verify) treats any datastore-resolved OAuth user as proof that the current session may be marked fresh. oauth_verify_response() calls _oauth_response_common(), then on a truthy user writes session['fs_paa']=time.time() with no check that that user is current_user. An attacker who already holds a stale authenticated victim session can start OAuth verify and complete the provider callback with a different account (attacker@example.com). causal_research.bug_semantics: A malicious repository can put traversal components in a .gitmodules section name. GitPython parses that attacker-controlled section name without validation, assigns it to Submodule._name, and during Submodule.update(init=True) uses it to form <parent git dir>/modules/<name>. The resulting escaped path is passed to directory and clone operations, so initialization creates an attacker-controlled Git repository outside the intended clone directory.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _module_abspath() with os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name) and changed the initialization branch of Submodule.update() from the tree-backed submodule path to this unchecked name-derived path before Repo.clone_from(). That is the first causal connection between an untrusted .gitmodules name and the filesystem repository-creation sink; the pre-existing unchecked sm_name() parser alone did not create this attack path.

evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc states that <=3.1.57 is affected and >=3.1.58 is patched. It identifies the flow sm_name(section) -> Submodule.iter_items() assigning sm._name -> _module_abspath() joining parent_repo.git_dir/modules/name -> clone/filesystem operations, and documents a released-3.1.57 PoC that creates /tmp/gitpython_poc_escaped_root/modules_dir while core Git rejects the suspicious name.

At 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc, git/objects/submodule/util.py sm_name() returns section[11:-1] unchecked; git/objects/submodule/base.py iter_items() reads n = sm_name(sms) and assigns sm._name = n. The same commit adds _module_abspath() at then-lines 204-210, whose Git-file branch returns os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name).

The 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc diff changes the Submodule.update() initialization branch from module_path = join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) to module_path = self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name), after which Repo.clone_from(self.url, module_path, n=True) creates the repository. The path value in the parent was constrained by the required pc.tree[path] lookup; the newly used section name was not validated.

Direct inspection of the parent update branch shows only join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path) feeding Repo.clone_from(). The BIC tree contains _module_abspath at base.py:204, the unchecked join at :206, and update's call at :422.

causal_research.bug_semantics: indiserver accepts unauthenticated TCP on port 7624 and feeds every received byte into lilxml. causal_research.bug_semantics: Attacker-controlled HEIC/AVIF ISO-BMFF data reaches the public load path. The box walker accepts only an 8-byte top-level header, but getBoxLength reads absent 64-bit extended-size words and the later shared parseBox implementation also reads a full-box version byte past an 8-byte box. DataView raises an uncaught RangeError, allowing one malformed image to abort an unguarded request or worker.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mercurius serves GraphQL over HTTP at /graphql. A CORS-simple request can include cookies without an OPTIONS preflight. In v16.3.0 the GET handler reads query/variables from the query string and executes GraphQL, so a cross-origin GET /graphql?query=... with credentials can run authenticated queries (and any query with side effects). The GHSA/CVE text and PoC instead describe Fastify mis-parsing application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, or text/plain as application/json on POST. Mercurius 16 depends on Fastify 5, whose default JSON parser matches only application/json (plus parameters); urlencoded/multipart yield 415 and text/plain is a string, so that POST PoC does not execute GraphQL on the v16 stack. Mercurius itself only extra-parses application/graphql. The vendor fix is Apollo-style CSRF prevention: require a non-simple Content-Type or a custom header so the browser must preflight. POST application/json already preflights; GET was the Mercurius-owned simple-request sink in the affected v16 range.

causal_research.bug_semantics: POST /api/av/getAttributeViewFieldViews is a reader-reachable missing-authorization disclosure (CWE-862). CheckAuth accepts RoleReader (and other authenticated roles) but the route has no CheckReadonly, CheckAdminRole, or publish-access filter. The handler binds caller-supplied avID and keyID (ID-pattern check only), then GetAttributeViewFieldViews parses the AV storage file and returns every view's id, icon, name, layout type, and the requested field's Hidden flag. A publish reader who already sees one embedded database can thus enumerate unpublished views and concealment choices. Sibling getAttributeViewKeys, registered immediately above it, does apply FilterBlockAttributeViewKeysByPublishAccess for read-only roles.

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS promised to bound each render with renderLimit, but Render.renderTemplates checked elapsed time only inside its loop over template nodes. An empty for or tablerow body parses to an empty templates array, so every attacker-controlled collection iteration calls renderTemplates([]), executes no check, and consumes CPU linearly up to the separate memoryLimit while bypassing the configured wall-clock budget.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 introduced the renderLimit feature and its first enforcement point as ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now()) inside for (const tpl of templates). The existing for and tablerow tags could pass an empty body array once per collection element, so placing the new security check exclusively inside the zero-trip inner loop created the bypass at the moment the guard was introduced.
