In the validated full-history clone, `git log master -L '/public \* renderTemplates/,/^  }/':src/render/render.ts` and `git log -S 'ctx.renderLimit.check(performance.now())' -- src/render/render.ts` show e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 first adding the check inside the template-node loop; later commits only change the clock source and unrelated loop state until the fix. `git cat-file -p e443068...` gives sole parent fad00aa14e8beac0514ec4196944b33276f1ff2c and the human-only commit object. Direct parent-tree verification with `git show fad00aa...:src/render/render.ts` shows the same zero-trip template loop without any limiter check, while `git grep -n renderLimit fad00aa... -- src` returns no matches: the renderLimit option and flawed enforcement are absent in the immediate parent. At the BIC, src/tags/for.ts and src/tags/tablerow.ts both build `templates = []` for empty bodies and call renderTemplates(this.templates, ctx, emitter) inside attacker-sized collection loops. `git tag --contains e443068... --sort=version:refname` starts at v10.15.0 and excludes v10.14.0, establishing the feature's first release boundary. `git show 5b9c346...` adds an unconditional `ctx.renderLimit.check(getPerformance().now())` at renderTemplates entry plus empty-for and empty-tablerow regressions. `git tag --contains 5b9c346...` starts at v10.26.0 and excludes v10.25.7; resolved release commits are v10.25.7=34877950bfd0f88666f4ef61f7704defdea546b0 and v10.26.0=c20c0af02d33e8d2ca6b08925eadca8755257c39. causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is not merely that large loops existed; it is that the newly documented renderLimit security control claimed a per-render time bound but its only check was conditional on rendering at least one body node. Empty loop bodies made that condition false on every iteration while the outer for/tablerow machinery continued, producing the advisory's availability attack. History isolates e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 as the smallest real BIC because it simultaneously introduced renderLimit and wrote the exact misplaced check; older loop machinery alone could not bypass a control that did not yet exist. causal_research.bug_semantics: A logged-in user could submit a saved graph configuration whose config_json was checked only for syntactically valid JSON. The server stored and returned the object without a property allowlist; an administrator's list included every user's saved configurations. Loading one parsed the stored JSON and applyConfig spread every property of attacker-controlled stixStyles or mispStyles entries into GRAPH_CONFIG. Those style maps were then passed to Pivotick as nodeStyleMap/defaultNodeStyle, and Pivotick interpreted a supplied svgIcon as HTML, so viewing/loading the saved configuration could execute attacker script in another user's browser.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit a0a9834b21b40ab570db54e1c6e6c2cf100b5f9a introduced the complete unsafe saved-configuration path in one focused feature commit: the graph_config model and save/list routes, unrestricted JSON persistence, the saved-config loader, and applyConfig's unrestricted style-object spreads. Its immediate parent had none of the graph-config persistence, loading, or patch-application mechanism, making this ordinary one-parent feature commit the smallest reconstructable BIC rather than the later branch merge or a release commit.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Every unauthenticated WebSocket connection follows the default connection listener into requestClientId and rpc.send('get-client-id'); a silent client leaves both the queued RPC request and its 10 ms setInterval alive after socket close, so repeated connections cause unbounded timer, CPU, and heap growth.
evidence: The CVE.org CNA record is PUBLISHED and describes the unauthenticated get-client-id RPC waiter leak as fixed in 0.2.16; the bundled GHSA is not withdrawn.

The f5d03cac30baa3f9d066095962e08df3c61112ce diff adds RPC.requests/responses, this.requests.push(payload), and setInterval polling whose only clearInterval/queue cleanup path requires a matching response; it also changes the default connection path to await requestClientId({ws,rpc}). Its new clientId.js explicitly notes that missing timeout could queue unactioned promises and become a DoS vector.

Immediate parent d5cb93d5d6f5b7d8e77c998cf74125383d95232b has no lib/clientId.js and its RPC implementation has no requests queue, response waiter, or setInterval; its client-ID request is a plain WebSocket send, so the vulnerable resource-retention mechanism is absent.

The BIC has exactly one parent, no local pull/member refs, and ordinary author and committer metadata for Paul Jensen dated 2020-10-12; its message and raw commit metadata contain no AI-generation or Co-Authored-By marker. No finer public member is available, so no squash decomposition is applicable.
Commit 990461ee58370b5f1cc2c2c2f1efd827a08cecbd later copies the already-vulnerable JavaScript waiter into src/lib/rpc.ts during TypeScript conversion and is a migration, not the BIC.

In parent 6c97a4f2c5d0e69881c5d5710a17e60ca1dc37ec the TypeScript waiter still clears its interval and removes its request only after a reply. Direct fix 931576db3cdbf4f1583bd2c3c8759c4f4e032ab3 passes ws into waitForReply, installs a once('close') handler, clears the interval, removes the pending request, and rejects the waiter.

Tag ancestry excludes the BIC from v0.0.2 and includes it in v0.0.3; it excludes the direct fix from v0.2.15 and includes it in v0.2.16. Commit 67260d2a1407a77f082f02dc9e1f0891222c306d changes package metadata from 0.2.15 to 0.2.16 and is the release carrier, while 931576db3cdbf4f1583bd2c3c8759c4f4e032ab3 is the direct fix.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Single-parent commit f5d03cac30baa3f9d066095962e08df3c61112ce is the smallest surviving public object that first coupled the default client-ID request path to an RPC implementation that queues every reply-bearing request and polls forever without timeout or socket-close cleanup.
causal_research.reasoning: The real advisory is confirmed, the source-to-sink mechanism is present, the immediate-parent absence check identifies f5d03cac30baa3f9d066095962e08df3c61112ce rather than the later TypeScript migration or release carrier, and the direct repair is independently mapped. AI attribution is evaluated only on that BIC: the 2020 single-parent commit has named matching human author/committer metadata and no AI marker or AI co-author trailer. Therefore the vulnerability is human-introduced and the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL took the directory of the file being edited and interpolated it verbatim into the PowerShell program -NoExit -Command "Set-Location -Path '<directory>'". A Windows directory name may contain a single quote, so an attacker-controlled directory can terminate the PowerShell single-quoted literal and append PowerShell statements. When a victim opens a file from that directory and invokes Open PowerShell/Open Terminal (including the administrator variant), ShellExecuteW starts powershell.exe and executes the injected statements with the victim's privileges.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 converted the existing Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL scaffold from a cmd.exe invocation to powershell.exe and first added the vulnerable Set-Location command template using strFolder.c_str() without PowerShell single-quote escaping. Its immediate parent still constructed a cmd.exe '/k cd /d' command and had neither the PowerShell Set-Location template nor the vulnerable single-quoted interpolation.

This non-merge, single-parent commit wrote the unsafe language boundary itself; the later merge c18e549fcb7c877bf57287cea857a6ef7d49898b merely aggregated the visible feature commits.

History cross-check: `git log -L '/void CViewCommander::Command_OPEN_POWERSHELL/,/^}/':sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` traces the vulnerable template to 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7. Subsequent commits in that line history change comments/types/refactoring but retain the same unescaped strFolder template until the security fix, so neither the later merge nor the 2025 file move is the BIC.

Immediate-parent absence: `git cat-file -p 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7` gives sole parent de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a. A direct `git diff de6749296b8b9a3ffa2c281d26758770a956f31a 3340e0d352a795ddfaf89214e66f7989371b21c7 -- sakura_core/cmd/CViewCommander_File.cpp` shows the parent used cmd.exe with `/k cd /d "%s"`; the BIC adds both powershell.exe and `Set-Location -Path '%s'`. Thus the advisory's vulnerable PowerShell interpolation is absent from the immediate parent tree.

Exploitability follows the parser boundary visible in the BIC: strFolder is derived from the opened document path, and a directory component such as `name'; <attacker-statement>; '` closes the quoted -Path value. PowerShell then parses the appended statement because the whole interpolated value is supplied as executable `-Command` text, rather than as an opaque working-directory argument.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Velociraptor client artifacts run on the endpoint without per-plugin ACL checks. The server is supposed to gate dangerous artifacts via the artifact's required_permissions list, enforced in services/launcher/acls.go CheckAccess before CompileCollectorArgs/ScheduleArtifactCollection. Admin.Client.UpdateClientConfig overwrites the client config file with caller-supplied YAML (copy to ConfigPath) and rekeys or kills the client process so the new config takes effect, enabling endpoint takeover. The artifact shipped with RequiredPermissions unset, so CheckAccess returned nil after the usual COLLECT_CLIENT check. The Investigator role grants CollectClient but not EXECVE or FILESYSTEM_WRITE, so a user who could already collect artifacts could run this admin artifact and rewrite client config.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is unset or empty, TaxHacker substitutes a public constant as the better-auth JWT HMAC secret. At HEAD that constant is the Zod default 'please-set-your-key-here' on envSchema.parse in lib/config.ts (lines 14-17), assigned to config.auth.secret (line 65) and passed into betterAuth({ secret, session.strategy: 'jwt' }) in lib/auth.ts. Empty env values are stripped before parse, so docker-compose BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=${BETTER_AUTH_SECRET:-} also lands on the default. An attacker who knows the default can mint HS256 taxhacker session JWTs and, in SELF_HOSTED_MODE=false (cloud/SaaS), pass proxy.ts cookie presence checks and auth.api.getSession verification, impersonating any user. In SELF_HOSTED_MODE=true the app auto-logs in via getSelfHostedUser and does not verify JWTs, but the same secret still keys better-auth and, via a sibling fallback in lib/encryption.ts, email-credential encryption. causal_research.bug_semantics: XKB SetMap stack buffer overflow (CWE-121, ZDI-CAN-30161). _XkbSetMapChecks (originally ProcXkbSetMap) declares a CARD8 mapWidths[XkbMaxLegalKeyCode+1] stack array of 256 elements. CheckKeyTypes, when XkbSetMapResizeTypes is set, computes nMaps = firstType + nTypes from client-controlled request fields with only a lower bound (XkbNumRequiredTypes) and then writes mapWidthRtrn[i+firstType] / mapWidthRtrn[i] for i in those ranges. The firstType > num_types check uses > rather than >=, so a two-request sequence SetMap(firstType=0, nTypes=255, ResizeTypes) then SetMap(firstType=255, nTypes=10, ResizeTypes) makes nMaps=265 and writes mapWidths[255..264], overflowing into adjacent stack (symsPerKey[]). A local X client can crash the server or escalate if it runs as root. Fixed in xorg-server 21.1.23 and xwayland 24.1.12 by rejecting nMaps > XkbMaxLegalKeyCode+1.
causal_research.flaw_origin: xkb/xkb.c CheckKeyTypes ResizeTypes path nMaps = req->firstType+req->nTypes with no upper bound vs mapWidths[], plus mapWidthRtrn[i+req->firstType] writes, plus CARD8 mapWidths[XkbMaxLegalKeyCode+1] in ProcXkbSetMap. First write in this repo is ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 (2003-11-14, Kaleb Keithley, 'R6.6 is the Xorg base-line'), which adds xkb/xkb.c from /dev/null already containing that pattern. causal_research.bug_semantics: free5GC NEF treats an outbound PFD-subscription notification failure as process-fatal. PfdChangeNotifier.FlushNotifications() asynchronously POSTs a PfdChangeNotification to the stored subscriber notifyUri; on any client error (connection refused, DNS failure, TLS error, timeout) it calls logger.PFDManageLog.Fatal(err). PFDManageLog is a logrus.Entry, so Fatal is os.Exit(1)-equivalent: it bypasses Gin recovery, deferred cleanup, and connection draining and terminates the entire NEF process. An attacker who can create a PFD subscription with an unreachable notifyUri and then trigger a PFD change (AF traffic-influence + PFD subscription + PFD transaction) gets a deterministic NEF crash. The PFD transaction itself returns 201; the exit happens on the async notify. In v4.2.1 the trigger chain is unauthenticated because the NEF SBI route groups lack inbound auth (tracked separately in free5gc#858/#859/#862); this case is the Fatal-on-delivery-failure defect (CWE-617/CWE-755/CWE-20).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated ticket routes accepted a user-controlled numeric ticket id without constraining the selected Ticket to the authenticated user's company_id. GET /ticket/update/{id} exposed another tenant's ticket content and, once attachment support existed, its attachments; POST /ticket/save loaded another tenant's Ticket and then reassigned company_id and saved it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} deleted an arbitrary Ticket while its generic Request type also bypassed TicketDeleteRequest authorization.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A cross-site request can route an authenticated administrator to install_package($package). Through 9.5.0, the method checks canInstallPackages but does not require POST and, when the package has no install-options screen, does not validate any CSRF token before resolving a package already present under DIR_PACKAGES/<handle>/ and invoking PackageService::install(), which executes its package controller as the web server user and can yield RCE.

The same-commit helper is_path_under_parents used os.path.commonpath correctly for cache, so the startswith gate was a distinct, weaker confinement.

Trino OAuth endpoints have no client-supplied redirect_uri/callback query parameter. startOAuth2Challenge issues HTTP 303 to the configured identity-provider authorization URI (NimbusOAuth2Client.createAuthorizationRequest); the OAuth redirect_uri query string on that IdP URL is server-constructed from the request base URI (Web UI: request.getUriInfo().getBaseUri().resolve("/oauth2/callback"); CLI/token exchange: externalUriInfo.absolutePath("/oauth2/callback")). Authorization-code theft as described in issue 29754 additionally requires the IdP to accept an unregistered redirect_uri, which RFC 6749 forbids and which Trino docs require operators to register as the exact coordinator callback.

docs/src/main/sphinx/security/oauth2.md: 'Set the callback/redirect URL to https://<trino-coordinator-domain-name>/oauth2/callback' when configuring the authorization server. RFC 6749 §3.1.2.3 requires the authorization server to match a registered redirection URI.

Airlift RejectForwardedRequestCustomizer rejects any header whose name starts with 'x-forwarded-' with HTTP 406 unless process-forwarded is ACCEPT/true. Trino 481 depends on airlift 424, which includes that reject-by-default behavior (airlift#1183, 2024-06-05).

causal_research.reasoning: Vulnerability-first review of CVE-2026-16336 against the assigned clone shows the advisory is factually wrong, not an unpatched Trino CWE-601. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED (VulDB CNA) and the GHSA is an unreviewed import with null withdrawn_at; NVD is Deferred. Vendor disposition is silence on still-open issue 29754, which is not a withdrawal, but the claimed mechanism does not exist in code. ExternalUriInfo has no redirect_uri argument; no OAuth resource accepts a redirect/callback query parameter. Trino's browser redirect on challenge start is to the configured IdP authorization endpoint. The OAuth redirect_uri value is derived from the request the client already made (Host/base URI, plus X-Forwarded-Prefix only as a path prefix). X-Forwarded-Host/Proto/Prefix cannot be injected in the default deployment because Airlift rejects x-forwarded-* unless operators opt in to http-server.process-forwarded behind a TLS-terminating proxy that is trusted to set those headers. The residual story in issue 29754 (IdP wildcard redirect_uri matching) is an authorization-server misconfiguration contrary to RFC 6749 and to Trino's own OAuth setup docs, not an open redirect implemented by Trino. No BIC or fix SHA is recorded because FALSE_POSITIVE does not require one; later history was still checked and contains no redirect_uri pin that would recharacterize this as a patched real bug.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated n8n member could keep attacker-controlled responseText containing script while making the expression-capable respondWith parameter resolve to redirect. renderFormCompletion read responseText independently of the response mode, omitted its sandbox Content-Security-Policy for redirect, and passed the raw value to a Handlebars template whose triple-brace responseText branch precedes the redirect branch. A visitor submitting the public form therefore received attacker HTML without the sandbox, allowing script to execute same-origin with the visitor's n8n session.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unified FastAPI server enabled both JWT-protected modules by default while supplying public, hardcoded 39-character HS256 signing secrets for each module. Startup validation checked only that each secret was at least 32 characters and that the two values differed, so both defaults passed. Because TokenAuth.verify_token() trusted any correctly signed token with the module issuer and the route dependencies returned the attacker-controlled sub claim without requiring that client_id to exist, anyone knowing the source could forge a bearer token for an arbitrary client_id and reach authenticated keyserver upload/revocation and telemetry event APIs.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/security/advisories/GHSA-qc6h-gfjh-7qqg names openssl_encrypt_server/config.py, describes hardcoded defaults passing the >=32 check, states affected <1.4.0, and identifies resolution commit 6090a8e.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A user who can configure a Budibase automation can supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) URL to the outgoing-webhook (and later Zapier, n8n, Slack, Discord, and Make.com) step. The server dereferenced that URL with axios/node-fetch without destination validation, so it could reach loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud-metadata, and other internal services (CWE-918). The REST datasource's separate guard was also fail-open by default because an unset BLACKLIST_IPS produced an empty list and isBlacklisted returned false; it neither protected automation fetches nor supplied secure defaults.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 first created and registered the executable OUTGOING_WEBHOOK automation. Its run function accepted inputs.url, normalized it only by adding http://, and called axios(request) with no allowlist/denylist or resolved-address check. Commit 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb later changed axios to node-fetch, and a3bb2e0d770fe0c66f0382aebef86faa2bbcc696 renamed/migrated the same step to TypeScript; those are implementation changes preserving the pre-existing SSRF, not introducers. Commit 564c724be11895fa6bc1766aef3a149fae3223e3 later added an opt-in REST-only blacklist whose empty-default behavior left that separate path unprotected when BLACKLIST_IPS was unset.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Netty codec-dns encodes and decodes DNS domain names without RFC 1035 size/content checks. On encode, a user-influenced name is split on '.' and each label's Java length is written as a single length byte followed by the raw bytes (ByteBufUtil.writeAscii / getBytes), so a NUL in a label is emitted, a label >63 can write 0xC0-0xFF (compression-pointer range), an empty label historically terminated or truncated the rest of the name, and the total encoded name can exceed 255 octets. On decode, each non-pointer length byte is trusted: the decoder only checks that that many bytes exist, then appends them to an unbounded StringBuilder, so a malicious DNS response can produce labels >63 and decoded names >255. Downstream resolvers, caches, and allowlists that assume RFC 1035 names can then disagree with Netty (cache poisoning / validation bypass) or spend unbounded memory. The 2026 fix rejects empty interior labels, labels >63, embedded NULs, and names >255 on encode, and throws TooLongFrameException for decoder label >63 or decoded name >255.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ProcXFixesSetClientDisconnectMode in xfixes/disconnect.c does a REQUEST() cast of the client request buffer and then copies stuff->disconnect_mode without REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH. A local X11 client can send a shorter-than-struct SetClientDisconnectMode request so the CARD32 disconnect_mode field is filled from leftover bytes still sitting in the shared request buffer from a previous request, leaking residual request data (CWE-200). The swapped-client SProc only used REQUEST_AT_LEAST_SIZE, which still does not enforce an exact request length. The sibling GetClientDisconnectMode handler in the same file already used REQUEST_SIZE_MATCH, so the missing check is specific to Set.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2025-49177 (CNA Red Hat, updated 2026-06-30) and GHSA-pw35-9xmg-v8xw (withdrawn_at null) describe a real XFIXES request-length leak; not withdrawn/rejected. causal_research.bug_semantics: In Basic Authentication, check_request in src/basic_auth.rs returns 401 immediately when the supplied username does not equal the configured userid, and only then calls bcrypt::verify on the password. Invalid usernames therefore skip the expensive bcrypt path while valid usernames always pay that cost, producing a measurable response-time gap that lets an unauthenticated attacker enumerate valid usernames (CWE-204).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Composer Perforce::generateP4Command() built a single shell string by concatenating the p4 executable with unescaped -u (user), -c (client), and -p (port) values, then ProcessExecutor::execute() ran that string via the shell. A payload such as url=localhost:1666; touch /tmp/pwned becomes `p4 -u … -p localhost:1666; touch /tmp/pwned …`; the shell still executes the injected command if p4 is missing. Dependency composer.json files are not a vector. Distinct from GHSA-gqw4-4w2p-838q (unescaped $sourceReference on sync) and from later rsh:/jsh: P4PORT transport execution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Langchain-Chatchat's uploaded-file handler derives file_id as URL-safe base64 of purpose/date/filename. evidence: GitHub commit 4507c7078486ee95778bad6a96840f421dec98c0 shows one parent a1429a350a1433d548680f2a712b2aec205562e4 and adds _get_file_id returning base64.urlsafe_b64encode(f"{purpose}/{today}/{filename}".encode()).decode(), together with the decoding file-path and content/delete routes.

PR #3573 exposes exactly one pre-squash member, 4507c7078486ee95778bad6a96840f421dec98c0; upstream landing 27f0f512a37db4b816da543ca566b0e70d395f4d has the same 107-addition/5-deletion patch and one parent a1429a350a1433d548680f2a712b2aec205562e4.

The path history shows 5c650a8 as a 100%-similarity move from chatchat-server/.../openai_routes.py to libs/chatchat-server/.../openai_routes.py, preserving rather than introducing the vulnerable lines.

The v0.3.0 tag contains the deterministic encoder and reversible decoder. The published CVE record marks versions 0.3.1.0 through 0.3.1.3 affected, while the GitHub advisory reports <=0.3.1.3 and no patched version.
Current upstream master still contains the same deterministic _get_file_id implementation. Issue #5464 has no linked development branch or pull request, so no direct fix commit is available.

potential_fix.approach: Generate a cryptographically random opaque identifier for each upload, store the identifier-to-file metadata mapping server-side, and authorize every read, overwrite, and delete against the owning principal.
potential_fix.rationale: An unpredictable identifier removes the date/filename guessing oracle, while server-side ownership checks prevent possession or construction of an identifier from granting access.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated caller of BrokerView.addNetworkConnector or addConnector (Jolokia /api/jolokia exec on org.apache.activemq:* when activemq-http is present) can pass a first-stage http:// discovery URI. HTTPDiscoveryAgent polls that registry and treats each response line as a service URI with no scheme validation. DiscoveryNetworkConnector then connects to that second-stage URI. causal_research.bug_semantics: When forgotten-password recovery is enabled, forgot_send.cgi builds the reset URL as get_webmin_email_url() + '/forgot.cgi?id=' + token and emails it. Commit f5305eb06577f96af6e1fef3e989ff9a2678b695 taught get_webmin_email_url() to prefer the attacker-controlled HTTP Host header over the configured/system hostname whenever HTTP_HOST is present. A network attacker who can reach the reset form sets Host to an attacker domain, causing the mailed link to point at that domain with a valid reset token. If the victim opens it, the attacker captures the token and completes reset on the real Webmin instance. Pre-f5305eb0 the same CGI used a hostname from config/miniserv/get_system_hostname(), so Host injection into the mail URL was not this mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan is a denylist scanner: it disassembles pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL imports and marks a global Dangerous only when its module is in _unsafe_globals (historically _suspicious_globals) and the name matches '*' or the listed function. profile.Profile.runctx is a stdlib method that exec()s a statement string, so a pickle __reduce__ returning (Profile.runctx, (Profile(), payload, {}, {})) yields RCE on pickle.load(). Before 0.0.29 the 'profile' module was absent from the denylist, so GLOBAL profile/Profile.runctx was not counted as Dangerous/infected and the scan could be treated as clean. Attack path: craft pickle with that reduce gadget -> victim scans with picklescan -> no dangerous hit -> pickle.load() executes payload.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Archive extraction trusted attacker-controlled archives.FileInfo.LinkTarget values. The default, strip, and filtered handlers passed those values to os.Symlink without proving that the link resolved beneath the extraction root, so a crafted relative target such as ../../../../etc/shadow could create an escaping symlink and later archive entries could read or overwrite files outside the destination.

causal_research.bug_semantics: After scoped access tokens exist, several privileged admin routes still authorize only on user.IsAdmin and omit RequireScopes, so a deliberately limited admin access token (for example echo:read) can call /api/inbox, /api/panel/comments*, /api/addConnect, /api/delConnect/:id, and /api/migration/*. Backup export is a stronger variant: /api/backup/export is public, reparses a query JWT, and rebuilds viewer.NewUserViewer(claims.Userid), dropping token type, scopes, audience, and jti before ExportBackup, so the same low-scope token can download a full backup ZIP.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated HTTP clients can force the TSA to allocate O(n) memory while parsing a request. api.getContentType reads the Content-Type header and calls strings.Split on the substring `application/` with no occurrence cap, so a header containing many copies of that token produces a large []string of substrings. Independently, api.ParseJSONRequest JSON-unmarshals tsaPolicyOID and calls strings.Split on `.` with no component cap, so a long dotted OID produces another large []string plus an int slice of similar length. Both values are attacker-controlled (header and JSON body). Go's strings.Split has no internal bound, which is CWE-405 amplification. The December 2025 fix rejects OID strings with more than 128 dots (RFC 2578) and Content-Type values that do not contain exactly one `application/`, then uses SplitN.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On an installation whose active cluster credential was the compiled-in default, any network client that copied the public source constant into X-WolfStack-Secret passed require_auth() as the synthetic cluster-node principal without a session, API key, or user account. That principal could call management endpoints, including POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec, which passed attacker-controlled command text to sh -c inside the selected Docker or LXC container as root.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc replaced the parent implementation's per-node, randomly generated /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key with one source-published CLUSTER_SECRET shared by every installation and made load_cluster_secret() return that constant. The pre-existing request gate compared X-WolfStack-Secret with state.cluster_secret without any source-address or recorded-peer check, so this replacement converted possession of public source text into authentication.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names human author and committer Paul C <paulc@wolf.uk.com> and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI attribution, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wolfsoftwaresystemsltd/WolfStack/security/advisories/GHSA-r3mw-2wmq-j6jg states affected versions <=25.9.1, patched version 25.9.2, the any-source X-WolfStack-Secret bypass, the cluster-node identity, and the container exec impact. It limits affected configurations to nodes still using/falling back to the built-in default; nodes already rotated to a per-install secret were not affected.

git log -L 25,32:src/auth/mod.rs v25.9.1 and git log -S of the exact constant identify 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc as the first commit that writes CLUSTER_SECRET. Its focused diff replaces CLUSTER_KEY_PATH plus random UUID generation/persistence with the fixed source constant and CLUSTER_SECRET.to_string(); Cargo.toml changes 5.9.3 to 5.9.4 in the same implementation commit. An all-ref -S search found no earlier copy of the constant.

Direct parent-tree verification: git grep of the exact constant at a05c0870a84981d639067719de6be2395c958852 exits 1 with no match. parent:src/auth/mod.rs instead reads /etc/wolfstack/cluster.key, generates two random UUID-derived values when absent, persists the result, and chmods it 0600. Thus the public shared credential mechanism is absent in the immediate parent.

At the BIC tree, src/api/mod.rs require_auth() reads X-WolfStack-Secret, compares it against state.cluster_secret, and returns cluster-node on equality, with no peer/source check. At v25.9.1, src/api/mod.rs:7144-7153 shows POST /api/containers/{runtime}/{id}/exec guarded only by require_auth() before invoking sh -c with the supplied command.

Lifecycle history explains but does not replace the BIC: c8e3c7f08ba3c4a172e311ecd83b0419ebd4a6c1 temporarily removed the constant for a per-install secret in 11.26.3; 15772636355c6159d6c2dd6a608265ac65f4c208 restored it in 11.26.4 to repair inter-node communication. Because 15772636355c6159d6c2dd6a608265ac65f4c208 is a revert/reintroduction of lines first authored by 2d2d371527bde1e9d72eadcd2ee3e7c0ee3adfbc, it is not the smallest original BIC. Later custom-secret rotation retained the built-in value as a fallback, leaving unrotated/read-failure configurations exposed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Traefik BasicAuth is supposed to run a dummy password-hash comparison when the username is missing so that existing-user bcrypt (~tens of ms) and missing-user paths take similar time. The CVE-2026-32595 mitigation stored a fallback secret by taking a value from the username→hash map and then indexing that map again with the hash as if it were a username. Because hashes are not keys, the fallback is always the empty string. On a missing user, goauth.CheckSecret(password, "") does not match a bcrypt/apr1/SHA prefix and compareMD5HashAndPassword returns immediately, restoring a network-visible timing oracle that enumerates valid usernames. Existing users with a wrong password still pay the real hash cost.

Symfony's ParamConverter loaded any Invoice by numeric id and the handler serialized it, with no CustomerVoter 'access' check on invoice.getCustomer(). ROLE_TEAMLEAD grants view_invoice, so a teamlead assigned only to Team B could read invoices for customers assigned exclusively to Team A (IDOR / CWE-285, CWE-862). The collection endpoint scoped results via InvoiceArchiveQuery::setCurrentUser() (later BaseApiController::prepareQuery), but the single-item path bypassed that query. The web downloadAction already required is_granted('access', subject.getCustomer()) on the invoice.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated Core-protocol connection could send a FEDERATION_DOWNSTREAM_CONNECT packet on the federation channel. causal_research.bug_semantics: Netmaker exposed an HTTP handler that terminates the server process with syscall.Kill(Getpid(), SIGINT). As shipped this was POST /api/server/shutdown in controllers/server.go serverHandlers, registered with no Authorize, allowUsers, or logic.SecurityCheck wrapper while neighboring /api/server routes used those wrappers. HttpMiddlewares carried no authentication (only an optional Pro unlicensed-API gate), so any network client could POST the endpoint and interrupt the process. With a restart supervisor this produced cyclic denial of service at roughly 3-second intervals. CVE-2026-29771 / GHSA-rhr9-hgcm-x289 (CWE-404); CVSS 4.0 PR:N matches the unauthenticated registration. The first code-level patch wrapped the handler in logic.SecurityCheck(true).

causal_research.bug_semantics: CheckAuth() is the gin middleware on essentially every /api/* route. After cookie/session auth, it independently accepts HTTP Basic Auth whose password is the workspace lock-screen secret Conf.AccessAuthCode (username = util.WorkspaceName). A match sets RoleAdministrator and continues. Unlike LoginAuth(), this branch never consults NeedCaptcha()/WrongAuthCount and, before the fix, never incremented any failure counter or applied a delay/lockout. An unauthenticated network attacker can therefore send unlimited Basic Auth guesses against any CheckAuth-guarded endpoint (for example /api/system/getConf) until the access code is found, obtaining full administrator API access. The same branch used a non-constant-time Go string == comparison, which the advisory treats as a contributing CWE-208 timing leak.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An administrator who can view /dashboard/pages/types/form posts ptComposerFormLayoutSetControlCustomTemplate when saving a page-type composer form layout control. Through 9.5.0 the save path (getPostedTemplate / earlier tools/composer/form/edit_control.php) accepted that string after HTML-only sanitizeString, which does not strip ../, and stored it in PageTypeComposerFormLayoutSetControls. On composer render, FormLayoutSetControl::render() passes the stored filename into CorePageProperty::render (and BlockControl::render). Those methods concatenate the attacker-controlled segment into Environment::getRecord / FileLocator paths (AbstractLocation::contains uses getPath().'/'.$file and filesystem exists with no canonical jail) and include the resolved file. A traversal such as ../../../../application/files/<id>/evil.png therefore becomes local file inclusion of any readable path. Combined with upload validation that keys on extension only, a PHP payload saved as .png yields authenticated RCE. The 9.5.1 fix allowlists the posted template against getPageTypeComposerControlCustomTemplates() so traversal strings never persist.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A crafted Juniper-Ethernet pcap can advertise unsupported extension media/encapsulation while still being long enough for dlt_jnpr_ether_decode() to treat the post-extension bytes as Ethernet. A successful en10mb subdecoder decode is followed by tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state(), which assigns the subcontext-owned decoded_extra allocation directly to the outer context. Cleanup then traverses the outer context and the recursively owned subcontext; dlt_linuxsll2_cleanup() frees each context's decoded_extra pointer, so the aliased allocation is freed twice and tcprewrite aborts or corrupts memory.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6 introduced the Juniper subdecoder lifecycle as one cohesive feature: it created an en10mb subcontext, copied subdecoder state by borrowing the decoded_extra pointer without transferring or recording ownership, and recursively destroyed the subcontext during outer cleanup. It also continued to decode Juniper payloads as Ethernet without validating the extension-declared media type and encapsulation. Those combined lines first created the aliased-ownership double-free path; later aggregate/import commit 77387f1580220c1232a9091c79d0db83ba7ac5b0 merely reintroduced the already-existing mechanism into the 4.0 line.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MISMATCH RESOLVED: the advisory's getJoinedRooms title is naming-only; the patched code path is getVisibleRooms (merge message says 'Validate room upgrade relationships in MatrixClient::getJoinedRooms' but touches getVisibleRooms; the HTTP API getJoinedRooms at /joined_rooms, unchanged since ~2018 and still present in both ff89c9ec and 43c72d5b, never touches predecessor/tombstone state and is unaffected). Mechanism: getVisibleRooms() trusted each room's own m.room.create predecessor pointer (later also MSC3946 dynamic predecessor) as proof of a genuine upgrade and hid any tombstoned room whose roomId appeared in some other room's predecessor pointer, so an attacker-supplied unrelated room whose create event names a tombstoned room could make that tombstoned room disappear from the visible list (CWE-345, insufficient verification of data authenticity). BIC 962ec7bb (2018-08-22, single-parent commit on 52fad6ae) adds MatrixClient.prototype.getVisibleRooms to src/client.js, filtering allRooms via each room's m.room.create content.predecessor plus the room's own m.room.tombstone, with no tombstone/replacement_room cross-check; parent 52fad6ae has NO getVisibleRooms at all, so absence of the vulnerable filtering logic at the parent is direct evidence the vulnerability's enabling code (not just a hardening) was introduced by this commit. The direct fix 43c72d5b (2025-09-16, Michael Telatynski <7t3chguy@gmail.com>, 'Merge commit from fork') rewrites getVisibleRooms in src/client.ts to collect predecessors through findPredecessorRooms(..., verifyLinks=true) and only hide a room whose predecessor room reciprocally has a tombstone naming it as replacement_room; leavesRoomChain's call to getRoomUpgradeHistory gained verifyLinks=true; adds a regression test 'should ignore room replacements which are not reciprocated by the predecessor'. The merge's full stat is 2 files (+30/-14: src/client.ts, spec/unit/matrix-client.spec.ts), so the security patch is the minimum viable repair. OSV GIT fixed 4a9006aea68f9d4d7fad3965e754e89b03fb286f is exactly tag v38.2.0 and has 43c72d5b as its direct parent (43c72d5b is an ancestor of the v38.2.0 marker), so the release-marker boundary is confirmed: vulnerable in <= 38.1.0, fixed in 38.2.0. causal_research.bug_semantics: Default `agent-coderag sync <path>` always calls `CodeRAGManager.sync_dependencies()`. If the target tree contains `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts`, `_sync_gradle()` prefers a repository-local `gradlew`/`gradlew.bat` over PATH `gradle` with no integrity check, then `_execute_gradle_init()` runs that binary via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(..., cwd=repo_root)`. A crafted wrapper therefore executes with the victim's OS privileges during ordinary indexing. Affected pip `agent-coderag` `<= 1.3.0`; first patched version `1.3.1`. GHSA-wg5p-8h9p-3mr7 is GitHub-reviewed, not withdrawn, and has no CVE identifier.
evidence: GHSA-wg5p-8h9p-3mr7 (https://github.com/naranor/agent-coderag/security/advisories/GHSA-wg5p-8h9p-3mr7 and https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wg5p-8h9p-3mr7): reviewed GitHub advisory, withdrawn_at=null, identifiers=[GHSA only], cve_id=null, nvd_published_at=null; pip agent-coderag vulnerable_version_range '<= 1.3.0', first_patched_version 1.3.1; mechanism is unconditional local gradlew execution during default sync.
GitHub Advisories API 2026-08-29: type=reviewed, cve_id=null, withdrawn_at=null; no CVE.org/NVD record exists because no CVE was assigned (not a withdrawn/rejected CVE).

Call chain at BIC b6bb9d7f25dc37497ecae03048f4e79d7249ed0c: code_rag/entry/cli.py:107 `await manager.sync_dependencies(args.path or ".")`; code_rag/core/manager.py:36-47 `sync_dependencies` detects `build.gradle*` and calls `_sync_gradle(root)`; manager.py:109-122 prefers `root/gradlew` or `gradlew.bat` then `shutil.which('gradle')`; manager.py:151-160 `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(gradle_bin, '-q', '--init-script', ..., 'printCodeRagCP', cwd=str(root))`.

Parent verification: `git rev-parse b6bb9d7^` = c32d5030b465a2feda946792f48a6ae0733160cb. `git grep gradle_wrapper|gradlew|_execute_gradle_init|printCodeRagCP` on that parent for manager.py is empty. Parent `_sync_gradle` is only `logger.warning('Gradle dependency sync not yet implemented')`. `git log -L 108,160:code_rag/core/manager.py b6bb9d7` starts at b6bb9d7 replacing the stub with wrapper selection and the subprocess sink.

Earlier `5b2a0874ac3cac9672768784d02048529fddc9cb` introduced the `_sync_gradle` stub and Maven `create_subprocess_exec` of PATH `mvn` only; it is not this ACE. `git log --all --reverse -S gradle_wrapper` first hits b6bb9d7, then the fix. `git log --all --reverse -S printCodeRagCP` first hits b6bb9d7.

PR #23 rebase twin `596b2fd88159b6441367645ca135d303cab65eea` has the identical `code_rag/core/manager.py` blob `98cfc80fdd547d27874f65f1b68b28a4eeee905b` and the same message, but is not an ancestor of v1.3.0/main and sits on no advertised ref; it is a 1:1 rewrite, not a finer gradle-only public member. squash_decomposed=false.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /images handler accepts request.query.src and passes it to imageProcessor. For any value beginning with http:// or https://, imageProcessor treats it as external, skips all local-path validation, and calls fetch(src) without a destination allowlist or network-address restriction. An attacker can therefore make the EverShop server request attacker-selected external or internal HTTP(S) resources, including link-local metadata services, producing blind SSRF.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 created both the front-store images handler and imageProcessor.ts. Its newly written external-URL branch classified a URL only by its http/https prefix and then directly executed fetch(src); the validation in the same function applied only to non-external filesystem paths. This is the first repository commit that contains both the public request path and the flawed server-side fetch mechanism, not a later move, refactor, revert, or release aggregate.

At tag v2.1.0, packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts reads request.query.src and passes it to imageProcessor. In packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts, lines 74-75 recognize only the http/https prefix, lines 177-204 enter the external branch and call fetch(src), and lines 210-211 consume the response body. The local-path restrictions are confined to the !isExternalUrl branch.

git log -L 202,211:packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts v2.1.0 follows the vulnerable fetch block directly to new-file commit 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143. git blame -L 74,77 -L 177,211 v2.1.0 attributes the classifier and entire external-fetch block to the same commit. git log --all -S'const response = await fetch(src)' for that path returns only its addition in 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 and removal in fix af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7.

git show 5ed5ba31913ae69d617089988aa4ffe8015d6143 shows both packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts and packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts added from /dev/null. Direct parent-tree verification: git cat-file -e 753e8aeac5e7a9753731a8ad0f449c05cb2fa61e:packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/services/imageProcessor.ts fails because the path is absent, and the identical check for packages/evershop/src/modules/cms/pages/frontStore/images/images.ts also fails. Fix lifecycle: the immediate parent b6333774b58359c806683c3135efba41af20cd69 of af6e6fd935c4194668b11a924b847542598941f7 still contains const response = await fetch(src). causal_research.bug_semantics: CRuby Nokogiri with packaged libraries compiles a pinned libxml2 tarball and links it into the native extension. Before 1.13.9 the last released pin was libxml2 2.9.14, which is before the libxml2 2.10.3 fixes. CVE-2022-40304: xmlCreateEntity stored short entity content (and ExternalID/SystemID) in the document dict; when an entity-reference cycle was detected, libxml2 zeroed the first byte of that content, corrupting the dict entry and later allowing double-free / logic errors while parsing crafted DTD entities. CVE-2022-40303: with XML_PARSE_HUGE (Nokogiri ParseOptions::HUGE), parser length counters in parser.c could overflow (negative 2GB offsets / missing HUGE-mode caps) on multi-gigabyte input. CVE-2022-2309 (NULL deref in iterwalk/canonicalize) is cited by the Nokogiri advisory but maintainers found it does not affect Nokogiri users. Sink is process crash or memory corruption in the packaged libxml2 parser, not Nokogiri Ruby code.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker can place OSC/CSI control bytes in a filesystem entry name. When a user scans that entry in `dua i`, marks it, and quits without deleting it, the marked `PathBuf` is taken from the TUI mark pane. After `drop(terminal)` has restored the real terminal, the program passed `path.display()` directly to `println!`. No encoding or control-character filtering occurred at that output boundary, so a terminal emulator interpreted the embedded bytes rather than displaying an inert path, enabling such effects as terminal-title spoofing or clipboard manipulation.

That commit first created both the attacker-controlled path flow and the unsanitized post-TUI terminal sink; its immediate parent contains neither the extraction helper nor this print loop.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated Webmin user with Squid module access and the cms (Cache Manager Statistics) ACL can request squid/cachemgr.cgi with a query string. miniserv.pl URL-decodes a no-'=' query into $queryargs and splits it on whitespace into @ARGV. cachemgr.cgi then builds a shell command via two-arg open(MGR, "$mgr ".join(" ", @ARGV)." |") (and the POST variant with <$temp). Unquoted ARGV shell metacharacters therefore execute as the Webmin daemon user (typically root). The 2.600 fix quotemeta()s each argument before the same open() calls.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TagReference.create() accepted caller-controlled path/reference positionals and passed them directly as (path, reference) to repo.git.tag() without an option terminator or unsafe-option inspection. A reference such as --file=/secret was therefore parsed by git tag as its file-input option, and GitPython returned the file contents through the annotated tag message. The later kwargs-only guard inspected Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), so it still omitted both vulnerable positional values.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-915 mass assignment in @adonisjs/lucid BaseModel.merge() (propagating to fill/create/updateOrCreate and bulk writers) and later $consumeAdapterResult(). After column/relation checks, any payload key that passes this.hasOwnProperty(key) is assigned with this[key] = value. Internal ORM fields ($attributes, $original, $isPersisted, $isDeleted, $preloaded, $extras, $sideloaded, fillInvoked, forceUpdate, and similar) are initialized as own instance properties, so they satisfy that check. Unfiltered input such as request.all() can therefore set $isPersisted and force save() down the UPDATE path, overwrite $attributes/$original, or flip $isDeleted. Applications that drop unknown keys with a strict allowlist are not affected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated GET /ccm/system/summary_template/render/{categoryHandle}/{memberIdentifier}/{templateID} is routed to Concrete\Controller\Backend\SummaryTemplate::render. That controller extends Controller, not Backend\UserInterface, so it never runs a canAccess() permission check. render() resolves the summary category driver, loads the page or calendar event by attacker-supplied memberIdentifier (PageDriver: Page::getByID($identifier, 'ACTIVE')), loads the named summary template, and the view calls Renderer::renderSummaryForObject(). Extractors (BasicPageDriver::extractData) populate title, collection path/link, description, and author. Any visitor who knows or enumerates a page/event ID and a configured summary template ID therefore learns that private, draft, or restricted objects exist and receives those metadata fields. The 9.5.1 fix refuses missing objects and requires canViewRenderedSummaryTemplates (page: canEditPageTemplate; calendar event: canEditCalendar).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated web-console queue browse (QueueBrowseServlet) accepts a JMS selector query parameter and also binds every request parameter onto the chosen MessageRenderer through IntrospectionSupport.setProperties. SimpleMessageRenderer advertised a public setContentType setter defaulting to text/xml, so an attacker can send contentType=text/html and force the XML-shaped browse response to be served as HTML (CWE-915). printHeader then interpolates browser.getMessageSelector() (and queue/message id) into attribute context with writer.print and no escaping (CWE-79). A selector that is valid enough to create a QueueBrowser and contains HTML/script therefore executes in the victim browser while viewing queues. The 2026 fix removes the content-type setters and XML-escapes those fields.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Freeform form editors may set a Submission Title that is evaluated as Twig when a submission is stored. The 5.10.16 fix removes `call` and stops passing PHP callables into CP Twig.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The Vision Chat paste-image handler derives the uploaded PNG filename from MD5(PIL.Image.tobytes()). PIL tobytes() serializes pixel or palette-index bytes but omits image dimensions, mode, palette, and transparency metadata, so visually different palette images can share the same digest and filename. In a shared instance, a second upload can overwrite the first file, and the vision model later fetches attacker-controlled content through the unchanged file URL.

causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan is a pickle/PyTorch-model scanner whose security control is a module/name denylist. It disassembles pickle opcodes, collects GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL imports, and marks a global Dangerous only if the module is in the denylist and the name matches ("*" or an explicit set). timeit.timeit() is a stdlib helper that execs/evals the supplied statement (and can therefore import os and run os.system). Before 0.0.25 the denylist had no "timeit" entry, so a payload class whose __reduce__ returns (timeit.timeit, ('', 'import os; os.system(...)')) is classified Suspicious or not reported at all; issues_count and infected_files stay 0; the CLI summary shows a clean scan; pickle.load() then executes the statement. Source: incomplete _suspicious_globals/_unsafe_globals. Sink: _build_scan_result_from_raw_globals / original scan_pickle_bytes lookup that only increments issues for listed names. Attack path: attacker ships a malicious .pkl/.pt; victim trusts picklescan; victim deserializes.

causal_research.bug_semantics: After password login, Scheb issues a TwoFactorToken and a KIMAI_SESSION cookie while the browser is held at /auth/2fa. ApiRequestMatcher.matches() returns false for requests that already have a session (`return !$request->hasPreviousSession()`), so /api/* is served by the session firewall rather than the stateless API firewall. access_control then required only IS_AUTHENTICATED for `^/api`. A TwoFactorToken is a real non-anonymous token, so IS_AUTHENTICATED is true and Scheb TwoFactorAccessDecider lets the request through; web routes stay blocked because they need ROLE_USER. From 2.15 onward controllers use #[IsGranted('API')]; ApiVoter grants that attribute to any User (default EVERYONE has api_access; from 2.18 session tokens `return true`) and did not reject TwoFactorTokenInterface. Replaying the pre-TOTP cookie therefore yields full authenticated API access without the second factor.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Horizon generates downloadable OpenRC bash scripts that interpolate the current Keystone project/tenant name into a double-quoted assignment (historically OS_TENANT_NAME, later also OS_PROJECT_NAME). Django HTML auto-escape does not neutralize `$`, and the dedicated shellfilter later escaped only `\` ` ' " — not `$` or `!`. A privileged actor can create a project whose name contains `$(cmd)` (Launchpad PoC: openstack project create 'hzn01-$(printf${IFS}...|base64${IFS}-d|sh)'). A victim who downloads the RC file from the API Access panel and sources it executes that command in their local shell (CWE-78). Exploit needs project-create (typically domain/admin) plus user interaction. CVE.org PUBLISHED this as CWE-78 affecting Horizon from 8.0.0 until 25.3.3/25.5.3/25.7.4; OpenStack VMT declined an OSSA (class D / OSSN-0097, OSSA status Won't Fix) and called it hardening against user error, but still shipped OSSN-0097 and merged a code fix. The CVE is not rejected or withdrawn.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The runner registration-token API exposed token creation through GET routes. The token-scope middleware derives Read versus Write from the HTTP method and classifies GET as Read, but shared.GetRegistrationToken creates a runner token when no active token exists and returns it. A leaked read-scoped user, organization, repository, or admin token could therefore obtain a runner registration credential and register a malicious Actions runner able to receive workflow jobs with access to repository source and secrets.

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS accepted a lexically resolved template pathname as proof that the file opened was inside a configured root, partials, or layouts directory. Node then followed symlinks at the file operation, so a symlink placed under an allowed template directory could point to an arbitrary readable file outside that directory and include, render, or layout would parse and render the external target. The assigned advisory records liquidjs <= 10.25.2 as vulnerable and 10.25.3 as the first patched version.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 8fbbec089fa4e3db4bec47462b1c08dd65c36648 is the smallest real BIC. Although the commit also moved existing modules, its newly added index.js handleCache() resolved an include name with path.resolve(this.options.root, filepath) and passed that non-canonical pathname to fs.readFileSync(), while the newly added tags/include.js evaluated the include name and called handleCache(). The immediate parent had neither handleCache/renderFile nor tags/include.js, so the causal filesystem-template load path was absent; later loader extractions, path checks, and file moves merely preserved or re-expressed this same symlink-following flaw.

causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan is a denylist scanner: it disassembles pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL opcodes and flags a file as infected only when (module, name) matches _unsafe_globals (historically _suspicious_globals). CPython lib2to3.pgen2.pgen.ParserGenerator.make_label evals a double-quoted grammar label, so a pickle whose __reduce__ returns (ParserGenerator.make_label, (None, state, '""+__import__("os").system(...)')) executes attacker-controlled code on pickle.load. Before 0.0.30 the denylist had no lib2to3.pgen2.pgen / ParserGenerator.make_label entry (v0.0.29 listed only lib2to3.pgen2.grammar.Grammar.loads), so the gadget was classified Suspicious or ignored, issues_count stayed 0, and a victim who trusted a clean scan would load the pickle and hit RCE.

causal_research.bug_semantics: DaoAuthenticationProvider equalizes username-existence timing by running PasswordEncoder against a dummy hash when UserDetailsService throws UsernameNotFoundException. AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider.authenticate() still invokes DefaultPreAuthenticationChecks (UserDetails.isAccountNonLocked/isEnabled/isAccountNonExpired) before additionalAuthenticationChecks (the real passwordEncoder.matches). causal_research.bug_semantics: The REST frontend registered an /engine-ui proxy whose request path supplied both the destination host and port. EngineUIProxyServlet parsed /engine-ui/<host>:<port>/..., then constructed and issued an HTTP request to that destination without an enable/disable gate or destination allowlist. A remote requester able to reach the proxy could therefore make the Kyuubi server contact arbitrary hosts reachable from the server, yielding SSRF/open-proxy behavior.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A Netty RedisDecoder that handles untrusted RESP treats bulk-string and array headers by calling decodeLength, which uses readLine to scan the cumulative ByteToMessageDecoder buffer for '\n'. If the attacker never sends CRLF after the type byte and a digit stream (for example '$1111...' or '*1111...'), readLine returns null and pre-fix decodeLength returns false with no size check, so the decoder keeps the connection open and appends every subsequent chunk. Direct memory grows until OutOfDirectMemoryError, denying service to other connections. decodeInline already rejected oversize incomplete lines via maxInlineMessageLength; parseRedisNumber's 19-digit bound only runs after a complete line exists, so it is not a defense. The 2026 fix rejects incomplete length prefixes longer than a signed 64-bit decimal (plus sign and CR) and discards the buffer on RedisCodecException.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MessagePackReader.ReadDateTime deserializes a timestamp extension by calling MessagePackPrimitives.TryReadDateTime, which sets tokenSize = checked((int)header.Length) from the attacker-controlled MessagePack extension body length and returns DecodeResult.InsufficientBuffer when the current span is shorter than that size, before checking that only the legal timestamp encodings (4, 8, or 12 bytes) are present. The reader's InsufficientBuffer slow path then does stackalloc byte[tokenSize]. A tiny Ext32 payload can therefore declare a huge timestamp body, force a single-frame stack allocation large enough to throw an uncatchable StackOverflowException, and terminate the host. MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and MaximumObjectGraphDepth do not apply because the crash is not object-graph recursion. The CWE-789 fix is to reject non-{4,8,12} lengths before any insufficient-buffer handling so the slow path never stack-allocates from an untrusted body length.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SiYuan publish mode proxies requests to the kernel with an X-Auth-Token JWT. CheckAuth accepts a valid publish JWT (RoleReader, or the anonymous account when Publish.Auth.Enable is false), so POST /api/asset/resolveAssetPath is reachable without admin role. The handler resolves the caller-supplied relative asset path via GetAssetAbsPath/GetAssetAbsPathInBox and returns the absolute filesystem path in ret.Data with no redaction. A reader who copies an assets/… URL from a published document therefore learns the workspace absolute path, typically embedding the OS username and install layout. Sibling CheckAuth-only inventory APIs getUnusedAssets/getMissingAssets had the same authz gap. The project already treated those paths as sensitive in getConf (HideConfSecret / later browser WorkspaceDir stripping) but did not apply equivalent controls here until CheckAdminRole was added.

causal_research.bug_semantics: AIT CSV Import/Export through 3.0.3 exposed admin/upload-handler.php as a directly reachable unauthenticated multipart upload endpoint. It neither restricted the uploaded file to safe CSV content/types nor prevented a PHP filename from being placed in WordPress's web-executable wp-content/uploads directory. causal_research.evidence: Mechanism: UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.findClosestMethodAnnotations fails to locate @PreAuthorize on a method inherited through an unbounded generic supertype when the subclass does not redeclare the method, so scan() returns null and the PreAuthorize expression is never built (CWE-863 authorization bypass, HIGH per spring.io advisory, credited to Avgustin Marinov). BIC verified by local git: 626610a 'Polish Annotation API' (2024-08-29) is the creation commit of UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.java; diff-tree against parent cc6de8fa shows the file added (status A) together with the rest of the scanner family replacing the AnnotationSynthesizer-based lookup, so the vulnerable traversal is co-extensive with the file itself. The dossier's BIC dc2e1af (gh-16751, authored 2025-01-08, committed 2025-03-17, first tag 6.4.4; parent 4993fa86 verified) is the immediate parent of the fixed line: its diff adds hasSameGenericTypeParameters using ResolvableType.forMethodParameter(candidateMethod, i, sourceDeclaringClass).resolve(). However the fix's own regression scenario (gh-17898: GenericInterfaceImpl with no redeclared processOneAndTwo) already fails on the pre-BIC traversal, which matched overrides only via exact erased signatures getDeclaredMethod(name, Long, Object) against the interface method erased to (Object, Object); the raw 6.4.0 blob shows that original lookup, and the vendor affected range starting at 6.4.0 corroborates it. dc2e1af therefore changed the miss mechanism (unresolved type variable makes .resolve() return null, failing the parameter comparison) rather than introducing the vulnerable class, and is not the true BIC. Minimal fix: e5694ac 'Fallback to Object When Determining Overridden Methods' (gh-17898, 2025-09-15) changes exactly one main-code line, .resolve() to .toClass(), so unresolvable type variables fall back to Object and match the erased root parameter type; it adds the regression test scanWhenAnnotationOnParameterizedUndeclaredMethodAndThenLocates. Merge d0f93fa6d8338149943ae640c53db07de827867f ('Merge branch 6.4.x into 6.5.x', 2025-09-15, second parent = e5694ac) carries the fix into 6.5.x. AI exclusion rests on positive evidence, not trailer absence: calibrating the 6.4.4..e5694ac window shows 297 non-merge commits of which 227 carry trailers and all 227 are Signed-off-by; a repo-wide 2025 body census finds zero Co-authored-by/Generated-with markers, so this repo has no AI-marker convention and marker absence is non-informative. Positive human signals: all four lineage commits are authored by Josh Cummings (2024 creation commit GPG-signed with personal gmail; 2025 commits under his GitHub noreply identity); each closes a distinct upstream issue (gh-16751, gh-17143, gh-17898) in the repo's human-issue workflow; the fix was authored and committed within 15 minutes on 2025-09-15 during same-day security-release cadence with the 6.5.x merge 15 minutes later; Josh has 22 commits in the window with zero AI-marker bodies; the BIC itself (2024-08-29) predates the dossier's 2025 coverage window so the missing-2025-trailer concern does not apply. No AI co-author evidence exists anywhere in the lineage. Version boundaries from git tag ancestry on a full clone: vulnerable traversal first shipped in 6.4.0-M4 then 6.4.0 GA (2024-11-18); dc2e1af first in 6.4.4 (2025-03-17); fix e5694ac is absent from 6.4.9/6.5.3 and present in 6.4.10/6.5.4 (tags 2025-09-15 16:03/16:17 UTC) and all later tags. The spring.io advisory (fetched directly, no API) lists affected 6.4.0-6.4.10 and 6.5.0-6.5.4 with OSS fix versions 6.4.11/6.5.5 and history '2025-09-15: Initial vulnerability report published; 2025-09-17: Updated Affected and Fix versions'.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and made server-side requests whose response data was returned to the caller. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but accepted every ordinary hostname without resolving it, so an attacker could use a hostname resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved address to reach and read an internal HTTPS service. The routes were also callable anonymously, increasing exposure, while the unresolved-hostname allow decision was the SSRF root cause.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 directly added website/web/convert/convert.py::_validate_misp_url and both outbound-request routes. Its ValueError branch used `pass  # it's a domain name — OK`, accepting non-IP hostnames without checking resolved destinations. The same direct feature commit added the unauthenticated request sinks; it was not an import, move, refactor, revert, release commit, or decomposed squash member.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Ech0 globally installed its i18n middleware and passed unauthenticated request-controlled locale values, including the raw Accept-Language header after only TrimSpace, to go-i18n and golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage without a size or shape bound. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 mitigation counted '-' separators but the parser also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB malformed underscore-separated value bypassed the guard and exercised quadratic parsing, allowing unauthenticated CPU denial of service on every route. X-Locale and the lang query parameter also reached the same unbounded parser through ResolveLocale.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 first created Ech0's complete remotely reachable vulnerable path: it added internal/i18n/i18n.go, forwarded unbounded locale values to ParseAcceptLanguage and goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request, and registered the middleware globally. The parser weakness pre-existed in x/text, but the immediate parent did not contain Ech0's i18n parser path or global exposure.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On an MQTT connector, after CONNECT/auth, each inbound control packet encodes Remaining Length as 1–4 continuation bytes (MQTT v3.1.1). MQTTCodec.variableLengthParser (NIO/WebSocket) and MQTTWireFormat.unmarshal (TcpTransport.readCommand loop) both did length += (digit & 0x7F) * multiplier; multiplier <<= 7 with no byte-count cap. A fifth continuation byte overflows Java int so the decoded length wraps; leftover payload bytes are then parsed as additional MQTT frames. Brokers without mqtt transport are out of scope. The 4-byte MAX_MULTIPLIER check rejects a continuation bit on the fourth Remaining Length byte and stops the wrap.

evidence.observed: The 2012 MQTTWireFormat.unmarshal already contains `do { digit = dataIn.readByte(); length += (digit & 0x7F) * multiplier; multiplier <<= 7; } while ((digit & 0x80) != 0);` with only the `length > MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH` value guard - the byte-count bound is absent from the first version.

The MQTTCodec header parser added in 2012 has the same unguarded loop (`digit = input.readByte(); length += (digit & 0x7F) * multiplier; multiplier <<= 7; read++;`), so both decoders of the advisory's mechanism were introduced together with the MQTT transport.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The unbounded Remaining Length decoder was first written in MQTTWireFormat.unmarshal when MQTT support landed in cfc6917a79dd1c5ba3be70edf49a9a70393179ba (Robert Davies, AMQ-3786, svn r1304984, 2012-03-25). Immediate parent 555d8890acc3f743584b37670ee10d124c06e8d2 has no MQTT sources. MQTTCodec later copied the same loop; AMQ-5307 rewrote it into FrameParser form without adding a 4-byte bound.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object cfc6917a79 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the encoder in the same file emits a compliant field (marshal writes at most four bytes via `remaining >>>= 7`), so the defect is decode-only and cannot be reached from a compliant peer. Checked that a size guard still exists but is keyed on the wrapped value: MQTTWireFormat.unmarshal tests `length > getMaxFrameSize()` with MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 256 MiB (MQTTWireFormat.java:40-45) and MQTTCodec tests `length > getMaxFrameSize()` before switching to the content parser, so what is missing is exactly the byte-count bound, not a size limit. Simulated both loops on the wire bytes: the compliant maximum 0xff 0xff 0xff 0x7f decodes to 268435455 and terminates, a 3 MiB payload (0x80 0x80 0xc0 0x01) is accepted by the codec loop, and a continuation chain (0x81 x6 + 0x01) wraps to length 16513, so the overflow is reachable in both decoders.
mechanism.impact: Parser-level integer overflow in the broker's MQTT codec: the Remaining Length guard no longer matches the bytes actually consumed, so attacker-chosen bytes are interpreted as additional MQTT control packets and the broker mis-frames the stream. The advisory rates it CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N (CWE-190) - unexpected broker behavior when talking to a non-compliant client, with limited confidentiality and integrity impact and no availability claim; Java excludes memory-corruption consequences.
mechanism.preconditions: The MQTT transport connector is enabled (the advisory states brokers that do not enable mqtt connectors are not impacted); the attacker has an established, authenticated connection (the advisory places the scenario after authentication); the client sends a non-compliant remaining-length field of five or more bytes with the continuation bit set.
mechanism.summary: MQTT remaining-length decoding in ActiveMQ is not bounded in the number of length bytes: `length += (digit & 0x7F) * multiplier; multiplier <<= 7;` never checks the byte count, so the int multiplier wraps after four continuation bytes and the accumulated length wraps to a small or negative value, defeating the `length > maxFrameSize` guard and letting one malformed packet be re-framed as one or more different MQTT control packets (CWE-190 integer overflow or wraparound).
mechanism.trigger: Open an MQTT connection to a broker with an mqtt transport connector enabled (mqtt:// or mqtt+ssl:// decodes through MQTTWireFormat.unmarshal, mqtt+nio through MQTTCodec.parse), authenticate, then send a control-packet header followed by a remaining-length field with five or more continuation bytes, for example 0x81 0x81 0x81 0x81 0x81 0x81 0x01; the fifth byte is weighted with a wrapped multiplier so the decoded length stays small or goes negative, and the bytes after the wrapped length are consumed as the next MQTT control packet instead of the declared payload.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: activemq-mqtt/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/transport/mqtt/MQTTCodec.java:154-171 (variableLengthParser.parse, unguarded loop at :162-163) and activemq-mqtt/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/transport/mqtt/MQTTWireFormat.java:89-94 (unmarshal) at tag activemq-6.2.0 (tag object 0a0448ef6fe00befff6949fad5583c9edcbe71b1, commit 6d5b6bf45cd80d7a3f3cbb1126f28fac8ffd7fdf); the identical lines are present at tag activemq-5.19.1 (tag object 5be5171d870215e4d62397da3e02bb6a5b978c63, commit 242ff9b0db9f8c0d155876ee3a5092364fb5443d) and were introduced by 4c3843809eecd4948919e0c1690b283e0a69748b (MQTTCodec) and cfc6917a79dd1c5ba3be70edf49a9a70393179ba (MQTTWireFormat).

causal_research.reasoning:
CVE-2025-66168 is a real CWE-190 in ActiveMQ MQTT Remaining Length decoding. The smallest first writer is named-human Robert Davies on 2012-03-25 (cfc6917a); the BIC commit object has no AI marker, so the verdict is NOT_AI. The minimum repair is AMQ-9810 on MQTTCodec (165e80ba) with companion MQTTWireFormat (d0df9e24). 5.19.2 contains those cherries. Originally claimed 6.1.9 was never published and 6.2.1 still ships the unbounded decoder; 6.2.4 received the backport (7ec363bd+4977d14a). Fix-side authors are also named humans; that does not change BIC attribution.
The advisory's single mechanism reproduces in primary code: both MQTT decoders accumulate Remaining Length with `length += (digit & 0x7F) * multiplier; multiplier <<= 7;` and never count length bytes, so the int multiplier wraps after the fourth continuation byte and the decoded length stops matching the bytes actually consumed. The defect sits in two sibling decode loops that arrived with the first MQTT transport in this tree, MQTTWireFormat.unmarshal in cfc6917a79d (2012-03-25, AMQ-3786 initial MQTT files) and MQTTCodec's variable-length parser in 4c3843809ee (2012-04-11, AMQ-3786 NIO support), each verified by showing the file is absent at the immediate parent (git cat-file -e <parent>:<path> rc 128) and by a repo-wide -S search over mqtt paths that returns only those two commits. The fix is the AMQ-9810 pair 165e80bad45 and d0df9e24313 plus the release cherry-picks 3f0720c085b/ebed70bcd22 (5.19.2 through 5.19.10) and 7ec363bdcd6/4977d14a582 (6.2.4 through 6.2.9), which throw as soon as a fifth length byte would be required, and HEAD still carries the guard. The vendor's own follow-up announcement contradicts the GHSA fixed-version ranges by stating the fix was missed in previous 6.x releases until 6.2.4, and the wireformat variant of the guard is additionally off by one byte-count iteration and now rejects spec-legal 4-byte lengths (payloads of 2 MiB or more); both are recorded as residual gaps rather than closed out. Neither BIC commit object contains any AI marker, and both are person-attributed 2012 commits by the same human author with git-svn provenance, which is positive evidence against an AI role rather than an inference from a missing trailer, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
