causal_research.bug_semantics: In policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles, the DEFAULT restore path used find to select entries with unlabeled or undefined SELinux contexts and then invoked a separate privileged chcon process on each pathname. The non-full-cleanup relabel path reached the same code. An attacker controlling a searched directory could replace an intermediate component with a symlink after find checked the entry but before chcon resolved the pathname, causing an arbitrary target such as /etc/shadow to receive the attacker's chosen SELinux label. chcon --no-dereference protected only the final component and did not make the find-to-chcon pathname handoff atomic.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable find-then-chcon mechanism predates the validated Git history. Root object 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549 is an aggregate snapshot named `initial import from svn trunk revision 2950`; it already contains the vulnerable /tmp and /var/tmp commands and has no Git parent. It is therefore a history boundary, not the smallest real BIC. Later commits only changed label selection, broadened the searched directories, moved the existing block, or added final-component --no-dereference handling without originating the race. The pre-r2950 Subversion member revision that first wrote the mechanism is unavailable in the clone.
causal_research.ai_marker: unavailable: the smallest real BIC is a pre-r2950 Subversion member revision with no commit object in the validated Git clone, so its author, committer, message, trailers, and bot identity cannot be inspected; the no-AI metadata on aggregate import 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549 is excluded because that object is not the BIC
evidence: The assigned GHSA bundle describes CWE-367 in fixfiles relabel/restore: a local attacker races the find/chcon handoff by replacing directory components with symlinks, allowing privileged relabeling of arbitrary files. The bundle reports no package-version ranges and identifies a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679 as the upstream fix.

`git show --format=fuller --stat --patch a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679 -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles` shows a one-file direct fix deleting all ten cleanup lines. Its message says that find and chcon re-look up full pathnames and are subject to TOCTOU. `git rev-parse a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679^` returns 7fd20e48504069fe1541f809de7566283f8ec7db.

`git grep -n -E 'find /(tmp|var/tmp|var/run|var/lib/debug).*chcon' 7fd20e48504069fe1541f809de7566283f8ec7db -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles` returns the four vulnerable --no-dereference find/chcon commands at lines 297-300, directly verifying the fix parent's vulnerable state.

`git log --all --follow --format='%H %P %s' -S 'find /tmp' -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles` reaches root import 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549 after later edits. `git grep -n -E 'find /(tmp|var/tmp)|chcon' 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549 -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles` shows the imported snapshot already has separate find/chcon commands for /tmp and /var/tmp; `git show 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549:policycoreutils/VERSION` returns 2.0.54.

`git show --patch 3475893b6f369b880267e920a5604174b6eaa3cd -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles` moves the already-existing cleanup block into a RESTORE_MODE case, so that refactor is rejected as a BIC. `git show --patch 2608b4d6660af0fb8ad93f2cc144bdaab3c2afa8 -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles` only adds --no-dereference to the existing four chcon commands, and `git show --patch 5bd734dd7395a2f6c87546b8e7159b02544405f9 -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles` only replaces hard-coded types with kernel-derived types and --reference; neither originated or eliminated the intermediate-component race.

`git rev-list --parents --max-count=1 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549` prints only that SHA. `git cat-file -p 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549` has no parent header, names Joshua Brindle as author and committer, contains the subject `initial import from svn trunk revision 2950`, and has no AI trailer. Because the object is an aggregate import rather than the smallest BIC, its human identity and absent AI trailer cannot establish NOT_AI.

The listed primary/reviewer marker_state disagreement resolves to `unavailable`. The primary's normalized unavailable state wins: BIC-only attribution cannot be closed without the missing pre-r2950 BIC object. The reviewer's observation that the import object has no AI trailer is factually confirmed, but any interpretation of that observation as a closed NOT_AI marker is rejected because the protocol excludes non-BIC imports. Thus the two reports' underlying Git observations are compatible, while only the primary's explicit unavailable state is a gate-valid marker result.

Version boundary checks resolve `policycoreutils-3.11` to 2233a23a4d4f1bf29054037babec13f30d038e65. The tagged tree still contains all four vulnerable find/chcon commands. `git merge-base --is-ancestor policycoreutils-3.11 a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679` exits 0, the reverse ancestry check exits 1, and `git tag --contains a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679` returns no tags. Therefore released 3.11 is vulnerable and the direct fix lands later on main with no fixed upstream tag in the validated history.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory mechanism is the non-atomic handoff of attacker-influenced pathnames from find to a separate privileged chcon, so final-component --no-dereference handling does not close the race. The direct fix deletes that mechanism, and its immediate parent demonstrably retains it. History tracing reaches an already-vulnerable SVN snapshot at Git root; the intermediate refactor, label-selection edits, scope expansions, and no-dereference change are not first introductions. Protocol therefore forbids naming the root import as the BIC or using its commit-object metadata for AI attribution. This resolves marker_state in favor of the primary's unavailable state rather than a closed NOT_AI conclusion: the true BIC object and its direct predecessor are both outside the validated clone. With no verified smallest BIC or BIC-only marker evidence, the gate-complete outcome is BLOCKED even though the direct fix and vulnerable release boundary are verified.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Obtain authoritative Subversion history before trunk revision 2950, identify the exact member revision that first added the separate find/chcon relabel mechanism, verify the vulnerable lines are absent in its immediate predecessor, and inspect that true BIC revision's original author/committer-equivalent metadata and message/trailers. Until those objects are available, introducer SHA, immediate parent, direct parent absence, squash decomposition, and BIC-only AI attribution remain unverified.

causal_research.bug_semantics: NRF's unauthenticated OAuth2 token endpoint POST /oauth2/token parses application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies by reflecting over models.NrfAccessTokenAccessTokenReq (historically models.AccessTokenReq). String and NF-type fields are SetString(); every other matched yaml-tag field is json.Unmarshal'd into a models.PlmnId and assigned with reflect.Value.Set. When the real field type is a slice ([]PlmnId, []Snssai, []PlmnIdNid, []string) or a different pointer (*PlmnIdNid), Go panics with 'reflect.Set: value of type *models.PlmnId is not assignable to type ...'. Gin recovery converts the panic to HTTP 500 without killing the process, so a remote client can repeatedly trigger expensive stack-trace panics on the token-issuance path. This is parser type-confusion (CWE-843) plus missing input-type validation (CWE-20), not an auth bypass.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In ReadRequestFromClient (os/io.c), an oversized Big Request is not disconnected; leftover payload is tracked as ConnectionInput.ignoreBytes and skipped instead of parsed. After consuming a request, if gotnow becomes 0 the same ConnectionInput buffer is published on AvailableInput and later recycled to another live client via FreeInputs. The share predicate historically checked only !gotnow, so a client that finished a request with leftover ignoreBytes could donate a buffer whose ignoreBytes was still nonzero. The next client then entered the ignoreBytes path and skipped its real request, hanging that client (DoS). CWE-667 / local authenticated availability. First-party fix: only set AvailableInput when !gotnow && !oci->ignoreBytes.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In Saloon before v4, PendingRequest built its destination with URLHelper::join(connector base URL, request resolveEndpoint()). When resolveEndpoint() returned an attacker-controlled absolute URL, URLHelper::join() returned that URL unchanged, discarding the trusted connector host; the request was then authenticated and could be sent to the attacker host with connector/request headers, cookies, or tokens, enabling SSRF and credential disclosure.
evidence: The published CVE.org record for CVE-2026-33182 is PUBLISHED and states that prior to 4.0.0 an absolute resolveEndpoint URL replaced the connector base and received attached authentication material; it identifies 4.0.0 as the fix and links the vendor advisory https://github.com/saloonphp/saloon/security/advisories/GHSA-c83f-3xp6-hfcp.

git diff bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c^ bef86d8bdec2deec452695cac9517b9ec0b63d7c -- src/Helpers/URLHelper.php shows the atomic addition `if (static::isValidUrl($endpoint)) { return $endpoint; }`; git show of parent 161aadb2180a61691d7a6345830ca52531507c25 confirms that early return is absent and the parent joins the base and endpoint.

At v3.15.0, src/Http/PendingRequest.php assigns URLHelper::join(resolveBaseUrl(), resolveEndpoint()) to the destination, then resolves the authenticator and runs MergeRequestProperties and AuthenticatePendingRequest, closing the absolute-endpoint-to-authenticated-request path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In publish mode the kernel mux serves several workspace directories as static HTTP routes behind model.CheckAuth only. CheckAuth treats a publish JWT RoleReader as authenticated, and the publish proxy injects that JWT for reader accounts or, when Publish.Auth.Enable is false, for the anonymous account. GET /templates/<file>.md therefore returns user-authored template Markdown to a reader, while POST /api/file/getFile {"path":"data/templates/<file>.md"} is refused by refuseToAccess for non-administrators. The same CheckAuth-only gap exposes /snippets/* (JS/CSS by name), whole /widgets/, /plugins/, and /emojis/ trees, and /export/* artifacts that lack the publish-path gate /assets/* already had. Confidentiality-only CWE-862: missing authorization on static routes relative to REST/publish-access policy.

causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 4d9cdb9750ceba2bfc634b03b77dc82494742269 added and auto-registered the header-directed RoutingFunction without rejecting a route back to itself or a composition containing itself. Its parent already supported Function-to-Function composition via function1.andThen(function2), so adding this recursively selectable function was the smallest commit that first made the mechanism vulnerable. The later 2023 direct-target guard was incomplete because a composed wrapper has a different target.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle starts when 4d9cdb9750ceba2bfc634b03b77dc82494742269 introduces a catalog-registered router into a catalog that already permits arbitrary Function composition. The immediate parent cannot self-route because RoutingFunction.java and its bean do not exist there, satisfying the parent-absence gate. A 2023 guard prevents lookup of the bare router target but not a composed wrapper such as functionRouter|functionRouter, whose lambda target passes that check and re-enters routing. The advisory-linked 6bcd55803c5a2ce0adec794fee1e03c2fac36cf9 closes the bypass at the composition primitive by rejecting two wrappers with the same definition; public tag ancestry aligns that fix with 4.3.3, and its sibling aligns with 5.0.2. Because the atomic BIC is a normal human-authored commit with no commit-object AI marker, this real vulnerability is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Fluentd's out_http plugin treats the configured endpoint as a placeholder template. At flush time parse_endpoint calls extract_placeholders(@endpoint, chunk) and then URI.parse on the result with no hostname check, so an attacker-controlled tag (or other placeholder) can rewrite the host of the outbound POST/PUT (e.g. endpoint http://${tag}/path to 169.254.169.254 or an internal service). CWE-918 SSRF; patched by requiring allowed_hosts whenever the expanded host differs from the configured host.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PodProbeMarker TCPSocket probes (and later HTTPGet on master) accept an unrestricted Host. kruise-daemon runs with hostNetwork=true, so the daemon dials that Host from the node network namespace and writes probe success/failure plus dial errors into NodePodProbe status. causal_research.bug_semantics: ByteBuffer stores reader/writer indices and capacity as UInt32. The Int-to-UInt32 helpers (_toIndex/_toCapacity, originally toIndex/toCapacity) converted with a truncating initializer, which on 64-bit platforms silently discarded the high 32 bits instead of trapping. Safety preconditions then observed the already-truncated value, so an attacker-influenced Int > UInt32.max (for example 0x100000000) became 0 and passed checks. copyBytes(at:to:length:) reserved/copied using the truncated destination index while ptr.dropFirst(toIndex) still used the original Int, producing an out-of-bounds write. writeWithUnsafeMutableBytes(minimumWritableBytes:) reserved via _toCapacity, so a crafted request larger than UInt32.max yielded a pointer whose length did not match the requested size and could be overflowed on the subsequent write. moveReaderIndex/moveWriterIndex(forwardBy:) and ByteBuffer(takingOwnershipOf:allocator:) wrap logically but do not expose wild pointers. Fixed by switching the helpers to trapping UInt32(_:), leaving truncatingIfNeeded only in getSlice after Int-domain bounds checks.

causal_research.bug_semantics: pyasn1 BER/CER/DER decoders parse OBJECT IDENTIFIER and RELATIVE-OID payloads by walking each sub-identifier octet and growing an immutable tuple with oid += (subId,) (and the multi-octet-arc equivalent). Each concatenation copies all arcs seen so far, so N arcs is O(N^2) CPU. A small crafted substrate (advisory: tens of kilobytes; regression tests: 4096 single-byte 0x01 arcs under tag 0x06/0x0D) makes decode() take seconds, denying service to any consumer of untrusted ASN.1 (certificates, LDAP, SNMP, Kerberos). ObjectIdentifierEncoder and RelativeOIDEncoder have the same quadratic outer-loop concatenation (octets += (subOid,)), reachable when an application re-encodes previously decoded attacker values. CVE-2026-23490 only bounded per-arc continuation-octet length, not arc count. The 0.6.4 fix accumulates into a list (append/extend) and converts to a tuple once.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A RECORD user who can SELECT a table with an array-element SELECT permission (DEFINE FIELD items[*] / field.* PERMISSIONS FOR select) still sees a subset of denied elements. The three filter sites (reduce_document / filter_computed_field_permissions in doc/reduce.rs, the post-projection pass in doc/output.rs, and filter_fields_by_permission in exec/operators/scan/pipeline.rs) expand the field idiom with Value::each, which yields ascending array-index paths, then Value::cut (historically Value::del) does Vec::remove at each index. Removing while walking forwards shifts every later index down, so a deny-all leaks the odd-indexed elements and a per-element WHERE keeps/drops the wrong identities. Non-wildcard field-level SELECT permissions are enforced correctly; root and record-owner sessions skip this filter.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-863 cross-organization authorization bypass on HTTP filestore GET. A root-org user with only the reader role (READ_RESULTS) can call GET /api/v1/DownloadVFSFile with attacker-controlled fs_components pointing under the root filestore prefix orgs/<other_org>/... and read arbitrary files from other orgs. CheckAccess is applied only to the current (root) org; the path is not isolated. The reverse does not work because a sub-org filestore does not contain sibling/root org data.

causal_research.bug_semantics: For a plugin-defined Backend\Widgets\Filter numberrange scope with a conditions string, an authenticated backend user can submit attacker-controlled options.numbers through the filter AJAX handler. numbersFromAjax() used /\d/ as a presence check rather than validating the complete numeric value, so strings containing both a digit and SQL syntax were returned unchanged. applyScopeToQuery() then replaced :min and :max in the configured SQL with those raw strings and passed the result to whereRaw(), allowing the value to alter the SQL statement.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 completed the numberrange AJAX path by adding numbersFromAjax() with the permissive /\d/ check and unchanged return values. causal_research.bug_semantics: TemplateContext.LimitToString bounded one ObjectToString conversion rather than cumulative rendered output. Each rendered expression entered a fresh top-level ObjectToString call, which reset _currentToStringLength, and StringBuilderOutput appended every resulting chunk without a render-wide cap. A template could therefore emit a near-1 MiB string in each of 1,000 loop iterations, pass the per-call check each time, and accumulate roughly 1 GiB until the host exhausted memory.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit b858377886c35bfedb2768de9b057377909c2e95 is the smallest real BIC: it directly added LimitToString, _currentToStringLength, and the top-level reset that made the safety counter restart for every ObjectToString conversion. Its two-file focused patch is neither a merge, aggregate, import, nor move, and its immediate parent lacks both LimitToString and _currentToStringLength. The older unconditional StringBuilderOutput append was a necessary sink but did not create the advisory-specific limit-bypass invariant; b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 later enabled the already-flawed limit by default. Commit 98563216488161a9edeba6c37c7cf82c98319c9b directly fixed the flaw by adding cumulative output accounting across write chunks.

causal_research.bug_semantics: joserfc accepted zero-length symmetric key material and passed it to Python's HMAC implementation for HS256, HS384, and HS512 verification. Because an empty HMAC key is public and deterministic, an unauthenticated attacker can compute a matching signature and have jwt.decode accept forged claims whenever application configuration or key lookup supplies an empty secret.
evidence: Official GitHub advisory API for GHSA-gg9x-qcx2-xmrh reports withdrawn_at=null, vulnerable range <=1.6.7, first patched version 1.6.8, and references commit 86d00910b2b2d2d07503fee9b572906daefab7f1: https://github.com/authlib/joserfc/security/advisories/GHSA-gg9x-qcx2-xmrh

Official CVE.org record CVE-2026-49852 is PUBLISHED and states that versions before 1.6.8 accept attacker-forged HMAC JWTs when the supplied key is empty; its references name the vendor advisory, fix commit, and 1.6.8 release: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-49852

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory describes a real CWE-863 defect in the publish UILayout filter, reproduced in v3.7.3 source: getConf serves administrator Conf.UILayout to RoleReader after a walker that fail-opens and ignores the password tier and non-editor tabs. That walker was first written by named human YuxinZhao in public PR member 63c8ee2, whose parent lacks the function; the master squash is the carrier. Daniel's 63c7d54 removes the walker and returns an empty UILayout to readers, which is present in v3.8.0. The BIC commit object has no AI authorship or co-authorship marker, so the case is a real vulnerability with human introduction: NOT_AI. Fix-side AI is also ABSENT and is not used for the verdict.
In publish mode kernel/server/proxy/publish.go injects X-Auth-Token with the anonymous publish account's reader JWT, and POST /api/system/getConf is guarded only by model.CheckAuth, which accepts RoleReader, so an unauthenticated publish reader receives model.GetMaskedConf(). HideConfSecret, added with the read-only publish service in ba2193403da71a679dcde24e5b6284278b7240da, blanks AI/Api/Publish/Repo/Sync/Secrets/Variables/System fields but never UILayout, so administrator layout tabs (document titles), dock titles, search-panel config terms, assetPath and pluginData shipped to readers, exactly the surfaces the advisory lists. The immediate parent 536879cb848c634743a6559e55c2aa3aa291eaff has no kernel/model/auth.go, no kernel/model/role.go and no kernel/server/proxy/ at all, and its getConf has no role branch, so the behaviour is absent in the parent and present in the child. The later 2026-03-12 commit 3facc37df999583fac6103e2f067a517b8cc0d5e added FilterConfByPublishIgnore, a partial mitigation that rewrites only uiLayout['layout'] tabs and leaves dock data and search config intact, and its own parent already returned the unfiltered layout, so it is not the introducer. The fix 63c7d5474a0c841898671a9df915dd7b194e3ff5 replaces the filter with maskedConf.UILayout = &conf.UILayout{}, is contained in v3.7.4-alpha.3 and later, and is contained in no v3.7.3 tag. The BIC commit object carries a named human author (Yingyi / 颖逸, GitHub account 49649786+Zuoqiu-Yingyi), the GitHub merge identity and a web-flow GPG signature, with no Co-Authored-By or AI trailer in its message or in the eight PR commits its body lists. A later cargo-hierarchy check compares the target employee to the same overwritten $id_pessoa, so the identifier spoof also distorts self-vs-other authorization. The employee row itself is still selected via id_funcionario; the IDOR sink is the session-derived person id used after extract. causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS (CWE-79) in winter/wn-backend-module Brand Settings. A user who holds backend.manage_branding can save custom CSS at Settings → Customize Backend → Styles (the custom_css field). That string is concatenated into Less_Parser input together with bundled custom.less, compiled, and emitted raw inside a backend <style> block via BrandSetting::renderCss() in modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php. No HTML sanitization was applied to the compiled output, so a closing </style> (or other markup that survives LESS) breaks out of the style context and executes as HTML/JS on every backend page for every authenticated backend user. Affected <=1.2.12; first-party advisory names v1.2.13 / d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 as the patch (strip_tags on the compile-miss return). Editor Settings markup styles share the same sink but are a separately advised issue.
causal_research.flaw_origin: First-write of user-controlled custom_css into the Brand Settings LESS compile-and-render path. On 2014-10-16, 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 changed BrandSettings::renderCss() from parsing only bundled custom.less to File::get(...custom.less).self::get('custom_css'), stored the unsanitized compiled CSS, and the backend layout continued to dump that CSS into a <style> tag. Immediate parent fbaab26bfbcfef96bac4802fd6dd62ec5557c8e7 still parses only the static LESS file. The custom_css form field already existed from the BrandSettings rename (9f5646d2733fc0cd29ecc115c5f2b3fc93ad2d3f, previous day) but was not compiled or rendered until 1203043. Later cache extraction (e7c33467), model rename BrandSettings→BrandSetting, and error-message escaping (c9dab67) are refactors of the same unsanitized return, not first-writes.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With allow_unsafe_options at its safe default, a caller can put an unsafe Git option such as --upload-pack=<attacker command> in the value of a single-character kwarg such as n. The guard examines only the kwarg name, which is n in the original implementation and -n after candidate reconstruction, but transform_kwarg emits the value as a separate argv token. The check therefore misses the attacker-controlled option that Git executes. The defect first affected fetch, pull, and push, was later copied to clone/clone_from, and was later centralized and extended to ls_remote, revision traversal/iter_commits, blame, and archive.
causal_research.flaw_origin: e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 is the smallest real BIC: it introduced default unsafe-option guards for Remote.fetch, Remote.pull, and Remote.push and fed check_unsafe_options only list(kwargs.keys()), while the existing single-character kwarg transformation emitted an option-like value as a second argv token. 5c59e0d63da6180db8a0b349f0ad36fef42aceed later propagated the same mistake to clone/clone_from. 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 later replaced the existing key-list checks with the still-key-only _option_candidates helper and added more guarded APIs; it expanded/refactored the already-present mechanism rather than introducing it.

evidence: The assigned bundle identifies GHSA-PJJH-F8RP-RJV3/CVE-2026-73625, describes the check_unsafe_options single-character-kwarg value-smuggling RCE, and states that versions before 3.1.54 are affected.

The primary chose e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 with parent 2625ed9fc074091c531c27ffcba7902771130261 and verdict NOT_AI; the reviewer instead chose 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 with parent 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 and verdict AI_ROOT_CAUSE. Re-running git log --all --reverse -S'options=list(kwargs.keys())' -- git/remote.py git/repo/base.py returns e6108c7 first, 5c59e0d6 second, and 701ce32f third.

git show e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 -- git/remote.py git/cmd.py shows the direct addition of unsafe fetch/pull/push denylists, allow_unsafe_options=False, and check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), ...). git diff-tree --name-status -r -M reports only modified files, so this is not an import, move, merge carrier, or aggregate. Its commit object has exactly one parent, so no squash decomposition is needed.

The immediate-parent check resolves introducer_parent and parent absence: git grep for check_unsafe_options, the remote unsafe-option lists, and allow_unsafe_options in 2625ed9fc074091c531c27ffcba7902771130261:git/remote.py and git/cmd.py returns no matches. At the same time, git blame 2625ed9f -- git/cmd.py shows the already-existing transform_kwarg branch returning ['-%s' % name, '%s' % value] for a non-boolean one-character kwarg. Thus e6108c7, not its parent, first creates the defective safe-default guard/executed-argv mismatch.

The reviewer's proposed BIC fails the direct-parent gate. git grep in 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 finds check_unsafe_options(options=list(kwargs.keys()), ...) already present in fetch, pull, push, and clone, and the same tree's transform_kwarg still emits the value as a separate token. git diff 65a72839c92768754bd51a37381235842a5ae0d8 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 shows 701ce32f replacing those existing calls with Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), whose loop still appends only the reconstructed key, while adding other guarded consumers. Therefore the exact bypass is present in 701ce32f's direct parent; absence of the helper name is not absence of the vulnerability.

Release ancestry confirms the lifecycle rather than the reviewer's later boundary: git tag --contains e6108c7997f5c8f7361b982959518e982b973230 --sort=version:refname starts at 3.1.30, while 3.1.29 resolves to 19aaa74aafc06663644d634f33bb8af871d58536 before the BIC. git show e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453 -- git/cmd.py test/test_git.py directly repairs the disputed mechanism by adding dash-prefixed split single-character values to _option_candidates and checking n='--upload-pack=helper'. git cat-file -p gives parent faf3c09038b03bc2bdd8545ef34bbf6d7f1cd11f, which is the 3.1.53 tag commit, and git tag --contains e8d0fbf774d1f6baa3b481adfe48bd262e43b453 starts at 3.1.54, matching the bundle's patched boundary.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The authenticated POST /contact/save path trusted the request's numeric contact id and loaded Contact::find(...) without company_id scoping before overwriting the record, so a user could blindly modify another tenant's contact. The authenticated GET /contact/export-vcard/{id} path likewise used Contact::findOrFail($id) without company_id scoping and returned the selected record's vCard, allowing cross-tenant PII disclosure by id enumeration.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The write primitive originated in 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9, which added the authenticated /contact/save route and a new ContactSaveController whose update branch selected a Contact solely by attacker-controlled id; contacts were already owned through company-scoped leads, so the missing ownership check was exploitable at introduction. Commit 9fda3ee70b7b6035f729a154f7bf50bfabbd3b7f later added an explicit contact.company_id on creation while retaining the unscoped update. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d merely moved the same vulnerable save logic into ContactRepository and is not the BIC. The independent vCard disclosure surface was added from scratch by a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9 shows author Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, a plain one-line message, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity
evidence: The first-party CNA record at https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-19433-idor-in-prospero-flow-crm-contact-save-and-vcard-export identifies ContactRepository::save and ContactExportVCard::export, the POST /contact/save and GET /contact/export-vcard/{id} attack paths, affected versions before 5.4.8, and direct patch f16b4af2027b17bef7c604c92dbd86cf38082398; it explicitly says the supplier equivalents changed by the patch were outside the proof of concept.

At vulnerable parent f36c2a115f4c28c82181f1798c01582ae953b932, routes/module/contact.php exposes both routes; both controllers extend MainController, whose middleware is auth and locked. app/Repositories/ContactRepository.php uses Contact::find($data['id']) and then writes names, phones, email, job title, social profiles, and notes, while app/Http/Controllers/Contact/ContactExportVCard.php uses Contact::findOrFail($id) and downloads vCard content. Neither query constrains company_id. The sibling ContactUpdateController and ContactDeleteController do constrain id with Auth::user()->company_id, confirming the missing ownership predicate.

git log -L and git log -S traced the save lookup backward through app/Repositories/ContactRepository.php: 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d created the repository during a deduplication refactor but simultaneously removed the identical Contact::find($request->id) update branch from ContactSaveController. Continuing -L/-S on that controller reaches 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9, which added the controller and /contact/save route from scratch; thus 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d is a move, not the real BIC.

Direct parent-tree verification: git diff --name-status f84405497c20f4744b3ce55c847a122d9a77326d 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9 reports A app/Http/Controllers/Contact/ContactSaveController.php, and git ls-tree of f84405497c20f4744b3ce55c847a122d9a77326d at that path is empty. The BIC diff also adds the /contact/save route, so both the vulnerable handler and its exposure are absent from the immediate parent.

The disclosure primitive has its own smallest BIC: git log -L on app/Http/Controllers/Contact/ContactExportVCard.php reaches a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830, which creates the controller with Contact::findOrFail($id) and adds the GET route. Its parent c679dd4c6c19f9af636a61efc9408c18a4ad4239 has no such file (git ls-tree empty; name-status A). Its commit object is also solely human-authored and human-committed by Gustavo Novaro with no trailers.

The lifecycle begins with the blind-write sink in 266c2bec31a4ef56431f0ee9ed4dfadfa12661b9: an authenticated numeric-id update endpoint was created without checking that the target contact belonged to the caller's company. Tenant ownership already existed via the contact's company-scoped lead relationship; explicit contact.company_id was added later without repairing the lookup. The vulnerable lookup survived formatting and feature edits, then moved unchanged into ContactRepository in 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d. The vCard read sink was independently created in a0306e77f95aaf57afec25ef74e4aa2da275c830 and survived until the same fix. Immediate-parent trees prove the selected earliest BIC's handler and route did not exist before it, and separately prove the export primitive's absence before its own BIC. Both primitives shipped in tagged releases. Commit f16b4af2027b17bef7c604c92dbd86cf38082398 directly closes both by adding authenticated company_id predicates; the next descendant version bump establishes 5.4.8 as the patched boundary. Because the smallest selected BIC's raw commit object has no AI marker and is wholly human-authored/committed, later Claude attribution on the fix cannot causally attribute the introduction, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CredentialsPermissionChecker authorizes only credential IDs whose credential-type keys appear in a set inferred statically from unresolved node parameters. An authenticated member with edit access to a shared workflow can place another user's known credential ID on an HTTP Request node and make genericAuthType or nodeCredentialType an expression. The pre-execution checker sees the expression text rather than its runtime-resolved credential type, omits the credential ID from the ownership query, and execution later resolves and loads the unauthorized credential, allowing use or exfiltration.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The smallest causal source change is PR #25599 member 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b. It changed mapCredIdsToNodes from checking every referenced credential to skipping credential keys absent from getActiveCredentialTypes, whose static inference did not fail closed for expressions. Public squash 608e3bf214328e679c03da3e4a6e9c22ceaac9ca carried the flaw but is not the smallest BIC. Later bundle 2d9a2ec76e180b54e8091e31b1e0638c909abd99 added the unresolved genericAuthType value to the set, fixing literal generic types but preserving the advisory's expression mismatch and therefore not originating the flaw.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: the complete BIC commit object 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b names human author and committer Guillaume Jacquart <jacquart.guillaume@gmail.com> and contains only the message 'refine credential access check to discard not actively used credentials', with no AI, bot, generation, or co-author marker.
causal_research.evidence: The assigned primary and reviewer agree on release landing fix_sha f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f but disagree on direct_fix_sha: the primary claims mainline bundle 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624, while the reviewer claims the 2.32.x backport bundle f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f. Re-run object checks show that both direct-fix claims are wrong. `git show --stat` identifies f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f as `chore: Bundle/2.x (backport to release-candidate/2.32.x) (#34692)` changing 79 files and 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 as `chore: Bundle/2.x (#34680)` changing 77 files, so neither is a smallest direct patch. The public PR #34680 body says it was cherry-picked from inaccessible n8n-private PR #279. `GET /repos/n8n-io/n8n/pulls/34680/commits` returns only aggregate import 97f5ba3f824019665adb81a9976174e5f778d71d and test-helper follow-up f65845e5fb0cb6a59c3385095b9ed2bee2e738ed; the aggregate message lists `fix(core): Improve credential type matching in pre-execution checks (#215)` among unrelated changes, and `GET /repos/n8n-io/n8n-private/pulls/279` returns 404, so no public full SHA for the underlying direct fix can be verified. The release landing remains verified: `git diff db5e2d068bc92a28a455598daa578fe405dce4bc f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f -- packages/cli/src/executions/pre-execution-checks/credentials-permission-checker.ts` adds the isExpression import and returns null for expression-valued nodeCredentialType and genericAuthType, forcing mapCredIdsToNodes to authorize every referenced credential. `git tag --contains f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f --list 'n8n@2.32.*' --sort=version:refname` begins at n8n@2.32.1, and `git grep` finds both expression guards in n8n@2.32.1 but none in n8n@2.32.0, matching the first-party advisory's patched boundary 2.32.1 (alongside 1.123.67 and 2.31.5). For origin and parent, the API commit object for 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b gives sole parent 0970e4f32cb7efbe257f0ea8105233c3b3a4e179 and the human, trailer-free message; its production patch adds activeCredTypes filtering. Direct parent-tree `git grep -n -E 'Object\.values\(node\.credentials\)|activeCredTypes|getActiveCredentialTypes' 0970e4f32cb7efbe257f0ea8105233c3b3a4e179 -- .../credentials-permission-checker.ts` finds only the unconditional Object.values mapping and no active-type helper/filter, directly proving parent absence.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability begins when 7d6023fe3478df86d88f3602f1ea5b53819a050b replaces the conservative invariant of checking every referenced credential with a static active-type filter. Expression parameters resolve later, so a credential may be runtime-active while omitted statically; the immediate parent cannot take this path because it maps every credential ID. PR #25599 is publicly decomposable and its first member contains the production mechanism, so neither its squash nor the later genericAuthType bundle is the BIC. The fix disagreement cannot be resolved by choosing one aggregate: f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f is the verified 2.32.1 release landing and is therefore retained as fix_sha, but both proposed direct_fix_sha values are bundle commits and are rejected. Because the underlying source fix was imported from a private repository and its commit object is unavailable, direct_fix_sha is justified null rather than falsely naming an aggregate or import. The public landing diff and adjacent tag boundary nevertheless verify the fix completely for the selected release line. AI attribution depends only on the smallest BIC commit object, which has a human identity and no AI marker; AI markers on later bundles, imports, or fixes are irrelevant. The gate-complete verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: The full SHA and commit object of the smallest direct source fix in private PR #215/#279 are not publicly accessible; only the public aggregate import, squash landing, and release backports can be verified. This does not affect the verified BIC, BIC-only AI attribution, public fix behavior, or patched version boundary.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When Kubernetes Ingress NGINX is enabled and an Ingress uses nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target with a regex that can capture text adjacent to the prefix (example path /api(.*) and rewrite /$1), Traefik selects the public PathRegexp router on a request such as /api../admin. Default entry-point sanitizePath leaves that URL unchanged because api.. is one ordinary segment. After routing, RewriteTarget.ServeHTTP runs regexp.ReplaceAllString, producing /../admin, PathUnescapes it, and forwards without checking that url.URL.JoinPath() would normalize the path. A backend that collapses dot-segments dispatches to /admin, which is intended to be reachable only through a separate router that has BasicAuth/DigestAuth/ForwardAuth. The same class of check already existed on ReplacePathRegex (GHSA-cxjq-mrr5-89rv, in v3.7.7) but not on this separate ingress-nginx middleware.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the authenticated WebUI RSE-management flow. A privileged attacker can persist attacker-controlled markup in city, country_name, or ISP through the RSE creation path. The RSE list passes those stored values to DataTables as renderable data, while the RSE detail page concatenates them into HTML passed to jQuery.append. causal_research.bug_semantics: File Browser authorized only the requested source root and, for copy or rename, the destination root, then recursively removed, renamed, or copied the whole source tree without checking rules on every descendant. An authenticated restricted user could therefore operate on an allowed parent containing a denied child, exposing or relocating the child at an allowed destination or deleting it with the parent.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /images endpoint accepts an image source and sends the resulting bytes to Sharp. For SVG input, imageProcessor deliberately rasterizes at density 300 with limitInputPixels disabled and performs no structural bound on use-element shadow-tree depth or pattern-tile dimensions. A crafted SVG can therefore make the underlying SVG renderer consume unbounded CPU or memory until the application server, and potentially the host, is denied service.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Webmin miniserv disables cookie session auth when the request User-Agent matches /webmin/i (the RPC client fingerprint), then accepts HTTP Basic Authorization with only username and password. Session-form login for the same account still requires the configured second factor (typically TOTP via validate_twofactor). An attacker who already knows a 2FA-protected account password can send User-Agent: webmin plus Authorization: Basic and become a fully authenticated Webmin user without the second factor (CWE-308). Credentials are still required; 2FA is the control that is skipped. Vendor security copy groups this with CVE-2026-42210; CISA's CVE-2026-56022 text specifically names the User-Agent trigger. The 2.640 fix does not remove the UA session skip; it rejects Basic auth when get_user_details() reports twofactor_provider.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated attacker sends a client-portal login URL with an absolute external intended query value. ContactLoginController::showLoginForm copies that string into the session key url.intended with no same-origin/host allowlist. After the victim authenticates, authenticated() sees url.intended and returns Laravel redirect($url) (bare Redirector, not redirect()->intended()), so the 302 Location is the attacker URL. The hosted password path calls authenticated() directly; sendLoginResponse's later redirect()->intended($this->redirectPath()) is dead once the override returns. sendLoginResponse also assigns the raw intended value to $this->redirectTo, which would become the fallback default if intended() rejected the session URL. Impact is post-login phishing against Invoice Ninja clients (CWE-601).

causal_research.bug_semantics: When an application programmatically puts attacker-controlled text in a DocumentType publicId, systemId, or internalSubset and serializes it, the serializer concatenates those fields into the DOCTYPE declaration without validating their XML grammar. A quote or '>' can escape a public/system identifier and ']>' can close the internal subset, causing attacker-chosen markup or declarations to be emitted outside the intended DOCTYPE context; a downstream parser with entity expansion can then expose an XXE-class impact.
evidence: The frozen bundle for GHSA-f6ww-3ggp-fr8h / CVE-2026-41674 identifies programmatic DocumentType serialization as the attack path: publicId, systemId, and internalSubset are stored and emitted verbatim; its affected ranges are @xmldom/xmldom <0.8.13 and >=0.9.0,<0.9.10 plus legacy xmldom <=0.6.0.
The CVE.org CVE JSON endpoint returned cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED, GitHub_M as CNA, the same verbatim-DocumentType mechanism, and fixed boundaries 0.8.13 and 0.9.10; it is not rejected or withdrawn.

git show 64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 -- dom.js shows the causal hunk in the DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE branch: it deletes `var buf = ['<!DOCTYPE ',nodeName]` and instead calls `buf.push('<!DOCTYPE ',node.name)`, after which unchecked publicId, systemId, and internalSubset text is appended to the caller-owned output buffer.

Direct parent-tree inspection at 4e759a92ea4dab7e88dbd9317869447629b5f369 shows XMLSerializer.serializeToString creates an outer buffer, calls serializeToString(node, buf), and joins only that outer buffer, while the DocumentType branch shadows it with a new local buffer and never returns or joins the new buffer. Thus the vulnerable emitted-DOCTYPE mechanism is absent in the immediate parent.

causal_research.bug_semantics: UDR exposes DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/application-data/influenceData/:influenceId/:subscriptionId because Gin cannot register both a static subs-to-notify segment and :influenceId. The intended gate is that only influenceId==subs-to-notify may delete a Traffic Influence Subscription. After the 2024 processor refactor, HandleApplicationDataInfluenceDataSubsToNotifySubscriptionIdDelete sent 404 for any other influenceId but did not return, so ApplicationDataInfluenceDataSubsToNotifySubscriptionIdDeleteProcedure still deleted the in-memory subscription by subscriptionId. An unauthenticated SBI caller who knows or guesses a subscriptionId can DELETE via an invalid path, observe 404, and still remove the subscription.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SubjectX500PrincipalExtractor turns an X.509 client certificate's X500Principal into an RFC2253 (CN) or RFC1779 (email OID) DN string and takes matcher.find() group(1) from the regex CN=(.*?)(?:,|$) or OID.1.2.840.113549.1.9.1=(.*?)(?:,|$). Because the regex is unanchored and stops at the first CN=/OID= substring, a CN or OU value that embeds a second DN-like fragment (for example OU=CN=duke,) is parsed as that other username. A crafted client certificate can therefore impersonate another user in X.509 pre-authentication. The vendor advisory and CVE.org record keep this as a real published issue affecting Spring Security 7.0.0–7.0.4 (CWE-297); exploitation assumes the cert already passed a trusted upstream.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The regex-on-stringified-DN extractor was first written when SubjectX500PrincipalExtractor was added and made the default X509AuthenticationFilter extractor. That commit copied the historical CN=(.*?)(?:,|$) approach onto X500Principal.getName() output rather than parsing RDNs. A later encapsulate commit only moved the same patterns to static fields; it did not invent the match-first-CN behavior. The 7.0.5 fix replaces the regex with javax.naming.ldap.LdapName/Rdn iteration so an embedded CN= inside another RDN is no longer treated as the subject.
causal_research.reasoning: CVE-2026-22747 is a published VMware/Spring advisory, not withdrawn: SubjectX500PrincipalExtractor mis-parses malformed certificate CN/email DN strings and can bind the wrong username. The vulnerable mechanism is unanchored regex extraction against X500Principal.getName() output. git log -L/-S and parent-tree checks place the first write of those lines at aba437d4698c0b30559021e3f41b85607fee8ce0, which also made the new class the default extractor; the parent e8f920e0eeafff1af55427c13db054a3b6b13830 has neither the file nor the class name. The deprecated SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor already used a similar CN regex on getSubjectDN(), but that is a different class/DN source, was left unpatched by this CVE, and is absent from 7.0.0–7.0.4 scope; aba437d is a new-file first-write, not a move. Encapsulate commit f690a7f is a refactor of the same patterns. The GHSA fix 88118afb8f9357ae7cc215500a441e89fee701c3 is the direct RDN-parsing patch, present in 7.0.5 and not 7.0.4, matching the vendor boundary. causal_research.bug_semantics: A request such as GET /service/sub-path/%2e%2e/other-path is parsed by net/http with Path=/service/sub-path/../other-path and RawPath preserving %2e%2e. After CVE-2025-32431, sanitizePath calls url.JoinPath(), which path.Joins EscapedPath, so the %2E%2E segment is not treated as '..'. setPath then writes decoded Path back to contain '..'. PathPrefix/Path/PathRegex (v2 gorilla/mux SkipClean(true); v3 strings.HasPrefix on req.URL.Path) therefore still match the pre-traversal prefix, selecting the more specific router and skipping the middleware that should apply to the collapsed path. Literal /../ was already collapsed; encoded dots were not.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The encoding residual was introduced when PR 11684 switched sanitization from path.Clean(req.URL.Path) to url.JoinPath() on EscapedPath. Commit caf83746bc7c22c04dab6603c9315de12fb265a8 (parent 6a4b0f387a30f6f92bb3b40bd9d000cd3e6550ed) is the first writer of that JoinPath hunk. The parent still cleaned the decoded Path and would have collapsed %2E%2E. The same JoinPath body later landed on v2.11 as squash dd5cb68cb1aeda490adefdbb5bb8887aef9cc699 and is what v2.11.23/v2.11.24 and v3.4.0 ship.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object caf83746bc to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the encoded form is materially different from the plain form: Go's net/url decodes /%2e%2e/ into URL.Path as /../ while RawPath and EscapedPath keep %2e%2e, and the containous/mux fork's cleanPath operates on the decoded path with a 301 redirect when skipClean is false, so 82cb21fc removing cleaning is what removed pre-match canonicalization. Checked dd5cb68b's parent 299a16f0a45: it still has SkipClean(true) and zero sanitizePath/normalizePath occurrences, so dd5cb68b cannot be the introduction. Checked that v3.4.0 is genuinely pre-fix (matcher.go compares req.URL.Path at 145/160/174, normalizePath absent) and that v2.11.25 and v3.4.1 contain the fixes (git merge-base --is-ancestor). Checked that later code motion is not an introduction (7fcb7b86d3 extraction and the muxer relocation carry the flag; the master tree no longer contains SkipClean at all). Checked the AI surface: no AI trailers on the causal or fix commits, and the repo-wide scan over 6503 master commits finds one unrelated Copilot docs commit.
mechanism.impact: Traversal to a backend path that a different, middleware-protected router should have served, skipping the intended router's middleware chain (CWE-22; CVSS4 AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N; GitHub severity LOW). In the advisory example the request reaches service-a through the unprotected /service/sub-path router even though the resolved request is /service/other-path, which belongs to the router that carries my-middleware-a.
mechanism.preconditions: Path-based routing rules plus a router layout where the un-normalized prefix selects a router with a different middleware set; the request must carry dot segments that Go's URL parsing decodes into URL.Path while keeping RawPath/EscapedPath encoded (%2e and %2E escapes do), and no canonicalization may run before matching in the pre-fix state. Sanitization was absent before dd5cb68b and, in the pre-fix order, its sanitizePath (URL.JoinPath over the escaped path) could not collapse %2e-encoded dot segments.
mechanism.summary: An HTTP request whose path carries percent-encoded dot segments (for example /service/sub-path/%2e%2e/other-path) is matched by Traefik's Path, PathPrefix and PathRegexp rules against the un-normalized request path, because the router skips gorilla/mux path cleaning (router.SkipClean(true) at server.go:671, 82cb21fca3f6598fa5451d73034b8a90a4b1db77, still carried as mux.NewRouter().SkipClean(true) at pkg/muxer/http/mux.go:51 in the pre-fix v2.11.24/v3.4.0 states). The router that matches is therefore not the router that would match the resolved path the backend serves, so the request reaches the backend without the middleware chain (authentication, authorization, rate limiting, redirects) attached to the intended router.
mechanism.trigger: Any request with percent-encoded dot segments in the path, for example /service/sub-path/%2e%2e/other-path or /foo/%2E%2E/bar, against a default entrypoint whose routing rules use Path, PathPrefix or PathRegexp, where a less specific rule carries the middleware chain and a more specific rule without that chain matches the encoded prefix; the upstream migration tables record exactly this, with /foo/%2E%2E/bar matching PathPrefix('/foo') before the fix and PathPrefix('/bar') after it.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: server.go:671 router.SkipClean(true) (82cb21fca3f6598fa5451d73034b8a90a4b1db77, 2016); pre-fix carry at pkg/muxer/http/mux.go:51 mux.NewRouter().SkipClean(true) (v2.11.22, v2.11.24, v3.4.0) plus pkg/muxer/http/matcher.go:145/160/174 path/pathRegexp/pathPrefix comparing req.URL.Path (v3.4.0).

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-22 routing bypass: encoded unreserved dots survive JoinPath sanitization, so Path matchers still see '..' and skip the middleware that the collapsed path would use. The smallest introducing change is PR 11684 member caf83746, which replaced path.Clean(decoded Path) with JoinPath(EscapedPath). That commit is named-human Romain/rtribotte with no commit-object AI marker, so AI attribution is ABSENT. The CVE-cited fix 08d5dfee is present in v2.11.25 and v3.4.1 and absent from v2.11.24 and v3.4.0. Successful human repair does not create an AI verdict. Therefore the verdict is NOT_AI.
The defect is a path-canonicalization gap in Traefik routing: percent-encoded dot segments survive into rule evaluation, so Path/PathPrefix/PathRegexp rules select a router whose middleware chain differs from the one that should have served the resolved path (GHSA-vrch-868g-9jx5, CVSS4 VC:L/VI:L). The smallest original change that removed canonicalization is 82cb21fca3f6598fa5451d73034b8a90a4b1db77 (2016-09-20, 'Disable gorilla/mux URL cleaning to prevent sending redirect', Yoann Dubreuil), which added router.SkipClean(true) at server.go:671; the gorilla/mux default would have 301-redirected the decoded dot-segment path to canonical form before matching, and that default is still present in the verified parent 7e8937a332fc850ba13ecabff21bacb5aa5808b9, where SkipClean is absent. The 2025 candidate dd5cb68cb1 ('Sanitize request path') is not the introducer: its parent 299a16f0a45e564c7a9ac2de9a1fee5bdd9d753c already carries mux.NewRouter().SkipClean(true) with no normalization, and the sanitizePath it added runs URL.JoinPath over the escaped path, which cannot collapse %2e-encoded dot segments, so dd5cb68b is a partial guard layered on the vulnerable behavior. The advisory patch 08d5dfee0164aa54dd44a467870042e18e8d3f00 closes the mechanism by normalizing the request path (decoding unreserved characters and capitalizing escapes) before the default-on sanitization removes dot segments, and 859f4e886860442207d7ebc3b047d0bad44ba461 completes the v3 line by making the matcher tree read the routing path; upstream migration notes record the flip of /foo/%2E%2E/bar from PathPrefix('/foo') matching in v2.11.24/v3.4.0 to PathPrefix('/bar') matching in v2.11.25/v3.4.1. The BIC object carries a named human identity with no AI markers and predates generative-AI code contribution; the single repo-wide AI-marked commit (8ac8473554d758459ae4e99dab4be7dcbb167a07, Copilot, docs guide) is not on the causal chain, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Traefik v1 (Go module github.com/traefik/traefik) is listed by the advisory as affected with last_affected 1.7.34 and no fixed event, so the v1 line has no patch; only v2.11.25 (08d5dfee) and v3.4.1 (08d5dfee + 859f4e88) are fixed. Documented operator residual: entrypoints with sanitizePath explicitly disabled (the default is true) skip dot-segment removal, which upstream documentation calls unsafe; normalization cannot be disabled, but the traversal removal depends on sanitization.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Clatter exposed post-quantum PSK0 handshake patterns without enforcing the Noise PSK validity rule. In the affected patterns, PSK-derived cipher state could be used before the sending party had contributed fresh self-chosen ephemeral randomness, so repeated or attacker-influenced handshakes could lose the intended key-randomization guarantee and risk catastrophic key reuse.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With channels.msteams.groupPolicy set to allowlist, a configured teams/team/channel route allowlist was incorrectly treated as sufficient authorization when the effective sender groupAllowFrom list was empty. A message from any sender in a matched route therefore passed the route gate and skipped the sender gate, allowing an unauthorized Teams group sender to trigger bot processing and replies.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit c7ea47e88682283f87cb8d6481df67f4def0258f added Teams route allowlisting and changed the empty-sender-allowlist rejection from an unconditional effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0 check to effectiveGroupAllowFrom.length === 0 && !channelGate.allowlistConfigured. That conflated route authorization with sender authorization and first created the bypass. Commit 27dad962fee567e50ed7e293a4d8eb67cc7da8e6 later preserved the same behavior while refactoring it into an explicit ["*"] sender list; it was not the behavioral introducer.

causal_research.bug_semantics: RustCrypto ml-dsa signature decoding reused one monotonicity predicate for two encodings with different rules. Hint cut offsets may repeat because a polynomial may have no hints, but hint indices inside each polynomial must be strictly increasing. Changing the shared comparison from < to <= made repeated cuts valid while also accepting duplicate indices. Verification could therefore accept a non-canonical, byte-distinct signature carrying a repeated hint index, causing ML-DSA signature malleability across ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The assigned c2sp/wycheproof repository supplies detecting conformance vectors, not the vulnerable verifier. The flaw originated in RustCrypto/signatures PR #895. Its first member commit 92d2a8211581610191ee489372231aa644760c1a directly changed ml-dsa/src/hint.rs from strict < to non-strict <=; later PR members did not first write that condition. The five-member PR was squash-merged to mainline as b01c3b73dd08d0094e089aa234f78b6089ec1f38, whose tree matches the final PR member, so the squash carrier is not the smallest real BIC.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated SSRF in the SMF image proxy (CWE-918). An authenticated user embeds an attacker-controlled HTTP URL in a BBCode [img] tag. Url::proxied()/parse_bbc auto-generates a valid HMAC for any such URL and rewrites it to proxy.php. ProxyServer::checkRequest() historically rejected only literal IP hosts, 'localhost', and the board host; it never resolved the hostname or checked the destination against private, loopback, or link-local ranges. cacheImage() then calls WebFetchApi::fetch() / curl_fetch_web_data, so a hostname that resolves to 169.254.169.254, RFC1918, or loopback is fetched. Redirect hops were likewise unguarded. NVD/VulnCheck swapped the branch mapping: git shows 4bf35cf on release-3.0 (WebFetch) and b4d23df on release-2.1 (fetch_web_data).
causal_research.flaw_origin: dcbaefb0976cf3e9d9490455bb59504d5c807847 (2014-06-14) first added proxy.php with cacheImage() fetching the signed request URL via curl_fetch_web_data() and no destination-IP validation. Parent eb7314fc8e763023a2f02790669e1d224a6a74d6 has no proxy.php. The next-day commit a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b wired BBCode [img] auto-HMAC, completing the advisory attack path. Later hostname-only IP/localhost filters were incomplete remediations. 2022/2023 ProxyServer/WebFetch moves are refactors, not first-write.

causal_research.bug_semantics: HandlerMethod tries to associate a concrete @Controller data-fetcher method with declarations in its generic interfaces so that interface parameter annotations are merged into the concrete method. Its fallback override check compared each concrete parameter Class by identity with ResolvableType.forMethodParameter(...).resolve(). In a generic interface hierarchy, bridge erasure or an incompletely resolved type can make resolve() fail to yield the raw Class that the concrete method exposes; the candidate interface method is then rejected and its annotations are omitted. Under the vendor's stated conditions (Spring Security, @EnableMethodSecurity, and @Controller classes in type hierarchies), the missed annotation detection can cause authorization annotations to be ignored at runtime and allow unauthorized access to protected GraphQL data fetchers.
evidence: Vendor advisory https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-41856 states that annotation detection can fail for @Controller data fetchers in type hierarchies, that security annotations can then be ignored with Spring Security and @EnableMethodSecurity, and lists OSS fixes 2.0.4 and 1.4.6.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A remote caller could supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) target in GET /api's url query parameter. PullMD passed that value to its server-side web extractor and returned the fetched content without rejecting loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT, or cloud-metadata destinations or revalidating redirect targets, so a request such as /api?url=http://100.100.100.200/latest/user-data could disclose cloud instance metadata and reach other internal services.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The root release commit wired req.query.url directly from server.js into extractWebFn(url), while lib/web.js wrapped globalThis.fetch only with a timeout and then called fetchFn(url, { headers }). causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-297: default TLS RemoteCertificateValidationCallback in the Couchbase .NET SDK accepted a server certificate whenever the chain could be built against bundled/user CAs, without failing on SslPolicyErrors.RemoteCertificateNameMismatch unless a user-supplied callback was set. After NCBC-3173, ConnectionFactory and CouchbaseHttpClientFactory installed that callback whenever Kv/HttpCertificateCallbackValidation was null: IgnoreNameMismatch only short-circuited the ignore-true path, then ValidateWithDefaultCertificates/GetValidatorWithPredefinedCertificates returned chain.Build(cert) and never consulted the name-mismatch bit. A MITM with any cert chaining to the trusted/Capella CA therefore passed hostname verification. Compounding this, ClusterOptions.ForceIpAsTargetHost defaulted to true (NCBC-2959; IP was hardcoded as AuthenticateAsClient targetHost from SDK3 SSL wiring), so even .NET's built-in name check was bound to the peer IP rather than the configured hostname.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The byte-slice decoder dispatches MessagePack extension frames to the built-in timestamp decoder before proving that the complete frame is present. For a truncated fixext value (format byte 0xd4-0xd8 with a missing type byte and/or payload), timeDecoder.IsType and DecoderCommon.ReadSize1/ReadSize4/ReadSize8 index or slice beyond the supplied buffer. Untrusted input reaching Unmarshal, UnmarshalAsMap, UnmarshalAsArray, or struct decoding can therefore trigger a Go runtime panic and terminate the caller, causing denial of service.

causal_research.bug_semantics: conflux_send_switch_command() encodes a RELAY_COMMAND_CONFLUX_SWITCH cell and calls relay_send_command_from_edge() without checking the return. That helper packages the cell onto the circuit queue and, on failure, logs, calls circuit_mark_for_close(), and returns -1. Closing a conflux leg runs conflux_circuit_has_closed() -> cfx_del_leg(), which NULLs cfx->curr_leg when it matches the closing leg and tor_free()s the leg object. conflux_decide_circ_for_send() has already swapped cfx->curr_leg to the new hop and, treating the SWITCH send as success, writes cfx->curr_leg->last_seq_sent; after the free/NULL that store is a NULL write after free and crashes. CWE-252 (unchecked return) is the direct defect; the crash is TROVE-2026-017 / bug 41263.

causal_research.bug_semantics: AzureKeyVaultBackend, in multi-team mode, looks up a Connection or Variable by first probing the caller's team-scoped vault name and, on miss, falling through to a team-agnostic lookup that uses the caller-supplied id as the secret name. A guard `_is_team_specific_accessed_as_global` was meant to stop an id that already names a team namespace, but it is gated on `team_name is None`, so it never runs for a team-scoped caller. A caller authorized for team A can therefore pass an id that spells out another team's namespace (after the TEAM_SEP refactor, e.g. `otherteam--secret`); the team-A probe misses and the fall-through returns that other team's credentials in full (CWE-639).

causal_research.bug_semantics: On Windows, an authenticated admin-role desktop session can POST /api/system/addMicrosoftDefenderExclusion after a Defender-exclusion prompt. AddMicrosoftDefenderExclusion() concatenates the user-chosen util.WorkspaceDir into a single string (powershell -Command Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath <install> , <workspace>) and launches bundled elevator.exe via ShellExecute with the runas verb. The helper's original main() prepends cmd /c and execs that line elevated. A workspace path containing cmd.exe metacharacters therefore runs as Administrator after the user approves a routine UAC dialog. This is CWE-88/CWE-78 leading to local privilege escalation (CWE-269). Preconditions: Windows, Microsoft Defender present, attacker-controlled workspace path, UAC approval. Counterevidence to network RCE: local/UI:R; the API is CheckAuth+CheckAdminRole.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that the path really reaches a re-parsing interpreter rather than a safe argv hand-off: the pre-fix helper (siyuan-note/elevator init commit 15d97ff3, 2024-12-28) is a `cmd /c <os.Args[1:]>` passthrough, and the kernel never quoted the path (syscall.UTF16PtrFromString(strings.Join(ps, " ")) with no EscapeArg); confirmed the construction is absent from the BIC parent tree and present in the BIC child; confirmed the fix parent (39ed33479e8^) still carries the raw join and HEAD does not; checked that no sibling caller (for example the admin branch that used exec.Command directly with argv, or the non-Windows stub kernel/model/elevator.go) offers a non-injectable path to the same goal.
mechanism.impact: Local privilege escalation to high integrity: the injected command inherits the elevated elevator.exe/powershell context (CWE-78 OS command injection, CVSS:3.1 8.2/8.4, S:C because the elevated process escapes the user's security scope).
mechanism.preconditions: Windows; Microsoft Defender active; exclusion not yet recorded in conf; attacker-influenced workspace directory path (or a custom install path) containing cmd/PowerShell metacharacters; the user approves the UAC prompt (UI:R, local AV, low PR).
mechanism.summary: On Windows with Microsoft Defender active and no recorded exclusion, SiYuan builds the elevated helper's command line by space-joining the install path and the user-selected workspace path into `powershell -Command Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath <install>, <workspace>` and passes that raw string to windows.ShellExecute("runas", elevator.exe); a path containing cmd.exe or PowerShell metacharacters is re-parsed inside the elevated helper, so whoever controls the workspace (or install) path gets arbitrary command execution with administrator rights after the user approves the UAC prompt.
mechanism.trigger: Windows host with Microsoft Defender in use and Conf.System.MicrosoftDefenderExcluded unset; the user selects, or is induced to open, a workspace directory whose path contains metacharacters (the workspace path comes from the workspace chooser or a `--workspace=` launch argument) and confirms the message-252 "Add" button (POST /api/system/addMicrosoftDefenderExclusion) or the older automatic check - the elevated call then runs the concatenated command.

causal_research.reasoning:
Mechanism is a real local elevated command-injection via unescaped WorkspaceDir in the elevator.exe command line; vendor GHSA-vmp7-pm7g-ghcc and CVE-2026-74801 agree, and GHSA-pmhp-gmf7-7vhj is the published NVD GHSA alias, not a withdrawal. The smallest first writer of that Join is named-human commit e6ecfc5cbb9a5ec5b40d66b5a88cd0464f1407cb with no commit-object AI marker, parent tree lacks the files, and it is not a squash/merge. The minimum repairing siyuan commit is 39ed33479e829f0558e120324c2ccdaa52f0b1ab, present from v3.8.0-alpha.1 / stable v3.8.0 (the advisory's v3.7.4 tag does not exist). Fix-side AI is also absent and does not affect attribution. Therefore the case is a real vulnerability with human BIC: NOT_AI.
The advisory's single mechanism - the workspace (and install) path concatenated unescaped into the UAC-elevated elevator.exe command line - is present in this clone exactly as described: it is introduced by e6ecfc5cbb9, which creates kernel/model/elevator.go with strings.Join([... installPath, ",", util.WorkspaceDir], " ") handed to ShellExecute("runas", elevator.exe), and that construction is still unescaped at the fix commit's parent (39ed33479e8^). The immediate parent of the introducing commit contains no elevator or Defender code at all, so the BIC is a tree boundary, and no earlier occurrence of Add-MpPreference exists in any reachable ref. The mechanism is closed by 39ed33479e8 (validateExclusionPath plus syscall.EscapeArg plus an operation-restricted helper), with the helper binaries corrected in e94bc96f625, and HEAD v3.8.1 retains that form. Attribution on the BIC is human: e6ecfc5cbb9 is authored and committed by Daniel <845765@qq.com>, OpenPGP-signed, carrying the project's single-line convention message with no trailers, while this repository's Copilot-authored commits and AI co-author trailers only appear from 2026 and never touch kernel/model/elevator*.go. Upstream labelled the patched version v3.7.4, but no such release exists and the fix first ships in 3.8.0; that metadata error and an arity-guard no-op in the helper are recorded as non-causal residuals.
causal_research.remaining_gap: The injection is closed but two verifiable residuals sit outside it. (1) Metadata: the vendor advisory (and the OSV record behind CVE-2026-74801 / GHSA-pmhp-gmf7-7vhj) states 'patched in v3.7.4' and 'before 3.7.4', yet no v3.7.4 release exists (releases/tag/v3.7.4 returns 404; only v3.7.4-alpha.1..6 were tagged), the fix is not an ancestor of v3.7.4-alpha.6 (2026-08-02) and first ships in v3.8.0-alpha.1 (2026-08-05) / v3.8.0 (2026-08-12), so published copy must read 3.8.0 rather than 3.7.4; next minimal question for the publication leg: confirm no 3.7.4 stable artifact was ever distributed from another branch. (2) Functional regression in the remediation's helper: siyuan-note/elevator main.go at its fix commit 9a1ae3da (and current main) guards on 'if 3 != len(os.Args)' while the kernel passes the operation plus two paths (len 4), so the elevated call takes usage() and the Defender exclusion is silently skipped while the kernel still sets Conf.System.MicrosoftDefenderExcluded; no closing commit observed upstream, and the Windows binary could not be executed on this Linux host to confirm the built guard.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An OpenWire client or scanner that can complete a TCP (non-mTLS) handshake sends a command whose inner byte-array or ByteSequence length is a raw dataIn.readInt() value. OpenWireFormat.unmarshal may accept the outer frame-size prefix against maxFrameSize (default Long.MAX_VALUE, and even a tightened prefix still does not bind inner fields). BaseDataStreamMarshaller then executes int size = dataIn.readInt(); new byte[size] (looseUnmarshalByteSequence and the tight/loose byte-array helpers), so a value such as 2131230728 allocates a huge heap buffer and can OOM the broker or client (CWE-789 DoS). Mutual TLS is the documented mitigation for unpatched brokers.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the sites that could have bounded the length. readString reads a short length (at most 32 KiB) and is not part of the fix; the frame-prefix check (maxFrameSizeEnabled && size > maxFrameSize) applies to the frame prefix only and is a no-op at the default Long.MAX_VALUE; the commented-out 'Packet size does not match marshaled size' branch compares the frame prefix against the actual sequence length and never guarded inner lengths; and dataIn.readFully(rc) runs after the allocation, so a truncated frame cannot prevent the request. Both mechanisms named by the advisory (arrays and ByteSequences) were resolved, and the fix's own regression tests exercise exactly these four helper methods.
mechanism.impact: Memory allocation with excessive size value (CWE-789): the allocation is requested by the attacker and happens before any payload byte is consumed, so crafted traffic can repeatedly force multi-gigabyte allocation attempts on the broker JVM, exhausting heap/GC capacity and denying broker service to legitimate clients; the advisory rates the issue moderate with availability impact only.
mechanism.preconditions: Network reachability to an OpenWire listener and no mutual TLS (per the advisory, transport-level mTLS is the mitigation). The frame is unmarshalled before any authentication decision, so no broker credentials are required, and the default OpenWireFormat keeps maxFrameSizeEnabled=true but maxFrameSize=Long.MAX_VALUE, so the frame-prefix guard does not bound the inner buffer length.
mechanism.summary: An OpenWire frame supplies an int buffer length that is never validated against the frame carrying it; BaseDataStreamMarshaller's tight/loose unmarshalling helpers use that value directly as new byte[size] before reading the payload, so a peer can make the broker request up to about 2 GiB of heap per field and exhaust process memory.
mechanism.trigger: Open a connection to an OpenWire port without mutual TLS (the advisory's documented mitigation) and send a command whose marshaller carries a byte array or ByteSequence field -- ActiveMQMessage content or marshalledProperties, WireFormatInfo.marshalledProperties, PartialCommand.data, XATransactionId.globalTransactionId -- with a huge length value and a short or absent payload; the length is consumed before any authentication decision, so no valid credentials are needed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: free5GC NEF exposes the AF-facing 3GPP PFD-management SBI (prefix /3gpp-pfd-management/v1, routes /:scsAsID/transactions and /:scsAsID/transactions/:transID) without inbound OAuth2/bearer verification. NewServer() always registered that gin group with applyRoutes and no authorization middleware, and ServiceList was not used as a mount gate, so the API stayed reachable even when config only listed nnef-pfdmanagement/nnef-oam. Context only implemented outbound GetTokenCtx. POST allocates an AfPfdTrans and PUTs PFDs into UDR; GET reads that state; DELETE removes it. A network attacker who can reach NEF therefore creates, reads, or deletes policy-classification state with a forged Bearer token, poisoning SMF/UPF detection rules or denying legitimate PFDs.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The asynchronous PNG metadata path accepted attacker-controlled zTXt and compressed iTXt chunks and passed their deflate streams to DecompressionStream, then materialized the entire result with Response.text() without any decompressed-size bound. A small image chunk could therefore expand by orders of magnitude and consume excessive heap and CPU. Later JPEG XL Brotli and custom decompressor paths shared the same unbounded utility, widening reachability but not originating the flaw.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Rendering a ScriptObject recursively stringifies each stored member value without object-identity cycle detection. A member that points back to its containing ScriptObject therefore repeatedly re-enters object rendering; because ObjectRecursionLimit defaulted to 0 (unlimited), the guard was disabled and recursion continued until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminated the host process.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Apache Airflow EnvironmentVariablesBackend stored a team-scoped Connection or Variable as AIRFLOW_CONN__<TEAM>___<ID> / AIRFLOW_VAR__<TEAM>___<ID>. get_variable/get_conn_value probed only the caller's own namespace and then fell through to os.environ.get(PREFIX + id.upper()). Supplying the encoded identifier _<TEAM>___<ID> made that global read byte-identical to another team's namespaced variable. A later guard, _is_team_specific_accessed_as_global, was supposed to stop this but only ran when team_name is None and used re.fullmatch(r'_[^_]+___.+', secret_id), which cannot span a legal underscore-bearing team name (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{3,50}$). With the guard inapplicable, an authenticated user of one team could have POST /api/v2/connections/test call Connection.get_connection_from_secrets(connection_id) and authenticate outward with the other team's credentials. Exploitation requires [core] multi_team, [core] test_connection=Enabled (ships Disabled), team-scoped secrets in the API-server environment, and knowledge of the encoded identifier.
evidence: NVD CVE-2026-68076 vulnStatus=Analyzed (not Rejected); GHSA-75mg-c62r-v95g withdrawn_at=null; Apache oss-security 2026-08-12 (Message-ID 1bd3834d-91da-f208-64d1-f0a57169ed32@apache.org) assigns CVE-2026-68076, affected apache-airflow before 3.3.1, credit Andrew Rukin (finder) / Jarek Potiuk (remediation). causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated Magento GraphQL (frontName graphql) accepts a query document and executes it through QueryProcessor::process without bounding field aliases. An attacker POSTs a document that aliases expensive operations (for example many products selections) so each alias independently runs a costly resolver. Pre-fix production-mode checks only ran QueryComplexityLimiter::validateFieldCount plus webonyx QueryComplexity/QueryDepth (defaults queryComplexity=1000, queryDepth=20), which still allow a large number of aliased root fields under the field budget and do not stop alias-driven resource exhaustion. That is CWE-20 improper input validation leading to application DoS (CVSS AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N, no admin). APSB25-71 added validateAliasCount (default maximum_alias_allowed=10) as a preliminary check before those validators.
