causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-639 IDOR on Askbot avatar mutation views. `admin_or_owner_required` in askbot/views/avatar_views.py is supposed to allow only an administrator or the profile owner, but two interacting mistakes let any authenticated user change another user's avatar: (1) it compared `request.user.id` (int) to the Django URL capture `user_id` (always a string from `^avatar/upload/(?P<user_id>\d+)/$` and sibling routes), so the owner check never succeeded in Python 2 or 3; (2) when that check failed it fell through to `login_required(func)(request, user_id)`, which only tests authentication and then still invokes the view. The decorated sinks (`upload`, `set_primary`, `enable_gravatar`, `enable_default_avatar`, `disable_gravatar`) then `get_object_or_404(User, pk=user_id)` and write the victim's Avatar/avatar_type. A logged-in attacker POSTs to `/avatar/upload/<victim_id>/` (or intercepts and rewrites user_id) and replaces the victim's profile picture. CVE-2026-1213 remains PUBLISHED (Fluid Attacks CNA; GHSA withdrawn_at=null).

causal_research.bug_semantics: CIPster's generic attribute encode/decode treats a kCipByteArray and a companion kCipByteArrayLength as views over the same ByteBuf, which stores only start/limit and derives size() as limit-start with no immutable backing-store capacity. A remote SetAttributeSingle on a writable kCipByteArrayLength reaches CipAttribute::SetAttrData -> DecodeData(kCipByteArrayLength), which rebuilds the shared ByteBuf as ByteBuf(bb->data(), aBuf.get16()) from an attacker-supplied uint16 and thereby poisons limit. A subsequent GetAttributeSingle on the aliased kCipByteArray (GetAttrData -> EncodeData) over-reads the real allocation, and a subsequent SetAttributeSingle (SetAttrData -> DecodeData(kCipByteArray)) constructs a BufWriter from the inflated end() and memcpy-writes past the backing buffer. Stock Assembly instance attr 4 registers kCipByteArrayLength as gettable-only (isSetableSingle default false), so the default sample is not the demonstrated path; the public AttributeInsert API can register both types writable against one ByteBuf, which is the confirmed API-enabled attack.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The authenticated PUT /user/{id} flow accepted a full JSON user object, copied its client-controlled IsAdmin boolean into the domain.User, and allowed a non-admin to update their own identifier. UpdateUser preserved only BaseModel and LinkedPeerCount before saving, so it did not restore the stored IsAdmin value. A non-admin could therefore submit IsAdmin=true for their own account, persist administrator status, and obtain an administrator session after reauthentication.
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-5rmx-256w-8mj9 and the CVE.org API record for CVE-2026-27899 describe the same privilege-escalation mechanism, list versions before 2.1.3 as affected, and identify v2.1.3 as patched; the CVE record state is PUBLISHED, not rejected or withdrawn.

At vulnerable tag v2.1.2 (6e47d8c3e91a83bfdae10f97b740a22d247fb847), internal/app/api/v0/handlers/endpoint_users.go decodes the PUT body into model.User and passes model.NewDomainUser(&user) to UpdateUser; internal/app/api/v0/model/models_user.go exposes IsAdmin as json:"IsAdmin" and copies src.IsAdmin into domain.User.

At v2.1.2, internal/app/users/user_manager.go permits an authenticated user to update their own identifier, then calls user.CopyCalculatedAttributes(existingUser) and saves; internal/domain/user.go CopyCalculatedAttributes copies only BaseModel and LinkedPeerCount, leaving the request-controlled IsAdmin unchanged.

git blame at v2.1.2 attributes the vulnerable handler, model IsAdmin binding, NewDomainUser IsAdmin assignment, UpdateUser save path, and incomplete CopyCalculatedAttributes implementation to squash commit 8b820a5adf119f50757e0236ac98e842eedd35db.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Anyquery server mode binds a MySQL-wire TCP listener and forwards client SQL to the backing SQLite connection with no SQLITE_ATTACH authorizer. SQLite ATTACH DATABASE (and VACUUM INTO, which SQLite implements as attach) creates or overwrites a file at an attacker-chosen path. The Vitess/MySQL rewriter treats ATTACH as unparsable MySQL and, on StmtUnknown, runs the original statement against SQLite. Default auth is AuthServerNone when AuthFile/Users are empty, so an unauthenticated mysql client can write arbitrary files (cron, webroot PHP, authorized_keys) wherever the process can write, enabling AFW and environment-dependent RCE. Affected through 0.4.4; 0.4.5 installs a sandbox authorizer that denies non-memory ATTACH unless --allow-attach plus allowed dirs.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can add an account identity can POST an identity string containing HTML or JavaScript to /accounts/<account>/identities. The backend stores that identity string and the account-identities GET endpoint returns it. On the WebUI account page, load_identities handed the returned objects directly to jQuery DataTables as data and selected the identity and type properties as columns. DataTables treated those string values as cell HTML, so merely viewing the affected account page inserted the persisted identity into the DOM and executed attacker-controlled script in the viewer's WebUI origin.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 created the account-administration page and lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js. Its new load_identities function passed the server response directly to DataTable with `data: data` and `columns: [{'data': 'identity'}, {'data': 'type'}]`, without encoding the identity before the HTML sink. The same feature commit also added the UI's identity-creation helper, completing the store-and-render path. The pre-existing backend identity model/API stored and returned the supplied identity as data; the vulnerability began when this commit added the unsafe browser rendering, not when later code was moved or refactored.

Vulnerable flow at the fix parent: lib/rucio/web/rest/flaskapi/v1/accounts.py parses the POST identity and calls add_account_identity, while its GET generator serializes every result of list_identities; lib/rucio/core/identity.py add_identity assigns the supplied string directly to models.Identity.identity. The WebUI client lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rucio.js requests /accounts/<account>/identities, and account.js load_identities sent the returned objects directly to DataTables. `git log -L :load_identities:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003^` traces the vulnerable `data: data` identity/type block to 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 (2017-11-06), where account.js was a new file; the only later change shown before the encoding fix changed an unrelated url_param error sink. `git show --format=raw 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78` gives sole parent 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e and the exact author/committer/message above. Direct parent-tree checks are negative: `git cat-file -e 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js` reports that the path does not exist, and `git grep -E 'load_identities|identities_table|DataTable.*identit|identity.*DataTable' 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e -- lib/rucio/web/ui` returns no match. This proves the immediate parent lacks both the new file and an equivalent account-identity DataTable sink. Release introduction: `git tag --contains 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 --sort=version:refname` begins at 1.13.3; tag 1.13.3 contains account.js load_identities and `data: data`, while tag 1.13.2 has no account.js and 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 is not its ancestor. Fix: direct master commit b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25 (`fix(WebUI): fix XSS using DataTable`, first committed to master on 2026-02-25) replaces direct response rendering with sanitisedData, encoding identity/type via `$('<div>').text(String(value)).html()` and retaining raw values only under non-displayed $identity/$type keys for API operations. The same patch was applied to release lines as a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 (contained by tag 35.8.3), abf5e978ee3910590a23c6705e6a0105c0b847c7 (contained by 38.5.4), and 80b91dd0c6737b2ab9aed039470e8e81028def41 (contained by 39.3.1); 3b6cea7848eea31a6342190d1cdb680b8fcb1eb2 carries it on the 39.4 line. A six-tag `git grep` verifies account.js:136 is still `data: data` in 35.8.2, 38.5.3, and 39.3.0, whereas 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1 contain sanitisedData and feed that encoded array to DataTables, exactly matching all three advisory patch boundaries. Release references: https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/35.8.3, https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/38.5.4, and https://github.com/rucio/rucio/releases/tag/39.3.1.
causal_research.reasoning: The security property that fails is output encoding at a browser HTML sink. Arbitrary identity text is intentionally valid backend data, so persistence alone is not the BIC; the exploitable mechanism appears when the account page first renders that server-controlled identity through DataTables without encoding. Line history identifies 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 as the first writer of the exact vulnerable load_identities block. It is an ordinary one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, backport, merge, or squash aggregate, so there is no smaller reconstructable member commit to substitute and no squash decomposition to record. The master fix b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25 is the direct source patch; a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 is recorded as fix_sha because it is the patch carried by the advisory's first listed fixed release, with the other release-line copies fully identified in evidence. causal_research.bug_semantics: A signed user TA can set TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT in its ta_head.flags even though that flag is documented as pseudo-TA only. The user-TA loader accepts any bits in TA_FLAGS_MASK and copies them onto the shared tee_ta_ctx. tee_ta_try_set_busy() then returns immediately without taking the busy lock, so two sessions of a single-instance multi-session user TA run concurrently on one context. Both sessions map and unmap memref parameters against the same uctx->vm_info.regions list with no lock, corrupting the list and freeing vm_region nodes still in use: a use-after-free in S-EL1.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-71968 state=PUBLISHED (cveMetadata.state, datePublished 2026-08-10, dateUpdated 2026-08-17); not rejected. GHSA-p84g-83m7-53p6 withdrawn_at is null. Vendor/CNA: OP-TEE optee_os affected 0 through 4.10.0, unaffected git 8794043c4065c26a2b8b1313794ba5ba5f06d296. Finder credit Argus Systems / ByteRay Ltd.

PR/commit text: flag sits inside TA_FLAGS_MASK so a user TA can set it; tee_ta_try_set_busy() skips serialization; concurrent memref map/unmap corrupts uctx->vm_info.regions and frees live vm_region nodes.

Named Fixes: tag c7c4b6e31b3ba5b1c92a50fc00680fc07755e4ef (2017-11-14, Jens Wiklander) introduced TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT (bit 8, comment 'pseudo-TAs only') and the skip-lock in tee_ta_try_set_busy()/tee_ta_clear_busy(). BIC 387b0ee39b1b8d5a8a0db68a0a4535d2d621342d (author Etienne Carriere, 2018-04-05) first wrote #define TA_FLAGS_MASK GENMASK_32(8,2) in lib/libutee/include/user_ta_header.h and replaced the whitelist with if (ta_head->flags & ~TA_FLAGS_MASK) in core/arch/arm/kernel/user_ta.c ta_load(), then utc->ctx.flags = ta_head->flags. GENMASK_32(h,l) is inclusive; GENMASK_32(8,2) includes bit 8 (TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT). Single parent, not a merge. git log -S TA_FLAGS_MASK -- lib/libutee/include/user_ta_header.h starts at this commit.

Parent-tree verification at 027f050651f1729eac3c50ecd8e8d3941463bf51: user_ta_header.h has TA_FLAG_CONCURRENT but no TA_FLAGS_MASK; user_ta.c still uses the optional_flags whitelist that omits CONCURRENT. Immediate parent therefore cannot accept a user TA with the concurrent bit. At the BIC, skip-lock already existed in tee_ta_manager.c and utc->vm_info->regions / tee_mmu_map_param already existed, so the UAF race is reachable as soon as the mask allows the flag.

Later loader rewrites are moves/refactors of the same check, not a new BIC: 7509ff7ce5e5a7679319e6fa059b71dd6f6cc8b9 and d1911a85142da16fef5ebdcdac0348d29ce37cd8 copied if (flags & ~TA_FLAGS_MASK) into ldelf/ta_elf.c and the kernel ldelf path; 486d6e395e6146bba6d45838e59a737494819ba4 moved it to ldelf_loader.c. causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan classifies pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL opcodes as Dangerous only when the (module, name) pair hits its denylist (_suspicious_globals, later renamed _unsafe_globals). logging.FileHandler was never on that denylist through v1.0.0, so a REDUCE payload that instantiates logging.FileHandler(path) scans without a Dangerous finding. Loading the pickle constructs FileHandler in default append mode: a missing path becomes a new zero-byte file at an attacker-chosen location (lock-file / filesystem-pollution DoS); an existing path is opened without overwrite. The scanner itself uses pickletools.genops rather than pickle.loads; the bypass is that downstream users who trust a clean/non-Dangerous scan then deserialize the file.

causal_research.bug_semantics: picklescan is a denylist scanner of pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL imports, not an unpickler. A crafted pickle REDUCE of torch.utils.data.datapipes.utils.decoder.basichandlers with extension 'pickle' and nested pickle bytes is extracted as that single (module, name) pair. Through 0.0.27 the pair is absent from _unsafe_globals (originally _suspicious_globals), so it is not counted as Dangerous: original scan_pickle_bytes only increments issues_count on denylist hits, and v0.0.27 _build_scan_result_from_raw_globals else-branch sets Suspicious without incrementing issues_count. cli.py returns 0 when issues_count==0, so a clean scan is reported. The victim then pickle.load()s; PyTorch basichandlers pickle.loads the nested bytes and executes the inner reduce (PoC os.system). Inner dangerous globals are not visible in the outer opcode stream. Impact is scanner-bypass RCE for users who treat a clean picklescan as a load gate.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) starts a recursive SCP receive and trusts the filename captured from each server-controlled C (file) or D (directory) protocol record. It joins that unvalidated value to the current local download directory and then creates the directory or opens the file for writing. A malicious, compromised, or MITM server can therefore supply ../ components (and, after the later Path.Combine form, rooted paths) to escape the caller's destination and create or overwrite any path writable by the client process. Exploitation requires the victim to initiate a recursive directory download from the attacker-controlled endpoint.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A Netty HTTP/2 server tracks client-initiated streams on connection.remote(). DefaultEndpoint constructs that endpoint with maxActiveStreams/maxStreams = Integer.MAX_VALUE, so createStream refuses only after ~2^31 streams. SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS advertised by the local endpoint is applied to remote.maxActiveStreams only in DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder.applyLocalSettings, which runs on SETTINGS_ACK of locally sent settings. Http2Settings.defaultSettings() historically omitted that key (only maxHeaderListSize), so ACK application was a no-op and the cap stayed MAX_VALUE. A client can therefore open unbounded streams on one TCP connection (each allocating DefaultStream, PropertyMap, flow-controller state, IntObjectHashMap entry), causing CWE-400 memory/CPU exhaustion and amplifying Rapid Reset. Even after #16804/#16816 put 100 into defaultSettings (already in 4.1.134.Final / 4.2.14.Final), enforcement still waited for ACK, so a client that omits the setting or opens streams before ACK still saw MAX_VALUE. The 4.1.135.Final / 4.2.15.Final builder calls connection.remote().maxActiveStreams from initialSettings at build time, closing that window.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The unbounded default was first written in 754e08796b83da4e682167914041cd03350cda4a (2014-03-27) as DefaultEndpoint.maxStreams = Integer.MAX_VALUE in the original HTTP/2 draft-10 codec. Immediate parent 5d141242c998adfe5525c33dbd3799f85e73d871 has no codec-http2 tree. Subsequent draft-12 rewrite (ca7c53d) and 4.1 backport (2d24e1f) copied the same default; they are not the original introducer. ACK-gated application (f978999, 2014-05-09) is a later contributing exposure for advertised limits, not the first writer of the unbounded default.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 754e08796b to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: The advisory stated root cause is only half right: Http2Settings.defaultSettings() already sets maxConcurrentStreams(DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS = 100, Http2CodecUtil.java:116/126) and AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.java:80 defaults initialSettings to exactly that, so a default server does advertise a limit and the pre-ACK window is the defect, not a missing advertisement. I also confirmed the guard itself works after the ACK (applyLocalSettings installs 100 and later streams are refused), so this is not a total absence of enforcement.
mechanism.impact: One TCP connection can hold hundreds of thousands of long-lived DefaultStream objects plus flow-controller and header-decoding state, exhausting server memory and CPU; the absent low cap is also the amplification precondition the advisory names for rapid-reset style abuse.
mechanism.preconditions: Default builder construction (or any path where the local settings are not enforced before the ACK); attacker controls the client connection and can open streams before acknowledging the server SETTINGS; no application code sets connection.remote().maxActiveStreams itself.
mechanism.summary: An HTTP/2 client that withholds or delays the SETTINGS ACK while opening many HEADERS streams -> the server advertised max concurrent streams is only copied onto connection.remote() inside applyLocalSettings, which runs only from onSettingsAckRead, so the remote endpoint keeps its DefaultEndpoint default of Integer.MAX_VALUE -> the server accepts unbounded concurrent streams on one connection (CWE-400 resource exhaustion, and the precondition the advisory names for CVE-2023-44487-style amplification).
mechanism.trigger: Server built through AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder with settings whose maxConcurrentStreams has not yet been applied, plus an attacker-controlled client that opens streams and never (or very late) sends the ACK for the server SETTINGS frame. The client still sends its own preface SETTINGS first (RFC 7540 section 3.5), but its ACK is untimed and fully attacker-controlled.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder.java:469-474 (onSettingsAckRead is the only caller of applyLocalSettings) and :499 (connection.remote().maxActiveStreams((int) min(maxConcurrentStreams, MAX_VALUE))), with DefaultHttp2Connection.java:742 (maxActiveStreams = MAX_VALUE), :772 (canOpenStream), :937-940 (checkNewStreamAllowed throws REFUSED_STREAM), at netty-4.1.134.Final (970b248b56653f7fff8b18c5cc06c71ac344851e).

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real CWE-400 HTTP/2 concurrent-stream DoS: remote endpoint starts at Integer.MAX_VALUE and the advertised SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS is not applied to that endpoint until SETTINGS_ACK, and historically was omitted from defaultSettings entirely. The smallest original writer of that unbounded default is 754e08796b83da4e682167914041cd03350cda4a; its parent tree has no HTTP/2 codec. 4.1/4.2 received the same default via backport 2d24e1f, which is rejected as BIC. The minimum closer is #16876 / f5da73e (4.1.135.Final) and fd6f314 (4.2.15.Final), which apply initialSettings.maxConcurrentStreams to connection.remote() at builder time. BIC commit-object attribution is named human nmittler@gmail.com with no AI markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Fix-side authors are also named humans; that does not change BIC-side attribution.
The advisory describes a real defect: a Netty HTTP/2 server copies its own advertised MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS onto the remote endpoint only inside applyLocalSettings, which is called solely from onSettingsAckRead, so until the peer acknowledges the server SETTINGS frame the remote endpoint keeps its DefaultEndpoint default of Integer.MAX_VALUE and the server accepts unbounded streams. I verified that the immediate parents of both fixes lack enforceMaxActiveStreams, and that both fixes add the same 15-line builder hunk enforcing initialSettings.maxConcurrentStreams() at handler-build time. The vulnerable shape enters the 4.1 lineage with the 2015-01-19 backport 2d24e1f27d0, whose parent ed10513238c2 contains no codec-http2 directory, and whose commit object is a named-human change (author Nitesh Kant, committer Scott Mitchell) with a human-written motivation and no AI or tool trailers. The underlying design is 2014 master-lineage code, already present in Http2InboundConnectionHandler.java at 741ea7766c before the decoder was split into its own class, and every candidate object along that path is a pre-LLM named-human commit. The fixes are likewise named-human (Norman Maurer, Chris Vest) with no AI markers. One advisory detail is inaccurate: Http2Settings.defaultSettings() does set maxConcurrentStreams to DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS (100) and the builder uses those defaults, so a default server does advertise 100; the defect is the enforcement timing, not a missing advertisement. Verdict NOT_AI: this is human-introduced 2014-2015 codec behaviour and no AI contribution is visible on the BIC side.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Two limits, neither affecting the verdict. First, BIC minimality is lineage-bounded: 2d24e1f27d0 is a declared backport of master-authored code and the 2014 master-side objects are missing from the partial clone, so the exact first 2014 commit is not pinned; the next minimal question is whether ca7c53d45f (2014-05-03, Add support for HTTP/2 draft 12) already contains the ACK-gated applyLocalSettings, answerable from its github.com raw or patch page. Second, the fix is builder-scoped: hand-constructed Http2ConnectionHandler instances and custom initialSettings without maxConcurrentStreams are not covered by enforceMaxActiveStreams.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Angular SSR reconstructed the request's absolute base URL from attacker-controlled Host and X-Forwarded-* headers without syntax or destination validation, then used that URL as the server-rendering origin and exposed the request to application code. An attacker able to supply those headers could therefore steer relative HttpClient requests or application-built requests to an attacker-selected external or internal host, with malformed host/path/port values also enabling header or URL injection behavior.

causal_research.bug_semantics: asbplayer loads user-supplied subtitle files and, when the SubtitleHtml.render setting is on, leaves markup in cue text. SubtitleReader._filterText only optionally calls _decodeHTML (innerHTML-then-textContent strip) when subtitleHtml===remove; it performed no sanitization on the render path. Cue text is then interpolated unescaped into the video overlay via subtitle-controller._buildTextHtml → element-overlay innerHTML, and into the subtitle list via React dangerouslySetInnerHTML. A crafted .srt with HTML such as <script><button onmouseover=...> is therefore executed in the hosting streaming-site origin after the user loads the file with render-HTML enabled. Default remains SubtitleHtml.remove, so the setting is part of the UI:R path. This is stored XSS (CWE-79), not unrestricted upload/RCE; NVD later corrected the English description from file-upload RCE to XSS while leaving CWE-434.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An application can put request-derived text into HttpException::setTitle() or setDescription(). With displayErrorDetails=false, HtmlErrorRenderer::__invoke() copied those values into an HTML paragraph and into renderHtmlBody(), which inserted the title into both <title> and <h1>, without HTML escaping. An attacker-controlled title or description therefore becomes executable markup in the reflected error response.
evidence: The frozen bundle records GHSA-53h4-8rc4-f539 / CVE-2026-48157 as reflected XSS in HtmlErrorRenderer, affecting slim/slim >=4.4.0 through 4.15.1 and patched in 4.15.2; its stated attack condition is untrusted data supplied to HttpException::setTitle() or setDescription(), including when displayErrorDetails=false.

The CVE.org record fetched from https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-48157 is PUBLISHED, describes the same title/description-to-HTML attack path, marks >=4.4.0,<4.15.2 affected, and names 4.15.2 as fixed; this is not a rejected or withdrawn advisory.

, and line 35 passes getErrorTitle() to renderHtmlBody().

causal_research.bug_semantics: CIPster's generic AttributeInsert(CipDataType, void*) binds an untyped storage cookie to an arbitrary CIP type with no layout check. An API-enabled deployment can register the same ByteBuf object as both a writable kCipByteArray and a writable kCipUdint. A remote unauthenticated EtherNet/IP SetAttributeSingle on the UDINT view hits DecodeData(kCipUdint), which stores 32 bits into ByteBuf.start (the first pointer of {start, limit}) while leaving limit unchanged, inflating logical size. A following GetAttributeSingle or SetAttributeSingle on the byte-array view hits EncodeData/DecodeData(kCipByteArray), which construct BufReader/BufWriter from that poisoned ByteBuf; BufWriter::append then memcpy's against attacker-controlled start/limit (ASan: 80-byte OOB read/write from backing-16). The default sample is not claimed exploitable; the primitive is CIPster's public attribute-registration API plus generic Get/SetAttrData.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-13592 state=PUBLISHED (CNA VulDB, datePublished 2026-06-29, dateUpdated 2026-07-01); GHSA-xxw5-vgjv-jc6g withdrawn_at=null. Not withdrawn/rejected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can influence the Base64-encoded REDIRECT_URI cookie supplies an absolute or protocol-relative URI. CookieServerRequestCache decoded that untrusted cookie and returned URI.create(decoded) without restricting it to a relative path; post-authentication RedirectServerAuthenticationSuccessHandler passed the result to the redirect strategy. The Servlet implementation likewise decoded the cookie into scheme, host, port, path, and query for a SavedRequest that its authentication-success handler redirected to. Thus cookie control reached the post-login redirect sink and enabled an attacker-controlled cross-origin redirect.

causal_research.bug_semantics: nltk.pathsec is the centralized I/O sentinel (path, file://, urlopen/SSRF, zip-slip, and pickle-adjacent loads). Through 3.9.4 it initialized ENFORCE=False, so every validation gate that detected an unauthorized path or URL emitted RuntimeWarning and then continued instead of raising PermissionError. With the default unset, pathsec.open('/etc/passwd') and equivalent untrusted loads succeed; NLTK_PATHSEC_ENFORCE / nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE=True is required to actually block. This is CWE-1188 (insecure default), not a missing check: the checks exist but fail open. First-party GHSA-p3m8-78j2-g5p3 (published, not withdrawn) and CVE-2026-62388 (CVE.org PUBLISHED) both name this default. Affected shipped range is the pathsec-bearing 3.9.4 line; 3.10.0 flips the default to ENFORCE=True.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The HTML writer passed an attacker-controlled cell value through a custom number format and escaped the result only when the formatted string exactly equalled the original value. For an unquoted @ text placeholder plus any literal text, such as '. @' or '@ ', Formatter substituted the raw cell value and returned early without invoking the HTML writer's escaping callback; the added literal made the formatted value unequal to the original, so Writer/Html.php also skipped htmlspecialchars(). An uploaded spreadsheet could therefore emit a raw script-capable tag into generated HTML and cause stored XSS when that HTML was viewed.
evidence: CVE.org record CVE-2026-40296 is PUBLISHED and describes stored XSS caused by Writer/Html skipping escaping when custom @ number formats make the formatted value differ; it lists affected ranges through 1.30.3, 2.1.15, 2.4.4, 3.10.4, and 5.6.0 and fixes 1.30.4, 2.1.16, 2.4.5, 3.10.5, and 5.7.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An Ingress that sets nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-type to basic or digest declares that the location must not reach the backend without BasicAuth/DigestAuth. Traefik resolves the referenced auth-secret while building the data-plane config. On missing, empty, malformed, unreadable, or policy-denied secrets, resolveBasicAuth (post-metamodel) or applyBasicAuthConfiguration (original kubernetes.go) returns an error. The controller logs that error and omits the auth middleware, but still publishes a router to the real backend (original: conf.HTTP.Routers[key]=rt after a logged applyMiddlewares error; v3.7.0–3.7.4: loc.Error stays false so translator.go does not rewrite the service to unavailable-service). Nearby failures fail closed (custom-headers sets loc.Error; auth-tls-secret skips the ingress). Preconditions: KubernetesIngressNGINX provider enabled, Ingress with auth-type basic/digest, auth-secret unusable. Impact: unauthenticated access to a route operators marked as auth-protected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The Markdown and PDF evaluation-export routes checked only whether the requester could view the conversion, while build_evaluation_report() selected every non-deleted evaluation comment and serialized each comment's content and author's first name without applying the existing per-comment privacy rule. A requester allowed to view a conversion could therefore export private evaluation comments that should have been visible only to the conversion owner, the comment author, or an administrator.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f directly introduced both export routes and build_evaluation_report(). The new routes called the report builder after only conversion-level authorization, and the new builder unconditionally appended all evaluation comments. The immediate parent already had the ordinary comment-visibility policy but had neither the report builder nor the export routes, so this is a direct feature introduction rather than a later import, move, rename, refactor, or aggregate.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated Teamlead (or anyone who may edit a Team) can call POST /api/teams/{id}/members/{userId}, /customers/{customerId}, /projects/{projectId}, or /activities/{activityId} and persist a relation to a referenced User/Customer/Project/Activity that the caller cannot see or manage in the UI. The controller historically authorized only the team (is_granted('edit_team'), later TeamVoter #[IsGranted('edit', 'team')] requiring teamlead-of-this-team plus edit_team) and then addUser/addCustomer/addProject/addActivity without a second IsGranted on the MapEntity target. Downstream RolePermissionManager::checkTeamAccess* treats those relations as legitimate, so the team becomes an expansion container for out-of-scope users and entities, affecting visibility, time-entry, reporting, and team isolation. 2.58.0 closed this GHSA by adding #[IsGranted('access_user', 'member')] and #[IsGranted('view', customer|project|activity)] on those grant actions.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated static-download route passes request.getParameter("version") into BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension without validating it. For a request to the route base (/file/static/noauth in the renamed endpoint, formerly /downloadFile/static/noauth), the path-derived fileName is "noauth", whose full-path component is empty, so the helper replaces it entirely with attacker-controlled version. A value such as ../../etc/passwd is then handed to FileUtils.readFile(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName, ...), which constructs new File(APP_DOWNLOAD_FOLDER_PATH, fileName) and can escape the intended download directory, exposing arbitrary readable files without authentication.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46 added version as a cache/content-identity filename override during a resources/web-client refactor. The normal producer generated an ID for version, but DownloadFileRequestHandler treated the HTTP parameter as if it were trusted and reused it as a filesystem child path. The already-existing security rule exempted /downloadFile/static/noauth/** from authentication, making this new trust-boundary error remotely reachable immediately.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46` shows human author AlexKirkouski <alex.kirkouski@gmail.com> and the same human committer, subject `Resources / web client refactoring`, and no body or trailers; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other commit-object AI marker.
causal_research.evidence: First-party report https://github.com/lsfusion/platform/issues/1543 identifies unauthenticated `/file/static/noauth` plus attacker-controlled `version`, the handler path, arbitrary file read, and affected versions through 6.1. In the validated full-history clone, `git log -L 44,46:web-client/src/main/java/lsfusion/http/controller/file/DownloadFileRequestHandler.java 9dc9a7889f8120d6bd6802c09b374639642cbcb9^` resolves the complete vulnerable three-line version block to b34987f7b37b5fd6a03b9dd9092bd18efc936d46; reverse `git log -S'request.getParameter("version")'` over both historical handler paths finds the same sole introduction. `git show b34987...` shows the exact addition: read `version`, test only for non-null, then call `BaseUtils.replaceFileNameAndExtension(fileName, version)`. At that tree, BaseUtils.java implements that helper as `FilenameUtils.getFullPath(filePath) + toName`; FileUtils.java:57 reads `createFile(relativePath, fileName)`, and createFile at line 81 is `new File(relativePath, fileName)`. The same BIC tree's applicationContext-security.xml:39-44 exempts `/downloadFile/static/noauth/**` and requires authentication only for the remaining `/downloadFile/**`. Direct parent-tree verification is concrete: `git show 51dd90c21ec7e7b289fde206208106cf80b835f8:web-client/src/main/java/lsfusion/http/controller/file/DownloadFileRequestHandler.java` contains the path extraction and FileUtils.readFile sink but no `version` parameter read or filename replacement, while `git diff 51dd90c... b34987f... -- <handler>` adds exactly those four vulnerable lines. Tag ancestry establishes the boundary: `git tag --contains b34987...` returns 5.0-beta0, 5.0, 5.1, all 6.0 tags, 6.1, and 6.2, while 4.1 does not contain it; thus repository history narrows the advisory's unbounded `<= 6.1` statement to introduction beginning with 5.0-beta0. Original fix 9dc9a7889f8120d6bd6802c09b374639642cbcb9 (`Fixed unauthorized arbitrary file read (closes #1543)`) rejects version values containing `..` with HTTP 400 before replacement. Release-bearing commit d828168524d47f78426b68a58ef7905eb2d4dca0 applies the identical patch and records `(cherry picked from commit 9dc9a788...)`; `git tag --contains d828168...` returns 6.2, while no tag contains 9dc9a788... and 6.1 contains neither fix. Therefore 6.1 remains vulnerable and 6.2 contains the fix, despite the advisory snapshot's null first_patched_version.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerable mechanism is not merely the later endpoint rename: commit 256ae9dcb19d8762b1cb43f2d1e688d46592581c changed `/downloadFile` to `/file` while preserving both the unauthenticated `static/noauth` exception and the pre-existing unvalidated version override. The BIC is a single-parent repository commit whose vulnerable hunk is directly present; no smaller member commit is exposed in the clone, so no squash decomposition is claimed. The original direct fix is 9dc9a7889f8120d6bd6802c09b374639642cbcb9; d828168524d47f78426b68a58ef7905eb2d4dca0 is its explicit cherry-pick and the fix object actually contained by release tag 6.2. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object: it has only human AlexKirkouski author/committer metadata and no AI trailer or bot marker. That supports the closed NOT_AI verdict independently of any later history.

causal_research.bug_semantics: devalue.parse accepts attacker-controlled flattened JSON and sends it to unflatten. For the SPARSE encoding [-7, length, index, value, ...], the vulnerable parser passed the untrusted declared length directly to new Array(length). On V8, many small payload entries with large declared lengths can therefore trigger eager contiguous backing-store allocations far exceeding the input size and exhaust process memory, causing denial of service.
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-77vg-94rm-hx3p and the PUBLISHED CVE.org record CVE-2026-42570 describe remotely reachable excessive memory consumption in devalue.parse for sparse-array deserialization, affect >=5.6.3 and <5.8.1, and identify 5.8.1 as patched.

git log -L 218,238:src/parse.js 14933f78ff6b712829162628682b0a1993e75d19 and git log -S 'const array = new Array(len)' -- src/parse.js both trace the vulnerable allocation to 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0 and its removal to 206ca6712fbc380a4571c59de9ab04b91110792d.

git diff 0f04d4d678eac39ad5d7a07d1956275d7874e81c 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0 -- src/parse.js shows the BIC adding src/parse.js:205-215, including const len = value[1] and const array = new Array(len); direct inspection of 0f04d4d678eac39ad5d7a07d1956275d7874e81c:src/parse.js finds no SPARSE branch, sparse-array encoding, or new Array(len).

The public BIC object has exactly one parent, 0f04d4d678eac39ad5d7a07d1956275d7874e81c. Its aggregate 'Merge commit from fork' message lists development subjects, but exact subject searches over all validated-clone refs recover no separate member SHA for the introducing SPARSE parser change, so the first surviving public object cannot be decomposed further.

Tag topology verifies the advisory boundary: 819f1ac7475ab37547645cfb09bf2f678a799cf0 is an ancestor of v5.6.3 (tag target a4a37d208a4d1bdd0d58c82e5644c87cab855259) but not v5.6.2 (fcf4e88275f2e2e45b9ea70ffaa5247c8f55f057).

Direct fix 206ca6712fbc380a4571c59de9ab04b91110792d replaces new Array(len) with an initially empty array, forces dictionary-elements mode by touching and deleting MAX_ARRAY_INDEX, hydrates supplied entries, and assigns array.length only afterward; its regression test documents payloads whose implied eager allocation is about 20 GB.

The direct fix parent is 14933f78ff6b712829162628682b0a1993e75d19, the v5.8.0 tag target, and still contains src/parse.js:226 const array = new Array(len). The fix is an ancestor of v5.8.1 (tag target 796ea83a76eb7e0f2af376f9c2c875f1d057f50f) but not v5.8.0.

BIC 4c277fe1 (2018-09-02, PR #296, allow markdown in timesheet descriptions) introduced the Twig filter desc2html (timesheetContent, is_safe html) routing the description through Markdown::toHtml($content, false), i.e. Parsedown 1.x setSafeMode(false); with kimai.timesheet.markdown enabled, the user timesheet template switched from entry.description|nl2br to unescaped entry.description|desc2html, so HTML/SVG in a description renders as trusted markup for anyone viewing timesheet/export/invoice. Parent 9f6079ad (2018-09-02, added option to delete invoice template, #294) renders the same field as entry.description|nl2br in templates/timesheet/index.html.twig (auto-escaped) and plain entry.description in templates/admin/timesheet.html.twig, with no desc2html filter anywhere (checked src/Twig/MarkdownExtension.php, config/services.yaml and both templates). git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms 9f6079ad is the immediate parent of 4c277fe1. Minimum fix a0e8aa3a (2019-07-14, PR #962, fixed xss in timesheet description) adds the Twig |escape filter before desc2html at every remaining desc2html call site (templates/timesheet/index.html.twig, templates/timesheet/export.html.twig, templates/timesheet-team/export.html.twig, templates/invoice/index.html.twig, templates/export/renderer/default.html.twig, templates/export/renderer/pdf.html.twig); the former admin/timesheet.html.twig call site had already been removed, so the fix covers all remaining vulnerable call sites. causal_research.bug_semantics: Cachet 3.x incident templates (implemented in dependency cachethq/core) store a user-authored template body and compile it when an incident is created from that template. BladeRenderer::render() passes the stored string to Laravel Blade::render(), so @php / raw Blade executes as PHP. TwigRenderer::render() builds a non-sandboxed Twig\Environment and createTemplate()s the stored string, so callable filters (map/filter/reduce/sort) and source() can invoke PHP functions or read files. CreateIncident::parseTemplate() is the trigger. Any authenticated user who can create templates and incidents (Filament IncidentTemplate/Incident resources have no isAdmin canAccess; API tokens with incident-templates.manage / incidents.manage, defaulting to *) obtains RCE as the web server.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-69118 state=PUBLISHED (assigner VulnCheck, datePublished 2026-08-10); GHSA-9qx4-4584-p9h2 type=unreviewed, withdrawn_at=null. Not rejected/withdrawn.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The DuckDB AWS extension exposed SQL table function load_aws_credentials, which resolved the AWS default credential provider chain (profile files, env, IMDSv2, IRSA, ECS task role, EC2 instance role) and returned access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token, and region as result columns. Named parameter redact_secret (default true) gated only the secret_access_key column; CALL load_aws_credentials(redact_secret=false) emitted the secret in plaintext. That opt-out was independent of DuckDB's later database-wide allow_unredacted_secrets=false policy (AllowUnredactedSecretsSetting), so any principal with SQL execution could dump live AWS credentials without enabling unredacted secrets. The original return path also always printed session_token unredacted. The complete fix deleted the function rather than relying on a bind-time policy check.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-58139 state=PUBLISHED (cveMetadata.state, datePublished 2026-08-03, dateUpdated 2026-08-14); CNA VulnCheck title 'DuckDB AWS Extension Security Policy Bypass via load_aws_credentials Procedure'; affected duckdb/duckdb-aws git version 0 lessThan 7d04119ee8d3f8836e278f0e8cbf21827ff5338b; GHSA-g2r8-97m7-62w9 withdrawn_at=null. Not withdrawn/rejected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated board editor could send a single-block or batch PATCH naming a comment block created by another member. The handlers checked only the caller's general ability to manage board cards and the target block's board, then applied the caller-controlled patch; they never enforced comment ownership or the elevated permission for acting on other users' comments. This let an editor alter another member's comment and caused unauthorized integrity loss.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The atomic PR-member commit 7c1d63a9d9ee6a5f82655f780196d96f35cdd12e first added the PATCH route, handlePatchBlock, App.PatchBlock, BlockPatch.Patch, and SQLStore.PatchBlock. handlePatchBlock accepted any authenticated workspace member resolved by getContainer and passed the requested block ID and patch to storage without comparing the caller to the comment creator. The later mainline squash c734cfb8d16b1a4a20e3fb03b3afdf052fa53fce preserved that vulnerable handler; 3450eb6d4ffda75d303f53795b3d7c38cecd2330 later added the similarly vulnerable batch endpoint but was not the first exposure.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ClassroomIO treated email-verification state and token contents as client authority. The profile table's existing own-row UPDATE policy allowed an authenticated user to set the newly added is_email_verified column directly through PostgREST. Independently, the emailed verification value was only Base64-encoded JSON containing a client-selected profileId and orgSiteName; /api/verify decoded it without a signature, expiry, one-time-use check, authenticated-user binding, or ownership check and used profileId in a privileged profile update. An attacker could therefore self-verify through the profile API or forge data for the verification endpoint to mark a chosen profile verified without controlling its mailbox.
causal_research.flaw_origin: PR #215's first member commit, 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf, created the verification-email route, the /api/verify route, and the profile verification columns. It first wrote both the unsigned btoa(JSON.stringify({ profileId, orgSiteName })) token construction and the unvalidated profile update, while the pre-existing policy "Users can update own profile." permitted an authenticated owner to update all profile columns. Member 947cfc06ca3a858972e8faafd096c7f662ef6086 later changed /api/verify to getServerSupabase, completing the arbitrary-profile service-role attack path, but it retained rather than originated the client-authoritative token and update mechanism. GitHub squash bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc landed the reconstructed member series on main.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Apache Airflow Task SDK deserialized JSON Variables and then dispatched masking on the top-level Python type. After json.loads, only str values (and, after CVE-2026-59244, dict values) were passed to mask_secret; a top-level list matched neither branch and was returned unmasked. Secrets stored as a JSON array therefore never entered the secrets masker, so they appeared in cleartext in task logs and in the Rendered Templates UI to any authenticated user who could read those views. add_mask already walked iterables under a supplied name, so nested lists inside a dict were masked; only a top-level list was skipped. The correct list handling is mask_secret(list, variable_key) so elements inherit the Variable key's sensitivity without anonymously over-masking ordinary values.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated stored XSS in the server-database avatar pipeline. user.updateAvatar accepts any data:image* payload (including data:image/svg;base64,...) with no MIME allowlist or SVG sanitization, derives the object extension from the attacker-controlled subtype, and stores the bytes at user/avatar/<userId>/<uuid>.svg. GET /webapi/user/avatar/[id]/[image] then returns those bytes with Content-Type image/svg+xml (CONTENT_TYPE_MAP.svg), no Content-Disposition: attachment, no nosniff, and no script-blocking CSP. A victim who navigates to that same-origin URL (or any embed that parses the SVG as a document) executes the attacker's script in the LobeChat origin. UI avatar widgets rasterize uploads to WebP via canvas, but the tRPC mutation and CLI path do not. CVE.org CVE-2026-72594 is PUBLISHED (TuranSec, not rejected/withdrawn); GHSA-cjxw-hmxq-h489 withdrawn_at is null. Affected through v2.2.13 as stated; the same sink is still present at clone HEAD.

causal_research.bug_semantics: MessagePack skip-entire-structure walks nested arrays and maps by recursion and never increments MessagePackReader.Depth or consults MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth. In the 2.x/3.x API this is MessagePackReader.TrySkip(): maps/arrays call TrySkipNextMap/TrySkipNextArray, which loop TrySkip() on each child, so a skipped unknown field whose value is a chain of single-element fixarrays/fixmaps grows C# stack frames until an uncatchable StackOverflowException kills the process. Generated/dynamic formatters, IgnoreFormatter, and unknown-key/default branches invoke reader.Skip() during ordinary deserialization of untrusted payloads; UntrustedData does not mitigate because skip does not participate in depth accounting. The same recursion existed earlier as MessagePackBinary.ReadNextBlock (v1 formatters used that to skip unknown members).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Non-deterministic claim validation in fast-jwt (GHSA-3j8v-cgw4-2g6q): allowedAud/allowedIss/allowedSub/allowedJti/allowedNonce matchers were built by ensureStringClaimMatcher, which returned a caller-supplied RegExp unchanged - so a stateful RegExp (/g or /y) keeps lastIndex between calls and makes validation non-deterministic (roughly half of valid tokens rejected depending on call order). causal_research.bug_semantics: Access-rule authorization compared raw virtual paths as case-sensitive, slash-separated strings, while the host filesystem resolved equivalent names using its own case and separator semantics. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant of a denied path therefore missed the rule but reached the same file; on Windows, backslashes and traversal components likewise missed slash-based rules but were normalized by the filesystem. An authenticated user could consequently read or, subject to ordinary permissions, mutate an administrator-denied file while remaining inside the user's filesystem scope.

causal_research.bug_semantics: univ.Real stores ASN.1 REAL as (mantissa, base, exponent). Real.__float__ computed float(mantissa * pow(base, exponent)) with exact big-integer exponentiation. prettyPrint, str, comparisons, arithmetic, and int() all funnel through float(self). A compact BER/CER/DER REAL (or Real((m, b, e)) constructed directly) can encode a huge exponent; pow() then tries to materialize an enormous integer and the process hangs (CWE-400). Decoding itself only builds the tuple; the DoS fires on conversion. The 2011 RealDecoder left binary REAL as pass; binary encoding/decoding landed later (ae6f36fe, 2011-03-15 parent of the inf wrap) and still produced unbounded exponents that the same __float__ consumed. Fix in 0.6.4: base-2 via math.ldexp, base-10 overflow-checked against sys.float_info.max_10_exp so out-of-range values raise OverflowError and prettyPrint stays '<overflow>' without huge intermediates.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire vector-store converters serialize a caller-supplied Filter.Key into a Lucene-style query string. Their escaping left tab, LF, CR, and U+3000 ideographic space unescaped, so a key can introduce token boundaries and operators such as OR; the resulting string is passed to the backend query parser, allowing an attacker to replace the intended metadata predicate with arbitrary query clauses.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627 first added an affected backend and the causal pattern: ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.doKey() appended the metadata-prefixed Filter.Key directly to the query string with only trim(), while ElasticsearchVectorStore supplied that converted string to Elasticsearch queryString(). OpenSearch later copied the affected converter in 46e47849cec4b8a6fffbd13997f3cce4f886347b, and GemFire added the same kind of filter-query path in 833a856f51090f0eb98332db2341ce7a107af1fd. Later shared-converter refactors and partial escaping changed the location and reduced the character set but did not create the vulnerability or close the whitespace bypass.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627 shows human author Jemin Huh <hjm1980@gmail.com> and human committer Christian Tzolov <ctzolov@vmware.com>; the commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
causal_research.evidence: First-party advisory https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47835 states that special characters could force arbitrary queries in Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and GemFire VectorDB and identifies affected Spring AI 1.0.0-1.0.8 and 1.1.0-1.1.7, fixed in 1.0.9 and 1.1.8; GHSA references direct commits https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/commit/2b20cfc8f478444f942d4be7a867d254441ff991 and https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/commit/9787991aa1ed92c511131ddf4e142bd94051e6e7. In the validated full-history clone, git log -L 86,95:vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.java 9334d7d... resolves the raw doKey implementation to the new-file commit 9334d7d540f8d0ee7cb09e44b272c95c2c159627; git log -S 'context.append(prefixedIdentifier.trim()).append(":");' confirms 9334d7d... added that statement and later fc1f92d11cacc79bdf8d41eb7f941a64fdf67482 only moved/refactored it. The BIC also added vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchVectorStore.java, whose getElasticsearchSimilarityQuery() sends getElasticsearchQueryString(filterExpression) into queryString(...). Direct parent-tree check `git cat-file -e 8e50802eb8dd9044c15d7e75ad94ae618dca5c12:vector-stores/spring-ai-elasticsearch-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/ElasticsearchAiSearchFilterExpressionConverter.java` fails because the path is absent, while the BIC adds it from /dev/null. GitHub's commit-to-pulls API returns [] for 9334d7d..., and the one-parent commit object contains the actual feature diff, so there is no squash member history to substitute. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeds from 9334d7d... to v1.0.0 (fcd2803f36f35939c20ed152c9c1b0863fa35dcf), v1.1.0 (fa4c61eabeba0a69147b3c00a3b50380c1f25a75), and both fixes. At v1.0.8, AbstractFilterExpressionConverter.emitLuceneString() escapes ordinary space and Lucene punctuation but not tab/LF/CR/U+3000, and Elasticsearch doKey() routes the metadata field path through that helper. Direct fix 2b20cfc8f478444f942d4be7a867d254441ff991 adds cases for '\t', '\n', '\r', and '\u3000' plus regression tests for all three stores; its equivalent 1.0.x backport is 9787991aa1ed92c511131ddf4e142bd94051e6e7. `git tag --contains` maps 2b20cfc... to v1.1.8 and 9787991... to v1.0.9; ancestry checks place neither fix in v1.1.7/v1.0.8 respectively, and place each in its patched tag.
causal_research.reasoning: The security boundary is the construction of a backend query string, not merely the later helper method. The smallest affected-history commit that first made attacker-controlled metadata keys reach such a sink is 9334d7d..., which simultaneously introduced the Elasticsearch converter's unescaped doKey() and the queryString sink. The earlier similar Azure converter is not the BIC for this advisory because it enforces an allowedIdentifierNames whitelist and is not one of the affected products; 9334d7d... removed that safety in the newly affected backend. OpenSearch and GemFire are later ports of the same causal design. Refactors in 2026 centralized escaping and a partial hardening added ordinary-space handling, but the vulnerable capability already existed and the last vulnerable tags still failed to escape alternate whitespace. Both supported release lines then received the same four-character escaping patch at the documented fixed boundaries. The immediate parent lacks the affected converter and sink, the BIC predates both affected version lines, and the BIC commit object has no AI attribution signal; therefore the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can POST to django.views.i18n.set_language() (not installed in URLconf by default) sends many distinct, very long language parameter values. Each value is passed unchanged to django.utils.translation.check_for_language(). Before the 2026 fix that function was decorated with functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1000), so the raw lang_code is retained as a cache key before language_code_re or any length check runs. Up to 1000 oversized keys stay in process memory, causing a bounded denial of service (DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, default 2.5 MB, caps each request). The 2026 fix rejects codes longer than LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH (500) in an uncached wrapper and only then calls translation_catalog_exists().

causal_research.flaw_origin: The retained-key mechanism was first written in 26e3e7ecb5e4c9af4cd5aa178f65ce1585d3ae07 (2013-05-19), which wrapped check_for_language with memoize(_checked_languages, 1). The immediate parent 4ad1eb1c14b629cf5bcfd253ed40e875f1bddd47 performed catalog lookups without storing lang_code. Later lru_cache refactors (9b7455e9, 2bab9d6d, f356b6ecc3f, 3cc5f01d9bd) kept caching the raw argument; CVE-2024-39614 added a 500-character limit only on get_supported_language_variant(), leaving the set_language -> check_for_language path ungated until 27137e655e442e81095f1f8f77ff3870d9fdf169.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 26e3e7ecb5 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked the sibling request paths, which are already bounded: get_supported_language_variant() rejects codes over LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH (:513), parse_accept_language_header() truncates at the same limit (:646,:652), and the cookie branch of get_language_from_request() requires membership in get_languages() (:583). Measured the pre-fix language_code_re guard locally on 2.5 MB adversarial values: worst case 113 ms for an unmatched input and ~0 ms for simple runs, so the regex cost is linear and only cache retention carries the impact; a well-formed over-long code passes the regex and costs one failing gettext find() per locale path before being cached. The 2025-07-22 django-bot docstring rewrap (69a93a88ed) touches neighbouring text with no behaviour change, so it is not a causal or attribution source. Upstream's release note confirms the memory is bounded by request size and cache size, which matches a low-severity bounded effect rather than unbounded growth.
mechanism.impact: Per-process memory growth: up to 1000 distinct over-length codes retained simultaneously per process (up to the request-size limit each), degrading availability on deployments that route the view; upstream rates the issue low severity (CWE-789).
mechanism.preconditions: The set_language view must be routed (django/conf/urls/i18n.py urlpatterns is not part of the default URLconf), and the attacker must be able to issue many POSTs with distinct over-length `language` values. The cache is per process and capped at 1000 entries and request bodies are capped by DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, which is what bounds the total impact.
mechanism.summary: A POST to django.views.i18n.set_language() with an over-long `language` value reaches check_for_language(lang_code) in django/utils/translation/trans_real.py, whose functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1000) stores every distinct argument as a key; many distinct, very long codes are retained as cache keys and consume process memory.
mechanism.trigger: Repeated POSTs to a routed set_language view with distinct `language` values longer than 500 characters (each up to DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE, 2,621,440 bytes), so that distinct over-length strings fill the language-code cache.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:465-478 function check_for_language (parent 27137e655e^): decorator '@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1000)' at :465, unguarded length at :477; entered from django/views/i18n.py:59.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real, published Django DoS: set_language POST language values were retained as check_for_language lru_cache keys. The smallest first-writer of that retained-key mechanism is the 2013 memoize wrap by named human Łukasz Langa; the immediate parent tree has no such cache; later lru_cache commits are refactors. The 2026 Natalia Bidart commit and branch backports are the minimum fix and also lack commit-object AI markers. BIC-only attribution is therefore named-human with ABSENT AI markers, which is NOT_AI.
The defect is a bounded memory-retention denial of service: every distinct language code passed to check_for_language() is stored as an lru_cache(maxsize=1000) key, so an attacker who can POST many distinct over-length `language` values to the set_language view grows process memory up to the cache bound. The first change in the tree that retains these values is 26e3e7ecb5 (2013-05-19), which added `_checked_languages = {}` and `check_for_language = memoize(check_for_language, _checked_languages, 1)`; its immediate parent computes and discards each code. Every later commit in the chain only swaps or resizes the same cache (9b7455e918, 2bab9d6d9e, f356b6ecc3) and is therefore not an introduction. The BIC commit object carries a named human author and committer (Łukasz Langa <lukasz@langa.pl>), no trailers and no bot identity, with hand-written ticket content, and it landed in 2013, years before generative code assistants existed. The fix 27137e655e rejects codes longer than LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH before the cached lookup, which covers all callers, and was backported to 5.2.17, 6.0.8 and 6.1.x. Nothing in the BIC or fix objects shows machine-generated or AI-marked authorship, so this case is not AI-caused.
causal_research.remaining_gap: Out-of-support series named in the advisory (5.1.x, 5.0.x, 4.2.x) were not evaluated upstream and carry no fix, so they may still be exposed; maintained series 5.2.x, 6.0.x and 6.1.x are closed by 27137e655e and its backports. No closing commit exists or is expected for the EOL series.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With escapeParameter/escapeParameterHtml enabled, Vue I18n escaped only interpolation values before inserting them into a translation template. When a trusted translation contains an HTML attribute and the translated result is rendered as HTML, an attacker-controlled parameter can still participate in an executable attribute context (including onerror or javascript: URL contexts); the option therefore did not provide the advertised DOM-XSS protection for the completed HTML string.
evidence: Assigned bundle identifies GHSA-x8qp-wqqm-57ph / CVE-2025-53892, affected vue-i18n and @intlify packages, vulnerable ranges >=9.0.0 <9.14.5, >=10.0.0 <10.0.8, and >=11.0.0 <11.1.10, and first patched versions 9.14.5, 10.0.8, and 11.1.10.

CVE.org API record CVE-2025-53892 is PUBLISHED, names the same escapeParameterHtml DOM-XSS through tag attributes, confirms the vendor repository advisory, and references PRs #2229/#2230, commits 49f982443ab8fd94ecc427b265ce97d57df94d7e and a47099619fb9b256e86341a8658ebe72e92ab099, and releases v9.14.5, v10.0.8, and v11.1.10.

git show 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef -- src/core/translate.ts src/utils.ts shows the first addition of escapeParameter, escapeParams(options), and escapeHtml; escapeParams transforms only list/named interpolation values before resolveMessageFormat, while translate returns the completed message without final-context sanitization.

git log -S'escapeParams(options)' -- src/core/translate.ts identifies 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef (2020-10-07, 'feat: escap html parameter options (#139)') as the first writer; later commits 22d57666e60e84a6c277cb24ac3c08f4e100d390 and 9ed153596c714f8542c1f8886b7034f361ab73bb are package-structure moves and are not BICs.

git rev-list --parents -n 1 gives immediate parent 34a31a83f6a712327774db2a7badda9866926c1a; git grep for escapeParameterHtml, escapeParameter, and escapeParams in that parent tree returns no match, directly proving parent absence.

git show -s --format=fuller plus the raw BIC message shows human author kazuya kawaguchi, GitHub committer, and no AI/co-author/generated trailer; no reconstructable PR-member ref for #139 exists in the validated local full-history clone, so 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef is the smallest surviving public first-write object.
merge-base ancestry checks show the BIC is contained in v9.0.0 and in affected-boundary tags v9.14.4, v10.0.7, and v11.1.9.

The branch-equivalent direct fixes 4aad98ee8c0e3de93c2b7de99fc5c745623cb1c4 (v11), 49f982443ab8fd94ecc427b265ce97d57df94d7e (v10), and a47099619fb9b256e86341a8658ebe72e92ab099 (v9) add sanitizeTranslatedHtml to the completed translation result and neutralize event-handler attributes and javascript: URLs; each immediate parent lacks sanitizeTranslatedHtml.

Tag containment and tree checks map 4aad98ee8c0e3de93c2b7de99fc5c745623cb1c4 to v11.1.10, 49f982443ab8fd94ecc427b265ce97d57df94d7e to v10.0.8, and a47099619fb9b256e86341a8658ebe72e92ab099 to v9.14.5; v11.1.9, v10.0.7, and v9.14.4 lack sanitizeTranslatedHtml, while each corresponding first-patched tag contains it.
causal_research.flaw_origin: PR #139 member 69489802dea27889ce323a8dd528a8d9da4aa0db first wrote the escapeParameter feature by applying escapeHtml only to list/named values before message interpolation and returning the completed translated string without sanitizing HTML attribute contexts. GitHub squash-merge 154076727da3aa1c3b5f70abd46c5d5a9c3a35ef landed the identical tree on master. That incomplete security design is the vulnerable mechanism later corrected by sanitizing the final translated HTML.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is real and follows a closed source-to-sink lifecycle: attacker-controlled interpolation values flow through escapeParams/escapeHtml into a trusted translation's HTML attribute and then to an HTML-rendering sink, but the original option never sanitizes the resulting attribute context. causal_research.bug_semantics: On a server-capable NextChat deployment, app/mcp/actions.ts is a Next.js Server Action module because it begins with "use server". An unauthenticated caller can therefore supply an MCP configuration containing an arbitrary command, args, and env, persist it, and cause initialization to pass it to StdioClientTransport and client.connect(), spawning the process. The first form required invoking exported updateMcpConfig and then exported restartAllClients; the advisory-named later form, exported addMcpServer(clientId, config), performs persistence and initialization in one request. Neither form enforces authentication, authorization, ENABLE_MCP, or a command allowlist.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 (feat: MCP market) is the smallest real BIC. It first replaced repository-owned static MCP configuration with writable configuration and added the exported Server Actions updateMcpConfig(config) and restartAllClients(), connecting caller-controlled ServerConfig data to the pre-existing StdioClientTransport process-spawn sink. Its direct parent 0c14ce6417821d512d04dec5a5755bf35deed51d has only a static mcp_config.json import and no caller-controlled write/restart route. Commit 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 is a later consolidation that makes the same flaw one-request through addMcpServer; it is not the origin.

Re-running the disputed checks supports the reviewer. The bundled GHSA-2jqp-6hx7-phh8/CVE-2026-7644 identifies addMcpServer in app/mcp/actions.ts, says versions through 2.16.1 are affected, and supplies no patched-version boundary. `git log --all -S'export async function updateMcpConfig' -- app/mcp/actions.ts` reaches 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8 before the later 8aa9a500fdee762abe5fd8e0bba00065be1725f4 rewrite, while `git log --all -S'export async function restartAllClients' -- app/mcp/actions.ts` also starts at 7d51bfd42e0f60a328abed353ab1ef717b6f3ba8. The process sink predates the BIC: parent app/mcp/client.ts passes serverConfig.command, args, and env to StdioClientTransport and connects it. Direct-parent `git grep -n -e updateMcpConfig -e restartAllClients -e reinitializeMcpClients -e addMcpServer 0c14ce6417821d512d04dec5a5755bf35deed51d -- app` returns no matches, and the parent action code imports repository-owned mcp_config.json, proving the attacker-controlled source-to-spawn route is absent. causal_research.bug_semantics: A project-scoped owner member or lessee administrator who may PATCH a volume target but is not permitted by baremetal:volume:view_target_properties can change an unrelated allowed field and receive the complete updated target in the HTTP 200 response. PATCH authorizes baremetal:volume:update, loads and updates the existing target, and serializes new_target without applying the target-properties redaction used by GET/list, thereby disclosing pre-existing iSCSI connection data or credentials. POST had the same unredacted response shape, but its caller supplied the returned values; the advisory's confidentiality escalation is the PATCH disclosure of existing secrets.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The original volume-target REST API commit c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d created an admin-only PATCH response that returned the complete target, so it is the latent response-shape origin, not the security BIC. Commit 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 later rewrote the representation to plain JSON without changing that behavior. The vulnerability first became real in e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9: that commit expanded baremetal:volume:update from system-only access to system/project owner-member and lessee-admin access, introduced a stricter baremetal:volume:view_target_properties boundary, enforced the new boundary on GET/list, and left PATCH returning the full target without the new check. causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: the LFS upload API builds the blob-store path from the client-controlled oid query parameter with no validation or sanitization. Commit 0a573a56 added app/api/controller/lfs/upload.go whose Upload() handler does objPath = getLFSObjectPath(pointer.OId) and passes it straight to blobStore.Upload; getLFSObjectPath (app/api/controller/lfs/controller.go) is fmt.Sprintf(lfsObjectsPathFormat, oid) with lfsObjectsPathFormat = 'lfs/%s' (controller.go:35). The route (app/router/git.go, GitLFSHandler) binds PUT /info/lfs-objects to HandleLFSUpload, which reads the oid via request.GetObjectIDFromQuery -> QueryParamOrError with no format or path checks; the controller also only checks repo push permission (getRepoCheckAccess), so any authenticated user with push access can supply an oid containing ../ to escape the lfs/ prefix and write arbitrary files via blobStore.Upload (arbitrary file write, CWE-22/CWE-73, CVSS 8.8 PR:L). BIC/parent comparison: immediate parent 6da9821b lacks app/api/controller/lfs/upload.go entirely; the BIC added upload.go plus the LFS controller/handler/router/store wiring, including the unvalidated path construction, so the BIC is the original introduction. History checks: no lfs-related files exist in the parent lineage; git log -S getLFSObjectPath over 6da9821b..21c5ce42 shows no intermediate introduction or change; and v3.2.0 tag (2025-05-22) contains the BIC, proving the defect shipped in a public release before the 3.3.0 fix. Minimal fix: commit 21c5ce42 (2025-08-08, PR #4235 per subject, squash) touches only app/api/controller/lfs/upload.go and (a) rejects upload when lfsStore.Find shows the OID already exists, (b) hashes the limited upload body with SHA-256 and requires hex(sha256(content)) == strings.TrimPrefix(pointer.OId, 'sha256:') before calling getLFSObjectPath, and (c) improves a duplicate error message; since any successful upload now requires the OID to equal the content hash, the path component is confined to hex characters and traversal/absolute-path injection is closed; this is the only change to the vulnerable function, so it is the minimum repair. causal_research.bug_semantics: A pipeline that includes HAProxyMessageDecoder (opt-in codec-haproxy handler) accepts attacker-controlled bytes. After 13 readable bytes, findVersion matches the 12-byte PROXY v2 BINARY_PREFIX (0D 0A 0D 0A 00 0D 0A 51 55 49 54 0A) and reads the 13th byte with ByteBuf.getByte, which sign-extends. Byte 0xFF becomes int -1. decode() uses field version=-1 as the need-more-data sentinel, so (version=findVersion(in))==-1 returns without advancing readerIndex and without constructing HeaderExtractor. ByteToMessageDecoder therefore retains the readable cumulation and appends every subsequent chunk. Header size limits never apply, so direct-memory exhaustion is reachable over the network with no privileges. After getUnsignedByte, 0xFF is 255; the v2 path frames/rejects under v2MaxHeaderSize and decodeHeader throws HAProxyProtocolException.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An adjacent-network attacker could send a crafted mDNS response whose TXT, HINFO, A, or AAAA payload length exceeded the bytes actually available or whose decoded payload did not consume exactly the record's declared RDLENGTH. Python byte slicing silently returned a short payload while DNSIncoming advanced its offset by the attacker-declared length; _read_others appended the resulting record before a later parse error, answers() returned the already-appended prefix, and RecordManager then inserted those records into DNSCache for ServiceInfo consumers.
evidence: The published CVE.org record at https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-48487 states that versions before 0.149.16 are affected, describes attacker-declared RDLENGTH advancing _read_character_string/_read_string past _data_len and contaminating DNSCache/ServiceInfo, and identifies 544449596e645fcaad3834fa0cb614a54f847a82 and release 0.149.16 as the fix.

Direct parent-tree verification with git show 488de8826ddd58646358900d057a4a1632492948:Zeroconf.py shows lines 511-517 using struct.unpack(format, self.data[self.offset:self.offset+length]); a short slice cannot satisfy the declared struct width and therefore raises before returning or appending a truncated record.

git show ac081cf00addde1ceea2c076f73905fdb293de3a -- src/zeroconf/_protocol/incoming.py shows _read_character_string changed from calling the already-vulnerable _read_string(length) to an equivalent direct slice and offset increment, so this later optimization preserved rather than introduced the flaw.

At fix parent 28bb01f23951f7883d8c3af66b6d537c34c516c7, src/zeroconf/_protocol/incoming.py lines 253-265 slice without checking _data_len, lines 283-301 append rec without requiring self.offset == end, and answers() lines 188-200 catches a later decode exception and returns the accumulated _answers.

At the same vulnerable tree, src/zeroconf/_handlers/record_manager.py lines 77-91 obtains msg.answers(), lines 117-125 accepts unexpired records, and lines 154-158 calls cache.async_add_records; src/zeroconf/_services/info.py lines 430-441 parses cached TXT bytes into properties.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated proxy client can put an arbitrary HTTP(S) origin in x-headroom-base-url. Headroom uses that origin as the upstream without establishing that its resolved addresses are public, forwards the incoming request headers and body to it, and returns the upstream response. A caller can therefore reach loopback, link-local/cloud-metadata, RFC 1918, and other internal services through the proxy and read their responses; the incoming Authorization header also follows the caller-selected destination. The reference compose deployment amplified reachability by publishing the proxy on 0.0.0.0 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN.

causal_research.bug_semantics: withCredentials (BindingStep) binds credential plaintext into the Pipeline body environment. ConsoleLogFilter/MaskingOutputStream redacts those values on the build console stream, but Pipeline failures persist the Throwable on flow ErrorAction and print it with Functions.printThrowable, which does not pass through ConsoleLogFilter. A body that interpolates a bound secret into error()/Exception (or any nested/suppressed cause) therefore writes the secret to the build log and stores it unmasked on the run. Attackers with permission to read that log (Jenkins advisory CVSS PR:L) recover the credential. The 2025 fix installs a FailureHandler that, when the printed throwable matches the secret pattern, rethrows MaskedException copies whose messages have secrets replaced with asterisks, including cause and suppressed chains.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PickleScan classified a pickle only from GLOBAL/INST/STACK_GLOBAL module-and-name references found in its opcode stream. A malicious pickle could import the unblocked pkgutil.resolve_name, call it by REDUCE with data such as 'os:system' to obtain a blocked callable without importing that callable, then invoke the returned callable with a second REDUCE. causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated HTTP client of ActiveMQ Classic's Jolokia JMX-HTTP bridge (POST /api/jolokia/, often admin:admin) can invoke exec on BrokerViewMBean.addNetworkConnector(String) or addConnector(String) because the shipped jolokia-access.xml allows operation=* on org.apache.activemq:*. Those JMX methods pass the attacker-controlled discovery URI straight into BrokerService with no scheme checks. A URI such as static:(vm://rce?brokerConfig=xbean:http://attacker/payload.xml) is parsed as a discovery/composite network connector whose component is the in-JVM vm transport. VMTransportFactory, when the named broker does not exist, reads brokerConfig and treats it as a broker factory URL; the xbean: scheme loads that URL with Spring ResourceXmlApplicationContext, which instantiates all singleton beans (ProcessBuilder.start / Runtime.exec / MethodInvokingFactoryBean) before BrokerService validates the resulting configuration. The result is RCE in the broker JVM. Native JMX would hit the same unvalidated BrokerView methods; Jolokia is the documented HTTP source.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-426/CWE-427 untrusted search path: two NLTK Graphviz helpers executed the `dot` program by bare name (`subprocess.Popen`/`subprocess.run` argv starting with `"dot"`), so the OS resolved the binary via PATH and, on Windows, the current working directory. An attacker who can plant a file named `dot` in CWD or a relative/writable PATH entry gets that binary executed instead of Graphviz (arbitrary code execution). At <=3.10.2, `nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img` called `find_binary("dot")` but discarded the returned absolute path and still ran `["dot", ...]`; `nltk.translate.api.AlignedSent._repr_svg_` ran the bare name with no validation. `DependencyGraph._repr_svg_` had been refactored to call `dot2img`, so it inherited the same sink. The 3.10.3 fix runs the absolute path `find_binary` already returns (it refuses a CWD-relative match for a bare tool name).

causal_research.bug_semantics: With RBAC enabled, check_rbac() matched role-restricted paths against the raw, percent-encoded ngx.var.request_uri using ngx.re.find(). causal_research.bug_semantics: phpseclib 3 parses untrusted ASN.1 (X.509 certificates, PKCS#8 EC keys, etc.) that may carry explicit specifiedCurve parameters over a characteristic-two field. Common.php copies the attacker-controlled INTEGER m (field degree) into BinaryCurve::setModulo, which constructs Math\BinaryField without bounding m. BinaryField::__construct then does str_repeat('0', $m) (unbounded allocation) and builds a reduction closure whose loop bound is 2*m-2. A huge m therefore causes memory exhaustion and/or excessive iteration (CWE-400/CWE-834) during key/certificate load, including when point decompression runs F2^m arithmetic. The 3.0.34 fix rejects degrees larger than 571 (largest SECG binary curves sect571r1/k1) before those operations.
