causal_research.bug_semantics: The PATCH /api/customers/:id endpoint is reachable without an authenticated admin or customer session and trusts the attacker-controlled path UUID as the record to update. Its only route-local middleware parses JSON; the handler selects that UUID, spreads attacker-controlled fields (including email and password) into the customer update, and returns the updated record without checking that the caller owns the customer, enabling unauthenticated account takeover and lockout.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 first made the predeclared /customers/:id route operational by adding updateCustomer.js and body-parser middleware while simultaneously adding the global API auth middleware whose explicit rule treated every route with no access property as public. The route then had no access property, so the new mutating handler was unauthenticated from its first executable revision. Commit 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b later changed the default to private but explicitly labeled this route public, preserving rather than originating the flaw.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 names author and committer The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>, has the single message 'RESTful api implementation', has no trailers (including Co-Authored-By or Generated-with), and neither commit-object identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/evershopcommerce/evershop/issues/952 documents unauthenticated PATCH /api/customers/:id account takeover, identifies route.json, the body-parser-only middleware, and updateCustomer.js, and records the maintainer's statement that it was fixed in v2.2.1. The GitHub advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m3qj-pp48-6w2p describes the same mechanism and states that v2.2.1 changes access to private.

git diff 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 -- packages/evershop/src/modules/customer/api/updateCustomer shows a2f514... adding [context]bodyParser[auth].js, payloadSchema.json, and updateCustomer.js. The new handler selects and updates customer where uuid equals request.params.id, spreads request.body into the update, and performs no authentication or ownership check.

The same a2f514... diff adds packages/evershop/src/modules/auth/api/global/[jwtTokenVerify]auth.js with the comment 'Missing access property means public' and the condition !currentRoute?.access || currentRoute?.access === 'public', which calls next(). At that revision route.json contains only PATCH and /customers/:id, so the newly operational mutation endpoint bypasses auth.

Immediate-parent tree verification against 4e518e617b76928656936e0048da852229acf24e: git ls-tree shows only updateCustomer/route.json; git cat-file -e for updateCustomer/updateCustomer.js and auth/api/global/[jwtTokenVerify]auth.js both fail because neither path exists. The parent route has no access property. Thus the executable unauthenticated update mechanism is absent from the immediate parent.

git log -S"where('uuid', '=', request.params.id)" -- updateCustomer.js resolves the vulnerable UUID-based update code to a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095. git log -S'"access": "public"' -- route.json resolves the later explicit public label to 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b and its removal to f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9. git log -L on the route confirms that sequence.

git show 4b97829de4acc674cd2282af3d2b61ec3416f72b shows a coordinated access-model change: the global auth rule changes from missing-is-public to only explicit-public, while updateCustomer/route.json gains access public. Because the endpoint was already public by omission, this commit preserves the vulnerable behavior and is not the smallest BIC.

At tag v2.1.2, route.json still says access public; [getCurrentUser]auth.ts calls next() for public routes; the only route-local middleware parses JSON; and updateCustomer.js hashes an attacker-supplied password, updates the UUID from request.params.id, and returns the updated customer. This directly matches the published attack path.

Fix commit f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9 changes only updateCustomer/route.json from access public to access private. Its parent 8861498694b46f944767c49cc03180a96b38aac3 contains public, while tag v2.2.1 contains private.

Version ancestry checks: a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 is an ancestor of the repository's earliest available release tag 1.0.0-rc.9 and all later tags through v2.1.2; f92b832255102af8db796245db01e38ea70504e9 is not an ancestor of v2.1.2 and is an ancestor of v2.2.1. git tag --contains f92b832... returns only v2.2.1, establishing the observed vulnerable/patched boundary despite the advisory listing package ranges as unknown.

git cat-file -p a2f514ad10073fb9ae164446f30205086151c095 shows one parent, human author/committer The Nguyen, the plain subject 'RESTful api implementation', and no commit-message trailers or AI/bot marker. No squash/member history is exposed by the commit object; it is treated as the smallest available public-history commit, not decomposed.
causal_research.reasoning: The advisory's explicit public line is not by itself the first causal point. The route JSON was created earlier in 4e518e6..., but that parent had no update handler and therefore lacked the dangerous mutation. Commit a2f514... added both the unauthenticated-by-default global auth behavior and the UUID-directed customer update handler, creating the complete exploit path in one smallest reachable commit. Its parent directly lacks both new code paths. The later 4b9782... access refactor merely translated the already-public omission into an explicit public declaration, so selecting it would mistake a preservation refactor for the BIC. Subsequent refactors, database migration, password hashing, and formatting retained the same missing-authorization mechanism through v2.1.2. The one-line direct fix f92b832... makes the route private and is included in v2.2.1 but not v2.1.2. Finally, BIC-only commit-object inspection provides no AI authorship or co-authorship signal, so the supported closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: bgp_flowspec_op_decode() in bgpd/bgp_flowspec_util.c walks a chained FlowSpec numeric-operator NLRI and, on BGP_FLOWSPEC_CONVERT_TO_NON_OPAQUE, writes each decoded operator into a caller-supplied struct bgp_pbr_match_val array sized BGP_PBR_MATCH_VAL_MAX (5) via mval++. The loop guard was `if (loop > BGP_PBR_MATCH_VAL_MAX) *error = -2` and the write path only skipped when *error == -2, so loop==5 still wrote mval[5] — one element past the end. A crafted FlowSpec component with more than five chained operators therefore caused a CWE-787 off-by-one out-of-bounds write (DoS). bgp_flowspec_bitmask_decode() used the same `>` comparison against the same 5-slot arrays.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-37457 state=PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected); CNA description matches bgp_flowspec_op_decode() OOB write via crafted FlowSpec; GHSA-q7jj-qhhg-6m9g withdrawn_at=null; Red Hat CSAF/VEX rates CWE-787 Important and ships RHSA-2026:24340/24347/24370/24371.

Merged as 3063564fed00da64fc7679ecdfcac9d7679e8c06 (PR #21054).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mojolicious signs session cookies with HMAC over the cookie name/value using app->secrets->[0] as the key. From 0.999922 the default key was a hard-coded string ('MojoliciousRocks1234!', later 'You really should change this!'), then the application class name, then the decamelized moniker. Those defaults are public and stable per app class, so an attacker can compute a valid HMAC and forge or hijack sessions without stealing a real secret. Padding (mojo#1791 / v9.19) and optional CryptX encrypted cookies (v9.39) do not replace the default key. hashcat mode 16501 (PR 4090) is a public cracker for the padded HMAC-SHA256 cookie format, cited by the CNA as an exploit, not a hashcat vulnerability.

potential_fix.approach: Stop using the moniker or any other application-derived/hard-coded string as the default HMAC key. Generate a CSPRNG secret at first use (mojo#2200) and/or refuse to set signed/encrypted cookies or session data while secrets->[0] equals the moniker unless an explicit override is set (mojo#2252). Document that existing deployments must rotate to a unique >=128-bit secret.
potential_fix.rationale: HMAC security is entirely in the key. A log warning does not prevent production apps from shipping the guessable default, which is what CPANSec, Synacktiv, and hashcat 16501 exploit. Padding and optional CryptX encryption leave the default key in place.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated stored XSS on invoice/bill detail timelines. An authenticated user stores HTML/JavaScript in their profile name (PATCH profile/{user}; User request only validates name as required|string; UpdateUser persists raw input). When that user creates or cancels a document, Create.php/Restore.php copy owner->name into $user_name and the Blade views interpolate it unescaped into trans('documents.slider.create'|cancel) replacements such as ':user created this :type on :date'. The date field is already a trusted HTML <span>, so the composed description is passed with {!! trans(...) !!} into x-show.accordion.head, which emits {!! $description !!}. Laravel trans() does not HTML-escape replacements, so another viewer of the document executes the stored name as HTML/JS.

causal_research.bug_semantics: cqlsh records every executed statement in a local readline history file and never redacts secrets. Commands such as LOGIN <user> '<password>', CREATE/ALTER USER|ROLE ... WITH PASSWORD, and other password-bearing CQL therefore persist in cleartext in ~/.cassandra/cqlsh_history (migrated from ~/.cqlsh_history). Anyone with local read access to that file recovers prior-session credentials. CVE.org and Apache (CASSANDRA-21180 / oss-security) treat this as a real CWE-532 leak in Cassandra 4.0.0–4.0.19, not a withdrawn or rejected record. The 4.0.20 vendor patch does not strip passwords from history; it adds --disable-history / cqlshrc [history] disabled=true, skips readline.write_history_file when disabled, and prints a warning that history may contain passwords.

causal_research.bug_semantics: IPIPANCorpusReader metadata APIs (channels, domains, categories, and fileids filtered by those fields) all funnel through _get_tag(). Helpers derive a header path by calling str.replace('morph.xml','header.xml') on FileSystemPathPointer values from abspath/abspaths(). Because FileSystemPathPointer is a str subclass, replace() returns a bare string and drops the PathPointer wrapper, so _get_tag opens the path with builtin open() and never hits PathPointer.open() or nltk.pathsec. After 3.10.0, join() blocks literal '..' fileids and PathPointer.open() is sandboxed, but an in-root symlink whose name has no separators still passes join() and is followed by open(), disclosing arbitrary files the process can read. That is CWE-22/CWE-59 symlink escape of the pathsec sandbox, not a '../' traversal regression.

causal_research.bug_semantics: llama-server use-after-free of ctx_server.vocab on six HTTP tokenization-family endpoints (/tokenize, /detokenize, /infill, /apply-template, /rerank, /anthropic/count_tokens) when --sleep-idle-seconds is enabled. Those handlers construct server_res_generator, which calls wait_until_no_sleep() and then drops mutex_tasks; they then tokenize or otherwise dereference ctx_server.vocab on the HTTP worker thread, bypassing the completion task queue. Concurrently the main loop can observe an empty queue, enter sleep, and run destroy() -> llama_init.reset(), which frees llama_model (and the embedded llama_vocab) without nulling the cached vocab pointer. The TOCTOU window after the awake check lets a worker finish using a dangling vocab pointer, causing crash or potential code execution via heap reclaim.

causal_research.bug_semantics: js_typed_array_constructor snapshots offset/len from an existing ArrayBuffer, then calls js_create_from_ctor, which does JS_GetProperty(new_target, prototype) and can run a getter. causal_research.bug_semantics: Kimai issues password-reset and admin login URLs via Symfony LoginLinkHandler. The firewall config at 2.57.0 (config/packages/security.yaml:73-77) sets signature_properties to only ['id'], so the HMAC does not include User::getPassword(). PasswordResetController::sendEmailAction (2.57.0 line 107) creates that link with lifetime getPasswordResetRetryLifetime() (default 3600s). After the victim uses the link, WizardController.php:105 clears the __pw_reset__ user preference, so a later consume of the same URL is a normal login. Symfony still allows max_uses: 3 on the same signed URL, and re-issuing a new link does not invalidate old ones. An interceptor of the original URL can therefore authenticate as the user after the password hash has changed. The same unsigned-to-password scheme is used by UserLoginLinkCommand.php:77. Preconditions: attacker obtains a still-unexpired link (email leak, logs, shared inbox, or the console command); the account is an internal user. Counterevidence: vendor rates this Low and notes mailbox compromise is outside Kimai; GitHub/CVE still treat it as a real CWE-640 defect, and the 2.58.0 regression test encodes the post-password-change reject.

causal_research.bug_semantics: For a window drawable, do_get_buffers allocated only count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots, filled count client-requested slots, and then used arithmetic attachment counters to decide whether to append implicit front buffers. With at least two DRI2BufferBackLeft requests and one DRI2BufferFrontLeft request, need_real_front remained positive even though FrontLeft was already present, so a redundant real-front pointer was appended at buffers[count]. The FrontLeft request also made need_fake_front positive, so the fake-front pointer was then written at buffers[count + 1], one pointer beyond the heap allocation. The DRI2GetBuffers and DRI2GetBuffersWithFormat request paths both called this helper, allowing a local X client to crash the server or potentially escalate privileges when it ran as root.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 replaced the parent's bulk CreateBuffers path with per-attachment allocation and introduced need_real_front++/-- alongside the existing fake-front accounting, while retaining an allocation sized for only one implicit attachment. The parent could append at most one fake front and therefore respected its count + 1 capacity; the new combination could append both a redundant real front and a fake front. Treating attachment presence as signed counts rather than boolean presence broke the allocation invariant.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When phpseclib validates an untrusted X.509 certificate, X509::validateSignature() (caonly=true by default) falls through to testForIntermediate() if the issuer is not already in the CA store. That helper reads the AIA caIssuers uniformResourceIdentifier straight from the certificate and fetchURL() does fsockopen() to the attacker-chosen host and port with no loopback/private/link-local/metadata or port restriction. causal_research.bug_semantics: In CRuby Nokogiri built with packaged libxml2 < 2.9.14, parsing or serializing an attacker-crafted multi-gigabyte XML document (sizes around or above INT_MAX) reaches libxml2 xmlBuf* (buf.c) and xmlBuffer* (tree.c) helpers. Those functions computed new buffer sizes with wrapping arithmetic (for example buf->use+len+2, buf->size*2) without SIZE_MAX/UINT_MAX checks, allocated an undersized buffer, then wrote past it. The result is out-of-bounds writes that can disclose unrelated memory, corrupt data, or crash. The sink is entirely in packaged libxml2; Nokogiri's exposure is shipping that library by default (and earlier in Windows native gems). JRuby and builds that link system libxml2 are out of scope per the vendor advisory.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A minimum-size X Render CreateAnimCursor request carries zero cursor elements. ProcRenderCreateAnimCursor accepts that size, computes ncursor as zero, allocates a zero-length cursors/deltas buffer, skips the population loop, and passes it to AnimCursorCreate. AnimCursorCreate assumes element zero exists and reads cursors[0] to copy foreground and background colors, producing an out-of-bounds read and potentially crashing the X server.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated request to /api/<unrecognized-provider>/<path> reaches the provider route's default branch, which invokes proxyHandler. proxyHandler constructs fetchUrl by concatenating the entirely client-controlled x-base-url header with the requested path and query string, performs fetch(fetchUrl, ...), and streams the upstream response back to the requester. Because neither the fallback nor proxyHandler restricts schemes, hosts, loopback/private/link-local addresses, redirects, or allowed plugin origins, a remote caller can make the server request internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary external hosts and read the response, producing SSRF/open-proxy behavior.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A Netty Redis pipeline that includes RedisArrayAggregator is reachable by any network peer speaking RESP. decode() treats ArrayHeaderRedisMessage(length>0) as the start of an aggregate: it pushes AggregateState onto the per-handler depths deque and returns without producing an outbound message. Subsequent non-header RedisMessages are ReferenceCountUtil.retain'd and appended to AggregateState.children; if children.size() < length the method returns while still holding those messages. FullBulkStringRedisMessage and similar holders wrap ByteBufs that are typically slices of PooledByteBufAllocator chunks. The original class defined no handlerRemoved, channelInactive, or exceptionCaught, so a close or handler removal before the array completes drops the only references without release. Chunks stay checked out of the process-wide direct pool. Repeating incomplete arrays plus disconnects monotonically exhausts that pool and causes allocation failures on unrelated channels. Preconditions: codec-redis on the pipeline and an incomplete RESP array at teardown. Counterevidence that this is not a decoder-length bug: RedisBulkStringAggregator uses MessageAggregator (which already releases on removal); this leak is specifically the hand-rolled array aggregator state.

mechanism.summary: A peer-controlled Redis pipeline that starts a RESP array aggregate and aborts before it completes leaves the retained child messages in RedisArrayAggregator's depths state with no release path, so the pooled direct-memory buffers behind them can never return to the JVM-wide PooledByteBufAllocator; repetition drains the shared pool and eventually fails allocations on every Netty channel in the process.
mechanism.trigger: Attacker opens a connection to a Netty endpoint that decodes untrusted RESP with RedisArrayAggregator, sends an array header with a positive length (for example *2 followed by CRLF) plus at least one complete element (for example $3, CRLF, foo, CRLF) so the first child message is retained and buffered, then closes the connection before the remaining elements arrive.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In non-export deployments, Next.js attaches Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to every /api/:path* response and, by v2.16.1, also advertises wildcard methods and request headers. An attacker-controlled web origin can therefore read non-credentialed API responses and send normally preflight-restricted headers. In the reported high-impact chain, cross-origin JavaScript supplies x-base-url to the unauthenticated fallback proxy; app/api/proxy.ts builds the server-side destination from that header and injects the configured OpenAI key whenever the supplied value contains api.openai.com, allowing cross-origin SSRF and reflected key disclosure. The invalid Allow-Credentials: true plus wildcard-origin combination does not make credentialed wildcard fetches work in modern browsers, but credentials are unnecessary for the exposed read/proxy path.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 50cd33dbb2992066dae8c51c2da6ef4781e4500a first created nextConfig.headers for non-export builds and applied Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (plus Allow-Credentials: true) to /:path*, thereby first granting every web origin read access across the application, including API routes. Its immediate parent had no response-header policy at all. Commit 0fb775d71a0fac5ce4aa802bc3eb0b066c12ed7b then scoped the rule to /api/:path* while widening Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers to * and adding a one-day max age, which intensified the later x-base-url attack but did not originate the permissive-origin flaw. Commit 6f83fbd21278c90cd978108abe54291c38ec10d7 only extracted the unchanged headers into CorsHeaders and is a move/refactor, not the BIC.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PHProxy's intended SSRF control for user-supplied proxy targets is a hostname-string regex blacklist ($_hosts, default '#^127\.|192\.168\.|10\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.|localhost#i') applied with preg_match against parse_url() host only. Unauthenticated callers supply the target via the configured URL parameter (url_var_name; '_proxurl' in v1.1.1 and HEAD). A hostname that does not literally match those prefixes (PoC: a public DNS name such as vul.aegisrisk.xyz bound to 127.0.0.1) is allowed, after which the proxy opens a server-side HTTP(S) connection to the resolved internal address. That bypasses the blacklist and reaches loopback/RFC1918 services (CWE-918). CVE-2025-52362 / GHSA-37c4-9pw5-3r33 (published, not withdrawn) affect v1.1.1 and prior.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2025-52362 state=PUBLISHED (datePublished 2025-07-21, not REJECTED/WITHDRAWN); GHSA-37c4-9pw5-3r33 withdrawn_at=null; CNA MITRE description matches _proxurl URL-processing SSRF in PHProxy 1.1.1 and prior.

potential_fix.approach: After parsing the target URL, resolve the host to all A/AAAA records, pin the outbound socket to those IPs, and reject the request if any address is loopback, RFC1918, link-local (including 169.254.169.254), CGNAT 100.64/10, RFC2544, IPv6 ::1/ULA/mapped, or other reserved ranges; re-validate after every redirect; restrict schemes to http/https. Apply the same resolved-IP check in the browser _proxurl flow and in ?api=fetch/portcheck/dns/cert.
potential_fix.rationale: The disclosed bypass is that a non-matching hostname can still resolve to a blocked address. Checking and pinning resolved IPs closes that hole; hostname-regex replication cannot.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user holding any one granular Theme Editor permission could enter Cms\Controllers\Index because the controller authorization was an OR gate, while AJAX code trusted the request-supplied template type without consistently checking the permission mapped to that type. The user could therefore reach pages, partials, layouts, content, or assets outside the granted scope. AssetList was also registered without requiring cms.manage_assets, and its upload path omitted the active-theme validation applied to other mutating asset handlers.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Single-parent commit 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 first added modules/cms/controllers/Index.php and modules/cms/widgets/AssetList.php while registering distinct cms.manage_* permissions. The new controller used a section-wide cms.* gate, unconditionally constructed every template widget, and dispatched request-controlled types without per-type authorization; the new AssetList upload processor lacked validateRequestTheme(). Its direct parent lacks both source paths and the granular permission-bearing implementation, so the vulnerable boundary first exists in this commit. The commit directly adds the affected files rather than moving them and has one parent with no public constituent commits to decompose.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The interactive OIDC/OAuth authorization-code flow generates a random CSRF `state`, includes it on the authorization request, then accepts the IdP callback's `code` without comparing the returned `state` to the session value. An attacker who can complete a parallel auth request and deliver that callback (MITM / CSRF of the localhost redirect) can cause sigstore-python to exchange the attacker's authorization code, so the user signs under an attacker-controlled identity. The missing check is in `Issuer.identity_token()` (`code = server.auth_response["code"][0]` with no `state` compare); `_OAuthSession` only stores and sends `state`.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A Dag author who can set a task instance's next_kwargs (task execution API) embeds a serde-encoded SyncCallback whose path field names an arbitrary module. The 3.3.0 scheduler awaiting_input timeout sweep always runs and resumes timed-out HITL tasks through handle_event_submit, which serde-deserializes next_kwargs in the scheduler process. SyncCallback is an airflow.* class, so it satisfies the default allowed_deserialization_classes allow-list. Callback.deserialize pops path and reconstructs via the constructor; get_callback_path then import_string()s that path, executing module-level code of whatever the stored string names. No non-default config is required. Pre-3.3.0 releases had the gadget but not this scheduler sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An administrator can store a webhook URL and cause Ech0 to POST to that URL with a default http.Client that never inspects DNS-resolved addresses. CreateWebhook only rejected empty names/URLs. A later validateWebhookURL (webhook_setting_service.go) tried to block private targets but used net.ParseIP on the hostname, so literals such as 10.0.0.1 were rejected while hostnames such as 169.254.169.254.nip.io returned nil and passed. TestWebhook and the dispatcher then resolved those hostnames and requested cloud-metadata and other internal endpoints; delivery status leaked reachability.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A locally supplied truncated pcap (wire length greater than captured length) processed by tcprewrite --fixlen pad reaches untrunc_packet, which reallocates the packet buffer and may free its old address. tcpedit_packet has already cached packet and IP-header aliases into that old allocation and does not rebase them after untrunc_packet returns; its later DLT merge path calls dlt_en10mb_l2len/get_l2len/get_l2len_protocol through the stale packet address, producing the reported heap use-after-free read (and other post-padding paths could likewise use stale header aliases).
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 changed untrunc_packet from padding the caller-provided buffer in place to safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len), and changed the API/caller to pass u_char **pktdata, but tcpedit_packet continued retaining its pre-call local packet, ip_hdr, and ip6_hdr aliases. In that original commit untrunc_packet did not even assign the new packet back through *pktdata; b58b23a52ffd23c3b1a2e2fe8b868aff0239560d later added *pktdata = packet but still did not rebase tcpedit_packet's cached aliases, so it did not cure the causal stale-pointer mechanism. The smallest first-writer is therefore 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14, not the later headroom adjustment 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 shows author and committer Fred Klassen <fklassen@appneta.com>, one parent, and only the message 'remalloc packets before padding to ensure not overwriting memory - closes #80'; there are no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI trailers/identities in the BIC commit object.
causal_research.evidence: First-party advisory issue https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/973 supplies the ASan chain: tcprewrite rewrite_packets -> tcpedit_packet -> untrunc_packet realloc -> tcpedit_dlt_merge_l3data -> dlt_en10mb_l2len -> get_l2len -> get_l2len_protocol, with the read at src/common/get.c:360 and the free at src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c:562 in 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a. The related maintainer-tracked instance https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/970 identifies the same untrunc_packet realloc root in the checksum path; maintainer fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da is titled 'Bug #970 tcprewrite: --fixlen: do not use realloc' and its changelog explicitly says '--fixlen use-after-free (#970)'. git log -L 575,575:src/tcpedit/edit_packet.c 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da^ and git log -S show that 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 first replaced in-place memset with packet = safe_realloc(packet, pkthdr->len); 64132c54c4000046b30f1fc3fe612db9b2f26860 only added PACKET_HEADROOM. Direct parent diff/tree verification against 16abc7fe749bd3c130204d0b2707caf7cab5894e shows untrunc_packet still accepted u_char *pktdata and performed only memset(pktdata + caplen, ...), with no realloc/free, so the UAF mechanism is absent at the immediate parent. Release ancestry checks show v4.0.4 (9ab0e75ca894ad48402265d524207e4e1e8734bb) excludes the BIC; v4.0.5 (4d25e6f59b0cdef57cbd3e910652babe362ea4eb), v4.5.1 (0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e), and v4.5.2-beta2 (a1778a25a2f8dc4de879782567abab6b923e9694) contain the BIC but not the fix. Direct fix 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da removes safe_realloc, adds a pkthdr.len > MAX_SNAPLEN guard before copying into the already-MAXPACKET tcprewrite buffer, and changes configure.ac from 4.5.2-beta2 to 4.5.2-beta3; tagged v4.5.2 (98169912173986cc48a4ad325997dcc20c38af28) contains the fix. This matches the advisory boundary of affected through 4.5.1 and sufficient upgrade to 4.5.2-beta3.
causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability requires the realloc transition, not get_l2len_protocol itself: that parser is merely the observed stale-pointer consumer. History proves 69831b8186513309f4dd43ca5bacfc34b554ad14 is the atomic commit that first introduced realloc into the --fixlen pad branch while tcpedit_packet retained aliases established before the call. Its immediate parent cannot free or move pktdata on this path, establishing parent absence. Later commits changed pointer propagation and allocation headroom without removing the stale-alias hazard, and the flaw remained in every checked release from v4.0.5 through v4.5.1/v4.5.2-beta2. Commit 73008f261f1cdf7a1087dc8759115242696d35da fixes the root by eliminating the realloc and bounding wire length to the preallocated capacity, with its own version metadata marking 4.5.2-beta3 and the v4.5.2 tag containing it. The BIC is a normal single-parent commit, not a merge/squash/backport, so no decomposition is applicable. Finally, the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker; under the required BIC-only attribution rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated workflow editor controls the MCP endpoint URL. McpClient.node.ts passes that value into connectMcpClientForCredential, whose transport fetch wrapper sent the initial request and redirect hops through proxyFetch without the instance NodeEgressFilter or a secure DNS lookup. The server therefore connected to internal, link-local, or otherwise blocked destinations and returned MCP tool metadata/results into the workflow. The fix validates every hop through getSecureEgressFilter and pins the validated address at connect time.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated client first requests /login.php to obtain an ICTBroadcast session cookie, then replaces the cookie value (observed as BROADCAST, although the applicable cookie name can vary) with shell metacharacters such as a backtick command substitution. ICTBroadcast passes the attacker-controlled session identifier into a shell-backed session-log command of the form sh -c echo "... Session read requested with id: <cookie> ..." >> gui.log. Because the cookie is not shell-neutralized, the shell evaluates the embedded backticks; a payload that base64-decodes and pipes a command to sh therefore executes arbitrary commands as the web-service account before authentication.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The causal flaw is in ICTBroadcast's product-side session read/logging implementation: it interpolates the untrusted cookie/session identifier into a shell command merely to append a diagnostic log line. The assigned rapid7/metasploit-framework repository does not contain that product implementation; it contains only a later exploit module and its documentation. ICTBroadcast's corresponding proprietary source repository and revision history are not publicly identified, so the commit that first introduced the shell interpolation cannot be reconstructed from this clone.
causal_research.ai_marker: not inspectable: no vulnerability-introducing ICTBroadcast commit object is available. Per the BIC-only rule, no AI attribution was inferred from rapid7/metasploit-framework PR #20446, its branch commits, its merge commit, the PR body, or later material because those objects add exploit tooling and do not introduce the product flaw.
evidence: The bundle's GitHub advisory (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3h67-687r-7fpc) says ICTBroadcast passes session-cookie data to shell processing, lists affected/patched versions as unknown, and explicitly reports 'Source code: No known source code.' NVD (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-2611) and VulnCheck (https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/ictbroadcast-unauthenticated-session-cookie-rce) bound the known affected range to ICTBroadcast <= 7.4; neither supplies a product source commit or fix commit.

First-party disclosure context in rapid7/metasploit-framework PR #20446 (https://github.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/pull/20446) records discovery on 2025-03-19, repeated unanswered vendor contact, and the researcher's statement on 2025-08-02: 'As of today, I have no idea whether it's been patched.' causal_research.bug_semantics: A default-constructed Http3ConnectionHandler (localSettings == null, or a settings frame without HTTP3_SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE) does not advertise or enforce a small max field-section size. After incubator #221 the missing setting is treated as Long.MAX_VALUE, later retargeted to (2^62)-1, and that value is stored as Http3FrameCodec.maxHeaderListSize. Incoming HEADERS/PUSH_PROMISE are decoded into Http3HeadersSink, which only rejects when accumulated QPACK header size exceeds maxHeaderListSize. With an unbounded cap a network peer can keep sending headers until the process hits OutOfMemoryError. HTTP/1.1 HttpObjectDecoder and HTTP/2 Http2CodecUtil.DEFAULT_HEADER_LIST_SIZE already default to 8192 bytes; HTTP/3 followed RFC 9114's unlimited default instead. Preconditions: application uses netty-codec-http3 with the default constructor/settings. Counterevidence: a caller who already set a finite MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE was not on this default path; the pre-#221 0xffffffffL default was large (4GiB) but still advertised and finite.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked that no other layer caps the field section independently: Http3FrameCodec has only the maxHeaderListSize-based checks (enforceMaxPayloadLength for HEADERS/PUSH_PROMISE and Http3HeadersSink for decoded headers), QPACK itself has no field-section ceiling, and the earlier 16MB Http3Settings.defaultSettings() value (fd8c4330829, 2026-01-08) is not used by the null-settings path, which builds an empty DefaultHttp3SettingsFrame. mechanism.impact: Memory-exhaustion denial of service. Each connection can force unbounded allocation through the QPACK decoder and Http3HeadersSink path until the JVM dies with OutOfMemoryError; advisory CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H, CWE-1188 and CWE-400, HIGH.
mechanism.preconditions: Default construction path: localSettings is null or lacks HTTP3_SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE, so the handler falls back to the unbounded value. Applications that pass an explicit finite HTTP3_SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE are not affected by the default, and the attacker needs a live HTTP/3 connection (no privileges or user interaction).
mechanism.summary: A remote HTTP/3 peer that leaves HTTP3_SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE unspecified hits an unbounded default: Http3ConnectionHandler falls back to (1L << 62) - 1 and passes it as maxHeaderListSize to Http3FrameCodec, whose enforceMaxPayloadLength/H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD checks and Http3HeadersSink ceiling therefore never trip, letting the peer grow a decompressed header section until the process dies with OutOfMemoryError.
mechanism.trigger: Establish an HTTP/3 connection to a Netty server (or connect Netty's HTTP/3 client codec to a malicious server) whose handler was built through the default path (localSettings == null, or without HTTP3_SETTINGS_MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE), then stream a HEADERS or PUSH_PROMISE field section larger than available memory; no authentication or user interaction is required. causal_research.bug_semantics: For a private 802.1X (WPA-Enterprise) profile (connection.permissions / priv->private_user), NetworkManager already reads FILE-typed cert/key properties as the owning user and hands them to wpa_supplicant as blobs. 802-1x.ca-path and 802-1x.phase2-ca-path are directories, so they cannot be blobs and were still emitted as raw ca_path/ca_path2 strings. An unprivileged local user with settings.modify.own can therefore point a private profile at an attacker-controlled CA directory, bypass server certificate validation, and steal EAP credentials via a rogue AP. The REST users.forgotPassword path is separately bounded; the DDP method was not.

mechanism.impact: Availability only: unauthenticated remote process-kill DoS on the SMF management plane. Fatalf bypasses Gin's per-goroutine recovery, so the whole process exits (docker ps shows Exited (1), log line [FATA][SMF][Init] overlap cidr value between UPFs); all SMF SBI services (PDU session establishment, UE policy lookups, UPF association) are lost until an operator restarts the NF, and the attacker can repeat the request to sustain the outage.
mechanism.preconditions: Network reach to the SMF SBI HTTP/2 port (8000), no token: at the affected pin the UPI group is mounted without util_oauth middleware while other service groups have it, and the handler requires no session or UE state. The overlap must be against a pool the instance already knows (the default UPF pool in the compose lab, 10.60.0.0/16, suffices).
mechanism.summary: An attacker who can reach the SMF SBI sends POST /upi/v1/upNodesLinks with JSON that adds a UPF whose UE IP pool overlaps an existing pool; the handler passes the body straight to UpNodesFromConfiguration, whose overlap check calls logger.InitLog.Fatalf, which is os.Exit(1)-equivalent and terminates the whole SMF process, so one unauthenticated request drops all of SMF's SBI surface until restart.
mechanism.trigger: curl -X POST http://<smf>:8000/upi/v1/upNodesLinks -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"links":[...],"upNodes":{"UPF-OVERLAP":{"type":"UPF",...,"pools":[{"cidr":"10.60.0.0/16"}]}}}' where 10.60.0.0/16 overlaps a pool already registered by the default UPF; repeatable after each restart, and the sibling invalid-pool and static-pool-exclusion Fatalfs give the same process kill through the same single handler.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated SSRF (CWE-918) on the XXL-JOB admin manual trigger path. An attacker who can log in and who has permission on at least one job group posts /jobinfo/trigger with an arbitrary addressList. JobInfoController.triggerJob forwards that string through XxlJobServiceImpl.trigger (login + job-group ACL only) into JobTrigger.trigger, which overwrites the in-memory XxlJobGroup to addressType=1 and addressList=user input. getRegistryList() then splits that CSV into executor URLs. doTrigger builds an HTTP ExecutorBiz client to each URL, attaching XXL-JOB-ACCESS-TOKEN and POSTing a TriggerRequest (jobId, handler, params, glueSource, logId, etc.). The admin therefore originates server-side HTTP from its network position to attacker-chosen destinations, leaking the platform token and job metadata. JobGroupController HTTP/HTTPS checks on saved groups do not apply to this per-trigger override. CVSS PR:L matches the login/ACL preconditions; the maintainer dispute does not remove the request-forgery mechanism.

potential_fix.rationale: Job-group ACL only proves the caller may trigger that job; it does not bind the HTTP client target. causal_research.bug_semantics: GuardDog's programmatic remote project scanner (`ProjectScanner.scan_remote` / `PypiRequirementsScanner.scan_remote`) takes a caller-supplied repository URL, rewrites it with the blind substring `url.replace("github", "raw.githubusercontent")`, concatenates `/{branch}/{requirements_name}`, and then `requests.get`s that URL with HTTP Basic auth from `GIT_USERNAME`/`GH_TOKEN`. The rewrite never parses hostname, userinfo, or port, so a crafted URL such as `http://github@127.0.0.1:18081/owner/repo` becomes `http://raw.githubusercontent@127.0.0.1:18081/owner/repo/main/requirements.txt`. Requests treats that as a request to `127.0.0.1:18081` and attaches the GitHub PAT, yielding SSRF plus `GH_TOKEN` exfiltration (CWE-918).

causal_research.bug_semantics: An untrusted plugin class controls plugin.plugin_id. PluginManager instantiated the class and accepted any nonempty string of at most 50 characters, then propagated that value into PluginSecurityContext. For a plugin without READ_FILES, the sandbox intercepted file operations and called _is_safe_path, but _is_safe_path resolved ~/.openssl_encrypt/plugins/<plugin_id> without validating plugin_id and treated every path with that resolved prefix as allowed. Traversal such as '../../.ssh' therefore changes the purported per-plugin config root to a user directory outside ~/.openssl_encrypt/plugins, allowing the sandboxed plugin to read or write paths there despite lacking general file capability.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Bitcoinrb's experimental SPV RPC HTTP server (lib/bitcoin/rpc/http_server.rb) parses a POST JSON body into method/params and dispatches with Ruby Object#send(command, *args) while including RequestHandler. There is no allowlist that command is an intended RPC method, so a client can invoke Kernel#eval / Kernel#system (and any other reachable method) with attacker-controlled arguments. The published PoC POSTs {"method":"eval","params":["File.write(\"/tmp/pwned\",\"owned\")"]} to the EventMachine listener (binds 0.0.0.0:8332 by default). The sink is the unvalidated send of JSON method plus splatted JSON params; CWE-77 as reviewed by GHSA-q66h-m87m-j2q6. Affected gem range is < 1.12.0; 070327133a2a3e5a6d265b2d82f06f9414c01e74 added SUPPORTED_COMMANDS and rejects unknown methods before send.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When ospfd has `debug ospf packet <type|all> ... detail` enabled, ospf_packet_dump() walks an LS Update and, for Opaque Link/Area/AS LSAs, calls ospf_opaque_lsa_dump(), which invokes show_opaque_info_detail(NULL, lsa, NULL). That helper is itself NULL-safe, but it then calls the registered show_opaque_info callback with vty==NULL. ospf_ext_init() always registers ospf_ext_link_show_info and ospf_ext_pref_show_info for Extended Link/Prefix Opaque LSAs. Those callbacks browse TLVs and, for an unknown type or an oversized TLV, call show_vty_unknown_tlv(), which at frr-10.4.1 does vty_out(vty, ...) with no NULL check. vty_out() reads vty->status, so a network-adjacent OSPF packet containing such a TLV crashes ospfd (DoS). VTY `show` paths pass a real vty and do not hit this sink.

causal_research.bug_semantics: NLTK 3.9.4 introduced nltk.pathsec as a centralized I/O sentinel. pathsec.open() calls validate_path() and, when ENFORCE is True, raises PermissionError for paths outside allowed NLTK data roots before delegating to builtins.open(). StreamBackedCorpusView in nltk/corpus/reader/util.py accepts a raw string fileid and, in _open(), still calls builtins.open(self._fileid, "rb") (and SeekableUnicodeStreamReader on that handle). That path never hits validate_path, so an attacker who can supply fileid (web/API/multi-tenant NLP pipeline) can read arbitrary local files such as /etc/passwd even with ENFORCE=True. XMLCorpusView subclasses StreamBackedCorpusView, so the same _open sink applies. The content-read is the open() branch; os.stat on the string fileid leaks size/existence only.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-121 stack buffer overflow: CheckKeyTypes() accepts XkbSetMap key types with client-controlled numLevels in [1,255] and never clamps non-canonical types to XkbMaxShiftLevel (63). Those widths are stored in the server type table. Later XkbUpdateKeyTypesFromCore / XkbKeyTypesForCoreSymbols / XkbChangeTypesOfKey index stack arrays tsyms/oldSyms/oldActs sized XkbMaxSymsPerKey (XkbMaxShiftLevel*XkbNumKbdGroups = 252) via XKB_OFFSET(g,l)=(g*groupsWidth)+l. With numLevels=255, groupsWidth=255, indices reach 3*255+254=1019 and overflow the 252-entry buffers. Local X client can crash the server or escalate if it runs as root. Incomplete prior XKB overflow work left this CheckKeyTypes upper bound unenforced. Fixed in xorg-server 21.1.23 and xwayland 24.1.12.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Unauthenticated panic DoS (CWE-476/CWE-20). Source: StartActionByGet accepts an arbitrary actionId, looks up a binding with FindBindingByID, and still calls Executor.ExecRequest when the lookup is nil. ExecRequest allocates and SetLog()s an InternalLogEntry (Binding copied from the request, so nil) before the command chain runs. stepRequestActionHasBinding then returns false, so execution stops, but the tracking ID remains in the log map. Sink: KillAction and RestartAction load that log and immediately evaluate execReqLogEntry.Binding.Action without testing Binding; the nil pointer panics in the HTTP/Connect handler (curl 52 empty reply), before ACL. Because StartActionByGet does not wait on the executor goroutine, an attacker can mint orphan tracking IDs and repeatedly crash handlers. Parent behavior was nil-safe: KillAction used cfg.FindAction(title) and returned when action was nil; RestartAction did not exist.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GitPython's config writer interpolates option names verbatim into git-config lines (`write_section` emits `\t%s = %s\n`). Through 3.1.57, `_assure_config_name_safe(option, "option")` rejected only CR/LF/NUL, so `=`, `#`, `;`, brackets, and whitespace in an option name were accepted. A caller-controlled name such as `sshCommand = touch /tmp/RCE #` is written as `\tsshCommand = touch /tmp/RCE # = <value>`, which git parses as `core.sshCommand=touch /tmp/RCE` (the `#` comments out the intended value). That forges `core.sshCommand` / `core.hooksPath` / `alias.*` and yields RCE on a later git operation. Distinct field and character class from section-header bracket injection and from newline injection.

causal_research.bug_semantics: RabbitConnectionFactoryBean.setUri() immediately delegated an amqps URI to the RabbitMQ client while the bean's secure setUpSSL() path remained conditional on a separate useSSL flag. With the default false flag, the client created encrypted TLS using its permissive trust-everything setup, so neither the broker certificate nor hostname was verified and an active network attacker could impersonate the broker.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A site with both a publicly votable survey and a restricted survey is required. causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated IDOR (CWE-639) on /api/annotations/{id}/. AnnotationAPI is RetrieveUpdateDestroyAPIView whose queryset is Annotation.objects.all() with no get_queryset, so DRF looks up any annotation by sequential integer PK. permission_required maps GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to annotations.view/change/delete, all registered as rules.is_authenticated. DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES also include HasObjectPermission, but OSS Project.has_permission is a stub True at 1.23.0 (HEAD only rejects deleted org membership, not active_organization mismatch), so object-level org isolation does not run. causal_research.bug_semantics: Apache MINA IoBuffer.getObject() deserializes with a custom ObjectInputStream. After the CVE-2024-52046 allowlist, AbstractIoBuffer.resolveClass() still had two branches: if ObjectStreamClass.forClass() was non-null it consulted acceptMatchers, but if forClass() was null (primitive/type-0 and other unresolved descriptors) it called Class.forName(name, false, classLoader) with no filter. An attacker who can supply serialized bytes to getObject() therefore bypasses the classname allowlist and can cause arbitrary class loading / gadget deserialization (CWE-502 RCE). The 2026 patch applies acceptMatchers before any Class.forName, on both branches.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-41635 state=PUBLISHED (cvelistV5 2026/41xxx/CVE-2026-41635.json); CNA Apache; GHSA-8297-v2rf-2p32 withdrawn_at=null. Title: AbstractIoBuffer.resolveClass() null-clazz branch skips acceptMatchers. Affected 2.0.0-2.0.27 / 2.1.0-2.1.10 / 2.2.0-2.2.5; claimed patched 2.0.28 / 2.1.11 / 2.2.6.

Vendor: https://lists.apache.org/thread/1l91w1mqsb3lwfd504fs045ylxntt2tm and http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/04/27/4 (Emmanuel Lecharny, 2026-04-27, ZDRES-059). Mechanism: one resolveClass branch (static/primitive) does not check the class; fix applies allowlist before Class.forName. Reporter Venkatraman Kumar, Securin. Attack surface: IoBuffer.getObject().
Sibling incomplete-fix CVE-2024-52046 (no allowlist) was claimed fixed in 2.0.27/2.1.10/2.2.4; this CVE is the remaining null-clazz skip of that allowlist, not a withdrawn/false positive.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated users persist Rules Engine scripts that the server later executes on inbound IoT messages. Go scripts are evaluated by Yaegi with the full stdlib.Symbols table (os.ReadFile/WriteFile/Remove, os.Environ, net/http, and the rest of the standard library). The only gate is a regex in re/service.go AddRule/UpdateRule that rejects some goroutine and panic() spellings; Lua scripts have no equivalent gate. processLua preloads gopher-lua-libs db (arbitrary DB), ioutil (file I/O), filepath (traversal), and http/client (SSRF). That is server-side code injection (CWE-94) from a low-privileged authenticated caller, matching CVE-2026-71235 / GHSA-vq5v-m87m-6pqm.

causal_research.bug_semantics: AES-CBC decrypt (default mode) PKCS#7-style unpads by reading the last plaintext byte as pad length and taking a data-dependent path when that length is invalid (0 or greater than the block size). In the pre-fix form the length predicate used boolean `||`, which short-circuits so a zero pad byte skips `$length > $this->block_size`; valid vs invalid padding therefore differ in both control flow and wall-clock time, and invalid padding later returns false / throws instead of the stripped plaintext. A chosen-ciphertext attacker who can observe decrypt timing (or the validity signal) can recover CBC plaintext (CWE-208 padding-oracle timing).

causal_research.bug_semantics: llama.cpp DRY sampler stores caller-supplied dry_allowed_length as a signed int32 with no lower bound. An HTTP /v1/completions or /v1/chat/completions body can set dry_allowed_length to INT32_MIN; json_value copies that value into sampling params and llama_sampler_init_dry stores it unchanged. llama_sampler_dry_apply then (1) fails the last_n_repeat <= dry_allowed_length early-return because any token count is greater than INT32_MIN, (2) treats every repeat_len as eligible because repeat_len >= INT32_MIN is always true, and (3) computes int repeat_exp = repeat_len - dry_allowed_length, a signed integer underflow of INT32_MIN that is undefined in int32 and yields an out-of-range exponent used to mutate logits. Cyera/VulnCheck observed the resulting heap OOB read/underflow as SIGSEGV DoS or corrupted sampling probabilities. The same unbounded int is also accepted by --dry-allowed-length.

causal_research.bug_semantics: During ListFonts/ListFontsWithInfo font-alias resolution, a client-controlled fonts.alias target accepted by libXfont2 can be 257-1023 bytes, while the server used 256-byte XLFDMAXFONTNAMELEN-backed stack-resident tmp_pattern and current.pattern buffers. The alias paths copied resolvedlen or namelen bytes into those buffers without a preceding bound check, so a client that adds a crafted directory with SetFontPath and requests the alias can overflow the stack, crash the server, or potentially escalate privileges when the server is privileged.

causal_research.bug_semantics: SimpleGCMConfig.getSecretKeySaltGenerator() falls back to org.jasypt.salt.ZeroSaltGenerator (16-byte all-zero salt) whenever jasypt.encryptor.gcm-secret-key-salt is unset. SimpleGCMByteEncryptor.loadSecretKey then feeds that salt into PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 (getAESKeyFromPassword / PBEKeySpec) to derive the AES-256 key, so every deployment that shares a master password derives a byte-identical key. Captured GCM ciphertext from one environment decrypts on any other with the same password, and a single rainbow table applies worldwide (CWE-760/CWE-759, plus CWE-1188 insecure default). The default path is the documented GCM master-password recipe. A later same-branch commit also dropped the GCM iteration default from 65536 to 1000 (CWE-916), compounding offline brute-force cost, but the CVE/GHSA sink is the predictable-salt generator. causal_research.bug_semantics: CorpusReader.open(fileid) is the source: after optional lexical rejection of absolute paths and '..' components, it calls FileSystemPathPointer.join(fileid) then opens the joined path. join() builds os.path.join(root, fileid) (later plus os.path.normpath and a startswith(root) prefix test) without resolving symlinks. A directory or file symlink planted inside the corpus root keeps a lexical path under root (e.g. JOINED=/tmp/nltk-root/link/secret.txt) while REALPATH is outside (e.g. /tmp/outside/secret.txt or /etc/hostname). The OS follows the link on open, so a local attacker who can place a symlink in an attacker-controlled corpus directory reads arbitrary files the process can read (CWE-59). 3.9.3 #3479/#3480 blocked only lexical traversal; 3.9.4 1b0e519e2 closes this open() path by Path.resolve() scoped-root validation.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Vert.x's RFC 3986 dot-segment remover mishandled rule C when processing /../ or terminal /.. after an output segment containing no slash: the pos != -1 guard left that whole segment in the output instead of clearing it. Consequently a decoded path such as bar/../index.html normalized to bar/index.html rather than /index.html; a crafted static-handler request containing bar%2F..%2F could resolve a nonexistent offset and cache that negative result so later requests for the real static file returned HTTP 404, causing unauthenticated availability loss.
evidence: The Eclipse CNA record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-1002 is PUBLISHED and describes network-triggered static-handler cache manipulation and availability loss; it marks Vert.x 4.0.0 through 4.5.23 and 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 affected.

Vendor issue https://github.com/vert-x3/vertx-web/issues/2836 demonstrates removeDotSegments("bar/../index.html") returning "bar/index.html" instead of "/index.html" and records that a bar%2F..%2F request caches a nonexistent file result, after which the normal file request returns 404.

causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit d5f646b101377ed2a842dfef00139b509b3bbd71 first added HttpUtils.removeDots and both flawed rule-C branches, using lastIndexOf("/") followed by deletion only when the slash existed. Its immediate parent 5a79bf707794078a842800be5ba862a218e64c6c contains HttpUtils.java but no removeDots implementation. causal_research.reasoning: The vendor and CNA evidence establish a real availability vulnerability, not a withdrawn or rejected advisory. The defective behavior is the rule-C output-buffer update itself: when no slash is present, retaining the segment violates RFC 3986 and enables the encoded traversal-shaped request to poison the static handler's negative cache entry. History follows that exact mechanism backward. The 2024 RFC3986 helper commit only relocates the already-flawed code; the smallest public first-write is the 2017 PR member d5f646b101377ed2a842dfef00139b509b3bbd71, and its immediate parent directly proves the implementation absent. The maintained 4.5 and 5.x fixes replace the guard with an unconditional setLength that clears the buffer when lastIndexOf returns -1, and tag ancestry matches the vendor's affected/patched boundaries. Because the BIC commit object is authored and committed by Julien Viet and has no AI marker or trailer, the causal verdict is NOT_AI; later repository AI signals and the 2026 fixes do not alter BIC attribution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CRuby Nokogiri, when built with packaged libxml2, downloads and links a libxml2 older than 2.10.4. An attacker who feeds a crafted XSD through Nokogiri::XML::Schema (xmlSchemaNewMemParserCtxt/xmlSchemaNewDocParserCtxt → xmlSchemaParse) reaches libxml2 xmlSchemaFixupComplexType, which dereferences NULL baseType->subtypes on invalid complexType extension of simpleContent (CVE-2023-28484), and a related NULL deref in xmlSchemaCheckCOSSTDerivedOK for circular substitution groups. The process can segfault (DoS). JRuby and --use-system-libraries builds are out of this advisory's scope; system libxml2 is a distro issue.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Ech0 access tokens created with expiry=never (NEVER_EXPIRY, duration 0) are signed as JWTs with no exp claim. jwt/v5 and JWTAuthMiddleware accept that token, so a stolen bearer stays cryptographically valid until JWT_SECRET rotation. Three independent revocation paths then fail for this token class: AuthHandler.Logout dereferences claims.ExpiresAt.Time and panics on the nil field so the JTI never reaches the blacklist; AuthRepository.RevokeToken returns immediately when remainTTL <= 0; SettingService.DeleteAccessToken deletes only the metadata row and does not blacklist the JTI. Finite-expiry tokens can still age out; never-expire tokens cannot.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user could bypass the profile image input's client-side accept hint and submit an SVG File. The profile flow uploaded the supplied bytes unchanged to the public Supabase avatars bucket, merely naming the object with a .webp suffix, then persisted its public URL. Directly viewing that stored object from the trusted storage origin caused JavaScript embedded in the SVG to execute, yielding stored XSS.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0 introduced the profile-avatar upload end to end: a new UploadImage component accepted a File without validating its MIME type, extension, or contents, and src/routes/profile/[id].svelte uploaded that untrusted File directly to the public avatars bucket and stored its URL. The accept=".jpg, .jpeg, .png" attribute was only a browser file-picker hint, while forcing a .webp object name did not decode or transcode the uploaded bytes.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names human author and committer rotimi-best <best@classroomio.com>, has the subject "Upload avatar", and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, trailer, or other AI marker.
evidence: The reporter disclosure at https://github.com/Rivek619/CVE-2025-65675 identifies ClassroomIO 0.1.13 and reproduces the issue by logging in, uploading a crafted SVG as the profile picture, saving it, and opening the stored image in a new tab; the embedded script then executes.

At tag v0.1.13 (peeled commit 876a785b3c467b809804f56e0981bff448fcfdb5), apps/dashboard/src/lib/components/UploadImage/index.svelte:20-37 takes e.target.files[0], checks only size, reads it, and assigns the File to avatar; apps/dashboard/src/routes/profile/[id]/+page.svelte:51-63 uploads avatar unchanged to supabase.storage.from('avatars') under a filename ending in .webp and persists response.publicUrl.

git log -L 51,65:apps/dashboard/src/routes/profile/[id]/+page.svelte v0.1.13 followed the upload block backward through non-causal API/refactor edits 32d0198d3da4ef52b303369846420844ddad5b1c, d542a4f7e3f1b71c4e43304f0d2c89bd5618e917, and 4a7843b0b40707f94828c9dce18f54d8eb821ae2 to its zero-line addition in 05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0. v0.1.13 blame likewise assigns the original File acceptance, FileReader flow, avatar assignment, if (avatar), forced .webp filename, and upload/public-URL structure to 05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0; later commits only moved, typed, or adapted that mechanism.

Direct diff 26798f1e93d437f0a2661333450c7b669e365de1..05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0 shows src/components/UploadImage/index.svelte created from /dev/null and the complete unvalidated storage upload added to src/routes/profile/[id].svelte. Direct parent-tree checks found no src/components/UploadImage/index.svelte at all (git cat-file -e exited 128), and the parent's profile page had no File selection, avatars-bucket upload, generated public URL, or attacker-controlled profile-picture persistence path.

05ed2b74ee25aaeddefc62121202ee97ed8637f0 is a single-parent commit, not a merge or release aggregate, and is an ancestor of v0.1.13 and every listed v0.1.x tag. Same-message commits on unrelated histories were not ancestors of v0.1.13 and therefore are not the BIC for this release lineage.

The direct fix commit 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5 adds validateImageUpload calls before UploadImage and UploadWidget accept a file, central JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP MIME and extension allowlists, explicit SVG rejection, and SVG/data-URL sanitization. Its message expressly says it fixes stored XSS through malicious SVG profile uploads.

The version boundary is direct: v0.2.4 peels to 4ac242d918988855db54aff3578aa73a6d408d2e, does not contain 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5, and has no validateImageUpload reference in the profile UploadImage component. Annotated security tag v0.2.5 peels directly to 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5 and contains those checks. Thus the advisory-named v0.1.13 is demonstrably vulnerable and the repository's first tagged patched boundary is v0.2.5.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An attacker who can create an accepted HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, TCPRoute, or TLSRoute on a shared Gateway chooses a namespace/name pair that hyphen-concatenates to the same string as a victim Route (team/a-app vs team-a/app). Traefik builds routeKey via provider.Normalize of kind-namespace-name-gw-gatewayNS-gatewayName-ep-entryPoint-ruleIndex, then makeRouterName appends a SHA-256 of the match rule only. Normalize collapses non-alphanumerics to '-' and does not encode field lengths, so the two Routes produce one router (and derived middleware/WRR) name. mergeHTTPConfiguration maps.Copy then lets the later-loaded Route overwrite the earlier router, sending the victim hostname/path to the attacker backend. Preconditions: kubernetesgateway provider, a Gateway that accepts the attacker Route (allowedRoutes from All or a colliding namespace), and equivalent match rules so the rule hash matches. Same-namespace, same-gateway collisions of this form do not arise because the shared suffix (gateway + entrypoint) would require identical route names; cross-namespace attachment is required for the advisory PoC.

mechanism.counterevidence: I re-read the join at the introducer and at the fix parent (both boundary-free) and Normalize at the introducer (no length encoding), and checked that the advisory's v3.7.8 reproduction is consistent with maps.Copy replace semantics; the weakening condition I found is that at the 2020 introducer routes were fetched only from the Gateway's own namespace (client.GetHTTPRoutes(gateway.Namespace, ...)), so the cross-namespace hijack only becomes reachable with 969dd088a2 (2021-10-04) - the non-injective identity itself is present from c21597c593.
mechanism.impact: Cross-namespace traffic hijack on a shared Gateway: requests addressed to the victim's hostname/path (including credentials and authorization headers) are served by the attacker's backend, and forged responses or state-changing requests can be accepted; nothing in Kubernetes or in Traefik reports the collision, so the victim Route object stays intact while its traffic is silently reassigned.
mechanism.preconditions: The attacker may create a Route the shared Gateway accepts (Gateway API itself imposes no constraint on the colliding names); the Gateway allows routes from the attacker's namespace (e.g. allowedRoutes.namespaces.from: All, reachable since 969dd088a2 added RouteNamespaces support); the namespace/name concatenation collides with a victim Route attached to the same Gateway; the attacker's match rule must be equivalent so makeRouterName's sha256 of the rule comes out identical.
mechanism.summary: An attacker who can create a Gateway API Route accepted by a shared Gateway picks a namespace/name pair whose hyphen-join collides with a victim Route's identity; the provider derives router and service keys by boundary-free hyphen concatenation (namespace, name, Gateway identity, entry point, rule index) and maps.Copy then lets the later Route's entries overwrite the victim's, redirecting victim traffic to the attacker backend.
mechanism.trigger: Create or update an HTTPRoute/GRPCRoute (TCPRoute/TLSRoute use the same join) in a namespace the shared Gateway accepts, with namespace and name whose concatenation equals the victim's, e.g. team/a-app vs team-a/app, using the same hostname/path match so the rule hash is also identical.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: At the introducer c21597c593, pkg/provider/kubernetes/gateway/kubernetes.go builds routerName := httpRoute.Name + "-" + gateway.Name + "-" + ep and routerKey := makeRouterKey(router.Rule, makeID(httpRoute.Namespace, routerName)) with func makeID(namespace, name string) string returning namespace + "-" + name; at the fix parent b5ace8eb the same join is pkg/provider/kubernetes/gateway/httproute.go:140 provider.Normalize(fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s-%s-gw-%s-%s-ep-%s-%d", kindHTTPRoute, route.Namespace, route.Name, gatewayNamespace, gatewayName, listener.EPName, ri)) feeding makeRouterName(rule, routeKey) in kubernetes.go; pkg/provider/configuration.go:380 Normalize joins non-alphanumeric runs with '-' without length encoding, so component boundaries are not preserved.

causal_research.reasoning:

The smallest first writer of that identity is named-human PR member f034143 (Romain / rtribotte), verified absent in parent ea418aa7. Squash landing c21597c is a carrier, not the BIC. Cross-namespace exposure (969dd088) and later sprintf reformulations are human as well. BIC-local commit objects have no AI authorship or co-authorship markers, so the verdict is NOT_AI. Fix-side author gndz07 is informational only.
The advisory mechanism reproduces in the tree: Gateway API router and service identities are built by hyphen-joining namespace, route name, Gateway identity, entry point and rule index, and provider.Normalize collapses punctuation to the same '-' delimiter, so distinct objects such as team/a-app and team-a/app produce one identity and maps.Copy lets the later Route replace the earlier backend. causal_research.bug_semantics: Ech0 stored local-account passwords as a single unsalted MD5 hex digest. MD5Encrypt(text) is crypto/md5.New, Write([]byte(text)), Sum(nil), hex.EncodeToString — no salt, no iteration, no memory-hard KDF. Through 5.4.1 every local-password path used that helper: InitOwner and Register persist MD5Encrypt(password) into users.password; Login hashes the submitted password the same way and does a string equality check against the stored digest; UpdateUser rewrites users.password with another unsalted MD5. An attacker who obtains data/ech0.db (backup export, mis-served static files, or filesystem access) can extract the 32-hex hashes and recover owner/admin plaintext with rainbow tables or GPU hashcat -m 0, then POST /api/login for a full session JWT. CWE-327. Fixed in 5.4.2 by moving the secret into user_local_auth, hashing new passwords with bcrypt, and lazily upgrading leftover MD5 rows on next successful login.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A user allowed to create/configure OAuth2 credentials controls accessTokenUrl. During the authorization callback, n8n converts that value to ClientOAuth2.accessTokenUri and code.getToken constructs an authorization_code POST with fixed OAuth fields. Before the fix, @n8n/client-oauth2 sent that request through axios without the SSRF-protection service's initial-URL, DNS-rebinding, or redirect checks. The target's OAuth-shaped success data could be stored and error bodies were rendered into the callback page, allowing bounded internal response disclosure in addition to the server-side request.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The remotely reachable /uploadFile multipart handler parsed an uploaded FileItem and constructed its destination name by concatenating the request-controlled sid, an underscore, and the client-controlled upload filename beneath an intended temporary upload directory. Because sid was not validated and the resulting path was not canonicalized or checked for containment, ../ segments in sid escaped the upload directory; an attacker could select the uploaded bytes and filename (for example a JSP) and place the file in a web-accessible location.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 7436c2f0b67128a558e3ac3a820ef8e0a01f59c0 introduced the /uploadFile servlet mapping and the first upload handler in one feature commit. Its new UploadFileHandler passed request.getParameter("sid") + "_" + item.getName() directly to a java.io.File rooted at WEB-INF/temp and wrote attacker bytes there. Later package moves and the 2022 conversion to FileUtils.writeFile preserved the same unvalidated path composition, so they are not origins of the flaw.

causal_research.bug_semantics: IPX filesystem storage decides whether a requested image id stays inside the configured dir(s) with a raw string prefix check: join/resolve(dir, id) then filePath.startsWith(dir) without a trailing path separator. When dir is a resolved path such as /cwd/public, an id of ../public123/test.png (normalized by ipx withLeadingSlash to /../public123/test.png) becomes /cwd/public123/test.png via path/pathe join, which still startsWith('/cwd/public') and is served. The GHSA PoC contrasts that with ../publi123/test.png, which fails the prefix test. CWE-22 path traversal; library and HTTP callers can read images from a sibling directory that shares the allowed prefix. Affected npm ipx ranges are <1.3.2, >=2.0.0-0 <2.1.1, and >=3.0.0 <3.1.1.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In 3.3.0, HITL tasks park in scheduler-owned AWAITING_INPUT instead of deferring onto the triggerer. The worker/Dag author supplies next_kwargs via the Execution API park payload; every 15s the scheduler timeout sweep calls handle_event_submit on each timed-out TI. handle_event_submit first runs airflow.sdk.serde.deserialize (allow-listed) and, on ImportError/KeyError/AttributeError/TypeError, falls back to BaseSerialization.deserialize, which at 3.3.0 import_string()s exception-node class names from the blob with no allowed_deserialization_classes gate. A Dag author can therefore instantiate an arbitrary imported class inside the scheduler, or raise out of the fallback and abort the entire sweep. Source: a Dag author/worker writes attacker-controlled next_kwargs through the Execution API TIAwaitingInputStatePayload (park path added in PR #68028).

Sink: SchedulerJobRunner.check_awaiting_input_timeouts (3.3.0 scheduler_job_runner.py:3374) runs every trigger_timeout_check_interval (fallback 15s) and calls handle_event_submit, which at 3.3.0 trigger.py:520-524 does serde.deserialize then on ImportError/KeyError/AttributeError/TypeError falls back to BaseSerialization.deserialize with no allowed_deserialization_classes check.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Karakeep's public NextAuth credentials login (POST /api/auth/callback/credentials) reaches CredentialsProvider.authorize() in apps/web/server/auth.ts, which calls validatePassword() and then either issues a session cookie or returns a normal CredentialsSignin failure. Until the 2026-07-04 patch there was no in-product rate limit, failed-attempt lockout, CAPTCHA, or backoff on that path, so an unauthenticated client could send unlimited password guesses against a known email (CWE-307 / CWE-799). bcrypt cost 10 is the only inherent slowdown and does not stop online stuffing of weak or reused passwords. Signup later gained tRPC rate-limit middleware and optional Turnstile; login never did, because it is not a tRPC procedure.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked for any pre-existing validation and found none: save() stores the URL verbatim; form_setup_html.php has a plain text input; the block controller defines no validate() override; FeedService is identical at 9.5.0 and at the fix parent; HttpClientFactory::getDefaultOptions only handles proxy values. Confirmed the fetch is triggered by block rendering/indexing rather than by pre-auth input, and that responses are not returned verbatim to the attacker (consistent with the LOW rating); no withdrawn or rejected advisory evidence exists, so the defect is real as described.
mechanism.impact: SSRF from the web server: internal-only HTTP services, admin interfaces bound to loopback and cloud metadata endpoints can be requested and triggered with the site's network position; feed responses are parsed and partially rendered in the block (or folded into searchable content), giving limited content disclosure, and redirect support also defeats naive URL allowlisting. The vendor rates it CVSS:4.0 LOW (VC:N, VI:L, SC:L).
mechanism.preconditions: The attacker has page edit rights on at least one page where the RSS Displayer block can be added or edited (the advisory's 'any page editor'); the block URL field is unrestricted text with only required='required'; the outbound client is not confined by a proxy/allowlist (the factory defaults add only concrete.proxy settings and the 5 second timeout).
mechanism.summary: A user with page-edit rights saves an arbitrary feed URL in an RSS Displayer block; block render (view) and search indexing (getSearchableContent) fetch that URL server-side through Concrete\Core\Feed\FeedService::load() with default Guzzle options, i.e. no scheme/host/IP validation and redirects enabled, exposing loopback/RFC1918/link-local targets to the CMS host's HTTP client, either directly or through a public URL that redirects to an internal one.
mechanism.trigger: Add or edit an RSS Displayer block on any page the attacker can edit and set 'Feed URL' to an internal target (for example http://127.0.0.1:PORT/..., http://10.0.0.1/..., or a public host whose response is a redirect to such a target); the next block render or content re-index performs the server-side fetch with no validation.

The first writer of that mechanism is the 2008 named-human root import, not an AI-assisted change; later Guzzle/FeedService commits only moved the same sink. The 9.5.1 squash was decomposed to H1 3636720 member 1c09181, which adds RemoteUrlValidator plus redirect-off/DNS pin and is present in tag 9.5.1 via landing f22b9df. BIC commit-object AI markers are absent, so the verdict is NOT_AI rather than an AI class or FALSE_POSITIVE.
GHSA-gjwq-9v8p-47w7 / CVE-2026-7890 describes the RSS Displayer block fetching a page-editor-supplied feed URL server-side without validation, and the code confirms it: at 9.5.0 and at the fix's parent, concrete/blocks/rss_displayer/controller.php view() line 193 and getSearchableContent() line 245 call the feed helper, whose Concrete\Core\Feed\FeedService::load() lines 41-45 fetch the raw URL with a default Guzzle client (redirects enabled, no scheme/host/IP checks, no DNS pinning) while save() line 219 stores the URL verbatim. mechanism.impact: Cross-site forgery of a state-changing backend action: the victim's session re-scans the selected files, refreshing stored attributes (refreshAttributes in the 2014 body, RescanFileCommand via doRescan today) without the user's intent. mechanism.summary: A logged-in file-manager user can be induced by a cross-site request to run the backend rescan action: public rescan() at concrete/controllers/backend/file.php:88 (9.5.0) performs the state-changing doRescan($files[0]) after only a file-permission lookup, without validating a CSRF token, so a third-party page can force the victim's session to re-scan (update stored attributes of) files the victim can edit.
mechanism.trigger: A victim with file edit rights and a live session visits an attacker-controlled page that submits a request to the backend file controller's rescan action carrying one or more fID values; no ccm_token is required because the action never validates one.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-674 uncontrolled recursion in liquidjs `{% layout %}` / `{% block %}`. In STORE mode, `src/tags/block.ts` `getBlockRender` records a per-name render function in `ctx.getRegister('blocks')[this.block]`. When a child template nests a block inside another block of the same name (including anonymous `{%block%}`), the inner tag looks up that register, wraps the outer render as `renderChild`, and overwrites the slot. OUTPUT-mode layout then calls the inner wrapper; the outer templates still contain the inner same-name block, which looks up the same register and re-enters `renderChild` with no cycle check. Recursion allocates renderer/emitter frames until the Node.js heap OOMs (~4GB). The 2016 layout/block implementation stored rendered HTML strings and could not form this call cycle. GHSA-4rc3-7j7w-m548 / CVE-2026-41311 (NVD Analyzed, not withdrawn) patch the path in `e2311dfd6e82f73509308aa8a3a1fafc92e226f0` by pushing the current Tag onto a `blockStack` register and throwing `block tag cannot be nested`. Advisory range is `< 10.25.7` (first_patched 10.25.7); the fix commit is already an ancestor of tag v10.25.6.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Harden-Runner Community Tier before v2.14.2 installed a non-TLS step-security/agent release whose audit-mode network monitor registered only the connect syscall and whose packet parser recognized TCP but not UDP. Code already executing in a workflow could therefore transmit UDP with sendto, sendmsg, or sendmmsg without producing the expected outbound-connection audit log; block mode and Enterprise Tier were not affected.

causal_research.bug_semantics: rConfig deliberately disabled Laravel self-registration with Auth::routes(['register' => false]), but a later bare Auth::routes() call registered the framework's default registration endpoints again. An unauthenticated POST /register therefore reached RegisterController, whose create() method omitted role; the users.role database column defaulted to Admin, and the RegistersUsers flow authenticated the newly created account. The attacker consequently obtained a logged-in Administrator account without invitation, approval, or prior credentials.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The optimized constant-integer for-loop exposed its native stack-local counter to script code through var(&i).
