causal_research.reasoning:
CVE-2026-6611 / GHSA-hq9j-qh3w-qvg3 describe a real default-config file-upload bypass: csrf-exempt /upload treats a static HMAC of Django SECRET_KEY as the only credential, and SECRET_KEY has a public committed fallback, so the signature is computable from the repository. That HMAC-of-SECRET_KEY check was first introduced by named human liangliangyy in 9d414015 (2018) as an incomplete remediation of earlier unauthenticated upload (37137ce/619ab8d). The BIC commit object has no AI authorship markers. No merged repair exists on 2.1.0.0 or master. Successful later Copilot activity and an unmerged Copilot security branch do not attribute the BIC. causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated GET /tokenTransfer/:uuid handler retrieved a token-bearing transfer record but never checked its createdAt timestamp, never removed the record after redemption, and serialized the whole record in the response after setting the author cookie. causal_research.bug_semantics: Penpot MCP automatically started an Express ReplServer whose POST /execute route accepted an unauthenticated JSON code string and sent it through PluginBridge as an ExecuteCodePluginTask; the plugin handler evaluated that string with new Function in a context exposing the Penpot API, storage, console, and PenpotUtils. ReplServer called app.listen(this.port) without a host, so Node/Express listened on all interfaces rather than loopback. Consequently, an unauthenticated adjacent-network peer that could reach port 4403 could cause arbitrary JavaScript execution in the connected Penpot plugin context.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Angular SSR passed an attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-Prefix into joinUrlParts when constructing redirect targets. The shared helper removed only one leading slash from each part, so a prefix such as ///evil.com became //evil.com; when emitted as a Location header, browsers interpreted that value as a protocol-relative external redirect.
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-xh43-g2fq-wjrj and the published CVE.org record CVE-2026-27738 identify a real CWE-601 open redirect in @angular/ssr, with patched boundaries 19.2.21, 20.3.17, 21.1.5, and 21.2.0-rc.1; the GHSA has withdrawn_at=null and the CVE state is PUBLISHED.

Issue #32501 documents the source-to-sink path: X-Forwarded-Prefix ///evil.com enters app.ts, joinUrlParts removes one slash, and a redirect response emits Location: //evil.com/home. The pre-fix tree at f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323^ contains that one-slash operation at packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/url.ts:107 and the header-to-helper call at packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts:197-200.

git log -S for 'export function joinUrlParts' and 'normalizedPart = normalizedPart.slice(1)' identifies landed object bca56838937f942c5ef902f5c98d018582188e84. GitHub's PR #28183 API reports exactly one member, 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364; local git verifies that member and the landed squash have the same tree 8f828397f4008883e27ad803054125e004d73e24 and the same parent 37693c40e3afc4c6dd7c949ea658bdf94146c9d8.

Direct parent-tree verification shows 37693c40e3afc4c6dd7c949ea658bdf94146c9d8 has no packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/url.ts, while 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364 adds the flawed normalizedPart.slice(1) line at url.ts:53; therefore the vulnerable normalization is absent in the immediate parent.

The raw BIC object for 8db316149ed6d728981653e3091a244920cf8364 names human author and committer Alan Agius <alanagius@google.com> and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI marker trailer.

Commit 4dac5f25106162d9cbf20ec2bf4fe02c47409c41 adds the later X-Forwarded-Prefix source-to-joinUrlParts paths in packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts and packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/ng.ts; grep of its parent 59319b8d6f02f857ab375f330812ff430e90f059 confirms those header uses are absent there.

PR #32521 has one commit and reports merge_commit_sha f086eccc36d10cf01c426e35864bc32e1e292323. Its diff directly replaces one-slash trimming with loops that remove all leading and trailing slashes and adds X-Forwarded-Prefix validation, plus regression tests for multiple slashes/backslashes and dot segments.

causal_research.bug_semantics: For an LZ4 extension, deserialization reads an attacker-controlled Int32 declared decompressed length from the wire and, when it exceeds the reusable buffer, allocates new byte[length] (later writer.GetSpan(uncompressedLength)) before validating the compressed bytes. Lz4BlockArray likewise consumes attacker-controlled per-block lengths and allocates each output without an aggregate cap. A tiny input can therefore request disproportionate memory and cause memory pressure or process termination.
evidence: CVE.org primary record: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-48510 (state PUBLISHED; affected >=3.0,<3.1.7 and <2.5.301; fixed 3.1.7 and 2.5.301).
Vendor primary advisory: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/security/advisories/GHSA-v72x-2h86-7f8m (unbounded declared decompressed sizes for Lz4Block and Lz4BlockArray).

BIC and parent: git diff 23674873e020d8ce96e4bd2b87b3ed2856ce06fa bf5f2dd91bad2948063668de3703259f7562cf73 -- src/MessagePack.LZ4/LZ4MessagePackSerializer.cs; the condition flip first routes oversized declared length to new byte[length].

causal_research.bug_semantics: In @angular/ssr, Node incoming requests are converted to a Web Request via createRequestUrl. That helper used the WHATWG URL constructor as new URL(requestPath, `${protocol}://${hostnameWithPort}`). If requestPath (IncomingMessage.url, or later Express originalUrl) begins with // or \\, the constructor treats it as a scheme-relative URL and replaces the intended host with the attacker-controlled hostname while keeping the base scheme. The resulting Request.url becomes Angular SSR's virtual location (DOCUMENT / PlatformLocation). Any relative HttpClient/fetch during SSR then goes to that host, which is SSRF. Example: GET http://localhost:4200//attacker-domain.com/some-page makes HttpClient.get('assets/data.json') contact http://attacker-domain.com/assets/data.json.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When an app selects the ImageMagick CLI handler (imagick), ImageMagickHandler::_resize() and _text() build convert command strings by interpolating filesystem paths and text/options into a shell command, then process() executes that string with PHP exec(). Double-quote/single-quote wrapping does not neutralize backticks, $(...), or quote-breaking metacharacters in a user-supplied upload filename or text overlay. An attacker who can upload a crafted filename and trigger resize(), or pass crafted text/options to text(), injects OS commands as the web server user. Other methods (crop/rotate/flatten/flip/save) were already passed through escapeshellarg() before 4.6.2; the 4.6.2 patch applies the same escaping to the remaining resize and text operands.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In joserfc 1.3.4 and 1.4.0–1.4.1, compact/JSON JWS and JWE parsers call registry size validators before decoding. Those validators raise ExceededSizeError whose message interpolates the entire oversized raw segment (header!r, payload!r, signature!r, and the JWE ek/iv/ciphertext/tag equivalents). An attacker who can deliver a huge bearer token (absent or weak HTTP header limits) triggers jwt.decode()/deserialize_compact(); application logging or APM that records the exception then stores, ships, and processes a multi-copy of the attacker-controlled blob, amplifying disk/memory/CPU (CWE-770). The size check itself is intended DoS mitigation; the defect is embedding the rejected bytes in the exception text. jwe_zips.py ExceededSizeError is unaffected because it does not include the payload.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ZPan initialized its process-wide HS512 JWT helper with the public constant "123". A remote attacker who knows that repository-visible secret can sign a z-token whose subject and roles claim an administrator identity; LoginAuthWithRoles accepts the signature and then authorizes protected API routes from the attacker-controlled roles, bypassing password authentication.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 4fae6e2bdcab183ef59dd9f4055e2633ec2523f5 added the new user/token authentication subsystem. Its newly created internal/app/service/token.go made NewToken call jwtutil.Init("123") and used that same global helper to issue and verify RoleClaims; the same commit added the cookie-to-roles authentication middleware and protected-route role checks. The hard-coded signing key, rather than a per-installation secret, is therefore part of the original implementation of this authentication mechanism, not a later move or refactor of pre-existing vulnerable lines.

An all-history `git log -S 'jwtutil.Init("123")' --pickaxe-all --find-renames -- '*.go'` finds that addition, the later v2 reset removal, and the v1 security fix, with no earlier writer. The advisory package range is <1.6.6 with first patched version 1.6.6; tag v1.6.6 points exactly to 8662db8d4b06057631faf3deba4132e66705e947, whose sole parent is the v1.6.5 commit 33eec01e971f206356c76df79c4148e3f8d1752f. causal_research.bug_semantics: The published dssrf is_url_safe path accepted bracketed IPv6 SSRF targets. URL.hostname retained square brackets, so is_ipv6/ipaddr validation did not recognize the literal; even without that parsing miss, is_ip_internal classified only loopback, link-local, and unique-local IPv6 as internal, leaving IPv4-mapped/compatible, NAT64, SRv6, documentation, and deprecated site-local ranges allowed. The function then returned true when DNS resolution produced no blocking result, permitting access to internal or translated targets.
evidence: The advisory identifies npm dssrf < 1.0.3 as vulnerable and 1.0.3 as the first patched version, with PoCs spanning loopback, ULA, link-local, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, SRv6, documentation, site-local, and IPv4-compatible IPv6 literals.

At vulnerable mainline parent 5bf7d73e41bf2fb01e19f80cc16ac2bb6f8e7d7b, package.json is version 1.0.2 and dist/helpers.js passes parsed.hostname unchanged, while is_ip_internal blocks only loopback, linkLocal, and uniqueLocal IPv6 ranges.

Atomic fix member 49d6685fdebd19c05fe3ecde187f54f95ec15eba strips IPv6 brackets before validation, recursively checks IPv4-mapped/rfc6145 addresses, rejects every non-unicast IPv6 range, and explicitly blocks 64:ff9b:1::/48, 5f00::/8, 3fff::/20, and fec0::/10 in dist/helpers.js.

Mainline carrier 3b1236e9f5ab1d48a128198900938966ac422dd5 has an identical dist/helpers.js result to member 49d6685fdebd19c05fe3ecde187f54f95ec15eba and is an ancestor of HEAD; the member itself is not, establishing the PR member/carrier relationship.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In examples/acf-can/linux/acf-can-listener.c, num_can_msgs is a uint8_t assigned from int avtp_to_can(), which returns -1 on rejection (wrong subtype, stream-id mismatch, invalid ACF, failed Avtp_Can_IsValid, or EFF/CAN-ID inconsistency). The conversion truncates -1 to 255. The subsequent write loop then iterates 255 times over the 15-slot stack array frame_t can_frames[MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF] and write()s each slot to the CAN socket, leaking ~18 KB of adjacent stack as ~240 CAN frames. An unauthenticated UDP datagram with the default stream id 0xAABBCCDDEEFF0001 that later fails parsing is sufficient; no authentication exists on this path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: nltk.pathsec.urlopen first calls validate_network_url on the caller-supplied URL, which resolves the hostname in-process and rejects non-global IPs under ENFORCE. If urllib.request._opener has a non-empty ProxyHandler, or if no ProxyHandler is present and urllib.request.getproxies() is non-empty, urlopen sets proxied=True and does not install _SafeHTTPHandler/_SafeHTTPSHandler. Those handlers are the connect-time IP pin that makes validation and egress observe the same address. The opener then lets the proxy resolve and fetch. A public URL therefore passes local validation while the proxy can return loopback/internal HTTP. nltk.data.load and Downloader.index/download call this urlopen, so a forged index or ZIP can be parsed and installed. Direct non-proxied fetches still pin.

mechanism.impact: Internal-only HTTP resources can be read, forged downloader indexes parsed, and attacker-chosen package content installed from the proxy's network view; NLTK's SSRF validation is bypassed because the proxy resolves the name and performs the egress.
mechanism.preconditions: A proxy must be in effect for the request (environment proxy variables or an explicit ProxyHandler installed on urllib.request's global opener); the caller must treat pathsec as the SSRF barrier; the advisory's own negative control states that published 3.9.4 (pre proxy-handler inheritance, ce1d0ef99) did not reproduce.
mechanism.summary: A configured proxy makes nltk.pathsec.urlopen() delegate the fetch to the proxy while skipping the connect-time IP-pinning handlers (_SafeHTTPHandler/_SafeHTTPSHandler), so the pre-flight validate_network_url() check no longer reflects the actual egress destination. Traffic then reaches loopback/link-local/private services in the proxy's network view, leaking internal HTTP resources and forged downloader content (CWE-918, SSRF).
mechanism.trigger: A proxy is in effect for the request (environment proxy variables or a caller-installed ProxyHandler on urllib.request's global opener) and the caller relies on pathsec as the SSRF barrier: pathsec.urlopen() / nltk.data.load() / Downloader.index() / Downloader.download() fetch a URL whose local validation passes while the proxy resolves and routes the request to an internal target.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The attachment-approval path obtains the boards on which the authenticated user has approve_posts permission, but its per-attachment authorization predicate uses assignment rather than comparison: in 2.1, `$allowed_boards = array(0) || in_array(...)`, and in 3.0, `$allowed_boards = [0] || \in_array(...)`. Because `||` binds more tightly than `=`, the non-empty array on the left of `||` is truthy, the membership test is short-circuited, and boolean true is assigned to `$allowed_boards`; every queried pending attachment therefore passes the guard. A low-privileged authenticated user can approve, reject, or delete pending attachments on boards where that user lacks approve_posts.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Xinference model loaders invoke Hugging Face AutoTokenizer/from_pretrained (and sentence-transformers/FlagEmbedding equivalents) with trust_remote_code hardcoded or defaulted to True, so a model directory can execute its own modeling_*.py via tokenizer_config.json/config.json auto_map. Five sibling sites (SentenceTransformer rerank/embedding load, FlagEmbedding load, PytorchModel._sanitize_model_config setdefault True, and PytorchModel._get_components default True) independently enable the same remote-code flag. Before 2.12.0 there was no operator opt-out; 2.12.0 gates generic loaders with XINFERENCE_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE (default off) and allow_trust_remote_code(model_family) so only bundled is_builtin families keep remote code.

causal_research.bug_semantics: PhpSpreadsheet HTML Writer XSS via NumberFormat @ text substitution. Writer/Html.php formats a cell with NumberFormat::toFormattedString(..., [$this,'formatColor']) and applies htmlspecialchars only when the formatted string strictly equals the original cell value. Html::formatColor htmlspecialchars-escapes its argument, but only if the formatter actually invokes the callback. Commit edc003ad1 added an early return for single-section masks containing @: it substituted the raw cell value into the mask (including extra literals such as 'Hello @', '@ "items"', '. @') and returned without calling $callBack. The formatted result then differed from $origData, so the Html.php htmlspecialchars gate was also skipped, and attacker-controlled markup from a crafted spreadsheet reached generateHTMLAll() output. A 2026-04-05 incomplete patch invoked the callback only on quoted-literal @ masks; unquoted extra literals stayed unsanitized until the 2026-04-18 callback on the unquoted path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated CWE-434 RCE via POST /admin/tinymce/upload (admin.tinymce.upload). TinyMCEController::storeMedia() accepted any uploaded file, stored it on Laravel's default public disk under tinymce/, and returned Storage::url() so the file was web-reachable. No MIME/extension allowlist existed. At introduction the sink was $file->store('tinymce') (Laravel hashName/guessExtension); libmagic reports a PHP one-liner as text/x-php, so a crafted .php payload was persisted as a public .php object. On 2.2.x (including PoC commit ba25b7e7) the same sink used getClientOriginalExtension() plus storeAs, so the client-supplied .php suffix was kept even if Content-Type was spoofed as image/jpeg. Bouncer exempts this route from ACL, so any logged-in staff user can upload a webshell and execute it with a GET to /storage/tinymce/<file>.php.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CanInstall is global middleware and recognizes an installed application, but e050c9d66656ae50fe208f4ce0a91c2f5956c77d made that protection conditional on the request not being classified as AJAX. Because the classification is controlled by an HTTP header rather than authentication, an unauthenticated caller can make an AJAX-classified request to /install/api/admin-config-setup. That route removes the web middleware and invokes adminConfigSetup, whose database sink writes the id=1 administrator credentials from request input.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CipAppPath::deserialize_symbolic trusts a symbolic-segment header's self-declared length and copies that many bytes from the current input pointer without checking remaining readable size. CipMessageRouterRequest::DeserializeMRReq (and historically InitRequest) only validates the outer path word-count (path_size = word_count*2) and then hands a 2-byte BufReader/limit to the app-path parser. A remote unconnected SendRRData Message Router request with body 0e 01 7f 41 therefore passes the outer check (path word count 1 → 2 path bytes 7f 41) while first=0x7f yields symbol_size=31; after consuming the header only 1 byte remains and memcpy/pointer-walk reads past the path window into/beyond the global TCP receive buffer s_buf. The same unbounded copy exists on the ANSI Extended Symbol branch. Demonstrated impact is a remotely triggerable out-of-bounds read / ASan global-buffer-overflow DoS on the official POSIX sample (CWE-125/CWE-119).

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-552 information exposure: Tainacan stores item documents under the web-accessible WordPress uploads tree at wp-content/uploads/tainacan-items/{collection_id}/{item_id}/. When an item or collection is not public, only the on-disk folder name is prefixed with the constant _x_ (TAINACAN_PRIVATE_FOLDER_PREFIX); wp_get_attachment_url / image_get_intermediate_size strip that prefix so the published URL looks like a normal uploads path. Unauthenticated attackers who request the real _x_ path (collection/item IDs are already in the public URL; the prefix is a known constant) are served the file directly by Apache/nginx because nothing at the web-server layer denied _x_ directories until 1.0.1. At 1.0.0, add_htaccess_rules() only wrote Deny from all into uploads/tainacan (logs/csv), not uploads/tainacan-items.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An ASP.NET Core MVC MessagePackInputFormatter consumes context.HttpContext.Request.Body, an HTTP-controlled byte stream, and deserializes it using the formatter's implicit default when the parameterless constructor is selected. A request body targeting dictionary-like model properties can therefore retain attacker-controlled hash collisions and consume excessive CPU; UntrustedData selects collision-resistant comparers at this boundary.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: getDiff.js treated commitFrom == 0000...0 as a brand-new branch and diffed the pushed commits against the empty tree (4b825dc...), so a new branch b cut from an unapproved commit on branch a could be approved on b and later pushed back to a without that parent-lineage commit ever being policy-checked (advisory GHSA-39p2-8hq9-fwj6, CVE-2025-54585: 'new branch approval exploit'; getDiff.ts and parsePush.ts both zero-SHA branches named). BIC vs parent: 879e26c8 (grovesy, 2020-10-12, 'working on diffs on new branches') is the first commit that creates the zero-SHA branch: its only change is getDiff.js, and its new code 'if (action.commitFrom == 0000...0) { if (commitData[0].parent != 0000...0) cmd = git diff <parent> <commitTo> } else cmd = git diff <commitFrom> <commitTo>' is exactly the advisory-named zero-SHA handling; parent b9e1dc8 (2020-10-12) always used the empty-tree fallback 'git diff 4b825dc... HEAD' for new branches, which ignores commitFrom/commitTo but has no parent-boundary branch. Follow-up 66285509 (same day, same author) changed commitData[0].parent to commitData[len-1].parent in getDiff and made parsePush set commitFrom = last-commit parent on zero SHA; both zero-SHA branches existed on main by v1.0.0, so the advisory-specific parent-boundary mechanism was active in all affected releases. Minimum fix vs parent boundary: the shipped fix is the security merge a620a2f3 (Thomas Cooper, 2025-07-30, 'Merge commit from fork / fix: all vulnerability issues'), 53 commits, first parents d4d9239a -> 60e77d1c, shipped in 1.19.2 (12fce21a is the version bump; tags v1.19.2+ and v2.0.0 contain it). The advisory-specific minimum fix for the push-path exploit is the pairing 9c1449f4 (fabiovincenzi, 2025-05-16, 'feat: add check for hidden commits', no AI trailers) + 1fd86acb (newIdxFiles tracking) + 87f73b4f: checkHiddenCommits is inserted into the push chain (chain.ts: parsePush ... writePack, checkHiddenCommits, ... getDiff) and blocks any pack whose commits are outside the introduced range, which directly closes the 'unapproved commit smuggled via child branch' hole, including for paths the old getDiff branch did not flag. The getDiff.ts change is only the adjacent clearer branch: on zero SHA it now sets commitFrom = action.commitData[len-1].parent and diffs commitFrom..commitTo, matching the advisory wording that commits on branch a now require approval, but by itself it does not cover every contributing path (parsePush also normalizes zero-SHA commitFrom to the last parent at a620a2f3: parsePush.ts lines 93-94, getMissingData.ts mirrors it for fast-forward refs, and checkHiddenCommits relies on the normalized boundary), so treating the getDiff hunk alone as full coverage is not supported. causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated admin-controlled HTTP type query parameter reached ProductController::view without allowlist validation. The shared reporting Blade view concatenated that value into a translation expression located inside a Vue text/x-template. For an unknown key containing template syntax such as {{7*7}}, the syntax survived server rendering into the client-side runtime-compiled template and was evaluated there; the vendor classified this as SSTI with possible code execution. Restricting type to the controller's known function keys before rendering closes the source-to-sink path.
evidence: Official CVE record: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-21450 (PUBLISHED; affected <2.3.10; fixed in 2.3.10).
Vendor advisory: https://github.com/bagisto/bagisto/security/advisories/GHSA-9hvg-qw5q-wqwp (type={{7*7}} reproducer; not withdrawn).

BIC: https://github.com/bagisto/bagisto/commit/71b8aa0a2280294a383cbbd834045f94c9d8c5f3; parent 75a47568006720d3b7b153181b269d56edae0aec; exact parent/BIC blobs independently hash to the object IDs in their local trees.
Direct fix: https://github.com/bagisto/bagisto/commit/b1b276a34bc8413bb64fabcb7fb35f2b36144864 adds the pre-render type allowlist guard.
Advisory fix: https://github.com/bagisto/bagisto/commit/3f294b4837595929107d9c1bbd6d5b1222ef9fea centralizes and broadens type validation.
Release: https://github.com/bagisto/bagisto/releases/tag/v2.3.10; local ancestry verifies v2.3.9 contains the BIC without the direct fix and v2.3.10 contains the BIC plus both fix commits.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Stored XSS through the admin appearance logo uploader. POST /admin accepts logoNavbar and logoLogin as FileType fields constrained only with Symfony Image() (no mime-type allowlist) and HTML accept=image/*. FileUploaderService then writes the file under public/uploads using UploadedFile::guessExtension(), so a script-bearing SVG is stored as logo-navbar.svg or logo-login.svg and served as a static document. Direct GET of /uploads/logo-navbar.svg?_=<id> or /uploads/logo-login.svg?_=<id> executes the embedded script in the visitor's browser. The PoC SVG is <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" fill="none"><script>alert(...)</script></svg>. CVSS lists PR:H (admin session required to upload); the GHSA/CVE named range is NovoSGA <= 2.2.9.

causal_research.bug_semantics: In applyNaive (pkg/archive/tar.go), image unpack previously called fs.RootPath live for every tar entry so parent paths were re-walked and re-bounded to the unpack root. CVE-2025-47290 is a sequential TOCTOU (CWE-367) introduced when those RootPath results were memoized in cachedRootPath.get: after the first walk of a parent path, later entries reuse the cached lexical path and then create/link through it. A crafted layer can create a directory, have its resolved path cached as in-root, replace that directory with a symlink (or otherwise mutate the tree), and then unpack further names under the stale cached parent so kernel path resolution follows the symlink out of the unpack root onto the host filesystem. The same cache is used by hardlinkRootPath. Only containerd v2.1.0 is affected; v2.1.1 restores per-entry fs.RootPath.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2025-47290 state=PUBLISHED (CNA GitHub_M, datePublished 2025-05-20); not rejected/withdrawn. GHSA-cm76-qm8v-3j95 withdrawn_at=null. Vendor: only v2.1.0 affected, patched in v2.1.1. CWE-367.

causal_research.bug_semantics: FluentCMS File Management stores uploaded SVG bytes unsanitized and later serves them with the client-supplied MIME type image/svg+xml. FileController.Upload copies formFile.ContentType and the raw stream into FileService.Create, which persists via fileStorageProvider.Upload with no SVG sanitization. causal_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS replace_first performs first-occurrence substitution by delegating to JavaScript String.prototype.replace (originally lodash _.replace, which is native String#replace). A string replacement is therefore a JS replacement pattern: $& expands to the entire matched substring, and $` / $' expand similarly. After memoryLimit landed, the filter charged only the input length (later input+args), never the expanded output. An attacker who can supply a Liquid template can chain assign plus replace_first with a replacement of many $& tokens, amplifying a 1-byte string through ~50x stages to hundreds of megabytes while the limiter records only the unamplified inputs, causing heap growth and event-loop DoS. Sibling replace uses split/join (literal $&) and replace_last uses substring, so only replace_first has this expansion path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: xml.etree.ElementTree honors <!ENTITY> declarations in a document's internal DTD subset. On NLTK <= 3.10.2, six remaining call sites still invoked that parser directly: nltk.internals.ElementWrapper.__init__ (ElementTree.fromstring on any string argument), nltk.chunk.named_entity.load_ace_file (ET.parse of ACE annotation XML), and nltk.downloader Package.fromxml, Collection.fromxml, _find_collections, and _find_packages (ElementTree.parse of package/collection XML). A crafted few-hundred-byte payload with nested entities expands by 10x per nesting level into megabytes of in-process memory (CWE-776). Preconditions: the attacker must supply the XML that those entry points parse (ElementWrapper string, ACE .xml beside a .sgm, or downloader package/collection XML). External entities are not resolved, so this is memory-amplification DoS rather than XXE disclosure. libexpat 2.6.0+ may cap expansion only above ~8 MiB and only when the interpreter's libexpat is new enough; NLTK itself imposed no cap at these sites.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated user who can create or execute a workflow configures the Edit Fields (Set) node with a field name that is a dot-notation path into an inherited built-in, e.g. toString.call. With dot-notation enabled (the default), configureFieldHelper/SetV1 forwards that name to lodash/set. Unpatched baseSet treats an inherited function such as Object.prototype.toString as the nested object because isObject(objValue) is true, then writes the next segment onto that shared function (toString.call = attacker value). The overwritten global is later used on the request-authentication path, so every authenticated request fails with a process-wide 500 until n8n is restarted. The 2026 pnpm patch changes baseSet to reuse a nested value only when it is an own property, so inherited method paths are stored as plain own data on the item instead of mutating builtins.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Mechanism: the plugin ships a Vite dev-server middleware (apply: serve; wired in configureServer in src/serve.ts; no build path). Commit d9cd9ba6 (Fix: directory copy not working during dev, 2022-04-06, sapphi-red <green@sapphi.red>) added a second lookup loop to viaLocal() in src/middleware.ts: for the first fileMap directory key that the request URI starts with, it returns resolve(root, val.src, uri.slice(dir.length)) and serves it via statSync/toHeaders. uri derives from the raw request URL with only decodeURIComponent, query/import stripping, and leading-slash trimming, so traversal segments such as ../ or %2e%2e%2f reach uri.slice(dir.length); resolve() then normalizes them outside val.src, and the result is served without any containment check. causal_research.bug_semantics: GHSA-j934-vjh5-vf9r / CVE-2025-47110 is a published, still-open Adobe CNA record (withdrawn None, published 2025-06-10): stored XSS (CWE-79, CRITICAL, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H) reached through Magento email/CMS template rendering. The defect lives in Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::blockDirective(): a {{block}} directive creates a layout block, copies every remaining directive parameter onto it through the setDataUsingMethod($k, $v) loop, and renders it, but never pins a cache key; AbstractBlock::getCacheKey() selects the block-HTML cache entry from cache_key data (CUSTOM_BLOCK_ prefix) or falls back to a key derived from getCacheKeyInfo() plus the crypt key, so blocks that expose a stable key tuple share one cache entry regardless of injected parameters and attacker markup stored through directive parameters is served from that shared entry to later sessions (mechanism as recorded by the round14 independent audit w196 and the round17 row; the first-party reads above show the exact loop the fix changes and the getCacheKey() contract it depends on). The smallest public write of that loop is the import commit 4bdbf6b6 (2011-12-02, mage2-team, Merged commits from the original repository.): git log --diff-filter=A shows it as the sole addition of the historical core path app/code/core/Mage/Core/Model/Email/Template/Filter.php, that blob contains blockDirective with the parameter loop at line 172 and zero cache_key handling, and its parent be09cb92 contains only LICENSE.txt, so no earlier in-tree copy exists (parent_absent true; later commits, such as the 2013 module consolidation, keep moving the same loop rather than introducing it). The fix b535da75 (2025-05-20, Binh Tran, committer Nishant Rana, AC-14694:: Update template rendering) adds exactly the missing pin - if (!$block->hasData(cache_key)) { $block->setDataUsingMethod(cache_key, $block->getCacheKey()); } - with a unit test covering both branches, and the guard string appears in every tag the advisory lists as fixed (2.4.8-p1, 2.4.7-p6, 2.4.6-p11, 2.4.5-p13, 2.4.9-alpha1/2, 2.4.9) and in none of its affected tags (2.4.8, 2.4.7-p5, 2.4.6-p10, 2.4.5-p12, 2.4.4, 2.4.4-p13); 2.4.8 carries the fix's parent blob and 2.4.8-p1 carries the post-fix blob f86deaca, so the fixed-version claim holds by content even though tag containment reaches only 2.4.9*. The fix b535da75 (2025-05-20, Binh Tran, committer Nishant Rana, AC-14694:: Update template rendering) adds exactly the missing pin - if (!$block->hasData(cache_key)) { $block->setDataUsingMethod(cache_key, $block->getCacheKey()); } - with a unit test covering both branches, and the guard string appears in every tag the advisory lists as fixed (2.4.8-p1, 2.4.7-p6, 2.4.6-p11, 2.4.5-p13, 2.4.9-alpha1/2, 2.4.9) and in none of its affected tags (2.4.8, 2.4.7-p5, 2.4.6-p10, 2.4.5-p12, 2.4.4, 2.4.4-p13); 2.4.8 carries the fix's parent blob and 2.4.8-p1 carries the post-fix blob f86deaca, so the fixed-version claim holds by content even though tag containment reaches only 2.4.9*. Both objects of the pair are human-authored with no AI trailer (the import predates LLM tooling; the 2025 fix is an Adobe engineer's commit reviewed by a second Adobe account), in a repository whose recent history does carry Cursor/Claude/Copilot trailers, so the record is NOT_AI with ai_hunk FAIL because the candidate hunk is a human 2011 core-team write.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Client-side heap OOB write in smb2_add_iovector(): it stores into v->iov[v->niov] and increments niov with no upper bound against the fixed array iov[SMB2_MAX_VECTORS] (256). On receive, a compound SMB2 response with NextCommand set keeps the same smb2->in vector set, appending header/fixed/variable/pad iovecs for each chained PDU and then, when is_chained, adding another header and looping via goto read_more_data without resetting niov. A malicious server can therefore drive niov past 256 and write adjacent heap. SMB2_OPLOCK_BREAK notifications with message_id 0xffffffffffffffff skip smb2_find_pdu(), so the chain need not match outstanding request IDs; that is an exploitability amplifier, not the overflow sink. Unauthenticated remote DoS / potential RCE against a libsmb2 client.

causal_research.bug_semantics: phpseclib Net_SSH2/_get_binary_packet() and later SSH2::get_binary_packet() compared a received SSH MAC/HMAC against the locally computed tag with PHP != (and, after 2019, the same != on the UMAC branch). Every non-AEAD post-KEX packet hits this path; a mismatch disconnects, so the leak is one sample per connection against a fresh session key and is Low/defense-in-depth rather than a practical remote oracle.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The navigation endpoint loaded administrator-controlled NAV_ITEM_* values from configuration and rendered each value as a clickable href without validating its URL scheme. A javascript: value therefore survived HTML escaping and executed in another authenticated user's browser when clicked, producing stored XSS.
evidence: The GitHub PR #113 commits API exposes exactly one member, a43333496010cfe8e10ea2397e389029e32d4e0a, with parent 37d32d2cba3921c4afbcfb0e0c2c641f12bbc697. Its patch adds Nav.java loading NAV_ITEM_* via findStringMatchMap and changes emissary_nav.js to append '<a ... href="'+link+'">' for every returned navItems value.

The parent 37d32d2cba3921c4afbcfb0e0c2c641f12bbc697 version of emissary_nav.js contains only hard-coded site-relative href values and no NAV_ITEM_* configuration source or /api/nav-driven link insertion.

The squash commit 3d867c96f0a160e87cb854ec0bd53e53c393cf93 has the same vulnerable change, while 52d54de57e69798b163119daf1052904f56e90ad later moves the already-vulnerable behavior into NavAction.java and nav.mustache; neither is the atomic first-write BIC.

The BIC member's author and committer are dev-mlb, its message is 'generate nav using config files', and its metadata and message contain no Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, OpenAI, Anthropic, generated-by, AI-assisted, or AI-bot marker.

Commit e2078417464b9004620dde28dcbca2f73ea06c13 directly fixes the source-to-sink path by filtering configured links through an allowlist that accepts only http://, https://, or site-relative URLs before constructing NavItem values; it also adds rel="noopener noreferrer" as defense in depth and tests rejected javascript: and ftp: schemes.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ZeroBrew's Ruby formula compatibility shim downloaded secondary formula resources and URL-based patches with curl and then extracted or applied them during `zb install --build-from-source` without ever comparing the bytes to the sha256 values the formula DSL had already parsed. A network attacker who can substitute those URLs (MITM or compromised host) can inject attacker-controlled archives or diffs that execute as build steps with no integrity warning. Primary formula tarballs in zb_io/src/build/source.rs already verified SHA-256; only the shim resource/patch paths omitted the check. CWE-494.

Verified in local clone netty__netty: BIC 4ac032c6 (2008-11-19, Trustin Lee, 'Merged the HTTP branch into the trunk', single parent e29ba2ee) is the first write of HttpMessageDecoder with READ_CHUNK_SIZE - the parent has no HTTP codec at all, so the vulnerable stop-at-first-CR/LF line reader is born here. Later 2009 commits (44498e06, 66423e0c) added semicolon extension delimiters but still terminated at the first CRLF; the 2013 HttpObjectDecoder overhaul b7de8680 is a rewrite/move of the same pattern, not the origin. Direct fix 60e53c99 (2026-03-24, Chris Vest, 'Stricter HTTP/1.1 chunk extension parsing (#16537)', parent 9f47a7b6) introduces HttpChunkLineValidatingByteProcessor, the first code that rejects illegal bytes (including CR/LF) inside chunk-ext. Release boundary by tag ancestry: earliest Netty tags containing the fix are netty-4.1.132.Final and later 4.1.x line (4.1.131 and earlier do not contain it). OSV SHAs 4cc98736/ec119d48 are release tags, not the parser change. causal_research.bug_semantics: When the opt-in Management API is enabled with its token left empty, its authentication middleware treats the empty secret as successful authentication. The server listens on all interfaces at port 9820, and an unauthenticated remote POST to /api/v1/cron can copy attacker-controlled JSON exec text into a persisted CronJob. The cron scheduler identifies a nonempty Exec as a shell job and ultimately runs that text through the configured shell, so the attacker obtains command execution when the job fires; later code also added an immediate /api/v1/cron/{id}/exec trigger, but that was not necessary for the original scheduled-execution path.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable trust-boundary crossing was created in one change: c2681402a7686294174a263e31245a52d4fea380 added the network-facing Management API, deliberately made authenticate return true for an empty token, registered the cron endpoints behind that fail-open middleware, and assigned untrusted req.Exec directly to CronJob.Exec. The shell-capable CronJob and its sh -c execution sink already existed in the parent; c2681402 is the smallest commit that made that sink reachable from an unauthenticated remote management request.

causal_research.bug_semantics: openssl_encrypt/modules/pqc.py is the post-quantum KEM/hybrid-encryption module. causal_research.bug_semantics: find-my-way lookup() forwards unsanitized req.method into find(), which does currentNode = this.trees[method] on a prototype-bearing object (this.trees = {}). Inherited keys such as constructor, toString, and __proto__ therefore resolve to Object.prototype properties instead of undefined. The truthy/undefined checks do not reject those values, so find() treats Function or Object.prototype as a radix node and throws when reading currentNode.prefix.length (originally split as prefix = currentNode.prefix; prefixLen = prefix.length). HTTP/2 is the remote trigger because Node's HTTP/2 :method is not restricted to http.METHODS the way HTTP/1 is. Route registration (on/off) does assert http.METHODS, but the request path never did.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A malicious relay can supply concatenated gzip or zlib members to Tor's directory decompression path. tor_compress_impl() retains the cumulative output buffer but frees and recreates the backend state whenever one member returns TOR_COMPRESS_DONE with input remaining. causal_research.bug_semantics: devalue.parse JSON.parses a payload into a values array, then unflatten/hydrate walks it. Plain-object records are rebuilt with `for (const key in value) { object[key] = hydrate(value[key]); }` on a normal `{}`. A crafted key `__proto__` therefore hits Object.prototype.__proto__ and installs a new prototype, so later own properties (including getters such as magnitude in the GHSA Vector PoC) can be overwritten. Property values that are strings rather than numeric indices are passed to hydrate; because hydrate used `index in hydrated` / `values[index]` on an Array without requiring typeof index === 'number', strings such as `push` or `toString` resolve to Array.prototype methods and get assigned onto the revived object (GHSA PoC `[{ "toString":"push" }]`). Attacker-controlled serialized input is the source; polluted prototypes and hijacked methods on the parsed object are the sink (CWE-1321).

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS pop (src/filters/array.ts) clones its input with [...toArray(v)] and returns clone.pop() without charging this.context.memoryLimit.use(...). causal_research.flaw_origin: Smallest first writer of the leaky getters is PR #258 member 49bc8658e5fdda3f0b384d6eb130be7aacf83fc1 (2018-08-08), which added User::getApiToken()/getPlainApiToken() while invoice Twig already received Timesheet User objects via model.entries. Parent a7780dac lacks those methods. GitHub squash 2f84f375 landed that PR on master. The 2026 DefaultPolicy denylist (686473c / 2.46) and StrictPolicy move (aa9bc72 / 2.47) copied an incomplete secret list and left getApiToken allowed; they are incomplete remediation and a move, not the original introduction.
causal_research.flip_condition: A first-party record binding the introducing object 49bc8658e5 to an AI tool (an AI trailer, an agent or bot author, or a disclosure on that commit or its PR) would change this verdict; the commit object, the clone history and the advisory carry none.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked (1) getPlainApiToken() is a transient getter usually returning null, so the leak is the hash from getApiToken() only; (2) the blocklist is effective for invoice rendering in 2.46 because InvoicePolicy was changed to consult DefaultPolicy before its getter short-circuit, and the renderer still used InvoicePolicy at 6a86afb5f; (3) no older api-token blocklist exists anywhere in history - the pre-2.46 DefaultPolicy body was empty and InvoicePolicy returned early for every get*/is*/has* method, so unrestricted getter access predates the blocklist (it is older than, not introduced by, the omission); (4) the fix's substring tests match both accessor names, so no residual path through these two methods remains.
mechanism.impact: Disclosure of the user's stored API password hash (bcrypt/sodium) into invoice output (HTML/PDF served or mailed by the installation); the plaintext cannot be recovered directly but the hash enables offline cracking, and getPlainApiToken() is a normally-null transient setter field so it adds no further data.
mechanism.preconditions: OnPremise installation with invoice-template upload active; attacker holds ROLE_ADMIN plus manage_invoice_template; the victim must have configured an API password/token; the sandbox must be the only barrier, i.e. no other review of uploaded templates (the advisory notes the Kimai cloud does not allow template upload).
mechanism.summary: An admin with manage_invoice_template embeds {{ model.user.getApiToken() }} in an invoice template; the invoice Twig sandbox enforces only the enumerated user-secret blocklist in StrictPolicy::checkMethodAllowed(), which omits getapitoken/getplainapitoken, so every invoice later generated from that template renders the generating user's stored API token hash.
mechanism.trigger: An admin who can upload/edit invoice templates stores a template containing a call such as {{ model.user.getApiToken() }} (the advisory's repro); a user who is then invoiced through that template (or generates the invoice) has the resolved User object passed into the sandboxed render, and the sandbox allows the call.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: src/Twig/SecurityPolicy/StrictPolicy.php:155-157 checkMethodAllowed (App\Twig\SecurityPolicy\StrictPolicy) at tag 2.52.0 (cad9f587033945bfc748c318ec9d2ea0dba4f0ce); identical text at the pre-fix main head fe4185ae45fc6663c7e12bd706250d20336b980f.

causal_research.reasoning:
The advisory is a real residual information leak: invoice Twig can invoke User::getApiToken() because the sandbox User-secret denylist never named it until 2.53.0. The original introducing change is the 2018 addition of those getters onto User while invoice Twig already exposed User objects; the 2026 denylist is incomplete remediation of a pre-existing leak, and StrictPolicy is a later move of the same list. Both the BIC commit object and the minimum fix commit object are named-human Kevin Papst with no commit-object AI markers. That is NOT_AI, not FALSE_POSITIVE, and not an evidence gap: parent-tree absence, squash decomposition, affected 2.52.0 membership, and fixed 2.53.0 membership all verified from the local clone plus GitHub HTML/patch pages.
The invoice Twig sandbox lets a template call getApiToken() and getPlainApiToken() on the User object exposed as model.user, because the user-secret method blocklist in src/Twig/SecurityPolicy/StrictPolicy.php:156 enumerates only getpassword/gettotpsecret/getplainpassword/getconfirmationtoken/gettotpauthenticationconfiguration and omits both api-token accessors; getApiToken() then renders the stored bcrypt/sodium hash of the invoice creator's API password into the invoice. I confirmed the vulnerable list at tag 2.52.0 (cad9f587033945bfc748c318ec9d2ea0dba4f0ce) and traced the list to 6a86afb5fd79f6c1825060b87c09bd1909c2e86f (Release 2.46, PR #5757), whose parent 9e87fc131b7bf757986afc85f18396cf75d7a7ca has an empty DefaultPolicy::checkMethodAllowed and therefore no blocklist at all. The 2.47 file creation of StrictPolicy.php (d429c566876f3ac384e46270fc15c0cd29886401) moves the same list out of DefaultPolicy, so it is a consolidation, not the introduction. The repair lands in 999d820d4ca1fb3bb83395ad9bfc73d73b5eb04a (tag 2.53.0) via the dedicated commit f8457e7428688e204a57b33a56eeda5b1c15af61, which replaces the enumerated list with str_contains checks on password/totp/api/secret/token and adds getApiToken plus getPlainApiToken to the blocked-method assertions, closing both methods named by the advisory. Verdict NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The unauthenticated Monitor Agent HTTP API accepted attacker-controlled debug=1 or with_ivars query parameters and serialized loaded plugins' internal instance variables. A network client able to reach the default port 24220 could therefore retrieve secrets such as database passwords, API keys, or cloud credentials held by plugins.
evidence: The GitHub security advisory GHSA-pr7j-96cj-549h identifies CVE-2026-44025, affected fluentd versions <= 1.19.2, patched version 1.19.3, and unauthenticated disclosure of plugin instance variables through /api/plugins.json and related Monitor Agent endpoints.

git show fe73c272eed3c512c9ac31c0408c7c5e4d280451 shows the BIC deleting the configured debug_mode gate and adding query-string debug handling that sets opts[:with_debug_info] before plugin_info methods serialize instance variables.

git show of parent d7b53295286ab8cd23056e02562ca312264521e6 shows that instance-variable serialization existed only behind the agent's configured debug_mode; the request query did not control that gate.

git cat-file and rev-list show fe73c272eed3c512c9ac31c0408c7c5e4d280451 is a normal one-parent public commit, not a merge or squash aggregate; its sole parent is d7b53295286ab8cd23056e02562ca312264521e6.
Tag topology shows v0.10.32 does not contain the BIC while v0.10.34 does; v1.19.2 contains the vulnerable path. The advisory independently declares the supported affected boundary as <= 1.19.2.

Direct fix 990921518971699b9a97441970674d1800e29177 changes include_config and include_retry defaults to false, adds include_debug_info default false, ignores debug/with_ivars unless that server-side option is enabled, and adds regression tests for both disabled and explicitly enabled behavior.

GitHub PR #5392 records one source commit, 30fbbd74bccc5824b81a04fac197fb531512f106, merged as 990921518971699b9a97441970674d1800e29177 into v1.19; tag v1.19.2 excludes the merged fix and tag v1.19.3 contains it and lists #5392 in its release notes.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit fe73c272eed3c512c9ac31c0408c7c5e4d280451 moved the debug-mode decision from trusted server configuration into each HTTP request's query string and propagated with_debug_info into plugin serialization. Its parent required an operator-set debug configuration, so fe73c272eed3c512c9ac31c0408c7c5e4d280451 is the smallest public commit that first granted an unauthenticated requester control over the sensitive instance-variable export.
causal_research.reasoning: This is a real information-disclosure vulnerability, not a withdrawn or rejected advisory. The vulnerable capability is not merely the serializer introduced with the plugin: in the immediate parent, an operator had to enable debug mode in configuration. The BIC is fe73c272eed3c512c9ac31c0408c7c5e4d280451 because it first made the sensitive export remotely selectable through an unauthenticated query parameter while the service defaulted to 0.0.0.0. Later commits copied, refactored, or extended the same mechanism (including with_ivars) but did not first introduce it. The BIC is an atomic single-parent 2013 commit with only conventional human author/committer metadata and no AI marker, so AI causation is excluded and the verdict is NOT_AI. The v1.19 backport 990921518971699b9a97441970674d1800e29177 directly closes the path by restoring a server-side opt-in gate and ships in v1.19.3, matching the advisory's affected and patched boundaries.

causal_research.bug_semantics: FormFields.add() in @adonisjs/bodyparser copies unauthenticated multipart field names into lodash.set/get via @poppinss/utils. CVE-2026-25754 / GHSA-f5x2-vj4h-vg4c was 'fixed' by changing the root store from {} to Object.create(null), which only stops first-segment payloads such as __proto__.polluted and constructor.prototype.polluted. lodash.set still materializes intermediate objects as plain {}, so nested keys (user.__proto__.polluted, user[__proto__][polluted], user.constructor.prototype.polluted2) write onto Object.prototype process-wide. Any route behind BodyParserMiddleware that accepts multipart/form-data is an unauthenticated remote sink. Affected published ranges are >=10.1.3 <10.1.5 and >=11.0.0-next.9 <11.0.3; v11.0.2 still carries Object.create(null) without path-segment rejection even though the GHSA text stops at 11.0.1. causal_research.bug_semantics: Malformed LAN-local mDNS packets reach DNSIncoming name decoding. The exception-dedup path keyed a process-lifetime dictionary by attacker-varying exception text and stored the full sys.exc_info() triple; each retained traceback kept frame locals including the raw packet buffer, so unique malformed packets caused unbounded memory growth and eventual denial of service.

git grep against parent 94570b730aaab606db820b9c4d48b1c313fdaa98 finds none of _seen_exceptions, sys.exc_info, or log_exception_warning; the parent constructs DNSIncoming without this retention path.

causal_research.reasoning: The vulnerability is real and the complete source-to-sink lifecycle closes locally. The smallest public commit that created the retained-traceback dedup mechanism is 061a2aa3c6e8a7c954a313c8a7d396f26f544c2b, not later moves, logging-level changes, or additions of self.source to error strings. causal_research.bug_semantics: Preact distinguishes genuine VNodes by giving them an own constructor value of undefined. In the affected client renderer, the gate became `if (newVNode.constructor != UNDEFINED) return NULL`; JavaScript loose equality treats null and undefined as equal, so a JSON-parsed attacker object shaped as a VNode and carrying `constructor: null` passes the gate. If an application passes that unsanitized object into the render tree, Preact consumes its attacker-controlled type and props as a VNode and can inject HTML, with script execution possible where CSP or other defenses do not stop it. The companion loose `childVNode.constructor == UNDEFINED` check also admits null as the VNode sentinel in child processing. The server-side preact-render-to-string path was not affected.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The smallest first-writer is PR #4723 member 017ac5e370c9198b12b61818279eb84f221d7747, a byte-golfing refactor that changed the JSON-injection guard in src/diff/index.js from strict `!== UNDEFINED` to loose `!= UNDEFINED` and the VNode child check in src/diff/children.js from strict `=== UNDEFINED` to loose `== UNDEFINED`. Its second member 7ed5aeb0246305e3b42e314c1a59bcaa405e6a8c restored three unrelated strict comparisons but retained both vulnerable changes; GitHub then squash-merged the resulting tree as a69aada2799626d3afbfc1eb6550611ca2444a4d. An older loose isValidElement check alone was not sufficient because the strict renderer gate still rejected forged JSON objects; 017ac5e370c9198b12b61818279eb84f221d7747 is the first commit that softened the enforcement point and made the advisory's render path exploitable.

causal_research.bug_semantics: devalue.uneval serializes a value to JavaScript source that callers eval to rehydrate it. For plain objects it walks enumerable own keys and emits them as unquoted identifiers via safe_key/safe_prop whenever they match /^[_$a-zA-Z][_$a-zA-Z0-9]*$/. An attacker-controlled object can carry an own enumerable `__proto__` key (JSON.parse('{"__proto__": <payload>}')), which passes that regex. The generated code is therefore `{__proto__:<payload>}` for a non-repeated object or `name.__proto__=<payload>` for a repeated one. Evaluated as JS, those forms are prototype setters, not own-property writes: the reconstituted object lacks the own `__proto__` key and instead has a polluted [[Prototype]]. That is CWE-1321 and matches the advisory (output shape differs from input). The 5.6.3 fix fails closed by throwing DevalueError before emission when any own key is `__proto__`.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated users who can run Code-node JavaScript in the n8n JS task runner execute inside node:vm against host prototypes. The runner injects a require resolver; when a host builtin such as crypto is allowlisted (official runners image sets NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto), user code loads a host EventEmitter subclass (crypto.createHash), then uses the host module constructor's getPrototypeOf (crypto.constructor.getPrototypeOf) to bypass the VM's shimmed Object.getPrototypeOf and walk to EventEmitter.prototype. That prototype is not on globalThis, so the freeze loop that only freezes globalThis functions leaves emit/on/once/addListener/prependListener/prependOnceListener writable. process inherits those methods, so overriding them intercepts host process.emit, hands the attacker process, and yields arbitrary require/command execution in the runner container. The polluted prototype is process-wide, so later tenants on the same shared runner are also corrupted. On v1.x without task runners, comparable Code-node JS runs in the main process with higher impact.

causal_research.bug_semantics: RSA NOPAD encrypt/decrypt left-aligns TA-supplied input into a modulus-sized S-EL1 heap buffer with memcpy(buf + rsa_len - src_len, src, src_len) and no src_len <= rsa_len check. Both lengths are size_t; when a Trusted Application calls TEE_ALG_RSA_NOPAD with src_len > modulus size, the subtraction wraps and memcpy writes attacker-controlled bytes before the destination (heap underwrite of allocator metadata or adjacent core objects). The syscall in core/tee/tee_svc_cryp.c only checks access rights. The same sink exists in the mbedTLS software backend (sw_crypto_acipher_rsanopad_{en,de}crypt in lib/libmbedtls/core/rsa.c) and the NXP SE050 driver (encrypt_nopad/decrypt_nopad in core/drivers/crypto/se050/core/rsa.c). libtomcrypt is not this sink (rsa_exptmod rejects invalid size). causal_research.bug_semantics: MessagePack typeless deserialization (ext type 100) lets the payload name a .NET type. TypelessFormatter resolves that name and, starting in 2019, calls MessagePackSerializerOptions.ThrowIfDeserializingTypeIsDisallowed before constructing a formatter. The default implementation compared only the outer type.FullName to a small DisallowedTypes set (and any user override of the virtual method likewise saw only the wrapper). An attacker who can submit typeless data can therefore send a blocked gadget as T[] or List<T> (or another constructed generic): the wrapper name is not on the list, the check returns, and the formatter pipeline still instantiates formatters for the inner blocked type. That is CWE-470/CWE-502 weakening of the advertised type-restriction hook, not a new gadget by itself. The 2026 fix keeps the leaf check in ThrowIfDeserializingTypeIsDisallowedCore and recursively walks array/pointer/byref element types and constructed generic arguments before formatter resolution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ChaiScript evaluated user-defined function bodies through ordinary native C++ recursion without enforcing a maximum ChaiScript call depth. A script-defined operator can re-enter itself from a ${...} string-interpolation expression, repeatedly traversing function dispatch and AST evaluation until the process exhausts its native stack and terminates with stack overflow/SIGSEGV instead of raising a recoverable script or host exception.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The omission originates in 8f89e446087be57559cda289c342ee9227cb7140, the first commit that made parsed ChaiScript function definitions executable: wesley/main.cpp added eval_function0 through eval_function3, each directly re-evaluating the stored function-body AST via eval_token, and registered those callbacks from the Function_Def evaluator with no recursion-depth check. Later commits completed dispatch, added string interpolation, introduced call_depth bookkeeping, and moved/refactored the evaluator, but those changes did not first create the underlying unbounded recursive script-call mechanism.

causal_research.bug_semantics: GraphQL-Ruby’s `Schema.max_query_string_tokens` is a parse-time throttle (CWE-770) intended to reject maliciously large query strings. In the default Ruby lexer, `Lexer#advance` skipped `IGNORE_REGEXP`, which treated GraphQL comments (`#...`) as ignorable whitespace, then incremented `@tokens_count` only for the remaining punctuation/name/number/string tokens. An attacker can pad a small executable query with thousands of `# comment N\n` lines so the lexer still scans and allocates over the configured token budget while `@tokens_count` never trips `This query is too large to execute.` GraphQL-CParser is not affected: its ragel lexer `emit()`s COMMENT tokens and increments `tokens_count` before dropping comments from the parser token list. The limit was introduced in v2.3.1 and patched in 2.3.23 / 2.4.18 / 2.5.26 / 2.6.1.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-3h96-34p3-xm76 (cve_id null, withdrawn_at null, identifiers GHSA-only): Ruby lexer does not count comment tokens toward max_query_string_tokens; CParser unaffected; feature introduced v2.3.1; patched 2.3.23 / 2.4.18 / 2.5.26 / 2.6.1. GitHub advisory API and OSV (nvd_published_at null, no CVE alias) match. CVE.org has no CVE record for this GHSA.

git log -S '@tokens_count += 1' -- lib/graphql/language/lexer.rb yields only c634445febcc93cf70bc4a38fe1f10aa2c40d495 (add increment after skip IGNORE) and 2a8d95680bf1ed9bb7c0d89345a736f57b10877b (count comments).

IGNORE_REGEXP at lexer.rb:166-171 includes `#.*$`. schema.rb:646-655 documents the limit as preventing maliciously-large query strings; query.rb:398 passes max_tokens: @schema.max_query_string_tokens into GraphQL.parse.

causal_research.flaw_origin: The incomplete throttle was written in the first `max_query_string_tokens` implementation, not a later regression. `c634445febcc93cf70bc4a38fe1f10aa2c40d495` added `@tokens_count += 1` in `Lexer#advance` immediately after `@scanner.skip(IGNORE_REGEXP)`. That IGNORE pattern already contained `#.*$` from the 2023 parser rewrite (`7f18613b523bed53f7623e9975e16a5ff898be2c`); comments were therefore never tokens for the new limit. The same PR’s C-parser follow-up (`8acc70892485da3a623afe955a3d875f2d8e14ec`) counted COMMENT via `emit()`, so the Ruby skip-then-count path was the flawed mechanism from first write.
causal_research.reasoning: This is a real CWE-770 incomplete-throttling bug, not a withdrawn advisory: GHSA-3h96-34p3-xm76 is reviewed, not withdrawn, has no CVE alias, and the vendor patch plus regression test (comment-padded query vs max_query_string_tokens) match the described mechanism. Pre-limit, the Ruby lexer correctly treated comments as ignorable. The security limit was then grafted onto that skip, so comments were never budgeted. The smallest public first-write of that skip-then-count throttle is c634445febcc93cf70bc4a38fe1f10aa2c40d495, a non-squash PR member whose parent tree contains no max_tokens/tokens_count/max_query_string_tokens. The later merge 2f46e14ec, C-parser counting commit, and 2026 lexer comment-split fix are not BICs. Tag membership aligns: BIC lands in v2.3.1 (first affected) and the master fix 88d6c1ca / 2a8d956 lands in v2.6.1 with matching backports on the other patched tags. AI attribution is taken only from that BIC commit object: human maintainer author and committer, no AI/co-author/bot trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: uuid v3()/v5() (shared helper src/v35.ts) and v6() accept a caller-supplied output buffer and offset, then copy 16 UUID bytes with buf[offset+i]=bytes[i] and return buf, without rejecting offset<0 or offset+16>buf.length. On Uint8Array, out-of-range index assignment is a silent no-op, so a too-small buffer or too-large offset yields a mixed/truncated identifier (new bytes plus stale tail) with no exception. v1()/v4()/v7() already throw RangeError on the same bounds, so callers that treat a returned buffer as a complete 16-byte UUID get integrity failures only on v3/v5/v6. This is CWE-787/CWE-1285 in JS typed-array terms (silent partial write), not a native memory smash.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On CUSTOM_ROLES-licensed instances, DELETE /roles/:slug authorized project-role deletion with only assertCanManageRoleType (role:manage, or role:manageProject for roleType=project) and then passed the caller-controlled reassignRoleSlug query string into RoleService.removeCustomRole. The service required the target to exist and to have the same roleType as the deleted role, then RoleRepository.reassignUsersAndRemove updated every matching ProjectRelation.role in one transaction. Because project:admin is a same-type built-in project role, a user with only the narrow global scope role:manageProject could delete any in-use custom project role and reassign its holders instance-wide to project:admin, taking administrative control of projects they were not entitled to manage. The 2.33.4/2.34.1 patch refuses reassignment unless the role is global and the caller has role:manage plus user:changeRole (and is not deleting their own role), and the DTO accepts only assignable global role slugs.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Admin UsersController#profile is excluded from the validate_role before_action (except: profile, profile_edit) so that any authenticated user can open their own profile. causal_research.bug_semantics: With server-side SNI enabled and a wildcard or otherwise broad certificate mapping, an unauthenticated TLS client can submit arbitrarily many distinct matching server names. Each name becomes a key in an unbounded SslContext map, retaining contexts and allowing memory-exhaustion denial of service.

causal_research.bug_semantics: LiquidJS documents `root` as the directory (or list of directories) against which `renderFile()` / `parseFile()` filenames are resolved, but top-level loads use `LookupType.Root` and skip the containment check applied to `{% include %}` / `{% render %}` / `{% layout %}`. At v10.25.4, `Parser._parseFile` (`src/parser/parser.ts:88-89`) defaults to `LookupType.Root` and calls `loader.lookup`. `Loader.lookup` (`src/fs/loader.ts:46-54`) sets `const enforceRoot = type !== LookupType.Root` and only runs `fs.contains` when `enforceRoot` is true. `candidates()` still yields `fs.resolve(dir, file, extname)` and optional `fs.fallback(file)`; Node `path.resolve` ignores `dir` when `file` is absolute, so `renderFile('/etc/hosts')` with `root` pointing at an unrelated temp directory returns `/etc/hosts` if the process can read it. Impact is arbitrary local file disclosure (CWE-22) for apps that treat `root` as a sandbox and forward attacker-controlled template names into those APIs.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-39859 state=PUBLISHED (datePublished 2026-04-08, not rejected/withdrawn); GHSA-v273-448j-v4qj withdrawn_at=null; vendor GHSA + NVD published. CNA text incorrectly says affected <10.25.3 / fixed in 10.25.3; git and GHSA patched version 10.25.5 are authoritative.

PoC and mechanism match GHSA: Liquid({root:[tempdir]}).renderFile('/etc/hosts') succeeds because LookupType.Root skips contains(). v10.25.4 src/parser/parser.ts:88-89 `_parseFile` -> loader.lookup(..., LookupType.Root); src/fs/loader.ts:46 `const enforceRoot = type !== LookupType.Root` then 47-54 skip contains when false; candidates() 67-74 still yield path.resolve and fallback.

BIC 822ba0be0f1cfbedd50376aff8ac49eee71bd48c (2021-10-06, Harttle <yangjvn@126.com>, subject 'fix: skip root check for renderFile()'): single parent a3455ebd0b207141c34630c0af44d917db2ca1dd; not a merge/squash. causal_research.bug_semantics: On Linux/Unix, LocalFolderExtractor first constructs and canonicalizes new File(destination, archiveEntryName) while backslashes in the untrusted RAR name are still literal filename characters. A name such as '..\..\tmp\evil' therefore passes the destination-prefix check. If the file does not exist, makeFile then splits that same name on backslashes and rejoins the components with File.separator, turning the previously literal '..' components into real '/' traversal. extract subsequently opens FileOutputStream on that reconstructed path and writes attacker-controlled archive content outside the extraction directory.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The causal flaw is the two-stage, inconsistent interpretation of an archive pathname: validation and use do not operate on the same normalized representation. The backslash-splitting/reconstruction and write path first appear in the repository's root initial-import commit 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 in testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java. That implementation was later promoted and moved through production paths without changing the mechanism; e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a added canonical-path validation but left it before the separator reinterpretation, creating the advisory's explicit validation bypass rather than originating the underlying arbitrary-write mechanism.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent — `git cat-file -p 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519` shows author and committer `Edmund Wagner <edmund-wagner@web.de>` at Unix time 1284206829 (+0200), message `initial import`, no bot identity, no Co-Authored-By trailer, no Generated-with trailer, and no other AI marker in the BIC commit object.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Freeform ships precompiled browser JavaScript that webpack-bundles the Axios HTTP client. Axios 0.8.1 through 1.5.1 (CVE-2023-45857) always copies the XSRF cookie (xsrfCookieName, default XSRF-TOKEN) into request header X-XSRF-TOKEN for every request, including cross-origin ones. In this plugin the first shipped copy is packages/plugin/src/Resources/js/app/vendor.js, driven by packages/app/src/welcome-screen/shared/requests/push-data.ts which sets axios.defaults.baseURL and posts JSON. The GHSA-named public asset /freeform/plugin.js is packages/plugin/src/Resources/js/scripts/front-end/plugin/freeform.js, which later bundles the same Axios via packages/scripts drag-and-drop file-upload.ts (axios.post to /freeform/files). If that Axios instance is used for a credentialed request to an unintended origin, the XSRF token is disclosed in the header. The 4.x fix rebuilds those assets on Axios 1.7.7, which adds withXSRFToken and same-origin gating. No unauthenticated Craft/PHP RCE path is claimed.

causal_research.flaw_origin: Original OpenWire topic-consumer path in AMQConsumer creates a temporary multicast queue (createQueue(..., temporary=true)) for non-durable topic subscriptions without checking auto-create-addresses or CREATE_ADDRESS. AMQSession.createConsumer only ran the auto-create gate for queues, so the topic path reached createQueue and the address was created anyway.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authorized client controls the 32-bit nClients and nRanges fields of an X Record RegisterClients/CreateContext request. The server checked that the request payload length equaled 4*nClients + sizeof(xRecordRange)*nRanges, but the unchecked integer arithmetic could wrap and make a short request pass. The server then used those counts for pointer derivation and repeated xRecordRange reads/conversion, so the bypass reaches out-of-request memory access and can disclose or corrupt data or crash the server.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The IdentityServer profile page at /identity-server/account/profile is a cookie-authenticated UI that immediately commits email (and username) changes through DefaultUserService.UpdateAsync -> UserManager.SetEmailAsync with no confirmation step. The first-party PoC is not a token-less cross-site POST: an attacker uploads HTML as a Squidex asset and serves it inline on the same origin, then iframes the real profile form under a decoy overlay so the victim's click submits that form. Assets are delivered with Content-Disposition inline (unless download=1) and only Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'none', which blocks stored XSS but not iframe/CSS UI-redress. Durable impact is changing the victim's email without verification and pivoting account recovery. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED (CNA MITRE, CISA-ADP CWE-352); GHSA withdrawn_at is null.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated n8n user who can run a Snowflake node with usable Snowflake credentials supplies free-form SQL in the Execute Query field. Snowflake.node.ts reads that Query parameter (later also interpolating n8n expressions via getResolvables) and calls GenericFunctions.execute(connection, query, binds). execute() forwarded sqlText unchanged to snowflake-sdk Connection.execute(). The Node.js Snowflake driver intercepts client-side PUT/GET commands and performs local filesystem upload/download (PUT file://<host-path> @stage reads a host file onto a Snowflake stage; GET @stage file://<host-path> writes a staged file onto the n8n host, including overwrite). n8n's N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO / isFilePathBlocked controls were never applied on this path, so a workflow author could read arbitrary process-readable files off the n8n host or overwrite process-writable files. The 2026-08-05 fix rejects queries whose first non-comment token is PUT or GET before calling the SDK.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Scriban's template builtin array.insert_at (ArrayFunctions.InsertAt) pads the target list by running a tight C# for-loop from list.Count up to an attacker-controlled index and calling Add(null) each step, then Inserts the value. That fill never calls TemplateContext.StepLoop and never consults LoopLimit, LimitToString, RecursiveLimit, or ObjectRecursionLimit, even though LoopLimit (default 1000) existed from the first commit for script for-statements. A one-line template such as {{ [1] | array.insert_at 200000000 'x' | array.size }} therefore allocates unbounded memory, raises OutOfMemoryException, and can terminate the host process in well under a second. The 7.0.0 sibling hardening (dde661d36bb6b06414546c6b1272fc1b517078c9) added StepLoop overloads to other ArrayFunctions primitives and still left InsertAt on the unbounded IEnumerable/int/object signature. causal_research.bug_semantics: OliveTin JWT authentication accepts a validly signed token whose aud claim does not match the configured authJwtAud when the token is verified with a local RSA public key (authJwtPubKeyPath) or HMAC secret (authJwtHmacSecret). parseJwtTokenWithLocalKey and parseJwtTokenWithHMAC call github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 jwt.Parse with only a keyfunc and no jwt.WithAudience option, so golang-jwt never checks audience. The sibling remote JWKS path parseJwtTokenWithRemoteKey does pass jwt.WithAudience(cfg.AuthJwtAud). An attacker who holds a token minted for a different audience/service that shares the signing material can authenticate (WhoAmI and other JWT-gated APIs). ACL authorization is not bypassed; this is authentication-time audience non-enforcement (CWE-287/CWE-345).

causal_research.bug_semantics: In bgp_attr_nhc(), a crafted BGP UPDATE carrying a Next Hop Dependent Characteristics (NHC) attribute can underflow the remaining-length counter. Remaining NHC length is a uint16 bgp_size_t. The TLV loop reads the 4-byte TLV header (code+length = BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN) then checks only `if (length < tlv_length)` before later doing `length -= tlv_length + BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN`. When remaining length is in [tlv_length, tlv_length+3], the check passes and the unsigned subtract wraps (e.g. 5-6 -> 65535). The loop is `while (length && STREAM_READABLE(s) >= BGP_NHC_TLV_MIN_LEN)`, and STREAM_READABLE is the whole UPDATE stream, so a wrapped length keeps parsing subsequent UPDATE bytes as NHC TLVs (allocations/DoS). STREAM_READABLE < tlv_length can stop an over-read of the stream itself, but does not stop the underflow. CWE-191; unauthenticated remote DoS via BGP UPDATE.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Spring Security one-time-token login authenticates by calling OneTimeTokenService.consume(); a successful consume must be single-use. JdbcOneTimeTokenService.consume() issues an auto-commit SELECT (selectOneTimeToken) and, if a row exists, a separate auto-commit DELETE (deleteOneTimeToken) whose jdbcOperations.update rowcount is discarded; it then returns the already-loaded token unless isExpired(). Two concurrent /login/ott submissions with the same valid token can both pass the SELECT before either DELETE commits, both treat consume as success, and both establish sessions. InMemoryOneTimeTokenService is unaffected because ConcurrentHashMap.remove is atomic. Attack requires explicit oneTimeTokenLogin() plus an explicit JdbcOneTimeTokenService bean.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Webmin miniserv.pl authenticates SSL-client-certificate users by mapping a certificate DN through find_user_by_cert() and setting $validated=2. After trust_real_ip was reused as a proxy-header trust flag, a client-supplied X-SSL-Client-DN header was treated as that DN without a verified TLS client certificate from this connection. With proxy-IP trust enabled and at least one user bound to a client cert, an unauthenticated peer that reaches miniserv directly (not via the intended reverse proxy) can forge X-SSL-Client-DN and impersonate that user (CWE-290). Preconditions match the vendor write-up: trust_real_ip plus client-cert users; AC:H/AT:P in the CVSS vectors.

causal_research.bug_semantics: On instances with N8N_SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED=true, n8n's centralized SSRF policy is applied through request helpers / outboundHttp.transport({ ssrf }). The SearXNG Agent tool did not use that path. An authenticated user who can create a searXngApi credential sets apiUrl to an internal or link-local host (for example http://127.0.0.1 or http://searxng.internal:8080). When an AI Agent (ToolSearXng sub-node) or a personal agent with fallback web_search provider=searxng runs a search, the server issues HTTP to `${apiUrl}/search` via LangChain SearxngSearch or global fetch, then returns titles/URLs/snippets (or the raw body) through Agent chat/tool output, disclosing internal service responses (CWE-918).

causal_research.bug_semantics: django.utils.archive.extract() unpacks tar/zip members for startapp --template and startproject --template (TemplateCommand.extract -> archive.extract). After CVE-2021-3281, BaseArchive.target_filename computed filename = abspath(join(target_path, name)) and rejected members only when not filename.startswith(target_path). Because startswith is a string prefix test without a directory-separator boundary, a member whose resolved path is target_path + extra_suffix (for example /tmp/django_proj_template_XXX_extractabc/evil.txt versus target /tmp/django_proj_template_XXX_extract) is treated as in-tree and written outside the intended extraction directory (CWE-23). The 2021 tests covered .., absolute /tmp/evil.py, and Windows d: paths, not this prefix-sharing case. The 2025 fix requires os.path.commonpath([target_path, filename]) == target_path.

causal_research.bug_semantics: fgetl() in src/filehandling.c treats line_sz as content capacity and then always writes a NUL at line_buf[line_len]. When an input line is exactly line_sz bytes, line_len equals the caller's allocation and the terminator is a one-byte heap write past the buffer (CWE-193/CWE-787). The CVE/GHSA PoC is a hash/potfile/wordlist line of exactly HCBUFSIZ_LARGE (16,777,216) bytes with no newline; callers such as hlfmt_detect (src/hlfmt.c), hashes_init_stage1 (src/hashes.c), potfile_read (src/potfile.c), and outfile_check (src/outfile_check.c) allocate hcmalloc(HCBUFSIZ_LARGE) and pass that size, leaving no room for the terminator. count_lines() in the same file already allocates HCBUFSIZ_LARGE+1. At v7.1.2 the write is src/filehandling.c:1059. Local file input, UI required; ASAN reports WRITE of size 1 / SIGSEGV. CVE-2026-68767 is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected).
