Immediate parent 1ecdffb580201684adbec00c88740540fe50ab09 still clamps line_len to HCBUFSIZ_LARGE-1, so the terminator stays inside an HCBUFSIZ_LARGE buffer. c6ac3069504d3a7db7949884569eaa1ca2ff255c (2021-09-13, 'Fix fgetl() logic') rewrote the loop into the v7.1.2 shape (break on newline before storing, strip only CR) but kept `line_len == line_sz` plus the same terminator write; it is a refactor of the already-vulnerable mechanism, not a first-write. git log -S 'line_len == line_sz' -- src/filehandling.c only adds the test in 97c9e86d and removes it in the 2026 fix.
causal_research.reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-68767 is a published VulnCheck CNA record (GHSA not withdrawn) for an off-by-one NUL write in hashcat fgetl() when a line fills the caller buffer. The v7.1.2 and fix-parent bodies match the advisory: characters are stored until line_len == line_sz, then line_buf[line_len] = 0 writes one past a HCBUFSIZ_LARGE heap allocation used by hash/potfile/wordlist readers. count_lines() already used +1, confirming the intended safe pattern. BIC search used function history and pickaxe on the capacity test, not AI markers. The smallest first-write of the flawed mechanism is 97c9e86d155df741fc50bc61453d63888427ef86, which introduced line_sz and dropped the HCBUFSIZ_LARGE-1 clamp so line_len can equal the allocation at the terminator store. The 2026 block-reader commit 93b55d37 is the direct fix: it reserves the last byte (line_max = line_sz - 1) and documents the overflow; it is after v7.1.2 and not in any tag. causal_research.bug_semantics: When Traefik's errors middleware sees a backend status in the configured range, it builds a secondary GET to errors.service. From 580157a onward the default path copies the original request header map (Authorization, Cookie, and other credentials) onto that cross-service request via utils.CopyHeaders. Operators attaching a distinct error-page service therefore receive end-user credentials that were only meant for the original backend. Preconditions: errors middleware enabled, errors.service distinct, status match, client sent sensitive headers. NginxHeaders, when set, uses a different header set and is not this default path.

mechanism.counterevidence: Checked whether an earlier error-page implementation already copied request headers (no: c99266e961 and the pre-2018 middlewares/error_pages.go create the request without any copy, so the introduction is not older and not a rename artifact); checked whether the nginx-headers variant was the causal code path (no: the forwardNginxHeaders branch copies only explicitly named headers and is not the default branch); checked whether the upstream fix changes the default behaviour (it does not: the copy-all branch is retained when errorRequestHeaders is nil, so 'fixed' means 'opt-in control plus documentation'); checked the BIC and fix commit objects for AI markers (none present, and the bot committer is Traefik's own automation account, which is not AI evidence).
mechanism.impact: Any error-page render hands the operator's separate error page service the client's Authorization, Cookie and every other request header; a bearer token or session cookie captured there can be replayed against the protected backend, crossing a trust boundary that the operator established by hosting the error page service elsewhere (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:L/SI:N/SA:N, CWE-200).
mechanism.preconditions: Traefik with an errors middleware whose service is a distinct error page service (not the same trusted backend); the incoming request carries Authorization and/or Cookie; the backend returns a status within the configured ranges; errorRequestHeaders is unset, which is the default on every affected release including the 'fixed' ones.
mechanism.summary: When the errors middleware catches a configured status range it constructs the error-page request and copies the whole original request header map onto it, so the client's Authorization and Cookie headers are forwarded to the separate error page service, which receives credentials it was never meant to see (CWE-200, information disclosure).
mechanism.trigger: A router with the errors middleware configured (status ranges + service pointing at a separate error page service + query), whose backend returns a status inside the configured range, while the client request carries Authorization and/or Cookie headers and errorRequestHeaders is unset; Traefik then sends the error-page GET request to that service with the client's full header map attached.
mechanism.vulnerable_code: pkg/middlewares/customerrors/custom_errors.go:160 in customErrors.ServeHTTP at v3.7.0-rc.2 (a47e15f1299d23fec1bcbb78bece4325a40d63f2); same call at pkg/middlewares/customerrors/custom_errors.go:148 in v3.6.14 (a6664c95b589842489d37d73e7d01bf1c8881685) and originally middlewares/errorpages/error_pages.go:99 in Handler.ServeHTTP at 76dcbe34291f7e53c68f10a93ec7b32bc749c24d.

causal_research.bug_semantics: in_s3 downloads an S3 object and fully materializes the decompressed payload in memory before parsing. Default store_as is gzip; GzipExtractor.extract wraps the object body in Zlib::GzipReader and calls gz.read with no decompressed-size cap (later rewritten to loop concatenated members, still unbounded parts << gz.read / parts.join). gzip_command/lzma2/lzo extractors do the same via Open3.capture2 of gzip/xz/lzop -dc, returning the entire stdout. An attacker who can PUT a highly compressed object into the watched bucket can force Fluentd to expand a small blob into an arbitrarily large string, OOM-kill the process, and stop log collection on the node (CWE-770).

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated GET /download-export request supplied filename directly to download_export(), which concatenated export_path() with the raw $_GET['filename'] value and, after only file_exists(), passed the resulting path to response()->download(). causal_research.bug_semantics: Spring Security HeaderWriterFilter defaults to lazy header writing (shouldWriteHeadersEagerly=false). It wraps the servlet response in HeaderWriterResponse, which extends OnCommittedResponseWrapper, and writes security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP, Cache-Control, HSTS, etc.) only when the wrapper believes the response is about to commit, or in a finally block after the chain. OnCommittedResponseWrapper historically tracked Content-Length only via addHeader/setContentLength/setContentLengthLong. If an application or framework sets Content-Length through setHeader, setIntHeader, or addIntHeader, the wrapper does not record the length. When the body size then matches Content-Length, Tomcat commits the response; later setHeader calls from HeaderWriterFilter are no-ops. Protective headers are silently omitted, enabling cache leakage and missing browser security headers. Spring Framework 7.0.5 made this path common by applying Content-Length via setHeader immediately, but any setHeader Content-Length client could trigger it on the lazy default.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Spring Security SAML2 POST binding emits a self-submitting HTML page whose form action is the asserting-party SSO/SLO URL taken from RelyingPartyRegistration (authenticationRequestUri / location / responseLocation). From the first POST-binding implementation, SAMLRequest/SAMLResponse and RelayState were passed through HtmlUtils.htmlEscape before being written into hidden inputs, but the action URL was concatenated raw. An attacker who can influence RelyingPartyRegistration (for example by supplying or tampering with asserting-party metadata) can place a quote-breaking payload in that URL, break out of the action attribute, and run script in the service provider origin when a victim loads the auto-submit page. The same unescaped action builder was later copied into Saml2LogoutRequestFilter and Saml2RelyingPartyInitiatedLogoutSuccessHandler. The 2026 fix stops synthesizing that HTML in the SAML filters and instead posts via FormPostRedirectStrategy, which HTML-escapes the action URL (and the parameter names/values) before writing the page.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An unauthenticated network client can complete the RTMP handshake/connect/createStream/publish sequence and receive NetStream.Publish.Start because SRS treats RTMP publishing as permitted unless an operator explicitly enables a vhost security policy (or supplies a separate hook/token control). In the default state, SrsSecurity::check returns success immediately when security.enabled is false, so the publish path has no mandatory authentication boundary.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 first completed the FMLE publish command path in trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp: it consumed SrsPublishPacket and unconditionally emitted onFCPublish/onStatus NetStream.Publish.Start, with no credential or authorization decision. Its immediate parent only handled releaseStream/FCPublish/createStream and returned before consuming or accepting publish. Commit 75f2607685814b86ad030df703834cf06f91447f later added optional vhost allow/deny security with a false default and an explicit allow-all bypass, preserving rather than originating the already unauthenticated publish behavior.
causal_research.ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file commit 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` shows author and committer `winlin <winterserver@126.com>`, the message `support fmle publish. fix bug of rtmp chunk stream.`, and no trailers, bot identity, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Copilot, Claude, Codex, or other AI marker.
evidence: Public disclosure: https://github.com/xuwu-xuwu/CVE-2026-68004/blob/main/CVE_Report_SRS_Unauth_Publish.md describes the RTMP handshake/connect/createStream/publish path, uses receipt of NetStream.Publish.Start as its confirmation condition, identifies disabled vhost.security as the root cause, and reports SRS 4.0.268 and 5.0.213 as vulnerable.

Origin search: `git log --all --reverse -S'NetStream.Publish.Start' -- trunk/src` identifies 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972 as the first commit containing that publish-acceptance status. `git show 33c586... -- trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` shows the new SrsPublishPacket receive and unconditional onFCPublish/onStatus NetStream.Publish.Start responses in identify_fmle_publish_client.

Immediate-parent tree verification: `git show e598616e14e4875bc5c7fcaf3ad981e7c992753e:trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` shows identify_fmle_publish_client ending immediately after the createStream response. `git diff e598616e... 33c58618... -- trunk/src/core/srs_core_rtmp.cpp` shows the publish receive, StatusCodePublishStart definition, both success responses, and receive loop as additions. The vulnerable publish-acceptance mechanism is therefore absent from the direct parent.

BIC object: `git cat-file commit 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` records the single parent e598616e14e4875bc5c7fcaf3ad981e7c992753e, human author/committer winlin <winterserver@126.com>, timestamp 2013-10-22, and no trailers. It is an ordinary one-parent source commit, not a merge, move, release aggregate, revert, or squash requiring decomposition.

Security feature chronology: `git show 75f2607685814b86ad030df703834cf06f91447f` adds trunk/src/app/srs_app_security.cpp with `if (!_srs_config->get_security_enabled(req->vhost)) return ret`, documents security as `default: off`, and defines SRS_CONF_DEFAULT_SECURITY_ENABLED false. Because unauthenticated publish acceptance already existed in 33c58618, 75f26076 is not the smallest BIC.

Version membership: `git describe --tags --contains 33c586181de6b3a0cee61022066cb6e61c666972` returns `v0.1.0~18`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeds for the BIC against v4.0-r4 (2573a25101514f0e3d152b96cd33b31bd00e136d, release v4.0.268), v5.0-r3 (313913737f13f97d9816dbc3d729e7bcd454a531, v5.0.213), and validated-clone HEAD b0d775a316046d4dd1ed87c0f0a9871c614f56f8.

No patch boundary exists in the validated history: at v4.0-r4, v5.0-r3, and HEAD, trunk/src/app/srs_app_security.cpp still immediately returns success when security is disabled, while trunk/src/app/srs_app_config.cpp still sets the security default to false. The advisory reference https://github.com/ossrs/srs/releases/tag/v5.0-r3 points to v5.0.213 but that release preserves the bypass; the reporter likewise explicitly says 5.0.213 is vulnerable. Therefore neither v5.0-r3 nor any later commit through HEAD is a fix, and fix_sha/direct_fix_sha are justified nulls.

Current attack path: trunk/src/app/srs_app_rtmp_conn.cpp identifies the remote client and stream, calls security_->check, and then starts FMLE/Flash publishing. With the default-false configuration, trunk/src/app/srs_app_security.cpp returns success before evaluating any rules, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach start_fmle_publish and receive NetStream.Publish.Start unless a deployment adds an independent control.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A malicious Nomad task that can modify its allocation logs directory can replace a stdout or stderr FIFO, or the logs directory itself, with a symlink. On task restart, the host-side logmon process follows that symlink as the Nomad process user: a substituted FIFO can make logmon read a host file into attacker-readable task logs, while a substituted logs directory can make logmon create partially attacker-named FIFOs or log files in a host directory. The fix confines FIFO operations with os.Root and mkfifoat and mounts the allocation logs subdirectory read-only for filesystem-isolated tasks.

causal_research.bug_semantics: ImportedClusterSecrets stores the complete imported Talos cluster secrets bundle, including CA private keys. The resource was placed in ResourceService's ordinary role-by-verb access branch, where Get/List/Watch require only Reader, so an authenticated Reader could retrieve those keys and use them outside Omni to obtain control of the imported Talos, Kubernetes, and etcd APIs.
evidence: Bundle SHA-256 is 25ec9d9616f720808b16b6077583cd5e5d914fa3cd6a2ba726ebab9d30c25a7a and its active GitHub advisory says Reader can retrieve ImportedClusterSecrets containing the full CA bundle; GitHub's advisory API reported withdrawn_at=null on 2026-08-30.

That case calls auth.CheckGRPC(ctx, auth.WithRole(verbToRole(access.Verb))), while verbToRole maps Get/List/Watch to role.Reader. The same commit's auth test lists importedClusterSecret with all verbs and no admin/operator restriction.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Causal mechanism (authorization-context interaction now resolved): CVE-2025-49594 is a cross-user token-minting flaw (CWE-285) in the OIDC provider template userapplications.vm. At BIC f8b522c (OIDC-229, 2025-04-30 16:25 +02:00), token operations were retargeted from the authenticated caller ($xcontext.userReference) to the viewed profile ($doc.documentReference) for both addConsent and getConsents, while the surrounding guard remained: if caller != viewed profile AND !hasAccess('programming') then deny. The one-argument hasAccess('programming') does not take the (caller, target) pair; for a VIEW-only visitor of another user's profile it evaluates the programming right in the wrong scope (document/page-author context instead of the visiting subject) and returns true, so the guard passes and addConsent($doc.documentReference, ...) mints an access token for the viewed user. The template evaluates this guard before every action path (line 36, then addConsent at line 67 inside the #else branch), so the UI gate is the user-facing control; the backend script addConsent's AccessDeniedException for script author is defense in depth, not the bypassed layer. With token authentication enabled, any VIEW-able profile becomes impersonable. BIC vs parent (local git, blob-complete clone, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH): parent 18ae19e (merge PR #81, same day) still calls addConsent($xcontext.userReference)/getConsents($xcontext.userReference) — self-targeted only; even with the dead guard (typo hasAcess since OIDC-195 040eb6c, 2024-10-02) viewing another profile could not mint that user's token. f8b522c is the first commit that both retargets to the viewed profile and makes the guard actually evaluate (typo fix hasAcess→hasAccess). git log -S confirms 'doc.documentReference' enters this template only at 040eb6c (as guard RHS, not as consent target) and reaches addConsent/getConsents first at f8b522c. causal_research.evidence: Causal mechanism (authorization-context interaction now resolved): CVE-2025-49594 is a cross-user token-minting flaw (CWE-285) in the OIDC provider template userapplications.vm. At BIC f8b522c (OIDC-229, 2025-04-30 16:25 +02:00), token operations were retargeted from the authenticated caller ($xcontext.userReference) to the viewed profile ($doc.documentReference) for both addConsent and getConsents, while the surrounding guard remained: if caller != viewed profile AND !hasAccess('programming') then deny. The one-argument hasAccess('programming') does not take the (caller, target) pair; for a VIEW-only visitor of another user's profile it evaluates the programming right in the wrong scope (document/page-author context instead of the visiting subject) and returns true, so the guard passes and addConsent($doc.documentReference, ...) mints an access token for the viewed user. The template evaluates this guard before every action path (line 36, then addConsent at line 67 inside the #else branch), so the UI gate is the user-facing control; the backend script addConsent's AccessDeniedException for script author is defense in depth, not the bypassed layer. With token authentication enabled, any VIEW-able profile becomes impersonable. BIC vs parent (local git, blob-complete clone, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH): parent 18ae19e (merge PR #81, same day) still calls addConsent($xcontext.userReference)/getConsents($xcontext.userReference) — self-targeted only; even with the dead guard (typo hasAcess since OIDC-195 040eb6c, 2024-10-02) viewing another profile could not mint that user's token. f8b522c is the first commit that both retargets to the viewed profile and makes the guard actually evaluate (typo fix hasAcess→hasAccess). git log -S confirms 'doc.documentReference' enters this template only at 040eb6c (as guard RHS, not as consent target) and reaches addConsent/getConsents first at f8b522c. OSV's introduced 46f78862c24fa2df959293bdb58fd148fc0cfda1 is '[maven-release-plugin] prepare release oidc-2.17.1' (2025-04-30), a version-range marker, not the bug-introducing change. Minimal fix: d90d717 (OIDC-240, 2025-06-12 11:16 +02:00) changes the single template line to three-argument hasAccess('programming', $xcontext.userReference, $doc.documentReference), explicitly binding the check to the exact (caller, target) pair and removing the self-targeting exemption that the one-arg call inadvertently granted to cross-profile viewers; adds integration test asserting a guest visiting another user's profile cannot access token management (OIDCTest asserts OIDCApplicationsUserProfilePage.isAllowed() is false before login, plus pageobject helper @since 2.18.2). Three files, +32/-6 lines, template check is the sole behavioral change; nothing else regresses OIDC-229's legitimate programming-right feature. Positive NOT_AI attribution evidence (independent of marker absence): (1) JIRA OIDC-229 (https://jira.xwiki.org/browse/OIDC-229) was filed by tmortagne (thomas.mortagne@xwiki.com, matching commit author/committer Thomas Mortagne) at 2025-04-30T16:11:30+02:00 — 14 minutes before the BIC commit at 16:25:14+02:00 — with first-person description 'That was the intent of the code, but looks like I did not tested that use case...', a self-documented intent-vs-implementation gap predating the vulnerable commit. (2) Repo-level AI-trailer convention calibrated: three commits (131bf6e, d71eafe, 1b888ca, all 2026-08-19, 16 months after BIC) carry byte-exact 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>' trailers in their commit bodies; BIC f8b522c and fix d90d717 bodies contain no such trailer (checked with cat -A at byte level). This gives trailer absence real probative weight here: the convention existed in the same repo and postdates the audited commits. (3) Commit shape matches interactive human work: single-file 4+/4- template edit bundling a typo fix with a retarget, author==committer, and the same maintainer has continuous repo history since the first commit on 2016-03-25. Together the JIRA-report→commit identity chain, the maintainer's own first-person intent admission, and the calibrated trailer convention affirmatively support human authorship. Version boundary: git tag --contains shows BIC f8b522c is first contained in tag oidc-2.17.1 (tag commit is 46f7886, one commit after BIC, same day); fix d90d717 is first contained in tag oidc-2.18.2 (tag commit f01756b, 2025-06-12, same day as the fix). Vulnerable range is therefore >= 2.17.1 and < 2.18.2, fixed in 2.18.2, matching CVE-2025-49594 (CWE-285), GHSA-f2hf-pfrj-vrm7, NVD, and OSV, with the documented workaround 'disable token access'.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A remote attacker can POST a large URL containing Unicode code points that are expensive under NFKC (Django's regression uses U+00BE '¾' repeated) into a forms.URLField. to_python() always ran urllib.parse.urlsplit() on the raw value to prepend a default scheme and rebuild host/path. On Windows, CPython urlsplit() NFKC-normalizes that string, so an unbounded input burns CPU before URLValidator runs (CWE-400/770 DoS). The 2026 fix stopped calling urlsplit() and detects a scheme with str.partition(':'), leaving structural checks to validators.

Vendor advisory https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/mar/03/security-releases/ and 6.0.3 notes: django.forms.URLField.to_python() used urllib.parse.urlsplit() to decide whether to prepend a scheme; on Windows urlsplit() NFKC-normalizes via unicodedata.normalize and is disproportionately slow for large inputs with certain Unicode characters.

Attack path: untrusted URL (form POST / model field) -> URLField.to_python() -> urlsplit(value) -> Windows NFKC on unbounded input -> CPU DoS (CWE-400/CWE-770). Reporter Seokchan Yoon; severity moderate (Django policy) / CVSS 7.5.

causal_research.reasoning: This is a real, still-published Django DoS: URLField.to_python() fed attacker-controlled URLs to urllib.parse.urlsplit(), and Windows NFKC inside urlsplit could be driven into pathological CPU use. The 2026 main fix 951ffb3832cd83ba672c1e3deae2bda128eb9cca (backported to 6.0.3/5.2.12/4.2.29) removes that call and matches the vendor description. Tracing git log -S/-L through the later clean()->to_python() move and scheme-detection rewrite, the first public commit that wrote urlsplit(user_value) in URLField is 108b604b51948a3aa8a5c789887a97eb417d3cb5; its parent tree lacks urlsplit entirely. That 2008 git-svn revision is a single-parent human commit by Malcolm Tredinnick with no commit-object AI markers, so AI did not author or co-author the BIC. Later wrappers, import updates, assume_scheme, and the AI-irrelevant fix authorship do not change BIC attribution.

causal_research.bug_semantics: The script-visible async() function launched std::async(std::launch::async, t_func) without making the spawned work part of the ChaiScript engine's lifetime. A script could finish while async functions were still evaluating identifiers against Dispatch_Engine maps; engine teardown then freed those map nodes, and a worker's subsequent lookup compared a freed std::string key in chaiscript::str_less::operator(), producing a heap use-after-free.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Commit 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2 first registered the ChaiScript async() API in include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp and returned an independently executing std::future, but introduced no engine-owned thread tracking or destructor join. Later commits only adjusted registration syntax, module ownership, bootstrap qualification, and formatting while preserving that lifetime mismatch until the 2026 fix.

The smallest commit that made this attack path possible is 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2: it added both future support and the script-visible async() wrapper that launches immediately on another thread, without any relationship to Dispatch_Engine destruction. Line history shows subsequent commits preserved the same mechanism rather than introducing it. The BIC falls between v5.5.1 and v5.6.0 and remains in v6.1.0. The direct fix 8dbb5eddcead54ff8b44b6646d491fec921a1720, landed by squash as 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484 after v6.1.0, makes the engine own and join outstanding worker threads before teardown. AI disclosure on the 2026 fix cannot retroactively attribute the vulnerable introduction, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When [api] expose_config is enabled, an authenticated Viewer with configuration-read can call GET /api/v2/config (as_dict, display_sensitive=False) or GET /api/v2/config/section/{section}/option/{option}. Sensitive options such as celery.broker_url are registered only under the base pair (celery, broker_url). Team overrides live as config-file section [team=celery] or env AIRFLOW__TEAM___CELERY__BROKER_URL. as_dict copies every ConfigParser section verbatim, then masks by iterating sensitive_config_values and looking up those base names only, so [team=celery] broker_url is never visited. _include_envs splits the team env var on '__' with maxsplit=2 into section=TEAM key=_CELERY__BROKER_URL, reconstructs the same env var, and fails the (section, key) membership test, emitting the broker URL (including embedded credentials) in cleartext under a synthetic section. get_config_value likewise compared the URL section/option literally to sensitive_config_values, so a request for section=team=celery&option=broker_url returned conf.get() unmasked. Global [celery] broker_url was correctly hidden. Attack requires multi-team team-scoped sensitive config plus Config API exposure; no prior access to the secret is needed.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Renovate's npm manager generateLockFile() builds lockfile-update commands as single shell strings. User-influenced packageName values (and workspace directory names) are concatenated into `npm install ...` without quoting. util/exec spawn() forces shell:true, so shell metacharacters in packageName execute as commands on the Renovate host. Attackers with repository write access can set a malicious packageName (PoC: renovate.json5 packageRules.overridePackageName = "; kill 1; echo ") and trigger lockfile updates. First-party GHSA-fr4j-65pv-gjjj and CVE-2026-76230 both name this packageName injection; affected >=35.63.0 <40.33.0; patched in 40.33.0 by shlex quote() around workspace and packageKey tokens.

causal_research.bug_semantics: devalue's uneval and stringify serialize Array instances by walking every index in [0, length) rather than only populated keys. uneval (from the original devalue() function) uses Array.prototype.map, which visits holes, then joins the members into a JS array literal; stringify later used an equivalent for-loop that emits a HOLE sentinel (-2) for each empty slot. A sparse array such as const a=[]; a[1e8]=1 has length 100000001 but one own index, so serialization is O(length) CPU and produces an O(length) string, exhausting memory/CPU on the server (CWE-770). Exploitation requires the attacker to already have a huge sparse Array in-process (not via JSON/typical wire formats) and then pass it to uneval/stringify. GHSA-33hq-fvwr-56pm, no CVE, not withdrawn; affected npm devalue <=5.6.2, patched in 5.6.3 by encoding very-sparse arrays as index/value lists (SPARSE/-7) or Object.assign(Array(n),{...}) after Object.keys-based valid_array_indices().

causal_research.bug_semantics: CRI checkpoint restore (CreateContainer → CRImportCheckpoint) treats attacker-controlled checkpoint metadata as authoritative image identity. It reads RootfsImageRef/RootfsImageName from the checkpoint config.dump, pulls that ref, then ImageService.Create-tags the pulled content as RootfsImageName without verifying that the name matches the digest or that the caller is allowed to bind that local tag. A pod-create attacker can therefore inject a malicious image under an arbitrary NAME:TAG on the node; later pods using IfNotPresent/Never on the poisoned tag run the attacker image under the victim identity. ImageService.Create AlreadyExists is ignored, so a missing local tag is created; an existing NAME:TAG is not overwritten, but first-writer cache poisoning is enough.

Later rewrites (483a1497 2021, DataBuf std::copy/std::copy_n migration b9f9d041/ae4df712 2022) restructure but do not remove the quadratic accumulation. causal_research.bug_semantics: When Tor decompresses a truncated zlib/gzip stream and finalizes it with done/finish=1, zlib consumes the available input but cannot reach Z_STREAM_END and repeatedly returns Z_BUF_ERROR with avail_in==0. The vulnerable backend maps that no-progress error to TOR_COMPRESS_BUFFER_FULL. buf_add_compress() interprets BUFFER_FULL as a request for more output space, allocates another chunk, and loops without any input or state progress, producing an infinite allocation/retry denial of service instead of rejecting the corrupt stream.
evidence: CVE.org primary record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-77640 is PUBLISHED and specifies the affected range 0.2.6.1-alpha to before 0.4.9.9 and the exact truncated-stream infinite-loop mechanism.

Tor primary ChangeLog https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/raw/tor-0.4.9.9/ChangeLog identifies TROVE-2026-021, bug 41274, bugfix on 0.2.6.1-alpha, and the direct error-return remediation in 0.4.9.9.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Scriban expression evaluation (CWE-400) lets a template author exhaust memory or CPU on three paths that ignore existing LoopLimit/LimitToString controls. Vector 1: ScriptBinaryExpression.CalculateToString implements string*int as an unbounded C# for-loop that Appends into a StringBuilder, so '{{ 'AAAA' * 500000000 }}' attempts a multi-gigabyte allocation even when LimitToString defaults to 1MB. Vector 2: CalculateLongWithInt and CalculateBigIntegerNoFit apply BigInteger << (int)right with no cap, so '{{ 1 << 100000000 }}' allocates an arbitrarily large integer (Power is capped with MaxBigInteger, but shift is not). Vector 3: '..' / '..<' produce lazy RangeInclude/RangeExclude iterators; ArrayFunctions.Size fully enumerates via Cast<object>().Count() and Join appends with no size bound, never calling StepLoop(), so '{{ (0..1000000000) | array.size }}' burns CPU despite LoopLimit=1000. OutOfMemoryException typically terminates the host process. Vendor/CVE range is all versions before 7.0.0.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Composer debug verbosity (-vvv) printed credentials that were placed in the username slot of a repository or package URL (the documented GitHub PAT form https://TOKEN@host/), while already masking the password slot of user:password@ URLs. Source: a token or other secret embedded as URL userinfo without a password, typically in composer.json repositories or dist/source URLs, not auth.json/COMPOSER_AUTH. Sinks: (1) ProcessExecutor::outputCommandRun / execute() wrote 'Executing command …' after a sanitizer that only matched ://user:password@, so ://TOKEN@ passed through; (2) Url::sanitize() used the same colon-required regex, so CurlDownloader/RemoteFilesystem 'Downloading'/'Following redirect' debug lines showed the token; (3) AuthHelper basic-auth debug wrote the raw HTTP-Basic username. Attack path is local/log disclosure (CVSS AV:L/AC:H): anyone who can read captured -vvv output (CI logs, pasted terminals) obtains the token. Short ordinary usernames were intentionally left visible; long/token usernames were the secret.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Velociraptor org_delete is a cross-org operation that must require ORG_ADMIN on the ROOT org. OrgDeleteFunction.Call is the sink: it calls vql_subsystem.CheckAccess for a single permission, then OrgManager.DeleteOrg, which deletes another org's datastore/services with no further ACL check. Before the fix, ServerACLManager.CheckAccess always evaluated that permission against the calling org's effective policy (GetPolicyInOrg(config_obj.OrgId)). The original org_delete therefore accepted a child-org SERVER_ADMIN token. After the permission name was changed to ORG_ADMIN, a child-org administrator (SERVER_ADMIN in that org, not ROOT) could still succeed by writing OrgAdmin/org_admin onto their child-org ACL (SetPolicy and the user-inspector GUI did not forbid it); CheckAccess then saw ORG_ADMIN on the calling-org token and allowed deletion of other tenants. The 0.77.2 fix keeps org_delete's ORG_ADMIN requirement but forces that permission to be read from ROOT and prevents attaching it to non-root orgs.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Scriban's recursive-descent parser treats nested array initializers as expressions. ParseArrayInitializer consumes '[' then calls ExpectAndParseExpression, which calls ParseExpression; ParseExpression on TokenType.OpenBracket calls ParseArrayInitializer again. Deeply nested input such as '{{ ' + new string('[', 5000) + '1' + new string(']', 5000) + ' }}' therefore grows C# call-stack frames without a terminating depth bound. The GHSA-wgh7-7m3c-fx25 6.6.0 mitigation (default ExpressionDepthLimit applied inside EnterExpression) did not wrap ParseArrayInitializer, and at 6.6.0 EnterExpression only logged once then continued parsing, so Template.Parse of untrusted nested arrays still raised an uncatchable StackOverflowException and killed the process (CWE-674).

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated SQL injection (CWE-89) in Camaleon CMS PostUniqValidator. Creating or editing a post with editor/author privileges submits post[slug]; the validator splits record.slug via translations_array and interpolates each fragment s into an ActiveRecord where() fragment as posts.slug LIKE '%-->#{s}<!--%'. Only the equality arm (slug = ?) is bound. A crafted slug with SQL metacharacters is therefore compiled into the uniqueness query, enabling boolean- or union-style blind extraction (and limited modification) of SQLite application tables, including admin credentials and configuration. Draft posts skip the check; published/pending posts hit it on save.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Authenticated PATCH /api/v2/connections and PATCH /api/v2/variables accept a BulkBody whose only top-level key is actions; Variable values and Connection extra sit in actions[].entities[]. action_logging() records the JSON body into airflow.models.Log.extra. Any user who can read audit logs can recover them, including after UI Import Variables. This is a different path from the 3.3.0 single-entity masking fix.

causal_research.bug_semantics: devalue.parse JSON-parses a payload then unflatten/hydrate reconstructs values. Two typed-array encodings can yield a result object that owns a `__proto__` key. (1) Malformed Object-wrapper: stringify of boxed primitives emits ["Object", primitive], but parse historically did Object(value[1]) on the raw JSON slot. A payload such as [["Object",{"__proto__":1}],{}] therefore returns the JSON.parse object whose own `__proto__` property JSON.parse created via [[DefineOwnProperty]]. (2) Null-prototype objects: ["null", key, idx, ...] does Object.create(null) and assigns keys with obj[key] = hydrate(idx); key '__proto__' becomes an own property because there is no prototype setter. A caller that then does Object.assign(target, result) copies that enumerable own `__proto__` via [[Set]], invoking target's setter and replacing target's [[Prototype]]. Regular POJO hydration already rejected `__proto__` keys from 5.3.2 (0623a47 / GHSA-vj54-72f3-p5jv / CVE-2025-57820); this GHSA is the remaining emission paths. It is not CVE-2026-30226 / GHSA-cfw5-2vxh-hr84 (in-library prototype pollution).

With the ImageMagick CLI backend, crop/resize interpolated bg into an xc: shell argument and rotation interpolated it into the -background argument without shell escaping. A crafted value could break the quoted command context and execute operating-system commands as the web-server user. The path requires the resize command and ImageMagick CLI backend to be enabled and reachable.

The object-level route parameter {fee_invoice} is therefore gated only by school membership and a generic permission, with no owner/guardian/relationship check: any same-school holder of 'read fee invoice' can read any student's invoice by ID (CWE-639 same-school IDOR). This is an application-wide origin problem, not a school-isolation bug: BIC itself correctly scopes list/create paths by users.school_id, and no guardian/staff-scoped policy variant exists anywhere in the code at BIC, tag V2.6.4, or HEAD. BIC/parent comparison: parent b5b9d825 'Changed timetable button size' (same author) has zero FeeInvoice controller/policy/model/routes/views paths (tree grep count 0); BIC adds all of them (controller, policy, model, service, migrations, seeder, factories, views, routes, tests) in one 42-file, +1459/-26 commit. Minimum fix: strengthen view() with owner/guardian-scoped checks after the school-scope precondition; no such fix exists on main. Unmerged branch modernization/domain-slices commit 7ac395937ca4 'fix portal role boundaries and invoice replay' (2026-09-03, Marvellous) does implement it: view() keeps permission+current-school gate but then requires student->student_record_id == $user->studentRecord->id, parent->child-link exists() through parent_records.user_id, and blocks portal-only roles from viewAny() via isPortalOnly(), with a new child-scoped portal invoices screen (17 files, +453/-54). It is NOT reachable from HEAD 8de86bac (merge-base --is-ancestor fails; remote branch head 99f363a4). Main's only later policy change is 76294e072655 'Awoken' (2026-08-20, Marvellous), which merely rewrites '$feeInvoice->user->school_id == auth()->user()->school_id' to the semantically equivalent '$feeInvoice->user->belongsToCurrentSchool()' inside a 619-file/+24721/-8794 modernization sweep; the school-scope-only authorization persists at HEAD, so the vuln is unpatched on main (fix_sha null). causal_research.bug_semantics: On --restore, hashcat reads argc/argv from a binary restore file and re-parses them with the full option table (user_options_getopt; originally getopt_long) after discarding the user's typed command line. There is no allowlist or denylist, so a crafted restore file can inject output-redirecting options such as --outfile/--outfile-format and --potfile-path. With a guaranteed-crack hash+wordlist pair, cracked plaintext is appended to an attacker-chosen writable path (e.g. ~/.bashrc), yielding arbitrary file write and follow-on command execution. CWE-88. CVE.org PUBLISHED, affected through 7.1.2; GitHub advisory not withdrawn.
evidence: CVE.org CVE-2026-68766 state=PUBLISHED (assigner VulnCheck, datePublished 2026-08-22); not rejected. Affected hashcat versions 0 through 7.1.2 inclusive. GHSA-5qq7-x27p-hfq4 withdrawn_at=null.

causal_research.bug_semantics: An authenticated BGP peer can place an IPv4 martian address such as 0.0.0.0 in the IPv4/VPNv4 next-hop field of MP_REACH_NLRI. bgp_mp_reach_parse copied that attacker-controlled value into attr->mp_nexthop_global_in without the validation applied to ordinary NEXT_HOP. causal_research.bug_semantics: Applications that deserialize untrusted MessagePack maps into System.Dynamic.ExpandoObject via ExpandoObjectFormatter.Deserialize or ExpandoObjectResolver (including nested maps from PrimitiveObjectWithExpandoMaps.DeserializeMap / the original PrimitiveObjectFormatter.InstanceWithExpandoObject path) allocate an ExpandoObject and call IDictionary<string, object>.Add once per map key. ExpandoObject stores member names in array-like structures, so each insert can scan and copy existing members. An attacker-controlled map with many distinct keys therefore costs quadratic CPU and allocations relative to encoded size. MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData only swaps dictionary comparers and does not bound or hash ExpandoObject insertion, so the UntrustedData preset advertised on ExpandoObjectResolver.Options does not stop the super-linear work. The 2026 fix rejects maps larger than 1024 entries when options.Security.HashCollisionResistant is set.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CVE-2026-73522 is a CWE-121 stack buffer overflow in Open1722's ACF-CAN example listener. avtp_to_can() in examples/acf-can/acf-can-common.c walks every ACF-CAN message in a received AVTP/UDP datagram and writes into can_frames[i++] with no capacity argument and no bound against MAX_CAN_FRAMES_IN_ACF (15). The Linux listener allocates a 15-slot stack array and the default stream ID 0xAABBCCDDEEFF0001 is hardcoded and unauthenticated on the wire, so an unauthenticated sender can put more than 15 valid ACF-CAN messages in one datagram and overflow adjacent stack (researcher ASan: 15 messages clean, 16 overflow at the payload memcpy). The same unbounded writer is reused by the Zephyr bridge. Distinct from CVE-2026-73523 (uint8_t truncation of a -1 return).

mechanism.impact: Unbounded single-threaded CPU consumption while tokenizing one small request body; any service that runs TweetTokenizer or casual_tokenize on submitted text can be stalled per request, unauthenticated (CVSS v4 8.7, VA:H).
mechanism.preconditions: Untrusted text reaches TweetTokenizer.tokenize / casual_tokenize on a worker; no special configuration; the payload only needs a long alternating label-separator run that no trailing TLD can terminate.
mechanism.summary: TweetTokenizer.tokenize() (or casual_tokenize) is applied to attacker-supplied text; the URLS naked-domain branch [a-z0-9]+(?:[.\-][a-z0-9]+)* demands a trailing [.][a-z]{2,13}\b that a label-separator flood never supplies, so a backtracking engine re-partitions the run at every offset and burns seconds of CPU per few-KB input (CWE-1333 availability DoS).
mechanism.trigger: TweetTokenizer().tokenize("a." * n) or casual_tokenize on a few KB of alternating label separators with no valid TLD terminator; the pre-compiled HANG_RE.sub does not collapse it because no character repeats four times.

causal_research.bug_semantics: AWS CDK L2 CodeBuild Project.renderLoggingConfiguration maps user-facing S3LoggingOptions.encrypted (positive polarity: true means encrypt S3 build logs) directly onto CloudFormation AWS::CodeBuild::Project LogsConfig.S3Logs.EncryptionDisabled (negative polarity: true means do not encrypt). Explicit encrypted:true therefore synthesizes EncryptionDisabled:true and disables CodeBuild's default AWS-managed encryption of S3 logs; encrypted:false synthesizes EncryptionDisabled:false and leaves encryption on. Omitting encrypted passes undefined, so CloudFormation keeps the encrypt-by-default behavior. The same module already implemented the correct negation for artifact encryption (artifacts.ts: encryptionDisabled: this.props.encryption === false ? true : undefined). After 2023-01-05, S3 SSE-S3 default encryption still encrypts new objects, so residual exposure is mainly pre-that-date logs in buckets without default encryption, matching the low-severity GHSA.

causal_research.bug_semantics: TransitionParser.parse(depgraphs, modelFile) opens a caller-supplied model path and deserializes it with unrestricted pickle. In 3.9.4 that is pickle_load(f) defaulting to restricted=False, which uses WarningUnpickler: it emits a RuntimeWarning then calls pickle.Unpickler.load() without overriding find_class(), so pickle GLOBAL opcodes resolve arbitrary callables (os.system, subprocess.Popen, etc.). An attacker who can place or substitute the model file gets code execution when the victim parses with that path. RestrictedUnpickler existed in nltk/picklesec.py but no production TransitionParser path passed restricted=True.

causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-416 use-after-free of a function pointer in miSyncDestroyFence(). When a fence is destroyed, the function sets sync.beingDestroyed and walks pFence->sync.pTriglist, invoking each trigger's CounterDestroyed callback (SyncAwaitTriggerFired for Await) before capturing ptl->next and freeing the list node. CounterDestroyed can FreeResource the Await, and FreeAwait then frees the entire SyncAwaitUnion for that Await group while skipping SyncDeleteTriggerFromSyncObject because beingDestroyed is already set. If one Await has multiple conditions on the same fence, later SyncTriggerList nodes still hold pTrigger pointers into the freed union; the next iteration performs (*ptl->pTrigger->CounterDestroyed) on dangling memory. A local client can Await a fence with multiple triggers, then a second connection DestroyFence to crash the server or escalate if it runs as root.

causal_research.bug_semantics: Invoice Ninja 5 admin Restore (POST import_json) accepts chunked backups when the request carries metadata. ImportJsonRequest authorizes only isAdmin() and mime-checks the files field as zip; the chunked path instead reads request file 'file' and JSON metadata with no type/path validation. handleChunkedUpload() builds sys_get_temp_dir()/{$fileHash}/app/chunks/, mkdir 0777, writes the raw chunk as {$currentChunk}, then concatenates to {$fileName} and Storage::put('migrations/'.$fileName). An admin can set fileHash/fileName/currentChunk to path-traversal values and upload .php content, landing an executable file on the server (CWE-434 / CAPEC-175). causal_research.bug_semantics: In SPIP 4.4.20, analyse_resultat_skel() examined the inner text of each PHP block with an anchored header() regular expression that mistakenly retained PCRE's multiline modifier. Because ^ and $ therefore matched individual lines rather than the whole PHP block, an unauthenticated attacker could inject a newline-delimited header("X-Spip-Filtre: intval|_request|system") line into generated template code. SPIP extracted that attacker-selected filter chain, intval reduced the body to the key 0, _request read attacker-controlled POST parameter 0, and system executed it, yielding pre-authentication remote code execution.
causal_research.flaw_origin: The vulnerable product code is in the upstream spip/ecrire repository, not in the bundled rapid7/metasploit-framework reference. Commit d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d rewrote public/composer.php to collect individual PHP blocks and first added the vulnerable /^...$/ims match over each block's innerHtml. Its immediate parent used a materially different whole-page preg_match_all implementation and did not contain this vulnerable collector-plus-multiline-anchors mechanism. Rapid7 commit b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c only added an exploit module and documentation after the SPIP flaw existed; it neither introduced nor fixed SPIP.

causal_research.bug_semantics: With OAuth enabled behind a reverse proxy that terminates browser-facing HTTPS and forwards the callback to Temporal UI Server over HTTP, authentication cookies used c.Request().TLS != nil to choose Secure. That request describes only the proxy-to-server hop, so the server could emit user* access/ID-token cookies and, later, refresh-token cookies without Secure even though the browser authenticated over HTTPS. Exploitation additionally requires steering the UI hostname to attacker-served HTTP, preventing HTTPS, and receiving a later same-site plaintext request while the credential is live; malicious content alone or passive observation of the successful TLS session is insufficient.

causal_research.bug_semantics: A quote may carry orig_order_id via Magento\Quote\Api\Data\CartInterface (getOrigOrderId/setOrigOrderId). Magento\Quote\Model\QuoteManagement::submitQuote assigns that value to the new order's entity_id, so Magento updates an existing sales_order row instead of inserting a new order. PUT /V1/carts/mine persists the cart through CartRepositoryInterface::save (ACL resource self); async Web API (Magento_WebapiAsync) queues the same service and the consumer runs outside the webapi_rest area. Until the 2025 fix, ownership of orig_order_id was either unchecked (GA 2.4.4–2.4.7) or checked only by Magento\Quote\Plugin\ValidateQuoteOrigOrder registered in webapi_rest/di.xml (2.4.8 / *-p security lines before APSB25-50). An attacker who can save a quote with another customer's order id and then place the order overwrites that prior order: CWE-284, limited integrity write, matching APSB25-50 / CVE-2025-27206. Preconditions: reachable cart-save + placeOrder (customer self and/or async consumer); no extra UI click. Counterevidence: XSS in Email Template\Filter is CVE-2025-47110; downloadable/guest checkout observers are CVE-2025-43585; B2B CVEs 27207/43586 are out of scope.

causal_research.bug_semantics: When ospfd has `debug ospf packet ... detail` enabled, ospf_packet_dump() walks an LS Update and, for opaque LSAs, calls ospf_opaque_lsa_dump(), which invokes show_opaque_info_detail(NULL, &lsa, NULL). The Extended Link functab callback ospf_ext_link_show_info is registered at ospf_ext_init() during ospf_opaque_init(), so a received Type-10 opaque LSA with an Extended Link TLV and a LAN-Adjacency-SID sub-TLV reaches show_vty_ext_link_lan_adj_sid with vty==NULL and json==NULL. That function then calls vty_out(vty, ...) (and, on a length mismatch, check_tlv_size's vty_out) without testing vty. vty_out dereferences vty->status, crashing ospfd (CWE-476 DoS). Preconditions: packet-debug DETAIL on, and an OSPF LS Update carrying that sub-TLV; local Segment Routing need not be enabled because the show callback is registered at init. Counterevidence that this is VTY-only is false: the dump path has passed NULL vty since before the function existed.

Mechanism: the BIC family parses attacker-controlled header fields (posEps, posEndEps = getULong(...)+posEps, posWmf/sizeWmf, posTiff/sizeTiff) and validates them with unscaled arithmetic 'posX < 30 || posX + sizeX > size' / 'posEndEps > size'; on the write path the checked offsets are then used unchecked to memcpy whole sections out of the mmap ('writeTemp(tempIo, data + posWmf, sizeWmf)' at epsimage.cpp:1009 in the fix parent), so a size/offset that wraps or underflows the comparison (e.g. uint32_t sizeX such that posX+sizeX wraps; posX+sizeX was computed in 64-bit size_t for posX but sizeX is uint32_t since vog's own 115ba5a0 narrowed the declarations) passes the check and makes MemIo::write read far past the mapping. GHSA-496f-x7cq-cq39 stack trace confirms OOB read in MemIo::write <- writeTemp <- readWriteEpsMetadata (epsimage.cpp:1009) <- Exiv2::EpsImage::writeMetadata <- 'exiv2 -d a'; CVE record: CWE-125, affected < 0.28.6. Minimum fix f02c970a ('Better bounds checking to fix GHSA-496f-x7cq-cq39', Kevin Backhouse, 2025-07-29) changes only src/epsimage.cpp (+11/-29): replaces the weak checks with overflow-safe 'enforce(posEps <= posEndEps && posEndEps <= size)'; 'enforce(posWmf <= size && sizeWmf <= size - posWmf)'; 'enforce(posTiff <= size && sizeTiff <= size - posTiff)' and enforce(size >= 30), keeping the same error semantics (throw on write path). causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-22 / CWE-59 path traversal through a symlink whose name passes the guard. FramenetCorpusReader validates only the name it interpolates into a corpus-relative XML path (no separators, no '..', no Windows drive prefix) and never validates the resolved path. A symlink planted inside the corpus's own subdirectory (frame/, lu/, fulltext/) carries a clean name, so it passes; FileSystemPathPointer.join performs only a lexical normpath prefix check on the un-resolved path; and the file is then opened through FileSystemPathPointer.open -> nltk.pathsec.open -> validate_path(path, context='pathsec.open') with required_root unset, so only the global NLTK sandbox applies and the corpus-root boundary is not enforced. Impact: an XML file outside the corpus root but inside the global sandbox (nltk_data roots, the system temp dir) is parsed and its text returned to the caller through frame_by_name(), _lu_file() or doc(); the advisory scores it CVSS 3.1 7.5 and CVSS 4.0 8.7 HIGH, and CISA ADP lists Exploitation=poc. An owner-authorized DELETE invokes a synchronous unguarded child descent before commit. A reachable remaining cycle causes unbounded CPU work while request/session data remains live and blocks the selected asyncio worker. Default startup has one worker; no universal replica outage, RSS measurement or runtime exploit result is asserted.
causal_research.counterevidence: Owner checks, update-path normalization, current-ID repair and normalized message rows do not enforce acyclicity on the own-chat JSON creation/deletion path. Default one-worker impact does not extend automatically to all replicas. Ordinary deletion terminates and intentionally changes the caller's own chat.

causal_research.decomposition_probe: Not applicable: coherent original member is recovered; its main carrier is independently content-matched.

Full ownership/JSON-engine patches do not introduce relevant exposure or attempt cycle repair. Auditor2 local commits are a strict subset. This does not rule out undisclosed private assistance or absent deleted remote history.

causal_research.ai_admissibility: No positive causal AI evidence admitted. Marked exact-helper descendants change other operations. Human/unmarked current-ID hardening and successful repair do not establish AI participation in the reported failure.

fix_ai_marker.basis: Actual original member and dev squash metadata contain no AI marker; default integration is kept separate from repair attribution.

causal_research.remaining_gap: No decisive causal fact remains open within the public local-history and official source-release scope. Undisclosed private assistance, every deployment's runtime outage magnitude and distributed platform-byte identity are outside the assertions.

A different causal parent/member or an official released source with different caller/guard would change the corresponding history or repair finding.

causal_research.verdict_basis:
**NOT_AI under the frozen attribution threshold.** CakePHP Queue has a real conditional job-admission availability defect: uniqueness normalization discards parameter keys and positions, allowing semantically different data to have the same identifier and causing the second job to be omitted. The introducing object has a recovered named human identity, no AI marker, and a dated disclosure-convention check. This is an evidence classification, not proof that undisclosed private tool use never occurred.

The causal member is f3d2883b7482311c018da764d8c4c382a8b3ddd7; its default-branch carrier is fb2bd807e9ecf867a459a685a00e21572692b6ad. Repair member 13890591e248acc8824becb24ba1939fa061bd34 reaches the default branch through 4a9d77a4865896a8464318f36962e107a0757b22, tagged 2.3.1. The correct structured fix classification for that integration is **CARRIER_BUNDLE**, correcting auditor2's ATOMIC label without changing the demonstrated repair.

Independent research closes auditor2's disputed earlier-version question: the complete 0.1.10 producer and source inventory contain no uniqueness-cache admission path under another helper name. More strongly, the Composer distribution archives selected by current Packagist metadata were downloaded for 0.1.10, 0.1.11 and 2.3.1. All library source files in those archives match their corresponding Git source: respectively 16, 17 and 35 files. Thus the content boundary is established for these retrieved distribution artifacts as well as source tags. The first affected release is 0.1.11, contrary to the GHSA metadata's 0.1.10 lower bound. The current CVE description agrees with 0.1.11.
causal_research.cause: Attacker-influenced parameters of an enabled unique job pass through lossy value sorting, producing an identity already present in the configured cache and suppressing semantically distinct work before sendEvent. Application reachability and cache lifetime condition the availability impact.
causal_research.mechanism:
At affected 2.3.0, QueueManager::push resolves an application job class and selected method, obtains configuration, and gates uniqueness handling on shouldBeUnique. An unknown class fails before admission; missing required uniqueCache configuration raises an exception. getUniqueId takes an array by value and executes sort($data), then json_encode, concatenation with class/method, and MD5 hashing. The first-party PHP sort manual explicitly describes reassignment of keys. Values sorted into the same sequence therefore lose the distinction carried by the original keys or positional order. The demonstrated failure occurs before hashing; no cryptanalytic MD5 collision is needed.

The resulting ID is the unique-cache key. A truthy Cache::read returns from push before ClientMessage creation and sendEvent. After an admitted job is sent, Cache::add stores true under that ID. The message retains the original array in data and legacy args[0], because the normalization operated on a copy. Job/Message::getArgument retrieves that unmodified representation; Queue/Processor invokes the selected job with the Message. Thus the identity comparator can conflate data that the real consumer distinguishes. The protected operation is admission of legitimate, semantically distinct queued work.

The reported attack requires an integrating application to permit influence over relevant parameters, an enabled unique job, a configured cache, matching resolved class/method and cache namespace, and a still-live entry for the colliding identity. The library provides no universal unauthenticated network endpoint. The advisory's network/unauthenticated assessment depends on the integrating application's authorization and data flow. No such endpoint or deployed target was inspected. Job suppression supports conditional availability impact; no confidentiality or code-execution claim follows.

The configured cache defaults to a 24-hour duration unless overridden. The worker cleanup extension recomputes the ID from Message::getArgument and deletes it; 2.3.0/2.3.1 worker wiring passes the configured uniqueCacheKey. Cache expiration and successful worker progress limit the suppression window. Identical work being deduplicated is legitimate feature behavior, as PR #108 explains. Jobs with uniqueness disabled bypass this check. These contrasts constrain the claim and do not refute the key-loss defect.

Primary receipts: evidence/02-caller-chain.txt; 14-corrected-consumer-path.txt; 11-php-sort.body; 12-php-ksort.body; package-0.1.10-QueueManager.php; package-0.1.11-QueueManager.php; package-2.3.1-QueueManager.php. Static source and upstream regression test inspection establish the account; no runtime job or exploit was executed.
causal_research.bug_semantics: CWE-1023: comparison discards parameter keys and positions before hashing.
causal_research.flaw_origin: Named-human unique-jobs feature f3d2883b7482311c018da764d8c4c382a8b3ddd7 adds both the lossy identity and the admission/cleanup machinery; no prior origin is inferred.
causal_research.bic_note:
Immediate parent 906bc11fc161a308af42f0b32b01a12de1290863 lacks the uniqueness helper and suppressing producer path. **NOT_AI under the frozen attribution threshold.** CakePHP Queue has a real conditional job-admission availability defect: uniqueness normalization discards parameter keys and positions, allowing semantically different data to have the same identifier and causing the second job to be omitted. The introducing object has a recovered named human identity, no AI marker, and a dated disclosure-convention check. This is an evidence classification, not proof that undisclosed private tool use never occurred.

The causal member is f3d2883b7482311c018da764d8c4c382a8b3ddd7; its default-branch carrier is fb2bd807e9ecf867a459a685a00e21572692b6ad. The correct structured fix classification for that integration is **CARRIER_BUNDLE**, correcting auditor2's ATOMIC label without changing the demonstrated repair.

More strongly, the Composer distribution archives selected by current Packagist metadata were downloaded for 0.1.10, 0.1.11 and 2.3.1. All library source files in those archives match their corresponding Git source: respectively 16, 17 and 35 files. Thus the content boundary is established for these retrieved distribution artifacts as well as source tags. The first affected release is 0.1.11, contrary to the GHSA metadata's 0.1.10 lower bound. The current CVE description agrees with 0.1.11.

causal_research.landing_note: All 13 exposed PR members recovered. Parent has discovery scaffolding but no IPP config flow. The member adds discovery-controlled shared-session printer probing before confirmation when UUID is absent. The final member flow blob is carried by the squash; independent member-to-landing diff traces the same constructor/request hunk through extraction into validate_input, without claiming whole-file equality.
causal_research.decomposition_probe: Original bounded depth-16 PR-ref fetch succeeded for PR 32859 and PR 162941; preserved git-fetch.txt. Adjudicator inspected the copied retained Git objects with lazy fetching disabled, including parent/member/carrier diffs and all 40 local commit objects; no second membership hunt was required.
causal_research.bic_minimality: First recovered addition of the keyed automatic IPP discovery request. The 2016 helper creation refactors an existing core.websession and is neither first shared-session creation nor this IPP exposure.
causal_research.disclosure_convention_evidence: Full-SHA retrieval of the introducing member PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md shows no examined AI disclosure convention. Named author Chris Talkington <chris@talkingtontech.com>; all local commit metadata inspected.
causal_research.ai_admissibility: No accepted causal disclosure on the introducing member or recovered PR/repair members. Local inventory covers 40 selected shallow/promisor commit objects at four paths, not all upstream history. Copilot-marked OneDrive/Google descendants have empty relevant diffs. Additional Claude default-header, Copilot annotation-import, and Claude aioipp/logging changes are explicitly examined: none introduces this redirect exposure or attempts its security repair. Their markers are retained as noncausal evidence and do not attribute unchanged old logic. Undisclosed use remains outside this evidence threshold.

ai_evidence.basis: Preserves caller default headers; redirect guard unchanged.
IPP parent/child differs only by removal of future-annotations import.
Logging/dependency update; official aioipp package retains existing redirect defaults, with no new exposure or security-remediation contribution shown.

causal_research.cause: Active zeroconf discovery routes untrusted printer service information into a pre-confirmation shared-session IPP request. The redirect-following client can issue a request to a discovery-controlled different recipient, including loopback, under the Home Assistant process network authority.
causal_research.mechanism: Discovery host/port/rp -> IPPFlowHandler.async_step_zeroconf -> validate_input -> IPP.printer -> pyipp session.request -> aiohttp redirect loop. Current middleware validates Location only, while the version-matched consumer also accepts URI; validation does not cover all consumed redirect destinations.
causal_research.bug_semantics: Missing destination restriction at the untrusted automatic-discovery request boundary; partial repair checks fewer redirect representations than its consumer follows.
causal_research.counterevidence: Normal printer discovery, relative redirects and already-loopback operations are legitimate. Configured/ignored matches and disabled zeroconf avoid the automatic probe. No arbitrary response exfiltration or endpoint-specific compromise is established. Caller credentials are unset and aiohttp removes auth/Authorization on origin changes; network reachability is the demonstrated authority.
causal_research.fix: Confirmed unpatched residual in inspected source releases; published Location guard is partial, not a mechanism-closing change.

partial_repairs.role: stable landing of same partial-repair helper

unpatched.reason: The exact caller activates the shared client. Both 2026.2.3/aiohttp 3.13.3 and 2026.9.4/aiohttp 3.14.3 return through a Location-only validator to a redirect selector also accepting URI. This is a source-confirmed pre-request coverage failure; no exploit execution.
unpatched.scope: Inspected Home Assistant source releases with active accepted IPP discovery; binary/container identity and endpoint impact unmeasured.

potential_fix.approach: Align pre-request validation with the consuming redirect destination selection and normalization, or disable redirects for untrusted discovery retrieval.
potential_fix.rationale: The validator must cover every destination representation the actual dependency follows, while considering legitimate printer behavior.

versions.scope: Source release membership; no first-ever affected version or distributed-artifact claim.

causal_research.remaining_gap: No complete mechanism-closing object/release is demonstrated; current inspected source establishes the unpatched residual, rather than an unreadable repair. Runtime endpoint effects and distributed binaries are unmeasured and unclaimed. NOT_AI is scoped to causal object/convention evidence, not undisclosed assistance.
causal_research.flip_condition: A source-bound AI contribution introducing/exposing this mechanism or attempting incomplete security remediation changes attribution. A version-matched pre-request operation preventing the observed residual refutes it; a demonstrated complete repair and release membership establishes closure.
causal_research.reasoning: Direct independent parent/child and caller/dependency observations support the active defect and named human exposure. The 2016 helper is a move of an existing session, not the keyed introduction. Reported patch members/landings ship a partial guard; exact version-matched source supports a residual. Additional current AI-marked edits were examined and are noncausal. Source-release and authority qualifications are retained.

causal_research.cause: A consumed chunked response from an application-selected server enters urllib3 stream/read_chunked and buffers each framing line through unbounded fp.readline before validation. CPython retains line pieces and joins them, so per-operation memory scales with supplied bytes despite finite reusable buffers; body amt and read timeouts are not framing-byte budgets. Trailer reads share this operation. Direct urllib3 read uses bounded stdlib framing. Requests v2.32.5 ordinary adapter sets preload_content=False and both iter_content and eager content use raw.stream; even stream=False accesses content through that parser. This representative caller is supported without claiming every historical/custom adapter. Source-derived resource behavior was not measured with an exploit.

causal_research.cause: A plain stored options object resolves omitted Worker and balancer options through Object.prototype after public constructor sanitization.
causal_research.mechanism:
At pre-fix default parent a20ff72ec2fd9f7535c49320b3a4076d754f307d, public Piscina construction creates a null-prototype copy of own input fields. Validation and ThreadPool receive that copy. ThreadPool then stores `{ ...kDefaultOptions, ...options, filename, maxQueue: 0 }` as a normal object, restoring Object.prototype inheritance. This is the decisive lost boundary: constructor sanitization alone does not protect the eventual consuming reads.

Defaults give own values to filename/name, niceIncrement, closeTimeout, recordTiming, stricterFIFO, workerHistogram and trackUnmanagedFds. Ambient pollution of those names is shadowed in the stored pool at the inspected revision. There is no own default for resourceLimits, env, argv, execArgv, workerData or loadBalancer. When omitted, reads of those names can resolve through the ambient prototype. Explicit legitimate own options override that lookup. The spread itself copies own enumerable fields; it does not need to copy polluted inherited fields for the subsequent read to be dangerous.

Real activation: ThreadPool constructor calls _ensureMinimumWorkers, which calls _addNewWorker; default minThreads is at least one. Later task-driven expansion can activate worker creation when minThreads is zero. _addNewWorker assigns own env/argv/execArgv/resourceLimits/workerData fields from stored pool reads into WorkerInfo's worker parameter. WorkerInfo extracts filename and forwards the rest to `new Worker(filename, workerOpts)`. Thus an inherited pool option becomes an explicit own option at the consuming Node boundary. This is not a claim based solely on an unused helper or interface.

Official Node worker documentation binds execArgv to worker CLI options and module preloading. Execution requires an accepted option and a code/module source available to that worker; an arbitrary JSON pollution primitive does not automatically establish every prerequisite. env changes worker environment; env injection alone is not universal proof of arbitrary execution. resourceLimits and workerData can affect worker configuration and operation; resource impact was not measured. No operational payload was created.

loadBalancer is selected from `this.options.loadBalancer ?? LeastBusyBalancer(...)`, then invoked as this.balancer(task.interface, workers) during distribution. A callable inherited value can execute as a scheduler callback in the main thread. Producing a function requires stronger control than JSON-only data; malformed non-callable values can instead fail when this path runs. The trusted application's ordinary explicit callback configuration is legitimate; unintended inheritance supplies the crossing of authority.

The advisory survives the qualifications to its broader enumeration: inherited execArgv/env and a suitably controlled callable balancer remain supported paths. Initial direct constructor validation and other historical raw option reads are separate surfaces, not evidence that the missing worker options already existed in the first implementation. Nested explicitly supplied objects, hostile own getters, unrelated Node internals and downstream applications are outside the claimed universal repair assurance.

Primary observations: sources/a20ff72ec2fd9f7535c49320b3a4076d754f307d__src_index.ts and __src_worker_pool_index.ts, with exact Git commands in their source receipts; sources/node-worker-docs.md and node-docs-capture.json. Those are source-based observations and causal inferences, not an executed attack.

application retrieves labels from an untrusted PDF. Both original verdicts hold,
but auditor2's atomic origin/repair claims and carrier-coverage argument require
correction. The recovered introducing member is human-identified and lacks an AI
marker; contemporaneous disclosure convention was not observed. Inspected later
AI-marked carriers disclose work on other operations. This threshold does not

The original negative-number-tree-key path and the later `/St` path are separate
exposures to the same unsafe conversion. The computed-value guard closes both
Roman cases. Independently downloaded official source distributions establish
vulnerable 6.16.2 and repaired 6.17.0 source content and caller/parser wiring.
The affected historical feature begins in the inspected 3.2.0 source tag; the

causal_research.mechanism:
At a667e9db92b4fba4de03f6b782ba1f3afec4da62, PdfReader inherits PdfDocCommon.
The latter imports `_page_labels.index2label` and its public `page_labels`
property invokes it for every page, returning a list of completed label strings.
Calling this property is the activation condition; merely opening a PDF does not
establish that it is evaluated. A PDF author controls catalog `/PageLabels`, the
direct `/Nums` array or a selected `/Kids` leaf, the numbering style `/R` or `/r`,
the numeric range key, `/St`, and optional prefix. Parser-produced NumberObject
values are Python integers, including signed numbers. Array/dictionary parsing
does not enforce the label-specific nonnegative-key constraint.

The selected entry computes `index - start_index + start`, with `/St` default 1.
The Roman formatter's first denomination divides this positive value by 1000
and allocates `'M' * quotient`; subsequent terms add a bounded remainder.
The generator's results become a list and a joined string; lowercase calls the
same formatter and `.lower()`. Thus produced length grows with numeric *value*,
roughly floor(n/1000), rather than numeric-token byte length. The 64-byte numeric
token limit at this revision bounds parsing, not the expanded numeral.
Dictionary/type checks, the depth-100 number-tree traversal bound and the
positive-value check do not bound positive expansion. MemoryError/OverflowError
are not the caught TypeError/ValueError tuple.

Intermediate strings remain alive through joining; the property retains finished
strings for all pages in its result, and subsequent calls recompute them. Static
source establishes allocation amplification and potential availability loss in
the embedding Python process. Exact allocator capacity, RSS and deployment
failure thresholds were not measured. No network endpoint or privileged pypdf
role is necessary for the library path; network reachability depends on an
embedding service exposing this operation. Ordinary page count and literal
prefix bytes remain separate costs and are not claimed universally bounded.

Auditor2's retained scalar result, length 10000 for value 10000000, is a bounded

causal_research.mechanism: Accepted untrusted raw address headers reach the synchronous Mailparser 3.9.24 caller and affected Nodemailer accumulator. Its pinned splitter enforces a default 1 MiB header-block cap per MIME node, admitting the upstream-reported sub-cap input absent stricter application checks. Applicable Node 22.20.0/V8 source proves a non-flat cons-string slice(-1) path through single-character SubString, StringCharCodeAt, runtime Flatten and full-prefix WriteToFlat. Repeated re-append/read can sum prefix-copy costs quadratically. This is conditional engine implementation evidence, not an ECMAScript mandate or local timing claim. Libmime folding introduces spaces that can suppress noBreak and segment the accumulating run; universal RFC folding survival is rejected. Storage, lifetimes and cap are addressed in REPORT.md.
causal_research.fix_note: c07f17518d25aca8ab2ad66968dcbca538c24b89 is the first default-branch mechanism-closing change after affected ad54add4c71c3e1745189764bdab2218b9f1b91b. It caches the last character per accumulation state, updates nonempty appends and all pushes, handles empty stripped tokens, and has no other in-loop accumulation mutation. Post-loop changes happen after cache use; recursive groups start fresh caches. It closes both join alternatives; swapping boolean operands alone does not. Sixteen ordinary npm CJS affected/fixed comparisons passed without timing or exhaustive equivalence claims. Both shipped module formats carry the invariant.
